dr is future timelike on {r_0 ≤ r ≤ r^♮}, and χ ∈ C^∞(Ω_*) with

    χ = 0 on (t_*^♭)⁻¹([1, 2]) ∪ r⁻¹([r_0, r_1]),       χ = 1 on {t_*^♭ ≥ 3} ∩ {r ≥ r_1⁺}.    (16.2)

Fix weights ([Hin26c, (7.3)])

    α_I < −½ + p̄_1,       α_+ < α_I − ½,       α_K ∈ ℝ,    (16.3)

with p̄_1 of Definition 15.38, and order functions 𝗌_0 < 𝗌, admissible for P_0 with weights α_+, α_K and margin 0
(Definition 15.44, produced by Proposition 15.43). In particular 𝗌 and 𝗌_0 are constant near each radial set and near
the trapped set (Definition 15.29 (3)–(6) and Proposition 15.43 (5)), and they satisfy there the thresholds of
Definition 15.29 with margin 0.

**Theorem 16.2** (The global regularity estimate.) There is C such that

    ‖χu‖_(H^(𝗌,(2α_I,α_+,α_K))_e3b)
        ≤ C (‖Pu‖_(H^(𝗌,(2α_I+2,α_++2,α_K))_e3b(Ω_*;E)^(•,−))
              + ‖u‖_(H^(𝗌_0,(2α_I,α_+,α_K))_e3b(Ω_*;E)^(•,−)))    (16.4)

for P = P_0, in the strong sense: if the right side is finite, so is the left, and (16.4) holds. There is d_0,
depending only on 𝗌_0 and 𝗌, such that (16.4) holds also for every operator P relative to P_0 satisfying
conditions (1)–(2) of Definition 15.36 with ℓ_I ∈ (0, ½], ℓ_+ > 0, ℓ_K > 0 (condition (3) not assumed) and with ε_P
small, with C uniform.

This is [Hin26c, Proposition 7.1] in dimension 4 + 1. The estimate loses one derivative: Pu is measured in H^𝗌, where
real principal type propagation would need only H^(𝗌−1). The loss comes from the trapped set (Proposition 16.17). The
spaces are those of Section 14.7: u is supported at the initial hypersurface {t_*^♭ = 1} and extendible at the final
one in {r = r_0}. Extended by zero, u is a distribution on M supported in {t_*^♭ ≥ 1}, and so is Pu. The proof is in
Section 16.5.

**Remark 16.3** (Uniformity in the model.) The constants below depend on the stationary model only through
finitely many norms of its coefficients and through the dynamical constants of Chapter 15, which are uniform for the
stationary models of parameters b near b_0 (Remark 15.20, Proposition 15.43 (4), Proposition 15.55). So
(16.4) holds uniformly also when P_0 is replaced by those models, or perturbed within the stationary wave-type
operators. This is [Hin26c, Remark 7.2]. The statement on large perturbations of P_0 in [Hin26c, Remark 7.3] is not
used and not proved here.

### 16.2 Commutator lemmas

In this section L is any operator of the form of Section 14.13.1, possibly on a vector bundle of another rank, with
real scalar principal symbol ℓ of order m. L_R, L_I and C_ǎ are those of (14.15), ℓ_I is the principal symbol
of L_I (an Hermitian matrix of order m − 1), norms are those of H^𝗍_e3b, and B, E, G are carried by χ
(Section 14.8.3). In the proofs of this chapter, auxiliary operators (the localisers Φ_0, Φ_E and Φ′ below, and the
operators G″, G^♯ and the like of later sections) are chosen by the rules (R1)–(R3) of Section 14.8.3 for the
operators of the statement at hand, and so are the cut-off χ_* of error terms ((R2)) and inner cut-offs ((R3)). For a
positive symbol ρ, homogeneous of degree −1 near fibre infinity, and κ > 0, the regulariser is
φ_ε := (1 + ερ⁻¹)^(−κ), ε ∈ (0, 1], and θ_ε := ερ⁻¹(1 + ερ⁻¹)⁻¹; (14.13) holds with ρ in place of ρ_∞, and
φ_ε has the properties stated after it. Section 14.10 states both for κ ∈ (0, ½]; they hold for every κ > 0 with the
same proof, the identity being exact for every κ and |1 − φ_ε| ≤ min(1, κερ⁻¹) as in the proof of Lemma 14.39
(b). δ_c ∈ [0, ¼] is the constant in the a priori term of Lemma 14.44 (an
inequality with δ_c = 0 implies the same inequality with every δ_c > 0), and ς ∈ {1, −1} the sign there.

**Lemma 16.4** (One step with a characteristic cut-off.) Let (i)–(ii) of Lemma 14.44 hold, with its
localisers Φ_0, Φ_E and its operators Ǎ_ε, B_ε, E_ε, and in place of its (iii) the following: there are real scalar
symbols j_ε, bounded in C^(M)_ν S̃^(2𝗌−m) and, for each ε, in C^(M)_ν S̃^(2𝗌−m−2κ), supported in K_1, such that for every
w ∈ H^(K′)_e3b, with J_ε := Op(j_ε)Φ_0,

    ς⟨C_(ǎ_ε) w, w⟩ ≤ −‖B_ε w‖² + ‖E_ε w‖² + 2 Re⟨J_ε L w, w⟩ + C_0‖w‖²_(𝗌−½+δ_c).    (16.5)

Then the conclusion (14.17) of Lemma 14.44 holds.

*Proof.* As for Lemma 14.44, with two additions to the steps of that proof. In Step 1, for fixed ε, ⟨J_ε L w_t,
w_t⟩ → ⟨J_ε L v, v⟩ as t → 0: w_t → v in H^(𝗌−κ), so L w_t → L v in H^(𝗌−κ−m), and J_ε* w_t → J_ε* v in H^(−𝗌+m+κ), J_ε*
having order 2𝗌 − m − 2κ for this ε without loss (Proposition 14.40 (a), by duality). In Step 2 the new term is
bounded at v = Φu: Lv = ΦLu + [L, Φ]u, and J_ε[L, Φ] = Op(j_ε)(Φ_0(I − Φ))L − Op(j_ε)(Φ_0L(I − Φ)) has every order
uniformly, as in Step 0 (Lemma 14.35, Proposition 14.40 (e)); and |⟨ΦLu, J_ε* v⟩| ≤ ‖ΦLu‖_(𝗌−m+1)
‖J_ε* v‖_(−𝗌+m−1). J_ε* is uniformly of order 2𝗌 − m + δ for every δ > 0, so ‖J_ε* v‖_(−𝗌+m−1) ≤ C‖v‖_(𝗌−1+δ) ≤
C(‖Gu‖_(𝗌−1+δ) + ‖χu‖_(−N′)), the last by (c) of Step 2 of that proof at the order 𝗌 − 1 + δ. With δ ≤ ½ and Step 0,
2|⟨J_ε L v, v⟩| ≤ C(‖GLu‖²_(𝗌−m+1) + ‖Gu‖²_(𝗌−½+δ_c) + ‖χu‖²_(−N′)), which is of the form of the right side of
(14.17). The global error term C_0‖v‖²_(𝗌−½+δ_c) is that of (14.16), bounded by (c) of Step 2. ∎

**Lemma 16.5** (Iteration.) Lemma 14.45 holds with Lemma 16.4 in place of Lemma 14.44.
Its hypotheses include the localisers: for each U as there, φ_0 = 1 near K_1 and φ_E = 1 near the support of e_ε, both
supported in U near fibre infinity, and supp φ_E lies in the closed set K_E(U), whose intersection with fibre infinity
lies in U ∖ Γ; the E of the conclusion is elliptic on the union K_E^* of these sets.

*Proof.* The proof of Lemma 14.45 uses Lemma 14.44 only through its conclusion (14.17) at each
step, which Lemma 16.4 supplies under its hypotheses; the proof therefore applies without change. ∎

**Lemma 16.6** (From a symbol identity to (16.5).) Let s be a constant order, k := s − ½(m − 1),
ǎ ∈ C^(M+2) S̃^k real and scalar, supported in a compact set K_1 near fibre infinity, and ǎ_ε := φ_ε ǎ. Suppose that
near fibre infinity

    ς (H_ℓ(ǎ_ε²) + 2ǎ_ε² ℓ_I) = −b_ε* b_ε − Σ_j b′_(j,ε)* b′_(j,ε) + Σ_i e_(i,ε)* e_(i,ε) + j_ε ℓ + f_ε,    (16.6)

with matrix symbols b_ε, b′_(j,ε), e_(i,ε) bounded in C^(M+2) S̃^s and lying in C^(M+2) S̃^(s−κ) for each ε, scalar j_ε
as in Lemma 16.4 (with ν = 0), and f_ε bounded in C^(M+2) S̃^(2s−1), all supported in K_1. Let Φ_0 = Op(φ_0)
and Φ_E = Op(φ_E) be smooth localisers carried by χ, with φ_0 = 1 near K_1 and φ_E = 1 near the supports of the
e_(i,ε), and put Ǎ_ε := Op(ǎ_ε)Φ_0. Then (16.5) holds for every w ∈ H^(K′)_e3b, with B_ε := Op(b_ε)Φ_0,
E_ε := Op(e_ε)Φ_E for the column e_ε of the e_(i,ε), J_ε := ½ Op(j_ε)Φ_0 and δ_c = 0; C_0 depends on finitely many
norms of the symbols and on the localisers. The same holds with a localiser Φ_(E,i) for each e_(i,ε) in place of Φ_E.

*Proof.* With constant orders and index 0, the remainders of Proposition 14.40 (b)–(f) have exact orders, and the
identities φ_0ǎ_ε = ǎ_ε, φ_0b_ε = b_ε, φ_0b′_(j,ε) = b′_(j,ε), φ_0j_ε = j_ε and φ_Ee_(i,ε) = e_(i,ε) are exact. As in
the paragraph on the commutator in the proof of Proposition 14.48, i[L_R, Ǎ_ε* Ǎ_ε] = Op(H_ℓ(ǎ_ε²)) + R_1 with R_1 of
order 2s − 1. The operator L_I Ǎ_ε* Ǎ_ε + Ǎ_ε* Ǎ_ε L_I − Op(2ǎ_ε² ℓ_I) is an expression in quantisations whose
principal symbol vanishes at order 2s, ǎ_ε being scalar and φ_0ǎ_ε = ǎ_ε. So by Proposition 14.40 (f) it has order
2s − 1. Hence ς C_(ǎ_ε) is the quantisation of the right side of (16.6) plus an operator of order 2s − 1. By
Proposition 14.40 (b), (c), Φ_0* Op(b_ε)* Op(b_ε) Φ_0 = Op(φ_0 b_ε* b_ε φ_0) = Op(b_ε* b_ε) modulo order 2s − 1,
likewise for the b′_(j,ε) with Φ_0 and for the e_(i,ε) with Φ_E; and Op(j_ε ℓ) = Op(j_ε) Φ_0 L modulo order 2s − 1, as
L = Op(ℓ_f) + R_L with ℓ_f − ℓ of order m − 1 and j_ε φ_0 ℓ_f = j_ε ℓ_f. All remainders are uniformly of order 2s − 1,
so paired with w they are at most C‖w‖²_(s−½). ⟨C_(ǎ_ε) w, w⟩ is real, so taking real parts and dropping
−Σ_j ‖Op(b′_(j,ε)) Φ_0 w‖² gives (16.5). ∎

**Lemma 16.7** (Norms through symbols.) Let q ∈ C^(M) S̃^0 be matrix-valued, of index 0, and M_q := sup|q|,
the supremum of the operator norm. For every η > 0 there is C_η, depending on q through finitely many norms, such that
for every w ∈ L²

    ‖Op(q) w‖ ≤ (M_q + η) ‖w‖ + C_η ‖w‖_(−½).    (16.7)

*Proof.* (M_q + η)² − q*q ≥ η², so its positive square root c lies in C^(M) S̃^0 (Lemma 14.41 (i), for positive
definite matrices). By Proposition 14.40 (b), (c), with constant orders and index 0, Op(c)* Op(c) + Op(q)* Op(q) =
Op(c*c + q*q) + R = (M_q + η)² I + R, with R of order −1, as Op(1) = I (Section 14.9.1). Hence
‖Op(q) w‖² ≤ (M_q + η)² ‖w‖² + |⟨Rw, w⟩| ≤ (M_q + η)² ‖w‖² + C_η‖w‖²_(−½), and (16.7) follows. This is
the argument of Lemma 14.42, at constant order and index 0. ∎

*The localised form.* (16.5) is used below also at distributions that are regular only microlocally. Let the
localisers and operators be as in Lemma 16.6, with κ ≥ 2, and let G′ ∈ C_b^∞Ψ^0_e3b be carried by χ and elliptic on
(supp φ_0 ∪ supp φ_E) ∩ ᵉ³ᵇS*M. If G′v ∈ H^(s−½), G′Lv ∈ H^(s−m+½) and χv ∈ H^(−N′), then for each ε > 0 the pairing
⟨C_(ǎ_ε) v, v⟩ := 2 Im⟨Ǎ_ε L v, Ǎ_ε v⟩ is defined, and (16.5) holds at w = v with C_0‖w‖²_(s−½) replaced by
C(‖G′v‖²_(s−½) + ‖χv‖²_(−N′)). Indeed, let Φ′ be an auxiliary operator with φ′ = 1 near (supp φ_0 ∪ supp φ_E) ∩ ᵉ³ᵇS*M
and WF′(Φ′) ⊂ Ell(G′), and put w := Φ′v. By Lemma 14.29 (c), ‖w‖_(s−½) ≤ C(‖G′v‖_(s−½) + ‖χv‖_(−N′)), and
‖Φ′Lv‖_(s−m+½) ≤ C(‖G′Lv‖_(s−m+½) + ‖χ_*Lv‖_(−N′−m)) with χ_* of (R2), where ‖χ_*Lv‖_(−N′−m) ≤ C‖χv‖_(−N′) by
Lemma 14.31 (a). For fixed ε every operator in (16.5) has its order lowered by κ, so (16.5) holds
at w by the approximation of Steps 1–2 of the proof of Lemma 14.44, with Lw = Φ′Lv + [L, Φ′]v and Ǎ_ε[L, Φ′]
treated as Ǎ_ε[L, Φ] in its Step 0. Each term at w differs from the same term at v by pairings ⟨Tv, v⟩ in which,
after the operators are moved to one side, T contains as a factor one of Φ_0(I − Φ′) and Φ_E(I − Φ′), which lie in
Ψ̃^(−∞) (Lemma 14.35), or Φ_0L(I − Φ′) and (I − Φ′)*Op(j_ε)Φ_0, which have every order by Proposition 14.40 (e),
their outer factors being microsupported in disjoint closed sets. So T has every order uniformly in ε, and as all
these operators are carried by χ, the differences are at most C‖χv‖²_(−N′).

**Lemma 16.8** (Comparison of norms.) Let 𝗍 be a constant and z, x_1, …, x_m ∈ C^(M) S̃^0 matrix-valued and
supported in a compact set K_1 near fibre infinity, and suppose that z = Σ_i q_i x_i on a neighbourhood of supp z, with
q_i ∈ C^(M) S̃^0 and M_i := sup|q_i|. This holds with M_i = c_*^(−1/2) if |z| ≤ 1 and Σ_i x_i* x_i ≥ c_* > 0 on a
neighbourhood V of supp z. Let Φ_z = Op(φ_z) and Φ_i = Op(φ_i) be smooth localisers with φ_z = 1 near supp z and
φ_i = 1 near supp x_i (any of them may be I). Then for every η > 0 there is C_η, independent of ε ∈ (0, 1] and depending
on the symbols and the localisers through finitely many norms, such that for every w ∈ H^(K′)_e3b

    ‖Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε z) Φ_z w‖ ≤ Σ_i (M_i + η) ‖Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε x_i) Φ_i w‖ + C_η ‖w‖_(𝗍−½).    (16.8)

If κ ≥ ½, (16.8) holds also for every w ∈ H^(𝗍−½): for fixed ε both sides are then finite and continuous in w
on H^(𝗍−½), and Lemma 14.39 (b) approximates w. It is applied at localised w = Φu, Φ smooth, for which
‖w‖_(𝗍−½) is bounded by microlocal norms of u (Lemma 14.29 (c)).

*Proof.* Replacing q_i by ζ q_i, with ζ equal to 1 near supp z and supported in the neighbourhood, z = Σ_i q_i x_i
everywhere, so z = zφ_z = Σ_i q_i x_i φ_i exactly. By Proposition 14.40 (b), (f), with constant orders and index 0,
Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε z) Φ_z − Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε z φ_z) and Op(q_i) Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε x_i) Φ_i − Op(q_i ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε x_i φ_i) are uniformly
of order 𝗍 − 1, and by the exact identities Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε z φ_z) and Σ_i Op(q_i ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε x_i φ_i) are both
Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε z). So Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε z) Φ_z = Σ_i Op(q_i) Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε x_i) Φ_i + R_ε with R_ε uniformly of order
𝗍 − 1. Lemma 16.7 applied to Op(q_i) and Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε x_i) Φ_i w gives (16.8), as
‖Op(ρ^(−𝗍) φ_ε x_i) Φ_i w‖_(−½) ≤ C‖w‖_(𝗍−½). In the particular case put X := Σ_j x_j* x_j and
q_i := ζ z X⁻¹ x_i* with ζ supported in V. Then Σ_i q_i x_i = ζz = z and Σ_i q_i q_i* = ζ² z X⁻¹ z* ≤ c_*⁻¹, so each
q_i has norm at most c_*^(−1/2). ∎

In Lemma 16.6 and in Lemma 14.44 and Lemma 14.45, L enters only through L = Op(ℓ_f) + R_L, with ℓ_f
∈ C^(d_0) S̃^m (matrix-valued, with real scalar principal part ℓ) and R_L bounded of every order, and through
χ_*L = χ_*Lχ and the boundedness of L from H^(−N) to H^(−N−m) (Lemma 14.31 (a)), with χ_* of (R2) of
Section 14.8.3. So they hold for operators of that form, such as L plus the quantisation of a first-order symbol of
finite regularity: its boundedness is Proposition 14.40 (a), and χ_*L = χ_*Lχ holds once the kernel range of the added
quantisation is counted in the bound D of Section 14.8.3. We use this in Section 16.4.

The iteration of Lemma 14.45 uses its hypotheses only at the orders 𝗌_j = 𝗌 − τ + jκ with the exponent κ = τ/J,
for which the effective orders 𝗌_j − κθ_ε of the regularised commutant lie in [𝗌 − τ, 𝗌]. So in Lemma 16.5 it
suffices that the hypotheses hold for orders 𝗌′ and exponents κ with 𝗌 − τ ≤ 𝗌′ − κ and 𝗌′ ≤ 𝗌. This is what makes
thresholds compatible with the regularisation.

### 16.3 Radial point estimates

Each estimate below is proved by the same steps; we write them once.

*The pattern.* (1) Near the radial set R, a local operator L′ := W′⁻¹P (Section 16.1.1) is conjugated to L″ :=
A⁻¹w⁻¹L′wA (Lemma 16.1), acting on ũ := A⁻¹w⁻¹u, with A the frame of a fibre inner product chosen for R. (2) The
commutant is ǎ := ρ^(−s+½) Ψ χ_∞, with s the (constant) order, ρ the function of Section 16.1.1 for R, Ψ a product of
cut-offs, and χ_∞ a function of ρ equal to 1 near fibre infinity and supported where the coordinates are defined, whose
derivatives are of order −∞ and are put into f_ε; it is regularised by φ_ε with the same ρ. (3) With s_ε := s − κθ_ε
∈ [s − κ, s], (14.13) and (16.1) give, where χ_∞ = 1,

    H_ℓ(ǎ_ε²) + 2ǎ_ε² ℓ_I = ρ^(−2s) φ_ε² (−Ψ² Q_ε + 𝖧(Ψ²)),
    Q_ε := (2s_ε − 1) ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ − 2A⁻¹ (𝔭′ − ½ 𝖧 log W′ − 𝖧 log w) A,    (16.9)

with ℓ = W′⁻¹G, 𝖧 = ρH_ℓ and 𝔭′ = ρW′⁻¹ σ_1(Im_h P). Indeed H_ℓ = ρ⁻¹𝖧, 𝖧(ρ^(−2s+1) φ_ε²) = −(2s_ε − 1) ρ^(−2s+1)
φ_ε² ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ, and 2ρℓ_I = 2A⁻¹(⋯)A by (16.1). (4) At R, Q_ε ≥ 2c for some c > 0 and all s_ε in the range of
the iteration, by the threshold; so Q_ε ≥ c on supp Ψ once the cut-offs are localised close to R, and −Ψ² Q_ε ρ^(−2s)
φ_ε² = −b_ε* b_ε with b_ε := ρ^(−s) φ_ε Ψ Q_ε^(1/2) (Lemma 14.41 (i)), and ǎ_ε = z_ε b_ε, z_ε := ρ^(1/2)
Q_ε^(−1/2) (with Q_ε replaced by c, smoothly, off a neighbourhood of supp Ψ). (5) 𝖧(Ψ²) is a sum of terms 2𝔐 ψψ′(𝔐f)
𝖧f · (other factors)², one for each factor ψ(𝔐f) of Ψ, where ψ is the cut-off of Section 14.13.2: even, supported in
(−1, 1), equal to 1 on [−½, ½], non-increasing on [0, ∞), with −ψψ′ the square of a smooth function on [0, ∞). Where
𝖧f > 0 on the support of ψ′(𝔐f) the term is −b′*b′; where 𝖧f < 0 it is +e*e, and its support determines E. A factor
ψ(𝔐_Σ ρ²ℓ), a cut-off to the characteristic set, contributes j_ε ℓ, since 𝖧(ρ²ℓ) = 2(ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ) ρ²ℓ, 𝖧ℓ being 0. (6)
Lemma 16.6 gives (16.5) for L″, with localisers chosen as auxiliary operators: φ_0 = 1 near supp Ψ and
φ_E = 1 near the supports of the e-terms, both supported, near fibre infinity, in the neighbourhood U of R in which the
iteration places supp Ψ, and supp φ_E in a closed set that misses R at fibre infinity and on which an E with the
property (4) of the proposition can be elliptic; each proof below names this set. Then Lemma 16.4 and
Lemma 16.5 give the estimate for ũ with Γ := R (in Proposition 16.14, the part of R named there) and
τ := s − s_0, the E of the conclusion being elliptic on the union of these sets, and Section 16.1.2 returns it to u.

The constants depend on P through finitely many norms of the coefficients of L″, and through c and the signs in (5).
These hold with margins at R, where the quantities are those of the normal form of P (the second-order part of P − P_0
vanishes at the face containing R), and near R they change by O(ε_P) (Lemma 15.41). So the cut-offs chosen for P_0
serve for every P with ε_P small, and the estimates hold uniformly, with d_0 fixed by the regularity that
Lemma 16.4–Lemma 16.6 and Proposition 14.40 need at the orders involved. We prove the estimates on ∂Σ⁺. On
∂Σ⁻ the future field is −𝖧, ς = −1, and the antipodal map exchanges the two components. G is even, and σ_1(Im_h P) is
odd in the covector, so ς𝔭′ and every threshold are the same there. Throughout, B, E, G ∈ C_b^∞Ψ^0_e3b are carried by
χ, and "strong sense" means: if the right side is finite, so is the left, and the estimate holds.

**Proposition 16.9** (The horizon.) There are B, E, G such that (1) their operator wave front sets lie in
any fixed neighbourhood U of ∂R_(ℋ⁺); (2) their Schwartz kernels are supported in K × K for any fixed compact
neighbourhood K ⊂ M of ℋ⁺ ∩ K⁺ = {r = r_h, ρ_K = 0}; (3) B is elliptic at ∂R_(ℋ⁺); (4) the Schwartz kernel of E is
supported in (K ∖ K⁺)²; and such that for all constants s > s_0 > ½ + ϑ_ℋ ((11.5)), α_K ∈ ℝ, and χ̃ ∈ C^∞(M)
supported near K and equal to 1 near K,

    ‖Bu‖_(H^(s,α_K)) ≤ C (‖GPu‖_(H^(s−1,α_K)) + ‖Eu‖_(H^(s,α_K)) + ‖χ̃u‖_(H^(s_0,α_K)))    (16.10)

in the strong sense, for P = P_0 and every P with ε_P small, with d_0 depending only on s, s_0. Here H^(s,α_K) :=
H^(s,(2α_I,α_+,α_K))_e3b over K, where x_I and ρ_+ are smooth and positive, so that α_I, α_+ do not matter.

This is [Hin26c, Proposition 7.4] in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* W′ := 1, ρ the function of (H3) (extended positive, even and homogeneous of degree −1), 𝖧 = ρH_G, w :=
ρ_K^(α_K) with ρ_K = t_*⁻¹, and A the frame of an inner product for which ϑ_ℋ of (11.5) is attained (ϑ_ℋ is
at least the supremum of max spec(β_0⁻¹ p_(1,+)(0)) over ∂ℛ_+, with p_(1,+)(0) = ρ σ_1(Im_h P̂(0))). ∂R_(ℋ⁺) lies
over K⁺ in {σ = 0}, where σ_1(Im_h P_0) = σ_1(Im_h P̂(0)) (Section 15.10.3), and P − P_0 has coefficients vanishing
at K⁺; so 𝔭′ = p_(1,+)(0) there. By (15.11), ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ = β_0 and ρ_K⁻¹𝖧ρ_K = ρ_K(ρ_K⁻²𝖧ρ_K) = 0 at
∂R_(ℋ⁺). So at ∂R_(ℋ⁺), as A⁻¹𝔭′A has the eigenvalues of the h-self-adjoint 𝔭′,

    Q_ε = (2s_ε − 1)β_0 − 2A⁻¹𝔭′A ≥ (2s_ε − 1 − 2ϑ_ℋ)β_0 ≥ (2s_0 − 1 − 2ϑ_ℋ) inf β_0 =: 2c > 0

for s_ε ≥ s_0, which is the range of the iteration (Lemma 16.5 and the remark after Lemma 16.8).

Let F be the quadratic defining function of Lemma 15.11, with 𝖧F ≥ c_F F on a neighbourhood W of ∂R_(ℋ⁺) in
³ᵇS*_((K⁺)°) M_0. F does not depend on t_*, and the field of P_0 is invariant under t_*-translations, so 𝖧_(P_0)F ≥
c_F F on W × {ρ_K ≤ ρ_0}. For P, 𝖧 − 𝖧_(P_0) = O(ε_P ρ_K^(ℓ_K)) in C^(d_0−1), and |dF| ≤ CF^(1/2), so 𝖧F ≥ ½c_F F where
F ≥ (2𝔐_R)⁻¹ and ρ_K ≤ 𝔐⁻¹, for 𝔐 large given 𝔐_R. As F is defined only on W, extend it to a smooth t_*-independent
function bounded below by a positive constant outside a smaller t_*-invariant neighbourhood W′ of ∂R_(ℋ⁺) with closure
in W; for 𝔐_R large, ψ(𝔐_R F) is then a symbol supported in W′. Put Ψ := ψ(𝔐_R F) ψ(𝔐ρ_K). Then

    𝖧(Ψ²) = 2𝔐_R (ψψ′)(𝔐_R F) 𝖧F ψ(𝔐ρ_K)² + 2𝔐 (ψψ′)(𝔐ρ_K) 𝖧ρ_K ψ(𝔐_R F)².

The first term is ≤ 0 and is −b′*b′ with b′ := ρ^(−s) φ_ε θ(𝔐_R F) (2𝔐_R 𝖧F)^(1/2) ψ(𝔐ρ_K), θ := (−ψψ′)^(1/2), smooth
as 𝖧F ≥ c_F/(4𝔐_R) on the support of θ(𝔐_R F). In the second, 𝖧ρ_K = ρ_K²(ρ_K⁻²𝖧ρ_K) ≤ −½ββ_0ρ_K² < 0 near
∂R_(ℋ⁺) ((15.11)), so it is +e*e with e := ρ^(−s) φ_ε θ(𝔐ρ_K) (−2𝔐𝖧ρ_K)^(1/2) ψ(𝔐_R F), supported in {ρ_K ≥
(2𝔐)⁻¹}, away from K⁺. Choosing 𝔐_R and then 𝔐 large, supp Ψ lies in U, in W and in {Q_ε ≥ c}. The localiser φ_E of
the pattern (6) is taken supported, near fibre infinity, in U ∩ {ρ_K ≥ (4𝔐)⁻¹}. So the set of (6), the union of the
support of e and of supp φ_E, misses ∂R_(ℋ⁺) ⊂ {ρ_K = 0}, and its base projection is a compact subset of K ∖ K⁺ when U
is small; E can be chosen elliptic on it with Schwartz kernel in (K ∖ K⁺)², as (4) requires. No cut-off to the
characteristic set is needed, as the signs hold on a full neighbourhood of ∂R_(ℋ⁺) (Lemma 15.11); so
(16.6) holds with j_ε = 0. The pattern (6) gives (16.10), with ‖χũ‖_(−N′) ≤ C‖χ̃u‖_(H^(s_0,α_K)). ∎

**Proposition 16.10** (The incoming radial set over ∂K⁺.) There are B, E, G with (1) operator wave front
sets in any fixed neighbourhood of ∂R_(∂K⁺,in); (2) Schwartz kernels in K × K for any fixed compact neighbourhood K of
∂K⁺; (3) B elliptic at ∂R_(∂K⁺,in); (4) the Schwartz kernel of E supported in (K ∖ K⁺)²; such that for all constants
s > s_0, α_+, α_K with

    s_0 + α_+ > ½(−1 + ϑ^3b_in) + α_K    (16.11)

((15.23)), and χ̃ as before,

    ‖Bu‖_(H^(s,(α_+,α_K))) ≤ C (‖GPu‖_(H^(s−1,(α_++2,α_K))) + ‖Eu‖_(H^(s,(α_+,α_K)))
                               + ‖χ̃u‖_(H^(s_0,(α_+,α_K))))    (16.12)

in the strong sense, for P = P_0 and every P with ε_P small, d_0 depending only on s, s_0. Near ∂K⁺, x_I is smooth and
positive, so the weights are (α_+, α_K).

This is [Hin26c, Proposition 7.6] in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* W′ := ρ_+², with ρ_+ = r⁻¹ and ρ_K = r/t_*; ℓ = ρ_+⁻²G = G_3b ((15.6)); ρ := −σ_3b⁻¹, ξ̂, η̂ as in
(15.7), so 𝖧 is the field of (15.8); w := ρ_+^(α_+) ρ_K^(α_K); A the frame of an inner product
attaining ϑ^3b_in. Then 𝔭′ = ρ σ^1_3b(r² Im_h P), which at R := ∂R_(∂K⁺,in) is that of P_0, the coefficients of P − P_0
vanishing at ∂K⁺ (and the terms with χ_I in (15.26) vanishing near ∂K⁺). At R, 𝖧 = 0 and, by (15.8)
and its linearisation, ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ = 2, ρ_+⁻¹𝖧ρ_+ = 2, ρ_K⁻¹𝖧ρ_K = −2. So, at R,

    Q_ε = 2(2s_ε − 1) − 2A⁻¹𝔭′A + 2·2 + 2(2α_+ − 2α_K) ≥ 4(s_ε + α_+ − α_K − ½(−1 + ϑ^3b_in)),

which is at least 2c > 0 for s_ε ≥ s_0, by (16.11).

Put q := |η̂|² + (ξ̂ − 2)² and Ψ := ψ(𝔐_R q) ψ(𝔐ρ_+) ψ(𝔐ρ_K). Over ι⁺, where 𝖧 = 𝖧̄, (15.8) gives 𝖧̄ξ̂ =
−2(2 − ξ̂)ξ̂ and 𝖧̄|η̂|² = −4(1 − ξ̂)|η̂|² (the terms with ∂_ω|η̂|² and 𝖧̄ω cancel, the Hamilton field of |η̂|² on T*𝕊³
preserving it). Hence ([Hin26c, p. 120])

    𝖧̄q = 4(ξ̂ − 1)|η̂|² + 4ξ̂(ξ̂ − 2)² ≥ 2q     for |ξ̂ − 2| ≤ ½,

on the full phase space over ι⁺, not only on the characteristic set. 𝖧 − 𝖧̄ ∈ ρ_+² 𝒱_b plus O(ε_P ρ_+^(ℓ_+)
ρ_K^(ℓ_K)) (Section 15.3.1, Lemma 15.41), so 𝖧q ≥ (2𝔐_R)⁻¹ on supp ψ′(𝔐_R q) ∩ supp ψ(𝔐ρ_+)ψ(𝔐ρ_K) for 𝔐
large given 𝔐_R. Near R, ρ_+⁻¹𝖧ρ_+ ≥ 1 and ρ_K⁻¹𝖧ρ_K ≤ −1. So in (5) of the pattern, the factors ψ(𝔐_R q) and
ψ(𝔐ρ_+) give −b′*b′ terms, and ψ(𝔐ρ_K) gives +e*e, supported in {ρ_K ≥ (2𝔐)⁻¹}, away from K⁺; j_ε = 0. The
localiser φ_E of the pattern (6) is taken supported, near fibre infinity, in U ∩ {ρ_K ≥ (4𝔐)⁻¹}. So the set of (6)
misses R ⊂ {ρ_K = 0}, its base projection is a compact subset of K ∖ K⁺ when U is small, and E can be chosen elliptic
on it with Schwartz kernel in (K ∖ K⁺)², as (4) requires. The pattern gives (16.12). ∎

**Proposition 16.11** (The outgoing radial set over ∂K⁺.) There are B, E, G with (1)–(3) as in
Proposition 16.10 with ∂R_(∂K⁺,out) in place of ∂R_(∂K⁺,in), and (4) the operator wave front set of E disjoint from
∂W_out = {ρ_+ = 0, ξ̂ = 0, η̂ = 0}, the unstable manifold of ∂R_(∂K⁺,out) over ι⁺ (Lemma 15.9 (4)); such that for
all constants s > s_0, α_+, α_K with

    s + α_+ < ½(−1 + ϑ_out) + α_K    (16.13)

((15.23)), (16.12) holds in the strong sense, for P = P_0 and every P with ε_P small.

This is [Hin26c, Proposition 7.7] in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* As for Proposition 16.10, with A the frame of the inner product of Lemma 15.30, for which −A⁻¹𝔭′A ≥
ϑ_out at R := ∂R_(∂K⁺,out) (Lemma 15.31: there −𝔭′ = S + S^(*h)). At R, ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ = −2, ρ_+⁻¹𝖧ρ_+ = −2,
ρ_K⁻¹𝖧ρ_K = 2 ((15.8) at ξ̂ = 0). So at R

    Q_ε = −2(2s_ε − 1) − 2A⁻¹𝔭′A − 4 + 2(−2α_+ + 2α_K) ≥ 4(½(−1 + ϑ_out) + α_K − α_+ − s_ε),

at least 2c > 0 for s_ε ≤ s, by (16.13): the threshold is an upper bound, met by every order of the iteration.
Put q := |η̂|² + ξ̂²; by (15.8), over ι⁺,

    𝖧̄q = −4(1 − ξ̂)|η̂|² − 4(2 − ξ̂)ξ̂² ≤ −2q     for |ξ̂| ≤ ½,

which is [Hin26c, (7.18)]. With Ψ := ψ(𝔐_R q) ψ(𝔐ρ_+) ψ(𝔐ρ_K), now ψ(𝔐ρ_K) gives a −b′*b′ term (ρ_K⁻¹𝖧ρ_K ≥ 1 near
R), while ψ(𝔐_R q) and ψ(𝔐ρ_+) give +e*e terms (𝖧q < 0 on supp ψ′(𝔐_R q), ρ_+⁻¹𝖧ρ_+ ≤ −1). These are supported in
{q ≥ (2𝔐_R)⁻¹}, disjoint from {ξ̂ = η̂ = 0} ⊃ ∂W_out, and in {ρ_+ ≥ (2𝔐)⁻¹}, away from ι⁺ ⊃ ∂W_out. The localiser φ_E
of the pattern (6) is taken supported, near fibre infinity, in U ∩ ({q ≥ (4𝔐_R)⁻¹} ∪ {ρ_+ ≥ (4𝔐)⁻¹}). On ∂W_out ⊃ R,
q = 0 and ρ_+ = 0, so the set of (6) misses ∂W_out and, being compact, has a neighbourhood that misses the closed set
∂W_out. So E can be chosen elliptic on it with WF′(E) inside that neighbourhood, hence WF′(E) ∩ ∂W_out = ∅, as (4)
requires, and the set meets fibre infinity in U ∖ R, as
Lemma 16.5 requires. ∎

**Lemma 16.12** (The subprincipal symbol at ℐ⁺.) Near ℐ⁺ ∩ Ω, with ρ_+ = t_*⁻¹, x_I = (t_*/r)^(1/2), ω, the
eb-momenta of Section 15.7 and ρ := σ_eb⁻¹, ξ̂ := ξ_eb/σ_eb, 𝖧 := ρH_(G_eb), let h be a smooth fibre inner product
with Gram matrix 𝖦, and 𝔭 := ρ x_I⁻² ρ_+⁻² σ_1(Im_h P). Then over ℐ⁺

    𝔭 = (Re_h p_1)(ξ̂ − 2) + ½ 𝖦⁻¹ 𝖧 𝖦,       Re_h p_1 := ½(p_1 + p_1^(*h)),    (16.14)

with p_1 = S|_(∂X) + p̃_1 of Definition 15.36. In particular 𝔭 = 0 at ∂R_(ℐ⁺,in,+) and 𝔭 = −2 Re_h p_1 at
∂R_(ℐ⁺,out), where 𝖧 = 0.

This is [Hin26c, (7.22)] in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* *The density.* With t_* = ρ_+⁻¹ and r = ρ_+⁻¹ x_I⁻², |dt dx| = r³|dt_* dr dω| = 2ρ_+⁻⁵ x_I⁻⁸ |(dρ_+/ρ_+)
(dx_I/x_I) dω|, dω the round density of 𝕊³ (as |dt_* ∧ dr| = 2ρ_+⁻³ x_I⁻³ |dρ_+ ∧ dx_I|; Lemma 14.19). For it,
(x_I ∂_(x_I))* = −x_I ∂_(x_I) + 8, (ρ_+ ∂_(ρ_+))* = −ρ_+ ∂_(ρ_+) + 5, Δ_𝕊³ is symmetric, and so are multiplications by
real functions.

*The operator.* Put X_1 := x_I ∂_(x_I) − 2ρ_+ ∂_(ρ_+), X_2 := x_I ∂_(x_I), W := x_I² ρ_+². By Lemma 15.37, P =
P_s + W p_1 X_1 + ½W(p_0 + R) with P_s := ½W(−(X_2 − 3)X_1 + 2x_I² Δ_𝕊³) ⊗ Id and R ∈ C^((d_0;0),(2ℓ_I,0))_(eb;b)
Diff²_eb.

(i) P_s is symmetric for the standard inner product. X_1* = −X_1 − 2 and (X_2 − 3)* = −(X_2 − 5), so (W(X_2 − 3)X_1)* =
(X_1 + 2)(X_2 − 5)W. As X_2 W = W(X_2 + 2) and X_1 W = W(X_1 − 2), this is W X_1 (X_2 − 3) = W(X_2 − 3)X_1, X_1 and
X_2 commuting. And (W x_I² Δ)* = Δ x_I² W = W x_I² Δ. With h, P_s^(*h) = 𝖦⁻¹P_s𝖦 = P_s + 𝖦⁻¹[P_s, 𝖦], so
σ_1(Im_h P_s) = ½ 𝖦⁻¹ H_(σ_2(P_s)) 𝖦. Here σ_2(P_s) = W(G_eb + O(x_I^(2ℓ_I))), and H_(W G_eb) 𝖦 = W H_(G_eb) 𝖦 as 𝖦
and W are functions of the base.

(ii) (W p_1 X_1)^(*h) = 𝖦⁻¹ X_1* p_1* W 𝖦, and σ(X_1) = i(ξ_eb − 2σ_eb), so σ_1(Im_h(W p_1 X_1)) = W (Re_h p_1)
(ξ_eb − 2σ_eb), as 𝖦⁻¹ p_1* 𝖦 = p_1^(*h).

(iii) p_0 is of order 0. R has real scalar principal symbol and coefficients in x_I^(2ℓ_I) C^((d_0;0))_(eb;b), a class
preserved by eb-derivatives, so σ_1(Im_h R) is O(x_I^(2ℓ_I)).

Multiplying by ρW⁻¹ and setting x_I = 0 gives (16.14). ∎

In dimension 3 + 1 the density is r²|dt_* dr dω₂| = 2ρ_+⁻⁴ x_I⁻⁶ |⋯|, dω₂ the round density of 𝕊², for which ½ x_I²
ρ_+² (x_I ∂_(x_I) − 2)(x_I ∂_(x_I) − 2ρ_+ ∂_(ρ_+)) is symmetric. In dimension 4 + 1 the density r³ and the constant 3
of Lemma 15.37 match in the same way, so (16.14) has the same form as [Hin26c, (7.22)]. With a varying
inner product, the term ½𝖦⁻¹𝖧𝖦 appears, and it vanishes at the radial sets.

**Proposition 16.13** (The incoming radial set at ℐ⁺ ∩ ι⁺.) There are B, E, G with (1) operator wave front
sets in any fixed neighbourhood of ∂R_(ℐ⁺,in,+); (2) Schwartz kernels in K × K for any fixed compact neighbourhood K of
ℐ⁺ ∩ ι⁺; (3) B elliptic at ∂R_(ℐ⁺,in,+); (4) the Schwartz kernel of E supported in (K ∖ ι⁺)²; such that for all
constants s > s_0 and α_I, α_+ with

    α_+ < α_I − ½,    (16.15)

and χ̃ as before,

    ‖Bu‖_(H^(s,(2α_I,α_+))) ≤ C (‖GPu‖_(H^(s−1,(2α_I+2,α_++2))) + ‖Eu‖_(H^(s,(2α_I,α_+)))
                                + ‖χ̃u‖_(H^(s_0,(2α_I,α_+))))    (16.16)

in the strong sense, for P = P_0 and every P with ε_P small. Near ℐ⁺ ∩ ι⁺, ρ_K is smooth and positive, so the weights
are (2α_I, α_+).

This is [Hin26c, Proposition 7.8] in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* W′ := W = x_I² ρ_+², ℓ = G_eb, ρ := σ_eb⁻¹, 𝖧 the field of (15.15)–(15.16), w := x_I^(2α_I)
ρ_+^(α_+), A := Id. At R := ∂R_(ℐ⁺,in,+) = {ρ_+ = x_I = 0, ξ̂ = 2, η̂ = 0}, 𝖧 = 0, and by (15.16), ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ = 0,
x_I⁻¹𝖧x_I = ξ̂ − 1 = 1, ρ_+⁻¹𝖧ρ_+ = −ξ̂ = −2; and 𝔭′ = 0 by Lemma 16.12. So at R, independently of s_ε,

    Q_ε = 0 + 𝖧 log W + 2𝖧 log w = 2·1 + 2·(−2) + 2(2α_I·1 + α_+·(−2)) = 4(α_I − α_+ − ½) ≥ 2c > 0

by (16.15). Near R, ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ = O(x_I²) + O(ε_P x_I^(2ℓ_I)), as 𝖧^0 ρ = 0 exactly for the field 𝖧^0 of
(15.16); so the term (2s_ε − 1)ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ is small on supp Ψ, uniformly for s_ε in the range of the iteration, and
Q_ε ≥ c there.

Put q := (ξ̂ − 2)² + |η̂|² and Ψ := ψ(𝔐_Σ ρ²ℓ) ψ(𝔐_R q) ψ(𝔐x_I) ψ(𝔐ρ_+). Over ℐ⁺, 𝖧 = 𝖧^0, with 𝖧^0 ξ̂ = −2|η̂|² and
𝖧^0|η̂|² = 2(ξ̂ − 1)|η̂|² (the angular motion stops at x_I = 0). On the characteristic set over ℐ⁺, |η̂|² = ½ξ̂(2 −
ξ̂) (Lemma 15.16 (1)), so

    𝖧^0 q = −4(ξ̂ − 2)|η̂|² + 2(ξ̂ − 1)|η̂|² = 2ξ̂(2 − ξ̂)² + 2(ξ̂ − 1)|η̂|² ≥ q     for |ξ̂ − 2| ≤ ½,

which is [Hin26c, (7.21)]. Off the characteristic set, |η̂|² = ½ξ̂(2 − ξ̂) + ρ² G^0_eb, and ρ²(ℓ − G^0_eb) = O(x_I²) +
O(ε_P x_I^(2ℓ_I)); so 𝖧q ≥ (4𝔐_R)⁻¹ on supp ψ′(𝔐_R q) within the support of the other factors, for 𝔐_Σ, 𝔐 large
given 𝔐_R. Near R, x_I⁻¹𝖧x_I ≥ ½ and ρ_+⁻¹𝖧ρ_+ ≤ −1, on the full phase space. So in (5) of the pattern: ψ(𝔐_R q) and
ψ(𝔐x_I) give −b′*b′; ψ(𝔐ρ_+) gives +e*e, supported in {ρ_+ ≥ (2𝔐)⁻¹}, away from ι⁺; ψ(𝔐_Σ ρ²ℓ) gives j_ε ℓ,
with j_ε of order 2s − 2. The localiser φ_E of the pattern (6) is taken supported, near fibre infinity, in
U ∩ {ρ_+ ≥ (4𝔐)⁻¹}. So the set of (6) misses R ⊂ ι⁺, its base projection is a compact subset of K ∖ ι⁺ when U is
small, and E can be chosen elliptic on it with Schwartz kernel in (K ∖ ι⁺)², as (4) requires. The pattern gives
(16.16). ∎

**Proposition 16.14** (The outgoing radial set over ℐ⁺.) Let t_(*,−) ∈ ℝ. There are B, E, G with (1)
operator wave front sets in any fixed neighbourhood of ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out) ∩ {t_*^♭ ≥ t_(*,−) − ½}; (2) Schwartz kernels in
K × K for any fixed compact neighbourhood K ⊂ M̃ of cl(ℐ⁺ ∩ {t_* ≥ t_(*,−) − ½}); (3) B elliptic at ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out) ∩
{t_*^♭ ≥ t_(*,−)}; (4) WF′(E) ∩ ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out) ⊂ {t_*^♭ ≤ t_(*,−) − ¼}; such that for all constants s > s_0 and α_I,
α_+ with

    α_I < −½ + p̄_1    (16.17)

(p̄_1 of Definition 15.38, for P), (16.16) holds in the strong sense, for P = P_0 and every P with ε_P small.

This is [Hin26c, Proposition 7.9] in dimension 4 + 1, with t_(*,+) = ∞ and with property (4) in the form stated (see
Section 16.13).

*Proof.* W′, ℓ, ρ, 𝖧, w as in Proposition 16.13. Let δ′ := ¼(p̄_1 − ½ − α_I) > 0, and let h_I be a smooth fibre inner
product near cl(ℐ⁺ ∩ Ω) with Re_(h_I) p_1 ≥ p̄_1 − δ′ there. It is constructed as in Lemma 15.30: p_1 is continuous
on the compact closure of ℐ⁺ ∩ Ω (with p̃_1 ∈ ρ_+^(ℓ_+) C_b tending to 0 at ι⁺), so Jordan scalings at points,
continuity and a smooth partition of unity apply verbatim; h_I is extended independently of x_I. A is its frame. At R
:= ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out) = {x_I = 0, ξ̂ = 0, η̂ = 0}, over all of ℐ⁺, 𝖧 = 0; ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ = 0, x_I⁻¹𝖧x_I = −1, ρ_+⁻¹𝖧ρ_+ = −ξ̂ = 0
((15.16)); and 𝔭′ = −2 Re_(h_I) p_1 (Lemma 16.12). So at R

    Q_ε = 4A⁻¹(Re_(h_I) p_1)A − 2 + 2·2α_I·(−1) ≥ 4(p̄_1 − δ′ − ½ − α_I) = 12δ′ =: 2c > 0,

by (16.17), independently of s_ε; near R, ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ is small as before.

Put q := ξ̂² + |η̂|² and fix η_t ∈ C^∞(ℝ) with η_t = 0 on (−∞, −½], η_t = 1 on [−¼, ∞), η_t′ ≥ 0 and
(η_t η_t′)^(1/2) smooth. The pattern (6) is applied with Γ the closure of R ∩ {t_*^♭ ≥ t_(*,−) − ⅜} in the compactified
bundle, which is compact, and with U_0 inside the neighbourhood of (1). Given an open U with Γ ⊂ U ⊂ U_0, take
λ ∈ (0, ⅛] and ψ_− := η_t((t_*^♭ − t_(*,−) + ⅜)/λ), which equals 1 for t_*^♭ ≥ t_(*,−) − ⅜ − λ/4, and put
Ψ := ψ(𝔐_Σ ρ²ℓ) ψ(𝔐_R q) ψ(𝔐x_I) ψ_−, with λ small and 𝔐_Σ, 𝔐_R, 𝔐 large, so that supp Ψ lies in U near fibre
infinity. On the characteristic set over ℐ⁺, with |η̂|² = ½ξ̂(2 − ξ̂),

    𝖧^0 q = −4ξ̂|η̂|² + 2(ξ̂ − 1)|η̂|² = −2(2 − ξ̂)ξ̂² − 2(1 − ξ̂)|η̂|² ≤ −q     for |ξ̂| ≤ ½,

and off it, as in Proposition 16.13, 𝖧q ≤ −(4𝔐_R)⁻¹ on supp ψ′(𝔐_R q) within the support of the other factors. Near
R, x_I⁻¹𝖧x_I ≤ −½. So ψ(𝔐_R q) and ψ(𝔐x_I) give +e*e terms, supported in {q ≥ (2𝔐_R)⁻¹} and {x_I ≥ (2𝔐)⁻¹}, both
disjoint from R; ψ(𝔐_Σ ρ²ℓ) gives j_ε ℓ. The factor ψ_− gives 2λ⁻¹ η_t η_t′ 𝖧t_*^♭ · (other factors)², with η_t, η_t′
evaluated at (t_*^♭ − t_(*,−) + ⅜)/λ. Whatever its sign, with C_t := 1 + sup|𝖧t_*^♭| over the support, it is
e_−*e_− − b′_−*b′_− with e_−² := 2λ⁻¹ C_t η_t η_t′ (⋯)² and b′_−² := 2λ⁻¹ (C_t − 𝖧t_*^♭) η_t η_t′ (⋯)², both smooth
squares, supported in {t_*^♭ ∈ [t_(*,−) − ⅜ − λ/2, t_(*,−) − ⅜ − λ/4]}. The localiser φ_E of the pattern (6) is taken
supported, near fibre infinity, in U ∩ ({q ≥ (4𝔐_R)⁻¹} ∪ {x_I ≥ (4𝔐)⁻¹} ∪ {t_*^♭ ∈ [t_(*,−) − ⅜ − 3λ/4,
t_(*,−) − ⅜ − λ/8]}). On R, q = x_I = 0, so the set of (6) meets R only where t_*^♭ ≤ t_(*,−) − ⅜ − λ/8; it misses Γ,
as Lemma 16.5 requires, and its part off the last set has a neighbourhood that misses R. So E, elliptic on the
union of these sets over the finitely many U of the iteration, can be chosen with WF′(E) ∩ R ⊂ {t_*^♭ ≤ t_(*,−) − ¼},
which is (4); B is elliptic at Γ ⊃ R ∩ {t_*^♭ ≥ t_(*,−)}, which is (3). On the characteristic set over Ω°,
𝖧t_*^♭ > 0 (Lemma 15.35 (2)), and e_− is the a priori term at earlier times; off it the sign of 𝖧t_*^♭ is not
used. The pattern gives (16.16). Here supp Ψ is not compact in t_*^♭, but it is compact in M̃, its closure
meeting ℐ⁺ ∩ ι⁺, where (15.16) holds uniformly. ∎

In both uses below, t_(*,−) ≤ ½. The kernel of E near its e_−-set can then be supported in {t_*^♭ < 1}², where the u of
Theorem 16.2 vanishes, so that this part of ‖Eu‖ is zero. [Hin26c, Proposition 7.9] states the estimate for t_* ∈
[t_(*,−), t_(*,+)] with t_(*,+) ≤ ∞. For finite t_(*,+) its proof uses H_G t_* ≥ 0 on the support of the commutant,
which fails off the characteristic set near R: at x_I = 0, 𝖧t_*^♭ = t_* ξ̂, and ξ̂ < 0 occurs there. The case t_(*,+) <
∞ serves in [Hin26c] only for control near R at finite times, in Step 1 of its proof of Proposition 7.1, which
Section 16.5 does without.

**Remark 16.15** (First-order perturbations.) Proposition 16.9–Proposition 16.14 hold for P + P̃, with P̃ a
first-order operator of the form Op(p̃), p̃ ∈ C^(d_0) S̃^1 (or a finite combination of C^(d_0)_e3b coefficients and
smooth first-order operators). The thresholds are then calculated with σ_1(Im_h(P + P̃)) at R, where this symbol is
continuous. The proofs use P̃ only through ℓ_I in Q_ε, and Lemma 16.4–Lemma 16.6 hold for such operators
(the remark after Lemma 16.8). The constants are locally uniform in p̃. This is [Hin26c, Remark 7.5]; it is used
in Section 16.7.

### 16.4 The estimate at the trapped set

*Setting.* Near the trapped set W′ = 1 (Section 16.1.1). Over D = {t_* > T_♭, r_(Γ,−) < r < r_(Γ,+)} of
Section 15.16.2 (T_♭ = 2/C′ there) the e3b-structure is spanned by ∂_(t_*) and ∂_x, and ᵉ³ᵇT*_D M = T*D with
covectors −σ dt_* + ζ. There ρ_K = t_*⁻¹, while x_I and ρ_+ are smooth and positive, so only the weight α_K enters, and
we write H^(𝗍,α_K) := H^(𝗍,(2α_I,α_+,α_K))_e3b. We work on ∂Σ⁺, near the trapped set Γ = Γ_1 ⊂ Σ^♭_1 of (H7) at z_0 =
1, where σ > 0. The slice coordinates (t_*, x, z), z = ζ/σ, of Section 15.16.2 identify ᵉ³ᵇS*_D M ∩ {σ > 0} with (T_♭,
∞) × T*{r_(Γ,−) < r < r_(Γ,+)}, and ∂Γ_0 := {t_* > T_♭} × Γ. Put ρ := σ⁻¹ there, extended to a positive symbol of
degree −1 near fibre infinity (Section 16.2). Then 𝖧 := ρH_G is the field Ŵ of (15.41) with p = G, and ρ²G =
G(t_*, x; −dt_* + z). Three facts are used throughout.

(T1) 𝖧t_* ≥ ½β_Γ on a neighbourhood of ∂Γ_0 in the full phase space, for ε_P small (the paragraph after
Lemma 15.54), with β_Γ = ½ min_Γ |q_(z_0)| the constant of (Γ.4), not the horizon constant β_0. So 𝖧ρ_K = −ρ_K²
𝖧t_* < 0 there.

(T2) ρ⁻¹𝖧ρ = H_G(σ⁻¹) = −σ⁻² ∂_(t_*)G, as H_G σ = ∂_(t_*)G, σ being minus the momentum of t_*. It vanishes for P_0,
and for P it is O(ε_P ρ_K^(ℓ_K)) near ∂Γ_0, by the bounds on g⁻¹ − g_0⁻¹ before (15.40).

(T3) Let h_Γ be a fibre inner product as in Definition 15.26 for z_0 = 1 (it exists by Lemma 15.27 (a)), extended
to be stationary and homogeneous of degree 0, and 𝔭′ := ρ σ_1(Im_(h_Γ) P). At ∂Γ_(K⁺), 𝔭′ = p_1(1), by
Lemma 15.27 (b), the coefficients of P − P_0 vanishing at K⁺. So ϑ_Γ := sup over ∂Γ_(K⁺) of max spec 𝔭′ satisfies
ϑ_Γ < ½ν_min.

**Lemma 16.16** (The hypersurfaces as defining functions.) Let d_0 ≥ 5, let ϕ^u, ϕ^s be the functions of
Proposition 15.55 for the metric g of P, on the neighbourhood U of ∂Γ_0 there, let O be as in (H7) and O′ ⋐ O an open
neighbourhood of Γ. For δ > 0 let

    U(δ) := {ρ_K ≤ δ, |ϕ^u| ≤ δ, |ϕ^s| ≤ δ, |ρ²G| ≤ δ, (x, z) ∈ Ō′},

a subset of fibre infinity over {σ > 0}, closed in the compactified bundle, which includes ρ_K = 0. There is δ_U ∈ (0,
½C′), with C′ of Lemma 15.35, such that the following hold (ρ_K ≤ δ < ½C′ places U(δ) over {t_* > T_♭}, where
ϕ^(u/s) are defined, Proposition 15.55).

(a) For δ ≤ δ_U, U(δ) is a compact neighbourhood of ∂Γ_(K⁺), contained in {(x, z) ∈ O″} for an open O″ ⋐ O′
independent of δ, and ⋂_(δ>0) U(δ) = ∂Γ_(K⁺). Moreover Γ^u_(K⁺) ∩ U(δ_U) = U(δ_U) ∩ {ρ_K = 0, ϕ^u = 0, ρ²G = 0}.

(b) On a neighbourhood of U(δ_U) there are real functions w_u, r_u ∈ C^(d_0−3) and w_s, r_s ∈ C^(d_0−4), homogeneous of
degree 0, with bounded derivatives along ∂_(t_*), ∂_x and the fibres up to these orders, and continuous up to ρ_K = 0,
such that

    𝖧ϕ^u = −w_u ϕ^u + r_u ρ²G,       𝖧ϕ^s = w_s ϕ^s + r_s ρ²G.    (16.18)

(c) w_u = ν_u and w_s = ν_s on ∂Γ_(K⁺), so w_(u/s) ≥ ν_min there.

(d) c_us := ρ⁻¹{ϕ^u, ϕ^s} is continuous up to ρ_K = 0, and on ∂Γ_(K⁺) it equals {ϕ_u, ϕ_s} > 0, the bracket of T*X̃°
in condition (Γ.3) of (H7).

*Proof.* At ρ_K = 0 every function involved is that of the stationary model: ϕ̃^(u/s) → 0 with their derivatives
(Proposition 15.55); ρ²G − G_1 = g̃ = O(ε_P ρ_K^(ℓ_K)) with d_0 derivatives ((15.40)); and ϕ_0^(u/s) =
ϕ_(u/s) ∘ π_Y is independent of t_* and equal to ϕ_(u/s) on Y = {G_1 = 0} ∩ O_0, π_Y being the projection along the
transversal field N_Y of Section 15.16.3.

(a) On {G_1 = 0} ∩ O, ϕ_0^(u/s) = ϕ_(u/s), and Γ_u ∩ Γ_s = Γ by (Γ.1); so {ϕ_0^u = ϕ_0^s = G_1 = 0} ∩ Ō′ = Γ. By
compactness of Ō′ there are O″ ⋐ O′ and δ′ > 0 with {|ϕ_0^u|, |ϕ_0^s|, |G_1| ≤ 2δ′} ∩ Ō′ ⊂ O″, and these sets shrink to
Γ as δ′ → 0. For ρ_K ≤ δ the functions defining U(δ) differ from these by O(δ^(ℓ_K)). So for δ ≤ δ_U small, U(δ) ⊂
{(x, z) ∈ O″} and ⋂_δ U(δ) = {ρ_K = 0} × Γ = ∂Γ_(K⁺). U(δ) contains the set where the four inequalities are strict,
which is open and contains ∂Γ_(K⁺). The last assertion is Proposition 15.55 with Remark 15.56
(b), as ∂Σ⁺ = {ρ²G = 0} near ∂Γ_0.

(b) dϕ_u, dϕ_s and dG_1 are linearly independent at Γ (the proof of Lemma 15.52 (i)). On Y, d(ϕ_(u/s) ∘ π_Y) =
dϕ_(u/s) − (N_Y ϕ_(u/s)) dG_1, as d(ϕ ∘ π_Y) vanishes on N_Y and equals dϕ on TY = ker dG_1. So dϕ_0^u, dϕ_0^s, dG_1
are independent at Γ, hence near it, and together with dt_* near ∂Γ_0 for the stationary model. For ρ_K ≤ δ_U the
perturbations are O(δ_U^(ℓ_K)) in C¹, so the independence persists, with uniform bounds. Near each point of U(δ_U) we
can therefore complete y_1 := ϕ^u, y_2 := ρ²G by t_* and smooth t_*-independent functions y″ to coordinates of class
C^(d_0−1), with bounds uniform in t_*. f := 𝖧ϕ^u lies in C^(d_0−2), as 𝖧 has coefficients in C^(d_0−1), and f = 0 on
{y_1 = y_2 = 0}, as 𝖧 is tangent to Γ^u = ∂Σ⁺ ∩ U ∩ {ϕ^u = 0} (Proposition 15.55). Taylor's formula

    f(y) = Σ_(i=1,2) y_i ∫_0^1 (∂_(y_i) f)(τy_1, τy_2, y″) dτ,

in coordinate boxes convex in (y_1, y_2), gives f = −w_u y_1 + r_u y_2 locally with w_u, r_u ∈ C^(d_0−3), and a
partition of unity in (x, z), independent of t_*, patches them. The integral formula preserves the bounds along
∂_(t_*), ∂_x and the fibres, and the convergence as ρ_K → 0. For ϕ^s ∈ C^(d_0−2) the same argument loses one more
derivative.

(c) At ρ_K = 0, on {y_2 = 0} = {G_1 = 0}, 𝖧 = q_(z_0) ∂_(t_*) + H_(G_1) (Section 15.16.2, after Lemma 15.53) and
ϕ^u = ϕ_u, so f = H_(G_1) ϕ_u = −ν_u ϕ_u by (Γ.2). Thus w_u = ν_u on {y_2 = 0} where ϕ_u ≠ 0, hence on all of it by
continuity, as dϕ_u ≠ 0 there. Likewise w_s = ν_s.

(d) For functions F, F′ of (x, z) = (x, ζ/σ) alone, not depending on t_*, {F, F′} = σ⁻¹{F, F′}_(x,z), the terms with
t_* vanishing. ϕ^u and ϕ^s depend on t_* off ρ_K = 0, through ϕ̃^(u/s), and the formula is used only at ρ_K = 0, where
ϕ̃^(u/s) and its derivatives vanish; so there c_us = {ϕ_0^u, ϕ_0^s}_(x,z). At Γ, by the formula for d(ϕ ∘ π_Y), this is
{ϕ_u, ϕ_s} − (N_Y ϕ_s){ϕ_u, G_1} − (N_Y ϕ_u){G_1, ϕ_s}, and {ϕ_u, G_1} = −H_(G_1) ϕ_u = ν_u ϕ_u = 0, {G_1, ϕ_s} = ν_s
ϕ_s = 0 on Γ. Continuity up to ρ_K = 0 is as in (b). ∎

**Proposition 16.17** (The trapped set.) There are B, E, G ∈ C_b^∞Ψ^0_e3b such that (1) their operator wave
front sets lie in any fixed neighbourhood U_Γ of ∂Γ_(K⁺) in ᵉ³ᵇS*M; (2) their Schwartz kernels are supported in K × K
for any fixed compact neighbourhood K ⊂ M of the base projection of U_Γ; (3) B is elliptic at ∂Γ_(K⁺); (4) WF′(E) ∩
Γ^u_(K⁺) = ∅; and such that for all constants s > s_0 and α_K ∈ ℝ, and χ̃ ∈ C^∞(M) supported near K and equal to 1
near K,

    ‖Bu‖_(H^(s,α_K)) ≤ C (‖GPu‖_(H^(s,α_K)) + ‖Eu‖_(H^(s+1,α_K)) + ‖χ̃u‖_(H^(s_0,α_K)))    (16.19)

in the strong sense, for P = P_0 and every P with ε_P small, with d_0 depending only on s, s_0. Here ∂Γ_(K⁺) and
Γ^u_(K⁺) have one component over each of ∂Σ^±, and within Φ_1(O) (Definition 15.5), which contains U_Γ when U_Γ is
small, Γ^u_(K⁺) is the global unstable set ∂Γ̄^u_(K⁺) (Lemma 15.13 (b)).

This is [Hin26c, Proposition 7.10] in dimension 4 + 1. Against Proposition 16.9–Proposition 16.14 the estimate loses
one derivative: Pu is measured in H^s, not H^(s−1), and the a priori term in H^(s+1). The proof is the positive
commutator form of Section 12.6.5, whose defect measures are replaced by commutators with a common regulariser: an
equation with damping for Φ_u u (Step 1, the counterpart of (12.43)), a commutator with Φ_u that bounds u near
{ϕ^s = 0} by √δ (Step 2, the counterpart of (12.44)), a propagation estimate with the weight |ϕ^s|^(−β) (Step
3, the counterpart of Step 3 of the proof in Section 12.6.5), and their combination, which closes because β < ½ (Step
4).

*Proof.* We prove the estimate at the component over ∂Σ⁺; over ∂Σ⁻ the proof is the same with z_0 = −1, ς = −1 and the
future field −𝖧 (Section 16.3); c_us > 0 there too, as (Γ.3) holds for both z_0 = ±1. After Step 0 (a) norms are
those of H^𝗍_e3b without weights. C denotes constants independent of ε and, from Step 2 on, of δ; C_δ may depend on δ.
Neither depends on u.

*Step 0: reductions and choices.* (a) As in Section 16.1.2 with W′ = 1, w := ρ_K^(α_K) and A the frame of h_Γ, we
replace P by L″ = A⁻¹w⁻¹PwA and u by A⁻¹w⁻¹u, and keep the names P, u. The principal symbol is G, and by
(16.1) and (T1)

### 16.5 Proof of the global estimate

*Proof of Theorem 16.2.* Let u be as in Theorem 16.2 with the right side of (16.4) finite, and write
ℛ for that right side. Extended by zero, u and Pu are supported in {t_*^♭ ≥ 1} (Section 16.1.1). Below, ‖·‖_𝗍 is the
norm of H^(𝗍,(2α_I,α_+,α_K))_e3b, and Pu is measured in H^(𝗍,(2α_I+2,α_++2,α_K))_e3b, which is the measure of Lu =
W⁻¹Pu in H^𝗍 with the weights of u (Section 16.1.1). We say u is *controlled at order* 𝗍 on an open set V ⊂ ᵉ³ᵇS*M
if ‖Bu‖_𝗍 ≤ Cℛ, in the strong sense, for every B ∈ C_b^∞Ψ^0_e3b carried by χ with WF′(B) ⊂ V. Off the characteristic
set u is controlled at every order up to 𝗌 + 1 (Theorem 14.43), so only ∂Σ^± matter. We treat ∂Σ⁺; on ∂Σ⁻ the
future field is −𝖧, and the same steps apply to the antipodal images of the sets below, for which Section 16.3 and
Section 16.4 prove the same estimates.

Three facts are used throughout. (P1) *Propagation.* Theorem 14.49, for L and with the weights put into the
operator as in Section 16.1.2: control at order 𝗍 on an open set V gives control at order 𝗍 at every ϖ whose
backward 𝖧-curve enters V in finite time, provided 𝖧𝗍 ≤ 0 along it and Pu is in H^(𝗍−1) near it; for a compact set of
such ϖ the entrance times are bounded, the flow being continuous on the compactified bundle. The orders 𝗌 and 𝗌 + 1
are non-increasing along the future flow on ∂Σ⁺ for P (Proposition 15.43 (2)). (P2) *Initial surface.* As u = 0 in
{t_*^♭ < 1}, u is controlled at every order there. (P3) *Dynamics.* Over M° every backward curve in ∂Σ⁺ reaches
{t_*^♭ = 1} at a finite parameter (Proposition 15.42); over ∂M the curves are those of P_0 (Lemma 15.41), described
by Proposition 15.18, whose table we use with its notation R_ℋ, R^I_in, R^K_in, Γ_K, R^K_out, R^I_out.

*Step 1: finite times.* Let t^♯ ∈ (1, ∞) and 𝒱_out a neighbourhood of ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out). Then u is controlled at order 𝗌 + 1
on a neighbourhood of every compact subset of ∂Σ⁺ over Ω_* ∩ {t_*^♭ ≤ t^♯} disjoint from 𝒱_out, with C depending on
t^♯ and 𝒱_out. Indeed, a point over M° has its backward curve reach {t_*^♭ < 1} by (P3). A point over ℐ⁺ at finite t_*,
not in ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out), lies on a curve of the first row of the table, which reaches {t_* = 1} backward, and t_*^♭ = t_*
there (Lemma 15.35 (a)). (P1) at order 𝗌 + 1, with Pu ∈ H^𝗌, and (P2) give the claim. Points of ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out) are
fixed by the flow and are left to Step 6. ([Hin26c] propagates into them already here, by its Proposition 7.9 with
finite t_(*,+); see Section 16.13.)

*Step 2: the horizon and ∂R_(ℐ⁺,in,+).* Proposition 16.9 with the orders (𝗌 + 1, 𝗌_0), which are constant near
∂R_(ℋ⁺), with 𝗌_0 > ½ + ϑ_ℋ as 𝗌_0 is admissible (Definition 15.29 (4)), and Proposition 16.13 with the same orders,
whose condition (16.15) is (16.3), have their E supported at finite times: in {ρ_K ≥ (2𝔐)⁻¹}, resp.
{ρ_+ ≥ (2𝔐)⁻¹}. The E of Proposition 16.13 is microsupported near ξ̂ = 2, so away from ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out) = {ξ̂ = 0}, and that
of Proposition 16.9 lies over a neighbourhood of the horizon, away from ℐ⁺. So Step 1, with t^♯ large and 𝒱_out small,
bounds ‖Eu‖_(𝗌+1), and u is controlled at order 𝗌 + 1 on neighbourhoods V_ℋ of ∂R_(ℋ⁺) and V_I of ∂R_(ℐ⁺,in,+).

*Step 3: ∂R_(∂K⁺,in).* Proposition 16.10 with the orders (𝗌 + 1, 𝗌_0), where (16.11) holds as 𝗌_0 is
admissible (Definition 15.29 (6)). Its E has kernel supported away from K⁺, near ∂K⁺, and is microsupported in a small
neighbourhood of ∂R_(∂K⁺,in) where ρ_K⁻¹𝖧ρ_K ≤ −1. Let ϖ ∈ WF′(E) ∩ ∂Σ⁺. Over M°, its backward curve reaches {t_*^♭ <
1} (P3). Over (ι⁺)°, ρ_K increases backward from ϖ, and it keeps increasing: a backward critical point of ρ_K with
ρ_K > 0 would be a local maximum along the curve, against 𝖧²ρ_K > 0 there (Lemma 15.9 (3)). So the curve does not
tend to R^K_out backward, where ρ_K = 0, and by the table over (ι⁺)° it tends to R^I_in, entering V_I. Points over ℐ⁺
do not occur, ∂K⁺ being away from ℐ⁺. (P1) at order 𝗌 + 1 from V_I and (P2) bound ‖Eu‖_(𝗌+1), and u is controlled at
order 𝗌 + 1 on a neighbourhood V_K of ∂R_(∂K⁺,in).

*Step 4: the trapped set.* Proposition 16.17 with the orders (𝗌, 𝗌_0), constant over {r ≤ r_Γ} (Definition 15.29
(3)), with U_Γ ⊂ Φ_1(O) small and Pu ∈ H^𝗌. Let ϖ ∈ WF′(E) ∩ ∂Σ⁺. Over M°, its backward curve reaches {t_*^♭ < 1}.
Over (K⁺)°, ϖ ∉ Γ^u_(K⁺), so ϖ is not in the global unstable set ∂Γ̄^u_(K⁺), as ∂Γ̄^u_(K⁺) ∩ Φ_1(O) = Γ^u_(K⁺)
(Lemma 15.13 (b), from the no-return condition (H8) (b)); by Proposition 15.14 (2) its curve tends backward to
∂R_(ℋ⁺) or ∂R_(∂K⁺,in), entering V_ℋ ∪ V_K. As WF′(E) is compact and the entrance times are locally bounded, (P1) at
order 𝗌 + 1 and (P2) bound ‖Eu‖_(𝗌+1). So u is controlled at order 𝗌 on a neighbourhood V_Γ of ∂Γ_(K⁺). This is the
step that needs Pu in H^𝗌, and the reason Steps 1–3 work at the order 𝗌 + 1.

*Step 5: ∂R_(∂K⁺,out).* Proposition 16.11 with the orders (𝗌, 𝗌_0), with (16.13) from Definition 15.29 (5),
at the order 𝗌 itself, the threshold being an upper bound. Its E is microsupported near ∂R_(∂K⁺,out) with WF′(E) ∩
∂W_out = ∅. Let ϖ ∈ WF′(E) ∩ ∂Σ⁺. Over ∂K⁺ its curve is of type (R^K_in, R^K_out) and enters V_K backward. Over (K⁺)°,
of type (A, R^K_out) with A ∈ {R_ℋ, R^K_in, Γ_K}, it enters V_ℋ ∪ V_K ∪ V_Γ. Over (ι⁺)°, A ≠ R^K_out as ϖ ∉ ∂W_out,
the unstable manifold of ∂R_(∂K⁺,out) over ι⁺ (Lemma 15.9 (4)), so by the table A = R^I_in, and the curve enters
V_I. Over M°, it reaches {t_*^♭ < 1}. (P1) at order 𝗌 bounds ‖Eu‖_𝗌, and u is controlled at order 𝗌 on a neighbourhood
V_(K,out) of ∂R_(∂K⁺,out).

*Step 6: ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out).* Proposition 16.14 with t_(*,−) := ½, the orders (𝗌, 𝗌_0), constant near ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out)
(Proposition 15.43 (5)), and (16.17) from (16.3). Its B is elliptic on ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out) ∩ {t_*^♭ ≥ ½},
which contains all of it over Ω_*. The part of E from the cut-off ψ_− has kernel in {t_*^♭ < 1}², where u = 0 (the
paragraph after Proposition 16.14). The rest of E is microsupported in a punctured neighbourhood of ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out). Let ϖ
be a point of it in ∂Σ⁺. Over (ℐ⁺)°, its curve reaches {t_* = 1} backward (first row of the table). Over ℐ⁺ ∩ ι⁺ it is
of type (R^I_in, R^I_out), and over (ι⁺)° of type (R^I_in, ·) or (R^K_out, R^I_out); it enters V_I ∪ V_(K,out). Over
M°, it reaches {t_*^♭ < 1}. (P1) at order 𝗌 bounds ‖Eu‖_𝗌, and u is controlled at order 𝗌 on a neighbourhood V_(I,out)
of ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out) ∩ {t_*^♭ ≥ ½}.

*Conclusion.* Let ϖ ∈ ∂Σ⁺ over supp χ. If ϖ lies over M° or over ℐ⁺ at finite t_*, it is controlled at order 𝗌 by Step
1 when ϖ ∉ 𝒱_out, with t^♯ > t_*^♭(ϖ), and by Step 6 when ϖ ∈ V_(I,out), choosing 𝒱_out inside V_(I,out). If ϖ lies
over K⁺ ∪ ι⁺, it lies in one of the sets of Steps 2–6 or on a curve of the table, whose backward end A is {t_* = 1} or
one of R_ℋ, R^I_in, R^K_in, Γ_K, R^K_out, each of which has a controlled neighbourhood. This includes the curves inside
the black hole, from ∂R_(ℋ⁺) to {r < r_0 − δ_0} (Proposition 15.14), which reach supp χ ⊂ {r ≥ r_1}; (P1) at order 𝗌
applies. By compactness of the cosphere bundle over supp χ, finitely many such B, with elliptic estimates off Σ, are
jointly elliptic there, and the elliptic estimate (Lemma 14.29 (c)), with the a priori term ‖χu‖_(−N′) ≤
‖u‖_(𝗌_0), gives (16.4), in the strong sense since every step propagates regularity.

*Uniformity.* Each estimate used holds uniformly for P with ε_P small (Proposition 16.9–Proposition 16.14,
Proposition 16.17, Theorem 14.43 and Theorem 14.49). The flow of P agrees with that of P_0 over ∂M, and over
M° it differs by O(ε_P) in C¹ (Lemma 15.41 (a)), so the finitely many backward segments used above, which enter
open sets in bounded times, have nearby segments for P with the same properties. d_0 is the largest of those required
by the steps, at the orders 𝗌_0, 𝗌 and 𝗌 + 1. With Remark 16.3 this proves Theorem 16.2. ∎

### 16.6 Regularity with b-derivatives: the setting

b-regularity is tested by commuting b-vector fields through P. For the elliptic and real principal type estimates,
Section 14.14 commutes a spanning set of b-vector fields; the commutators enter the commuted system below principal
order, where those estimates do not see them. At a radial set or at the trapped set the subprincipal symbol of the
commuted system enters the threshold. There one uses families of commutator fields whose commutators with P either
decay at the face carrying the set, or contribute with the favourable sign, so that the commuted system has the
threshold of P. Section 16.7 writes the commuted system for an arbitrary family and proves, once, that the estimate
for it gives the estimate with b-regularity, and its tame version (Lemma 16.21, Lemma 16.22). The estimates
of Section 16.3 and Section 16.4 hold for the commuted systems (Lemma 16.23). Section 16.8–Section 16.11
supply the families: near ℐ⁺, at the horizon, over ∂K⁺ and at the trapped set. Section 16.12 proves the global
estimate. This is [Hin26c, Section 7.2] in dimension 4 + 1.

The setting is that of Section 16.1, now with k degrees of b-regularity. P is a weakly admissible wave-type operator
relative to P_0 of class ((d_0; k), (2ℓ_I, ℓ_+, ℓ_K)) (Definition 15.36), with ℓ_I ∈ (0, ½], ℓ_+, ℓ_K > 0, and ε_(P,k)
:= ‖P − P_0‖_((d_0;k),(2ℓ_I,ℓ_+,ℓ_K)) (Definition 15.39). The bundle E is the trivial bundle ℂ^(N_E)
(Section 15.9.1), and b-vector fields act on its sections componentwise, so no connection is needed. As in
Section 16.1.1, "of class" means conditions (1)–(2) of Definition 15.36; condition (3) is not used here either: the
proofs below use p_1 and p_0 only through Lemma 15.37 and the thresholds of Section 16.3.
H^((𝗌;k),(2α_I,α_+,α_K))_(e3b;b) are the mixed spaces of (14.6), with their supported and extendible versions
as in Section 14.7, and ‖·‖_(𝗌;k) their norms, weights suppressed where they are fixed. D^j_b is the schematic
notation of Section 14.14.3. Weights do not interfere with commutators: for a b-vector field V and a weight w (a
product of powers of boundary defining functions), w⁻¹Vw = V + (V log w) with V log w smooth. Two facts are used
throughout.

(F1) ‖v‖_(𝗍+1;k−1) ≤ C‖v‖_(𝗍;k), and microlocally ‖Gv‖_(𝗍+1;k−1) ≤ C(‖G′v‖_(𝗍;k) + ‖χv‖_(−N′;k)) for G′ elliptic on
WF′(G) (Lemma 14.29 (c)–(d)): an e3b-vector field is a b-vector field.

(F2) For elements X_1, …, X_q and P of a ring, [X_1 ⋯ X_q, P] = Σ_(∅≠S) (ad_(X_S) P) X^({1..q}∖S), the sum over subsets
S of the positions, ad_(X_S) the iterated commutator and the remaining factors in their order (Lemma 14.53,
(14.24)).

**Theorem 16.18** (The global estimate with b-regularity.) Let α_I, α_+, α_K, 𝗌_0 < 𝗌 and χ be as in
Theorem 16.2. For every k ∈ ℕ_0 there is C_k such that

    ‖χu‖_(H^((𝗌;k),(2α_I,α_+,α_K))_(e3b;b))
        ≤ C_k (‖Pu‖_(H^((𝗌;k),(2α_I+2,α_++2,α_K))_(e3b;b)(Ω_*;E)^(•,−))
                + ‖u‖_(H^((𝗌_0;k),(2α_I,α_+,α_K))_(e3b;b)(Ω_*;E)^(•,−)))    (16.31)

for P = P_0, in the strong sense, and for every P satisfying conditions (1)–(2) of Definition 15.36 at the class
((d_0; k), (2ℓ_I, ℓ_+, ℓ_K)) (condition (3) not assumed) with ε_(P,k) small, with C_k
uniform; d_0 depends only on 𝗌_0 and 𝗌. Moreover there is d ∈ ℕ such that for every k and every P of class ((d_0; k),
(2ℓ_I, ℓ_+, ℓ_K)) with ε_(P,d) small,

    ‖χu‖_(𝗌;k) ≤ C_k (‖Pu‖_(𝗌;k) + ‖u‖_(𝗌_0;k) + ε_(P,k) (‖Pu‖_(𝗌;d) + ‖u‖_(𝗌_0;d))),    (16.32)

with the spaces and weights of (16.31), and C_k depending on P only through a bound for ε_(P,d).

This is [Hin26c, Proposition 7.11] in dimension 4 + 1, with the weights of u in the last norm of (16.32) (see
Section 16.13). (16.32) is used for k ≥ d, and (16.31) for k < d. The proof is in
Section 16.12.

### 16.7 The commuted system

Throughout this section Γ ⊂ ᵉ³ᵇS*M is one of the sets of Section 16.3–Section 16.4 (a radial set or the trapped set,
over one of ∂Σ^±), U_0 an open neighbourhood of Γ near fibre infinity, and L the operator that the corresponding
estimate there treats (L = W′⁻¹P, Section 16.1.1). 𝔩 ∈ {0, 1} is the loss: 𝔩 = 0 at the radial sets and 𝔩 = 1 at
the trapped set, where the estimate loses one derivative. A *family* is 𝒳 = (X_1, …, X_J) with X_i ∈ Diff¹_b(M) acting
componentwise and X_J := I. For k ≥ 1, 𝒲_k := {1, …, J}^k is the set of words of length k, X^α := X_(α_1) ⋯ X_(α_k),
and for a position i and a letter j, j·(α∖i) is the word obtained by deleting the i-th letter of α and putting j in
front. The order of factors matters, as the X_i need not commute; words take care of it.

*Operators of limited regularity.* "Q is of class 𝒬^m_q" means that Q is a finite sum Σ a_l A_l, as in
Section 14.8.2, with A_l ∈ C_b^∞Ψ^m_e3b fixed and carried by the cut-off χ of the estimate (Section 14.8.3), and
a_l ∈ C^∞ + C^((d_0;k−q))_(e3b;b): q b-derivatives of the coefficients of P have been spent. Its *decaying part* is
the sum of the terms whose coefficients vanish at the face carrying Γ, at a rate ρ_Γ^ℓ for a defining function ρ_Γ of
that face and some ℓ > 0. The hypotheses on a family are:

(C) For each i < J, [L, X_i] = Σ_(j=1)^J Q_(ij) X_j + R_i, with Q_(ij) of class 𝒬^1_1 and R_i of class 𝒬^2_1 with
WF′(A_l) ∩ Ū_0 = ∅ for all its terms. For i = J put Q_(Jj) := 0 and R_J := 0, as [L, X_J] = [L, I] = 0.

(C2) (Only if 𝔩 = 1.) For i, i′ < J, [X_(i′), [X_i, L]] = Σ_(j,j′=1)^J Q^(2)_(i′i,jj′) X_j X_(j′) + R^(2)_(i′i), with
Q^(2)_(i′i,jj′) of class 𝒬^0_2 and R^(2)_(i′i) = R′ + Σ_j R″_j X_j with R′ of class 𝒬^2_2 and R″_j of class 𝒬^1_2, all
microsupported off Ū_0 as in (C). If i = J or i′ = J, put Q^(2)_(i′i,jj′) := 0 and R^(2)_(i′i) := 0, as the double
commutator then vanishes.

(M) Over a neighbourhood of the base projection of Ū_0, the X_i together with 𝒱_e3b span 𝒱_b over C^∞; and either the
X_i alone span 𝒱_b there, or there are i_0 < J and a bounded weight w, a product of non-negative powers of boundary
defining functions, with wX_(i_0) ∈ Diff¹_e3b elliptic on Ū_0. Each X_i, i < J, is a commutator field there:
[X_i, 𝒱_e3b] ⊂ 𝒱_e3b (Lemma 14.5, Lemma 14.9, Corollary 14.6). The four families of
Section 16.8–Section 16.11 extend to global elements of 𝒱_b that are commutator fields everywhere (∂_r and r∂_r
are e3b-fields, t_*∂_(t_*) is a commutator field everywhere, and the Ω_ab are 3b-fields near K⁺ and eb-commutator
fields near ℐ⁺), which is what the global statements of Lemma 14.5 and Lemma 14.29 (a) use.

*Parametrix remainders.* Lemma 14.29 (b) gives microlocal parametrices of a finite order J′; a remainder said
below to be microsupported off Ū_0 is the sum of such a term and of one of order −J′ near Ū_0. Every use needs only J′
large, depending on the orders, and we write as if the second term were absent.

**Lemma 16.19** (The commuted system.) Assume (C), and (C2) if 𝔩 = 1. For k ≥ 1 put u^(k) := (X^α
u)_(α∈𝒲_k) and f := Lu. Then

    L^(k) u^(k) = f^(k) + f̃^(k) + f̃^(k)_♭,       f^(k) := (X^α f)_α,    (16.33)

where L^(k) acts on (ℂ^(N_E))^(𝒲_k) by

    (L^(k) w)_α := L w_α − Σ_(i=1)^k Σ_(j=1)^J Q_(α_i j) w_(j·(α∖i))
                   + 𝔩 Σ_(i<i′) Σ_(j,j′) Q^(2)_(α_i α_i′, jj′) w_(jj′·(α∖{i,i′}))    (16.34)

(the last sum over pairs of positions, with jj′·(α∖{i,i′}) the word with those two letters deleted and j, j′ put in
front), f̃^(k)_α := −Σ_(|S|≥2+𝔩) (ad_(X_S) L) X^(α∖S) u, the sum over sets S of positions, and f̃^(k)_(♭,α) := Σ_i
R_(α_i) X^(α∖i) u − 𝔩 Σ_(i<i′) R^(2)_(α_i α_i′) X^(α∖{i,i′}) u.

This is [Hin26c, (7.32), (7.43), (7.61)] in dimension 4 + 1, written with words (see Section 16.13).

*Proof.* L X^α u = X^α f − [X^α, L]u, and (F2) expands [X^α, L] over the sets S of positions. For S = {i},
ad_(X_(α_i)) L = −[L, X_(α_i)] = −Σ_j Q_(α_i j) X_j − R_(α_i) by (C), and X_j X^(α∖i) = X^(j·(α∖i)). So −(ad_(X_(α_i))
L) X^(α∖i) u = Σ_j Q_(α_i j) u^(k)_(j·(α∖i)) + R_(α_i) X^(α∖i) u. If 𝔩 = 1, for S = {i, i′}, i < i′, (F2) gives
ad_(X_(α_i)) ad_(X_(α_i′)) L = [X_(α_i), [X_(α_i′), L]], which (C2) writes as Σ Q^(2) X_j X_(j′) + R^(2), with the
indices of (16.34) after relabelling; its contribution is moved to the left in the same way. ∎

*Commuting letters.* If a letter j < J commutes with every X_i, then for a word α and a position i, X_j X^(α∖i) =
X^(α[i→j]), where α[i→j] is α with its i-th letter replaced by j. So in (16.34) the term Q_(α_i j)
w_(j·(α∖i)) may be replaced by Q_(α_i j) w_(α[i→j]); the operator so modified is

    (L^(k) w)_α := L w_α − Σ_(i=1)^k Σ_(j=1)^J Q_(α_i j) w_(α⟨i,j⟩)
                   + 𝔩 Σ_(i<i′) Σ_(j,j′) Q^(2)_(α_i α_i′, jj′) w_(jj′·(α∖{i,i′})),    (16.35)

where α⟨i,j⟩ := α[i→j] if j < J and the letter j commutes with every X_i, and α⟨i,j⟩ := j·(α∖i) otherwise.
(16.33) holds for it with the same proof, since only L^(k) u^(k) enters, and Lemma 16.21–Lemma 16.23
use of L^(k) only that it is L ⊗ Id minus a coupling whose coefficients carry at most 1 + 𝔩 b-derivatives of those of
P, so they hold for (16.35). For a letter 1 with α_i = 1, α[i→1] = α: the coupling through that letter
is diagonal. This is what the horizon needs (Lemma 16.26 (c)). With (16.34) the word 1·(α∖i) differs
from α in general (for instance α = (2, 1), i = 2), and for k ≥ 2 the Hermitian part of the coupling is indefinite. At
the horizon Q_(1j) = 0 for j ≠ 1, and Q_(21), Q_(22) decay at K⁺ (Lemma 16.26 (b), (c) and their proofs); so at
∂R_(ℋ⁺), on the two components (1, 2, …, 2) and (2, 1, 2, …, 2), the principal symbol of Im(L^(k) − L ⊗ Id) for
(16.34) is σ_1(Im(−Q_11)) ≠ 0 times the matrix with rows (1, ½) and (½, 0), whose determinant is −¼.

The coefficients of L^(k) − L ⊗ Id carry at most 1 + 𝔩 b-derivatives of those of P, whatever k is; this is what makes
the tame estimate possible.

**Lemma 16.20** (Mixed norms.) Assume (M). Let B, B̃ ∈ C_b^∞Ψ^0_e3b be carried by χ, with operator wave
front sets in U_0 and B̃ elliptic on WF′(B), and χ̃ a cut-off equal to 1 near the base projection of Ū_0. Then for all
orders 𝗍, 𝗍_0 and k ∈ ℕ_0,

    ‖Bu‖_(𝗍;k) ≤ C (‖B̃u‖_(𝗍;k−1) + Σ_(α∈𝒲_k) ‖BX^α u‖_𝗍 + ‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k)),    (16.36)

    Σ_(α∈𝒲_k) ‖BX^α u‖_𝗍 ≤ C (‖B̃u‖_(𝗍;k) + ‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k)).    (16.37)

(16.37) holds without (M), for any family of b-differential operators of order 1. This is [Hin26c, Lemmas 7.15
and 7.19] in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* (16.37): BX^α u = X^α Bu − [X^α, B]u. The first term has H^𝗍-norm at most C‖Bu‖_(𝗍;k), as the X_i
are b-differential operators. By (F2), [X^α, B] is a sum of terms (ad_(X_S) B) X^(α∖S) with ad_(X_S) B ∈ C_b^∞Ψ^0_e3b
microsupported in WF′(B) (Lemma 14.29 (a)); moving the remaining factors to the left by (14.25) bounds
them by C‖B̃u‖_(𝗍;k) + C‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k), using an elliptic parametrix of B̃ (Lemma 14.29 (c)). ‖Bu‖_(𝗍;k) ≤
C(‖B̃u‖_(𝗍;k) + ‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k)) in the same way. (16.36): by (M) and the notation of Section 14.14.3,
‖Bu‖_(𝗍;k) is equivalent to the sum of ‖AX^β Bu‖_𝗍 over A ∈ Diff^(k−|β|)_e3b from a fixed finite set and words β in
the X_i with |β| ≤ k. If the X_i span 𝒱_b, only A = I, |β| = k is needed (words with the letter J give the lower
orders). Otherwise, let Q_q ∈ C_b^∞Ψ^(−q)_e3b be a microlocal parametrix of (wX_(i_0))^q on Ū_0, I =
Q_q (wX_(i_0))^q + R′_q with WF′(R′_q) ∩ Ū_0 = ∅ (with (wX_(i_0))^q = w^q X_(i_0)^q + Σ_(q′<q) w_(q′) X_(i_0)^(q′),
w_(q′) bounded, as X_(i_0) w ∈ wC^∞). Then for A of order q := k − |β|,

    AX^β Bu = AQ_q w^q X_(i_0)^q X^β Bu + Σ_(q′<q) AQ_q w_(q′) X_(i_0)^(q′) X^β Bu + AR′_q X^β Bu.

AQ_q w^q and AQ_q w_(q′) lie in C_b^∞Ψ^0_e3b (as w^q, w_(q′) are bounded and A has order q), so the first term is
bounded by ‖X^(i_0^q β) Bu‖_𝗍, a word of length k, and the second by words of length < k with letters J added. The
third is microsupported off Ū_0 after commuting X^β through B, and is at most C‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k). Finally X^γ Bu = BX^γ
u + [X^γ, B]u, and the commutator terms carry at most k − 1 factors and are at most C‖B̃u‖_(𝗍;k−1) + C‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k), as
in (16.37). ∎

In the estimates below, the operators B, E, G of an estimate of Section 16.3–Section 16.4 come with properties
(1)–(4) listed there (wave front sets in a given neighbourhood, Schwartz kernels in a given set, B elliptic at Γ, and a
condition on E). A finite union of closed sets each satisfying (4) satisfies (4); and an operator elliptic on such a
union, with wave front set in a small neighbourhood of it, can be chosen to satisfy (4) again; for Proposition 16.14 it
satisfies (4) with t_(*,−) + δ′ in place of t_(*,−), for any δ′ > 0, and since t_(*,−) is arbitrary there, starting the
inductions below from t_(*,−) − kδ′ gives (4) as stated at the order k. We use this without comment.

*The estimate for systems.* We say (E_𝔩) holds for a family on U_0 if, for every k ≥ 1, every neighbourhood U ⊂ U_0 of
Γ and every χ̃ as in Lemma 16.20, there are B_k, E_k, G_k with properties (1)–(4), wave front sets in U and B_k
elliptic at Γ, such that in the strong sense

    ‖B_k w‖_𝗍 ≤ C (‖G_k L^(k) w‖_(𝗍−1+𝔩) + ‖E_k w‖_(𝗍+𝔩) + ‖χ̃w‖_(𝗍_0))    (16.38)

for ℂ^(N_E |𝒲_k|)-valued w, with weights as in the estimate of Section 16.3–Section 16.4, and with C depending on k
and on P only through bounds for finitely many C^(d_0)-norms of the coefficients of L^(k). Lemma 16.23 gives
(E_𝔩) in each case below.

**Lemma 16.21** (The induction.) Assume (C), (M), (C2) if 𝔩 = 1, and (E_𝔩), at the constant orders 𝗍 > 𝗍_0,
and that P is of class ((d_0; k), …) with d_0 large depending on 𝗍, 𝗍_0. Then for every k ∈ ℕ_0 and every
neighbourhood U ⊂ U_0 of Γ there are B, E, G with properties (1)–(4), wave front sets in U and B elliptic at Γ, such
that in the strong sense

    ‖Bu‖_(𝗍;k) ≤ C_k (‖GLu‖_(𝗍−1+𝔩;k) + ‖Eu‖_(𝗍+𝔩;k) + ‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k)).    (16.39)

For k = 0 this is the estimate of Section 16.3–Section 16.4 itself. This is the induction in [Hin26c, proofs of
Propositions 7.17 and 7.22].

*Proof.* Induction on k. Let k ≥ 1 and assume (16.39) at k − 1 for every neighbourhood of Γ. Let U_(k−1) ⊂ U
be a neighbourhood of Γ on which the conclusion at k − 1 holds for operators B′ microsupported in U_(k−1), with
operators E′, G′ (the union of the sets of two applications, for B′ and a slightly larger one). Apply (E_𝔩) with
U_(k−1) in place of U, to w := u^(k), giving B_k, E_k, G_k microsupported in U_(k−1); choose auxiliary operators
G^♯_1, G^♯_2 ((R1) of Section 14.8.3) with WF′(G_k) ⊂ Ell(G^♯_1), WF′(G^♯_1) ⊂ Ell(G^♯_2) and
WF′(G^♯_2) ⊂ U_(k−1), and B with WF′(B) ⊂ Ell(B_k), B elliptic at Γ. By Lemma 16.19,
‖G_k L^(k) u^(k)‖ ≤ ‖G_k f^(k)‖ + ‖G_k f̃^(k)‖ + ‖G_k f̃^(k)_♭‖, all norms of order 𝗍 − 1 + 𝔩. We bound each term of
(16.38) at w = u^(k).

*The left side.* By (16.36) with B̃ := G^♯_1, ‖Bu‖_(𝗍;k) ≤ C(‖G^♯_1 u‖_(𝗍;k−1) + Σ_α ‖BX^α u‖_𝗍 +
‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k)), and ‖BX^α u‖_𝗍 ≤ C(‖B_k u^(k)‖_𝗍 + ‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k)), as B_k is elliptic on WF′(B) and ‖χ̃X^α u‖_(𝗍_0) ≤
C‖χ̃′u‖_(𝗍_0;k), χ̃′ slightly larger: here and below, a cut-off said to be slightly larger than χ̃ equals 1 near
supp χ̃. As L is a differential operator, χ̃L = χ̃Lχ̃′ for such χ̃′ (Section 14.8.3), so the nested choices of the
induction need no fixed margin. The first term is bounded by (16.39) at k − 1.

*The a priori terms.* By (16.37), ‖E_k X^α u‖_(𝗍+𝔩) ≤ C(‖Eu‖_(𝗍+𝔩;k) + ‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k)) for E elliptic on
WF′(E_k), and ‖χ̃u^(k)‖_(𝗍_0) ≤ C‖χ̃′u‖_(𝗍_0;k).

*The term f^(k).* By (16.37) for f, ‖G_k X^α f‖_(𝗍−1+𝔩) ≤ C(‖G^♯_1 f‖_(𝗍−1+𝔩;k) + ‖χ̃f‖_(𝗍_0−2;k)). Here
‖χ̃f‖_(𝗍_0−2;k) = ‖χ̃Lχ̃′u‖_(𝗍_0−2;k) ≤ C‖χ̃′u‖_(𝗍_0;k), as L is bounded on the mixed spaces with coefficients of
class (d_0; k) (Lemma 14.31 (a)), and ‖G^♯_1 f‖ ≤ C(‖GLu‖_(𝗍−1+𝔩;k) + ‖χ̃f‖_(𝗍_0−2;k)) for G elliptic on
WF′(G^♯_1).

*The term f̃^(k)_♭.* G_k R_i and G_k R^(2) have every order, the wave front sets being disjoint (Lemma 14.30 (b),
with the coefficient regularity (d_0; k − 2)); for the terms R″_j X_j X^(α∖{i,i′}) u of (C2) the word X_j
X^(α∖{i,i′}) has k − 1 letters. So ‖G_k f̃^(k)_♭‖_(𝗍−1+𝔩) ≤ C‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k−1).

*The term f̃^(k).* Let |S| = q ≥ 2 + 𝔩. ad_(X_S) L is a second-order operator of class 𝒬^2_q: each commutator with a
b-vector field preserves Diff²_e3b up to the coefficients (Lemma 14.15, and Lemma 14.5 near K⁺,
Lemma 14.9 near ℐ⁺), and differentiates the coefficients once. So by Lemma 14.31 (b) and (16.37),

    ‖G_k (ad_(X_S) L) X^(α∖S) u‖_(𝗍−1+𝔩) ≤ C (‖G^♯_2 u‖_(𝗍+1+𝔩;k−q) + ‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k)).

As q − 1 ≥ 1 + 𝔩, q − 1 applications of (F1) bound ‖G^♯_2 u‖_(𝗍+1+𝔩;k−q) by C(‖G^♯_3 u‖_(𝗍;k−1) + ‖χ̃u‖_(−N′;k)),
with an auxiliary operator G^♯_3 slightly larger than G^♯_2 and still microsupported in U_(k−1); this is bounded by
(16.39) at k − 1. This is where 𝔩 = 1 needs (C2): a term with q = 2 would need ‖G^♯_2 u‖_(𝗍+2;k−2), which
(F1) bounds only by the norm at (𝗍 + 1; k − 1), one order above what the induction controls.

Collecting the terms gives (16.39) at k, with E elliptic on the union of WF′(E_k) and the E-sets of the step
k − 1. Each quantity bounded is finite when the right side of (16.39) is, by (16.38) in the strong
sense and the inductive hypothesis, so the estimate holds in the strong sense. ∎

**Lemma 16.22** (Tame version.) Under the hypotheses of Lemma 16.21 there is d ∈ ℕ, depending only on
𝗍, 𝗍_0, such that for all k and P of class ((d_0; k), …), with the operators of Lemma 16.21,

    ‖Bu‖_(𝗍;k) ≤ C_k (ℛ_k + ε_(P,k) ℛ_d),       ℛ_q := ‖GLu‖_(𝗍−1+𝔩;q) + ‖Eu‖_(𝗍+𝔩;q) + ‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;q),    (16.40)

with C_k depending on P only through a bound for ε_(P,d). This is [Hin26c, (7.52), (7.68)] in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* Let d_1 and d̃ be the larger of the numbers d_0, resp. d̃, of Proposition 14.56 for the orders (𝗍 + 1 + 𝔩,
𝗍_0) and (𝗍_0 − 2, 𝗍_0 − 2); take d_0 ≥ d_1 + 2, enlarged to serve Lemma 16.21, and d := d̃ + 3. For k ≤ d,
(16.40) is (16.39), whose constant depends on ε_(P,k) ≤ ε_(P,d). Let k > d and assume
(16.40) below k. In the proof of Lemma 16.21 the coefficients of P enter with more than 2 b-derivatives
in two places only. The constant of (16.38) involves the coefficients of L^(k), which carry at most 1 + 𝔩
derivatives (Lemma 16.19), so it depends on ε_(P,3) ≤ ε_(P,d). (a) ‖χ̃Lχ̃′u‖_(𝗍_0−2;k): write L = L_0 + (L −
L_0), L_0 the operator of P_0; L_0 contributes C‖χ̃′u‖_(𝗍_0;k), and Corollary 14.57 bounds the rest by C_k(ε_(P,d̃)
‖χ̃″u‖_(𝗍_0;k) + ε_(P,k) ‖χ̃″u‖_(𝗍_0;d̃)). (b) ‖G_k (ad_(X_S) L) X^(α∖S) u‖_(𝗍−1+𝔩), |S| = q ≥ 2 + 𝔩: the coefficients
of ad_(X_S)(L − L_0) are sums of (D^(q′)_[b] p) times fixed operators, q′ ≤ q, p a coefficient of L − L_0; the part
with q′ ≤ 2 + 𝔩 is bounded as in Lemma 16.21 with constant depending on ε_(P,3). For q′ ≥ 3 + 𝔩, commute the
second-order factor to the front and G_k through it, as in [Hin26c, (7.55)–(7.56)]; it remains to bound
‖G̃ (D^(q′)_[b] D^(≤2)_e3b p)(D^(k−q)_[b] u)‖_(𝗍+1+𝔩) with G̃ microsupported in U_(k−1). Proposition 14.56, with
D^(2+𝔩)_[b] D^(≤2)_e3b p for its ℓ and (q′ − 2 − 𝔩, k′) for its (j, k), k′ := k − q + q′ − 2 − 𝔩 ≤ k − 2 − 𝔩, bounds
it, after enlarging k′ to k − 2 − 𝔩 in the norms of u (and the constant C_(k′) to C_k), by

    C_k (‖p‖_(d_1+2;d̃+2+𝔩) (‖G^♯u‖_(𝗍+1+𝔩;k−2−𝔩) + ‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;k))
          + ‖p‖_(d_1+2;k) (‖G^♯u‖_(𝗍+1+𝔩;d̃) + ‖χ̃u‖_(𝗍_0;d̃))),

as ‖D^(2+𝔩)_[b] D^(≤2)_e3b p‖_(d_1;q) ≤ C‖p‖_(d_1+2;q+2+𝔩) and k′ + 2 + 𝔩 ≤ k. By (F1), ‖G^♯u‖_(𝗍+1+𝔩;k−2−𝔩) ≤
C‖G^♯_1 u‖_(𝗍;k−1), bounded by (16.40) at k − 1, whose high norm ε_(P,k−1) multiplies ℛ_d only; and
‖G^♯u‖_(𝗍+1+𝔩;d̃) ≤ C‖G^♯_1 u‖_(𝗍;d̃+1+𝔩), bounded by (16.39) at the order d̃ + 1 + 𝔩 < d. Here
‖p‖_(d_1+2;d̃+2+𝔩) ≤ Cε_(P,d) and ‖p‖_(d_1+2;k) ≤ Cε_(P,k), as d_1 + 2 ≤ d_0, the coefficients of L − L_0 being those
of P − P_0 up to fixed smooth factors (Definition 15.39). The other terms of the proof of Lemma 16.21 involve no
coefficient with more than two derivatives. This gives (16.40). ∎

**Lemma 16.23** (The estimates of Section 16.3–Section 16.4 for systems.) Let m ∈ ℕ and L̃ := L ⊗ Id_m −
Q on (ℂ^(N_E))^m, with Q of class 𝒬^1_2 (with the regularity (d_0; 0) for its coefficients). Let Γ be one of the sets
of Proposition 16.9–Proposition 16.14 and Proposition 16.17, with the fibre inner product h used there, and suppose
that at Γ, as Hermitian matrices for h^(⊕m),

    ς ρ σ_1(Im_(h^(⊕m)) (−Q)) ≤ 0,    (16.41)

with ρ the function used at Γ in Section 16.3–Section 16.4 and ς = ±1 on ∂Σ^±. Then the estimate of
Section 16.3–Section 16.4 at Γ holds for L̃ in place of L, with the same orders, weights and thresholds, and with
constants depending on finitely many norms of the coefficients of Q.

*Proof.* L ⊗ Id_m is L for the bundle E^(⊕m) = ℂ^(N_E m), an operator of the same class with the same thresholds in the
inner product h^(⊕m), as all quantities are block diagonal. *Radial sets.* By Remark 16.15, the estimates hold for
L ⊗ Id + P̃ with P̃ first order of the form stated there, with the thresholds calculated from σ_1(Im_(h^(⊕m)) L̃) at Γ.
By (16.41) this differs from that of L ⊗ Id by a non-positive Hermitian matrix (times ς). In each quantity Q_ε
of Section 16.3 it enters as −2A⁻¹(·)A (the term −2A⁻¹𝔭′A, and at ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out) the term 4A⁻¹(Re_h p_1)A =
−2A⁻¹𝔭′A), so it only increases Q_ε, and every lower bound of Section 16.3 persists. *The trapped set.* In the proof
of Proposition 16.17 the operator enters through its principal symbol G Id, unchanged; through 𝔭 at ∂Γ_(K⁺), now 𝔭 −
ρσ_1(Im Q) after the conjugation of Step 0, whose largest eigenvalue is at most ϑ_Γ by (16.41), so (T3) and
(16.20) hold as stated; through the form Op(ℓ_f) + R_L of the remark after Lemma 16.8, which L̃ has; and
through the commutator (16.21), where [Q, Φ_u] has order 0 and joins R_2. Nothing else in Section 16.2 and
Section 16.4 uses the operator. ∎

In Section 16.8–Section 16.11, (16.41) holds because the first-order part of Q either decays at the face
carrying Γ, so that its principal symbol vanishes at Γ, or is diagonal with a non-positive contribution (at the
horizon). The part of Q of order 0 does not enter (16.41).

### 16.8 Near ℐ⁺

Near ℐ⁺ ∩ Ω we use the coordinates ρ_+ = t_*⁻¹, x_I = (t_*/r)^(1/2), ω ∈ 𝕊³ of Section 15.13.1, W := x_I² ρ_+² and L
:= W⁻¹P, as in Proposition 16.13 and Proposition 16.14. Put

    V_1 := x_I ∂_(x_I) − 2ρ_+ ∂_(ρ_+) = 2t_* ∂_(t_*),       V_2 := x_I ∂_(x_I) = −2r ∂_r,

the second at fixed t_*, and let Ω_ab, 1 ≤ a < b ≤ 4, be the six rotation fields y_a ∂_(y_b) − y_b ∂_(y_a) of 𝕊³ ⊂ ℝ⁴,
extended independently of (x_I, ρ_+). The family is 𝒳_I := (V_1, V_2, Ω_12, …, Ω_34, I), J = 9.

**Lemma 16.24** (Commutators near ℐ⁺.) (a) [V_1, V_2] = [V_i, Ω_ab] = 0, the Ω_ab span 𝔰𝔬(4), and
Σ_(a<b) Ω_ab² is the Laplace–Beltrami operator of 𝕊³, so Δ_𝕊³ of Lemma 15.37 is ±Σ_(a<b) Ω_ab² and commutes with
every Ω_ab. (b) The family 𝒳_I satisfies (C) on Ω_I = Ω ∩ {x_I ≤ ε_I} with R_i = 0, and each Q_(ij) is the sum of an
operator of order 0 and a first-order eb-operator whose coefficients lie in x_I C^∞ + x_I^(2ℓ_I) C^((d_0;k−1))_(eb;b).
(c) 𝒳_I spans 𝒱_b near ℐ⁺, and its elements are eb-commutator fields (Lemma 14.9), so (M) holds. (d) At
∂R_(ℐ⁺,in,+) and ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out), which lie over x_I = 0, the first-order part of each Q_(ij) has vanishing principal
symbol, so (16.41) holds with equality.

This is [Hin26c, Lemma 7.12] in dimension 4 + 1: there are six rotation fields on 𝕊³, Δ_𝕊³ is exactly ±Σ_(a<b) Ω_ab²,
the constant 3 = n − 1 of Lemma 15.37 replaces 2, and, the bundle being trivial with b-vector fields acting
componentwise, the fields V_1, V_2, Ω_ab commute with one another exactly where [Hin26c, (7.31)] has commutators in
x_I C^∞. None of this changes the structure of (C).

*Proof.* (a) V_1, V_2 are coordinate vector fields of the product coordinates (log x_I, log ρ_+), up to constant linear
combinations, and the Ω_ab act on ω alone. The Ω_ab are the generators of the action of SO(4) on 𝕊³, and Σ_(a<b) Ω_ab²
is the Casimir operator of this action on functions, which is the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the round metric (the
identity Σ_(a<b) (y_a ∂_b − y_b ∂_a)² = |y|² Δ_ℝ⁴ − (y·∂)² − 2 y·∂ restricted to |y| = 1, functions extended
homogeneously of degree 0). (b) By Lemma 15.37, near ℐ⁺,

    2L = −(V_2 − 3 − 2p_1) V_1 ± 2x_I² Σ_(a<b) Ω_ab² + p_0 + R̃,       R̃ ∈ C^((d_0;k),(2ℓ_I,0))_(eb;b) Diff²_eb,

with p_0, p_1 = S|_(∂X) + p̃_1 functions on ℐ⁺ extended independently of x_I, so V_2 p_0 = V_2 p_1 = 0. We calculate
[2L, X] for X ∈ 𝒳_I, X ≠ I, using [AB, X] = A[B, X] + [A, X]B and (a).

[−(V_2 − 3 − 2p_1)V_1, X] = 2[p_1, X]V_1 = −2(Xp_1)V_1: an operator of order 0 times V_1; it vanishes for X = V_2.
[±2x_I² Σ Ω_ab², X] = ∓2(X x_I²) Σ Ω_ab², which is ∓4x_I² Σ Ω_ab² for X = V_1, V_2 (as V_1 x_I² = V_2 x_I² = 2x_I²) and
0 for X = Ω_cd. Now x_I² Ω_ab² = x_I (x_I Ω_ab) ∘ Ω_ab with x_I Ω_ab ∈ 𝒱_eb: a first-order eb-operator with coefficient
in x_I C^∞, times Ω_ab. [p_0, X] = −(Xp_0), of order 0 (a term Q_(iJ) X_J). Finally [R̃, X] ∈
C^((d_0;k−1),(2ℓ_I,0))_(eb;b) Diff²_eb, as X is an eb-commutator field and differentiates the coefficients once
(Lemma 14.9 and Lemma 14.27 (b)). 𝒱_eb is spanned over C^∞ by V_1, V_2 and x_I Ω_ab, so every element of
x_I^(2ℓ_I) C^((d_0;k−1))_(eb;b) Diff²_eb is a sum Σ_j A_j X_j with A_j ∈ x_I^(2ℓ_I) C^((d_0;k−1))_(eb;b) Diff¹_eb (for j
a rotation, the factor x_I of x_I Ω_ab joins A_j; the first-order part of the operator is A_J X_J). Collecting,
[L, X_i] = Σ_j Q_(ij) X_j with Q_(ij) as stated. (c) Near ℐ⁺, 𝒱_b is spanned by ρ_+ ∂_(ρ_+), x_I ∂_(x_I) and the vector
fields on 𝕊³, which V_1, V_2 and the Ω_ab span. (d) The principal symbol of a first-order eb-operator with coefficients
in x_I C^∞ + x_I^(2ℓ_I) C^0 vanishes over x_I = 0. ∎

**Proposition 16.25** (The radial sets at ℐ⁺ with b-regularity.) Proposition 16.13 and Proposition 16.14
hold with H^((𝗍;k))_(e3b;b) in place of H^𝗍_e3b for every k ∈ ℕ_0:

    ‖Bu‖_((s;k),(2α_I,α_+)) ≤ C_k (‖GPu‖_((s−1;k),(2α_I+2,α_++2)) + ‖Eu‖_((s;k),(2α_I,α_+))
                                    + ‖χ̃u‖_((s_0;k),(2α_I,α_+))),    (16.42)

with B, E, G having the properties (1)–(4) stated there, in the strong sense, for P = P_0 and P of class ((d_0; k), …)
with ε_(P,k) small, d_0 depending only on s, s_0; and in the tame form (16.40), with ε_(P,k) times the right
side of (16.42) at the order d.

This is the analogue of [Hin26c, Propositions 7.8–7.9] in [Hin26c, Section 7.2.3], in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* Lemma 16.21–Lemma 16.23 with 𝔩 = 0, the family 𝒳_I and Lemma 16.24;
‖GLu‖_((s−1;k),(2α_I,α_+)) and ‖GPu‖_((s−1;k),(2α_I+2,α_++2)) are equivalent up to a microlocal error, W being a weight.
The thresholds ((16.15) and (16.17)) concern the weights only and are unchanged by Lemma 16.24
(d). ∎

### 16.9 The horizon

Near ℋ⁺ ∩ K⁺ = {r = r_h, ρ_K = 0} use the coordinates (t_*, r, ω), ρ_K = t_*⁻¹, with covectors −σ dt_* + ξ_0 dr + η;
W′ = 1 and L = P, as in Proposition 16.9. ∂R_(ℋ⁺) lies in {σ = 0, η = 0} with ξ_0 ≠ 0 (Definition 15.10: it is the
boundary of the conormal bundle of {r = r_h}), so we take U_0 ⊂ {|ξ_0| ≥ c(|σ| + |ξ_0| + |η|)}, a small neighbourhood
of ∂R_(ℋ⁺). The family is 𝒳_ℋ := (∂_r, t_* ∂_(t_*), I).

**Lemma 16.26** (Commutators at the horizon.) (a) (M) holds: 𝒱_b near ℋ⁺ ∩ K⁺ is spanned by 𝒱_3b and t_*
∂_(t_*) (Corollary 14.6); ∂_r ∈ 𝒱_3b is elliptic on Ū_0 (with w = 1); both are e3b-commutator fields
(Lemma 14.5). (b) (C) holds on U_0. (c) The system L^(k) = P ⊗ Id − Q of Lemma 16.19 in the form
(16.35), all letters commuting ([∂_r, t_* ∂_(t_*)] = 0), satisfies, at ∂R_(ℋ⁺),

    ς ρ σ_1(Im(−Q)) = −diag(j_α)_(α∈𝒲_k) β_0 ≤ 0,    (16.43)

with j_α the number of letters 1 (that is, of factors ∂_r) in α, ρ the function of (H3) and β_0 > 0 of
(15.11). So (16.41) holds, and the threshold of Proposition 16.9 for L^(k) is at most ϑ_ℋ.

This is [Hin26c, Lemmas 7.15–7.16] in dimension 4 + 1, with the sign at the horizon calculated from β_0 rather than
from the Kerr formula [Hin26c, (7.48)].

*Proof.* (b) Write P = Σ_l p_l A_l near ℋ⁺ ∩ K⁺, with A_l ∈ Diff²_3b fixed and independent of t_* (products of
∂_(t_*), ∂_r, ∂_ω), and p_l = p^♯_l + p̃_l, p^♯_l the coefficients of P_0, independent of t_*, and p̃_l ∈ ρ_K^(ℓ_K)
C^((d_0;k))_(3b;b) (Definition 15.36). Let Q_r ∈ C_b^∞Ψ^(−1)_3b be a microlocal parametrix of ∂_r on Ū_0: I = Q_r
∂_r + R_r, WF′(R_r) ∩ Ū_0 = ∅.

*The letter X_1 = ∂_r.* [P, ∂_r] is a second-order operator of class 𝒬^2_1. Put Q_11 := [P, ∂_r] Q_r, R_1 := [P,
∂_r] R_r, and Q_(1j) := 0 for j ≠ 1; then [P, ∂_r] = Q_11 ∂_r + R_1. The principal symbol of [P, ∂_r] is (1/i){G,
iξ_0} = H_G ξ_0, as ∂_r has symbol iξ_0. So Q_11 has principal symbol H_G ξ_0/(iξ_0) = −i(H_G ξ_0)/ξ_0, a purely
imaginary scalar, and σ_1(Im(−Q_11)) = (H_G ξ_0)/ξ_0. Its lower-order part (from the first-order part of P, composed
with Q_r) has order 0 and does not enter.

*The letter X_2 = t_* ∂_(t_*).* t_* ∂_(t_*) p^♯_l = 0, and by Lemma 14.5, [t_* ∂_(t_*), A_l] = ρ_K A^♭_l t_*
∂_(t_*) + ρ_K A^♯_l with A^♭_l ∈ Diff¹_3b, A^♯_l ∈ Diff²_3b. Hence

    [P, X_2] = −Σ_l ((X_2 p̃_l) A_l + p_l ρ_K A^♭_l X_2 + p_l ρ_K A^♯_l),

and with I = Q_r ∂_r + R_r on the second-order terms, Q_22 := −Σ_l p_l ρ_K A^♭_l, Q_21 := −Σ_l ((X_2 p̃_l) A_l + p_l
ρ_K A^♯_l) Q_r, R_2 := −Σ_l ((X_2 p̃_l) A_l + p_l ρ_K A^♯_l) R_r. Their coefficients carry a factor ρ_K or ρ_K^(ℓ_K)
(X_2 p̃_l ∈ ρ_K^(ℓ_K) C^((d_0;k−1))_(3b;b)), so they decay at K⁺.

(c) By (b) and (16.35), −Q has, at ∂R_(ℋ⁺) ⊂ {ρ_K = 0}, first-order principal symbol diag(j_α) i(H_(G_0)
ξ_0)/ξ_0: each letter 1 of α couples the component α to itself through Q_11, as α[i→1] = α, and the couplings through
Q_21, Q_22 decay; G = G_0 there. Let ρ̃ := |ξ_0|⁻¹ on U_0 and 𝖧 := ρH_G. Then ρ(H_G ξ_0)/ξ_0 = −ρρ̃⁻¹ H_G ρ̃ = −ρ̃⁻¹𝖧ρ̃.
