ρ_I^(z+1)-term with Re z < 5/2; so, by the last statement of Proposition 29.29 (with C_0 < 5/2), neither λ_♯ nor
any z ∈ π_1ℰ^C_I with Re z < 5/2 enters its ℰ^♯_+. The solution u′_(λ_0) vanishes on {t_* < 1} ∪ {ρ_I > ½c_I}, has
the ℐ⁺-data (⟨ℰ^C_I⟩, ℓ_I), and its ι⁺-exponents below α^♯_+ lie in λ_0 + ℰ^ι_ind + (0, k). The new error has the
plain ℐ⁺-weight ℓ_I + 1 and ι⁺-exponents below α^♯_+ + 2 in λ_0 + 2 + ℰ^ι_ind + (0, k), with real parts
≥ Re λ_0 + 2 + ε^ι_ind; near K⁺ it is the error of Corollary 26.44, of K⁺-weight c_K − ε, as u′_(λ_0) vanishes
there.

Replacing F by F − L_b(u_(λ_0) + u′_(λ_0)) for all λ_0 of the window raises c_0 by at least ε^ι_ind (the terms of F
above the window are untouched), keeps the plain ℐ⁺-weight ℓ_I + 1 and the K⁺-weight α̃_K (c_K − ε > α̃_K), and the
exponents that occur lie in ℰ^♯_+ + ℕ₀ℰ^ι_ind, an index set with finitely many elements below 2, none of real part
α^♯_+ by (31.35). So after finitely many rounds (c_0 < α^♯_+ < 2, starting at c_0 ≥ λ_♯) no ι⁺-term below
α^♯_+ + 2 is left. Let u_ι be the sum of the u_(λ_0) and u′_(λ_0). By inclusion (a),
u_ι ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),λ_♯−ε,0)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−), and

    u^♭ := u − u_I − u_ι :     L_b u^♭ = f^♭ := f^♭_0 − L_b u_ι ∈ H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,α^♯_++2,α̃_K)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−),
    (31.37)

and u^♭, which vanishes for t_* < 1, is the forward solution (Proposition 17.14).

*Step 3* (spectral; [Hin26, Step 3]). (31.37) is the right-hand side f^♭ of Step 1 of the proof of
Proposition 31.6 with α̃_K in place of α_K, and Steps 2–3 of that proof apply with (α^♯_+, α̃_K). They use α_K
only through the following, each of which holds for α^♯_+, α̃_K ∈ (1, 2) with α^♯_+ > α̃_K.

(i) Proposition 20.18 (1) and Proposition 20.20 (1) with β_K = α̃_K ∈ (1, 2) ∖ ℕ and one Taylor coefficient (of
order 0 < α̃_K − 1 < 1), and Lemma 29.32 with β_K = α̃_K ∈ (1, 2) ∖ ℕ and ℓ_I ≥ α^♯_+ + ε_1,
ε_1 := 2 − α^♯_+.

(ii) Proposition 28.8 at the weight α^♯_+ − 3 (α^♯_+ − 1 ∈ (0, 1)), and Lemma 29.33 at the weight α of
(28.1) with α + 2 = α^♯_+ − α̃_K ∈ (0, 1).

(iii) In (31.7), the column terms (N, 3 − ε, 1 − ε) and the commutator term lie in
(5/2 − ε, α^♯_+ + 1, α̃_K − 1), as α^♯_+ < 2 − ε and α̃_K − 1 < 1 − ε for ε small; and the third term of
(31.7) is taken by Lemma 31.4 (a) with γ_zf ∈ (α̃_K − 1, 1).

(iv) In Step 3.3, the tf-weights α̃_K + 1 − ε and α̃_K + 2 − ε of the remainders exceed 2 − ε and 3 − ε, and
1 − ε > α̃_K − 1; in the first integration, Lemma 29.31 applies with β_K := α̃_K − 1 ∈ (0, 1) ⊂ (−1, 1) ∖ {0},
β_K ≤ α^♯_+ − 1/2, and the tf-weight 3 − ε ≥ α^♯_+ + 1; in the second, Lemma 29.30 (1) applies with the
K⁺-weight α̃_K − 2 ∈ (−1, 0), which is not 0, and ℰ_K = {(−1, 0)}.

(v) In Step 3.4, the integrability, which needs α̃_K > 1.

So u^♭ = u_hi + u_reg + u_sing with ((31.9), (31.13), (31.14))

    u^♭ − χ^H_K t_* h_b(S_0) ∈ H^(∞,min(3/2,α^♯_+)−3ε,min(3/2,α^♯_+)−4ε,α̃_K−2)_b(M′),

S_0 being the 𝒮_1-component of L̃_b(0)⁻¹(f̂^♭(0), 0, 0) and χ^H_K the cut-off of Proposition 31.6 (which is harmless
here, as S_0 = 0 below). u_I and u_ι have the K⁺-weights ∞ and 0, and u has the K⁺-weight α′_K − 2 > −1 by
(31.34); so the coefficient h_b(S_0) of t_* in u at K⁺ vanishes, and S_0 = 0 (Lemma 31.2). As in
Step 3.4 of the proof of Proposition 31.6, replacing t_* h_b by h^(≤1)_b costs nothing.

*Step 4* (null infinity). u = u_I + u_ι + u^♭ has the ι⁺-weight
ℓ′_+ := min(3/2, α^♯_+, λ_♯) − 4ε = min(3/2, α^♯_+) − 4ε and the K⁺-weight α̃_K − 2. Proposition 29.27 with
ℓ_+ := min(ℓ′_+, min Re ℰ_+ − ε) (so ℓ_+ ∉ Re π_1ℰ_+), exactly as in Step 4 of the proof of Proposition 31.6 (near
ℐ⁺, Lu = f), gives the ℐ⁺-data (⟨ℰ^C_I⟩, ℓ_I). So (31.34) holds with (α̃_K,
min(ℓ′_+, min Re ℰ_+ − ε)) in place of (α′_K, β′_+), and, ε being arbitrary and α^♯_+ ≥ min(α_+, 3/2) − ε, with any
β′_+ < min(α_+, 3/2, min Re ℰ_+).

*Conclusion.* Each round raises α′_K to min(α′_K + a_K − 2, α_K), with a_K > 2, so finitely many rounds reach α_K;
this is (31.33). The growth: the K⁺-weight α_K − 2 and b-Sobolev embedding give |u| ≲ t_*^(2−α_K) in compact
spatial sets. *Continuity:* every map of the rounds is linear and bounded between the spaces above
(Proposition 31.16 (1), (29.15), Proposition 29.27, Proposition 29.29, Corollary 26.44, and Steps
2–3 of the proof of Proposition 31.6 with their continuity paragraph), with bounds uniform in b ∈ ℬ̄_* by
(BP1)–(BP5). ∎

In [Hin26], Step 2 begins at λ = 1, where ℰ^♯_+ ∋ (1, 0) forces [Hin26, Proposition 9.11] at λ = 1 and a logarithm
in a_s1; in dimension 4 + 1 the least exponent is λ_♯ > 3/2, and a_s1 is a power. Step 3 of [Hin26] needs the
expansion [Hin26, (11.107b)] of û_(reg,1)(0) over the indicial roots in (0, α_+ − 1], [Hin26, Lemma 11.33] for the
columns, and its Step 3.2, because its relative tf–zf order 1 + min Re ℰ_ind is below 2. Here none is needed: the
relative tf–zf order of the remainder, α^♯_+ − α̃_K + 2, lies in (2, 3) throughout. The step at ι⁺ is needed only
when α^♯_+ ≥ λ_♯, which is why Proposition 31.6, with α_K < 3/2, omits it; and since re-solving at null infinity
creates no new exponent below 5/2 (the last statement of Proposition 29.29), the iteration ends.

### 31.10 Extraction of the parameters: the setting and four lemmas

This section and the next are [Hin26, Section 11.6.1] in dimension 4 + 1: for right-hand sides with a little more
than t_*^(−2) decay at K⁺, a forward solution with no boost term is a cut-off linearised Myers–Perry metric, a cut-off
constant centre-of-mass shift, and a remainder that decays at K⁺ ([Hin26, Proposition 11.34]). The scheme is that of
[Hin26]: the steps at null infinity and at ι⁺, the zero energy inversion, a sub-leading zero energy inversion after
one order is gained at tf, the rest by the low-energy estimate, and one integration in t_*. Three things differ.
There is no logarithmic centre-of-mass term: in [Hin26] it comes from the exponent (1, 0) at ι⁺ ([Hin26, Proposition
9.11] at λ = 1, where a_s1 is a logarithm), while here the ι⁺-exponents begin at λ_♯ and give centre-of-mass motions
t_*^(−λ+1) that decay. At zero energy the step of [Hin26, Proposition 9.30] is not needed; the tf-improvement of
[Hin26, Proposition 9.35] is, and it is Proposition 27.58, because the first moment ∫ t_* f^♭ dt_* has the
borderline weight 2. And that proposition's solution has a term |σ|^(α−3)h_b(S), singular at zf, which the rows of the
augmented operator see; it is moved into the 𝒮_1-column exactly (Lemma 31.26).

L = L_(h,S), χ_K, ℓ_I (with (31.32)), λ_♯ and (31.31) are as in Section 31.8, at b ∈ ℬ̄_*.
On the spectral side, L̂_b(σ) = L_0 − iσL_1 − σ²L_2 with L_0 = L̂_b(0), L_1 = [L_b, t_*] and L_2 = ½[[L_b, t_*], t_*]
stationary (Section 28.1); near ∂X̄, L_1 ∈ ρ Diff¹_b and L_2 ∈ ρ²C^∞ ⊂ C^∞ (Cartesian derivatives lie in ρ𝒱_b, and
L_2 is of order 0). L̃_b(σ) is the augmented operator of Definition 28.7, with the rows
r(u) := (⟨u, f*_1⟩, ⟨u, f*_2⟩), f*_j ∈ C^∞_c(X°) normalised at b₀ by (28.9), their matrix B(b) on the states
at b being invertible on ℬ̄_* ((31.1), Lemma 31.1), and the columns
f̂_ḃ(σ) = L̂_b(σ)ĝ^aug(σ)(ḃ) and f̂_S(σ) = L̂_b(σ)ĥ^aug(σ)(S) (Lemma 28.5 (c)), where

    ĝ^aug(σ)(ḃ) = iσ⁻¹Ψ ġ_b(ḃ),        ĥ^aug(σ)(S) = ∂_σ(σ⁻¹Ψ) h_b(S) + iσ⁻¹Ψ h̆_b(S)    (31.38)

((28.8)), Ψ(σ, x) = Φ(σr) for r ≥ 1 with Φ(0) = 1 (Lemma 28.5 (b)), and ġ_b, h_b, h̆_b are the states
of (BP3). Then G_1(σ)(ḃ) = Ψġ_b(ḃ) = −iσĝ^aug(σ)(ḃ) and G_2(σ)(S) = (Ψ − σ∂_σΨ)h_b(S) − iσΨh̆_b(S) =
−σ²ĥ^aug(σ)(S) are the functions of Lemma 31.5. The constant c and the cut-off χ are fixed for each order k as
in Section 29.18, and the memberships of the spectral pieces below hold at order k for that c.

*Expansions at zf to first order.* For γ ∈ (1, 2), H^(k,(β_scf,β_tf,((0,0),γ)))_b(X^±_(sc-b)) is the space of
χ_zf v_0 + σχ_zf v_1 + ṽ with v_0 ∈ H^(k,β_tf)_b(X), v_1 ∈ H^(k,β_tf−1)_b(X) and ṽ ∈ H^(k,(β_scf,β_tf,γ))_b: the
space of Section 20.8.1 with the index set (0, 0) at zf, written with σ in place of powers of r̂; v_0 and v_1 are
the σ-Taylor coefficients of Proposition 20.18 (1).

**Lemma 31.23** (First-order expansions.) Let a ∈ (0, 1) and u_0 ∈ H^(∞,a)_b(X).

(a) (L̂_b(σ) − L_0)(χ_zf u_0) = −iσχ_zf L_1u_0 + R, with L_1u_0 ∈ H^(∞,a+1)_b(X) and R ∈ H^(∞,(∞,a+2,γ))_b for every
γ < 2.

(b) For the columns f of Lemma 28.2 (f = f_ḃ or f_S), f̂(σ) − χ_zf(f̂(0) + σf̂′(0)) ∈ H^(∞,(N,3−ε,2−ε))_b for all
N and ε > 0, with f̂′(0) := ∂_σ f̂(0) = i∫ t_* f dt_* ∈ H^(∞,2−ε)_b(X).

*Proof.* (a) (L̂_b(σ) − L_0)(χ_zf u_0) = −iσχ_zf L_1u_0 − iσ[L_1, χ_zf]u_0 − σ²χ_zf L_2u_0. By Lemma 31.3 (b)
(P = L_1, p = 1), σ[L_1, χ_zf]u_0 ∈ H^(∞,(∞,a+2,∞))_b, the factor σ adding 1 at tf and at zf; by
Lemma 31.3 (a) (P = L_2, p = 0, j = 2), σ²χ_zf L_2u_0 ∈ H^(∞,(∞,a+2,γ))_b for γ < 2.

(b) By Lemma 28.4 (a), f̂ = f̂_c + f̂_∞, with f̂_c entire in σ and supported in {r ≤ 2}, where χ_zf = 1
for |σ| ≤ c (Section 31.2); so its Taylor remainder is O(σ²) in C^∞, which gives the zf-weight 2 − ε and no condition
at tf or scf. And f̂_∞ = r⁻³G(σr, x) on {r ≥ 1}, with G entire and |(ζ∂_ζ)^j(r∂_r)^i∂^β_ω G| ≤ C⟨ζ⟩^(−N). With
ζ := σr, so that |ζ| ∼ r̂ on {r ≥ 1}, the function r⁻³(G(ζ, x) − χ_1(r̂)(G(0, x) + ζ∂_ζG(0, x))) is r⁻³ times a
function that is O(r̂²) for r̂ ≤ 1/8 and O(⟨r̂⟩^(−N) + r̂ 1_(r̂≤1/4)) beyond, with the same derivative bounds. In the
Fubini count of the proof of Lemma 31.4 (b) (ρ_zf ∼ r̂ and ρ_tf ∼ r⁻¹ near zf, ρ_scf ∼ r̂⁻¹ near scf) this gives
the weights (N, 3 − ε, 2 − ε): the remainder O(r̂²) contributes ∫_0^(1/⟨x⟩) σ^(4−2γ_zf) dσ/σ, finite for γ_zf < 2, where
the remainder O(r̂) gave 1 − ε. f̂′(0) = ∂_σ f̂_c(0) + r⁻²∂_ζG(0, x) is smooth and lies in 𝒜² ⊂ H^(∞,2−ε)_b near ∂X̄. ∎

**Lemma 31.24** (Conormal sections are admissible.) Let σ ∈ ℝ ∖ 0 be small and let v be smooth on X° and
b-conormal at ∂X̄ of μ_b-weight a. Then v lies in the space 𝒳′_σ, built as 𝒳_σ but with an admissible order family
(Section 11.7) lowered near R_out, the zero section over ∂X̄ ((11.17)), and unchanged near R_in. Moreover
𝒳′_σ ⊃ 𝒳_σ and 𝒴′_σ ⊃ 𝒴_σ, and on 𝒴_σ the inverses of L̂_b(σ), and of L̃_b(σ), on the two spaces agree.

*Proof.* Every part of L̂_b(σ) maps 𝒜^a into 𝒜^(a+1) (the proof of Theorem 11.33 (5)), so L̂_b(σ)v ∈ 𝒜^(a+1).
R_out lies in the characteristic set, and the admissibility conditions there ask the order to be constant near R_out
and below a threshold ((O2)–(O3) of Section 11.7). So 𝗋′ := 𝗋 − φ, with φ ≥ 0 constant near R_out, zero near R_in and
nondecreasing along the flow (the construction of Lemma 11.32 with a smaller value at R_out), is admissible, and φ
can be taken with 𝗋′ + α_+ < a − 2 near R_out. By Lemma 11.37 (a), v ∈ H̄^(s,𝗋′+α_+) and
L̂_b(σ)v ∈ 𝒜^(a+1) ⊂ H̄^(s−1,𝗋′+α_++1) for every s, so v ∈ 𝒳′_σ; the inclusions hold as 𝗋′ ≤ 𝗋. L̂_b(σ) is Fredholm of
index 0 on both spaces (Section 28.1, (H1)–(H5) at σ ≠ 0), and its kernel does not depend on the admissible order:
by Theorem 11.33 (5) and its proof a kernel element lies in ⋂_ε 𝒜^(3/2+S̄−ε), and such sections lie in every
admissible space. So it is injective on 𝒳′_σ as on 𝒳_σ (Corollary 28.13), hence invertible on both, and the
inverses agree on 𝒴_σ. L̃_b(σ) is a finite-rank augmentation of it with as many rows as columns, so it is Fredholm of
index 0 on both spaces. If (u, ḃ, S) lies in its kernel on the larger one, then
L̂_b(σ)(u + ĝ^aug(σ)(ḃ) + ĥ^aug(σ)(S)) = 0, so u = −ĝ^aug(σ)(ḃ) − ĥ^aug(σ)(S) ∈ 𝒳_σ (Lemma 28.5 (b)), and
(u, ḃ, S) lies in the kernel on 𝒳_σ, which is trivial for |σ| small (Theorem 28.10). So L̃_b(σ) is invertible on
both spaces, and the inverses agree. ∎

**Lemma 31.25** (Row data.) For e = (e_1, e_2) ∈ 𝔟_ℂ ⊕ 𝒮_(1,ℂ) put e′ = (e′_1, e′_2) := B(b)⁻¹e, with
B(b) the matrix (31.1) of the rows on the states, and w_e := χ_zf(ġ_b(e′_1) + h_b(e′_2)). Then r(w_e) = e,
and for 0 < |σ| ≤ c

    L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(0, e) = (w_e, 0, 0) − L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(L̂_b(σ)w_e, 0, 0),

whose 𝔟- and 𝒮_1-components are O(|σ|^(1−ε)) and whose first component lies in H^(∞,(3/2−ε,1−ε,0))_b, uniformly
for |e| ≤ 1 and b ∈ ℬ̄_*, for every ε > 0.

*Proof.* χ_zf = 1 on supp f*_j for |σ| ≤ c (Section 31.2), so r(w_e) = r(ġ_b(e′_1) + h_b(e′_2)) = B(b)e′ = e by
(31.1). w_e has compact support for σ ≠ 0, so it lies in 𝒳_σ, and L̃_b(σ)(w_e, 0, 0) = (L̂_b(σ)w_e, e), which
is the identity. For |e| ≤ 1, |e′| ≤ |B(b)⁻¹| ≤ 2 (Lemma 31.1), so ġ_b(e′_1) + h_b(e′_2) ∈ 𝒜² ⊂ H^(∞,2−ε)_b(X),
with seminorms at most 2 times those of the states, which are bounded uniformly on ℬ̄_* ((BP3)). It lies in the
kernel of L_0, so L̂_b(σ)w_e = [L_0, χ_zf](ġ_b(e′_1) + h_b(e′_2)) + (L̂_b(σ) − L_0)(χ_zf(ġ_b(e′_1) + h_b(e′_2))) lies
in H^(∞,(∞,4−ε,γ))_b for γ < 1 (Lemma 31.3 (b) and Lemma 31.4 (a), with a = 2 − ε), with norms bounded
uniformly for |e| ≤ 1 and b ∈ ℬ̄_*. Lemma 29.33 with β_scf := 3/2 − ε, β_zf := 1 − 2ε and β_tf := 1 − ε
(α + 2 = ε ∈ (0, 1)), whose constants are uniform in b (Proposition 30.5), gives the claim; w_e itself has the
zf-weight 0 and the tf-weight 2 − ε. ∎

At σ = 0 the identity reads L̃_b(0)⁻¹(0, e) = (ġ_b(e′_1) + h_b(e′_2), 0, 0), e′ = B(b)⁻¹e: row data are answered by
the nullspace, with no column. At b₀, B(b₀) = I and e′ = e.

**Lemma 31.26** (The boost-type term of Proposition 27.58.) Let α ∈ (1, 2),
S′ ∈ H^(∞,0)_b(±[0, 1)_σ, |dσ/σ|; 𝒮_1), and Σ(σ) := −σ²|σ|^(α−3)S′(σ). Let h^(≤3)_(b,s1)(σ, S) =
h_b(S) − iσh̆^(≤3)_(b,s1)(σ, S) be the state of Proposition 27.58. Then on {r ≤ R}, for each R,

    χ_zf h^(≤3)_(b,s1)(σ, |σ|^(α−3)S′(σ)) − ĥ^aug(σ)(Σ(σ)) = O(|σ|^(α−2))    in C^∞,    (31.39)

and near zf the difference has the zf-weight α − 2. ĥ^aug(σ)(Σ(σ)) has the tf-weight α − ε for every ε > 0 (b-Sobolev
embedding, and Lemma 29.34 with a = α − 3) and decays rapidly at scf.

*Proof.* By (31.38), ĥ^aug(σ)(Σ) = |σ|^(α−3)(Ψh_b(S′) − σ∂_σΨ h_b(S′) − iσΨh̆_b(S′)). The difference
is |σ|^(α−3)(1 − Ψ)h_b(S′) plus σ|σ|^(α−3) times bounded terms. Near zf ∩ tf the term
σ|σ|^(α−3)χ_zf h̆^(≤3)_(b,s1)(σ, S′) is controlled by Lemma 27.54 (h̆^(≤3)_(b,s1) is polyhomogeneous at tf with
the index set (0, 0) ∪ ℰ_ind), which gives it the zf- and tf-weight α − 2. On {r ≤ R}, |Ψ − 1| ≤ C|σ|
and |∂_σΨ| ≤ C (Lemma 28.5 (d)), with derivatives. For r ≥ 1, 1 − Ψ = 1 − Φ(σr) = O(|σ|r) and h_b(S′) ∈ 𝒜³,
so |σ|^(α−3)(1 − Ψ)h_b(S′) is |σ|^(α−2) times O(r⁻²) near zf. At tf
(σr ∼ 1), |σ|^(α−3)Φ(σr)r⁻³ ∼ |σ|^α, the tf-weight α − ε in H_b; at scf, Φ decays rapidly. ∎

### 31.11 Extraction of the parameters

**Proposition 31.27** (Extraction of the parameters; [Hin26, Proposition 11.34] in dimension 4 + 1.) Let
b ∈ ℬ̄_*, α_K ∈ (2, min(a_K, 2 + ε_ind, 5/2)), with ε_ind that of Proposition 27.58, and let
f ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′,ℓ_I+1),4−ε,α_K)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−) be real, with Ṡ(f) = 0 (Proposition 31.16 (1)).
Then the forward solution of Lu = f is

    u = χ_K ġ_b(ḃ) + χ_K h_b(Ṡ^(0)_1) + ũ,       ḃ ∈ 𝔟,   Ṡ^(0)_1 ∈ 𝒮_1,
    ũ ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β_+,α_K−2)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−)    (31.40)

for every β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+), with ḃ, Ṡ^(0)_1 and ũ depending continuously on f, uniformly in b. ũ decays at
K⁺, as α_K − 2 > 0.

[Hin26, (11.117)] has a third term χ_K h^(≤4)_(b,s1)(Ṡ^((0,1))_1 log t_*), the logarithmic centre-of-mass motion,
the ι⁺-weight 1 − ε, and α_K ∈ (2, 2 + ε_K) with ε_K < ε_ind. The cap 5/2 here is used only in Steps 1–2, through
c_K < λ_♯ + 1. [Hin26, (11.116)] also has a second class f_2 with the ι⁺-index set ℰ̃_+ + 2; in dimension 4 + 1 the
terms of that kind have ι⁺-order 4, so one class suffices, as in Proposition 31.21.

*Proof.* *Step 0* (the start). Proposition 31.21 (with any α_+ ∈ (α′_K, 2); f has the ι⁺-weight 4 − ε) gives
u ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β′_+,α′_K−2)_b for every α′_K < 2 and β′_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+). Fix
α′_K ∈ (max(1, α_K + 2 − a_K), 2), possible as α_K < a_K, and β′_+ ∈ (1, min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+)). (29.15) of
Proposition 29.12 gives (L − L_b)u the ι⁺-weight β′_+ + 2 + m_+ − ε ≥ 4 − ε (β′_+ + m_+ > 2) and the K⁺-weight
α′_K − 2 + a_K > α_K, so

    L_b u = f′ := f − (L − L_b)u ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′,ℓ_I+1),4−ε,α_K)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−).

*Steps 1–2* (null infinity and ι⁺; [Hin26, (11.118)–(11.120)]). Steps 1–2 of the proof of Proposition 31.21 apply
with α^♯_+ := 2 − ε (ε small, and 2 − ε off the excluded set of (31.35), which is finite below 2), with the
K⁺-weight α_K in place of α̃_K, and with c_K ∈ (α_K, λ_♯ + 1), off the finitely many excluded values; this interval is
nonempty, as α_K < 5/2 < λ_♯ + 1. Then ℓ_K(λ_0) = c_K − Re λ_0 ∈ (c_K − 2, 1), and the errors of Corollary 26.44
have the K⁺-weight c_K − ε > α_K, so the right-hand side keeps the K⁺-weight α_K, and each u_(λ_0) has the K⁺-weight
min(Re λ_0 − 1, ℓ_K(λ_0)) − ε ≥ c′_K := min(λ_♯ − 1, c_K − 2) − ε > α_K − 2 for
ε < min(c_K − α_K, λ_♯ + 1 − α_K). This gives u_I, u_ι ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),λ_♯−ε,c′_K)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−) (u_I supported
near ℐ⁺) and

    u^♭ := u − u_I − u_ι :     L_b u^♭ = f^♭ ∈ H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,4−ε,α_K)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−),    (31.41)

u^♭ being the forward solution (Proposition 17.14). From here on ε > 0 is fixed, small as above. The parameters ḃ,
Ṡ^(0)_1 found below are determined by the (0, 0)-coefficient ġ_b(ḃ) + h_b(Ṡ^(0)_1) of u at K⁺, its limit as t_* → ∞
in compact spatial sets, as ũ tends to 0 there (Lemma 31.2); so they and ũ do not depend on ε, and
(31.40) holds for every β_+. There is no logarithmic term: the least ι⁺-exponent is λ_♯, and the coefficient
a_s1 = (λ_0(λ_0 − 1))⁻¹t_*^(−λ_0+1) of (26.54) is a power for Re λ_0 > 1.

*Step 3* (the decomposition). As in Section 29.18, u^♭ = u_hi + u_reg + u_sing, with
(û_1, b̂_1, Ŝ_1) := L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(f̂^♭(σ), 0, 0), ℱu_reg = χ(|σ|)û_1, and

    ℱ(∂_(t_*)u_sing) = χ(|σ|)(G_1(σ)(b̂_1) + iσ⁻¹G_2(σ)(Ŝ_1))      for σ ≠ 0

((29.40); ∂²_(t_*) corresponds to −σ²). Lemma 29.32 (β^f_I = ℓ_I, β_ι = 2 − ε,
β_K = α_K ∈ (2, 3); ℓ_I + 1 ≥ 4 − ε − (1 − ε_1) as ℓ_I ≥ 2, with ε_1 ≤ ε) gives u_hi ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−ε,N,N))_b(M′).
Proposition 20.18 (1) (β_K = α_K ∈ (2, 3)) gives

    f̂^♭|_(±(0,c]) ∈ H^(∞,(3−2ε,3−ε,((0,0),α_K−1)))_b,        f̂^♭ = χ_zf f̂^♭(0) + σχ_zf f̂^♭_1 + ⋯,    (31.42)

with f̂^♭(0) = ∫ f^♭ dt_* ∈ H^(∞,3−ε)_b(X) and f̂^♭_1 = i∫ t_* f^♭ dt_* ∈ H^(∞,2−ε)_b(X), the same for both signs.

*Step 3.1* (zero energy; [Hin26, (11.123)]). Proposition 28.8 at the weight with α + 2 = 1 − ε (𝒴_0 has the
μ_b-weight 3 − ε, as in Step 3.1 of the proof of Proposition 31.6) gives (û_0, ḃ_0, S_0) :=
L̃_b(0)⁻¹(f̂^♭(0), 0, 0) with û_0 ∈ H^(∞,1−ε)_b(X). Here S_0 = 0. Indeed, f^♭ lies in the space of Step 3 of the proof
of Proposition 31.21 for every α̃_K < 2 and α^♯_+ < 2 − ε, and the inverses of Proposition 28.8 at the weights
1 − ε and α^♯_+ − 1 ≤ 1 − ε agree on f̂^♭(0) (the spaces are nested and both operators invertible). So that Step gives
u^♭ − χ^H_K t_* h_b(S_0) the K⁺-weight α̃_K − 2 > −1; and u, u_I, u_ι have K⁺-weights > −1. So h_b(S_0) = 0, and
S_0 = 0 (Lemma 31.2). As in (31.6), L̃_b(σ)(χ_zf û_0, ḃ_0, 0) = (f̂^♭(σ) − f̂_2(σ), 0, 0) with

    f̂_2 := (f̂^♭ − χ_zf f̂^♭(0)) − [L_0, χ_zf]û_0 − (L̂_b(σ) − L_0)(χ_zf û_0) − (f̂_(ḃ_0)(σ) − χ_zf f̂_(ḃ_0)(0)).

By (31.42), Lemma 31.3 (b) ([L_0, χ_zf]û_0 ∈ H^(∞,(∞,3−ε,∞))_b) and Lemma 31.23 (a)–(b),

    f̂_2 = σχ_zf F_1 + R_2,     F_1 := f̂^♭_1 + iL_1û_0 − f̂′_(ḃ_0)(0) ∈ H^(∞,2−ε)_b(X),
    R_2 ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,3−ε,α_K−1))_b,    (31.43)

F_1 being the same for both signs; the zf-weights of the remainders, α_K − 1, γ < 2 and 2 − ε, are at least α_K − 1,
as α_K < 3 − ε.

*Step 3.2* (one order at tf; [Hin26, (11.124)–(11.126)]). Put g̃ := σ⁻¹f̂_2. As |σ| = ρ_tf ρ_zf,
g̃ ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,2−ε,((0,0),α_K−2)))_b, with zf-coefficient F_1. Its tf-weight 2 − ε is too low for
Proposition 28.8 at the next order, which would need α + 2 = −ε. Proposition 27.58 on X^±_(sc-b) separately, with
α := 2 − ε, ℓ_scf := 3/2 − ε, ℓ_zf := α_K − 2 ∉ ℕ₀, k_0 := 0 and w = α_K − 2 + ε ∈ (−ε_ind, ℓ^max_K) (ε chosen with w
and every ε + j, j ∈ ℕ₀, off the set of the −μ, which is real and discrete), gives û_3^± = χ_zf u_b + χ^♯_tf ũ in
H^(∞,(3/2−2ε,−ε,−1−ε))_b with

    f̂_4 := g̃ − L̂_b(σ)û_3 ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,2+ε_ind−2ε,((0,0),α_K−2)))_b,    (31.44)

with zf-coefficients F_4^± ∈ H^(∞,2+ε_ind−2ε)_b(X), possibly different for the two signs. In u_b
((27.56)) the term h^(≤3)_(b,s1)(σ, |σ|^(α−3)S′(σ)), S′ := S^(−1)_1, is the only one of zf-weight below
α − 2; the others carry |σ|^(α−2) or |σ|^(α−2−μ), μ ≤ 0. With Σ_3 := −σ²|σ|^(α−3)S′ of Lemma 31.26 put

    û′_3 := û_3 − ĥ^aug(σ)(Σ_3) :     L̂_b(σ)û′_3 + f̂_(Σ_3)(σ) = L̂_b(σ)û_3    (31.45)

(Lemma 28.5 (c)). By Lemma 31.26, û′_3 ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−2ε,−ε,−ε))_b near zf and tf (χ^♯_tf vanishes near
zf, and the difference in Lemma 31.26 has the zf-weight α − 2), and r(û′_3) = O(|σ|^(−ε)) (on supp f*_j, by
(31.39) and the factor |σ|^(α−2) of the other terms of u_b). Σ_3 = O(|σ|^(1−ε)).

*Step 3.3* (the sub-leading zero energy piece; [Hin26, Step 4]). Proposition 28.8 at the weight with
α + 2 = ε_ind − 2ε ∈ (0, 1) (ε < ½ε_ind) gives (û_4, b̂_4, Ŝ_4)^± := L̃_b(0)⁻¹(F_4^±, 0, 0), with
û_4 ∈ H^(∞,ε_ind−2ε)_b(X). As in Step 3.1 (with Lemma 31.3 and Lemma 31.4 (a), (b) there, for the
zf-weight γ < 1 and the columns (N, 3 − ε, 1 − ε)),

    f̂_5 := f̂_4 − L̂_b(σ)(χ_zf û_4) − f̂_(b̂_4)(σ) − f̂_(Ŝ_4)(σ) ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,2+ε_ind−2ε,α_K−2))_b,    (31.46)

the zf-coefficient cancelling by the choice of (û_4, b̂_4, Ŝ_4), and r(χ_zf û_4) = r(û_4) = 0.

*Step 3.4* (the rest; [Hin26, Step 5]). Lemma 29.33 with β_scf := 3/2 − 2ε, β_tf := ε_ind − 2ε,
β_zf := α_K − 2 and α + 2 := β_tf − β_zf ∈ (0, 1) (α_K − 2 < ε_ind − 2ε for ε small) gives (û_5, b̂_5, Ŝ_5) :=
L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(f̂_5, 0, 0) with û_5 ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−3ε,ε_ind−2ε,α_K−2))_b and b̂_5, Ŝ_5 ∈ H^(∞,α_K−2)_b(±(0, c], |dσ/σ|).

*Step 3.5* (assembly). For 0 < ±σ ≤ c let (U_r, B_r, Σ_r) := L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(0, σr(û′_3)). Then

    (û_1, b̂_1, Ŝ_1) = (χ_zf û_0, ḃ_0, 0) + σ[(û′_3, 0, Σ_3) + (χ_zf û_4, b̂_4, Ŝ_4) + (û_5, b̂_5, Ŝ_5)]
                       − (U_r, B_r, Σ_r).    (31.47)

Indeed, apply L̃_b(σ) to the right side. By the definitions of f̂_2, g̃, f̂_4 and f̂_5, by (31.45), and as
the first component of L̃_b(σ)(û_5, b̂_5, Ŝ_5) = (f̂_5, 0, 0) is f̂_5, the first components add up to

    (f̂^♭ − f̂_2) + (f̂_2 − σf̂_4) + σ(f̂_4 − f̂_5) + σf̂_5 = f̂^♭;

the rows give 0 + σ(r(û′_3) + 0 + 0) − σr(û′_3) = 0. Every first component lies in the space 𝒳′_σ of
Lemma 31.24, which contains 𝒳_σ: χ_zf û_0, χ_zf û_4 and χ_zf u_b have compact support for σ ≠ 0; ĥ^aug lies
there by Lemma 28.5 (b); û_5 and U_r by construction; and χ^♯_tf ũ by Lemma 31.24, being b-conormal of
weight 3/2 − 2ε at ∂X̄. So (31.47) follows from the injectivity of L̃_b(σ) (Lemma 31.24).

The row term is bounded by Lemma 31.25 at b. Let E_1, …, E_11 be the basis of 𝔟_ℂ ⊕ 𝒮_(1,ℂ) fixed in
Lemma 31.1, and write σr(û′_3(σ)) = Σ_k e_k(σ)E_k. Then

    (U_r, B_r, Σ_r) = Σ_k e_k(σ) L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(0, E_k),

and the coefficients e_k(σ) are O(|σ|^(1−ε)) with σ∂_σ-regularity, as r(û′_3) = O(|σ|^(−ε)) (Step 3.2). For each k,
Lemma 31.25 with e = E_k (so e′ = B(b)⁻¹E_k, |e′| ≤ 2 by Lemma 31.1) bounds the 𝔟- and 𝒮_1-components of
L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(0, E_k) by O(|σ|^(1−ε)) and puts its first component in H^(∞,(3/2−ε,1−ε,0))_b, uniformly in b ∈ ℬ̄_*. So
B_r, Σ_r = O(|σ|^(1−ε)) · O(|σ|^(1−ε)) = O(|σ|^(2−2ε)), and, multiplication by e_k(σ) adding 1 − ε to the tf- and
zf-weights (|σ| = ρ_tf ρ_zf), U_r ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−ε,2−2ε,1−ε))_b ⊂ H^(∞,(3/2−ε,2−2ε,1−2ε))_b, uniformly in b ∈ ℬ̄_*.

Consequently, with all weights for ε small,

    û_1 ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−3ε,1−2ε,((0,0),α_K−2)))_b with zf-coefficient û_0,
    b̂_1 − ḃ_0,  σ⁻¹Ŝ_1 − Ŝ_4^± ∈ H^(∞,α_K−2)_b(±(0, c], |dσ/σ|),    (31.48)

since σû′_3, σχ_zf û_4, σû_5 and U_r have the zf-weight at least 1 − 2ε > α_K − 2 and the tf-weight at least 1 − 2ε,
σ(b̂_4 + b̂_5) − B_r = O(|σ|) (B_r = O(|σ|^(2−2ε)) and ε ≤ 1/2), and σ⁻¹Ŝ_1 − Ŝ_4 = Σ_3 + Ŝ_5 − σ⁻¹Σ_r =
O(|σ|^(α_K−2)) with σ∂_σ-regularity (Σ_3 = O(|σ|^(1−ε)), Ŝ_5 ∈ H^(∞,α_K−2)_b and σ⁻¹Σ_r = O(|σ|^(1−2ε)), with
α_K − 2 < 1/2 < 1 − 2ε). These bounds are uniform in b ∈ ℬ̄_*, as those of the row term are.

*Step 4* (the regular part). By Proposition 20.20 (1) with β_K := α_K − 1 ∈ (1, 2), the one Taylor coefficient (of
order 0 < α_K − 2) being û_0 for both signs, u_reg ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−4ε,2−2ε,α_K−1))_b(M′).

*Step 5* (the singular part; [Hin26, (11.130)–(11.133)]). By (31.48), Lemma 31.5 (for
G_1(σ)(ḃ_0) and G_2(σ)(Ŝ_4^±)) and Lemma 29.34 with a = α_K − 2 (for G_1(σ)(b̂_1 − ḃ_0) and
G_2(σ)(σ⁻¹Ŝ_1 − Ŝ_4)),

    ℱ(∂_(t_*)u_sing) = χ(G_1(σ)(b̂_1) + iG_2(σ)(σ⁻¹Ŝ_1)) ∈ H^(∞,(N,2−ε,((0,0),α_K−2)))_b,    (31.49)

with zf-coefficients ġ_b(ḃ_0) + h_b(iŜ_4^±). The distribution ℱ(∂_(t_*)u_sing) is bounded near σ = 0, and its
difference from the right side of (31.49), a bounded function with compact support, is supported at {0};
so the inverse transform of the difference is a polynomial in t_*, which the decay of both as t_* → −∞ forces to
vanish (∂_(t_*)u_sing = −∂_(t_*)(u_hi + u_reg) for t_* < 1, below; the other by the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma), and
(31.49) holds as distributions.

*Matching.* If the two zf-coefficients differed, ℱ(∂_(t_*)u_sing) would be c 1_(σ>0)χ(|σ|), with c ≠ 0 a section of X,
plus a function to which Proposition 20.20 (1) applies; the inverse transform of the first is
c · (2πi)⁻¹t_*⁻¹(1 + o(1)) as t_* → −∞, of K⁻-weight below 1 in spatially compact sets, while that of the second has
the K⁻-weight α_K − 1 > 1. But ∂_(t_*)u_sing = −∂_(t_*)(u_hi + u_reg) for t_* < 1, as u^♭ = 0 there, and this has the
K⁻-weight α_K > 1 (Step 4, and ∂_(t_*) ∈ ρ_ι ρ_K 𝒱_b). So Ŝ_4^+ = Ŝ_4^− (h_b is injective, Lemma 31.2), and
we drop the sign. Now Proposition 20.20 (1) with β_K := α_K − 1 gives
∂_(t_*)u_sing ∈ H^(∞,(3−2ε,3−ε,α_K−1))_b(M′), and Lemma 29.30 (1) with ℰ_K = ∅ and β_K := α_K − 2 ≠ 0, the a
priori bound on Ω_− being that of u_hi + u_reg, gives

    u_sing ∈ H^(∞,3/2−4ε,3/2−5ε,((0,0),α_K−2))_b(M′).

The (0, 0)-coefficient at K⁺ is

    lim_(t_*→∞) u_sing(t_*, x) = ∫_ℝ ∂_(t_*)u_sing dt_* = ℱ(∂_(t_*)u_sing)(0) = ġ_b(ḃ_0) + h_b(iŜ_4),

as u_sing → 0 as t_* → −∞ (K⁻-weight α_K − 1 > 0) and ∂_(t_*)u_sing is integrable (K-weights > 1). Replacing the
cut-off of the (0, 0)-term by χ_K changes u_sing by a term supported away from K⁺ and ℐ⁺ near (ι⁺)°, of ι⁺-order 2
(ġ_b, h_b ∈ 𝒜²). So, with

    ḃ := ḃ_0,        Ṡ^(0)_1 := iŜ_4    (31.50)

([Hin26, (11.133)]), u_sing − χ_K(ġ_b(ḃ) + h_b(Ṡ^(0)_1)) ∈ H^(∞,3/2−4ε,3/2−5ε,α_K−2)_b(M′). Their reality is shown
after Step 6.

*Step 6* (null infinity). ũ := u − χ_K(ġ_b(ḃ) + h_b(Ṡ^(0)_1)) = u_I + u_ι + u_hi + u_reg + (u_sing −
χ_K(ġ_b(ḃ) + h_b(Ṡ^(0)_1))) has the K⁺-weight α_K − 2 (Steps 1–5; c′_K, N and α_K − 1 are larger) and the ι⁺-weight
ℓ′_+ := 3/2 − 5ε. Near ℐ⁺, χ_K = 0 and Lũ = f; Proposition 29.27 with ℓ_+ := min(ℓ′_+, min Re ℰ_+ − ε), as in Step
4 of the proof of Proposition 31.6, gives the ℐ⁺-data (⟨ℰ^C_I⟩, ℓ_I). This is (31.40).

*Reality.* u is real, as f and L are and forward solutions are unique. ġ_b and h_b are real on real arguments ((BP3)),
so χ_K(ġ_b(Im ḃ) + h_b(Im Ṡ^(0)_1)) = −Im ũ has the K⁺-weight α_K − 2 > 0. A stationary tensor of positive K⁺-weight
vanishes on X°, so ġ_b(Im ḃ) + h_b(Im Ṡ^(0)_1) = 0. Applying the rows, B(b)(Im ḃ, Im Ṡ^(0)_1) = 0 by (31.1),
and Im ḃ = 0, Im Ṡ^(0)_1 = 0, as B(b) is invertible (Lemma 31.1).

*Continuity.* Every map above is linear and bounded between the spaces stated (Proposition 28.8, the construction
of Proposition 27.58, Lemma 29.33, Lemma 31.23–Lemma 31.26, Proposition 20.18 (1),
Proposition 20.20 (1), and Steps 0–2 as in Proposition 31.21), with bounds uniform in b ∈ ℬ̄_* by (BP1)–(BP5). ∎

The step of [Hin26, Proposition 9.30] and the expansion [Hin26, (11.107b)] of the zero energy solution are not needed
(see the end of Section 31.9); the tf-improvement of [Hin26, Proposition 9.35] is needed, because the first moment
∫ t_* f^♭ dt_* has the borderline weight 2. Proposition 27.58's solution contains |σ|^(α−3)h_b(S^(−1)_1), a
translation state with a coefficient singular at σ = 0. The rows of the augmented operator see it; left in the first
component, it would give a row correction of size |σ|^(−ε) in the 𝒮_1-component, which the integration in t_* would
turn into growth. Lemma 31.26 moves it into the 𝒮_1-column with the coefficient −σ²|σ|^(α−3)S^(−1)_1 =
O(|σ|^(1−ε)), and Lemma 31.25 shows that the remaining row data are answered by the nullspace, through the
inverse of the matrix B(b) of the rows on the states, with columns O(|σ|^(1−ε)). The identification (31.47)
needs every piece in 𝒳_σ; the conormal piece of Proposition 27.58's solution lies in it for an order family lowered
near R_out, a radial set where only an upper threshold applies, and the inverses on the two spaces agree, as the kernels
do not depend on the order (Lemma 31.24). The range α_K − 2 < ε_ind is that of [Hin26].

## 32. Undoing the parameter changes, centre-of-mass motions and corrections of the fourth kind

The forward solutions of Chapter 31 carry at K⁺ terms that do not decay, or decay slowly: a generalised boost, the
stationary terms χ_K ġ(ḃ) + χ_K h(S⁽⁰⁾_1) of Proposition 31.27, which record a change of the black hole parameters
and a shift of the centre of mass, and, at higher orders of decay, centre-of-mass motions and pure gauge terms. This
chapter shows that each of these terms is generated by a change of parameters that the forcing can be asked to absorb,
and eliminates them. It proves, in dimension 4 + 1, what [Hin26, Sections 11.6.2, 11.7 and 11.8.1] prove on Kerr
(pp. 256–277):

(1) the correction terms that let a forcing generate the change of the black hole parameters and the centre-of-mass
shift, the gauge-fixed Einstein operator with these parameters, its linearisation in them, and their elimination: for
a forcing with a little more than t_*⁻² decay at K⁺ there is a unique choice of the parameters for which the forward
solution decays at K⁺ (Corollary 32.18). These are [Hin26, (11.134a)–(11.147), Definitions 11.37, 11.40, 11.42,
11.44, Lemmas 11.38, 11.41, 11.43, 11.45, Corollary 11.46] in dimension 4 + 1;

(2) the correction terms for decaying centre-of-mass motions, the operator with these parameters, its linearisation in
them, and the elimination by induction on the rate: for forcings with almost three orders of decay at K⁺ there is a
unique choice of all modification parameters for which the forward solution has K⁺-weight α − 2 for every
α < min(a_K, 3), that is, decays like t_*^(−α+2), almost like t_*⁻¹, in compact spatial sets (Proposition 32.29).
These are [Hin26, Definitions 11.47–11.48, Lemma 11.49, Proposition 11.51] in dimension 4 + 1;

(3) the correction terms that undo the pure gauge terms of the K⁺-expansion which decay no faster than t_*⁻², the
gauge-fixed Einstein operator with all modification parameters, and its linearisation in the new parameters, which at
b₀ is exact up to a remainder of high order (Lemma 32.36). These are [Hin26, Definitions 11.55–11.56, Lemma
11.57] in dimension 4 + 1; the theorem that uses them is proved in Chapter 33.

The dimensional changes are these. In dimension 4 + 1 the exponents at future timelike infinity ι⁺ of the effective
forcings begin at the radiative exponent λ_♯ = 3/2 + (1 − e_Υ)γ_Υ > 3/2 ((29.32)), where those of Kerr begin
at 1. So there is no logarithmic centre-of-mass term (Proposition 31.27), and the parameters of the first step are
three, not four: the boost S, the black hole parameter b and the centre of mass S⁽⁰⁾_1; [Hin26, (11.136)–(11.138b),
Remark 11.39] and the correction h^((0,1))_s1 have no counterpart. The corrections carry no logarithm, so the
cancellation of a (3, 1)-coefficient behind [Hin26, (11.140)] is not needed. The centre-of-mass shift cannot be undone
by a correction alone: Hintz's metric term −dχ_K ⊗_s ω⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s1) has ι⁺-order 1, outside the class 𝒳 in dimension
4 + 1 (min Re ℰ_+ > 1, (29.3)), and it cannot be moved into the solution either, which must vanish at early
times. The exterior background is translated instead, as it is boosted in Chapter 29 (Definition 32.3), and the
correction becomes −dχ_K ⊗_s (ω_s1 − Θw⁰), of ι⁺-order 3 (Lemma 32.6).

The decaying centre-of-mass motions come only from the ι⁺-exponents λ of the effective forcing with Re λ ∈ [λ_♯, 2),
through the s1 row of Corollary 26.44, which is present exactly when ℓ_K = α_K − Re λ > 1; the zero energy
analysis produces none, as L̂_b(0) has no indicial root in (0, 1] (Proposition 25.6 (a)). So they are extracted
on spacetime by the step at ι⁺ of Proposition 31.21, where [Hin26] passes to the Fourier transform, and their rates
Re λ − 1 lie in [λ_♯ − 1, 1); they occur only for α_K > λ_♯ + 1 > 5/2. There is no proliferation of logarithms: the
ι⁺-normal operator has no pole below 2 (Lemma 26.29 (a)), and re-solving at null infinity creates no exponent
below 5/2 (Proposition 29.29). So the index set of the motions is fixed in advance and closed under the operations
that occur ((32.16)), the device u_Σ of [Hin26, (11.180)–(11.183)] and [Hin26, Remark 11.52] are not needed,
and each level of the induction is a finite-dimensional map close to the identity. The zero energy analysis is that of
Proposition 31.27, with the improvement at the transition face iterated once α_K ≥ 2 + ε_g (ε_g of Definition 32.1),
as in [Hin26, Step 1.6 of the proof of Proposition 11.51]. The gauge modifications use the generalised gauge 1-forms to
order 4 of Proposition 23.34, so that they decay to K⁺-order Re λ + 4.

For the pure gauge terms, the exponent 1 does not occur at ι⁺, so the logarithmic time reparametrisation of
[Hin26, (11.191)] and the exceptional parameters of [Hin26, (11.192)] do not arise. The rows of the table of roots of
Section 26.10 that reach K⁺-rate at most 2 are six: the boosts s1 (rate λ − 1), the rotations v1, the time
translation s0 and the s2 row at the root 0 (rate λ), and the class roots of types s0 and s1 in (−1, 0) (rate λ + d,
0 < d < 1); the rows at the root −1 of types s3 and v2, which [Hin26] keeps at the exponent 1, have rate above 5/2.
At the non-rotating b₀ every rotation is Killing, and the rotation rows carry no parameter (Section 32.10). And
the linearisation in the new parameters is exact up to a remainder r^ν that has ι⁺-weight above 5 + ε_+, with no
index set to track, and that at b = b₀ vanishes at the reference point (Lemma 32.36 (c)); at a general b the
remainder is joined by the difference E^ν, of size O(|b − b₀|), of the corrections built at b₀ and at b
(Lemma 32.36 (e)). This replaces [Hin26, (11.194)] and makes the elimination of Chapter 33 a perturbation of
the identity. Every dimensional change is mathematics and is carried below.

*The base point.* The base points of the linearisation have black hole parameter b in the closed ball ℬ̄_* about b₀
of Section 31.1, of radius at most 1/(2C_B) (Lemma 31.1), on which the states at b are injective uniformly
in b (Lemma 31.2). It is shrunk finitely many more times below, in Proposition 32.14, in the step of
Proposition 32.29, and for the joint injectivity Lemma 36.3 used in Section 32.11, each time to a smaller
ball about b₀; every statement holds on the final ℬ_*, and the segment from b₀ to each b ∈ ℬ̄_* lies in ℬ̄_*. On it the
model objects of Lemma 30.2 are uniform in b: the forward problem of Theorem 29.17 at b, with continuity
in (b, S, h) (property (P1) there); the ι⁺- and tf-normal operators and the indicial roots, which do
not depend on b (P2); the zero energy states and the 1-form towers at b, real and smooth in b, with index sets
independent of b (P3); the augmented low energy theory at b (P4); and the time translation, Killing for every g_b
(P5). Following Lemma 36.1, the rows (the cut-off pure gauge tensors m_ν, among them the motions of Section 32.7)
are built at the base point's b, while the correction terms and their counterterms are the tensors built from b₀, as
in [Hin26, p. 275, Definitions 11.55–11.56]. At the reference point (0, p⃗_b), p⃗_b := (0, b − b₀, 0), the background
in 𝒞 interpolates between g_(b₀) and g_b, so the parameter identities, exact at b₀, acquire an error of size
O(|b − b₀|) supported in 𝒞 (Lemma 32.11). The finite-dimensional maps of the elimination are therefore
inverted by direct bounds, uniform in b (Proposition 32.14, and the step of Proposition 32.29); continuity
statements at the reference point are used at fixed b only, with L_(0,p⃗_b) := D_hP_2(0, p⃗_b) as the reference
operator. Every result below holds at every b ∈ ℬ̄_*, uniformly in b, in the form in which it is stated, except the
exact identities Lemma 32.8, Lemma 32.22, Lemma 32.34 and Lemma 32.36 (c), which are
stated at b₀; their forms at b are Lemma 32.11, Lemma 32.25 and Lemma 32.36 (e), the
last being the identity (36.1). At b = b₀ the errors vanish and p⃗_(b₀) = 0. The results of Chapter 29
used at b are their statements at b, Proposition 30.5 (the first item of Theorem 36.10); Chapter 31 is
written at b. The results of Section 30.1 cited here are proved from this chapter's statements at b₀ and from
Lemma 32.4 (a), Lemma 32.32 (a)–(e) and Lemma 32.36 (e) at b, whose proofs use from that section
only (P3), (P5) and the choice of Lemma 36.1; so these citations are not circular.

*The inner radius.* The chapter works on Ω_* = cl_M{t^♭_* ≥ 1} with the b-Sobolev spaces of Chapter 19 and the
forward solutions of Chapter 29 and Chapter 31, which hold with the inner radius r₀ = r_♭ of Definition 22.1 as a
parameter. Its own radii are scale-free or far out ({|x| ≥ 4R₁} in Lemma 32.2 (c), {|x| ≤ 5R₁} for the
cut-offs), and its weights are fixed at infinity and at K⁺. So every result of this chapter holds with the inner
radius r₀ as a parameter.

*Notation.* In this chapter λ denotes an exponent at ι⁺ (an element of the projection π_1 of an index set), as in
[Hin26]; the wavelength of the main argument does not occur. A pair (λ, k) ∈ ℂ × ℕ₀ is an element of an index set, and
λ_♯ := 3/2 + (1 − e_Υ)γ_Υ is the least real part of the radiative index set ℰ^♯_+ of (29.32). A root of the
indicial family 𝒲(ℓ_K) of Section 26.10 is written μ, and the indicial roots of the gauge potential operator □^Υ are
ι^Υ_(s0,2), ι^Υ_(s1,2) as in (23.7). The black hole parameters are b = (m, A), b₀ = (m₀, 0). Weights are
listed at (ℐ⁺, ι⁺, K⁺), with the defining functions ρ_I, ρ_+, ρ_K, and ρ_0 at spatial infinity I_0; Ω_*, t^♭_*, the
density μ_b and the spaces H^(k,(…),(…),…)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−) of tensors vanishing near {t^♭_* = 1} are those of
Section 29.1, and the class of perturbations is 𝒳^k := H^(k,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,a_I),(ℰ_+,a_+),a_K)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)
((29.4)), with a_I > 3/2, a_+ > 1, a_K > 2 and the index set ℰ_+ of (29.3). We write m_+ := min(a_+,
min Re ℰ_+), ‖h‖ for the 𝒳^d-norm, a ⊗_s b := ½(a ⊗ b + b ⊗ a), and 𝒜^ℰ for the polyhomogeneous sections with index set
ℰ, near ι⁺ or near infinity in X̄ as stated. For an index set ℰ and w ∈ ℝ, ℰ + w is the shifted set and (ℰ, w) the data
"index set ℰ, remainder weight w".

### 32.1 Undoing the parameter changes: the translated background

*Notation.* The cut-offs χ_K, χ^♭_K, χ^♯_K, χ_r, χ_IVP, χ^♯_IVP are those of Section 21.7, with the nesting
(29.2); the set 𝒞 := supp χ_K ∩ supp(1 − χ_K) carries every derivative of χ_K, its closure meets ∂M only in
a compact subset of (ι⁺)°, and 𝒞 ⊂ supp χ_K ⊂ {t^♭_* ≥ 10}. The factor Θ := χ_r(|x|)χ^♯_IVP(1 − χ^♭_K), the boosts
φ_S and the 1-forms w(S) are those of Section 31.4. With a ⊗_s b as above,

    [δ*_g, χ]ω = dχ ⊗_s ω,          [δ_g, χ]h = −ι_(g⁻¹dχ) h,    (32.1)

which is (31.16), and three identities of Section 31.4 are used throughout: (i) Υ^(E_Υ)(g, g) = 0 for
every g, so (D_1 + D_2)Υ^(E_Υ)(g, g) = 0 and P(g, g) = Ric(g); (ii) D_1Υ^(E_Υ)(g, g) = −δ_(g,E_Υ)G_g; (iii) if
Ric(g) = 0 then D_gRic(ℒ_Y g) = 0 for every smooth vector field Y, so D_gRic ∘ δ*_g = 0. Here P(g, g_0),
Υ^(E_Υ)(g, g_0), δ*_(g_0,E_C) and δ_(g_0,E_Υ) are those of Definition 21.28, L^(g,g_0) := D_1P(·, g_0) at g, and
L_b := L^(g_b,g_b) = D_(g_b)Ric + δ*_(g_b,E_C) δ_(g_b,E_Υ) G_(g_b). The states ω_s1(S) := ω⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s1)(S),
h(S) := δ*_(g_(b₀)) ω_s1(S), the re-centred generalised state h^(≤1)_♮(S) of Definition 31.7, and the corrections
h^(−1)(S), ϑ^(−1)(S), ϑ_♯(S) of Definition 31.9 are those of Chapter 31; at b, h_b(S) := δ*_(g_b) ω_(b,s1)(S) and
h^(≤1)_(b,♮)(S) is the re-centred s1 state at b of Definition 31.7.

𝔟 = ℝ × 𝔰𝔬(4) is the parameter space of Proposition 25.26. For ḃ ∈ 𝔟 put ġ_(b₀)(ḃ) := ∂_b g_b|_(b=b₀)(ḃ),
ω̇(ḃ) := ω̇_(b₀)(ḃ) and

    ġ(ḃ) := ġ^Υ_(b₀)(ḃ) = ġ_(b₀)(ḃ) + δ*_(g_(b₀)) ω̇(ḃ)

((25.17)), which is the state ṁ ġ^Υ_(b₀)(1, 0) + ġ^Υ_(b₀)(0, Ȧ) of Section 28.1 for ḃ = (ṁ, Ȧ), by
linearity (Proposition 25.26 (3)). At b, ġ_b(ḃ) := ġ^Υ_b(ḃ) = ∂_b g_b(ḃ) + δ*_(g_b) ω̇_b(ḃ) is the gauge-corrected
state at b (Lemma 30.2 (P3)). In this chapter ℰ_ind is the union of the index sets of Proposition 23.28 and
Proposition 25.26 at b₀; by (P3) these serve at every b. By Proposition 25.26 (1)–(2) and Proposition 23.28,
on X̄ near infinity

    ω̇(ḃ) ∈ 𝒜^((1,0)∪(1+ℰ_ind)),   ġ(ḃ) ∈ 𝒜^𝒢,   ω_s1(S) − ω̄_s1(S) ∈ 𝒜^𝒢,   h(S) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+1),
        𝒢 := (2, 0) ∪ (2 + ℰ_ind),    (32.2)

with ω̄_s1(S_w) = d(|x|S_w) = w·dx for S_w(ω) = w·ω, w ∈ ℝ⁴. The tensors ġ(ḃ) and h(S) lie in
ker D_(g_(b₀))Ric ∩ ker δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)) (Proposition 25.26 (2), Section 31.4), and
(ḃ, S) ↦ ġ(ḃ) + h(S) is injective, by the rows of (28.9). At b the same holds for ġ_b and h_b: they span
the nullspace of L̂_b(0) in the space of Proposition 28.8, which near b₀ has the dimension it has at b₀, with the
continuous basis ġ_b(ḃ), h_b(S) (the proof of Proposition 28.8 at b, Lemma 30.2 (P4), and
Lemma 31.2). We assume

    2 + ℰ_ind ⊂ ℰ_+,    (32.3)

which is (31.20) for this union, so 𝒢 ⊂ ℰ_+ by (29.3). The weight ℓ_I is fixed as in
(31.32), and, as in Section 31.7, ℓ_I ≤ a_I (so a_I ≥ 2).

**Definition 32.1** (The two gaps.) Two gaps of indicial roots enter, and they are different numbers:
ε_ind is the constant of (25.10), fixed by the indicial roots of L̂_b(0), with which the hypotheses of
Proposition 27.58 are stated; ε_Υ is the constant of Section 23.13, fixed by the indicial roots of □^Υ_b, by which
the remainder (27.55) of Proposition 27.58 gains over the forcing at the transition face. Put

    ε_g := min(ε_Υ, ε_ind),

the lower bound used where a step uses both. As 0 < ε_Υ < 1/2 (Section 23.13: every integer in [−10, 10] lies in
the set that fixes ε_Υ), 0 < ε_g < 1/2.

The rate α_K ∈ (2, min(a_K, 2 + ε_g, 5/2)) lies in the range of Proposition 31.27, and

    𝒴 := ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′,ℓ_I+1),4−ε,α_K)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−),

real sections, is the class of forcings ([Hin26, (11.116)] in dimension 4 + 1). A large d, at least the d of
(31.26), is fixed throughout, and "h small" means h ∈ 𝒳^∞ vanishing near {t^♭_* = 1} with small 𝒳^d-norm.

*Translations.* For S = S_w ∈ 𝒮_1 put Y_S := w·∂_x = η⁻¹ω̄_s1(S), V⁰(S) := ½ΘY_S, ψ_S := exp V⁰(S) and
w⁰(S) := g_(b₀)(Y_S, ·), so that g_(b₀)(V⁰(S), ·) = ½Θw⁰(S) and, by ℒ_X g = 2δ*_g(g(X, ·)),

    ∂_S ψ*_(−S) g_(b₀)|_(S=0)(Ṡ) = −δ*_(g_(b₀))(Θw⁰(Ṡ)).

**Lemma 32.2** (Translations; Lemma 21.26 and Lemma 21.27 for translations.) (a) V⁰(S) lifts
to a b-vector field on M, vanishing near Σ^past ∪ K⁺ ∪ Σ^int and on {|x| ≤ 5R₁} and tangent to every boundary
hypersurface; so ψ_S is a diffeomorphism of M with the properties stated for φ_(S_w) in Lemma 21.26, depending
smoothly on S.

(b) There are w_0 > 0 and a neighbourhood 𝒩_0 of supp(χ_IVP(1 − χ_K)) such that for |w| < w_0 every integral curve of
V⁰(S_w) starting in 𝒩_0 stays, for times in [0, 1], either in {Θ = 1}, where ψ_(S_w) is the translation
τ_(w/2) : (t, x) ↦ (t, x + w/2), or in a fixed compact subset of M disjoint from I_0 ∪ ℐ⁺ ∪ ι⁺ ∪ K⁺.

(c) For b near b₀ and a ∈ ℝ⁴ small, τ_a*g_b − g_b has Cartesian components in |x|⁻³C^∞(X̄) on {|x| ≥ 4R₁}; it is
stationary, smooth in a and O(|a|).

*Proof.* (a) Y_S has constant Cartesian coefficients, so on the radial compactification of ℝ^(1+4) it is a boundary
defining function times a b-vector field; it is tangent to every submanifold of the boundary, Y_+ included, and lifts
to a b-vector field on M tangent to every boundary hypersurface. The factor Θ is the one of Lemma 21.26, with its
vanishing properties, and the rest is that lemma's proof. (b) As in Lemma 21.27: the strict nesting of the
cut-offs gives {Θ = 1} a neighbourhood margin around supp(χ_IVP(1 − χ_K)) near I_0 ∪ ℐ⁺ ∪ ι⁺, so a slightly larger
neighbourhood 𝒩_0 still has one; M is compact and the time-[0, 1] flow of V⁰(S_w), linear in w, tends to the identity
uniformly as w → 0; on {Θ = 1}, V⁰(S_w) = ½w·∂_x, whose time-1 flow is τ_(w/2). (c) g_b is stationary with
g_b − η ∈ |x|⁻²C^∞(X̄) on {|x| ≥ 3R₁} ((21.29), Proposition 21.21), and τ_a* acts on Cartesian components
by x ↦ x + a. For F ∈ |x|⁻²C^∞(X̄),

    F(x + a) − F(x) = ∫_0^1 a·(∇F)(x + sa) ds,

with ∇F ∈ |x|⁻³C^∞(X̄); x ↦ x + sa extends to a diffeomorphism of X̄ near infinity that is the identity on ∂X̄, so
composition with it preserves |x|⁻³C^∞(X̄), uniformly in s and smoothly in a. ∎

**Definition 32.3** (The translated background.) For p⃗ = (S, b − b₀, S⁽⁰⁾_1) with S, S⁽⁰⁾_1 ∈ 𝒮_1
small and b near b₀,

    g_p⃗ := (1 − χ_K)(ψ_(−S⁽⁰⁾_1) ∘ φ_(−S))*g_(b₀) + χ_K g_b,    (32.4)

so that g_((S,b−b₀,0)) = g_(b₀,b,−S) ((29.1)).

**Lemma 32.4** (Properties of the translated background.) For |S|, |S⁽⁰⁾_1| and |b − b₀| small:

(a) (21.40) holds with (ψ_(−S⁽⁰⁾_1) ∘ φ_(−S))*g_b in place of φ*_(S_w)g_b (S_w = −S), with the same leading
term; hence Lemma 29.11 holds for g_p⃗ (in particular (29.11) and g_p⃗ ∈ 𝒢⁺ there), with seminorms
O(|b − b₀| + |S| + |S⁽⁰⁾_1|), p⃗ ↦ g_p⃗ − g_b smooth into that class, and ∂_(S⁽⁰⁾_1) g_p⃗, ∂_S g_p⃗ in the class of
the background differences of Section 31.6 (the class of Lemma 29.11, vanishing near K⁺); and
Lemma 29.13 holds for g_p⃗.

(b) Proposition 29.6, Proposition 29.7, Proposition 29.12, Corollary 29.14, Corollary 29.16 and
Theorem 29.17 hold for g_0 := g_p⃗, with |S| replaced by |S| + |S⁽⁰⁾_1|, and the continuity of
Theorem 29.17 holds in (S, S⁽⁰⁾_1, h). At b ≠ b₀ the forward problem is that of Lemma 30.2 (P1), which
covers the backgrounds g_p⃗ by (a).

(c) On {Θ = 1} ∩ supp(1 − χ_K) near (ι⁺)°, ψ_(−S⁽⁰⁾_1) ∘ φ_(−S) is a Poincaré motion (a Lorentz boost followed by a
translation), and g_p⃗ − η, ∂_S g_p⃗, ∂_(S⁽⁰⁾_1) g_p⃗ lie in ρ_+²C^∞ near (ι⁺)°. On int χ_K⁻¹(0), g_p⃗ is Ricci
flat.

*Proof.* (a) Let p ∈ supp(χ_IVP(1 − χ_K)). On the first alternative of Lemma 21.27, φ_(−S) is the exact boost
near p, and φ_(−S)(p) ∈ 𝒩_0 for |S| small (the flow tends to the identity), so by Lemma 32.2 (b) ψ_(−S⁽⁰⁾_1)
is the translation τ := τ_(−w/2) (S⁽⁰⁾_1 = S_w) near φ_(−S)(p), or p lies in a fixed compact set away from the faces
at infinity, where everything is smooth. On the former,

    (ψ_(−S⁽⁰⁾_1) ∘ φ_(−S))*g_b = φ*_(−S)g_b + φ*_(−S)(τ*g_b − g_b).

By Lemma 32.2 (c), τ*g_b − g_b ∈ |x|⁻³C^∞(X̄) there, and on that
region |x|⁻³C^∞(X̄) ⊂ ρ_0³ρ_I³ρ_+³C^∞ (C^∞(X̄) lifts to C^∞(M) there, Section 21.4, as in the proof of
Lemma 21.27), a class which φ*_(−S) preserves (Lemma 21.26) and which lies in the remainder class
ρ_0²ρ_I³ρ_+²C^∞ of (21.40). This is (21.40) for the composite. The proof of Lemma 29.11 uses
(21.40) on the first alternative, smoothness on the second and Proposition 21.21, so it applies verbatim; the
dependence on (S, S⁽⁰⁾_1) is smooth as the flows and the remainders h_(S_w) of (21.40) are, and the parameter
derivatives vanish near K⁺ (where g_p⃗ = g_b), so they lie in the class of Section 31.6, as stated there for S. The
proof of Lemma 29.13 uses that the exterior metric is Ricci flat (it is a pullback of g_(b₀)), Lemma 29.11,
and that the exterior metric minus η lies in ρ_+²C^∞ near (ι⁺)°, which is (c).

(b) Proposition 29.6, Proposition 29.7, Proposition 29.12 and Corollary 29.16 are stated for g_0 ∈ 𝒢⁺ with
(29.11) (Proposition 29.7 "or more generally"), which (a) gives; Corollary 29.14 rests on
Proposition 29.12 and Lemma 29.13; the proof of Theorem 29.17 uses g_0 only through Corollary 29.16 and
(29.13), whose bound is linear in the seminorms of g_0 − g_(b₀), at b = b₀ now O(|S| + |S⁽⁰⁾_1|); the
continuity follows as g_p⃗ depends smoothly on p⃗. At b, Lemma 30.2 (P1) gives Theorem 29.17 for these
backgrounds with continuity in (b, S, h), its proof covering g_p⃗ through (a).

(c) On {Θ = 1} both flows are exact (Lemma 21.27, Lemma 32.2 (b)), so the composite is a Lorentz boost
followed by a translation, which preserves η; with g_(b₀) − η ∈ |x|⁻²C^∞ and |x| ≥ t/20 there,
g_p⃗ − η ∈ ρ_+²C^∞ near (ι⁺)°, the part χ_K g_b included, as g_b − η ∈ |x|⁻²C^∞ for every b near b₀
((21.29), Proposition 21.21). ∂_S and ∂_(S⁽⁰⁾_1) of (ψ ∘ φ)*g_(b₀) are Lie derivatives of the pulled-back
metric along a generator of the Poincaré group (a linear or a constant vector field, which is a b-vector field and
Killing for η), so they map η + ρ_+²C^∞ into ρ_+²C^∞. On int χ_K⁻¹(0), g_p⃗ is a pullback of g_(b₀) by a
diffeomorphism. ∎

### 32.2 The correction terms and the operator

**Definition 32.5** (Corrections of the second kind; [Hin26, Definition 11.37] in dimension 4 + 1.) For
ḃ ∈ 𝔟 and S ∈ 𝒮_1,

    h⁽⁰⁾(ḃ) := −[δ*_(g_(b₀)), χ_K] ω̇(ḃ) = −dχ_K ⊗_s ω̇(ḃ),     ϑ⁽⁰⁾(ḃ) := [δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)), χ_K] ġ(ḃ),
    h⁽⁰⁾_s1(S) := −dχ_K ⊗_s (ω_s1(S) − Θw⁰(S)),     ϑ⁽⁰⁾_s1(S) := [δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)), χ_K] h(S),

and, with the counterterms of [Hin26, Remark 11.27] as in Definition 31.9,
ϑ⁽⁰⁾_♯ := ϑ⁽⁰⁾ − δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)) h⁽⁰⁾ and ϑ⁽⁰⁾_(s1,♯) := ϑ⁽⁰⁾_s1 − δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)) h⁽⁰⁾_s1. All
are linear. By (32.1), [δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)), χ_K]k = −ι_(g_(b₀)⁻¹dχ_K) G_(g_(b₀)) k.

[Hin26]'s h⁽⁰⁾_s1 has ω⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s1) alone; Θw⁰(S) is the translation of (32.4), as Θw(S) is the boost's in
Definition 31.9. These tensors are built at b₀ and serve at every base point (Lemma 36.1).

**Lemma 32.6** ([Hin26, Lemma 11.38] in dimension 4 + 1.) The tensors of Definition 32.5 are smooth,
supported in 𝒞 (so disjoint from ℐ⁺ and K⁺ and from {t^♭_* < 10}), with seminorms O(|ḃ|), resp. O(|S|), and near
(ι⁺)°

    h⁽⁰⁾(ḃ) ∈ 𝒜^𝒢,    h⁽⁰⁾_s1(S) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+1),    D_(g_0)Ric(h⁽⁰⁾(ḃ)) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+2),    D_(g_0)Ric(h⁽⁰⁾_s1(S)) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+3),
    ϑ⁽⁰⁾(ḃ), ϑ⁽⁰⁾_♯(ḃ) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+1),    ϑ⁽⁰⁾_s1(S), ϑ⁽⁰⁾_(s1,♯)(S) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+2),    (32.5)

for every metric g_0 smooth on M near (ι⁺)° with g_0 − η ∈ ρ_+C^∞ there.

*Proof.* Each has a factor dχ_K, so it is supported in 𝒞 ⊂ supp χ_K ⊂ {t^♭_* ≥ 10}; it is smooth as ω̇, ġ, ω_s1,
w⁰, Θ and h are. Near (ι⁺)°, on 𝒞 ∩ {t ≥ T_1}, Θ = 1 and |x| ≥ t/10, so 𝒜^ℰ(X̄) lies in 𝒜^ℰ at ι⁺ (the proof of
Lemma 31.8 (b)). There, by (32.2), ω̇ ∈ 𝒜^((1,0)∪(1+ℰ_ind)), ġ ∈ 𝒜^𝒢, h(S) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+1), and

    ω_s1(S) − w⁰(S) = (ω_s1(S) − ω̄_s1(S)) + (η − g_(b₀))η⁻¹ω̄_s1(S) ∈ 𝒜^𝒢,

the second term because ω̄_s1(S) has constant Cartesian components and g_(b₀) − η ∈ |x|⁻²C^∞. With
dχ_K ∈ ρ_+C^∞, ι_(g_(b₀)⁻¹dχ_K) with coefficients in ρ_+C^∞, D_(g_0)Ric ∈ ρ_+²Diff²_b and
δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)) ∈ ρ_+Diff¹_b there (the proof of Lemma 31.10), (32.5) follows. ∎

[Hin26, Lemma 11.38] has the index sets (1, 1) ∪ (1 + ℰ_ind) and (1, 0) ∪ (1 + ℰ_ind) for the metric terms, and its
(11.140) needs the vanishing of a (3, 1)-coefficient; in dimension 4 + 1 there is no logarithm, and the translation
raises h⁽⁰⁾_s1 from ι⁺-order 1 to order 3.

**Definition 32.7** (The operator with the parameters; [Hin26, Definition 11.40] in dimension 4 + 1, in
the form of its Remark 11.27.) For p⃗ = (S, b − b₀, S⁽⁰⁾_1) small and h ∈ 𝒳^∞ with small 𝒳^d-norm, with g_0 := g_p⃗,

    h_tot(p⃗) := h^(−1)(S) + h⁽⁰⁾(b − b₀) + h⁽⁰⁾_s1(S⁽⁰⁾_1),
    ϑ_tot(p⃗) := ϑ_♯(S) + ϑ⁽⁰⁾_♯(b − b₀) + ϑ⁽⁰⁾_(s1,♯)(S⁽⁰⁾_1),

g′ := g_0 + h_tot(p⃗) + h, and

    P_2(h, p⃗) := Ric(g′) − δ*_(g_0,E_C)(Υ^(E_Υ)(g′, g_0) − ϑ_tot(p⃗)),    (32.6)

and L_(h,p⃗) := D_hP_2(·, p⃗) at h. P_2(h, (S, 0, 0)) = P_1(h, S, b₀) ((31.18)) and P_2(0, 0) = 0.

*Sizes.* [Hin26, Remark 11.36] accepts metric terms of size O(ρ_+) and gauge terms of size O(ρ_+²). In dimension 4 + 1
the metric terms lie in 𝒜^𝒢 ⊂ 𝒳 (by (32.3)) and the gauge terms in 𝒜^(𝒢+1), which
δ*_(g_0,E_C) ∈ ρ_+Diff¹_b maps to ι⁺-order 4, the order of the forcings from Section 31.6 on.

**Lemma 32.8** (The parameter identities; [Hin26, (11.78b), (11.134b), (11.135b)] in dimension 4 + 1.)
For Ṡ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾ ∈ 𝒮_1 and ḃ ∈ 𝔟,

    D_p⃗P_2(0, 0)(Ṡ, 0, 0) = L_(b₀)(χ_K h^(≤1)_♮(Ṡ)),    D_p⃗P_2(0, 0)(0, ḃ, 0) = L_(b₀)(χ_K ġ(ḃ)),
    D_p⃗P_2(0, 0)(0, 0, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾) = L_(b₀)(χ_K h(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾)).    (32.7)

All three are supported in 𝒞, and χ_K h^(≤1)_♮(Ṡ), χ_K ġ(ḃ) and χ_K h(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾), which vanish for t^♭_* < 10, are their
forward solutions (Proposition 17.14).

*Proof.* The first is Lemma 31.12, with its support statement in Lemma 31.15, as P_2 = P_1(·, ·, b₀)
where b = b₀ and S⁽⁰⁾_1 = 0. For the others: at p⃗ = 0, g′ = g_0 = g_(b₀) and
Υ^(E_Υ)(g_(b₀), g_(b₀)) − ϑ_tot(0) = 0, so for a parameter direction with ġ_0 := ∂g_0, ġ′ := ∂g′ and
ϑ̇ := ∂ϑ_tot, the derivative of δ*_(g_0,E_C) multiplies zero and, by (i),

    DP_2 = D_(g_(b₀))Ric(ġ′) − δ*_(g_(b₀),E_C)(D_1Υ (ġ′ − ġ_0) − ϑ̇),
    D_1Υ := D_1Υ^(E_Υ)(g_(b₀), g_(b₀)) = −δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀))

(the last by (ii)). We write δ*, δ_(E_Υ)G, δ*_(E_C) and DRic at g_(b₀). *The parameter b.* ġ_0 = χ_K ġ_(b₀)(ḃ), as
only χ_K g_b depends on b; ġ′ − ġ_0 = h⁽⁰⁾(ḃ) and ϑ̇ = ϑ⁽⁰⁾_♯(ḃ). By (32.1),
h⁽⁰⁾(ḃ) = χ_K δ*ω̇ − δ*(χ_K ω̇), so ġ′ = χ_K ġ(ḃ) − δ*(χ_K ω̇(ḃ)) and DRic(ġ′) = DRic(χ_K ġ(ḃ)) by (iii). And
D_1Υ h⁽⁰⁾ − ϑ⁽⁰⁾_♯ = −δ_(E_Υ)Gh⁽⁰⁾ − ϑ⁽⁰⁾ + δ_(E_Υ)Gh⁽⁰⁾ = −ϑ⁽⁰⁾(ḃ). So DP_2 = DRic(χ_K ġ) + δ*_(E_C)ϑ⁽⁰⁾(ḃ); and
as δ_(E_Υ)Gġ = 0, L_(b₀)(χ_K ġ) = DRic(χ_K ġ) + δ*_(E_C)[δ_(E_Υ)G, χ_K]ġ, the same. *The parameter S⁽⁰⁾_1.*
ġ_0 = −(1 − χ_K)δ*(Θw⁰(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾)) (Translations, above), ġ′ − ġ_0 = h⁽⁰⁾_s1(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾) and ϑ̇ = ϑ⁽⁰⁾_(s1,♯)(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾). With
(32.1), −(1 − χ_K)δ*(Θw⁰) = −δ*((1 − χ_K)Θw⁰) − dχ_K ⊗_s Θw⁰ and
−dχ_K ⊗_s ω_s1 = χ_K h(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾) − δ*(χ_K ω_s1), so

    ġ′ = χ_K h(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾) − δ*((1 − χ_K)Θw⁰(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾) + χ_K ω_s1(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾)),

and DRic(ġ′) = DRic(χ_K h(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾)) by (iii). The gauge term is δ*_(E_C)ϑ⁽⁰⁾_s1(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾) as before, and
δ_(E_Υ)Gh = 0 gives L_(b₀)(χ_K h). *Supports.* For k ∈ ker D_(g_(b₀))Ric, DRic(χ_K k) = [DRic, χ_K]k is supported in
𝒞, as are the ϑ's. ∎

As in [Hin26], (32.7) reads the late-time terms of (31.40) as generated by changes of the
parameters of the final black hole and of its centre, with no change of the initial state. At a base point with
parameter b ≠ b₀ the identities acquire an error; this is Lemma 32.11.

**Lemma 32.9** (The linearisation in h; [Hin26, Definition 11.40, last paragraph] in dimension 4 + 1.)
Let p⃗ = (S, b − b₀, S⁽⁰⁾_1), b ∈ ℬ̄_*, and h be small.

(a) h_tot(p⃗) ∈ 𝒳^∞, ‖h_tot(p⃗)‖_(𝒳^k) ≤ C_k|p⃗|, and L_(h,p⃗) = L^(g′,g_0) with g_0 = g_p⃗, g′ = g_0 + h′,
h′ := h_tot(p⃗) + h.

(b) Every result of Chapter 29 and Chapter 31 stated for L_(h,S) (or L^(g_S+h′,g_S)) holds for L_(h,p⃗), with
f^S_(h,p⃗) of Lemma 32.10 in place of the f_(h,S) of Lemma 31.15; at b these are the statements at b,
the boost column in the forms of Lemma 31.18 and Proposition 31.19.

(c) The bounds of Proposition 31.16 (1) and Proposition 31.27 (of Ṡ, ũ, resp. of ḃ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾_1, ũ, by f, at each
finite regularity) hold with constants uniform for (h, p⃗) small and b ∈ ℬ̄_*.

*Proof.* (a) ϑ_tot(p⃗) does not depend on h, so D_hP_2 = D_(g′)Ric − δ*_(g_0,E_C)D_1Υ^(E_Υ)(g′, g_0) = L^(g′,g_0). By
Lemma 32.6 and Lemma 31.10, h_tot(p⃗) is smooth, supported in 𝒞 and in 𝒜^𝒢 near (ι⁺)°, with seminorms
O(|p⃗|), and 𝒢 ⊂ ℰ_+ by (32.3); so it lies in H^(∞,(ℰ_+,a_+))_b at ι⁺ for every a_+, with norms O(|p⃗|),
as in Lemma 31.13. (b) The proofs of those results use the background g_S only through the results listed in
Lemma 32.4 (b), the class of Lemma 29.11 and its smooth dependence on the parameter
(Lemma 31.14), and, in Lemma 31.15, through the two properties of Lemma 32.4 (c); and they use
h′ only through h′ ∈ 𝒳 with small norm. Lemma 32.4 and (a) provide these for g_p⃗ and h′, and
Lemma 32.10 (a) below is Lemma 31.15 for P_2. At b they hold by Lemma 30.2 (P1)–(P4), with the
boost column of Lemma 31.18 and Proposition 31.19, and with the results of Chapter 29 in their statements at
b, Proposition 30.5. (c) In the proofs of these propositions every map is
fixed by the reference operator, or is the difference of L and the reference operator, bounded by (29.15)
with the coefficient bounds of Proposition 29.7, uniform for small (h′, p⃗) (Lemma 32.4 (b)), or is the
solution map of Proposition 29.35, or Proposition 29.27 applied to L itself (Step 4 of the proof of
Proposition 31.6, Step 6 of that of Proposition 31.27), whose bounds are locally uniform: the continuity
paragraph of Proposition 29.35 shows this for both, the proof of Proposition 29.27 being constructive with bounds
depending on L only through coefficient norms, locally uniform by Proposition 29.7; Lemma 31.17 (a) is this
argument for Ṡ. At b, Proposition 29.35 and Proposition 29.27 are their statements at b, Proposition 30.5,
with constants and smallness conditions uniform in b; with Lemma 30.2 (P1) and (P4) the constants are uniform
in b. ∎

### 32.3 The linearisation in the parameters

**Lemma 32.10** ([Hin26, Lemma 11.41] in dimension 4 + 1.) Let p⃗ = (S, b − b₀, S⁽⁰⁾_1) be small,
b ∈ ℬ̄_*, h ∈ 𝒳^k, k ≥ 5, with small 𝒳⁵-norm, ℰ̃_+ := 𝒢 ∪ (ℰ_+ + 𝒢) ((31.22) with this 𝒢), and

    f^S_(h,p⃗)(S′) := D_p⃗P_2(h, p⃗)(S′, 0, 0),   f^b_(h,p⃗)(b′) := D_p⃗P_2(h, p⃗)(0, b′, 0),
    f^s1_(h,p⃗)(S″) := D_p⃗P_2(h, p⃗)(0, 0, S″).

(a) f^S_(h,p⃗)(S′) and f^s1_(h,p⃗)(S″) satisfy (31.23) and the other statements of Lemma 31.15: they
vanish on int χ_K⁻¹(1), and for t^♭_* < c, c ≤ 10, if h does.

(b) f^b_(h,p⃗)(b′) is supported in supp χ_K (so it vanishes near ℐ⁺ and for t^♭_* < 10), and for every ε > 0

    f^b_(h,p⃗)(b′) ∈ H^(k−2,∞,(ℰ̃_++2,a_++4−ε),a_K)_b(Ω_*);    (32.8)

if h has K⁺-weight ℓ_K > 0 in place of a_K, the K⁺-weight of f^b_(h,p⃗)(b′) is ℓ_K.

(c) All three are linear in the direction, with norms O(|S′|), O(|b′|), O(|S″|), continuous in (h, p⃗) with h ∈ 𝒳^k,
and at (h, p⃗) = (0, 0) given by (32.7), supported in 𝒞.

*Proof.* (a) *For S:* the proof of Lemma 31.15, with g_p⃗, h_tot(p⃗), ϑ_tot(p⃗) for g_S, h^(−1)(S), ϑ_♯(S): the
S-derivative falls on g_0, h^(−1)(S) and ϑ_♯(S) only. On U_K := int χ_K⁻¹(1), P_2 does not depend on S. On
U_I := int χ_K⁻¹(0), g_p⃗ is Ricci flat (Lemma 32.4 (c)) and h_tot, ϑ_tot vanish, so
f = ∫_0^1 L̇_s h ds with L̇_s := ∂_S[L^(g_p⃗+sh,g_p⃗)](S′), and Lemma 31.14 applies, its proof needing that
∂_S g_p⃗ lies in the class of Section 31.6 (Lemma 32.4 (a)). On the neighbourhood U_ι of 𝒞 ∩ {t ≥ T_1}
of the proof of Lemma 31.15, Lemma 32.4 (c) gives g_0 − η, k_0 := ∂_S g_p⃗(S′) ∈ ρ_+²C^∞, and
h_tot ∈ 𝒜^𝒢, ϑ_tot ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+1) (Lemma 32.6, Lemma 31.10), so the three counts there apply unchanged.
*For S⁽⁰⁾_1:* the same, with k_0 := ∂_(S⁽⁰⁾_1) g_p⃗(S″) ∈ ρ_+²C^∞ near (ι⁺)° and in the class of Section 31.6
(Lemma 32.4), h⁽⁰⁾_s1(S″) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+1) ⊂ 𝒜^𝒢 in place of h^(−1)(S′), ϑ⁽⁰⁾_(s1,♯)(S″) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+2) ⊂ 𝒜^(𝒢+1) in
place of ϑ_♯(S′), and, in the third count, the definition of ϑ⁽⁰⁾_(s1,♯) in place of that of ϑ_♯:

    D_1Υ(g′, g_0)h⁽⁰⁾_s1(S″) − ϑ⁽⁰⁾_(s1,♯)(S″) = [D_1Υ(g′, g_0) − D_1Υ(g_(b₀), g_(b₀))]h⁽⁰⁾_s1(S″) − ϑ⁽⁰⁾_s1(S″).

On U_K, P_2 does not depend on S⁽⁰⁾_1, and on U_I, L̇_s := ∂_(S⁽⁰⁾_1)[L^(g_p⃗+sh,g_p⃗)](S″) with
Lemma 31.14.

(b) Outside supp χ_K, P_2 does not depend on b near each point: g_0 is the exterior metric there, and h⁽⁰⁾,
ϑ⁽⁰⁾_♯ are supported in 𝒞 ⊂ supp χ_K. *On U_K:* near each point g_0 = g_b and h_tot = 0, ϑ_tot = 0, so
P_2(h, p⃗) = P(g_b + h, g_b) and f^b = (D_1P + D_2P)(g_b + h, g_b) ∂_b g_b(b′). At h = 0 this is
(d/db)Ric(g_b)(b′) = 0, by (i) (P(g, g) = Ric(g)) and as every g_b is Ricci flat; so

    f^b = ∫_0^1 ∂_s[(D_1P + D_2P)(g_b + sh, g_b)] ∂_b g_b(b′) ds,

a sum of terms bilinear in (h, ∂h, ∂²h) and (∂_b g_b, ∂∂_b g_b, ∂²∂_b g_b) (Cartesian derivatives), with coefficients
smooth in g_b + sh, g_b and their first two derivatives. ∂_b g_b(b′) is stationary and in |x|⁻²C^∞(X̄) near infinity
(Proposition 21.21), so of ι⁺-order 2 and smooth and bounded with all b-derivatives at K⁺, and Cartesian derivatives
lie in ρ_+𝒱_b near (ι⁺)°; with h ∈ H^(k,(ℰ_+,a_+))_b at ι⁺ and of K⁺-weight a_K (or ℓ_K), the terms have ι⁺-data
(ℰ_+ + 4, a_+ + 4), ℰ_+ + 4 ⊂ ℰ̃_+ + 2 (as (2, 0) ∈ 𝒢), and K⁺-weight a_K (or ℓ_K). *On U_ι:* the b-derivative of
(32.6) is (31.24) with k_b := ∂_b g_p⃗(b′) = χ_K ∂_b g_b(b′) ∈ ρ_+²C^∞ in place of k_0,
h⁽⁰⁾(b′) ∈ 𝒜^𝒢 in place of h^(−1)(S′) and ϑ⁽⁰⁾_♯(b′) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+1) in place of ϑ_♯(S′) (Lemma 32.6), and the
three counts in the proof of Lemma 31.15 give the ι⁺-index set ℰ̃_+ + 2 at the weight a_+ + 4. On the compact
part it is in H^(k−2). Together, (32.8).

(c) Linearity and the bounds are clear from (a)–(b); continuity in (h, p⃗) as in Lemma 31.15 (each term is
linear in the direction and a product of factors continuous in (h, p⃗), with the bounds of Lemma 27.5; g_p⃗ is
smooth in p⃗ by Lemma 32.4 (a)); at (0, 0), (32.7). ∎

[Hin26, (11.144)] splits f^S as in its (11.86), and its (11.145)–(11.146) have the ι⁺-index set ℰ̃_+ + 2 ∋ (3, 0) and
the K⁺-order 5 of ϑ^((0,1))_s1; in dimension 4 + 1 no splitting is made, the least ι⁺-order is 4
(Lemma 32.6), and f^s1 vanishes near K⁺.

### 32.4 The parameter identities at a general base point

Lemma 32.8 is exact at the reference point (0, 0) only. At (0, p⃗_b), p⃗_b := (0, b − b₀, 0), the background
is G := g_(b₀,b,0) = (1 − χ_K)g_(b₀) + χ_K g_b ((32.4)), while the corrections of the first and second
kind and their counterterms, among them h⁽⁰⁾(ḃ) = −dχ_K ⊗_s ω̇_(b₀)(ḃ), are built at b₀ (Lemma 36.1).
So each parameter identity acquires an error, as the boost identity does in Lemma 31.18. The maps of the
elimination in Section 32.5, and the base step of Proposition 32.29, are then inverted at b by a direct bound
(Proposition 32.14) rather than by continuity from (0, 0).

**Lemma 32.11** (The parameter identities at b.) Let b ∈ ℬ̄_*, p⃗_b := (0, b − b₀, 0), and
L_(0,p⃗_b) := D_hP_2(0, p⃗_b). For Ṡ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾ ∈ 𝒮_1 and ḃ ∈ 𝔟,

    D_p⃗P_2(0, p⃗_b)(Ṡ, ḃ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾) = L_(0,p⃗_b)(χ_K(h^(≤1)_(b,♮)(Ṡ) + ġ_b(ḃ) + h_b(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾)))
                                  + E^mot_b(Ṡ, ḃ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾),    (32.9)

where E^mot_b is linear, supported in 𝒞, vanishes at b = b₀, and, near (ι⁺)°, lies in 𝒜^(𝒢+2−δ) for every δ > 0
(𝒢 = (2, 0) ∪ (2 + ℰ_ind)), with seminorms O(|b − b₀||(Ṡ, ḃ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾)|) uniformly on ℬ̄_*. So E^mot_b lies in the class
𝒴 of Section 32.1 with norm O(|b − b₀|). The tensors χ_K h^(≤1)_(b,♮)(Ṡ), χ_K ġ_b(ḃ) and χ_K h_b(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾) vanish
for t^♭_* < 10; the first has the form (31.25) with boost parameter Ṡ and ũ = 0, and the sum of the other
two the form (31.40) at b with parameters (ḃ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾) and ũ = 0 (Lemma 30.2 (P3)).

*Proof.* *Support.* By (32.4), in the interior of χ_K⁻¹(0) the background g_0 is a translate of g_(b₀) and
does not depend on b, and in the interior of χ_K⁻¹(1) it is g_b and does not depend on S or S⁽⁰⁾_1. The corrections of
the first and second kind and their counterterms are supported in 𝒞 (Lemma 31.10, Lemma 32.6). So on
the first set g′ = g_0 is Ricci flat and Υ^(E_Υ)(g_0, g_0) = 0 for every p⃗ near p⃗_b, and on the second g′ = g_0 =
g_(b′), with b′ the parameter of p⃗, again Ricci flat with Υ^(E_Υ)(g_0, g_0) = 0. Hence P_2(0, p⃗) = 0 on both sets for
every p⃗ near p⃗_b, and D_p⃗P_2(0, p⃗_b) = 0 there. The first term on the right of (32.9) vanishes on both
sets too: trivially on the first, and on the second it is L_b of h^(≤1)_(b,♮), ġ_b and h_b, which lie in ker L_b (the
proof of Lemma 31.18 for the first; the others span the nullspace of L̂_b(0) and are stationary). So E^mot_b is
supported in 𝒞. *At b₀.* p⃗_(b₀) = 0, L_(0,0) = L_(b₀), and the states at b₀ are those of Lemma 32.8, so
E^mot_(b₀) = 0 is (32.7). *Size.* Every term of E^mot_b is linear in the direction and a smooth function of
b on 𝒞. Its ingredients are: G − g_(b₀) = χ_K(g_b − g_(b₀)) ∈ |b − b₀|ρ_+²C^∞ near (ι⁺)° (on 𝒞, |x| ≥ t/10, and
g_b − g_(b₀) = O(|b − b₀||x|⁻²) with all Cartesian derivatives, Section 21.5); the states h^(≤1)_(b,♮), ġ_b and
h_b, smooth in b in 𝒜^(𝒢−δ) there (Lemma 30.2 (P3), with the loss of Remark 28.6, (P4); on
𝒞, |x| ≥ t/10, and the stationary states are O(|x|⁻²) with all Cartesian derivatives); the corrections and counterterms
built at b₀; and the values at p⃗_b of g′ − g_0 and of Υ^(E_Υ)(g′, g_0) − ϑ_tot, which are O(|b − b₀|) and supported
in 𝒞, the corrections of the second kind being linear in b − b₀. The count of the proof of Lemma 31.10, that
D_(g_0)Ric and δ*δG lie in ρ_+²Diff²_b near (ι⁺)°, takes 𝒜^(𝒢−δ) into 𝒜^(𝒢+2−δ), uniformly for b ∈ ℬ̄_*. So ∂_bE^mot_b
is bounded there by C times the size of the direction, and the mean value theorem along the segment from b₀ to b,
which lies in the ball ℬ̄_*, gives the bound. ∎

The Ṡ-part of E^mot_b is the analogue for P_2 of the error E^S_b of Lemma 31.18; it differs from it by the
S-derivative of the corrections of the second kind at p⃗_b, which has the same properties.

### 32.5 Elimination of the parameters

This section is [Hin26, Definitions 11.42, 11.44, Lemmas 11.43, 11.45, Corollary 11.46] in dimension 4 + 1, at every
base point near b₀. Let (h, p⃗) be as in Lemma 32.9, with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, and f ∈ 𝒴. Write Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(f) for
the boost parameter of Proposition 31.16 (1) for L_(h,p⃗), read at b with the leading term built at b
(Proposition 31.19): 𝒴 lies in its space of forcings for every α ∈ (1, min(a_K − 1, 3/2)) and α_+ ∈ (α, 2), and
Ṡ is determined by the forward solution, as the coefficient of t_* at K⁺ (S ↦ h_b(S) being injective,
Lemma 31.2). If Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(f) = 0, write Q_(h,p⃗)(f) := (ḃ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾_1) ∈ 𝔟 ⊕ 𝒮_1 for its parameters in
(31.40) at b, which are determined by the forward solution: a stationary tensor of positive K⁺-weight
vanishes, and (ḃ, S) ↦ ġ_b(ḃ) + h_b(S) is injective (Section 32.1). F_j → F in 𝒴 means convergence in each of
the finite-regularity spaces on which the bounds of Lemma 32.9 (c) hold, up to a regularity that d, being
large, allows; this is what Lemma 32.10 (c) gives for h → 0 in 𝒳^d. It is not convergence in ‖·‖_𝒴 alone,
which is the norm of one such space, fixed once and for all: the proof of Lemma 32.12 reads u_j two orders
above the norm in which it reads the parameters, and bounds u_j by F_j through a forward solution. For α and α_+ as
above let
𝒴^S_(α,α_+) := H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′,ℓ_I+1),α_++2,α)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−) be the space of forcings of Proposition 31.16 (1)
at the K⁺-weight α, normed in the same way; it contains 𝒴 with ‖·‖_(𝒴^S_(α,α_+)) ≤ C‖·‖_𝒴, and Ṡ_(h,p⃗) is bounded on
it uniformly for (h, p⃗) small and b ∈ ℬ̄_* (Lemma 32.9 (c)).

**Lemma 32.12** (The parameters near the reference point.) Fix b ∈ ℬ̄_*. Let (h_j, p⃗_j) → (0, p⃗_b), with
(h_j, p⃗_j) as in Lemma 32.9 with parameter b, and F_j → F in 𝒴.

(a) Ṡ_(h_j,p⃗_j)(F_j) → Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(F).

(b) If Ṡ_(h_j,p⃗_j)(F_j) = 0 for every j (so Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(F) = 0 by (a)), then Q_(h_j,p⃗_j)(F_j) → Q_(0,p⃗_b)(F).

*Proof.* Let L_j := L_(h_j,p⃗_j), L_0 := L_(0,p⃗_b), u_j the forward solution of L_ju_j = F_j and u that of L_0u = F.
Then u_j − u is the forward solution of

    L_0(u_j − u) = R_j := F_j − F − (L_j − L_0)u_j.    (32.10)

(a) Fix α ∈ (1, min(a_K − 1, 3/2)), α_+ ∈ (α, 2) and β_+ ∈ (1, min(α_+, 3/2, min Re ℰ_+)). By Proposition 31.16 (1)
for L_j (Lemma 32.9 (b)), u_j = χ_K h^(≤1)_(b,♮)(Ṡ_j) + ũ_j, bounded uniformly in j (Lemma 32.9 (c));
χ_K h^(≤1)_(b,♮)(Ṡ_j) vanishes near ℐ⁺, has K⁺-weight −1 − ε and is of ι⁺-order 2 (h^(≤1)_(b,♮) ∈ 𝒜^𝒢 near (ι⁺)°,
up to the loss of Remark 28.6, as in the proof of Lemma 31.8), and
ũ_j ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β_+,α−2)_b. L_j − L_0 has coefficients of the class (29.12) with norms
O(‖h_j‖ + |p⃗_j − p⃗_b|) (Lemma 32.9 (a), Lemma 32.4 (b)), so by (29.15)
(3/2 < ℓ_I < a_I + 1/2) (L_j − L_0)u_j → 0 in the space of forcings of Proposition 31.16 (1) for (α, α_+): the
K⁺-weights −1 − ε + a_K and α − 2 + a_K exceed α (α < a_K − 1); the ι⁺-weights ℓ_+ + 2 + m_+ − ε and
β_+ + 2 + m_+ − ε exceed α_+ + 2, the order-2 term being counted at ℓ_+ := min(2 − ε, max(a_+, min Re ℰ_+)) > 1 to
meet the hypothesis ℓ_+ ≤ max(a_+, min Re ℰ_+) of (29.15) (m_+ > 1, β_+ > 1, α_+ < 2); and the ℐ⁺-data are
(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′, ℓ_I + 1). So R_j → 0 there. By Proposition 31.16 (1) for L_0,
u_j − u = χ_K h^(≤1)_(b,♮)(Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(R_j)) + ũ_(R_j) with ũ_(R_j) of K⁺-weight α − 2 > −1; also
u_j − u = χ_K h^(≤1)_(b,♮)(Ṡ_j − Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(F)) + (ũ_j − ũ). A K⁺-weight above −1 forces the coefficient of t_* to
vanish, and S ↦ h_b(S) is injective (Lemma 31.2), so
Ṡ_j − Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(F) = Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(R_j) → 0.

(b) Now Proposition 31.27 for L_j gives u_j = χ_K ġ_b(ḃ_j) + χ_K h_b(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾_j) + ũ_j, bounded uniformly
(Lemma 32.9 (c)), with K⁺-weight −ε and ι⁺-order 2 for the first two terms ((32.2)) and
ũ_j ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β_+,α_K−2)_b, β_+ ∈ (1, min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+)). As in (a), (L_j − L_0)u_j → 0 in 𝒴: K⁺-weight
a_K − ε ≥ α_K for ε ≤ a_K − α_K, ι⁺-weights ℓ_+ + 2 + m_+ − ε (ℓ_+ as in (a)) and β_+ + 2 + m_+ − ε, both above
4 − ε as ℓ_+ + m_+ > 2. So R_j → 0 in 𝒴, and R_j is real. u_j − u has K⁺-weight −ε > −1, so Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(R_j) = 0 (by
the uniqueness used in (a)), and Proposition 31.27 for L_0 gives
u_j − u = χ_K ġ_b(ḃ_(R_j)) + χ_K h_b(Ṡ_(R_j)) + ũ_(R_j) with (ḃ_(R_j), Ṡ_(R_j)) = Q_(0,p⃗_b)(R_j) → 0. Comparing with
u_j − u = χ_K ġ_b(ḃ_j − ḃ) + χ_K h_b(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾_j − Ṡ⁽⁰⁾) + (ũ_j − ũ): the stationary tensor
ġ_b(ḃ_j − ḃ − ḃ_(R_j)) + h_b(Ṡ⁽⁰⁾_j − Ṡ⁽⁰⁾ − Ṡ_(R_j)) times χ_K has K⁺-weight α_K − 2 > 0, so it vanishes on X°, and
by injectivity Q_(h_j,p⃗_j)(F_j) − Q_(0,p⃗_b)(F) = Q_(0,p⃗_b)(R_j) → 0. ∎

The continuity of Lemma 32.12 is a statement at fixed b, with L_(0,p⃗_b) as the reference; no continuity across
b is claimed or used. The bounds of the elimination across b come from Proposition 32.14 below.

**Definition 32.13** ([Hin26, Definition 11.42] in dimension 4 + 1.) For p⃗′ = (S′, b′, S″) write
p⃗′^(<0) := S′ and p⃗′^(=0) := (b′, S″) ∈ 𝔟 ⊕ 𝒮_1. The first eliminates the asymptotic term of K⁺-order (−1, 0) (the
boost), the second the two of order (0, 0) (ḃ and Ṡ⁽⁰⁾_1); [Hin26]'s third, of order (0, 1), is absent.

*The boost map and the reduced map.* For (h, p⃗) as in Lemma 32.9 with parameter b, write f^•_(h,p⃗) for
D_p⃗P_2(h, p⃗) in the direction • (Lemma 32.10), f^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(b′, S″) := f^b_(h,p⃗)(b′) + f^s1_(h,p⃗)(S″), and
let the *boost map* be the linear map S^(−1)_(h,p⃗) := Ṡ_(h,p⃗) ∘ f^S_(h,p⃗) of 𝒮_1 ≅ ℝ⁴. Where it is invertible put,
for f ∈ 𝒴 and p⃗′^(=0) ∈ 𝔟 ⊕ 𝒮_1,

    p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗)(f, p⃗′^(=0))
        := (S^(−1)_(h,p⃗))⁻¹(Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(f) − Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(f^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(=0)))),    (32.11)

and F_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(=0)) := −D_p⃗P_2(h, p⃗)(p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗)(0, p⃗′^(=0)), p⃗′^(=0)). By linearity
Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(F_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(=0))) = −S^(−1)_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗)(0, p⃗′^(=0))) − Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(f^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(=0))),
which is 0, so the *reduced map*

    M_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(=0)) := Q_(h,p⃗)(F_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(=0)))

is defined; it is linear on 𝔟 ⊕ 𝒮_1. (In Lemma 32.15 and Definition 32.16, p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗) is the unique
choice of the boost and M_(h,p⃗) = ṗ^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(0, ·).)

**Proposition 32.14** (The elimination maps at b; Lemma 32.15, Lemma 32.17 and
Corollary 32.18 at b.) Let (h, p⃗) be as in Lemma 32.9, with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*. There are C and a
smallness of (h, p⃗ − p⃗_b), uniform on ℬ̄_*, with |S^(−1)_(h,p⃗) − id| ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|); after
shrinking ℬ_* and that smallness, S^(−1)_(h,p⃗) is invertible with inverse of norm at most 2, the map
A_(h,p⃗) := p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗)(0, ·) satisfies |A_(h,p⃗)| ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|), and

    |S^(−1)_(h,p⃗) − id| + |M_(h,p⃗) + id| ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|).    (32.12)

So, after shrinking ℬ_* and the smallness of (h, p⃗ − p⃗_b) once more, both maps are invertible with inverses of norm
at most 2, and Lemma 32.15, Lemma 32.17 and Corollary 32.18 hold at b, with constants uniform in b.
The same bounds give the base step of Proposition 32.29 at b, and the bounds on (S^(−1)_(h,p⃗))⁻¹ that the tame
estimates of Chapter 35 use.

*Proof.* At b the maps are built from Ṡ_(h,p⃗) (Proposition 31.16 (1) for L_(h,p⃗)) and Q_(h,p⃗)
(Proposition 31.27 for L_(h,p⃗), with the states at b), which are bounded on 𝒴 uniformly in b (Lemma 30.2
(P1), (P4), Lemma 32.9 (c)).

*Two bounds at fixed b.* (1) ‖f^•_(h,p⃗) − f^•_(0,p⃗_b)‖_𝒴 ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b|) per unit direction. Indeed f^• is
smooth in (h, p⃗), and the bounds of Lemma 32.10, which hold at b, apply to its derivative in (h, p⃗): the
h-derivative by (31.21), the p⃗-derivative by the count of (31.24); its terms are again polynomial
in the differences of the metrics, with coefficients smooth in their inverses. The mean value theorem along the segment
from (0, p⃗_b) gives the bound.

(2) Let ‖·‖^+_𝒴 be a norm of the same kind as ‖·‖_𝒴 at a larger regularity and a smaller ε, in which the bounds of
Lemma 32.9 (c) bound the forward solutions u_1 of the count below at the regularity of ‖·‖_𝒴 plus 2, d being
large enough for Lemma 32.10 (c) in it as well. For F ∈ 𝒴, Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(F) − Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(F) has norm at most
C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b|)‖F‖^+_𝒴.
And for F_1, F_2 ∈ 𝒴 with Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(F_1) = 0 = Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(F_2), where alone Q_(h,p⃗) and Q_(0,p⃗_b) are defined,

    |Q_(h,p⃗)(F_1) − Q_(0,p⃗_b)(F_2)| ≤ C‖F_1 − F_2‖_𝒴 + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b|)‖F_1‖^+_𝒴.

This is the comparison of Lemma 32.12 made quantitative. The second norm is not ‖·‖_𝒴: the count below reads
u_1 two orders above ‖·‖_𝒴, and bounds it by F_1 through a forward solution. Let u_1, u_2 be the forward solutions of
L_(h,p⃗)u_1 = F_1 and L_(0,p⃗_b)u_2 = F_2. Then L_(0,p⃗_b)(u_1 − u_2) = R := F_1 − F_2 − (L_(h,p⃗) − L_(0,p⃗_b))u_1. Both
backgrounds equal g_b near K⁺ (Lemma 29.11), so L_(h,p⃗) − L_(0,p⃗_b) has coefficients of K⁺-weight a_K there; at
ι⁺ it gains as in the proof of Lemma 32.12; and its coefficients have size O(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b|).
*The boost parameters.* Fix α ∈ (1, min(a_K − 1, 3/2)) and α_+ ∈ (α, 2). For a general F_1 ∈ 𝒴, u_1 carries a boost
term of K⁺-weight −1 − ε, so (L_(h,p⃗) − L_(0,p⃗_b))u_1 has K⁺-weight only a_K − 1 − ε, which may lie below α_K: R need
not lie in 𝒴. It lies in 𝒴^S_(α,α_+) of Section 32.5, by the count of the proof of Lemma 32.12 (a), with
‖(L_(h,p⃗) − L_(0,p⃗_b))u_1‖_(𝒴^S_(α,α_+)) ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b|)‖F_1‖^+_𝒴, u_1 being bounded by F_1 through
Proposition 31.16 (1) for L_(h,p⃗), uniformly (Lemma 32.9 (c)). With F_1 = F_2 = F, the boost terms of u_1
and u_2 are built from the same state at b, so the difference of the boost parameters is Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(R), of size at
most C‖R‖_(𝒴^S_(α,α_+)) ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b|)‖F‖^+_𝒴. *The parameters Q.* Under the condition
Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(F_1) = 0 = Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(F_2), u_1 has no boost term, so it has K⁺-weight −ε and is bounded by F_1 in the space of
Proposition 31.27 for L_(h,p⃗), uniformly; as in the proof of Lemma 32.12 (b), the K⁺-weight a_K − ε ≥ α_K
then gives ‖(L_(h,p⃗) − L_(0,p⃗_b))u_1‖_𝒴 ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b|)‖F_1‖^+_𝒴, and R ∈ 𝒴. Also u_1 − u_2 has no boost term,
so Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(R) = 0, and Q_(h,p⃗)(F_1) − Q_(0,p⃗_b)(F_2) = Q_(0,p⃗_b)(R), by the uniqueness in the proof of
Lemma 32.12 (b), which uses the injectivity of (ḃ, Ṡ) ↦ ġ_b(ḃ) + h_b(Ṡ). Its size is at most C‖R‖_𝒴.

*The boost map.* By (32.9), χ_K h^(≤1)_(b,♮)(S′) is the forward solution of
L_(0,p⃗_b)u = f^S_(0,p⃗_b)(S′) − E^mot_b(S′, 0, 0), so Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(f^S_(0,p⃗_b)(S′)) = S′ + Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(E^mot_b(S′, 0, 0)).
Hence

    S^(−1)_(h,p⃗)(S′) − S′ = Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(f^S_(h,p⃗)(S′) − f^S_(0,p⃗_b)(S′)) + (Ṡ_(h,p⃗) − Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b))(f^S_(0,p⃗_b)(S′))
                            + Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(E^mot_b(S′, 0, 0)),

and by (1), (2) and Lemma 32.11 the three terms are at most C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|)|S′|, as
‖f^S_(0,p⃗_b)(S′)‖^+_𝒴 ≤ C|S′| (Lemma 32.10 (c)).

*The reduced map.* At (0, p⃗_b), (32.11) gives
S′_0 := A_(0,p⃗_b)p⃗′^(=0) = −(S^(−1)_(0,p⃗_b))⁻¹Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(f^(=0)_(0,p⃗_b)(b′, S″)). By (32.9),
χ_K(ġ_b(b′) + h_b(S″)) is the forward solution of L_(0,p⃗_b)u = f^(=0)_(0,p⃗_b)(b′, S″) − E^mot_b(0, b′, S″); it has
K⁺-weight −ε > −1, so no boost term, and Q_(0,p⃗_b) of that forcing is (b′, S″). So
Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(f^(=0)_(0,p⃗_b)(b′, S″)) = Ṡ_(0,p⃗_b)(E^mot_b(0, b′, S″)), |S′_0| ≤ C|b − b₀||p⃗′^(=0)|, and

    M_(0,p⃗_b)(p⃗′^(=0)) = −p⃗′^(=0) − Q_(0,p⃗_b)(E^mot_b(0, b′, S″) + f^S_(0,p⃗_b)(S′_0)),

whence |M_(0,p⃗_b) + id| ≤ C|b − b₀|. For (h, p⃗) near (0, p⃗_b), M_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(=0)) = Q_(h,p⃗)(F_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(=0))) with
Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(F_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(=0))) = 0, and likewise at (0, p⃗_b). So (2), for the pair (F_(h,p⃗), F_(0,p⃗_b)), bounds
M_(h,p⃗) − M_(0,p⃗_b) by C‖F_(h,p⃗) − F_(0,p⃗_b)‖_𝒴 + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b|) per unit p⃗′^(=0), F_(h,p⃗) and
f^(=0)_(0,p⃗_b) being bounded per unit p⃗′^(=0) in ‖·‖^+_𝒴 (Lemma 32.10 (c), with the inverse of the boost map,
of norm at most 2); and (1) bounds ‖F_(h,p⃗) − F_(0,p⃗_b)‖_𝒴, with A_(h,p⃗) − A_(0,p⃗_b) bounded the same way through
(32.11), (1), (2) and the bound on the boost map. This proves the bound on A_(h,p⃗) and
(32.12), and the Neumann series gives the inverses. The proofs of Lemma 32.15, Lemma 32.17 and
Corollary 32.18 below, and the base step of Proposition 32.29, use, beyond Lemma 32.9 (c), only these
inverses and their bounds. ∎

**Lemma 32.15** ([Hin26, Lemma 11.43] in dimension 4 + 1.) For (h, p⃗) small as in
Proposition 32.14, with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, f ∈ 𝒴 and p⃗′^(=0) ∈ 𝔟 ⊕ 𝒮_1 there is a unique
S′ =: p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗)(f, p⃗′^(=0)) ∈ 𝒮_1 such that the forward solution of

    L_(h,p⃗)u = f − D_p⃗P_2(h, p⃗)(S′, p⃗′^(=0))    (32.13)

has vanishing boost parameter. It is linear in (f, p⃗′^(=0)), the forcing of (32.13) lies in 𝒴, and
p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗)(f, p⃗′^(=0)) = p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗)(f, 0) + A_(h,p⃗)p⃗′^(=0),
with |A_(h,p⃗)| ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|) in ℒ(𝔟 ⊕ 𝒮_1, 𝒮_1); at b = b₀, A_(h,p⃗) → 0 as (h, p⃗) → 0.

*Proof.* By Lemma 32.10 and ℓ_I ≤ a_I, f^S_(h,p⃗)(S′) and f^s1_(h,p⃗)(S″) lie in 𝒴 (ℐ⁺-data
(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′, a_I + 1), ι⁺-weight a_+ + 2 + min(2, m_+) − ε > 4 − ε, zero near K⁺), and so does f^b_(h,p⃗)(b′) (zero
near ℐ⁺, ι⁺-weight a_+ + 4 − ε, K⁺-weight a_K > α_K); all are real. By linearity the boost parameter of the forward
solution of (32.13) is Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(f) − S^(−1)_(h,p⃗)(S′) − Ṡ_(h,p⃗)(f^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(p⃗′^(=0))). By
Proposition 32.14, S^(−1)_(h,p⃗) is invertible, so it vanishes exactly for S′ given by (32.11),
which is linear in (f, p⃗′^(=0)); the last claim is the bound on A_(h,p⃗) of Proposition 32.14. ∎

At (0, 0) the boost map is the identity, S^(−1)_(0,0)(S′) = S′: the forward solution χ_K h^(≤1)_♮(S′) of
L_(b₀)u = f^S_(0,0)(S′) (Lemma 32.8) has the form (31.25) with ũ = 0. And A_(0,0) = 0: the forward
solution of L_(b₀)u = f^(=0)_(0,0)(b′, S″) is χ_K(ġ(b′) + h(S″)), of K⁺-weight −ε > −1, so it has no boost term.

**Definition 32.16** ([Hin26, Definition 11.44] in dimension 4 + 1.) For f ∈ 𝒴 and p⃗′^(=0), let
ṗ^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(f, p⃗′^(=0)) := Q_(h,p⃗)(F), F the forcing of (32.13) with S′ = p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗)(f, p⃗′^(=0)): the
parameters (ḃ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾_1) of (31.40) for the forward solution of (32.13). Both p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗) and
ṗ^(=0)_(h,p⃗) are linear in (f, p⃗′^(=0)), and ṗ^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(0, ·) = M_(h,p⃗).

**Lemma 32.17** ([Hin26, Lemma 11.45] in dimension 4 + 1.) For (h, p⃗) small as in Proposition 32.14,
with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, the map p⃗′^(=0) ↦ ṗ^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(0, p⃗′^(=0)) is within C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|) of
−id on 𝔟 ⊕ 𝒮_1, hence invertible, with inverse of norm at most 2. At (h, p⃗) = (0, 0) it is −id.

*Proof.* The map is M_(h,p⃗), and the bound is (32.12). At (0, 0), A_(0,0) = 0, and the forward solution of
L_(b₀)u = −f^(=0)_(0,0)(b′, S″) is −χ_K(ġ(b′) + h(S″)) (Lemma 32.8), which has the form (31.40) with
ũ = 0; so ṗ^(=0)_(0,0)(0, p⃗′^(=0)) = −p⃗′^(=0). ∎

[Hin26, Lemma 11.45] says "close to the identity": its proof solves with +D_((h,p⃗))P(0, 0, p⃗′^(=0)), while its
Definition 11.44 has the forcing f − D_((h,p⃗))P(0, p⃗′), for which the map is close to −id, as here; either is
invertible.

**Corollary 32.18** ([Hin26, Corollary 11.46] in dimension 4 + 1.) For (h, p⃗) small as in
Proposition 32.14, with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, and f ∈ 𝒴 there is a unique p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(f) ∈ 𝒮_1 ⊕ 𝔟 ⊕ 𝒮_1 such that
the forward solution of

    L_(h,p⃗)u = f − D_p⃗P_2(h, p⃗)(p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(f))    (32.14)

has neither a boost term nor the parameters of (31.40); therefore

    u ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β_+,α_K−2)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−)     for every β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+),    (32.15)

and u decays at K⁺ (α_K > 2). p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(f) and u are linear and continuous in f, with bounds uniform in b and in
