(h, p⃗) small.

*Proof.* By linearity, ṗ^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(f, p⃗′^(=0)) = ṗ^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(f, 0) + ṗ^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(0, p⃗′^(=0)), and by
Lemma 32.17 there is a unique p⃗′^(=0) =: p⃗′^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(f) for which it vanishes; put
p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(f) := (p⃗′^(<0)_(h,p⃗)(f, p⃗′^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(f)), p⃗′^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(f)). The forward solution of (32.14)
has no boost term (Lemma 32.15) and (ḃ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾_1) = 0, so (31.40) gives u = ũ, which is
(32.15). Uniqueness: a p⃗′ with these properties has vanishing boost parameter, which fixes p⃗′^(<0) given
p⃗′^(=0) (Lemma 32.15), and then ṗ^(=0)_(h,p⃗)(f, p⃗′^(=0)) = 0 fixes p⃗′^(=0) (Lemma 32.17).
Continuity: every map involved is linear and continuous (Proposition 31.16 (1), Proposition 31.27,
Lemma 32.10, finite-dimensional inverses), with the bounds of Lemma 32.9 (c) and
Proposition 32.14, uniform in b. ∎

[Hin26, Corollary 11.46] concludes u ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,3+ε_I),1−ε,α_K−2)_b with α_K ∈ (2, 2 + ε_K); in dimension 4 + 1
the ι⁺-weight is min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+) − ε, by Proposition 31.27.

### 32.6 Decaying centre-of-mass motions: setting

This section and the next three are [Hin26, Section 11.7] (pp. 262–273) in dimension 4 + 1. The scheme is an induction
on the K⁺-rate α: at each level the forward solution is expanded into finitely many decaying centre-of-mass motions
χ_K t_*^(−λ+1)(log t_*)^k h(S) plus a remainder, and these are then eliminated by gauge modifications.

Everything of Section 32.1 is kept: 𝔟, ℰ_ind with (32.2)–(32.3), 𝒢, ℓ_I with ℓ_I ≤ a_I, the
translated background (32.4), the cut-offs, 𝒞, Θ, the conventions (32.1) and the identities
(i)–(iii). ℰ_ind is enlarged to contain also the index sets of Proposition 23.34 (2) at b₀ (those of the 1-forms ω̆^i
of Section 32.7); everything of Section 32.1–Section 32.5 holds with the enlarged set, which only
strengthens the conditions on ℰ_+ there. ℰ^ι_ind is the index set of (26.56), and ℰ^♯_+ is the set of
(29.32) with Ĕ_+ = ∅, as in Proposition 31.21; min Re ℰ^♯_+ = λ_♯ = 3/2 + (1 − e_Υ)γ_Υ. Fix an index set
ℰ_++ with

    ℰ^♯_+ ∩ {Re < 2} ⊂ ℰ_++ ⊂ ℰ_+,    min Re ℰ_++ ≥ λ_♯,
    ℰ_++ + (ℰ^ι_ind ∪ ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ_+) ⊂ ℰ_++;    (32.16)

for instance the least index set containing ℰ^♯_+ ∩ {Re < 2} with the last property, provided ℰ_+ contains
ℰ^♯_+ ∩ {Re < 2} and ℰ_+ + (ℰ^ι_ind ∪ ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ_+) ⊂ ℰ_+ (conditions on ℰ_+ alone, as ℰ^♯_+, ℰ^ι_ind and ℰ_ind do not
depend on it). Then ℰ_++ + ℰ_++ ⊂ ℰ_++, and

    ℳ := {(λ, k) ∈ ℰ_++ : Re λ < 2}    (32.17)

is finite, with Re λ ∈ [λ_♯, 2). Its exponents may be complex. ℰ_++ is taken closed under conjugation (as ℰ^♯_+,
ℰ^ι_ind, ℰ_ind and ℰ_+ may be, coming from real operators); the motion parameters S^((λ−1,k))_1 below lie in 𝒮_(1,ℂ)
with S^((λ̄−1,k))_1 equal to the complex conjugate of S^((λ−1,k))_1 (for real λ, S^((λ−1,k))_1 ∈ 𝒮_1), which makes the
motion terms real, and the coefficients S_(λ,k) of a real u in (32.22) have the same symmetry. For
α ∈ (2, 3) put ℳ_α := {(λ, k) ∈ ℳ : Re λ − 1 < α − 2}.

*Admissible levels.* α ∈ (2, min(a_K, 3)) is *admissible* if α − 2 ≠ Re λ − 1 and α − Re λ ∉ {−Re μ} ∪ Re π_1ℰ_K
for every λ ∈ π_1ℳ and every root μ of the indicial family 𝒲(ℓ_K) of Section 26.10, with ℰ_K the index set of
Lemma 26.24 and π_1 the projection to the first component: a finite set of exclusions in (2, 3), the roots
being real and discrete. ℳ_(α_0) = ∅ for α_0 < λ_♯ + 1.

*Forcings.* For α ∈ (2, 3) let 𝒴_1(α) := ⋂_ε H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′,ℓ_I+1),4−ε,α)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−) (the class 𝒴 of
Section 32.1 with α for α_K), let 𝒴_2(α) be the sections supported in supp χ^♯_K ((29.2); so
vanishing near ℐ⁺ and for t^♭_* < 10) lying in ⋂_ε H^(∞,∞,(ℰ_+++2,4−ε),α)_b, and 𝒴(α) := 𝒴_1(α) + 𝒴_2(α), real
sections ([Hin26, (11.155)] in dimension 4 + 1). "h small" means as in Section 32.1. The base points have
parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, as throughout. 𝒴(α) is a Fréchet space, and bounds in it are taken in one fixed seminorm
‖·‖_(𝒴(α)): the quotient norm on 𝒴_1(α) + 𝒴_2(α) of the two defining spaces at one finite regularity and one ε > 0.
The regularity is taken so large, and ε so small, that the linear maps used below, which are continuous on 𝒴(α)
uniformly for (h, p⃗) small and b ∈ ℬ̄_* (in the proof of Lemma 32.27, the maps from the forcing f′ of its
Step 0 to the coefficients and to the remainder), are bounded in this seminorm. In the same way ‖·‖_(α′) is one fixed
seminorm of the space of the hypothesis of Lemma 32.27 at the level α′, of regularity at least that of
‖·‖_(𝒴(α)) plus 2, α the level above α′ there, as Step 0 of the proof of that lemma bounds (L − L_b)u in ‖·‖_(𝒴(α))
by ‖u‖_(α′). The bounds of Proposition 32.29 (i) are taken in a second seminorm ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α)), the same quotient
norm at a larger regularity and a smaller ε, which depends on the seminorm of the solution bounded and is fixed in the
proof: its step bounds the solution at a lower level α′ in ‖·‖_(α′) by (i) at α′, so its seminorm of the forcing must
bound the seminorm of (i) at α′ as well as ‖·‖_(𝒴(α)). For each seminorm that (i) bounds these choices are finitely
many and are made first; d is then taken so large that the bounds and the continuity used below hold in them,
uniformly for h small: those of Lemma 32.24 (b)–(c) and Lemma 32.25, and the count of Step 0 of
the proof of Lemma 32.27. F_j → F in 𝒴(α) is meant as F_j → F in 𝒴 is in Section 32.5, at the regularities
that d allows: the step of Proposition 32.29 (ii) applies (ii) at the level below to forcings that converge only as
Lemma 32.24 (c) allows for h_j → 0 in 𝒳^d.

### 32.7 Corrections of the third kind and the operator

*Generalised gauge 1-forms.* By Proposition 23.34 (2) at b₀, for S ∈ 𝒮_1 there are stationary 1-forms
ω̆^i(S) := ω̆^((0),i)_(b₀,s1)(S), i = 0, …, 4, linear in S, with ω̆⁰ = ω_s1, ω̆¹ = ω̆ (Section 31.4),
ω̆^i ∈ 𝒜^((−i,0)∪(−i+ℰ_ind)) for i = 2, 3, 4, and

    ω^(≤k) = Σ_(i≤k) (k!/(k − i)!) t_*^(k−i) ω̆^i ∈ ker □^Υ_(b₀)   for k ≤ 4,

with □^Υ_(b₀) = 2δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀))δ*_(g_(b₀)) ((23.29)). For a function a of t_* put
ω^(≤4)(aS) := Σ_(i=0)^4 a^((i))(t_*)ω̆^i(S), so that ω^(≤4)(t_*^k S) = ω^(≤k)(S) for k ≤ 4.

**Definition 32.19** (Corrections of the third kind; [Hin26, Definition 11.47] in dimension 4 + 1.) For
(λ, k) ∈ ℳ let a_(λ,k)(t_*) := t_*^(−λ+1)(log t_*)^k (on Ω_*, where t_* ≥ 1), and for S ∈ 𝒮_(1,ℂ)

    m_(λ,k)(S) := χ_K δ*_(g_(b₀)) ω^(≤4)(a_(λ,k)S),
    h^((λ−1,k))_s1(S) := −[δ*_(g_(b₀)), χ_K] ω^(≤4)(a_(λ,k)S) = −dχ_K ⊗_s ω^(≤4)(a_(λ,k)S),
    ϑ^((λ−1,k))_s1(S) := δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)) m_(λ,k)(S),
    ϑ^((λ−1,k))_(s1,♯) := ϑ^((λ−1,k))_s1 − δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)) h^((λ−1,k))_s1,

the last the counterterm of [Hin26, Remark 11.27], as in Definition 31.9 and Definition 32.5. m_(λ,k)(S) is the
cut-off centre-of-mass motion, the tensor of [Hin26, (11.181)].

**Lemma 32.20** ([Hin26, (11.152a)–(11.152b)] in dimension 4 + 1.) Let (λ, k) ∈ ℳ and a := a_(λ,k).
There are stationary operators A_1, A_2 with

    □^Υ_(b₀) ω^(≤4)(aS) = a^((5))(A_1ω̆⁴ + A_2ω̆³) + a^((6))A_2ω̆⁴.    (32.18)

Near (ι⁺)°, with ℱ := (0, 0) ∪ ℰ_ind: ω^(≤4)(aS) ∈ 𝒜^((λ−1,k)+ℱ), m_(λ,k)(S) ∈ 𝒜^((λ,k)+ℱ),
h^((λ−1,k))_s1(S) ∈ 𝒜^((λ,k)+ℱ), ϑ^((λ−1,k))_s1(S), ϑ^((λ−1,k))_(s1,♯)(S) ∈ 𝒜^((λ+1,k)+ℱ) and
D_(g_0)Ric(h^((λ−1,k))_s1(S)) ∈ 𝒜^((λ+2,k)+ℱ) (g_0 as in Lemma 31.10). h^((λ−1,k))_s1(S) is supported in 𝒞;
m_(λ,k)(S) and ϑ^((λ−1,k))_s1(S) in supp χ_K, and ϑ^((λ−1,k))_s1(S) has K⁺-weight Re λ + 4 − ε for every ε > 0.
Finally

    m_(λ,k)(S) − χ_K a_(λ,k) h(S)   has K⁺-weight Re λ − ε for every ε > 0.    (32.19)

All seminorms are O(|S|).

*Proof.* (32.18): □ := □^Υ_(b₀) is stationary and of second order in ∂_(t_*), so
□(φ(t_*)v) = Σ_(m=0)^2 φ^((m))A_mv for stationary v, with stationary A_m. Hence □ω^(≤4)(aS) = Σ_(j≤6) a^((j))B_j,
B_j := Σ_m A_mω̆^(j−m) (ω̆^i := 0 for i < 0 or i > 4). With a = t_*^k, k ≤ 4, this is □ω^(≤k) = 0, whose
t_*⁰-coefficient is k!B_k; so B_j = 0 for j ≤ 4, and B_5 = A_1ω̆⁴ + A_2ω̆³, B_6 = A_2ω̆⁴. *Orders.* Near (ι⁺)°, |x|
∼ t_* ∼ ρ_+⁻¹, so ω̆^i ∈ 𝒜^((−i,0)+ℱ) there (for i = 0, 1 by Section 31.4: ω_s1 − ω̄_s1 ∈ 𝒜^𝒢 with ω̄_s1 of
constant Cartesian components, and ω̆ − ω̆̄_s1 ∈ 𝒜^((1,0)+ℰ_ind) with ω̆̄_s1 homogeneous of degree 1), and
a^((i)) ∈ 𝒜^((λ−1+i,k)); so each term of ω^(≤4)(aS) lies in 𝒜^((λ−1,k)+ℱ). δ*_(g_(b₀)), D_(g_0)Ric and
δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)) lie in ρ_+Diff¹_b, ρ_+²Diff²_b and ρ_+Diff¹_b there, and dχ_K ∈ ρ_+C^∞ (the proof of
Lemma 31.10), which gives the ι⁺-orders. *Supports* are clear. *K⁺.* Near K⁺, χ_K = 1 and
ϑ^((λ−1,k))_s1 = ½□ω^(≤4)(aS), which by (32.18) is a^((5)) and a^((6)) times stationary tensors smooth on
compact spatial sets, of K⁺-weight Re λ + 4 − ε. (32.19): δ*_(g_(b₀))(a^((i))ω̆^i) =
a^((i)) (δ*_(g_(b₀)))^(0)ω̆^i + a^((i+1)) dt_* ⊗_s ω̆^i, and (δ*_(g_(b₀)))^(0)ω̆⁰ = h(S); every other term carries
a^((j)), j ≥ 1, of K⁺-weight Re λ − ε. ∎

Here (δ*_(g_(b₀)))^(0) is the zero energy operator of (23.28), δ*_(g_(b₀)) = (δ*_(g_(b₀)))^(0) +
dt_* ⊗_s (·)∂_(t_*); so δ*_(g_(b₀))(φ(t_*)v) = φ(δ*_(g_(b₀)))^(0)v + φ′ dt_* ⊗_s v for stationary v, which is also
(32.1).

**Definition 32.21** (The operator with the motions; [Hin26, Definition 11.48] in dimension 4 + 1.) For
p⃗ = (p⃗_(≤0), (S^((λ−1,k))_1)_((λ,k)∈ℳ)), p⃗_(≤0) := (S, b − b₀, S⁽⁰⁾_1), small and h small, with g_0 := g_(p⃗_(≤0))
((32.4)), let h_(tot,2)(p⃗_(≤0)) and ϑ_(tot,2)(p⃗_(≤0)) be the h_tot and ϑ_tot of Definition 32.7,

    h_tot(p⃗) := h_(tot,2)(p⃗_(≤0)) + Σ_((λ,k)∈ℳ) h^((λ−1,k))_s1(S^((λ−1,k))_1),
    ϑ_tot(p⃗) := ϑ_(tot,2)(p⃗_(≤0)) + Σ_((λ,k)∈ℳ) ϑ^((λ−1,k))_(s1,♯)(S^((λ−1,k))_1),

and, with g′ := g_0 + h_tot(p⃗) + h,

    P_3(h, p⃗) := Ric(g′) − δ*_(g_0,E_C)(Υ^(E_Υ)(g′, g_0) − ϑ_tot(p⃗)),    (32.20)

and L_(h,p⃗) := D_hP_3(·, p⃗) at h. P_3 = P_2 where the motion parameters vanish.

**Lemma 32.22** (The motion identity; [Hin26, (11.137), (11.154)] in dimension 4 + 1.) For (λ, k) ∈ ℳ and
S ∈ 𝒮_(1,ℂ), D_p⃗P_3(0, 0)(S^((λ−1,k))_1 = S) = L_(b₀)(m_(λ,k)(S)), and m_(λ,k)(S), vanishing for t^♭_* < 10, is its
forward solution (Proposition 17.14). The identities (32.7) hold for P_3.

*Proof.* At p⃗ = 0, g′ = g_0 = g_(b₀) and Υ^(E_Υ)(g_(b₀), g_(b₀)) − ϑ_tot(0) = 0; g_0 does not depend on
S^((λ−1,k))_1, and, by (32.1),

    ġ′ = h^((λ−1,k))_s1(S) = χ_K δ*ω^(≤4)(aS) − δ*(χ_K ω^(≤4)(aS)) = m_(λ,k)(S) − δ*(χ_K ω^(≤4)(aS)).

As in Lemma 32.8, DP_3 = DRic(ġ′) − δ*_(E_C)(D_1Υ ġ′ − ϑ^((λ−1,k))_(s1,♯)(S)) with D_1Υ = −δ_(E_Υ)G by (ii),
so DP_3 = DRic(m_(λ,k)(S)) + δ*_(E_C)ϑ^((λ−1,k))_s1(S) by (iii) and the counterterm, which is
L_(b₀)m_(λ,k)(S) = DRic(m) + δ*_(E_C)δ_(E_Υ)Gm by Definition 32.19. The rest is Lemma 32.8, as P_3 = P_2 on
the other directions at p⃗ = 0. ∎

As in [Hin26], the identity is exact because the gauge term is the full δ_(E_Υ)G of the cut-off motion, not a
commutator; (32.18) makes it decay to K⁺-order Re λ + 4, which is why four generalised gauge 1-forms are
used ([Hin26, Remark 11.39]).

**Lemma 32.23** (The linearisation in h.) Let p⃗ (with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*) and h be small. Then
h_tot(p⃗) ∈ 𝒳^∞ with ‖h_tot(p⃗)‖_(𝒳^k) ≤ C_k|p⃗|, L_(h,p⃗) = L^(g′,g_0), and Lemma 32.9 (b)–(c) hold for
L_(h,p⃗).

*Proof.* As Lemma 32.9, with Lemma 32.20: the new terms are supported in 𝒞 and lie in
𝒜^((λ,k)+ℱ) ⊂ 𝒜^(ℰ_++) ⊂ 𝒜^(ℰ_+) near (ι⁺)° by (32.16). ∎

**Lemma 32.24** ([Hin26, Lemma 11.49] in dimension 4 + 1.) Let p⃗ (with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*) and h ∈ 𝒳^k,
k ≥ 5, be small.

(a) The derivatives f^S_(h,p⃗), f^b_(h,p⃗), f^s1_(h,p⃗) of P_3 in S, b, S⁽⁰⁾_1 satisfy Lemma 32.10 up to terms
lying in 𝒴_1(α) for every α ∈ (2, 3); in particular they lie in 𝒴_1(α) for α ≤ a_K (with ℓ_I ≤ a_I).

(b) For (λ, k) ∈ ℳ, f^((λ,k))_(h,p⃗)(S) := D_p⃗P_3(h, p⃗)(S^((λ−1,k))_1 = S) is supported in supp χ_K and lies in
H^(k−2,∞,((λ+2,k)+ℱ+((0,0)∪ℰ_+),4−ε),Re λ+4−ε)_b, with norm O(|S|), so in 𝒴_2(α) when h ∈ 𝒳^∞ (as "h small"
requires).

(c) All are linear in the direction, continuous in (h, p⃗), and at (0, 0) given by Lemma 32.22.

*Proof.* (a) The proof of Lemma 32.10: its counts use h_tot only through g′ − η ∈ H^(k,(ℰ_+,a_+))_b near
(ι⁺)°, which still holds (Lemma 32.23). The derivative in each of S, b, S⁽⁰⁾_1 falls on the motion terms only
through δ*_(g_0,E_C), which depends on these parameters through g_0 and acts on
ϑ_mot := Σ_((λ,k)∈ℳ) ϑ^((λ−1,k))_(s1,♯)(S^((λ−1,k))_1), nonzero near K⁺. The extra term (∂δ*_(g_0,E_C))ϑ_mot is
linear in the motion parameters, supported in supp χ_K, of ι⁺-order at least Re λ + 4 (the derivative of g_0 has
ι⁺-order 2, and ϑ order λ + 1 by Lemma 32.20) and of K⁺-weight Re λ + 4 − ε ≥ λ_♯ + 4 − ε > 3, and continuous
in (h, p⃗); so it lies in 𝒴_1(α) for every α ∈ (2, 3). (b) P_3 depends on S^((λ−1,k))_1 only through h^((λ−1,k))_s1
(in 𝒞) and ϑ^((λ−1,k))_(s1,♯) (in supp χ_K), linearly; so, with h′ := h^((λ−1,k))_s1(S) and the definition of the
counterterm,

    f^((λ,k)) = D_(g′)Ric(h′) − δ*_(g_0,E_C)([D_1Υ(g′, g_0) − D_1Υ(g_(b₀), g_(b₀))]h′ − ϑ^((λ−1,k))_s1(S)).

With D_(g′)Ric ∈ ρ_+²(C^∞ + H^((ℰ_+,a_+))_b)Diff²_b, δ*_(g_0,E_C) ∈ ρ_+Diff¹_b, the bracket linear in
(g′ − g_(b₀), g_0 − g_(b₀)) ∈ H^((ℰ_+,a_+))_b and their first derivatives, and Lemma 32.20, the ι⁺-data are
((λ + 2, k) + ℱ + ((0, 0) ∪ ℰ_+), a_+ + Re λ + 2), and a_+ + Re λ + 2 > 4; near K⁺ only
δ*_(g_0,E_C)ϑ^((λ−1,k))_s1 remains, of weight Re λ + 4 − ε. (λ + 2, k) + ℱ + ((0, 0) ∪ ℰ_+) ⊂ ℰ_++ + 2 by
(32.16). (c) As in Lemma 32.10 (c). ∎

[Hin26, (11.153)] has the K⁺-order λ + 4 − ε and the index set (λ + 2, k) + ((0, 0) ∪ ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ_+ ∪ ℰ̃′_++); its
(11.154) serves its device u_Σ, which is not needed here.

*At a base point with parameter b.* The rows are built at b (Lemma 36.1): there m_(λ,k)(S) denotes
χ_K δ*_(g_b) ω^(≤4)_b(a_(λ,k)S), built as in Definition 32.19 from the 1-forms ω̆^i_b(S) := ω̆^((0),i)_(b,s1)(S) of
Proposition 23.34 (2) at b, while the corrections h^((λ−1,k))_s1 and their counterterms stay those built at b₀.
With ν := (s1, λ, k) we write m^(b₀)_ν(S) := χ_K δ*_(g_(b₀)) ω^(≤4)(a_(λ,k)S), h^(b₀)_ν := h^((λ−1,k))_s1 and
ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) := ϑ^((λ−1,k))_(s1,♯) for the tensors of Definition 32.19 built at b₀; so
ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) = δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀))(m^(b₀)_ν − h^(b₀)_ν) involves the row built at b₀, not m_(λ,k), and these
are the tensors in P_3 at every base point. Lemma 32.20 holds for these rows at b with the same proof, h_b(S) in
place of h(S) in (32.19): the 1-forms at b satisfy the tower relations (23.29) at b and have the
same index sets ((P3)). Lemma 32.23 and Lemma 32.24 hold at b as stated. The pairs (s1, λ, k),
(λ, k) ∈ ℳ, are rows of the set 𝒩 of Section 32.10 (Definition 32.31 gives the same tensors), and
Lemma 32.22 takes the following form.

**Lemma 32.25** (The motion identity at b.) Let (h, p⃗) be small, with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*,
(λ, k) ∈ ℳ and ν := (s1, λ, k). Write ω^b_ν(S) := ω^(≤4)_b(a_(λ,k)S), so that m_(λ,k)(S) = χ_K δ*_(g_b)ω^b_ν(S), and
let

    h^b_ν(S) := −dχ_K ⊗_s ω^b_ν(S),     ζ^b_ν(S) := δ*_(g_b)(χ_K ω^b_ν(S)),
    ϑ^b_ν(S) := δ_(g_b,E_Υ)G_(g_b) m_(λ,k)(S),     ϑ^b_(ν,♯) := ϑ^b_ν − δ_(g_b,E_Υ)G_(g_b) h^b_ν

be the tensors of Definition 32.19 built at b. Then

    f^((λ,k))_(h,p⃗)(S) = L_(h,p⃗) m_(λ,k)(S) + e^ν_(h,p⃗)(S),     e^ν_(h,p⃗) := r^ν_(h,p⃗) + E^ν_(h,p⃗),
    r^ν_(h,p⃗)(S) := −(L_(h,p⃗) − L_b)ζ^b_ν(S) + (δ*_(g_0,E_C) − δ*_(g_b,E_C))ϑ^b_(ν,♯)(S),
    E^ν_(h,p⃗)(S) := L_(h,p⃗)(h^(b₀)_ν − h^b_ν)(S) + δ*_(g_0,E_C)(ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) − ϑ^b_(ν,♯))(S),
    (32.21)

E^ν being the difference between the corrections and counterterms built at b₀ and at b; this is the identity
(36.1) for the row ν. For every α ∈ (2, min(a_K, 3)),

    ‖e^ν_(h,p⃗)(S)‖_(𝒴(α)) ≤ C|S|(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|),

uniformly on ℬ̄_*. At b = b₀, E^ν = 0, and at (h, p⃗) = (0, 0), e^ν = 0, which is Lemma 32.22.

*Proof.* *The identity.* P_3 depends on S^((λ−1,k))_1 only through h′ := h^(b₀)_ν(S) in g′ and ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯)(S) in
ϑ_tot, linearly, and g_0 does not depend on it. Differentiating (32.20), with
L_(h,p⃗) = L^(g′,g_0) = D_(g′)Ric − δ*_(g_0,E_C)D_1Υ^(E_Υ)(g′, g_0) (Lemma 32.23),

    f^((λ,k)) = D_(g′)Ric(h′) − δ*_(g_0,E_C)(D_1Υ^(E_Υ)(g′, g_0)h′ − ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯)(S))
              = L_(h,p⃗)h′ + δ*_(g_0,E_C)ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯)(S) = L_(h,p⃗)h^b_ν + δ*_(g_0,E_C)ϑ^b_(ν,♯) + E^ν.

By (32.1) at g_b, h^b_ν = m_(λ,k)(S) − ζ^b_ν. As g_b is Ricci flat, (iii) gives D_(g_b)Ric(ζ^b_ν) = 0, so

    L_bζ^b_ν = δ*_(g_b,E_C)δ_(g_b,E_Υ)G_(g_b)(m_(λ,k)(S) − h^b_ν) = δ*_(g_b,E_C)ϑ^b_(ν,♯).

Writing L_(h,p⃗)ζ^b_ν = L_bζ^b_ν + (L_(h,p⃗) − L_b)ζ^b_ν gives (32.21). At b = b₀ the tensors built at
b are those of Definition 32.19, so E^ν = 0; at (h, p⃗) = (0, 0) also g′ = g_0 = g_(b₀), so r^ν = 0.

*The bound on r^ν.* It is supported in supp χ_K. Near (ι⁺)°, L_(h,p⃗) − L_b lies in ρ_+²Diff²_b with
coefficients linear in g′ − g_b, g_0 − g_b and their b-derivatives of order at most 2 ((29.15)); there
g_0 − g_b ∈ ρ_+²C^∞ and g′ − g_0 ∈ H^(k,(ℰ_+,a_+))_b, of sizes O(|p⃗|) and O(|p⃗| + ‖h‖) (Lemma 32.4 (a), (c),
Lemma 32.23), both in ρ_+^(m_+−ε)H^k_b, and ζ^b_ν ∈ 𝒜^((λ,k)+ℱ). So the first term has plain ι⁺-weight
Re λ + 2 + m_+ − 2ε > 4 (m_+ > 1). Near K⁺, g_0 = g_b and h_tot(p⃗) = 0, so L_(h,p⃗) − L_b = L^(g_b+h,g_b) − L_b has
coefficients of K⁺-weight a_K with norm O(‖h‖); ζ^b_ν is m_(λ,k)(S) there, of K⁺-weight Re λ − 1 − ε, so the first
term has K⁺-weight Re λ − 1 + a_K − ε > a_K > α, as α < a_K. ζ^b_ν vanishes near ℐ⁺, and the two weights combine at
the corner of ι⁺ and K⁺ as in Proposition 29.12. The second term is supported in 𝒞, as
g_0 − g_b = (1 − χ_K)((ψ_(−S⁽⁰⁾_1) ∘ φ_(−S))*g_(b₀) − g_b) is supported in supp(1 − χ_K);
δ*_(g_0,E_C) − δ*_(g_b,E_C) ∈ ρ_+³Diff¹_b near (ι⁺)° with seminorms O(|p⃗|), so the term has ι⁺-order Re λ + 4. Hence
r^ν ∈ 𝒴_2(α) with norm at most C|S|(‖h‖ + |p⃗|), and |p⃗| ≤ |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|.

*The bound on E^ν.* The b-differences h^(b₀)_ν − h^b_ν and ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) − ϑ^b_(ν,♯) are supported in 𝒞
and in supp χ_K, and have every seminorm O(|b − b₀||S|), the towers being smooth in b ((P3)). Near K⁺ the corrections
vanish, and the counterterms are ½□^Υ_(b₀)ω^(≤4)(a_(λ,k)S) and ½□^Υ_bω^b_ν(S), of K⁺-weight Re λ + 4 − ε by
(32.18) at b₀ and at b, the K⁺-order of the tops of the towers; δ*_(g_0,E_C) = δ*_(g_b,E_C) there is
stationary and keeps that weight, which exceeds 3 > α. So E^ν is supported in supp χ_K, of size O(|b − b₀||S|) and of
K⁺-weight Re λ + 4 − ε. At ι⁺ the b-differences of the corrections and of the counterterms lie in
𝒜^((λ,k)+ℱ) and 𝒜^((λ+1,k)+ℱ) ((P3), Lemma 32.20); L_b and δ*_(g_0,E_C) add 2 and 1, and the parts of
L_(h,p⃗) − L_b from h, h_tot and g_0 − g_b gain ρ_+^(m_+−ε). So below the weight 4 its exponents lie in
(λ + 2, k) + ℱ ⊂ ℰ_++ + 2 ((32.16)), and beyond them its plain weight exceeds 4. So E^ν ∈ 𝒴_2(α) with norm
O(|b − b₀||S|). ∎

### 32.8 The expansion at one level

**Lemma 32.26** (The base level.) Let α_0 ∈ (2, min(a_K, 2 + ε_g, 5/2)) be admissible (ε_g as in
Definition 32.1). Then Proposition 31.27, Lemma 32.12, Lemma 32.15, Lemma 32.17,
Corollary 32.18 and Proposition 32.14 hold with 𝒴(α_0) in place of 𝒴, at the base points of
Lemma 32.23, with the conclusions at K⁺-weight α_0 − 2 − ε for every ε > 0.

*Proof.* Steps 0–2 of the proof of Proposition 31.27 change. Let the forcing be F = F_1 + F_2, F_j ∈ 𝒴_j(α_0), and
L := L_(h,p⃗). *Step 0.* Step 2 below, applied to F_2 alone (with L_b; F_2 vanishes near ℐ⁺), gives
u_F := Σ_(λ_0)(u_(λ_0) + u′_(λ_0)), over the finitely many λ_0 ∈ π_1ℰ_++ with Re λ_0 < 2, with F_2 − L_bu_F of plain
ι⁺-weight 4 − ε, of K⁺-weight α_0 − ε and with the ℐ⁺-data of 𝒴_1, for every ε > 0. u_F vanishes near {t^♭_* = 1}
(the pieces of Step 2 are cut off near ι⁺) and has ι⁺-weight λ_♯ − ε and K⁺-weight α_0 − 2 − ε (as there:
ℓ_K(λ_0) > α_0 − 2 and Re λ_0 − 1 > 1/2 > α_0 − 2), so (L − L_b)u_F has ι⁺-weight above 4 and K⁺-weight above α_0
((29.15), a_K > 2). So u − u_F is the forward solution of L(u − u_F) = F_1 + (F_2 − L_bu_F) − (L − L_b)u_F, a
forcing of plain ι⁺-weight 4 − ε whose boost parameter is that of F (Ṡ(Lu_F) = 0 by the uniqueness in
Proposition 31.16 (1), u_F being the decaying forward solution), and Proposition 31.21 applies to it with any
α_+ < 2: u − u_F has K⁺-weight α′_K − 2 for every α′_K < 2. With α′_K > α_0 + 2 − a_K (possible, as a_K > α_0),
(L − L_b)u has K⁺-weight above α_0 and ι⁺-weight above 4 − ε, which is the conclusion of Step 0 of the proof of
Proposition 31.27. Write f′_1 := F_1 − (L − L_b)u ∈ 𝒴_1(α_0), so that L_bu = f′_1 + F_2. *Step 1* applies
Proposition 29.29 (at b, Proposition 30.5) to f′_1 alone (Ĕ_+ = ∅), and f^♭_0 := f′_1 − L_bu_I + F_2; its ι⁺-terms
below α^♯_+ + 2 have exponents in (ℰ^♯_+ ∪ ℰ_++) + 2, with coefficients from L_bu_I (vanishing near K⁺) or from F_2
(supported in supp χ^♯_K, away from ℐ⁺), and (31.35) is taken with ℰ_++ added to the excluded exponents (still
finitely many below 2). *Step 2* takes c_K := α_0, so ℓ_K(λ_0) = α_0 − Re λ_0; its exclusions hold by admissibility, and
ℓ_K(λ_0) ∈ (α_0 − 2, 1) ⊂ (0, 1), as Re λ_0 ∈ [λ_♯, 2) and α_0 < 5/2 < λ_♯ + 1. The coefficients at λ_0 of F_2 and of
later errors (of K⁺-weight α_0 − ε for every ε) have R-weight at least ℓ_K(λ_0) − 2 − ε for every ε, which is the
hypothesis of Corollary 26.44; the errors have K⁺-weight α_0 − ε; and u_(λ_0) has K⁺-weight
min(Re λ_0 − 1, ℓ_K(λ_0)) − ε > α_0 − 2 for ε small. The iteration and its termination are those of the proof of
Proposition 31.21, all exponents lying in (ℰ^♯_+ ∪ ℰ_++) + ℕ₀ℰ^ι_ind ⊂ ℰ_++ below 2, by (32.16). So
f^♭ ∈ ⋂_ε H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,4−ε,α_0−ε)_b, and Steps 3–6 apply with α_0 − ε′ for α_K, for every small ε′ (their hypotheses on
α_K are open conditions). Section 32.5 uses Proposition 31.16 (1), whose space of forcings contains 𝒴(α_0)
(F_2 has ι⁺-weight above α_+ + 2 for α_+ < min Re ℰ_++), Proposition 31.27, and, in Lemma 32.12 and in the
proof of Proposition 32.14, the bound of the difference of L and the reference operator applied to the solution,
in the space 𝒴^S_(α,α_+) of Section 32.5 for the boost parameter and in 𝒴_1(α_0) for the parameters
(ḃ, Ṡ⁽⁰⁾_1), unchanged. ∎

**Lemma 32.27** (The expansion; [Hin26, Proposition 11.51, Part 1] in dimension 4 + 1.) Let α′ < α be
admissible, α − α′ < a_K − 2, let p⃗ (with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*) and h be small, and F ∈ 𝒴(α). Suppose that the forward
solution u of L_(h,p⃗)u = F lies in ⋂_ε H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β′_+,α′−2−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−) for some
β′_+ ∈ (1, min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+)). Then

    u = Σ_((λ,k)∈ℳ_α∖ℳ_(α′)) χ_K t_*^(−λ+1)(log t_*)^k h_b(S_(λ,k)) + ũ,
        ũ ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β_+,α−2−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−),    (32.22)

for every β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+), with S_(λ,k) =: S^(h,p⃗)_(λ,k)(F) ∈ 𝒮_(1,ℂ) determined by u (its K⁺-expansion)
and linear in F, and

    |S^(h,p⃗)_(λ,k)(F)| + ‖ũ‖_(α) ≤ C‖F‖_(𝒴(α)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u‖_(α′),

with ‖·‖_(α) and ‖·‖_(α′) the seminorms of Section 32.6 at the levels α and α′, and C uniform for (h, p⃗) small and
b ∈ ℬ̄_*. This is not a bound by F alone: the last term vanishes at (h, p⃗) = (0, 0), where b = b₀, but not at the
reference point (0, p⃗_b) with b ≠ b₀.

*Proof.* Write L := L_(h,p⃗) and F = F_1 + F_2, F_j ∈ 𝒴_j(α). *Step 0.* f′ := F − (L − L_b)u = f′_1 + F_2 with
f′_1 := F_1 − (L − L_b)u ∈ 𝒴_1(α): (29.15) (for L, Lemma 32.23) gives the ℐ⁺-data
(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′, ℓ_I + 1), the ι⁺-weight β′_+ + 2 + m_+ − ε > 4 − ε and the K⁺-weight α′ − 2 − ε + a_K ≥ α for ε small.

*Steps 1–2 (null infinity and ι⁺).* As in Lemma 32.26, with α for α_0 and α^♯_+ := 2 − ε: Step 1 gives u_I;
Step 2, with ℓ_K(λ_0) := α − Re λ_0 ∈ (α − 2, 3/2) (below the bound ℓ^max_K = min(3, 2 + 2γ_Cv_C) of
Section 26.10 and off its exclusions by admissibility), gives u_ι = Σ u_(λ_0) + Σ u′_(λ_0) with errors of K⁺-weight
α − ε, so

    u^♭ := u − u_I − u_ι :     L_bu^♭ = f^♭ ∈ ⋂_ε H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,4−ε,α−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−).    (32.23)

Now ℓ_K(λ_0) > 1 exactly when Re λ_0 − 1 < α − 2, and then −1 ∈ 𝒲(ℓ_K(λ_0)) and the s1 row of (26.55) is
present. By Corollary 26.44, u_(λ_0) has the K⁺-index set ℰ^gr_K(λ_0) + (0, k) at the weight ℓ_K(λ_0) − ε, whose
elements with real part below Re λ_0 are (λ_0 − 1, j), j ≤ k, from the s1 row: the v1 row gives λ_0 and the other rows
λ_0 − μ + j with Re μ ≤ 0 (Theorem 26.42). The s1 row is h^(≤3)_(b,s1) applied to functions of the type a_s1
times the coefficients S^((−1))_1, and its leading term at K⁺ is that function times h_b(·), the other terms carrying
derivatives of it, as in (32.19). So

    u_(λ_0) − Σ_(j≤k) χ_K t_*^(−λ_0+1)(log t_*)^j h_b(S_(λ_0,j))   has K⁺-weight min(Re λ_0, ℓ_K(λ_0)) − ε > α − 2,

the sum present only when Re λ_0 − 1 < α − 2, with S_(λ_0,j) linear in the coefficients of the forcing; u′_(λ_0)
vanishes near K⁺. As λ_0 runs over ℳ (the proof of Lemma 32.26),

    u_ι = Σ_((λ,k)∈ℳ_α) χ_K t_*^(−λ+1)(log t_*)^k h_b(S_(λ,k)) + (a term of K⁺-weight above α − 2);

every term of u_ι decays at K⁺ (weight at least min(λ_♯ − 1, α − 2) − ε > 0).

*Step 3 (zero energy).* Steps 3–3.3 of the proof of Proposition 31.27 apply to (32.23) with α − ε′ for
α_K (ε′ > 0 small, so α − ε′ ∈ (2, 3) with the same exclusions): they use α_K ∈ (2, 3) ∖ ℕ only (Proposition 20.18
(1), Lemma 29.32 in its statement at b, Proposition 30.5, Proposition 27.58 with ℓ_zf = α_K − 2 ∉ ℕ₀ and
w = α_K − 2 + ε, and the remainder weights of (31.43)). They give û_0, ḃ_0, S_0 = 0 (the argument there: u has
K⁺-weight > −1), û′_3, Σ_3, (û_4, b̂_4, Ŝ_4) and

    f̂_5 ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,τ_0,α−2−ε′))_b,     τ_0 := 2 + ε_g − 2ε     ((31.46));

with ε < ½ε_g, τ_0 is a lower bound for the tf-weight 2 + ε_Υ − 2ε that the gain ε_Υ − ε of (27.55) gives
in Step 3.2 there; ε_Υ − 2ε lies in the indicial gap (0, 1] of L̂_b(0), as the zero energy solve of Step 3.3 needs.

*Step 3.4′ (the iteration at the transition face; [Hin26, Step 1.6 of the proof of Proposition 11.51]).* Put
f̂^((0)) := f̂_5. While τ_i ≤ α − ε′, apply Proposition 27.58 on X^±_(sc-b) separately to
g_i := σ⁻¹f̂^((i)) ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,τ_i−1,α−3−ε′))_b (|σ| = ρ_tfρ_zf), with α_i := τ_i − 1 ∈ (1, 2) for its α,
ℓ_scf := 3/2 − ε, ℓ_zf := α − 3 − ε′ ∈ (−1, 0), k_0 := 1 (so the zf-expansion of its proof is empty), and
w = ℓ_zf − α_i + 2 = α − ε′ − τ_i ∈ [0, 1), inside (−ε_ind, ℓ^max_K); ε and ε′ are chosen so that w and every
2 − α_i + j, j ∈ ℕ₀, avoid the discrete set of the −μ (finitely many i). It gives
v_i = χ_zf u^((i))_b + χ^♯_tf ṽ_i ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−2ε,α_i−2,α_i−3))_b with
g_i − L̂_b(σ)v_i ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,α_i+ε_Υ−ε,α−3−ε′))_b ⊂ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,α_i+ε_g−ε,α−3−ε′))_b ((27.55): the
window −ε_ind < w is its hypothesis, the gain ε_Υ its conclusion). With the s1 coefficient S_i := S^((−1))_1 of u^((i))_b
((27.56)), Σ^((i)) := −σ²|σ|^(α_i−3)S_i and v′_i := v_i − ĥ^aug(σ)(Σ^((i))), Lemma 31.26 and
(31.45) give L̂_b(σ)v′_i + f̂_(Σ^((i)))(σ) = L̂_b(σ)v_i, v′_i of tf- and zf-weight α_i − 2 near zf and tf,
r(v′_i) = O(|σ|^(α_i−2)), and Σ^((i)) = O(|σ|^(α_i−1)). Put

    f̂^((i+1)) := f̂^((i)) − σL̂_b(σ)v_i ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,τ_(i+1),α−2−ε′))_b,     τ_(i+1) := τ_i + ε_g − ε.

The increments ε_g − ε are positive for ε < ε_g and below 1/2 (Definition 32.1), so after finitely many
steps, i_0 say, τ_(i_0) ∈ (α − ε′, α − ε′ + 1) (i_0 = 0 if τ_0 > α − ε′, which is the case α_K < 2 + ε_g of
Proposition 31.27). Then Lemma 29.33 (at b, Proposition 30.5) with β_scf := 3/2 − 2ε, β_tf := τ_(i_0) − 2,
β_zf := α − 2 − ε′, β_tf − β_zf ∈ (0, 1), gives (û_6, b̂_6, Ŝ_6) := L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(f̂^((i_0)), 0, 0),
û_6 ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−3ε,τ_(i_0)−2,α−2−ε′))_b, b̂_6, Ŝ_6 ∈ H^(∞,α−2−ε′)_b(±(0, c], |dσ/σ|). With
(U^((i)), B^((i)), Σ^((i))_r) := L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(0, σr(v′_i)),

    (û_5, b̂_5, Ŝ_5) := Σ_(i<i_0) [(σv′_i, 0, σΣ^((i))) − (U^((i)), B^((i)), Σ^((i))_r)]
                         + (û_6, b̂_6, Ŝ_6)    (32.24)

equals L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(f̂_5, 0, 0). Indeed, apply L̃_b(σ): the first components give Σ_i σL̂_b(σ)v_i + f̂^((i_0)) = f̂_5
(telescoping, with L̃_b(σ)(σv′_i, 0, σΣ^((i))) = (σL̂_b(σ)v_i, σr(v′_i)) by Lemma 28.5 (c)), the rows give
Σ_i(σr(v′_i) − σr(v′_i)) = 0, and every first component lies in the space of Lemma 31.24, so injectivity
applies. By Lemma 31.25, B^((i)), Σ^((i))_r = O(|σ|^(1−ε)·|σ|^(α_i−1)), and U^((i)) has zf- and tf-weight at
least α_i − 1 − ε. This replaces Step 3.4 of the proof of Proposition 31.27.

*Step 3.5′ (assembly).* (31.47) holds with this (û_5, b̂_5, Ŝ_5), by the same calculation. In
(31.48) the new terms are σ²v′_i, of zf- and tf-weight α_i ≥ 1 + ε_g − 2ε > α − 2, σU^((i)), σû_6
(zf-weight α − 1 − ε′), σB^((i)), σb̂_6, and, in σ⁻¹Ŝ_1 − Ŝ_4, the terms σΣ^((i)) = O(|σ|^(α_i)), Σ^((i))_r and Ŝ_6,
all O(|σ|^(α−2−ε′)) with σ∂_σ-regularity (α_i > 1 > α − 2). So (31.48) holds with α − ε′ for α_K.

*Steps 4–5.* Steps 4 and 5 of the proof of Proposition 31.27 then give u_reg of K⁺-weight α − 1 − ε′, u_hi of
arbitrarily large K⁺-weight, and u_sing − χ_K(ġ_b(ḃ_0) + h_b(iŜ_4)) of K⁺-weight α − 2 − ε′ (with the matching
there). *Step 6.* u^♭ = u − u_I − u_ι has positive K⁺-weight (u by hypothesis, α′ > 2; u_ι by Steps 1–2; u_I vanishes
near K⁺), so the stationary tensor ġ_b(ḃ_0) + h_b(iŜ_4) times χ_K has positive K⁺-weight and vanishes, and ḃ_0 = 0,
Ŝ_4 = 0 (injectivity, Section 32.1). *Step 7.* So u = u_ι + (u_I + u^♭) is (32.22) with the sum over
ℳ_α; the terms with (λ, k) ∈ ℳ_(α′) vanish, as u has K⁺-weight α′ − 2 − ε for every ε and Re λ − 1 < α′ − 2 (α′
admissible): a finite sum of such polyhomogeneous terms in that space is zero, the functions t_*^(−λ+1)(log t_*)^j
being independent and h_b injective. *Step 8.* The ℐ⁺-data of ũ follow from Proposition 29.27 as in Step 6 of the
proof of Proposition 31.27 (χ_K = 0 near ℐ⁺). *Determination, linearity, bounds.* The S_(λ,k) are the coefficients
of the K⁺-expansion of u below α − 2, and ũ is the rest; every map used is linear, and fixed by L_b, given by L − L_b,
or Proposition 29.27 applied to L (Step 8), with coefficient bounds uniform for small (h, p⃗) and b ∈ ℬ̄_*
(Lemma 32.23, Lemma 32.9 (c), Lemma 30.2 (P1)–(P4), and Proposition 30.5 for
Proposition 29.27 at b). In Steps 1–7 the coefficients and the parts u_I, u_ι and u^♭ are obtained from f′ of Step 0
by maps fixed by L_b, and Step 8 bounds the ℐ⁺-data of ũ by Lũ = F − L(Σ_((λ,k)) χ_K t_*^(−λ+1)(log t_*)^k h_b(S_(λ,k)))
and by those parts. So |S_(λ,k)| + ‖ũ‖_(α) ≤ C‖F‖_(𝒴(α)) + C‖f′‖_(𝒴(α)), and the count of Step 0, whose coefficients
L − L_b have size O(‖h‖ + |p⃗|), gives ‖(L − L_b)u‖_(𝒴(α)) ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u‖_(α′), so
‖f′‖_(𝒴(α)) ≤ ‖F‖_(𝒴(α)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u‖_(α′). At (0, p⃗_b) the coefficients of L_(0,p⃗_b) − L_b are of size |b − b₀|
on supp(1 − χ_K), so the last term is present there when b ≠ b₀. ∎

At a base point with parameter b no rotation row has rate below α − 2 for α < 3 (its K⁺-weight is Re λ − ε > 1); so
Lemma 32.27 holds at b as at b₀, with the states at b.

**Lemma 32.28** (The coefficients near the reference point.) Fix b ∈ ℬ̄_*. Let α′ < α be as in
Lemma 32.27, (h_j, p⃗_j) → (0, p⃗_b) with parameter b, F_j → F in 𝒴(α), and suppose that the forward solutions
u_j of L_(h_j,p⃗_j)u_j = F_j and u of L_(0,p⃗_b)u = F lie in the space of the hypothesis of Lemma 32.27, with
‖u_j − u‖_(α′) → 0 (so the u_j are bounded in ‖·‖_(α′)). Then S^(h_j,p⃗_j)_(λ,k)(F_j) → S^(0,p⃗_b)_(λ,k)(F) for every
(λ, k) ∈ ℳ_α ∖ ℳ_(α′). At b = b₀ it suffices that the u_j be bounded in ‖·‖_(α′).

*Proof.* u_j − u is the forward solution of

    L_(0,p⃗_b)(u_j − u) = R_j := F_j − F − (L_(h_j,p⃗_j) − L_(0,p⃗_b))u_j.

The coefficients of L_(h_j,p⃗_j) − L_(0,p⃗_b) have norm O(‖h_j‖ + |p⃗_j − p⃗_b|) (Lemma 32.23), and near K⁺ they
gain a_K, both backgrounds being g_b there (Lemma 29.11); so the count of Step 0 of the proof of
Lemma 32.27 gives ‖(L_(h_j,p⃗_j) − L_(0,p⃗_b))u_j‖_(𝒴(α)) ≤ C(‖h_j‖ + |p⃗_j − p⃗_b|)‖u_j‖_(α′) → 0, and R_j → 0 in
𝒴(α). u_j − u lies in the space of the hypothesis of Lemma 32.27, so that lemma applies to it, at (0, p⃗_b) with
the forcing R_j. Comparing the expansions (32.22) of u_j, u and u_j − u (their coefficients are unique, the
functions t_*^(−λ+1)(log t_*)^k being independent and h_b injective, as in Step 7 of that proof) gives
S^(h_j,p⃗_j)_(λ,k)(F_j) − S^(0,p⃗_b)_(λ,k)(F) = S^(0,p⃗_b)_(λ,k)(R_j), and the bound of Lemma 32.27 at (0, p⃗_b)
gives

    |S^(0,p⃗_b)_(λ,k)(R_j)| ≤ C‖R_j‖_(𝒴(α)) + C|p⃗_b|‖u_j − u‖_(α′),

which tends to 0, as R_j → 0 and ‖u_j − u‖_(α′) → 0. At b = b₀, p⃗_(b₀) = 0 and the second term is absent. ∎

### 32.9 Elimination of the motions

For an admissible α put 𝒫_α := 𝒮_1 ⊕ 𝔟 ⊕ 𝒮_1 ⊕ (⊕_((λ,k)∈ℳ_α) 𝒮_(1,ℂ))^sym, with the conjugation-symmetric tuples of
Section 32.6: the modification parameters with motion components only in ℳ_α. Write D_p⃗P_3(h, p⃗)(p⃗′) for
p⃗′ ∈ 𝒫_α (the other motion components zero). By Lemma 32.24, D_p⃗P_3(h, p⃗)(p⃗′) ∈ 𝒴(α).

**Proposition 32.29** ([Hin26, Proposition 11.51] in dimension 4 + 1.) Let α ∈ (2, min(a_K, 3)) be
admissible, and p⃗ (with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*) and h small. For every F ∈ 𝒴(α) there is a unique
p⃗′ = p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(F) ∈ 𝒫_α such that the forward solution of

    L_(h,p⃗)u = F − D_p⃗P_3(h, p⃗)(p⃗′)    (32.25)

satisfies

    u ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β_+,α−2−ε)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−)   for every β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+).    (32.26)

Moreover (i) p⃗′_(h,p⃗) and F ↦ u are linear, with bounds uniform for (h, p⃗ − p⃗_b) small and b ∈ ℬ̄_*: for each fixed
seminorm ‖·‖_(α) of the space of (32.26) there are a seminorm ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α)) of 𝒴(α), as in Section 32.6,
and C with |p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(F)| + ‖u‖_(α) ≤ C‖F‖^+_(𝒴(α)), d being large for ‖·‖_(α) (Section 32.6); (ii) at fixed b,
if (h_j, p⃗_j) → (0, p⃗_b) and F_j → F in 𝒴(α), then p⃗′_(h_j,p⃗_j)(F_j) → p⃗′_(0,p⃗_b)(F). In compact spatial sets
u = O(t_*^(−α+2+ε)), almost O(t_*⁻¹) as α → 3.

*Proof.* Choose admissible α_0 < α_1 < ⋯ < α_n = α with α_0 ∈ (2, min(a_K, 2 + ε_g, 5/2)) and
α_(i+1) − α_i < a_K − 2 (the excluded set is finite). By induction on i we prove the statement, with (i)–(ii), at α_i.
Write p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α_i) for the map at the level α_i.

*Base.* ℳ_(α_0) = ∅, as Re λ − 1 ≥ λ_♯ − 1 > 1/2 > α_0 − 2. By Lemma 32.26, Corollary 32.18 gives existence,
uniqueness and linearity. Its maps are continuous on 𝒴(α_0), so each fixed seminorm of their values is bounded by a
seminorm ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α_0)) of 𝒴(α_0), as (i) states. The bounds are uniform by Lemma 32.9 (c) and
Proposition 32.14, the finite-dimensional maps inverted in Lemma 32.15 and Lemma 32.17 lying within
C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|) of ±id; and (ii) holds as those maps converge at fixed b (by their construction and
Lemma 32.12, which allows forcings varying with j).

*Step.* Let the statement hold at α′ := α_i, and let α″ := α_(i+1), ℳ′ := ℳ_(α″) ∖ ℳ_(α′) and
F ∈ 𝒴(α″) ⊂ 𝒴(α′).

*The seminorms.* Fix the seminorm ‖·‖_(α″) of (i) at α″. Take ‖·‖_(𝒴(α″)) and ‖·‖_(α′) as in Section 32.6 for
Lemma 32.27 at the levels α′ < α″, with the remainder in ‖·‖_(α″); let ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) be the seminorm of (i) at
α′ for ‖·‖_(α′), and ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α″)) the quotient norm of Section 32.6 on 𝒴(α″) at a regularity at least those of
‖·‖_(𝒴(α″)) and ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) and an ε at most theirs. On 𝒴(α″) it bounds ‖·‖_(𝒴(α″)), and ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) up to a
constant: each defining space at α″ lies in the one at α′, its norm bounding that at a lower regularity and a larger
ε, as the K⁺-weight α″ exceeds α′.

For S⃗ = (S_ν)_(ν∈ℳ′) conjugation-symmetric (Section 32.6; the map T_(h,p⃗) below preserves these, L_(h,p⃗) and F
being real) put F(S⃗) := F − Σ_(ν∈ℳ′) f^ν_(h,p⃗)(S_ν) ∈ 𝒴(α″) (Lemma 32.24 (b)), and let u(S⃗) be the forward
solution of

    L_(h,p⃗)u(S⃗) = G(S⃗) := F(S⃗) − D_p⃗P_3(h, p⃗)(p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α′)(F(S⃗))) ∈ 𝒴(α″),

which lies in (32.26) at α′ by the hypothesis. Lemma 32.27 (with α′, α″) applies and gives the
coefficients C_ν(S⃗) := S^(h,p⃗)_ν(G(S⃗)), ν ∈ ℳ′, affine in S⃗: C(S⃗) = C(0) − T_(h,p⃗)S⃗, where
T_(h,p⃗)S⃗ := S^(h,p⃗)(G_1(S⃗)) with

    G_1(S⃗) := Σ_ν f^ν_(h,p⃗)(S_ν) − D_p⃗P_3(h, p⃗)(p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α′)(Σ_ν f^ν_(h,p⃗)(S_ν))).

*The level map.* By Lemma 32.25, f^ν_(h,p⃗)(S_ν) = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν(S_ν) + e^ν_(h,p⃗)(S_ν). For ν = (λ, k) ∈ ℳ′,
m_ν(S_ν) vanishes for t^♭_* < 10, has K⁺-weight Re λ − 1 − ε > α′ − 2 − ε and the other properties of
(32.26) at α′ (Lemma 32.20; it vanishes near ℐ⁺); so it is the forward solution of
L_(h,p⃗)u = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν(S_ν), and by uniqueness at α′, p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α′)(L_(h,p⃗)m_ν(S_ν)) = 0. By linearity, the forward
solution of L_(h,p⃗)u = G_1(S⃗) is Σ_ν m_ν(S_ν) + v(S⃗), where v(S⃗) is the forward solution of

    L_(h,p⃗)v(S⃗) = R(S⃗) := Σ_ν e^ν_(h,p⃗)(S_ν) − D_p⃗P_3(h, p⃗)(p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α′)(Σ_ν e^ν_(h,p⃗)(S_ν))).

By Lemma 32.25 (α″ < min(a_K, 3)), in ‖·‖_(𝒴(α″)) and in ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) (Section 32.6), and (i) at α′,
‖R(S⃗)‖_(𝒴(α″)) ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|)|S⃗|. The forward solution of G_1(S⃗) = G(0) − G(S⃗) is u(0) − u(S⃗),
which lies in (32.26) at α′, and so does Σ_ν m_ν(S_ν); hence v(S⃗) = u(0) − u(S⃗) − Σ_ν m_ν(S_ν) satisfies
the hypothesis of Lemma 32.27. Moreover ‖v(S⃗)‖_(α′) ≤ C|S⃗|: u(0) − u(S⃗) is the solution of (32.25)
at α′ for the forcing Σ_ν f^ν_(h,p⃗)(S_ν), of norm at most C|S⃗| in ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) by Lemma 32.24 (b), so (i) at
α′ bounds it by C|S⃗|, and ‖m_ν(S_ν)‖_(α′) ≤ C|S_ν| by Lemma 32.20. The coefficients of Lemma 32.27 are
read from the forcing f′ = R(S⃗) − (L_(h,p⃗) − L_b)v(S⃗) of Step 0 of its proof by maps fixed by L_b, and the count of
that step gives ‖(L_(h,p⃗) − L_b)v(S⃗)‖_(𝒴(α″)) ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖v(S⃗)‖_(α′), the coefficients of L_(h,p⃗) − L_b having
size O(‖h‖ + |p⃗|). So the coefficients of v(S⃗) satisfy

    |S^(h,p⃗)(R(S⃗))| ≤ C‖R(S⃗)‖_(𝒴(α″)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖v(S⃗)‖_(α′) ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|)|S⃗|,

as |p⃗| ≤ |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|; and the coefficients of Σ_ν m_ν(S_ν) are S⃗, by (32.19) at b
(Re λ − ε > α″ − 2). So

    |T_(h,p⃗) − id| ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|),

with C uniform on ℬ̄_*. At (0, 0), e^ν = 0 and T_(0,0) = id. On the finite-dimensional space of the conjugation-symmetric
tuples, T_(h,p⃗) is therefore invertible for (h, p⃗ − p⃗_b) and ℬ_* small, with inverse of norm at most 2. Put
S⃗ := T_(h,p⃗)⁻¹C(0) and p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α″)(F) := p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α′)(F(S⃗)) ⊕ S⃗ ∈ 𝒫_(α″). The forcing of (32.25) is then
G(S⃗) (linearity of D_p⃗P_3(h, p⃗) in the direction), whose solution u(S⃗) has no term of ℳ′ in (32.22), so
lies in (32.26) at α″. *Uniqueness:* if p⃗″ ∈ 𝒫_(α″) also gives (32.26) at α″, with ℳ′-part S⃗″,
then its solution lies in (32.26) at α′ with the forcing F(S⃗″) − D_p⃗P_3(h, p⃗)(q⃗), q⃗ ∈ 𝒫_(α′), so
q⃗ = p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α′)(F(S⃗″)) by uniqueness at α′, the solution is u(S⃗″), and C(S⃗″) = 0 gives S⃗″ = S⃗.

*(i) at α″.* Linearity holds by construction. Write ‖F‖ := ‖F‖^+_(𝒴(α″)), which bounds ‖F‖_(𝒴(α″)), and
‖F‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) up to a constant (*The seminorms*). By (i) at α′ and Lemma 32.24, ‖G(0)‖_(𝒴(α″)) ≤ C‖F‖, and
u(0), the solution of (32.25) at α′ for the forcing F, has ‖u(0)‖_(α′) ≤ C‖F‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) ≤ C‖F‖; so the
bound of Lemma 32.27 gives |C(0)| ≤ C‖F‖, and |S⃗| ≤ 2|C(0)| ≤ C‖F‖. Then
‖F(S⃗)‖_(𝒴(α″)) + ‖F(S⃗)‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) ≤ C‖F‖ (Lemma 32.24 (b)), and (i) at α′, with Lemma 32.24 for G(S⃗),
bounds p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α′)(F(S⃗)), G(S⃗) and u(S⃗), the solution of (32.25) at α′ for F(S⃗), by C‖F‖ in 𝒫_(α′),
𝒴(α″) and ‖·‖_(α′). So |p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α″)(F)| ≤ C‖F‖, and the bound of Lemma 32.27 on the remainder, which is u(S⃗)
itself, gives ‖u(S⃗)‖_(α″) ≤ C‖F‖. The constants are uniform for (h, p⃗ − p⃗_b) small and b ∈ ℬ̄_*, as those of (i) at
α′, of Lemma 32.27 and the bound on T_(h,p⃗)⁻¹ are, and that of the comparison of the seminorms.

*(ii) at α″, at fixed b.* Let (h_j, p⃗_j) → (0, p⃗_b) and F_j → F in 𝒴(α″). Write T_j, C_j for the objects above at
(h_j, p⃗_j) with the forcing F_j, and T, C for those at (0, p⃗_b) with F. We first show: *if Φ_j → Φ in 𝒴(α″), and w_j,
w are the solutions of (32.25) at α′ for the forcing Φ_j at (h_j, p⃗_j) and for Φ at (0, p⃗_b), with the
forcings*

    Ψ_j := Φ_j − D_p⃗P_3(h_j, p⃗_j)(p⃗′_(h_j,p⃗_j,α′)(Φ_j)),     Ψ := Φ − D_p⃗P_3(0, p⃗_b)(p⃗′_(0,p⃗_b,α′)(Φ)),

*then Ψ_j → Ψ in 𝒴(α″) and ‖w_j − w‖_(α′) → 0.* Indeed, p⃗′_(h_j,p⃗_j,α′)(Φ_j) → p⃗′_(0,p⃗_b,α′)(Φ) by (ii) at α′, and
D_p⃗P_3(h, p⃗) is linear in the direction, bounded uniformly and continuous in (h, p⃗) (Lemma 32.24), so
Ψ_j → Ψ. Next, w_j − w is the forward solution of

    L_(0,p⃗_b)(w_j − w) = R_j := Ψ_j − Ψ − (L_(h_j,p⃗_j) − L_(0,p⃗_b))w_j.

The Φ_j converge in 𝒴(α″) ⊂ 𝒴(α′), so, by (i) at α′, the w_j are bounded in each fixed seminorm of the space of
(32.26) at α′, among them one of regularity two above that of ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α′)). The coefficients of
L_(h_j,p⃗_j) − L_(0,p⃗_b) have norm O(‖h_j‖ + |p⃗_j − p⃗_b|) and gain a_K near K⁺, where both backgrounds are g_b; so the
count of Step 0 of the proof of Lemma 32.27, in ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α′)), gives (L_(h_j,p⃗_j) − L_(0,p⃗_b))w_j → 0 there,
and R_j → 0 in ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α′)), with R_j ∈ 𝒴(α″) ⊂ 𝒴(α′) real. w_j − w lies in (32.26) at α′, as w_j and w
do. So p⃗′ = 0 has, for (0, p⃗_b) and the forcing R_j, the property of the statement at α′; by uniqueness at α′,
p⃗′_(0,p⃗_b,α′)(R_j) = 0 and w_j − w is the solution of (32.25) at α′ for R_j, and (i) at α′ gives
‖w_j − w‖_(α′) ≤ C‖R_j‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) → 0.

For fixed S⃗ take Φ_j := Σ_ν f^ν_(h_j,p⃗_j)(S_ν) and Φ := Σ_ν f^ν_(0,p⃗_b)(S_ν), so that Φ_j → Φ (Lemma 32.24
(c)); then Ψ_j and Ψ are G_1(S⃗) at (h_j, p⃗_j) and at (0, p⃗_b), and w_j, w their forward solutions, so
Lemma 32.28 gives T_jS⃗ → TS⃗. On the finite-dimensional space of the conjugation-symmetric tuples this is
T_j → T, and as |T_j⁻¹| ≤ 2, T_j⁻¹ − T⁻¹ = T_j⁻¹(T − T_j)T⁻¹ → 0. Take next Φ_j := F_j and Φ := F; then Ψ_j and Ψ are
G(0) at (h_j, p⃗_j) with F_j and at (0, p⃗_b) with F, and Lemma 32.28 gives C_j(0) → C(0). So
S⃗_j := T_j⁻¹C_j(0) → S⃗ := T⁻¹C(0). Finally F_j(S⃗_j) → F(S⃗) in 𝒴(α″), as f^ν_(h,p⃗)(S_ν) is linear in S_ν with norm
O(|S_ν|) uniformly and continuous in (h, p⃗) (Lemma 32.24 (b), (c)); so (ii) at α′ gives
p⃗′_(h_j,p⃗_j,α′)(F_j(S⃗_j)) → p⃗′_(0,p⃗_b,α′)(F(S⃗)), and p⃗′_(h_j,p⃗_j,α″)(F_j) → p⃗′_(0,p⃗_b,α″)(F). ∎

[Hin26, Proposition 11.51] has f_2 of K⁺-weight 4 + ε_K and h with 4 + ε_K orders of decay ([Hin26, (11.148)]); here
α < a_K is what the b-derivative needs (Lemma 32.10 (b)), and the remainder is α − 2 − ε for every ε,
[Hin26]'s α_K − 2, since the step at ι⁺ takes c_K = α to admit forcings of K⁺-weight exactly α. Its index set ℰ̃′_++,
built by the procedure after its proof ([Hin26, (11.186)]), is here fixed in advance by (32.16). The motions
come from quasi-homogeneous ι⁺-terms that the formal solution at null infinity transports there, as in [Hin26, Remark
11.54]; in dimension 4 + 1 their least exponent is the radiative λ_♯, so the slowest motion decays like
t_*^(−1/2−(1−e_Υ)γ_Υ).

### 32.10 Corrections of the fourth kind: setting

This section and the next are the opening of [Hin26, Section 11.8] and its Section 11.8.1 (pp. 273–277) in dimension
4 + 1: for each pure gauge term of the K⁺-expansion that decays no faster than t_*⁻², a cut-off pure gauge tensor m_ν
built from the generalised gauge 1-forms of Proposition 23.34, with a correction h_ν at the cut-off and a gauge
counterterm ϑ_ν, so that the linearisation of the operator in the new parameter is L_(b₀)m_ν exactly.

Everything of Section 32.6 is kept: 𝔟, the enlarged ℰ_ind, ℰ^ι_ind, ℰ^♯_+ and λ_♯ = 3/2 + (1 − e_Υ)γ_Υ =
min Re ℰ^♯_+, the index set ℰ_++ with (32.16) and ℳ = {(λ, k) ∈ ℰ_++ : Re λ < 2} of (32.17),
𝒢 = (2, 0) ∪ (2 + ℰ_ind), ℓ_I ≤ a_I, the translated background (32.4), and the cut-offs, 𝒞, Θ, the
conventions (32.1) and the identities (i)–(iii). ℰ_ind is enlarged once more, to contain also the index
sets of Proposition 23.34 (1), (3) and (4)–(7) at b₀ (those of the towers of Section 32.11; there ℰ_ind changes
from line to line) and (2, 0) ((23.23)); (32.16), ℰ_++ and the conditions on ℰ_+ there are taken
with the enlarged set, which only strengthens them. Put ℱ := (0, 0) ∪ ℰ_ind, ℰ̃_+ := 𝒢 ∪ (ℰ_+ + 𝒢)
((31.22)), 2ℰ_+ := ℰ_+ + ℰ_+ (the product index set of (29.15)), and

    δ_♯ := λ_♯ − 3/2 = (1 − e_Υ)γ_Υ > 0,

which lies in (0, 1/4), as 0 < e_Υ < 1 and 0 < γ_Υ < 1/4 ((27.1)). Let ε_ind be the constant of
(25.10), with which the hypotheses of Proposition 27.58 are stated: (0, ε_ind] lies in the indicial gap of
L̂_b(0), and the real part of every non-integer root of modulus at most 50 has distance at least ε_ind from ℤ; ε_Υ and
ε_g = min(ε_Υ, ε_ind) are those of Definition 32.1. Fix constants

    0 < ε_K < ε_+ < min(δ_♯, ε_ind),      w_+ := 5 + ε_+,    (32.27)

[Hin26, (11.9)] with δ_♯ in place of ε_I. Chapter 33 may decrease them; every statement here holds for all smaller
values.

*Hypotheses on the class 𝒳* ([Hin26, (11.148) and Remarks 11.61–11.62] in dimension 4 + 1):

(H1) a_+ > λ_♯ and ℰ_+ ⊂ {Re ≥ λ_♯}; so m_+ = min(a_+, min Re ℰ_+) = λ_♯, as ℰ_+ ⊃ ℰ_++ ⊃ ℰ^♯_+ ∩ {Re < 2}.

(H2) a_K ≥ 4 + ε_K: h has 4 + ε_K orders of decay at K⁺.

(H3) is stated below, after the rows.

(H2) is what the b-derivative needs (Lemma 32.36 (a)) and what the K⁺-weight of the remainder r^ν needs
(Lemma 32.36 (c) and (e), which ask a_K > α + 1 − λ_♯); (H3) asks ℰ_+ to contain the index sets of the new
corrections; and (H1) gives the gain m_+ = λ_♯ at ι⁺ behind (32.35).

*The parameter exponents.* Fix an index set ℰ_par ⊂ ℂ × ℕ₀, closed under conjugation, with

    min Re ℰ_par ≥ λ_♯,      ℰ_par ∩ {Re < 2} = ℳ.    (32.28)

Chapter 33 fixes it (it is [Hin26]'s ℰ̃′_++ of Definition 11.56, built after Theorem 11.59); here it is any such set.

*Rows.* The types are 𝒯 := {s1, v1, s0, s2, c0, c1}: the rows of the table of Section 26.10 at the roots −1 (s1,
v1) and 0 (s0, s2) of L̂_(b₀)(0), and its class roots μ_c0 := 2 − ι^Υ_(s0,2) (type s0) and μ_c1 := 2 − ι^Υ_(s1,2)
(type s1). These are μ_s0 + 1 and μ_(1,0) + 1 for the class roots μ_s0, μ_(1,0) ∈ (−2, −1) of □^Υ of
Section 23.16, so μ_c0, μ_c1 ∈ (−1, 0); the table places them in [−4e_Υγ_Υ²/3, 0) and (−1/4, 0), by
(23.9).

**Definition 32.30** (The offsets of the rows.) Put

    d_s1 := −1,     d_v1 = d_s0 = d_s2 := 0,     d_c0 := −μ_c0,     d_c1 := −μ_c1,    (32.29)

so that d_c0, d_c1 ∈ (0, 1). A *row* is ν = (τ, λ, k) with τ ∈ 𝒯 and (λ, k) ∈ ℰ_par; its K⁺-exponent is
e_ν := λ + d_τ. The offsets d_c0, d_c1 of the two class roots enter the gap condition (G) of Definition 33.3: no
λ + d_c0 and no λ + d_c1, λ in the exponent set Λ of Definition 33.1, has real part in (2, 2 + ε_K].

Let

    𝒩 := {ν = (τ, λ, k) : τ ∈ 𝒯, (λ, k) ∈ ℰ_par, Re e_ν ≤ 2},

a finite set, with Re λ ≤ 3 on it. The row ν records the term t_*^(−e_ν)(log t_*)^k h_τ (Definition 32.31) that the
ι⁺-exponent (λ, k) produces at K⁺ through (26.55): the s1 and v1 terms through a_s1 ∼ t_*^(−λ+1) and
a_v1 ∼ t_*^(−λ) of (26.54), the others through t_*^(−λ+μ). The rows of the table of Section 26.10 outside
𝒯 have μ ≤ −1 and are not the boost or rotation rows (whose rates come from (26.54)), so
Re(λ − μ) ≥ λ_♯ + 1 > 5/2, and they need no correction. The s1 rows with Re λ < 2 are the motions of
Section 32.7: {(s1, λ, k) : (λ, k) ∈ ℳ}.

(H3) (λ, k) + ℱ ⊂ ℰ_+ for every (τ, λ, k) ∈ 𝒩. For Re λ < 2 this holds by (32.16), as
ℰ_++ + ℰ_ind ⊂ ℰ_++ ⊂ ℰ_+.

*Coefficient spaces.* 𝒲_s1 = 𝒲_c1 := 𝒮_1, 𝒲_s0 = 𝒲_c0 := 𝒮_0, 𝒲_s2 := 𝒮_2, and 𝒲_v1 := 𝒱′, a fixed complement in
𝒱_1 of

    𝒱_K := {V ∈ 𝒱_1 : δ*_(g_(b₀)) ω^((−1))_(b₀,v1)(V) = 0},

the kernel of the state h_(b₀,v1) of (23.25), which contains every V whose rotation R_V is Killing for
g_(b₀) (Proposition 23.28 (3)). For V ∈ 𝒱_K the v1 term of (26.55) has no t_*^(−λ)-part at K⁺: as
δ*ω̆⁰_v1(V) = 0, its leading term carries a′_v1, of rate λ + 1 > 5/2. A parameter in 𝒱_K would correct nothing that
needs correcting and would make the finite-dimensional map of the elimination singular; hence the complement. At
b₀ = (m₀, 0), the non-rotating member (Proposition 21.17), every rotation is Killing, so 𝒱_K = 𝒱_1 and 𝒱′ = 0: the
v1 rows are kept in the notation and carry no parameter. This choice is kept at every base point b ∈ ℬ̄_*; at a
rotating b the v1 terms are carried by the rotation rows of Chapter 34 and Chapter 36. 𝒲_(τ,ℂ) is the
complexification. The parameters are p⃗ = (p⃗_(≤0), (W_ν)_(ν∈𝒩)), with p⃗_(≤0) = (S, b − b₀, S⁽⁰⁾_1) as in
Section 32.2 and W_ν ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ), conjugation-symmetric: W_(ν̄) is the complex conjugate of W_ν for
ν̄ := (τ, λ̄, k), which lies in 𝒩 (ℰ_par is closed under conjugation, and d_τ is real); so W_ν ∈ 𝒲_τ for real λ. 𝒫 is
the real vector space of these tuples. For ν = (s1, λ, k) with (λ, k) ∈ ℳ, W_ν is the motion parameter S^((λ−1,k))_1
of Section 32.7.

*Forcings.* Let ℰ_rows := ⋃_((τ,λ,k)∈𝒩) ((λ, k) + ℱ + ((0, 0) ∪ ℰ_+)), and fix an index set ℰ_src, closed under
conjugation, with

    ℰ̃_+ ∪ 2ℰ_+ ∪ ℰ_rows ⊂ ℰ_src,      ℰ_src ∩ {Re < 2} ⊂ ℰ_++;    (32.30)

Chapter 33 may enlarge it within (32.30). The least choice satisfies the second condition: ℰ̃_+ and 2ℰ_+ lie
in {Re ≥ 2} ((H1): 2λ_♯ > 3), and an element of ℰ_rows with real part below 2 has no ℰ_+-summand (which adds at least
λ_♯ to Re λ ≥ λ_♯), so it is (λ, k) + (w, l) with (λ, k) ∈ ℳ and (w, l) ∈ ℱ, in ℰ_++ by (32.16). For
α ∈ (2, 4 + ε_K] let

    𝒴_1(α) := ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′,ℓ_I+1),((ℰ_src)_(≥2)+2,w_+−ε),α)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−),
    (ℰ_src)_(≥2) := ℰ_src ∩ {Re ≥ 2},

let 𝒴_2(α) be the sections supported in supp χ^♯_K ((29.2)) lying in ⋂_ε H^(∞,∞,(ℰ_src+2,w_+−ε),α)_b, and
𝒴(α) := 𝒴_1(α) + 𝒴_2(α), real sections: the analogue of [Hin26, (11.195)]. In this and the next section, and in
Chapter 33, 𝒴_1(α), 𝒴_2(α) and 𝒴(α) denote these classes. For α ∈ (2, 3), 𝒴(α) lies in the class of
Section 32.6 of the same name: 𝒴_1(α) has plain ι⁺-weight 4 − ε, and the exponents of ℰ_src + 2 below 4 lie in
ℰ_++ + 2 by (32.30). "h small" means as in Section 32.6. For complex W and h ∈ 𝒳^∞, the tensors f^ν(W),
r^ν(W) and E^ν(W) of Lemma 32.36 (b), (c) and (e) lie in 𝒴_2(α) + i𝒴_2(α); the conjugation-symmetric sums over 𝒩
are real and lie in 𝒴_2(α).

### 32.11 Correction terms of the fourth kind and the operator

*Towers.* Put K_s1 = K_s0 := 4, K_v1 = K_s2 := 3, K_c0 = K_c1 := 2. For τ ∈ 𝒯 and W ∈ 𝒲_τ let ω̆^i_τ(W),
0 ≤ i ≤ K_τ, be the following stationary 1-forms at b₀, linear in W (extended complex-linearly to 𝒲_(τ,ℂ)):

(s1) ω̆⁰ := ω⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s1)(S), ω̆¹ := ω̆^((0),1)_(b₀,s1)(S) (Proposition 23.28), ω̆^i := ω̆^((0),i)_(b₀,s1)(S),
i = 2, 3, 4 (Proposition 23.34 (2)): the ω̆^i(S) of Section 32.7;

(v1) ω̆⁰ := ω^((−1))_(b₀,v1)(V) (Proposition 23.28), ω̆^i := ω̆^((−1),i)_(b₀,v1)(V), i = 1, 2, 3
(Proposition 23.34 (3));

(s0) ω̆⁰ := ω⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s0)(S), ω̆^i := ω̆^((0),i)_(b₀,s0)(S), i = 1, …, 4 (Proposition 23.34 (1)), with 𝒮_0 = ℝ
acting by multiplication;

(s2) ω̆⁰ := ω^((−1))_(b₀)(S) and ω̆^i := ω̆^((−1),i)_(b₀)(S), i ≤ 3, of Proposition 23.34 (4)–(7) at the sl root
−l + 1 = −1, l = 2, of Section 23.16, whose range is 5 − l = 3;

(c0) the same at the s0 class root μ_s0 = μ_c0 − 1, range 2; (c1) the same at the s1 class root μ_(1,0) = μ_c1 − 1,
range 2.

In every case ω^(≤k)_τ := Σ_(i≤k) (k!/(k − i)!) t_*^(k−i) ω̆^i_τ ∈ ker □^Υ_(b₀) for k ≤ K_τ (Proposition 23.34,
in its convention, as in Section 32.7), with □^Υ_(b₀) = 2δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀))δ*_(g_(b₀)). Near infinity in
X̄, with the leading exponents ς_τ (ς_τ is an exponent, not a spectral parameter),

    ω̆^i_τ ∈ 𝒜^((ς_τ−i,0)+ℱ),     ς_s1 = ς_s0 := 0,     ς_v1 = ς_s2 := −1,
    ς_c0 := μ_c0 − 1,     ς_c1 := μ_c1 − 1:    (32.31)

for s1 by Section 31.4 and Proposition 23.34 (2) (as in the proof of Lemma 32.20); for v1 by
(23.23) (ω^((−1))_(b₀,v1)(V) − V ∈ 𝒜^((2,0)+ℱ), the rotation 1-form V homogeneous of degree 1) and
Proposition 23.34 (3); for s0 as ω⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s0) = g_(b₀)(∂_(t_*), ·) differs from a form with constant Cartesian
components by ρ²C^∞ ((23.22)–(23.23)), ω̆^((0),1)_(b₀,s0) − χ_∂W̄ ∈ 𝒜^((1,0)+ℰ_ind) with W̄
homogeneous of degree 1, and Proposition 23.34 (1) for i ≥ 2; for s2, c0, c1 by Proposition 23.34 (4)–(7). The
*states* are

    h_τ(W) := δ*_(g_(b₀)) ω̆⁰_τ(W)   (τ ≠ s0),        h_s0(S) := h⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s0)(S) = δ*_(g_(b₀)) ω^((0),≤1)_(b₀,s0)(S)

((23.32)); so h_s1(S) = h(S), h_v1 = h_(b₀,v1) of (23.25), which vanishes on 𝒱_K, and for s2,
c0, c1, h_τ = h^((μ+1))_(b₀) of Proposition 23.34 (4)–(7). ω⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s0) is Killing:
δ*_(g_(b₀))ω⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s0) = 0 (Proposition 23.28 (2)).

**Definition 32.31** (Corrections of the fourth kind; [Hin26, Definition 11.55] in dimension 4 + 1.) For
ν = (τ, λ, k) ∈ 𝒩 let r_ν(t_*) := t_*^(−e_ν)(log t_*)^k (on Ω_*, where t_* ≥ 1) and a_ν := r_ν for τ ≠ s0, while for
τ = s0

    a_ν(t_*) := A_ν(t_*) := (−1)^k ∂_λ^k (t_*^(1−λ)/(1 − λ)),     so that A′_ν = r_ν

([Hin26, (11.190)]; λ ≠ 1, as Re λ ≥ λ_♯). For W ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ) put

    ω_ν(W) := Σ_(i=0)^(K_τ) a_ν^((i))(t_*) ω̆^i_τ(W),     m_ν(W) := χ_K δ*_(g_(b₀)) ω_ν(W),
    h_ν(W) := −[δ*_(g_(b₀)), χ_K]ω_ν(W) = −dχ_K ⊗_s ω_ν(W),
    ϑ_ν(W) := δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)) m_ν(W),     ϑ_(ν,♯)(W) := ϑ_ν(W) − δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)) h_ν(W),

the last the counterterm of [Hin26, Remark 11.27], as in Definition 31.9, Definition 32.5 and
Definition 32.19. For ν = (s1, λ, k) with (λ, k) ∈ ℳ these are the m_(λ,k), h^((λ−1,k))_s1, ϑ^((λ−1,k))_s1 and
ϑ^((λ−1,k))_(s1,♯) of Definition 32.19 (a_ν = t_*^(−λ+1)(log t_*)^k). [Hin26] indexes its tensors by the K⁺-rate
([Hin26, footnote 123]); here the index is the ι⁺-exponent λ, with the rate e_ν recorded, as [Hin26, footnote 124]
does for the class-root parameters. Since a_(ν̄) is the complex conjugate of a_ν and the ω̆^i_τ are real on 𝒲_τ,
m_(ν̄)(W̄) is the complex conjugate of m_ν(W), and likewise for h_ν, ϑ_ν and ϑ_(ν,♯).

**Lemma 32.32** (The memberships of [Hin26, Definition 11.55] and [Hin26, (11.187)–(11.189)] in dimension
4 + 1.) Let ν = (τ, λ, k) ∈ 𝒩, W ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ) and a := a_ν.

(a) There are stationary operators A_1, A_2 with

    □^Υ_(b₀) ω_ν(W) = a^((K_τ+1))(A_1ω̆^(K_τ)_τ + A_2ω̆^(K_τ−1)_τ) + a^((K_τ+2))A_2ω̆^(K_τ)_τ.    (32.32)

(b) Near (ι⁺)°: ω_ν(W) ∈ 𝒜^((λ−1,k)+ℱ); m_ν(W), h_ν(W) ∈ 𝒜^((λ,k)+ℱ); ϑ_ν(W), ϑ_(ν,♯)(W) ∈ 𝒜^((λ+1,k)+ℱ); and
D_(g_0)Ric(h_ν(W)) ∈ 𝒜^((λ+2,k)+ℱ) (g_0 as in Lemma 31.10).

(c) h_ν(W) is supported in 𝒞; m_ν(W), ϑ_ν(W), ϑ_(ν,♯)(W) in supp χ_K; all vanish for t^♭_* < 10.

(d) Near K⁺, ϑ_(ν,♯)(W) = ϑ_ν(W) = ½□^Υ_(b₀)ω_ν(W), of K⁺-weight κ_ν − ε for every ε > 0, where

    κ_ν := Re λ + 4   (τ ∈ {s1, v1, s0, s2}),        κ_ν := Re λ + d_τ + 3   (τ ∈ {c0, c1});

in every case κ_ν > λ_♯ + 3 = 9/2 + δ_♯.

(e) m_ν(W) − χ_K r_ν h_τ(W) has K⁺-weight Re e_ν + 1 − ε, and m_ν(W) has K⁺-weight Re e_ν − ε, for every ε > 0.

(f) h_τ is injective on 𝒲_(τ,ℂ).

All seminorms are O(|W|).

*Proof.* (a) As (32.18): □ := □^Υ_(b₀) is stationary and of second order in ∂_(t_*), so
□(φ(t_*)v) = Σ_(m=0)^2 φ^((m))A_mv for stationary v, and □ω_ν = Σ_(j≤K_τ+2) a^((j))B_j,
B_j := Σ_m A_mω̆^(j−m)_τ (ω̆^i_τ := 0 for i < 0 and for i > K_τ). With t_*^k, k ≤ K_τ, in place of a this is
□ω^(≤k)_τ = 0, whose t_*⁰-coefficient is k!B_k; so B_j = 0 for j ≤ K_τ, and B_(K_τ+1), B_(K_τ+2) are as stated.

(b) Near (ι⁺)°, |x| ∼ t_* ∼ ρ_+⁻¹, so ω̆^i_τ ∈ 𝒜^((ς_τ−i,0)+ℱ) there by (32.31), and
a^((i)) ∈ 𝒜^((λ−1−ς_τ+i,k)): for τ ≠ s0, a^((i)) is a combination of t_*^(−e_ν−i)(log t_*)^j, j ≤ k, and
e_ν = λ − 1 − ς_τ (s1: λ − 1; v1, s2: λ; c0, c1: λ − μ_τ); for s0, A_ν^((i)) is a combination of
t_*^(1−λ−i)(log t_*)^j, j ≤ k. So each term of ω_ν lies in 𝒜^((λ−1,k)+ℱ). δ*_(g_(b₀)), δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀)) and
D_(g_0)Ric lie in ρ_+Diff¹_b, ρ_+Diff¹_b and ρ_+²Diff²_b there, and dχ_K ∈ ρ_+C^∞ (Section 31.4), which gives
the orders, as in Lemma 32.20.

(c) Every derivative of χ_K is supported in 𝒞, and supp χ_K ⊂ {t^♭_* ≥ 10} ((29.2));
δ_(E_Υ)Gh_ν is supported in 𝒞 ⊂ supp χ_K.

(d) Near K⁺, χ_K = 1, so h_ν = 0, m_ν = δ*ω_ν and ϑ_ν = ½□ω_ν, which by (32.32) is a^((K_τ+1)) and
a^((K_τ+2)) times stationary tensors smooth on compact spatial sets. For τ ≠ s0, a^((K_τ+1)) has K⁺-weight
Re e_ν + K_τ + 1 − ε: Re λ − 1 + 5 (s1), Re λ + 4 (v1, s2), Re λ + d_τ + 3 (c0, c1); for s0, A_ν^((5)) = r_ν^((4)) has
weight Re λ + 4 − ε. Since Re λ ≥ λ_♯ by (32.28) and d_τ > 0, κ_ν > λ_♯ + 3.

(e) For stationary v, δ*_(g_(b₀))(φ(t_*)v) = φ(δ*_(g_(b₀)))^(0)v + φ′ dt_* ⊗_s v ((32.1),
(23.28)). For τ ≠ s0 the term of δ*ω_ν without a derivative of a is a(δ*_(g_(b₀)))^(0)ω̆⁰_τ = r_νh_τ, and
every other term carries a^((j)), j ≥ 1, of K⁺-weight Re e_ν + 1 − ε. For s0, (δ*_(g_(b₀)))^(0)ω̆⁰ = 0 (Killing); the
terms carrying A′_ν = r_ν are r_ν(dt_* ⊗_s ω̆⁰ + (δ*_(g_(b₀)))^(0)ω̆¹) = r_νh⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s0) (as
h⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s0) = δ*(t_*ω̆⁰ + ω̆¹)), and the others carry A_ν^((j)) = r_ν^((j−1)), j ≥ 2, of weight Re λ + 1 − ε. h_τ is
stationary, which gives the weight of m_ν.

(f) s1: h is injective by the rows of (28.9) (Section 32.1). v1: by the choice of 𝒱′. s0: 𝒮_0 = ℝ, and
h⁽⁰⁾_(b₀,s0) has the nonzero leading term h̄⁽⁰⁾_s0 (Proposition 23.34 (1)). s2, c0, c1: h_τ(S) has the leading term
(δ̄*)^(0)ω̄, where (δ̄*)^(0) is the zero energy operator of δ* for the Minkowski model, and this is nonzero for the
nonzero indicial solution ω̄ that S ≠ 0 gives (Proposition 23.34 (4)–(7)). The
complex-linear extension keeps injectivity. ∎

Here (δ*_(g_(b₀)))^(0) is, as in Section 32.7, the zero energy operator of δ*_(g_(b₀)) of (23.28).
The gauge towers of Proposition 23.34 have exactly the lengths needed: every counterterm ϑ_ν has K⁺-order
κ_ν > 9/2 + δ_♯, above the 4 + ε_K that the forcings of Chapter 33 carry; the shortest towers (length 2, the class
roots) are compensated by their larger rate λ + d_τ.

**Definition 32.33** (The operator with all modification parameters; [Hin26, Definition 11.56] in
dimension 4 + 1.) For p⃗ = (p⃗_(≤0), (W_ν)_(ν∈𝒩)) ∈ 𝒫 small and h small, with g_0 := g_(p⃗_(≤0)) ((32.4)),

    h_tot(p⃗) := h_(tot,2)(p⃗_(≤0)) + Σ_(ν∈𝒩) h_ν(W_ν),     ϑ_tot(p⃗) := ϑ_(tot,2)(p⃗_(≤0)) + Σ_(ν∈𝒩) ϑ_(ν,♯)(W_ν),

the first terms those of Definition 32.7, and, with g′ := g_0 + h_tot(p⃗) + h,

    P_4(h, p⃗) := Ric(g′) − δ*_(g_0,E_C)(Υ^(E_Υ)(g′, g_0) − ϑ_tot(p⃗)),    (32.33)

and L_(h,p⃗) := D_hP_4(·, p⃗) at h. The sums are real by the conjugation symmetry (Definition 32.31). The formulas
extend holomorphically to tuples (W_ν) near 𝒫 without the symmetry; a derivative in one W_ν, written
D_p⃗P_4(h, p⃗)(W_ν = W), is taken in that extension and is complex-linear in W. P_4 = P_3 ((32.20), with
S^((λ−1,k))_1 = W_((s1,λ,k))) where W_ν = 0 for the rows outside {(s1, λ, k) : (λ, k) ∈ ℳ}, and P_4 = P_2
((32.6)) where every W_ν = 0.

**Lemma 32.34** (The row identity; [Hin26, (11.187)–(11.189)] in dimension 4 + 1.) For ν ∈ 𝒩 and
W ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ), D_p⃗P_4(0, 0)(W_ν = W) = L_(b₀)(m_ν(W)), and m_ν(W), vanishing for t^♭_* < 10, is its forward solution
(Proposition 17.14). The identities (32.7) hold for P_4.

*Proof.* At p⃗ = 0, g′ = g_0 = g_(b₀); g_0 does not depend on W_ν, and, by (32.1),
ġ′ = h_ν(W) = χ_Kδ*ω_ν − δ*(χ_Kω_ν) = m_ν(W) − ζ_ν(W), ζ_ν(W) := δ*_(g_(b₀))(χ_Kω_ν(W)). By (ii),
D_1Υ^(E_Υ)(g_(b₀), g_(b₀)) = −δ_(E_Υ)G, so DP_4 = DRic(ġ′) + δ*_(E_C)(δ_(E_Υ)Gġ′ + ϑ_(ν,♯)(W)); by (iii)
DRic(ζ_ν) = 0, and δ_(E_Υ)Gh_ν + ϑ_(ν,♯) = ϑ_ν = δ_(E_Υ)Gm_ν, so DP_4 = DRic(m_ν) + δ*_(E_C)δ_(E_Υ)Gm_ν = L_(b₀)m_ν. On
the directions of p⃗_(≤0), P_4 = P_2 at W = 0, which gives (32.7). ∎

The identity is exact because the gauge term is the full δ_(E_Υ)G of the cut-off pure gauge tensor, not a commutator;
(32.32) makes it decay to K⁺-order κ_ν, which is why the towers have length K_τ. [Hin26, (11.187)–(11.189)]
are the same calculation written as L_(b₀)(χ_Kδ*ω) = −DRic([δ*, χ_K]ω) + δ*_(E_C)δ_(E_Υ)G(χ_Kδ*ω).

**Lemma 32.35** (The linearisation in h.) Let p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 (with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*) and h be small. Then
h_tot(p⃗) ∈ 𝒳^∞ with ‖h_tot(p⃗)‖_(𝒳^k) ≤ C_k|p⃗|, L_(h,p⃗) = L^(g′,g_0), and Lemma 32.9 (b)–(c) hold for
L_(h,p⃗).

*Proof.* As Lemma 32.9 and Lemma 32.23: the new terms h_ν(W_ν) are supported in 𝒞, whose closure meets
∂M only in a compact subset of (ι⁺)°, and lie in 𝒜^((λ,k)+ℱ) ⊂ 𝒜^(ℰ_+) there, by Lemma 32.32 (b) and (H3). ∎

*At a base point with parameter b.* The rows and towers are built at b (Lemma 36.1): there
m_ν(W) := χ_K δ*_(g_b)ω^b_ν(W), with ω^b_ν(W) := Σ_(i=0)^(K_τ) a_ν^((i))(t_*)ω̆^i_(τ,b)(W) built as in
Definition 32.31 from the 1-forms ω̆^i_(τ,b)(W) of Proposition 23.34 at b, while the corrections and the
counterterms in P_4 stay those built at b₀. We write ω^(b₀)_ν := ω_ν, m^(b₀)_ν, h^(b₀)_ν, ϑ^(b₀)_ν and ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) for
the tensors of Definition 32.31 built at b₀; so ϑ^(b₀)_ν = δ_(g_(b₀),E_Υ)G_(g_(b₀))m^(b₀)_ν involves the row built at
b₀, not m_ν, and h^(b₀)_ν, ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) are the h_ν, ϑ_(ν,♯) of P_4 at every base point, which is how h_ν, ϑ_ν and
ϑ_(ν,♯) are read in (a), (b) and (d) of Lemma 32.36. Lemma 32.32 holds at b for the tensors built at b,
with the same proof ((P3); (P5) for the s0 rows, whose gauge 1-form is Killing for every g_b; (f) by
Lemma 36.3); the conjugation symmetry of Definition 32.31 holds for them, the towers at b being real ((P3));
and Lemma 32.35 holds at b. Lemma 32.34 is an identity at (0, 0), so at b₀; its form at b is
Lemma 32.36 (e) below.

**Lemma 32.36** ([Hin26, Lemma 11.57] in dimension 4 + 1.) Let p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 (with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*) and
h ∈ 𝒳^k, k ≥ 5, be small, and α ∈ (2, 4 + ε_K].

(a) The derivatives f^S_(h,p⃗), f^b_(h,p⃗), f^s1_(h,p⃗) of P_4 in S, b, S⁽⁰⁾_1 satisfy Lemma 32.10 up to a term
(∂δ*_(g_0,E_C))ϑ_rows, ϑ_rows := Σ_(ν∈𝒩) ϑ_(ν,♯)(W_ν), which lies in 𝒴_2(α). For h ∈ 𝒳^∞: f^S_(h,p⃗) and
f^s1_(h,p⃗) lie in 𝒴(α), and f^b_(h,p⃗) in 𝒴_2(α).

(b) For ν = (τ, λ, k) ∈ 𝒩 and W ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ), f^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) := D_p⃗P_4(h, p⃗)(W_ν = W) is supported in supp χ_K and, for
every ε > 0,

    f^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) ∈ H^(k−2,∞,((λ+2,k)+ℱ+((0,0)∪ℰ_+),a_++Re λ+2−ε),κ_ν−ε)_b(Ω_*),

with norm O(|W|); for h ∈ 𝒳^∞ it lies in 𝒴_2(α), and in the class 𝒴_2(α′) of Section 32.6 for every
α′ ∈ (2, 3).

(c) Let b = b₀. Then f^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν(W) + r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W), where, with
ζ_ν(W) := δ*_(g_(b₀))(χ_Kω_ν(W)) = m_ν(W) − h_ν(W),

    r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) = −(L_(h,p⃗) − L_(b₀))ζ_ν(W) + (δ*_(g_0,E_C) − δ*_(g_(b₀),E_C))ϑ_(ν,♯)(W).    (32.34)

r^ν_(0,0) = 0; r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) is supported in supp χ_K, and for every ε > 0

    r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) ∈ H^(k−2,∞,Re λ+2+λ_♯−ε,Re e_ν+a_K−ε)_b(Ω_*),   with norm ≤ C_ε|W|(‖h‖_(𝒳^k) + |p⃗|).    (32.35)

In particular, for h ∈ 𝒳^∞, r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) ∈ 𝒴_2(α), each seminorm bounded by C|W|(‖h‖_(𝒳^(k′)) + |p⃗|) for some k′.

(d) All are linear in the direction (complex-linear in W), continuous in (h, p⃗) with h ∈ 𝒳^k, and at (0, 0) given by
(32.7) and Lemma 32.34.

(e) Let b ∈ ℬ̄_*, with the rows m_ν built at b, and let h^b_ν, ϑ^b_ν, ϑ^b_(ν,♯) and
ζ^b_ν := δ*_(g_b)(χ_Kω^b_ν) = m_ν − h^b_ν be the tensors of Definition 32.31 and of (c) built at b, with g_b and the
1-forms ω̆^i_(τ,b) in place of g_(b₀) and ω̆^i_τ. Then

    f^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν(W) + r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) + E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W),
    r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) := −(L_(h,p⃗) − L_b)ζ^b_ν(W) + (δ*_(g_0,E_C) − δ*_(g_b,E_C))ϑ^b_(ν,♯)(W),
    E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) := L_(h,p⃗)(h^(b₀)_ν − h^b_ν)(W) + δ*_(g_0,E_C)(ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) − ϑ^b_(ν,♯))(W),    (32.36)

which is the identity (36.1). r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) is supported in supp χ_K and lies in the class
(32.35), with norm ≤ C_ε|W|(‖h‖_(𝒳^k) + |p⃗|) uniformly on ℬ̄_*; so it lies in 𝒴_2(α) for h ∈ 𝒳^∞, as in (c),
and r^ν_(0,p⃗_b)(W) = O(|b − b₀||W|). E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W), the difference between the corrections and counterterms built at
b₀ and at b, is supported in supp χ_K and lies in the class of (b): for every ε > 0

    E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) ∈ H^(k−2,∞,((λ+2,k)+ℱ+((0,0)∪ℰ_+),a_++Re λ+2−ε),κ_ν−ε)_b(Ω_*),   with norm ≤ C_ε|b − b₀||W|,

C_ε uniform for (h, p⃗) small and b ∈ ℬ̄_*. So, for h ∈ 𝒳^∞, E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) lies in 𝒴_2(α), and in the class 𝒴_2(α′)
of Section 32.6 for every α′ ∈ (2, 3), as f^ν does in (b), each seminorm bounded by C|b − b₀||W|(1 + ‖h‖_(𝒳^(k′)))
for some k′. At b = b₀, E^ν = 0 and (e) is (c).

*Proof.* (a) As Lemma 32.24 (a): the counts of Lemma 32.10 use h_tot only through
g′ − η ∈ H^(k,(ℰ_+,a_+))_b near (ι⁺)°, which still holds (Lemma 32.35), and the derivative in S, b or S⁽⁰⁾_1
falls on the row terms only through δ*_(g_0,E_C), which depends on these parameters through g_0, applied to ϑ_rows.
That term is linear in the W_ν and supported in supp χ_K; for S and S⁽⁰⁾_1 in 𝒞, as ∂g_0 is supported in
supp(1 − χ_K) there ((32.4)). Near (ι⁺)° its order is at least Re λ + 4 ≥ λ_♯ + 4 > w_+: the derivative of
g_0 has ι⁺-order 2 (Lemma 32.4 (c) for S, S⁽⁰⁾_1; ∂_bg_0 = χ_K ∂_bg_b ∈ ρ_+²C^∞ for b, as in the proof of
Lemma 32.10 (b)),
δ*_(g,E_C) ∈ ρ_+Diff¹_b, and ϑ has order λ + 1 (Lemma 32.32 (b)). Its K⁺-weight is
κ_ν − ε > 9/2 + δ_♯ − ε > 4 + ε_K ≥ α for ε small (Lemma 32.32 (d), (32.27)). So it lies in 𝒴_2(α).
Next, f^S and f^s1 satisfy (31.23) (Lemma 32.10 (a)): ℐ⁺-data (⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′, a_I + 1), contained in
those of 𝒴_1 as ℓ_I ≤ a_I; ι⁺-index set (ℰ̃_+ ∪ 2ℰ_+) + 2 ⊂ (ℰ_src)_(≥2) + 2 by (32.30) and
min Re(ℰ̃_+ ∪ 2ℰ_+) ≥ 2; remainder a_+ + 2 + min(2, m_+) − ε = a_+ + 2 + λ_♯ − ε by (H1), and
a_+ + 2 + λ_♯ > 2λ_♯ + 2 = 5 + 2δ_♯ > w_+ by (32.27); K⁺-weight ∞. So they lie in 𝒴_1(α) + 𝒴_2(α). f^b
satisfies (32.8): it is supported in supp χ_K, with ι⁺-data (ℰ̃_+ + 2, a_+ + 4 − ε), a_+ + 4 > w_+, and
K⁺-weight a_K ≥ 4 + ε_K ≥ α by (H2); so it lies in 𝒴_2(α).

(b) P_4 depends on W_ν only through h_ν(W_ν) in g′ (in 𝒞) and ϑ_(ν,♯)(W_ν) in ϑ_tot (in supp χ_K), linearly; so,
with h′ := h_ν(W),

    f^ν = D_(g′)Ric(h′) − δ*_(g_0,E_C)(D_1Υ^(E_Υ)(g′, g_0)h′ − ϑ_(ν,♯)(W))
        = D_(g′)Ric(h′) − δ*_(g_0,E_C)([D_1Υ(g′, g_0) − D_1Υ(g_(b₀), g_(b₀))]h′ − ϑ_ν(W))    (32.37)

by the definition of the counterterm and (ii). The counts are those of Lemma 32.24 (b):
D_(g′)Ric ∈ ρ_+²(C^∞ + H^((ℰ_+,a_+))_b)Diff²_b, δ*_(g_0,E_C) ∈ ρ_+Diff¹_b, the bracket linear in
(g′ − g_(b₀), g_0 − g_(b₀)) ∈ H^((ℰ_+,a_+))_b and their first derivatives, and Lemma 32.32 (b) give the
ι⁺-data; near K⁺ only δ*_(g_0,E_C)ϑ_ν remains (h′ = 0 there), and there g_0 = g_b ((32.4)), so it is
δ*_(g_b,E_C)ϑ_ν, of weight κ_ν − ε, δ*_(g_b,E_C) being stationary; at b = b₀ it is δ*_(g_(b₀),E_C)ϑ_ν. For 𝒴_2(α): the
index set lies in ℰ_rows + 2 ⊂ ℰ_src + 2 by (32.30); the remainder a_+ + Re λ + 2 > 2λ_♯ + 2 > w_+; and
κ_ν − ε ≥ α as in (a). For the class 𝒴_2(α′) of Section 32.6 (index set ℰ_++ + 2, remainder 4 − ε): if Re λ < 2, then
(λ, k) ∈ ℳ and (λ, k) + ℱ + ((0, 0) ∪ ℰ_+) ⊂ ℰ_++ by (32.16); if Re λ ≥ 2, every exponent has real part at
least 4; and κ_ν − ε > 3.

(c) L_(h,p⃗) = L^(g′,g_0) = D_(g′)Ric − δ*_(g_0,E_C)D_1Υ^(E_Υ)(g′, g_0) (Lemma 32.35), so (32.37)
reads f^ν = L_(h,p⃗)h_ν + δ*_(g_0,E_C)ϑ_(ν,♯) = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν − L_(h,p⃗)ζ_ν + δ*_(g_0,E_C)ϑ_(ν,♯). At (0, 0),

    L_(b₀)ζ_ν = D_(g_(b₀))Ric(ζ_ν) + δ*_(g_(b₀),E_C)δ_(E_Υ)Gζ_ν = δ*_(g_(b₀),E_C)(ϑ_ν − δ_(E_Υ)Gh_ν)
               = δ*_(g_(b₀),E_C)ϑ_(ν,♯),

by (iii) and ζ_ν = m_ν − h_ν. Subtracting gives (32.34), and r^ν_(0,0) = 0 as g′ = g_0 = g_(b₀) there.
ζ_ν is supported in supp χ_K, equals m_ν near K⁺ (weight Re e_ν − ε, Lemma 32.32 (e)), and lies in
𝒜^((λ,k)+ℱ) near (ι⁺)° (Lemma 32.32 (b)), with seminorms O(|W|). *The first term of (32.34).* Near
(ι⁺)°, L^(g′,g_0) − L^(g_(b₀),g_(b₀)) lies in ρ_+²Diff²_b with coefficients linear, with smooth bounded factors, in
g′ − g_(b₀), g_0 − g_(b₀) and their b-derivatives of order at most 2: the count of (29.15). There
g_0 − g_(b₀) ∈ ρ_+²C^∞ with seminorms O(|p⃗|) (Lemma 32.4 (c)), and h_tot(p⃗) + h ∈ H^(k,(ℰ_+,a_+))_b with norm
O(|p⃗| + ‖h‖_(𝒳^k)) (Lemma 32.35); as (2, 0) ∈ ℰ_+ and m_+ = λ_♯ (H1), both lie in ρ_+^(λ_♯−ε)H^k_b. So the
first term lies in ρ_+^(Re λ+2+λ_♯−2ε)H^(k−2)_b near (ι⁺)°. Near K⁺, g_0 = g_(b₀) and h_tot(p⃗) = 0 (every correction
is supported in 𝒞: Lemma 31.10, Definition 32.7 at b = b₀, Lemma 32.32 (c)), so
L_(h,p⃗) − L_(b₀) = L^(g_(b₀)+h,g_(b₀)) − L_(b₀) has coefficients of K⁺-weight a_K with norm O(‖h‖_(𝒳^k))
((29.15)), and the first term has K⁺-weight Re e_ν + a_K − ε. ζ_ν vanishes near ℐ⁺; the weights combine at
the corner of ι⁺ and K⁺ as in Proposition 29.12. *The second term.* At b = b₀,
g_0 − g_(b₀) = (1 − χ_K)((ψ_(−S⁽⁰⁾_1) ∘ φ_(−S))*g_(b₀) − g_(b₀)) is supported in supp(1 − χ_K) and ϑ_(ν,♯) in
supp χ_K, so the term is supported in 𝒞, away from K⁺ and ℐ⁺. δ*_(g,E_C) ∈ ρ_+Diff¹_b near (ι⁺)° with coefficients
depending smoothly on g and its first derivatives (Definition 21.28), so δ*_(g_0,E_C) − δ*_(g_(b₀),E_C) ∈
ρ_+³Diff¹_b there with seminorms O(|p⃗|), as in (a); the term has ι⁺-order Re λ + 4 ≥ Re λ + 2 + λ_♯. This gives
(32.35). Finally Re λ + 2 + λ_♯ ≥ 2λ_♯ + 2 = 5 + 2δ_♯ > w_+ by (32.27), and
Re e_ν + a_K ≥ λ_♯ − 1 + 4 + ε_K > α by (H2) (e_ν ≥ λ − 1); so r^ν ∈ 𝒴_2(α) when h ∈ 𝒳^∞, with the stated bounds
(each seminorm of H^(k″) uses h ∈ 𝒳^(k″+2)).

(d) Linearity is clear from (32.33); continuity as in Lemma 32.10 (c), g′ and g_0 depending smoothly
on (h, p⃗) (Lemma 32.4 (a), Lemma 32.35); the values at (0, 0) are Lemma 32.34.

(e) *The identity.* The first line of the proof of (c), f^ν = L_(h,p⃗)h^(b₀)_ν + δ*_(g_0,E_C)ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) (the tensors
of P_4 being those built at b₀), uses only (32.37) and L_(h,p⃗) = L^(g′,g_0), and holds at every base point;
adding and subtracting the tensors built at b, f^ν = L_(h,p⃗)h^b_ν + δ*_(g_0,E_C)ϑ^b_(ν,♯) + E^ν. By (32.1) at
g_b, h^b_ν = m_ν − ζ^b_ν, and the display of the proof of (c), at g_b, which is Ricci flat, gives
L_bζ^b_ν = δ*_(g_b,E_C)ϑ^b_(ν,♯). Writing L_(h,p⃗)ζ^b_ν = L_bζ^b_ν + (L_(h,p⃗) − L_b)ζ^b_ν gives
(32.36), as in the proof of Lemma 32.25. *The class of r^ν.* The counts of (c) apply with L_b,
g_b, ζ^b_ν and ϑ^b_(ν,♯) in place of L_(b₀), g_(b₀), ζ_ν and ϑ_(ν,♯). ζ^b_ν has the memberships of ζ_ν, by
Lemma 32.32 at b. Near (ι⁺)°, g_0 − g_b ∈ ρ_+²C^∞ with seminorms O(|p⃗|) (Lemma 32.4 (a), (c)). Near K⁺,
g_0 = g_b and h_tot(p⃗) = 0 ((32.4); every correction is supported in 𝒞), so
L_(h,p⃗) − L_b = L^(g_b+h,g_b) − L_b has coefficients of K⁺-weight a_K with norm O(‖h‖_(𝒳^k)). And
g_0 − g_b = (1 − χ_K)((ψ_(−S⁽⁰⁾_1) ∘ φ_(−S))*g_(b₀) − g_b) is supported in supp(1 − χ_K), so the second term is
supported in 𝒞. The constants are uniform in b by (P3), and the case h = 0, p⃗ = p⃗_b, |p⃗_b| = |b − b₀|, gives the bound
at (0, p⃗_b).

*E^ν: support and size.* Put Δh := h^(b₀)_ν − h^b_ν and Δϑ := ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) − ϑ^b_(ν,♯), so that
E^ν = L_(h,p⃗)Δh + δ*_(g_0,E_C)Δϑ. Δh = −dχ_K ⊗_s (ω^(b₀)_ν − ω^b_ν) is supported in 𝒞, and Δϑ in supp χ_K
(Lemma 32.32 (c) at b₀ and at b), so E^ν is supported in supp χ_K. By (P3) the 1-forms ω̆^i_(τ,b)(W) are smooth
in b as polyhomogeneous sections with the index sets of (32.31), which do not depend on b, and g_b is smooth
in b; so the tensors of Definition 32.31 built at b are smooth in b in the classes of Lemma 32.32 (b) and (d)
at b, and the mean value theorem along the segment from b₀ to b, which lies in ℬ̄_*, shows that Δh and Δϑ have the
memberships of h_ν and ϑ_(ν,♯) there, with every seminorm at most C|b − b₀||W|.

*E^ν at ι⁺.* Near (ι⁺)°, Δh ∈ 𝒜^((λ,k)+ℱ) and Δϑ ∈ 𝒜^((λ+1,k)+ℱ). There
L_(h,p⃗) = D_(g′)Ric − δ*_(g_0,E_C)D_1Υ^(E_Υ)(g′, g_0) lies in ρ_+²(C^∞ + H^((ℰ_+,a_+))_b)Diff²_b, as
g′ − η ∈ ρ_+²C^∞ + H^(k,(ℰ_+,a_+))_b and g_0 − η ∈ ρ_+²C^∞ (Lemma 32.35, Lemma 32.4 (c)), and
δ*_(g_0,E_C) ∈ ρ_+Diff¹_b with smooth coefficients. So, by the counts of (b), L_(h,p⃗)Δh and δ*_(g_0,E_C)Δϑ have the
ι⁺-data ((λ + 2, k) + ℱ + ((0, 0) ∪ ℰ_+), a_+ + Re λ + 2 − ε), with norms at most C_ε|b − b₀||W|.

*E^ν at K⁺.* Near K⁺, χ_K = 1, so Δh = 0 and, by Lemma 32.32 (d) at b₀ and at b,
Δϑ = ½(□^Υ_(b₀)ω^(b₀)_ν − □^Υ_bω^b_ν). By (32.32) at b₀ and at b this is a^((K_τ+1)) and a^((K_τ+2)) times
differences of stationary tensors, smooth on compact spatial sets and of size O(|b − b₀||W|) there; a^((K_τ+1)) has
K⁺-weight κ_ν − ε, and a^((K_τ+2)) a larger one (the proof of Lemma 32.32 (d)). δ*_(g_0,E_C) = δ*_(g_b,E_C)
there ((32.4)) is stationary and keeps the weight. So E^ν has K⁺-weight κ_ν − ε with norm at most
C|b − b₀||W|, and the two weights combine at the corner of ι⁺ and K⁺ as in Proposition 29.12. This is the class
stated in (e), with constants uniform in b ((P3)).

*E^ν in 𝒴_2.* The memberships follow from the class and the support (supp χ_K ⊂ supp χ^♯_K) as in the proof of (b).
For 𝒴_2(α): the ι⁺-index set lies in ℰ_rows + 2 ⊂ ℰ_src + 2 by (32.30); the remainder satisfies
a_+ + Re λ + 2 > 2λ_♯ + 2 > w_+ by (H1) and (32.27); and κ_ν − ε > 9/2 + δ_♯ − ε > 4 + ε_K ≥ α as in (a). For
𝒴_2(α′): if Re λ < 2, then (λ, k) ∈ ℳ and the index set lies in ℰ_++ + 2 by (32.16); if Re λ ≥ 2, every
exponent has real part at least 4; and κ_ν − ε > 3.
The seminorm bound holds as L_(h,p⃗) = L_b + (L_(h,p⃗) − L_b), the coefficients of the second having size
O(‖h‖_(𝒳^(k′)) + |p⃗|) at the regularity used. At b = b₀ the tensors built at b are those built at b₀, so E^ν = 0. ∎

*The exact linearisation.* By (c) and (e), f^ν = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν + r^ν + E^ν holds exactly, with E^ν = 0 at b₀, and r^ν
carries a factor of ι⁺-order at least λ_♯ (from h, h_tot, or g_0 − g_(b₀), resp. g_0 − g_b at b), which lifts it from
Re λ + 2 ≥ λ_♯ + 2 to at least 2λ_♯ + 2 = 5 + 2δ_♯ > w_+, past every exponent that could create a row: no ι⁺-index set of
r^ν needs to be tracked. (In dimension 3 + 1 the same count gives 2 + 2 = 4 < 5, and [Hin26] tracks an index set ℰ̃′_++
instead.) So the forward solution of L_(h,p⃗)u = F − Σ_ν f^ν_(h,p⃗)(W_ν) is u = v − Σ_ν m_ν(W_ν), where v is the forward
solution of L_(h,p⃗)v = F − Σ_ν(r^ν_(h,p⃗) + E^ν_(h,p⃗))(W_ν), and Chapter 33 eliminates the rows as Proposition 32.29
eliminates the motions.

[Hin26, Lemma 11.57] records the classes of the linearisations (the K⁺-order of its footnote 125, which is κ_ν here:
K_τ terms below the leading one, except K_s0 − 1 = 3 for s0, whose leading term is the A′_ν-term) and, in its
(11.194), that the leading ι⁺-part of f^ν is a cut-off of the model operator applied to the model of m_ν. At b₀,
parts (b) and (c) give the classes and the exact form f^ν = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν + r^ν, from which the analogue of [Hin26,
(11.194)] in its L_b form follows, at a plain ι⁺-weight: f^ν − L_(b₀)m_ν = (L_(h,p⃗) − L_(b₀))m_ν + r^ν has ι⁺-weight
Re λ + 2 + λ_♯ − ε; at b, by (e), the same holds for f^ν − E^ν − L_bm_ν. [Hin26]'s index set
(λ + 2, k) + ((0, 0) ∪ ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ_+ ∪ ℰ̃′_++) has here no ℰ̃′_++-term, the new corrections lying in 𝒳 by (H3) ([Hin26,
Remark 11.62]). [Hin26, (11.191)], for the logarithmic s0 correction at the exponent 1, has no analogue.

## 33. The expansion at the Kerr face

This chapter proves [Hin26, Theorem 11.59] (pp. 278–292) in dimension 4 + 1, following its proof. With the correction
terms of the fourth kind of Chapter 32, the forward solution of the linearised gauge-fixed Einstein equation, for a
forcing of K⁺-order α ≤ 4 + ε_K, is made to decay at K⁺ at the order α − 2 by a unique choice of the modification
parameters (Theorem 33.18, the form of [Hin26, (11.222)] in dimension 4 + 1). The solution so obtained is,
modulo a remainder of K⁺-order α, a sum of towers of the zero energy states whose coefficients are functions of t_*:
partially polyhomogeneous, except for a conormal boost coefficient of order α − 2 and a conormal black hole parameter of
order α − 1; and it is partially polyhomogeneous at ι⁺ with an index set ℰ_♯ to the order 3 + η_2, where η_2 < ε_+ is
as close to ε_+ as desired (Theorem 33.24, the form of [Hin26, (11.196)] in dimension 4 + 1). The expansion is
also obtained at every level β ∈ (3, 4 + ε_K], and for the enlarged sources that the linearisation in the black hole
parameters of Chapter 34 produces (Section 33.13).

The argument has two phases. In spacetime (Section 33.4) the ι⁺-terms of the forcing of u-exponent below 2 are
solved by the ι⁺-normal operator up to the K⁺-order α ≤ 4 + ε_K, and the K⁺-terms this produces below the order α − 2
are identified as rows. What is left is a forward problem whose forcing is partially polyhomogeneous at ι⁺ from the order
4 on; it is solved on the spectral side (Section 33.7), through four zero energy solves, at the Taylor levels 0 to
3 at zero frequency, and the transition face model between them. The rows are then eliminated by the choice of the
parameters (Section 33.8), and the solution is expanded at K⁺ modulo the order α (Section 33.11).

The dimension changes the scheme of [Hin26] in these places. (1) Under the hypothesis (C5) below, the K⁺-range of the
ι⁺-normal operator is ℓ^max_K = 3, so Corollary 26.44 solves the term at a u-exponent λ_0 with Re λ_0 < 2 with
ℓ_K = α − Re λ_0 for every α ≤ 4 + ε_K; [Hin26] uses its Proposition 9.11 at the exponent 1 only (Steps 2.A.2 and 4.1 of
its proof). The rows this produces are all the rows of Section 32.10 with Re λ < 2, and they are identified through
the towers (Lemma 33.4). (2) The parameter exponents, which [Hin26] builds after the proof by the procedure of
its (11.186), are fixed in advance (Definition 33.1), with logarithmic orders that grow with the real part. The rows'
own sources never enter the construction, since f^ν = Lm_ν + r^ν exactly (Lemma 32.36 (c); at a general b,
(e) adds a forcing term E^ν of K⁺-weight above α); this is how the self-consistency of [Hin26, Remark 11.62] enters.
(3) Two further conditions are needed: (H4), ℓ_I > 3 + ε_+, and the gap condition (G) on ε_K. (4) The zero frequency
Taylor expansion of the transformed forcing has four terms (orders σ⁰ to σ³, as α − 1 > 3); the four zero energy solves
are written out, with the polyhomogeneous transition face model Proposition 27.55 at the levels 1 and 2 and its
conormal form Proposition 27.58 at the level 3. (5) The spectral solution is written directly as a sum of physical
pieces (Lemma 33.14): L̂_b(σ) is injective on 𝒳′_σ (Lemma 31.24), so the rows of the augmented operator
and the column moves of Lemma 31.26 are needed only at zero energy and at the last level. (6) The K⁺-terms below
α − 2 come on the spectral side only from the pieces of Proposition 27.55 at the levels 1 and 2, which are homogeneous
functions of σ times spectral towers (Lemma 33.12); a lemma on forward tails (Lemma 33.7) turns them
into rows, among them the boost rows at the exponent 3 that the zero energy mass state produces. (7) The elimination is a
perturbation of the identity (Lemma 32.36 (c), and (e) at a general b; Corollary 33.6), where
[Hin26, Step 2.B] has ± the identity plus o(1); rows of different types at one rate are told apart by the degree of their
spherical type and, within a degree, by the order of their states at ∂X. (8) The expansion modulo the order α uses the
equation itself: below that order every coefficient section is a stationary solution of moderate growth
(Lemma 33.22), so the polyhomogeneous part at K⁺ is a sum of towers whatever the individual pieces are
(Lemma 33.23). (9) The spectral cut-off is an approximate identity with vanishing moments (Lemma 33.20),
so each spectral piece is, near K⁺, the spacetime tower of the inverse transform of its scalar coefficient. (10) Below
the order 4 the forcing of the last Taylor level has a negative zero frequency weight; the zero energy solve of that
level then drops out (Proposition 33.28).

The steps that [Hin26, Part 3 (5) of the proof of Theorem 11.59] calls analogous are written out: the order
4 + ε_K needs four zero energy solves, of which [Hin26] writes three (its Steps 2.A.3, 2.A.5, 2.A.7), the fourth, at
σ³, being implicit there as well.

### 33.1 The setting at a base point

The notation is that of Chapter 21–Chapter 32; n = 4 throughout. The black hole parameters are b = (m, A), b_0 =
(m_0, 0), with tangent space 𝔟 = ℝ ⊕ 𝔰𝔬(4). In this chapter λ denotes an exponent at ι⁺ (an element of the projection
π_1 of an index set), as in [Hin26]; the wavelength of the main argument does not occur. Weights and index sets are
listed at (ℐ⁺, ι⁺, K⁺), with the defining functions ρ_I, ρ_+, ρ_K; Ω_* = cl_M{t^♭_* ≥ 1}, the spaces
H^(k,(…),(…),…)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−) and the class 𝒳^k of perturbations are those of Section 29.1 and (29.4).
On the spectral side, X̄, M′, X^±_(sc-b) with the faces scf, tf, zf and the spaces on them are those of
Section 29.18 and Section 20.8.1; ρ = ⟨x⟩⁻¹ near ∂X, r̂ := |σ|r, and ℱ is the Fourier transform in t_*,
ŵ(σ) = ∫ e^(iσt_*) w dt_*. For an index set E, π_1E is the set of its exponents; "order w−" means order w − ε for every
ε > 0.

*The base point.* The base points of the linearisation are pairs (h, p⃗) as in Section 32.11, whose black hole
parameter b lies in the closed ball ℬ̄_* about b_0 of Section 29.6, shrunk as in Chapter 31 (to a radius at most
1/(2C_B), Lemma 31.1, and for Proposition 31.19), in Proposition 32.14 and the step of
Proposition 32.29, in Lemma 36.3 and in Proposition 36.8, each time to a smaller ball about b_0; every
