result below holds on this ball. On ℬ̄_* the model objects are uniform in b (Lemma 30.2): the forward problem
at b with continuity in (b, S, h) (property (P1) there); the ι⁺-normal operator, the transition face normal operator
and the indicial roots of L̂_b(0) at ∂X, which do not depend on b (P2); the zero energy states of the table of roots of
Section 26.10 for L_b, their companions, the 1-form towers of Proposition 23.34, the physical states of
Proposition 25.37 and ġ_b, which are real and smooth in b, with index sets in (μ − j) + ℰ_ind, ℰ_ind independent of b
(P3); the augmented low energy theory of Chapter 28 at b (P4); and the time translation, Killing for every g_b (P5). The
rows are built at the base point's b, and the correction terms and their counterterms are the tensors built from b_0
((P6) of Lemma 36.1). Every statement below is the statement at b: L_(b_0), g_(b_0) near K⁺, the states, towers
and companions at b_0 and ℰ_ind are replaced by those at b, and the splitting L_(h,p⃗) = L_b + (L_(h,p⃗) − L_b) near K⁺,
which moves a perturbation into the source, has the same K⁺-gain as at b_0, since the background equals g_b near K⁺
(Lemma 29.11). Every constant is uniform on ℬ̄_*.

At b_0 every rotation is Killing, so the rotation state vanishes, h_(b_0,v1) = 0. At a rotating b the rotation state
h_(b,v1) ∈ 𝒜³ is smooth in b and O(|b − b_0|) but need not vanish (Lemma 30.2 (P3)). The v1 terms of the
expansion then decay at K⁺ one order less than at b_0. The coefficient space of the v1 rows stays 𝒲_v1 = 𝒱′ = 0 at
every b (Section 32.10). The statements below keep these v1 terms explicit where h_(b,v1) ≠ 0 matters, and say so;
Proposition 36.5 writes them as rotation rows whose coefficients are read from the construction, without inverting
the map V ↦ h_(b,v1)(V), which degenerates as b → b_0.

*The inner radius.* The chapter works on Ω_* with the spaces of Chapter 19 and the forward solutions of Chapter 29,
which hold with the inner radius r_0 = r_♭ ∈ (0, ½R₁] of Definition 22.1, the radius of the artificial boundary, as
a parameter. Its own radii are scale-free
({r ≤ 2}, {r ≥ 1}, {r ≤ R} for arbitrary R), and its levels, loops and windows are fixed by weights at infinity and at
K⁺. So every result of this chapter holds with r_0 as a parameter.

### 33.2 The parameter exponents

Everything of Section 32.10 is kept, at b: the enlarged index set ℰ_ind, ℱ = (0, 0) ∪ ℰ_ind, the index sets ℰ_++,
ℳ ((32.17)), 𝒢 = (2, 0) ∪ (2 + ℰ_ind), ℰ̃_+ = 𝒢 ∪ (ℰ_+ + 𝒢) and 2ℰ_+ = ℰ_+ + ℰ_+, the number
δ_♯ = λ_♯ − 3/2 ∈ (0, 1/4), the constants (32.27),

    0 < ε_K < ε_+ < min(δ_♯, ε_ind),     w_+ := 5 + ε_+,

the hypotheses (H1)–(H3) on the class, the types 𝒯 = {s1, v1, s0, s2, c0, c1} with the shifts d_τ, the rows
ν = (τ, λ, k) with K⁺-exponent e_ν = λ + d_τ and the finite set 𝒩 of the rows with Re e_ν ≤ 2, the coefficient spaces
𝒲_τ (with 𝒲_v1 = 0), the index sets ℰ_rows and ℰ_src with (32.30), and the forcing spaces 𝒴_1(α), 𝒴_2(α),
𝒴(α). From Section 32.11 are kept the tower lengths K_τ, the stationary 1-forms ω̆^i_τ and their index sets
(32.31), the states h_τ, the functions r_ν, a_ν, the rows m_ν, the corrections h_ν and counterterms ϑ_ν, the
operator P_4, its linearisation L_(h,p⃗) and the tensors f^ν_(h,p⃗), r^ν_(h,p⃗). ℰ^♯_+ is the set (29.32),

    λ_♯ = 3/2 + (1 − e_Υ)γ_Υ = min Re ℰ^♯_+,

ℰ^ι_ind is the index set of Theorem 26.42 ((26.56)). The two gaps of indicial roots ε_ind and ε_Υ, and
ε_g = min(ε_Υ, ε_ind), are those of Definition 32.1: ε_ind, fixed by the indicial roots of L̂_b(0), is the constant
with which the hypotheses of Proposition 27.55 and Proposition 27.58 are stated (Section 27.10); ε_Υ is fixed
by the indicial roots of (□^Υ_b)^(0), and the index sets ℰ_ind of the corrections of the states have least real part
at least ε_Υ. The remainders of Proposition 27.55 ((27.52)) and Proposition 27.58 ((27.55))
gain over the forcing through the corrections of the states (Lemma 27.54); of this gain we use only the lower
bound ε_g of Definition 32.1. Definition 32.31 and Lemma 32.32 (b), (e) extend verbatim to every triple
(τ, λ, k) with τ ∈ 𝒯, Re λ ≥ λ_♯ and k ∈ ℕ₀; m_ν and r_ν denote these also for ν ∉ 𝒩. Two further hypotheses are made:

(C5) γ_C v_C ≥ 1/2 (Section 26.10), so that ℓ^max_K = min(3, 2 + 2γ_C v_C) = 3 ((26.43)).

(H4) ℓ_I > 3 + ε_+, with ℓ_I off the discrete exclusion sets of Proposition 29.29 and Theorem 26.42. As
ℓ_I ≤ a_I (Section 32.6; this is used in Lemma 32.36 (a), on which this section relies), (H4) asks
a_I > 3 + ε_+ of the class; the class of [Hin26] has the ℐ⁺-order 3 + ε_I. The condition ℓ_I < 3/2 + s_C of
Theorem 26.42 is no restriction, s_C being large by (C1) of Chapter 25.

*The sources.* Fix ℰ_src as the least choice in (32.30), and put

    ℰ⁰_src := ℰ̃_+ ∪ 2ℰ_+ ∪ (ℰ_rows ∩ {Re < 2}),          ℰ_src = ℰ⁰_src ∪ ℰ_rows.    (33.1)

𝒴⁰_1(α), 𝒴⁰_2(α), 𝒴⁰(α) are 𝒴_1(α), 𝒴_2(α), 𝒴(α) with ℰ⁰_src in place of ℰ_src. They hold the sources of the
theorems below (the form of [Hin26, (11.195)] in dimension 4 + 1) and the derivatives f^S_(h,p⃗), f^(s1)_(h,p⃗)
(in 𝒴⁰(α)) and f^b_(h,p⃗) (in 𝒴⁰_2(α)) of Lemma 32.36 (a): the term (∂δ*_(g_0,E_C))ϑ_rows there has plain
ι⁺-weight λ_♯ + 4 > w_+ (by its proof), and the rest is that of Lemma 32.10, with the index sets ℰ̃_+ and
2ℰ_+. The row exponents of real part at least 2 enter only through f^ν_(h,p⃗) = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν + r^ν_(h,p⃗), where
r^ν_(h,p⃗) carries no index set ((32.35)).

*The parameter exponents.* The index set ℰ_par of Section 32.10, which [Hin26] calls Ẽ′_++ and builds after the
proof of its Theorem 11.59 by the procedure of its (11.186), is fixed here in advance.

**Definition 33.1** (The parameter exponents.) Let Λ ⊂ ℂ be the smallest set, closed under conjugation,
that contains

    π_1(ℰ_++ ∪ 𝒢 ∪ ℰ^C_I) ∪ {λ_♯, 3} ∪ (2 + π_1ℰ_col)

and satisfies Λ + w ⊂ Λ for every w ∈ π_1(ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind) ∪ {1}. Here ℰ_++ is the least choice in (32.16),
and

    ℰ_col = ({(0, 0), (1, 0)} ∪ ℰ_ind ∪ (1 + ℰ_ind)) + ℕ₀ ⊂ {Re ≥ 0}

is the index set at ∂X of the column terms (Lemma 33.9), independent of b. Let

    η_0 := min Re(π_1(ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind) ∪ {1}) > 0,          J_* := ⌈5/η_0⌉ + 2;

let l_* ∈ ℕ₀ bound, at real part at most 5, the logarithmic orders of ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind ∪ ℰ^C_I, the orders of the
poles of N_ι⁺(L̄, ·)⁻¹ (Lemma 26.29) and the multiplicities of the indicial roots of L̂_b(0)
(Proposition 25.6); and let k̄_0 ∈ ℕ bound the logarithmic orders of ℰ⁰_src ∪ ℰ_++ ∪ 𝒢 ∪ (2 + ℰ_col) at real part
below 2λ_♯, and only there. For λ ∈ Λ let n(λ) be the number of λ′ ∈ Λ with Re λ′ < Re λ, and

    k̄(λ) := k̄_0 + (J_* + 1)(l_* + 1)(n(λ) + 1).

Put

    ℰ_par := ℳ ∪ {(λ + j, k) : λ ∈ Λ, 2 ≤ Re λ ≤ 3, k ≤ k̄(λ), j ∈ ℕ₀}.    (33.2)

The number 3 ∈ Λ is the u-exponent of the boost row that the zero energy mass state produces (Section 33.7); the
increment 1 accounts for the Taylor levels of the spectral construction, and 2 + π_1ℰ_col for the column terms at its
first Taylor level. Since 2 + π_1ℰ_col = ({2, 3} ∪ (2 + π_1ℰ_ind) ∪ (3 + π_1ℰ_ind)) + ℕ₀ lies in π_1𝒢 + ℕ₀ ⊂ Λ, this
last generator adds no exponent to Λ; the logarithmic orders of the column terms are bounded through k̄_0.

**Lemma 33.2** (a) Λ ∩ {Re ≤ R} is finite for every R, Λ ⊂ {Re ≥ λ_♯}, and Λ ∩ {Re < 2} = π_1ℳ.

(b) ℰ_par is an index set, closed under conjugation, satisfying (32.28), and

    ℰ_par ∩ {Re ≤ 3} = ℳ ∪ {(λ, k) : λ ∈ Λ, 2 ≤ Re λ ≤ 3, k ≤ k̄(λ)}.

ℰ_par does not depend on ℰ_+. Hence (H3), which asks ℰ_+ ⊃ (λ, k) + ℱ for the rows, can be imposed on the class
together with (H1): this is the form of [Hin26, Remark 11.62] in dimension 4 + 1.

(c) (The logarithmic count.) Applied to sources in 𝒴⁰(α), the constructions of Section 33.4 and
Section 33.7 change index sets only by: adding (w, l) ∈ ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind ∪ {(1, 0)} to an exponent; unions with
the column exponents (2 + j, 0) + ℰ_col at the Taylor level j + 1 (Lemma 33.11), of logarithmic orders at most
k̄_0; extended unions with ℰ^C_I ((29.32)) or with the indicial roots (Lemma 21.35), each raising the
logarithmic order at one exponent by at most l_* + 1; and raising the logarithmic order at a treated exponent by a pole
order of N_ι⁺(L̄, ·)⁻¹ (Corollary 26.44) or by 1 (Proposition 27.55 at α_0 = 2, Remark 27.56). At an
exponent of real part at most 3 + ε_+ at most J_* such raises occur: each belongs to one window of the iteration of
Section 33.4, of width at least η_0 below 2, or to one Taylor level of Section 33.7, of which there are
four. Hence every exponent (λ, k) produced with 2 ≤ Re λ ≤ 3 + ε_+ has λ ∈ Λ and k ≤ k̄(λ). These are all the
exponents recorded: the ι⁺-data of 𝒴⁰(α) stop at the weight w_+ − ε, that is, at the u-exponent 3 + ε_+ − ε.

*Proof.* (a) The generators are index sets of real parts at least λ_♯ (ℰ_++ ⊂ ℰ_+ by (H1); min Re ℰ^C_I >
3/2 + 2γ_Υ > λ_♯, by Step 1 of the proof of Proposition 31.21), finitely many below every bound, and the increments
have real part at least η_0; so below R only sums with at most R/η_0 increments occur. Below 2 the generators lie in
π_1ℰ_++: λ_♯ does, and so does every element of π_1ℰ^C_I below 2, since (29.32) puts it into ℰ^♯_+ and
ℰ_++ ⊃ ℰ^♯_+ ∩ {Re < 2} by (H1); 𝒢, 3 and 2 + π_1ℰ_col have real part at least 2. And π_1ℰ_++ ∩ {Re < 2} is closed
under the increments below 2 ((32.16); adding 1 leaves {Re < 2}, as λ_♯ + 1 > 2). So
Λ ∩ {Re < 2} = π_1ℳ.

(b) ℰ_par is an index set: by (a) it has finitely many exponents below each bound, with finitely many logarithms at
each, and it is closed under (z, k) ↦ (z + 1, k), as Λ + 1 ⊂ Λ, k̄(λ + 1) ≥ k̄(λ) (since n(λ + 1) > n(λ)), and, for
(z, k) ∈ ℳ, z + 1 ∈ Λ has real part in [2, 3) and k ≤ k̄_0 ≤ k̄(z + 1) (as ℳ ⊂ ℰ_++). The part below 3: if
Re(λ + j) ≤ 3 with j ≥ 1, then Re λ = 2, j = 1 and k̄(λ) ≤ k̄(λ + 1). Conjugation: Λ is closed under it,
n(λ̄) = n(λ), and ℳ = ℳ̄. (32.28): min Re ℰ_par ≥ λ_♯, and ℰ_par ∩ {Re < 2} = ℳ.

*Independence of ℰ_+.* The increments have positive real parts, so Λ ∩ {Re < R} is determined by the generators of real
part below R, and ℰ_par by Λ ∩ {Re ≤ 3} and k̄_0. Below 2λ_♯ = 3 + 2δ_♯ > 3 + ε_+ ((32.27)) nothing used
involves ℰ_+: 𝒢, ℰ^C_I and ℰ_col do not; the parts of ℰ⁰_src (and of ℰ_rows) that involve ℰ_+, namely ℰ_+ + 𝒢, 2ℰ_+
and (λ, k) + ℱ + ℰ_+, have real part at least 2λ_♯ by (H1); and the least ℰ_++ of (32.16) agrees below 2λ_♯
with the least index set that contains ℰ^♯_+ ∩ {Re < 2} and is closed under the addition of ℰ^ι_ind ∪ ℰ_ind, since
adding an element of ℰ_+ lands at real part at least 2λ_♯. So Λ ∩ {Re ≤ 3}, k̄_0 and ℰ_par do not depend on ℰ_+. The
conditions on ℰ_+ ((H1); (H3), which with (32.16) gives ℰ_+ ⊃ ℰ_par + ℱ; ℰ_+ ⊃ ℰ^♯_+ ∩ {Re < 2}; and
ℰ_+ + (ℰ^ι_ind ∪ ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ_+) ⊂ ℰ_+ there) are therefore conditions on ℰ_+ alone, and the least index set that contains
ℰ_par + ℱ and ℰ^♯_+ ∩ {Re < 2} and is closed under these additions meets them, its exponents being sums of exponents of
real part at least λ_♯.

(c) The exponents produced lie in Λ, which contains the generators and is closed under the additions listed (the
exponent 4 of (27.52), at the Taylor level j of Section 33.7, is the u-exponent 3 + j). Logarithmic
orders, by induction on n(λ): the logarithmic order at λ is the largest over its contributions, each either a
generator's or a column exponent's (at most k̄_0, as Re λ ≤ 3 + ε_+ < 2λ_♯) or (λ′, k′) + (w, l) with
Re λ′ < Re λ, k′ ≤ k̄(λ′) and l ≤ l_*, plus at most J_*(l_* + 1) from the raises at λ. As n(λ) ≥ n(λ′) + 1,

    k̄(λ) − k̄(λ′) ≥ (J_* + 1)(l_* + 1) ≥ l_* + J_*(l_* + 1),     and     k̄_0 + J_*(l_* + 1) ≤ k̄(λ).     ∎

**Definition 33.3** (The gap and admissible orders.) (G) ε_K is so small that no λ ∈ Λ has real part in
(2, 2 + ε_K] ∪ (3, 3 + ε_K], and no λ + d_c0 or λ + d_c1, λ ∈ Λ, has real part in (2, 2 + ε_K]. This is possible by
Lemma 33.2 (a), as Λ does not depend on ε_K; it implies d_c0, d_c1 > ε_K, since 2 ∈ Λ. The constants
(32.27) may be kept, decreasing ε_K; we also take ε_K < ε_Υ, so that ε_K < ε_g. A number α ∈ (2, 4 + ε_K] is
*admissible* if: for α < 3, it is admissible in the sense of Section 32.6; for α ≥ 3, α > 4 + ε_K − ε′_0, with

    ε′_0 := ½ min(ε_K, ε_+ − ε_K),

and α avoids the finite set of values for which α − Re λ_0, λ_0 ∈ Λ, Re λ_0 < 2, equals −Re μ for a root μ of
L̂_b(0) or lies in Re π_1ℰ_K (Lemma 26.24), and the finite exclusion set of Section 33.5.

For admissible α ≥ 3 the rows of K⁺-rate below α − 2 are exactly those of 𝒩: a row with (λ, k) ∈ ℰ_par has the rate
Re λ − 1 (s1), Re λ (s0, s2) or Re λ + d_τ (c0, c1), and by (G) no such rate lies in (2, 2 + ε_K] ⊃ (2, α − 2).

### 33.3 Towers, row expansions and forward tails

**Lemma 33.4** (Towers.) Let τ ∈ 𝒯 and W ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ), or, for τ = v1, W ∈ 𝒱_(1,ℂ), on which the 1-forms
ω̆^i_v1 of Section 32.11 are defined by the same formulas (Definition 34.3), and put

    h̆^i_τ(W) := δ̂*_(g_b)(0) ω̆^i_τ(W) + dt_* ⊗_s ω̆^(i−1)_τ(W),     i ≥ 0,

with ω̆^(−1)_τ := 0 and ω̆^i_τ := 0 for i > K_τ.

(a) For every function a = a(t_*) and K ≤ K_τ,

    δ*_(g_b)(Σ_(i=0)^K a^((i)) ω̆^i_τ(W))
        = Σ_(i=0)^K a^((i)) h̆^i_τ(W) + a^((K+1)) dt_* ⊗_s ω̆^K_τ(W).    (33.3)

So m_ν(W) = χ_K(Σ_(i≤K_τ) a_ν^((i)) h̆^i_τ(W) + a_ν^((K_τ+1)) dt_* ⊗_s ω̆^(K_τ)_τ(W)) for ν = (τ, λ, k); and
h̆⁰_τ = h_τ for τ ≠ s0, while h̆⁰_s0 = 0 and h̆¹_s0 = h_s0.

(b) The towers of Definition 26.37 at b for the types of 𝒯 are these:

    h^(≤k)_(b,s1)(aS) = Σ_(i≤k) a^((i)) h̆^i_s1(S),     h^((0),≤k)_(b,s0)(aY) = Σ_(i≤k) a^((i)) h̆^(i+1)_s0(Y),
    h^(≤k)_(b,v1)(aV) = Σ_(i≤k) a^((i)) h̆^i_v1(V),     V ∈ 𝒱_(1,ℂ),     h̆⁰_v1 = h_(b,v1),

and h^((μ),≤k)_(b,τ)(aY) = Σ_(i≤k) a^((i)) h̆^i_τ(Y) for τ = s2, c0, c1 (with μ = 0, μ_c0, μ_c1), for k up to the
lengths of the table of roots of Section 26.10.

(c) Let λ_0 ∈ ℂ with Re λ_0 ≥ λ_♯, j ∈ ℕ₀, and let u_(b,0) be (26.55) at b with λ_0 for λ, a factor
(log t_*)^j in each argument, and coefficients S^(−1)_1, V^(−1)_1, Y^(μ)_τ. For τ ∈ 𝒯 ∖ {v1} let
ν_τ := (τ, λ_τ, j) with λ_τ := λ_0, and W_s1 := (λ_0(λ_0 − 1))⁻¹S^(−1)_1, W_τ := Y^(μ_τ)_τ otherwise
(μ_s0 = μ_s2 := 0). Put V := −λ_0⁻¹V^(−1)_1. Then

    χ_K u_(b,0) − Σ_(τ∈𝒯∖{v1}) m_(ν_τ)(W_τ) − χ_K t_*^(−λ_0)(log t_*)^j h_(b,v1)(V)
        has K⁺-weight Re λ_0 + 1 − ε for every ε > 0.    (33.4)

The last term on the left vanishes when h_(b,v1) = 0, in particular at b_0.

(d) For a tempered a with Fourier transform â(σ) = ∫ e^(iσt_*) a dt_*, the Fourier transform in t_* of
δ*_(g_b)(Σ_(i≤K) a^((i)) ω̆^i_τ(W)) is â(σ)T^K_τ(σ, W), with the polynomial

    T^K_τ(σ, W) := Σ_(i=0)^K (−iσ)^i h̆^i_τ(W) + (−iσ)^(K+1) dt_* ⊗_s ω̆^K_τ(W)
                 = δ̂*_(g_b)(σ) Σ_(i=0)^K (−iσ)^i ω̆^i_τ(W).    (33.5)

*Proof.* (a) δ*_(g_b)(φ(t_*)v) = φ δ̂*_(g_b)(0)v + φ′ dt_* ⊗_s v for stationary v ((31.16)); sum over i and
collect the terms with a^((i)). For s0, ω̆⁰_s0 is Killing (Lemma 30.2 (P5)), so h̆⁰_s0 = 0, and
h̆¹_s0 = δ*(t_*ω̆⁰ + ω̆¹) = h_s0 (Section 32.11).

(b) The state column of the table of roots of Section 26.10 takes the states and their companions from
Proposition 23.28 and Proposition 23.34 (1)–(7), the same 1-form towers as Definition 32.31 (whose list cites
the same items), under δ*_(g_b): the tower of L_b-solutions δ*ω^(≤k), with ω^(≤k) = Σ_(i≤k) (k!/(k − i)!) t_*^(k−i)
ω̆^i, is by (33.3) with a = t_*^k the polynomial Σ_(i≤k) (k!/(k − i)!) t_*^(k−i) h̆^i, which is the
description of a tower with companions h̆^i in Lemma 26.33 (a). For v1 the 1-form towers are those of
Proposition 23.34 (3), on all of 𝒱_(1,ℂ), and the tower of Definition 26.37 has length k_μ = 2. For s0 the state is
h^((0))_(b,s0) = h̆¹, and the index is shifted by one.

(c) By (b), the term of u_(b,0) of type τ ∈ 𝒯 ∖ {v1} is the sum over i ≤ k_τ (the lengths k_μ of the table: 3 for s1,
2 for s0, s2, c0, c1) of a^((i)) times companions, with a = c r_(ν_τ): for s1,
a_s1(log t_*)^j = (λ_0(λ_0 − 1))⁻¹ t_*^(−λ_0+1)(log t_*)^j ((26.54); λ_0 ≠ 1); for s0, s2, c0, c1,
t_*^(−λ_0+μ)(log t_*)^j = r_(ν_τ) (for s0, a = r_ν = A′_ν, Definition 32.31). By (a), m_(ν_τ)(W_τ) is the same sum
with K_τ ≥ k_τ in place of k_τ, plus a^((K_τ+1)) dt_* ⊗_s ω̆^(K_τ) (for s0, K_s0 − 1 = 3 ≥ k_s0 after the shift of
index), times χ_K. The difference carries only a^((i)) with i ≥ k_τ + 1 ≥ 3, of K⁺-weight
Re e_(ν_τ) + 3 − ε ≥ Re λ_0 + 2 − ε. The v1 term is h^(≤2)_(b,v1)(a_v1 V^(−1)_1), times (log t_*)^j, with
a_v1 = −λ_0⁻¹ t_*^(−λ_0) ((26.54)); its bottom is the last term subtracted in (33.4), and the
rest carries a_v1^((i)), i ≥ 1, of K⁺-weight Re λ_0 + 1 − ε. At b_0 the bottom vanishes, every V ∈ 𝒱_1 being
Killing (Section 32.10). The rows of (26.55) outside 𝒯 have roots μ with Re μ ≤ −1 and rate
Re(λ_0 − μ) ≥ Re λ_0 + 1. On compact spatial sets χ_K = 1 for large t_*, and the stationary companions are smooth
there.

(d) ∫ e^(iσt) a^((i)) dt = (−iσ)^i â(σ), and (33.3). ∎

**Lemma 33.5** (Joint injectivity of the states.) For each τ ∈ 𝒯 ∖ {v1} let W_τ ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ). If
Σ_τ h_τ(W_τ) = 0, then every W_τ = 0. This holds at every b ∈ ℬ̄_*, for the states at b.

*Proof.* At the static, spherically symmetric b_0, every construction of Proposition 23.28 and
Proposition 23.34 stays in its isotypic component (the types in the proof of Proposition 23.34), and ω̆⁰_τ(W) is of
scalar type of degree l_τ: 0 for s0 and c0, 1 for s1 and c1, 2 for s2 (Proposition 23.28, Proposition 23.34 (1),
(4)–(7)). For s0, whose state is δ*(t_*ω̆⁰ + ω̆¹), ω̆¹_s0 is of degree 0 as well (Proposition 23.34 (1)). So h_τ(W)
lies in the isotypic component of degree l_τ, and these components are independent. Degree 2: h_s2 is injective
(Lemma 32.32 (f)). Degree 0: h_c0(W_c0) ∈ 𝒜^((μ_c0,0)+ℱ) has a nonzero ρ^(μ_c0)-coefficient if W_c0 ≠ 0 (the
proof of Lemma 32.32 (f)), while h_s0(W_s0) ∈ 𝒜^((0,0)+ℱ) ((23.32), with (2, 0) ∈ ℰ_ind,
Section 32.10) and μ_c0 < 0 ≤ min Re ℱ; so W_c0 = 0, and then W_s0 = 0. Degree 1: the same, with
h_s1(S) ∈ 𝒜^((3,0)∪(3+ℰ_ind)) ((25.23)) and μ_c1 < 0. At b ∈ ℬ̄_* the statement is Lemma 36.3,
which deduces it from the case b_0 by perturbation, with a lower bound uniform in b. ∎

**Corollary 33.6** (Uniqueness of row expansions.) Let 𝒩′ be a finite set of rows ν = (τ, λ, k),
τ ≠ v1, and W_ν ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ). If Σ_(ν∈𝒩′) m_ν(W_ν) has K⁺-weight w > max_(𝒩′) Re e_ν, then every W_ν = 0. This holds at
every b ∈ ℬ̄_*.

*Proof.* Suppose not, and let e_0 be the least real part of e_ν over the ν with W_ν ≠ 0. By Lemma 32.32 (e),
m_ν(W) − χ_K r_ν h_τ(W) has K⁺-weight Re e_ν + 1 − ε; this follows from the tower relations, which hold at b
(Lemma 30.2 (P3)). So on every compact spatial set, for large t_*,

    Σ_((e,k): Re e = e_0) t_*^(−e)(log t_*)^k Σ_τ h_τ(W_((τ,e−d_τ,k))) = O(t_*^(−e_0−δ))

for some δ > 0, the inner sum over the τ with (τ, e − d_τ, k) ∈ 𝒩′. The functions t_*^(−e)(log t_*)^k, finitely many
and distinct, with Re e = e_0, are linearly independent modulo O(t_*^(−e_0−δ)): with s = log t_*, a nonzero
Σ_(e,k) c_(e,k) s^k e^(−is Im e) does not tend to 0 as s → ∞. So each inner sum vanishes on X°, and
Lemma 33.5 gives W_ν = 0 for those ν, a contradiction. ∎

**Lemma 33.7** (Forward tails.) Let V be a Fréchet space, β > −1, β ∉ ℕ₀, E ⊂ ℂ × ℕ₀ finite with
−1 < Re z < β for (z, m) ∈ E, a^±_(z,m) ∈ V for (z, m) ∈ E, and r^± ∈ C^∞(±(0, c]; V) with
(σ∂_σ)^j r^± = O(|σ|^β) for all j. Let χ ∈ C_c^∞((−c, c)) equal 1 near 0,

    v(σ) := χ(σ) Σ_± 1_(±σ>0)(Σ_((z,m)∈E) |σ|^z(log|σ|)^m a^±_(z,m) + r^±(σ)),          w := ℱ⁻¹v,

and suppose that w(t) = O(|t|^(−β−1)) as t → −∞. Then:

(a) for z ∈ ℕ₀, with M the largest m such that (z, m) ∈ E: a^−_(z,M) = (−1)^z a^+_(z,M), that is, the coefficients of
σ^z(log|σ|)^M on the two sides agree; this is the matching condition (21.67) of Proposition 21.45 at z;

(b) as t → +∞, for every δ > 0,

    w(t) = Σ_((z,m)∈E) Σ_(j≤m) t^(−z−1)(log t)^j b_(z,j) + O(t^(−β−1+δ)),

where b_(z,j) is a linear combination, with coefficients depending only on z, m and j, of the a^+_(z,m′) with m′ ≥ j,
and with m′ ≥ j + 1 if z ∈ ℕ₀. In particular the log-free terms |σ|^z a^±_(z,0) with z ∈ ℕ₀ contribute nothing.

*Proof.* We use ŵ(σ) = ∫ e^(iσt) w dt. For Re z > −1 let s^±_z := (σ ± i0)^z, the boundary values from ±Im σ > 0 of σ^z
(principal branch, arg σ ∈ (0, π), resp. (−π, 0)), and s^±_(z,m) := ∂^m_z s^±_z = (σ ± i0)^z(log(σ ± i0))^m. On σ > 0
both equal σ^z(log σ)^m; on σ < 0 they equal |σ|^z(log|σ| ± iπ)^m e^(±iπz). As

    ∫_0^∞ e^(iσt) t^a dt = Γ(a + 1) e^(iπ(a+1)/2) (σ + i0)^(−a−1)     (Re a > −1),

continued analytically, ℱ⁻¹s^+_z = c(z) t_+^(−z−1) with c(z) := e^(iπz/2)/Γ(−z), an entire function with simple zeros
exactly at ℕ₀ (where s^+_z = s^−_z = σ^z is a polynomial), and ℱ⁻¹s^−_z = c̄(z̄) t_−^(−z−1) likewise, with t_− := −t
on t < 0. Differentiating in z: ℱ⁻¹s^+_(z,m) = ∂^m_z(c(z)t_+^(−z−1)) is supported in t ≥ 0 and equal for t > 0 to
Σ_(j≤m) C(m, j) c^((m−j))(z)(−log t)^j t^(−z−1), C(m, j) the binomial coefficient; its top power of log t is m, with
coefficient (−1)^m c(z) ≠ 0, if z ∉ ℕ₀, and m − 1, with coefficient (−1)^(m−1) m c′(z) ≠ 0, if z ∈ ℕ₀ and m ≥ 1. The
same holds for s^−_(z,m) on t < 0, with |t|. Multiplying by χ changes the inverse transforms by ℱ⁻¹((1 − χ)s), which
is smooth on t ≠ 0 and O(|t|^(−∞)), as (1 − χ)s is smooth and a symbol in σ. And ℱ⁻¹(χ1_± r^±) = O(|t|^(−β−1+δ)):
on |σ| < |t|⁻¹ the integrand is O(|σ|^β); on |σ| > |t|⁻¹ we integrate by parts ⌈β⌉ + 1 times,
using |∂^j_σ r^±| ≤ C|σ|^(β−j), the boundary terms at |σ| = |t|⁻¹ being of the same size.

Fix z with (z, m) ∈ E for some m, and let M be the largest such m. If z ∉ ℤ, the 2(M + 1) functions
1_(±σ>0)|σ|^z(log|σ|)^m, m ≤ M, and s^±_(z,m), m ≤ M, span the same space: the change of basis is block triangular in m
with the diagonal blocks

    ( 1         1        )
    ( e^(iπz)   e^(−iπz) ),

invertible as e^(2iπz) ≠ 1. If z ∈ ℕ₀, then s^+_(z,0) = s^−_(z,0), and the space spanned by the
1_(±σ>0)σ^z(log|σ|)^m, m ≤ M, is spanned by σ^z, the s^±_(z,m) with 1 ≤ m ≤ M, and s^+_(z,M+1) − s^−_(z,M+1), which on
σ < 0 is 2πi(M + 1)σ^z(log|σ|)^M plus lower powers of the logarithm and which vanishes on σ > 0; its coefficient in the
expansion of v is ((−1)^z a^−_(z,M) − a^+_(z,M))/(2πi(M + 1)), the data on σ < 0 being
a^−_(z,M)|σ|^z = (−1)^z a^−_(z,M)σ^z. So

    v = χ Σ_z (Σ_m B^+_(z,m) s^+_(z,m) + Σ_m B^−_(z,m) s^−_(z,m)) + χ Σ_± 1_± r^±,

with B^−_(z,M+1) = −B^+_(z,M+1) = (a^+_(z,M) − (−1)^z a^−_(z,M))/(2πi(M + 1)) for z ∈ ℕ₀, the polynomial σ^z
counted with s^+. As t → −∞ only the s^−-terms and r^± contribute beyond O(|t|^(−∞)):

    w(t) = Σ_(z,m) B^−_(z,m) ∂^m_z(c̄(z̄)|t|^(−z−1)) + O(|t|^(−β−1+δ)) = O(|t|^(−β−1)).

The functions |t|^(−z−1)(log|t|)^j, finitely many and distinct with Re z < β, are independent modulo
O(|t|^(−β−1+δ)) for small δ, and for each z the top powers of the logarithm found above are strictly increasing in m
(for z ∈ ℕ₀ from m = 1 on); so by descending induction on m every B^−_(z,m) with z ∉ ℕ₀, or with z ∈ ℕ₀ and m ≥ 1,
vanishes. For z ∈ ℕ₀ this includes m = M + 1, which is (a). On σ > 0 the s^+_(z,m) are σ^z(log σ)^m, so
B^+_(z,m) = a^+_(z,m) for m ≥ 1, and for m = 0 when z ∉ ℕ₀; and (b) follows from the formula for ℱ⁻¹s^+_(z,m) on t > 0,
σ^z (z ∈ ℕ₀) contributing O(t^(−∞)). ∎

The point of (b) is that the tail of a forward supported function is read off from the side σ > 0 alone, and that the
log-free pieces of integer degree (jumps, and the parts of the solutions of the transition face model that depend on
ρ, Section 33.7) do not reach K⁺.

### 33.4 The spacetime phase

This section is [Hin26, Theorem 11.59, Part 1 of the proof, with Steps 2.A.1–2.A.2 and 4.1] in dimension 4 + 1. Let

    𝒩_ι := {ν ∈ 𝒩 : λ_ν ∈ π_1ℳ},

the rows with Re λ < 2 (the s1 rows among them are the motions of Chapter 32), and 𝒩_σ := 𝒩 ∖ 𝒩_ι, the rows with
2 ≤ Re λ ≤ 3. By Section 33.2 these are the s1 rows with (λ, k) ∈ ℰ_par and 2 ≤ Re λ ≤ 3, the s0 and s2 rows
with Re λ = 2, and the v1 rows with Re λ = 2, which carry no parameter; by (G), a row of type c0 or c1 with Re λ ≥ 2 has
rate at least 2 + d_τ > 2 + ε_K.

**Proposition 33.8** (The spacetime phase.) Let α ∈ (2, 4 + ε_K] be admissible, and let f = f_1 + f_2
with f_j ∈ 𝒴⁰_j(α), real and vanishing for t_* < 1. There are real u_I, u_ι, vanishing for t_* < 1, coefficients
S_ν ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ), ν ∈ 𝒩_ι, and V_(λ_0,j) ∈ 𝒱_(1,ℂ), (λ_0, j) ∈ ℳ, all linear and continuous in f, the S_ν and the
V_(λ_0,j) conjugation-symmetric, such that, with

    u^rot_ι := Σ_((λ_0,j)∈ℳ) χ_K t_*^(−λ_0)(log t_*)^j h_(b,v1)(V_(λ_0,j)),

which vanishes when h_(b,v1) = 0, in particular at b_0:

(a) u_I ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(ℰ_I,3+ε_+−ε),∞)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−) vanishes on {ρ_I > ½c_I}, so near K⁺;

(b) u_ι − Σ_(ν∈𝒩_ι) m_ν(S_ν) − u^rot_ι ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),λ_♯−ε,α−2−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−);

(c) f^♭ := f − L_b(u_I + u_ι) ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,(ℰ^♭+2,w_+−ε),α−ε)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−), vanishing for t_* < 1,
where ℰ^♭ is an index set with π_1(ℰ^♭ ∩ {Re < 3 + ε_+}) ⊂ Λ ∩ {Re ≥ 2} and logarithmic order at most k̄(λ) at λ, and
ℰ_I in (a) is an index set with π_1(ℰ_I ∩ {Re < 3 + ε_+}) ⊂ Λ.

For α < 3 this is Steps 1–2 of the proof of Lemma 32.27, with the ι⁺-expansion recorded to the weight w_+; the
point here is α ≤ 4 + ε_K.

*Proof.* The construction is that of Steps 1–2 of the proof of Proposition 31.21 ((31.35)–(31.37)),
as Lemma 32.26 and Lemma 32.27 use it, with three changes: the step at ℐ⁺ goes to
ℓ̆_+ := w_+ − 2 − ε = 3 + ε_+ − ε; the K⁺-order of the steps at ι⁺ is c_K := α; and the identification of the K⁺-terms
below α − 2 includes all of 𝒯.

*Step 1 (ℐ⁺; [Hin26, Step 2.A.1]).* Proposition 29.29 with Ĕ_+ := (ℰ⁰_src)_(≥2) (the u-exponents of the ι⁺-index set
of f_1) and ℓ̆_+ := 3 + ε_+ − ε (below ℓ_I by (H4), and off the exclusions there for all but finitely many ε) gives
u⁽⁰⁾_I, vanishing on {t_* < 1} ∪ {ρ_I > ½c_I}, with ℐ⁺-data (⟨ℰ^C_I⟩, ℓ_I), ι⁺-data (ℰ^♯_+, ℓ̆_+) for this Ĕ_+, and
f_1 − L_b u⁽⁰⁾_I ∈ H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,(ℰ^♯_++2,w_+−ε))_b; near K⁺ it is f_1, of K⁺-weight α. f_2 is supported in supp χ^♯_K,
away from ℐ⁺, with ι⁺-index set ℰ⁰_src + 2. So f⁽⁰⁾ := f − L_b u⁽⁰⁾_I has plain ℐ⁺-weight ℓ_I + 1, an ι⁺-index set below
w_+ − ε with u-exponents in π_1(ℰ^♯_+ ∪ ℰ⁰_src) ⊂ Λ (by (29.32), π_1ℰ^♯_+ ⊂ π_1Ĕ_+ ∪ {λ_♯} ∪ π_1ℰ^C_I; and
π_1ℰ⁰_src ∩ {Re ≤ 3 + ε_+} ⊂ π_1(𝒢 ∪ ℳ) by the proof of Lemma 33.2 (b)), and K⁺-weight α − ε.

*Step 2 (ι⁺, the u-exponents below 2; [Hin26, Steps 2.A.2 and 4.1]).* Step 2 of the proof of Proposition 31.21 with
c_K := α is applied to the terms of f⁽⁰⁾ of u-exponent λ_0 with Re λ_0 < 2, in increasing order of the real part,
window by window. For each such λ_0, ℓ_K(λ_0) := α − Re λ_0 ∈ (α − 2, α − λ_♯]; as α ≤ 4 + ε_K < 3 + λ_♯ (since
ε_K < δ_♯ + ½), ℓ_K(λ_0) < 3 = ℓ^max_K by (C5), and ℓ_K(λ_0) > α − 2 > 0; it avoids the roots and Re π_1ℰ_K by
admissibility. The other hypotheses of Corollary 26.44 at b hold as in that step: Re λ_0 ≥ λ_♯ > 1; the pole order of
N_ι⁺(L̄, ·)⁻¹ at λ_0 is 0, as spec_ι⁺(L̄) ⊂ {Re ≥ 2} (Lemma 26.29 (a)); ℓ_I < 3/2 + s_C,
ℓ_I ∉ Re π_1ℰ^tot_(ι⁺,ℐ) and Re λ_0 < 2 < ℓ_I; and the coefficients at λ_0 have R-weight at least
α − ε − Re λ_0 − 2 = ℓ_K(λ_0) − 2 − ε, the current forcing having K⁺-weight α − ε (each error of Corollary 26.44 has
K⁺-weight Re λ_0 + ℓ_K(λ_0) − ε = α − ε, by (26.56), and the solutions at ℐ⁺ vanish near K⁺).
Corollary 26.44 gives

    u_(λ_0) = Σ_(j≤k) (χ_K u^((j))_(b,0) + χ_ι t_*^(−λ_0)(log t_*)^j ũ^((j))),

of K⁺-index set ℰ^gr_K(λ_0) + (0, k) at the weight ℓ_K(λ_0) − ε > α − 2. The expansion at ℐ⁺ of the error is removed by
Proposition 29.29 as in Step 2 of the proof of Proposition 31.21; its solution u′_(λ_0) vanishes near K⁺, and its
new ι⁺-exponents lie in λ_0 + ℰ^ι_ind + (0, k) or have real part at least 5/2 (there is no ρ_I^(z+1)-term with
Re z < 5/2). Every exponent created lies in Λ with logarithmic order at most k̄ (Lemma 33.2 (c)), and the
exponents below 2 lie in π_1ℳ with the logarithmic orders of ℰ_++ ((32.16), as in Lemma 32.26). After
finitely many windows no term of u-exponent below 2 is left. Put u_I := u⁽⁰⁾_I + Σ u′_(λ_0) and u_ι := Σ u_(λ_0). Then
(a) and (c) hold, (c) with ℰ^♭ the remaining u-exponents (at least 2), and u_I has its ι⁺-exponents in Λ.

*The rows.* By Lemma 33.4 (c), with the (log t_*)^j-versions, each χ_K u^((j))_(b,0) equals

    Σ_(τ∈𝒯∖{v1}) m_((τ,λ_0,j))(W^((j))_τ) + χ_K t_*^(−λ_0)(log t_*)^j h_(b,v1)(V^((j)))

up to K⁺-weight Re λ_0 + 1 − ε > α − 2 − ε (as λ_♯ + 1 > 5/2 > 2 + ε_K), V^((j)) being −λ_0⁻¹ times the v1
coefficient of (26.55) in the j-th term. The rows (τ, λ_0, j) so produced have (λ_0, j) ∈ ℳ; those of rate at
most 2 are in 𝒩_ι, and by (G) the others (c0 and c1 with Re λ_0 + d_τ > 2) have rate above 2 + ε_K ≥ α − 2, so that
m_((τ,λ_0,j)) has K⁺-weight at least α − 2 − ε (Lemma 32.32 (e)) and joins the remainder. The rest of u_(λ_0)
has K⁺-weight ℓ_K(λ_0) − ε > α − 2. Summing, with S_ν the sum of the W^((j))_τ for ν = (τ, λ_0, j) and V_(λ_0,j) the
sum of the V^((j)), gives (b); the ι⁺-weight λ_♯ − ε holds for u_ι and, by Lemma 32.32 (b), for each m_ν and
each term of u^rot_ι (h_(b,v1) ∈ 𝒜³).

*Reality and linearity.* Every map used is linear and continuous. f and L_b are real, and conjugation maps the
construction for λ_0 to that for λ̄_0; so u_I, u_ι may be taken real (or replaced by their real parts, which satisfy
(a)–(c) with the real parts of the identities), and the S_ν and V_(λ_0,j) are conjugation-symmetric
(m_ν̄(W̄) is the conjugate of m_ν(W), and h_(b,v1) is real, Lemma 30.2 (P3)). ∎

So for f ∈ 𝒴⁰(α) the forward solution u of L_b u = f is

    u = Σ_(ν∈𝒩_ι) m_ν(S_ν) + u^rot_ι + u_rem + v,

with u_rem of K⁺-weight α − 2 − ε and v the forward solution of L_b v = f^♭, a forcing partially polyhomogeneous at ι⁺
from the order 4 on, with plain ℐ⁺-weight ℓ_I + 1. Section 33.7 expands v at K⁺: its terms of rate below α − 2
are the rows of 𝒩_σ, together, at a rotating b, with v1 terms of exponent of real part 2. At a rotating b the terms of
u^rot_ι are the bottoms of the rotation rows of Proposition 36.5 (a).

### 33.5 The spectral setting

Everything of Section 33.2 is kept: (C5), (H4), Λ, k̄(λ), ℰ_par, (G), ℰ⁰_src and 𝒴⁰(α), and the rows
𝒩 = 𝒩_ι ∪ 𝒩_σ of Section 33.4.

*Spectral notation* (Section 29.18, Section 31.10, Section 31.11). X^±_(sc-b) carries the faces scf, tf, zf,
with |σ| = ρ_tf ρ_zf and r̂ = |σ|r; χ_zf, χ_tf and χ^♯_tf are the cut-offs there. L̂_b(σ) = L_0 − iσL_1 − σ²L_2, with
L_1 of one order of decay at ∂X (Lemma 31.23). L̃_b(σ) is the augmented operator of Chapter 28,
L̃_b(σ)(u, ḃ, S) = (L̂_b(σ)u + f̂_ḃ(σ) + f̂_S(σ), r(u)), with ĝ^aug(σ)(ḃ) = iσ⁻¹G_1(σ)(ḃ) and
ĥ^aug(σ)(S) = −σ⁻²G_2(σ)(S), where

    G_1(σ)(ḃ) := Ψ ġ(ḃ),          G_2(σ)(S) := Ψ h(S) − σ∂_σΨ h(S) − iσΨ h̆(S)    (33.6)

(Lemma 28.5, (28.8)); here Ψ(σ, x) = ∫ e^(iσt_*) ∂_(t_*)χ_K dt_* is entire in σ with Ψ(0, ·) = 1,
L̂_b(σ)ĝ^aug(σ)(ḃ) = f̂_ḃ(σ), L̂_b(σ)ĥ^aug(σ)(S) = f̂_S(σ), and for Im σ > 0 these are the Fourier transforms of
χ_K ġ(ḃ) and of h^aug(S). Here ġ = ġ_b, h = h_(b,s1) and h̆ = h̆¹_(b,s1) are the states at b.

*Dictionary* (Proposition 21.45 and Steps 3–5 of the proof of Proposition 31.27). A zf-term |σ|^z(log|σ|)^m
corresponds to the K⁺-term t_*^(−z−1)(log t_*)^(≤m), and a zf-weight w to the K⁺-weight w + 1; a tf-weight (exponent) w
of û to the ι⁺-weight (exponent) w + 1 of u; the ι⁺-exponent ζ + 2 of a forcing to the tf-exponent ζ + 1 of its
transform; and the Taylor coefficient of order m at zf of a function of tf-weight w has weight w − m at ∂X. *Levels.*
At the Taylor level j (after j divisions by σ), a tf-exponent ζ of the current forcing corresponds to the u-exponent
ζ + j − 1, and a zero energy solution at level j with the exponent w at ∂X to the u-exponent w + j + 1. A row of
u-exponent λ has the K⁺-rate λ − 1 (s1), λ (s0, s2) or λ + d_τ (c0, c1).

*Constants.* Let α = 4 + ε_K − ε′ be admissible (Definition 33.3; 0 < ε′ < ε′_0 < ε_K, so α > 4). Fix
η_1, η_2 ∈ (ε_K, ε_+) with η_1 < η_2 and η_1 < ε_g such that no λ ∈ Λ has real part 2 + η_1 or 3 + η_2; they lie below
ε_+, so that every exponent treated has u-exponent below 3 + ε_+, where the forcing is polyhomogeneous and
Lemma 33.2 (c) counts the logarithms. *The exclusion set of Definition 33.3* is the finite set of ε′ for
which one of the conditions (27.51) of Proposition 27.55 fails at the levels 1 and 2 below (for the finitely
many α_0 treated there, with ℓ_zf = α − 1 − j − ε), one of the conditions of Proposition 27.58 fails at level 3
(finitely many rounds), or α − 4 − ε is a real part excluded in Lemma 29.33 or in (28.1). Then ε > 0 is
taken small, with 2ε < ε_+ − η_2, and off a finite set as well. The orders q_j ∈ (2, 3) of the zero energy solves are
chosen off the real parts of the exponents at hand.

*The a priori facts.* f^♭ is the forcing of Proposition 33.8 (c) for f ∈ 𝒴⁰(α), and v is the forward solution of
L_b v = f^♭. In Section 33.7, v = u − u_I − u_ι with u as in the hypothesis of Lemma 33.16, so v has a
K⁺-weight w_v > 0 and the ι⁺-weight β′_+ (Proposition 33.8 (a)–(b): u_I vanishes near K⁺, the rows of 𝒩_ι have
rates at least λ_♯ − 1 > 0, and the terms of u^rot_ι have K⁺-weight Re λ_0 − ε > 0).

**Lemma 33.9** (The column terms.) On {r ≥ 1},

    f̂_ḃ(σ) = r⁻³G(σr, x),          f̂_S(σ) = r⁻³G(σr, x),

with G = G_ḃ, resp. G_S, linear in ḃ, resp. S, where G(ξ, x) = ∫_2^4 e^(iξs) F(s, x) ds and F is smooth in s, supported
in s ∈ [2, 4], and polyhomogeneous at ∂X with all its s-derivatives, with the index set

    ℰ_col := ({(0, 0), (1, 0)} ∪ ℰ_ind ∪ (1 + ℰ_ind)) + ℕ₀ ⊂ {Re ≥ 0},

which depends neither on ḃ, S nor on b ∈ ℬ̄_*. (On {r ≥ 1}, f_ḃ and f_S are supported in {2r ≤ t_* ≤ 4r}, by the proof of
Lemma 28.2 (b), and G is the function of (28.5) with f in place of f_∞.) Hence G(ξ, ·) is
polyhomogeneous with the index set ℰ_col, with coefficients and remainders entire in ξ and O(⟨ξ⟩^(−N)) on {Im ξ ≥ 0}
for every N; f̂_ḃ(0), f̂_S(0) ∈ 𝒜^(3+ℰ_col) near ∂X; and on X^±_(sc-b) near tf, where ρ_tf = r⁻¹ up to a factor smooth in
r̂ and σr = ±r̂, f̂_ḃ and f̂_S are polyhomogeneous at tf with the index set 3 + ℰ_col, smooth in r̂ up to zf, and rapidly
decaying at scf.

*Proof.* On {r ≥ 1}, χ_K = χ_c(r/t_*) ((28.2)), and L_b ġ(ḃ) = 0, L_b(t_*h(S) + h̆(S)) = 0
(Section 28.2); so there f = L_b(χ_K w) = [L_b, χ_K]w, with w = ġ(ḃ), resp. t_*h(S) + h̆(S). On sections a(t_*)w(x),
L_b = L_0 + L_1∂_(t_*) + L_2∂²_(t_*), with L_1 = [L_b, t_*] and L_2 = ½[[L_b, t_*], t_*] (Section 31.10), and
L_k ∈ ρ^(2−k)Diff^(2−k)_b(X̄) has smooth coefficients (Lemma 31.3, as it is applied to them there). The
t_*-derivatives and the b-derivatives in x of χ_c(r/t_*) are sums of terms r^(−k)φ(t_*/r), k ∈ {0, 1, 2}, with φ smooth
and, when at least one derivative falls on χ_c, supported in [2, 4]; for instance r∂_r[χ_c(r/t_*)] =
(r/t_*)χ′_c(r/t_*) and ∂_(t_*)[χ_c(r/t_*)] = −r⁻¹(r/t_*)²χ′_c(r/t_*). Every term of
[L_b, χ_K]w = Σ_(j≤2) [L_j∂^j_(t_*), χ_K]w carries at least one derivative of χ_K: a t_*-derivative of χ_K costs a
factor r⁻¹ (ρ times a function smooth at ∂X), and a b-derivative in x costs nothing; moreover
L_j ∈ ρ^(2−j)Diff^(2−j)_b, ∂_(t_*)w is 0, resp. h(S), and ∂²_(t_*)w = 0. So [L_b, χ_K]w is a finite sum of terms
φ(t_*/r)ρ²(Qv)(x) with v ∈ {ġ(ḃ), h̆(S)}, and of terms φ(t_*/r)ρ(Qh(S))(x), which come from t_*h(S) (there
ρ²t_* = (t_*/r)ρ, and the factor t_*/r is absorbed into φ); here φ is smooth and supported in [2, 4], and Q is a
b-differential operator whose coefficients are smooth at ∂X. With t_* = sr, F(s, x) = r⁴f(sr, x) is the corresponding
finite sum of terms φ(s)r²(Qv)(x) and φ(s)r³(Qh(S))(x), smooth in s and supported in [2, 4]. Now
ġ_b(1, 0) ∈ 𝒜^((2,0)∪(2+ℰ_ind)) and ġ_b(0, Ȧ) ∈ 𝒜^((3,0)∪(3+ℰ_ind)) ((25.18)),
h(S) ∈ 𝒜^((3,0)∪(3+ℰ_ind)) ((25.23)), and h̆(S) = h̆¹_(b,s1)(S) ∈ 𝒜^((2,0)∪(2+ℰ_ind)) ((23.25)).
So r²ġ_b(1, 0), r²h̆(S) and r³h(S) lie in 𝒜^((0,0)∪ℰ_ind), and r²ġ_b(0, Ȧ) lies in 𝒜^((1,0)∪(1+ℰ_ind)); b-derivatives
preserve these index sets, and the coefficients of Q, smooth at ∂X, add ℕ₀. Hence F, with all its s-derivatives, is
polyhomogeneous at ∂X with the index set ℰ_col, which lies in {Re ≥ 0} as min Re ℰ_ind > 0. These index sets depend
neither on ḃ and S nor on b (Lemma 30.2 (P3)). The statements on G follow by integrating the expansion of F
against e^(iξs), with integrations by parts in s for the decay in ξ (Im ξ ≥ 0, s > 0), and
r⁻³G(σr, x) = ρ³_tf G(±r̂, x). ∎

### 33.6 The lemmas of the spectral phase

**Lemma 33.10** (Zero energy with expansions.) Let q ∈ (2, 3), q′ ∈ (q, 5], and let
F ∈ H^(∞,(E,q′))_b(X̄) be partially polyhomogeneous at ∂X with an index set E, min Re E > q. Then
(û, ḃ, S) := L̃_b(0)⁻¹(F, 0, 0) (Proposition 28.8 at b, with its weight α_H := q − 4, so that α_H + 2 = q − 2 ∈ (0, 1)
is the L²-b-weight of a forcing of conormal order q) has û ∈ H^(∞,(E′,q′−2))_b(X̄), where E′ is the index set that
Lemma 21.35 builds from (E − 2) ∪ (1 + ℰ_col) and the indicial roots of L̂_b(0) (Proposition 25.6) with real
part in (q − 2, q′ − 2). Below the real part 3 the only such root is 2 (of type s0: the mass), so E′ lies in the extended
union of (E − 2) ∪ (1 + ℰ_col) and (2, l_*), plus ℕ₀; in u-exponents at level j these are Λ-valued
(Lemma 33.2).

*Proof.* Proposition 28.8 at b (Lemma 30.2 (P4)) gives û ∈ H^(∞,q−2)_b (conormal order q − 2, as in Step 3.1
of the proof of Proposition 31.27). Near ∂X, L̂_b(0) = ρ²A with A an elliptic b-operator (Section 25.6, as the
proof of Proposition 25.37 uses it), and L̂_b(0)û = F − f̂_ḃ(0) − f̂_S(0) there, with
f̂_ḃ(0), f̂_S(0) ∈ 𝒜^(3+ℰ_col) (Lemma 33.9). Lemma 21.35 with the weight q − 2 and with F replaced by ρ⁻²
times the right side (index set (E − 2) ∪ (1 + ℰ_col), remainder q′ − 2), applied finitely many times, each time from
the remainder order the previous application gave (each gains less than 1), gives the expansion up to q′ − 2. The
roots, which do not depend on b ((P2)): Proposition 25.6 (a) (none in (0, 1]) and its list of decaying roots: 2 for
s0; 3, 1 + λ^Υ_(s1,2), 1 + λ^Υ_(s1,3) and 5 for s1; 3 and 4 for v1; l + 2 ≥ 4 and above for l ≥ 2; and
1 + λ^Υ_(s0,2) ∈ (3, 3 + z_Υ/3] and 4 for s0. ∎

**Lemma 33.11** (One level.) Let j ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3} and g ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,(E,κ),((0,0),z)))_b(X^±_(sc-b))
with z > 0, its zf-coefficient g(0) ∈ H^(∞,(E,κ))_b(X̄), and let (û, ḃ, S) be as in Lemma 33.10 for F = g(0)
and q′ = κ (the same for both signs, or separately). Put

    g^(+1) := σ⁻¹(g − L̂_b(σ)(χ_zf û) − f̂_ḃ(σ) − f̂_S(σ)).    (33.7)

Then g^(+1) ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,(E^(+1),κ−1),((0,0),z−1)))_b and

    E^(+1) ⊂ (E − 1) ∪ (E′ + 1) ∪ (2 + ℰ_col),

E′ the index set of û; its zf-coefficient is g_1 + iL_1û + (…), where g_1 is the σ¹-coefficient of g, and the exact
formula is

    g^(+1) = σ⁻¹(g − χ_zf g(0)) − σ⁻¹[L_0, χ_zf]û + iχ_zf L_1û + i[L_1, χ_zf]û + σχ_zf L_2û
             − σ⁻¹(f̂_ḃ(σ) + f̂_S(σ) − χ_zf(f̂_ḃ(0) + f̂_S(0))).

*Proof.* Exactly,

    L̂_b(σ)(χ_zf û) = χ_zf L_0û + [L_0, χ_zf]û − iσ(χ_zf L_1û + [L_1, χ_zf]û) − σ²χ_zf L_2û,

and L_0û + f̂_ḃ(0) + f̂_S(0) = g(0); this gives the formula. The terms: σ⁻¹(g − χ_zf g(0)) has the tf-index set E − 1
(division by σ = ρ_tf ρ_zf) and the zf-data ((0, 0), z − 1); the commutators are supported where r̂ ∼ 1, away from zf,
and by Lemma 31.3 (b) both have the tf-index set E′ + 1 (E′ + 2 − 1 for σ⁻¹[L_0, χ_zf]û, and E′ + 1 for
[L_1, χ_zf]û, as L_1 ∈ ρDiff¹_b); χ_zf L_1û has E′ + 1, and σχ_zf L_2û has E′ + 1 (L_2 has no decay, and σ adds one at
tf); all are polynomial in σ at zf. The column terms: by Lemma 33.9, on {r ≥ 1},
σ⁻¹(f̂(σ) − χ_zf f̂(0)) = r⁻²H(σr, x) with H(ξ, x) := (G(ξ, x) − χ(|ξ|)G(0, x))/ξ and χ_zf = χ(r̂), which is smooth in ξ
up to 0 (G is entire), polyhomogeneous in x with the index set ℰ_col, and rapidly decaying as |ξ| → ∞; near tf,
r⁻² = ρ²_tf and ξ = ±r̂, so this has the tf-index set 2 + ℰ_col, Taylor expansions at zf and rapid decay at scf. On
{r ≤ 2}, f̂_c is entire (Lemma 28.4 (a)), and χ_zf = 1 there for small |σ|, so that part is polynomial at zf.
The tf-weights: κ − 1, and q′_û + 1 = κ − 1, with q′_û = κ − 2 the remainder order of û; the columns are
polyhomogeneous. ∎

**Lemma 33.12** (The pieces of the transition face model in compact sets.) Let u be the solution of
Proposition 27.55 at b for a forcing whose leading term at tf is at (α_0, k) with k = 0 (for k > 0 apply the following
to the α_0-derivatives). Let R < 2/ρ_0. On {r ≤ R} and for 0 < ±σ ≤ c_R, χ_zf = 1 and χ_tf = χ_2(ρ + |σ|) = 0
(Section 27.10), so u = |σ|^(α_0−2)u_b there, and

    |σ|^(α_0−2) u_b = Σ_τ c_τ(σ) T_τ(σ) + P_int(σ),    (33.8)

where:

- T_s1(σ) := h^(≤3)_(b,s1)(σ, S^(−1)_1) = Σ_(i≤3) (−iσ)^i h̆^i_s1(S^(−1)_1) and c_s1(σ) := |σ|^(α_0−1)σ⁻²/(2 − α_0)
  (−|σ|⁻¹ log|σ| at α_0 = 2);
- T_v1(σ) := h^(≤2)_(b,v1)(σ, V^(−1)_1) = Σ_(i≤2) (−iσ)^i h̆^i_(b,v1)(V^(−1)_1), whose bottom h̆⁰_(b,v1) = h_(b,v1)
  vanishes at b_0 (every V Killing), and c_v1(σ) := −i sgn(σ)|σ|^(α_0−2)/(2 − α_0) (i sgn(σ) log|σ| at α_0 = 2): this
  is the term l_(2−α_0)(r̂)G_v1 of (27.53). The v1 row is not a generic row of root −1: its tower starts at
  the bottom h_(b,v1) ∈ 𝒜³, and its state at the root −1 is the companion h̆¹_(b,v1) (Lemma 26.32). Accordingly
  −iσc_v1(σ) = −|σ|^(α_0−1)/(2 − α_0) (|σ| log|σ| at α_0 = 2) is the coefficient that a generic row of root −1 gives
  its state, and the bottom carries one power of |σ| less, as G_v1 of Lemma 27.54 prescribes;
- for the other rows (μ, τ) of the table of roots of Section 26.10, T_τ(σ) := h^((μ),≤c_μ)_(b,τ)(σ, Y^(μ)_τ) and
  c_τ(σ) := −|σ|^(α_0−2−μ)/β_μ(α_0), with |σ|^(⌊−μ⌋) log|σ| in place of the latter if β_μ(α_0) = 0, which for c0, c1
  happens at α_0 = 2 + μ ∈ (1, 2), and for the class rows in (−5/4, −1) and (−9/4, −2) at α_0 = 3 + μ and 4 + μ; here
  β_μ(α_0) = 2 − α_0 − {−μ} ((27.41));
- P_int is a finite sum of terms |σ|^m sgn(σ)^δ q(σ, x) with m ∈ ℤ, δ ∈ {0, 1} and q polynomial in σ (and in log r),
  without log|σ|: namely −|σ|⁻¹h(S^(−1)_1)/(2 − α_0) (for α_0 ≠ 2; at α_0 = 2 it is part of c_s1),
  i sgn(σ) r^(2−α_0) (h̆^(≤3)_(b,s1)(σ, S^(−1)_1) + T_v1(σ))/(2 − α_0) (with log r in place of r^(2−α_0)/(2 − α_0) at
  α_0 = 2), and |σ|^(⌊−μ⌋) r^(β_μ) T_τ(σ)/β_μ (with log r |σ|^(⌊−μ⌋) T_τ when β_μ = 0).

For larger R the tf-part adds log-free terms σ^j|σ|^k c(x) of integer degree and a zf-remainder of weight ℓ_zf + j; the
total χv̂ leaves no K⁺-tail from them by Lemma 33.7 (b), although a sign-odd term σ^j|σ|^k c(x) alone has a
two-sided one, which is recorded in item (vi) of the proof of Theorem 33.24; so the conclusions below are
unchanged. The towers T_τ(σ) are the first sum of (33.5) for the corresponding 1-form towers, without its
top term (−iσ)^(K+1) dt_* ⊗_s ω̆^K; the rows are unaffected, as that term has the rate e_ν + K + 1.

*Proof.* (27.53) with l_β(r̂) = (|σ|^β r^β − 1)/β (Definition 27.44) and G^exc_s1 = −|σ|σ⁻²h(S),
G_s1 = |σ|iσ⁻¹h̆^(≤3)_(b,s1)(σ, S), G_v1 = |σ|iσ⁻¹h^(≤2)_(b,v1)(σ, V), G_(μ,τ) = |σ|^(−μ)h^((μ),≤c_μ)_(b,τ)(σ, Y)
(Lemma 27.54, which holds at b by (P4)). The s1 and v1 terms: |σ|^(α_0−2)(−l_(2−α_0)(|σ|)|σ|σ⁻²h +
l_(2−α_0)(r̂)|σ|iσ⁻¹(h̆^(≤3) + T_v1)) equals (2 − α_0)⁻¹ times

    −|σ|⁻¹h + |σ|^(α_0−1)σ⁻²h + i sgn(σ) r^(2−α_0)(h̆^(≤3) + T_v1) − i|σ|^(α_0−1)σ⁻¹(h̆^(≤3) + T_v1),

as |σ|σ⁻¹ = sgn(σ); and |σ|^(α_0−1)σ⁻²(h − iσh̆^(≤3)) = c_s1(2 − α_0)h^(≤3)(σ, S) (the definition in
(27.56)), while −i|σ|^(α_0−1)σ⁻¹ = (2 − α_0)c_v1. At α_0 = 2, l_0(r̂) = log|σ| + log r. The other rows:

    |σ|^(α_0−2−μ) l_(β_μ)(r̂) = (|σ|^(α_0−2−μ+β_μ) r^(β_μ) − |σ|^(α_0−2−μ))/β_μ,     α_0 − 2 − μ + β_μ = ⌊−μ⌋.

At β = 0, l_0(r̂) = log|σ| + log r. The towers: Definition 27.52 defines them as Σ_j (−iσ)^j h̆^((μ),j)_b with the
companions of Section 26.11, which are those of Lemma 33.4 (b) (for s0 with the shift of index). ∎

**Lemma 33.13** (The column pieces.) For ḃ ∈ 𝔟_ℂ, S ∈ 𝒮_(1,ℂ) and j ∈ ℕ₀, the distributions
σ^j ĝ^aug(σ)(ḃ) and σ^j ĥ^aug(σ)(S) on ℝ (boundary values from Im σ > 0) are the Fourier transforms of
(i∂_(t_*))^j(χ_K ġ(ḃ)) and (i∂_(t_*))^j h^aug(S). In {r ≤ R}, for large t_*: the first is χ_K ġ(ḃ) for j = 0 and
vanishes for j ≥ 1; the second is t_*h(S) + h̆(S) for j = 0, ih(S) for j = 1, and vanishes for j ≥ 2. If ḃ(σ), S(σ) lie
in H^(∞,a)_b(±(0, c], |dσ/σ|), then χσ^j ĝ^aug(ḃ(σ)) and χσ^j ĥ^aug(S(σ)) have inverse transforms of K⁺-weight a + j and
a + j − 1, and of ι⁺-weight 3/2 − ε.

*Proof.* Lemma 28.5 (a) and ∂_(t_*) ↔ −iσ; χ_K = 1 near K⁺ in {r ≤ R}, and h^aug(S) = χ_K(t_*h(S) + h̆(S))
(Section 28.2). The last statement is Lemma 29.34 with a for their classes on X^±_(sc-b), and
Proposition 21.45 (2) for the inverse transforms: ĝ^aug carries σ⁻¹ and ĥ^aug carries σ⁻², which give the weights
a + j − 1 + 1 and a + j − 2 + 1. ∎

**Lemma 33.14** (The decomposition.) Let f̂ ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,κ,((0,0),z)))_b on ±(0, c], and suppose that
f̂ = Σ_(i∈I) L̂_b(σ)P_i + σ^J g_J on 0 < |σ| ≤ c, where each P_i(σ) lies in the space 𝒳′_σ of Lemma 31.24 for
σ ≠ 0 (a section smooth on X° and b-conormal at ∂X, or a sum of terms ĝ^aug and ĥ^aug), and let
(û_f, ḃ_f, S_f) := L̃_b(σ)⁻¹(g_J, 0, 0). Then the outgoing inverse satisfies, for 0 < |σ| ≤ c,

    L̂_b(σ)⁻¹f̂ = Σ_i P_i + σ^J(û_f + ĝ^aug(σ)(ḃ_f) + ĥ^aug(σ)(S_f)).    (33.9)

*Proof.* Apply L̂_b(σ): the right side maps to Σ_i L̂_b P_i + σ^J(L̂_b û_f + f̂_(ḃ_f) + f̂_(S_f)) = f̂, by
Lemma 28.5 (c) and the first component of L̃_b(σ)(û_f, ḃ_f, S_f) = (g_J, 0). Every term lies in 𝒳′_σ
(Lemma 28.5 (b), Lemma 31.24), on which L̂_b(σ) is injective, and L̂_b(σ)⁻¹f̂ is the element of
𝒳_σ ⊂ 𝒳′_σ with this image. ∎

The rows r(·) and the columns of L̃_b thus enter only through the zero energy solves (Lemma 33.10) and the last
level; no assembly of the augmented components, as in (31.47) and (32.24), is needed.

### 33.7 The spectral phase and the expansion below the order α − 2

This section is [Hin26, Theorem 11.59, Steps 2.A.3–2.A.8 and Part 3 of the proof] in dimension 4 + 1.

**Proposition 33.15** (The spectral phase.) Let α > 4 be admissible, and let f^♭ and v be as in
Section 33.5. There are S_ν ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ), ν ∈ 𝒩_σ, linear and continuous in f, and a finite sum v^rot of v1 towers
χ_K Σ_(i≤2) a^((i)) h̆^i_(b,v1)(Y), with a polyhomogeneous of exponents (α_0, l), Re α_0 = 2, and Y ∈ 𝒱_(1,ℂ) linear
and continuous in f, such that

    v − Σ_(ν∈𝒩_σ) m_ν(S_ν) − v^rot ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β′_+,α−2−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−).    (33.10)

The terms of v^rot have K⁺-weight 2 − ε, and 3 − ε > α − 2 when h_(b,v1) = 0; in that case, in particular at b_0,
v^rot may be put into the remainder.

*Proof.* *Step 0 (decomposition and transform; Step 3 of the proof of Proposition 31.27).* Write
v = v_hi + v_low with ℱv_low = χ(|σ|)v̂. Lemma 29.32 (with β^f_I = ℓ_I, β_ι = w_+ − 2 − ε, β_K = α − ε;
ℓ_I + 1 ≥ w_+ − ε − (1 − ε_1) by (H4)) gives v_hi ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−ε,j,j))_b(M′) for every j. Proposition 21.45 (1) with
β_I = ℓ_I + 1, β_ι = w_+ − ε, E_ι = ℰ^♭ + 2, E_I = ∅, β_K = α − ε, E_K = ∅ (its condition (21.65),
ℓ_I + 1 > w_+ − 1 − ε, holds by (H4)) gives

    g_0 := f̂^♭|_(±(0,c]) ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,(ℰ^♭+1,w_+−1−ε),((0,0),α−1−ε)))_b,

with tf-exponents of real part at least 3 and u-exponents (level 0) in Λ. We construct pieces P_i and g_J, J = 3, as in
Lemma 33.14.

*Step 1 (level 0; [Hin26, Step 2.A.3]).* Lemma 33.10 with q_0 := 3 − ε, q′ := w_+ − 1 − ε and F = g_0(0) gives
(û_0, ḃ_0, S_0), the same for both signs; û_0 has the exponents (ℰ^♭ − 1) ∪ (1 + ℰ_col) ∪ (2, ·) (and their
ℕ₀-shifts) below q′ − 2 = 2 + ε_+ − ε, the root 2 being the mass. S_0 = 0 by the argument of Step 3.1 of the proof of
Proposition 31.27 (f^♭ lies in the space of Step 3 of the proof of Proposition 31.21, and v has K⁺-weight above
−1). Pieces: χ_zf û_0 and ĝ^aug(ḃ_0). Lemma 33.11 gives g_1, with tf-exponents of real part at least 2,
u-exponents in Λ (level 1), tf-weight 3 + ε_+ − ε, and zf-data ((0, 0), α − 2 − ε).

*Step 2 (level 1; [Hin26, Steps 2.A.4–2.A.5]).* For each tf-exponent (α_0, k) of g_1 with 2 ≤ Re α_0 < 2 + η_1 (finitely
many), Proposition 27.55 with ℓ_zf := α − 2 − ε and ℓ_scf := 3/2 − ε applies (admissibility) to the corresponding
term, with its whole tf-coefficient, and gives u_((α_0,k)); the pieces are σu_((α_0,k)). The remainder
g_1 − Σ L̂_b(σ)u_((α_0,k)) has tf-exponents in ((α_0, k) + ℰ_ind) ∪ ((4, k + 1) + ℱ) ((27.52)), of real part
at least 2 + ε_g > 2 + η_1, and the other exponents of g_1, at least 2 + η_1 by the choice of η_1; the zf-data are
unchanged. Lemma 33.10 with q_1 := 2 + η_1 and q′ := 3 + ε_+ − ε on its zf-coefficient (both signs separately)
gives (û_1, ḃ_1, S_1)^±, with the pieces σ(χ_zf û_1 + ĝ^aug(ḃ_1) + ĥ^aug(S_1)); and Lemma 33.11 gives g_2, with
tf-exponents of real part at least 1 + η_1 (those of û_1, at least η_1, plus one; those of the remainder, at least
2 + η_1, minus one; the columns' 2 + ℰ_col), tf-weight 2 + ε_+ − ε, and zf-data ((0, 0), α − 3 − ε).

*Step 3 (level 2; [Hin26, Steps 2.A.6–2.A.7]).* For each tf-exponent (α_0, k) of g_2 with
1 + η_1 ≤ Re α_0 < 2 + η_2, Proposition 27.55 with ℓ_zf := α − 3 − ε; its remainder exponents α_0 + ℰ_ind may again
lie below 2 + η_2, and are treated in turn (finitely many rounds, the real parts rising by at least ε_g); (4, k + 1)
lies above. The pieces are σ²u_((α_0,k)). Then Lemma 33.10 with q_2 := 2 + η_2 and q′ := 2 + ε_+ − ε gives the
pieces σ²(χ_zf û_2 + ĝ^aug(ḃ_2) + ĥ^aug(S_2)), and Lemma 33.11 gives g_3, of tf-weight κ_3 := 1 + η_2 − 2ε
(conormal; its expansion is not needed) and zf-data ((0, 0), ℓ_3), ℓ_3 := α − 4 − ε ∈ (0, ε_K).

*Step 4 (level 3; [Hin26, Step 2.A.8 and Part 3]).* Fix δ > 0 with δ + ℓ_3 + 2ε < ε_g. While the tf-weight κ of the
current level-3 forcing is at most 2 + ℓ_3 + ε, apply Proposition 27.58 with α_κ := min(κ, 2 − δ) ∈ (1, 2) (the forcing
has the tf-weight α_κ), ℓ_zf := ℓ_3, the order 0 of the zf-index set there, and
w = ℓ_3 − α_κ + 2 ∈ [−ε, 1) ⊂ (−ε_ind, ℓ^max_K) (α_κ ≤ κ ≤ 2 + ℓ_3 + ε, and α_κ ≥ κ_3 > 1 + ℓ_3, as η_2 > ε_K > ℓ_3). Its
conditions w ≠ −μ and 2 − α_κ + j ≠ −μ hold for ε off a finite set (admissibility) and, when α_κ = 2 − δ, for δ off the
finite set {−μ − j}, which we impose on δ. It gives

    u = χ_zf u_b + χ^♯_tf ũ ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−2ε,α_κ−2,α_κ−3))_b

with a remainder of tf-weight at least α_κ + ε_g − ε, which exceeds κ by ε_g − ε when α_κ = κ, and, when α_κ = 2 − δ < κ,
exceeds 2 + ℓ_3 + ε (as δ + ℓ_3 + 2ε < ε_g), after which the loop ends; the pieces are σ³u. After finitely many rounds
κ > 2 + ℓ_3 + ε; lowering κ if necessary (a forcing of tf-weight κ has every smaller tf-weight), κ ∈ (2 + ℓ_3 + ε, 3).
Lemma 33.10 with q_3 := κ − ε, q′ := κ and E = ∅ gives (û_3, ḃ_3, S_3)^± and the pieces
σ³(χ_zf û_3 + ĝ^aug(ḃ_3) + ĥ^aug(S_3)). The rest,

    g_J := (the level-3 source) − L̂_b(σ)(χ_zf û_3) − f̂_(ḃ_3) − f̂_(S_3) ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,κ−ε,ℓ_3))_b

(the zf-coefficient is removed, the next Taylor order being 1; tf as in the proof of Lemma 33.11, without
the division), is inverted by Lemma 29.33 with β_scf := 3/2 − 2ε, β_tf := κ − 2 − ε, β_zf := ℓ_3,
β_tf − β_zf ∈ (0, 1):

    û_f ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−3ε,κ−2−ε,ℓ_3))_b,          ḃ_f, S_f ∈ H^(∞,ℓ_3)_b(±(0, c], |dσ/σ|).

*Step 5 (matching, and the pieces at K⁺).* By Lemma 33.14, on 0 < |σ| ≤ c, v̂ is the sum of the pieces and of
σ³(û_f + ĝ^aug(ḃ_f) + ĥ^aug(S_f)). The data at the levels 1–3 were found for each sign; write S^±_1 = S_e ± S_o.

*Matching* (as in Step 5 of the proof of Proposition 31.27, and [Hin26, p. 287]). Multiplied by σ, every piece is
bounded near σ = 0: σ · σĥ^aug(S^±_1) = −G_2(σ)(S^±_1) and σ · σĝ^aug(ḃ^±_1) = iσΨġ(ḃ^±_1) by (33.6);
σĝ^aug(ḃ_0) = iΨġ(ḃ_0); the columns of the levels 2–3 carry σ^(≥2); and the other pieces have degree at least 0
(Lemma 33.12: σ^(j+1)c_τ(σ) has degree at least α_0 − 2 + j ≥ 0, and σ^(j+1)P_int degree at least j ≥ 1) or
zf-weight above 0 (Step 4, the last level). So ℱ(∂_(t_*)v_low) = −iσχv̂ and −iσχ times the sum differ by a
distribution supported at 0, whose inverse transform, a polynomial, tends to 0 as t_* → −∞
(∂_(t_*)v_low = −∂_(t_*)v_hi = O(|t_*|^(−∞)) there, as v = 0 for t_* < 1; the other by the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma), and
so vanishes. Near σ = 0, −iσχ times the sum is iχ sgn(σ)h(S_o) (G_2(0) = h, Lemma 28.5 (b)) plus terms whose
inverse transforms have K⁻-weight above 1 in {r ≤ R}: the sign-even part of iG_2(σ)(S^±_1) and Ψġ(ḃ_0) (the
−iσ-multiples of the terms above) are smooth in σ; every other piece times σ is, in {r ≤ R}, a sum of terms
sgn(σ)^δ|σ|^z(log|σ|)^m times smooth sections with Re z > 0 (Lemma 33.12, with χ_zf = 1 there
for |σ| ≤ c_R), whose inverse transforms are O(|t_*|^(−1−Re z) log^m), or of zf-weight above 0 (Proposition 20.20 (1)).
The inverse transform of χ sgn(σ) is c t_*⁻¹(1 + o(1)) as t_* → −∞, with c ≠ 0. Hence h(S_o) = 0 on {r ≤ R}, so S_o = 0
((28.9)), and S_1 is the same for both signs. We then read the pieces of v̂ itself, the column pieces with
constant coefficients as boundary values (Lemma 33.13) and the others as locally integrable functions: as
before, χv̂ and χ times their sum differ by a distribution supported at 0, a polynomial in t_* after inverse transform,
which tends to 0 as t_* → −∞ (v_low = −v_hi there, the column pieces with constant coefficients vanish there as
χ_K = 0, and the others by Riemann–Lebesgue), and so vanishes. We sort the inverse transforms in {r ≤ R}, for large
t_*:

(i) *Zero energy pieces* σ^j χ_zf û^±_j: in {r ≤ R}, χ_zf = 1 for |σ| ≤ c_R, so they are sgn(σ)^δ times polynomials in
σ there (the data of the levels 1–3 may depend on the sign): of integer degree, with no log|σ|.

(ii) *Column pieces* (Lemma 33.13): χ_K ġ(ḃ_0) from level 0; ih(S_1) from σĥ^aug(S_1) at level 1 (S_1 being
independent of the sign); σĝ^aug(ḃ^±_1) = iΨġ(ḃ_e) ± iΨġ(ḃ_o), whose first part contributes nothing for large t_* and
whose second is sgn(σ) times a function smooth in σ (integer degree, no log|σ|); and at the levels 2 and 3 the
sign-even parts contribute nothing for large t_*, the sign-odd parts being again sgn(σ) times smooth functions of σ.

(iii) *The last level.* σ³û_f has zf-weight ℓ_3 + 3; σ³ĝ^aug(ḃ_f) and σ³ĥ^aug(S_f) give the K⁺-weights ℓ_3 + 3 and
ℓ_3 + 2 = α − 2 − ε (Lemma 33.13); the level-3 pieces of Step 4 have zf-weight α_κ − 3 + 3 ≥ κ_3 =
1 + η_2 − 2ε, so K⁺-weight at least 2 + η_2 − 2ε > α − 2 (η_2 > ε_K), by Proposition 21.45 (2) (on {r ≤ R},
Proposition 20.20 (1)).

(iv) *The transition face pieces at the levels 1 and 2*, by Lemma 33.12: σ^j(Σ_τ c_τ(σ)T_τ(σ) + P_int(σ)).
The terms of σ^jP_int are, in {r ≤ R}, finite sums of |σ|^m sgn(σ)^δ times polynomials in σ, with m + j ≥ 0 (m ≥ −1,
j ≥ 1): of integer degree, with no log|σ|. The terms σ^jc_τ(σ)(−iσ)^i h̆^i_τ have the degree α_0 − 3 + j + i for s1
(c_s1 has degree α_0 − 3), α_0 − 2 + j + i for v1 (c_v1 has degree α_0 − 2), and α_0 − 2 − μ + j + i for the other
rows, with log|σ| at integer degree when α_0 or β_μ is critical.

Now apply Lemma 33.7 to χv̂ in {r ≤ R} (V = C^∞({r ≤ R})), with β := α − 3 − 2ε (ε off a finite set, so that
β ∉ ℕ₀); the hypothesis as t_* → −∞ holds as above (v is forward). The terms of (i), the sign-odd column pieces of
(ii), those with j ≥ 1 in ĝ^aug and j ≥ 2 in ĥ^aug, and σ^jP_int have integer degree and no log|σ|, so they contribute
no tail (its (b)); (iii) contributes O(t_*^(−α+2+3ε)), as σ³ĥ^aug(S_f) has zf-weight ℓ_3 + 1 = α − 3 − ε > β. So, for
large t_* in {r ≤ R},

    v = χ_K ġ(ḃ_0) + ih(S_1) + Σ_(pieces (iv)) Σ_i (𝒯_+c_τ)^((i))(t_*) h̆^i_τ + O(t_*^(−α+2+3ε)),

where 𝒯_+c is the tail as t_* → +∞ of the forward part of σ^jc(σ) (Lemma 33.7 (b): a combination of
t_*^(−z−1)(log t_*)^l, with z = α_0 − 3 + j for s1, α_0 − 2 + j for v1 and α_0 − 2 − μ + j otherwise), and the
derivatives come from (−iσ)^i ↔ ∂^i_(t_*), as (σ + i0)^z σ^i = (σ + i0)^(z+i): the tail of a tower piece is the tower
Σ_i a^((i)) h̆^i_τ of a := 𝒯_+c.

*Step 6 (the stationary terms and the rows).* v has K⁺-weight w_v > 0, and every other term above decays
(Re z + 1 > 0); so the stationary tensor ġ(ḃ_0) + h(iS_1) (S_1 being independent of the sign by Step 5) vanishes, and
ḃ_0 = 0, S_1 = 0 ((28.9)), as in Step 6 of the proof of Lemma 32.27. The towers: at level 1 (j = 1,
2 ≤ Re α_0 < 2 + η_1, u-exponent α_0) the s1 tower has the rate α_0 − 1 and is the row (s1, α_0, ·); the s0 and s2
towers have the rate α_0, below α − 2 only for Re α_0 = 2 by (G) (the rows (s0, 2, ·), (s2, 2, ·)); the c0, c1 towers
have the rate α_0 + d_τ > 2 + ε_K by (G); the rows outside 𝒯 have rate at least α_0 + 1; and the v1 tower, whose
coefficient a = 𝒯_+c_v1 has the exponents (α_0 + j − 1, ·) = (α_0, ·), has the rate α_0 through its bottom
a h_(b,v1)(V^(−1)_1), and the rate α_0 + 1 when h_(b,v1) = 0. By (G) the v1 towers with Re α_0 > 2 have rate above
2 + ε_K ≥ α − 2; those with Re α_0 = 2 form v^rot. At level 2 (u-exponent α_0 + 1, of real part in [2 + η_1, 3 + η_2))
only the s1 tower can have a rate α_0 < 2 + ε_K, and by (G) then Re(α_0 + 1) ≤ 3; the s0, s2 and v1 towers have rate
at least α_0 + 1 ≥ 2 + η_1 > 2 + ε_K. So the towers of rate below α − 2, other than those of v^rot, are those of the
rows of 𝒩_σ, with (λ, k) ∈ ℰ_par by Lemma 33.2 (c). By Lemma 33.4, each such tower is m_ν(S_ν) in
{r ≤ R} for large t_*, up to the terms with a^((i)), i ≥ 4 (s1), i ≥ 3 (s0, s2), of rate at least
Re e_ν + 3 > α − 2; and the towers of rate at least α − 2 are O(t_*^(−α+2+3ε)). Hence
v − Σ_(ν∈𝒩_σ) m_ν(S_ν) − v^rot = O(t_*^(−α+2+3ε)) in {r ≤ R}, with all t_*∂_(t_*)- and spatial derivatives.

*Step 7 (joint weights).* The sum of the pieces other than the columns with constant coefficients lies, on each half, in
a space H^(∞,(3/2−3ε,(E_tf,β′_+−1),((0,0)∪̄(E_K−1),α−3−ε)))_b, with E_K the K⁺-exponents of Step 5 (the polyhomogeneous
zf-terms of the u of Proposition 27.55, with coefficients polyhomogeneous at tf by Lemma 27.54 and
(27.53), and the zero energy pieces), and the matching condition (21.67) of Proposition 21.45 holds,
by Lemma 33.7 (a) applied to the zf-coefficients in {r ≤ R} for every R. Proposition 21.45 (2) gives v_low
(minus the stationary columns, which vanish) in H^(∞,3/2−4ε,(E_ι,β′_+),(E_K,α−2−ε))_b(M′). Its K⁺-coefficients are
functions on K⁺ determined in K⁺ ∩ {r ≤ R} by Step 6, where they equal those of Σ_(𝒩_σ) m_ν(S_ν) + v^rot, which is
itself partially polyhomogeneous at K⁺ with these coefficients (Lemma 32.32 (b), (e), (32.31)). So
v − Σ m_ν(S_ν) − v^rot has K⁺-weight α − 2 − ε. Its ι⁺-weight is β′_+ (v, the m_ν and the terms of v^rot have it), and
its ℐ⁺-data are those of v: near ℐ⁺, χ_K = 0, and Proposition 29.27 applies as in Step 8 of the proof of
Lemma 32.27. *Linearity and continuity:* every map used is linear and bounded (Lemma 33.10–
Lemma 33.14, Proposition 27.55, Proposition 27.58, Lemma 29.32–Lemma 29.34,
Proposition 21.45), and the S_ν and the coefficients of v^rot are coefficients of the tails. ∎

**Lemma 33.16** (The expansion; [Hin26, Theorem 11.59, Parts 1–3, the extraction].) Let α > 4 be
admissible, let (h, p⃗) be a base point with black hole parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, with p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 and h ∈ 𝒳^∞ small, and let
G ∈ 𝒴⁰(α). Suppose that the forward solution u of L_(h,p⃗)u = G lies in
⋂_ε H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β′_+,w_0−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−) with w_0 > 0, w_0 + a_K > α and β′_+ ∈ (3/2 − (δ_♯ − ε_+), 3/2). Then

    u = Σ_(ν∈𝒩) m_ν(S_ν) + u^rot + ũ,     ũ ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β_+,α−2−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−)    (33.11)

for every β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+). Here u^rot := u^rot_ι + v^rot is the sum of the v1 terms of
Proposition 33.8 and Proposition 33.15 for the forcing f′ of the proof, and the coefficients
S_ν = S^(h,p⃗)_ν(G) ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ) are determined by u − u^rot (Corollary 33.6); u^rot and the S_ν are
conjugation-symmetric and linear in G, and for every w ∈ (0, w_0]

    |S^(h,p⃗)_ν(G)| + |u^rot| ≤ C‖G‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u‖_(w),

where |u^rot| is the size of the coefficients V_(λ_0,j) and Y of its terms, ‖·‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) is one fixed seminorm of
𝒴⁰(α) and ‖·‖_(w) one fixed seminorm of the space of the hypothesis with w in place of w_0, both chosen as in
Section 32.6, and C depends on w and is uniform for (h, p⃗) small and b ∈ ℬ̄_*. This is not a bound by G alone: the
last term vanishes at (h, p⃗) = (0, 0), where L_(0,0) = L_(b_0), but not at the reference point (0, p⃗_b) of
Lemma 33.17 with b ≠ b_0. When h_(b,v1) = 0, in particular at b_0, u^rot has K⁺-weight α − 2 − ε and is put
into ũ.

*Proof.* *Step 0.* Put f′ := G − (L − L_b)u, which equals L_b u. By Proposition 29.12 ((29.15)), for
L = L_(h,p⃗) (Lemma 32.35), (L − L_b)u has the ℐ⁺-data (⟨ℰ^C_I + 1⟩′, ℓ_I + 1), the plain ι⁺-weight
β′_+ + 2 + λ_♯ − ε > w_+ (as β′_+ > 3/2 − δ_♯ + ε_+, and m_+ = λ_♯ by (H1)), and the K⁺-weight
w_0 − ε + a_K ≥ α − ε. So f′ ∈ 𝒴⁰(α) for ε < w_0 + a_K − α, and L_b u = f′.

*Steps 1–2.* Proposition 33.8 gives u_I, u_ι, (S_ν)_(𝒩_ι), u^rot_ι and f^♭; v := u − u_I − u_ι is the forward
solution of L_b v = f^♭ and has the K⁺-weight min(w_0, λ_♯ − 1) − ε > 0.

*Step 3.* Proposition 33.15 gives (S_ν)_(𝒩_σ) and v^rot. Summing gives (33.11) with the ι⁺-weight
min(β′_+, λ_♯) − ε; the weight β_+ for every β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+) follows as in Lemma 32.27 (the ι⁺-terms
of ũ below 3/2 are those of u, by Step 1 of the proof of Proposition 31.21 with ℓ̆_+ < 3/2).

*Determination.* If two such expansions hold with the same u^rot, their difference is a sum of m_ν of K⁺-weight
α − 2 − ε, which is 0 by Corollary 33.6 (Re e_ν ≤ 2 < α − 2). *Reality:* u is real, m_ν̄(W̄) is the conjugate of
m_ν(W), and the expansion is unique. *Bounds:* Steps 1–3 obtain the S_ν and u^rot from f′ by maps fixed by L_b, linear
and bounded uniformly on ℬ̄_* (Proposition 33.8, Proposition 33.15, Corollary 33.6, Lemma 30.2),
so |S_ν| + |u^rot| ≤ C‖f′‖_(𝒴⁰(α)). The count of Step 0, whose coefficients L − L_b have size O(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)
(Lemma 32.35) and gain a_K at K⁺, applies with w − ε for w_0 − ε, as w − ε + a_K ≥ α for ε small (a_K ≥ 4 + ε_K
≥ α by (H2)); it gives ‖(L − L_b)u‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u‖_(w), so
‖f′‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) ≤ ‖G‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u‖_(w). ∎

Since f′ = L_b u, the coefficients S_ν and u^rot are linear functions of u.

**Lemma 33.17** (The coefficients near the reference point.) Fix b ∈ ℬ̄_* and let p⃗_b ∈ 𝒫 be the
parameter whose only nonzero component is b − b_0. In Lemma 33.16, if the base points (h_j, p⃗_j) have black
hole parameter b, (h_j, p⃗_j) → (0, p⃗_b), G_j → G in 𝒴⁰(α), and the forward solutions u_j of L_(h_j,p⃗_j)u_j = G_j and
u of L_(0,p⃗_b)u = G satisfy the hypothesis with the same w_0 and β′_+, the u_j being bounded there, then
S^(h_j,p⃗_j)_ν(G_j) → S^(0,p⃗_b)_ν(G). At b_0, p⃗_(b_0) = 0 and L_(0,0) = L_(b_0).

*Proof.* Write L_j := L_(h_j,p⃗_j). As in Lemma 32.28, with L_(0,p⃗_b) as the reference operator, u_j − u is the
forward solution of

    L_(0,p⃗_b)(u_j − u) = R_j := G_j − G − (L_j − L_(0,p⃗_b))u_j.

The coefficients of L_j − L_(0,p⃗_b) have size O(‖h_j‖ + |p⃗_j − p⃗_b|) (Lemma 32.35), and near K⁺ they gain a_K,
both backgrounds being g_b there (Lemma 29.11); so the count of Step 0 of the proof of Lemma 33.16, the
u_j being bounded, gives R_j → 0 in 𝒴⁰(α); R_j is real. u_j − u satisfies the hypothesis of Lemma 33.16 with
the same w_0 and β′_+, and the coefficients are linear functions of the solution, so
S^(h_j,p⃗_j)_ν(G_j) − S^(0,p⃗_b)_ν(G) = S^(0,p⃗_b)_ν(R_j), and the bound of Lemma 33.16 at (0, p⃗_b) gives, for
every w ∈ (0, w_0],

    |S^(0,p⃗_b)_ν(R_j)| ≤ C‖R_j‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) + C|p⃗_b|‖u_j − u‖_(w).

At b = b_0, p⃗_b = 0 and this tends to 0. For b ≠ b_0 it remains to show ‖u_j − u‖_(w) → 0 for one such w, and this
follows from part (i) of Proposition 32.29 at a level below 3. Fix an admissible α′ ∈ (2, min(3, 2 + w_0))
(Section 32.6; the excluded values are finitely many), and w ∈ (0, α′ − 2).

*u_j − u lies in (32.26) at α′.* Its K⁺-weight is w_0 − ε for every ε > 0, and w_0 > α′ − 2; its ℐ⁺-data are
(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩, ℓ_I); and u_j and u have the ι⁺-weight β_+ for every β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+), by (33.11), as
the m_ν and the terms of u^rot have ι⁺-weight above 3/2 (λ_♯ − ε for the m_ν, Lemma 32.32 (b), and for the
terms of u^rot_ι, Proposition 33.8; 2 − ε for the towers of v^rot, whose coefficients have exponents of real part 2
and whose order at ι⁺ is that exponent, Section 33.9).

*Uniqueness and (i) at α′.* The row components of p⃗_b vanish, so L_(0,p⃗_b) is the operator of P_3 at (0, p⃗_b)
(Lemma 32.35), and Proposition 32.29 at α′ applies at the base point (0, p⃗_b), whose black hole parameter b
lies in ℬ̄_*. R_j lies in 𝒴⁰(α) ⊂ 𝒴(α′), the class of Section 32.10 at α′, which lies in the class of
Section 32.6 of the same name, and R_j → 0 there. The forward solution u_j − u of L_(0,p⃗_b)(u_j − u) = R_j lies
in (32.26) at α′, so the parameter 0 has, for (0, p⃗_b) and the forcing R_j, the property of the statement at
α′; by uniqueness at α′, p⃗′_(0,p⃗_b,α′)(R_j) = 0, and u_j − u is the solution of (32.25) at α′ for the
forcing R_j. By (i) at α′ the map from the forcing to this solution is linear and bounded from 𝒴(α′) into the space
of (32.26) at α′, with bounds uniform at the base point (0, p⃗_b), in the fixed seminorm ‖·‖_(α′) of
Section 32.6 at α′. We take that seminorm, as Section 32.6 allows, with ι⁺-weight β′_+ (which lies in
(1, 3/2), and 3/2 ≤ min Re ℰ_+) and regularity at least that of ‖·‖_(w); so ‖u_j − u‖_(α′) → 0. As w < α′ − 2, the
seminorm ‖·‖_(w) is bounded by ‖·‖_(α′), and ‖u_j − u‖_(w) → 0. Hence S^(0,p⃗_b)_ν(R_j) → 0. ∎

### 33.8 Elimination

This section is [Hin26, Theorem 11.59, Step 2.B and Part 3 of the proof, (11.222)] in dimension 4 + 1, at base points
with black hole parameter b_0. For an admissible α′ ∈ (2, 3) (Section 32.6), 𝒫_(α′) is the space of
Section 32.9 (the parameters p⃗_(≤0) and the motions of K⁺-rate below α′ − 2), and

    𝒩′ := 𝒩 ∖ {(s1, λ, k) : (λ, k) ∈ ℳ_(α′)},

the rows of Section 32.10 not in 𝒫_(α′). For W⃗ = (W_ν)_(ν∈𝒩′), conjugation-symmetric, write
D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(W⃗) := Σ_(ν∈𝒩′) f^ν_(h,p⃗)(W_ν), and 𝒫^full for 𝒫_(α′) ⊕ {W⃗}, which is the space 𝒫 of
Section 32.10.

**Theorem 33.18** ([Hin26, Theorem 11.59, Parts 1–3: (11.222)], in dimension 4 + 1.) Let α > 4 be
admissible, and let (h, p⃗) be a base point with black hole parameter b_0, with p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 and h ∈ 𝒳^∞ small. For every
F ∈ 𝒴⁰(α) there is a unique p⃗′ = p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(F) ∈ 𝒫 such that the forward solution of

    L_(h,p⃗)u = F − D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(p⃗′)    (33.12)

satisfies

    u ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β_+,α−2−ε)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−)
        for every β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+).    (33.13)

Moreover p⃗′_(h,p⃗) is linear, with bounds uniform for (h, p⃗) small, and continuous at (0, 0) as in
Proposition 32.29 (ii). In compact spatial sets u = O(t_*^(−2−ε_K+ε′+ε)); letting ε′ → 0 along admissible values,
this is [Hin26, (11.222)] at K⁺, with the plain ι⁺-weight β_+. Its ι⁺-index set is part of Theorem 33.24.

*Proof.* Fix an admissible α′ ∈ (2, 3). (32.26) holds for every β_+ < 3/2, so β′_+ can be taken in
(3/2 − (δ_♯ − ε_+), 3/2), and w_0 := min(α′ − 2, λ_♯ − 1) satisfies w_0 + a_K > α (a_K ≥ 4 + ε_K by (H2), and
w_0 > 0).

*Proposition 32.29 for P_4.* That proposition is stated for P_3 at (h, p⃗_3). For p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 with row components
(W_ν)_(ν∉ℳ) put h′ := h + Σ_(ν∉ℳ) h_ν(W_ν), in 𝒳^∞ and small (Lemma 32.35). Then L_(h,p⃗) is the linearised
operator of P_3 at (h′, p⃗_3) (Lemma 32.35), and in the directions S, b, S⁽⁰⁾_1 the derivatives D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)
and D_(p⃗)P_3(h′, p⃗_3) differ by (∂δ*_(g_0,E_C))ϑ_rows (Lemma 32.36 (a)), which is linear in the direction,
lies in 𝒴_2(α) ⊂ 𝒴(α′) and is O(|W⃗|); in the directions of the motions they agree. So the finite-dimensional maps of
the base and induction steps of Proposition 32.29 stay within O(|W⃗|) of ± the identity, and that proposition, with
(i)–(ii), holds for (L_(h,p⃗), D_(p⃗)P_4) at small p⃗; this is the form used below.

*The map.* For W⃗ put F(W⃗) := F − D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(W⃗); by Lemma 32.36 (b) it lies in the space 𝒴(α′) of
Section 32.6, so Proposition 32.29 gives q⃗(W⃗) := p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α′)(F(W⃗)) ∈ 𝒫_(α′), and the forward solution u(W⃗) of

    L_(h,p⃗)u(W⃗) = F(W⃗) − D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(q⃗(W⃗))

lies in (32.26) at α′. Write D_(p⃗)P_4(q⃗) = f^S(q_S) + f^b(q_b) + f^s1(q_s1) + Σ_(ν∈ℳ_(α′)) f^ν(q_ν), and use
Lemma 32.36 (c) (the base point has black hole parameter b_0), f^ν = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν + r^ν, for every row. Then

    u(W⃗) = u_0(W⃗) − Σ_(ν∈𝒩′) m_ν(W_ν) − Σ_(ν∈ℳ_(α′)) m_ν(q_ν(W⃗)),

where u_0(W⃗) is the forward solution of L_(h,p⃗)u_0 = G(W⃗),

    G(W⃗) := F − Σ_(ν∈𝒩′) r^ν(W_ν) − f^S(q_S) − f^b(q_b) − f^s1(q_s1) − Σ_(ν∈ℳ_(α′)) r^ν(q_ν) ∈ 𝒴⁰(α)

(Section 33.2: r^ν ∈ 𝒴_2(α) without index set, f^S, f^s1 ∈ 𝒴⁰(α), f^b ∈ 𝒴⁰_2(α)). u_0(W⃗) = u(W⃗) + Σ m_ν has
the K⁺-weight min(α′ − 2, λ_♯ − 1) − ε > 0 and the other properties of the hypothesis of Lemma 33.16 (the m_ν
have ι⁺-weight λ_♯ > 3/2). By Lemma 33.16 (at b_0, where u^rot is put into ũ),

    u(W⃗) = Σ_(ν∈𝒩) m_ν(C_ν(W⃗)) + ũ,

with C_ν(W⃗) := S^(h,p⃗)_ν(G(W⃗)) − W_ν for ν ∈ 𝒩′ and C_ν(W⃗) := S^(h,p⃗)_ν(G(W⃗)) − q_ν(W⃗) for ν ∈ ℳ_(α′). As u(W⃗)
lies in (32.26) at α′, the coefficients C_ν(W⃗), ν ∈ ℳ_(α′), vanish by Corollary 33.6: the rows of
K⁺-rate below α′ − 2 are exactly those of ℳ_(α′) (the s0, s2, c0, c1 rows have rates at least λ_♯ > 1 > α′ − 2, every
s1 row of rate above α′ − 2 is in 𝒩′, and none has rate α′ − 2, by admissibility in the sense of Section 32.6), so
Σ_(ν∈ℳ_(α′)) m_ν(C_ν(W⃗)), the difference of u(W⃗) and terms of K⁺-weight above α′ − 2, has K⁺-weight α′ − 2 − ε. So
u(W⃗) satisfies (33.13) at α if and only if C_ν(W⃗) = 0 for ν ∈ 𝒩′ (by Corollary 33.6 again, all rates
being at most 2 < α − 2; ũ and the m_ν have the ι⁺- and ℐ⁺-data of (33.13)).

*At (0, 0).* Here r^ν = 0, and q⃗(W⃗) does not depend on W⃗: F(W⃗) = F − Σ L_(b_0)m_ν(W_ν), and the forward solution
m_ν(W_ν) of L_(b_0)m = L_(b_0)m_ν(W_ν) lies in (32.26) at α′ for ν ∈ 𝒩′ (its rate is at least α′ − 2 and
differs from it, by admissibility; Lemma 32.32), so p⃗′_(0,0,α′)(L_(b_0)m_ν(W_ν)) = 0 by the uniqueness at α′.
Hence G(W⃗) = G(0) and C(W⃗) = C(0) − W⃗ on 𝒩′: the equation has the unique solution W⃗ = S^(0,0)(G(0)).

*Near (0, 0).* C(W⃗) = C(0) − T_(h,p⃗)W⃗ with T_(h,p⃗)W⃗ := W⃗ − S^(h,p⃗)(G(W⃗) − G(0)), linear on the
finite-dimensional space of the W⃗. G(W⃗) − G(0) = −Σ r^ν(W_ν) − (the q⃗-terms of q⃗(W⃗) − q⃗(0)); the first is
O(|W⃗|(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)) in 𝒴_2(α) ((32.35)), and q⃗(W⃗) − q⃗(0) = −p⃗′_(h,p⃗,α′)(D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(W⃗)) tends to
−p⃗′_(0,0,α′)(Σ L_(b_0)m_ν(W_ν)) = 0 as (h, p⃗) → (0, 0), for fixed W⃗ (Proposition 32.29 (ii), with
Lemma 32.36 (b)–(d) for the convergence of the sources in 𝒴(α′)). Now S^(h,p⃗)(G(W⃗) − G(0)) are the
coefficients of u_0(W⃗) − u_0(0), and the bound of Lemma 33.16 with w = w_0 gives

    |S^(h,p⃗)(G(W⃗) − G(0))| ≤ C‖G(W⃗) − G(0)‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u_0(W⃗) − u_0(0)‖_(w_0).

The first term tends to 0 for fixed W⃗, by the above, the q⃗-terms being linear in q⃗ with bounds uniform for (h, p⃗)
small (Lemma 32.36 (a), (c), (d)). For the second, u_0(W⃗) − u_0(0) = u(W⃗) − u(0) + Σ_(ν∈𝒩′) m_ν(W_ν) +
Σ_(ν∈ℳ_(α′)) m_ν(q_ν(W⃗) − q_ν(0)), and u(W⃗) − u(0) is the solution of (32.25) at α′ for the forcing
F(W⃗) − F(0) = −D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(W⃗), of size O(|W⃗|) in 𝒴(α′) (Lemma 32.36 (b)). So Proposition 32.29 (i) at α′
bounds q⃗(W⃗) − q⃗(0) by C|W⃗|, and u(W⃗) − u(0) by C|W⃗| in the seminorm ‖·‖_(α′) of Section 32.6, taken as in the
proof of Lemma 33.17 with w_0 for w and with its ε at most that of ‖·‖_(w_0), which then bounds ‖·‖_(w_0) as
w_0 ≤ α′ − 2; and ‖m_ν(W)‖_(w_0) ≤ C|W| for every row, m_ν(W) having K⁺-weight at least λ_♯ − 1 − ε ≥ w_0 − ε and
ι⁺-weight λ_♯ − ε (Lemma 32.32). So the second term is O((‖h‖ + |p⃗|)|W⃗|), T_(h,p⃗)W⃗ → W⃗ for every W⃗, and on
the finite-dimensional space of the W⃗, T_(h,p⃗) → id; so T_(h,p⃗) is invertible for (h, p⃗) small,
with |T⁻¹_(h,p⃗)| ≤ 2. Put W⃗ := T_(h,p⃗)⁻¹C(0) and p⃗′ := q⃗(W⃗) ⊕ W⃗. The conjugation symmetry is preserved, as L and
F are real and T commutes with the conjugation of Section 32.10.

*Uniqueness.* If p⃗″ also gives (33.13) at α, its solution lies in (32.26) at α′, so its
𝒫_(α′)-part is q⃗(W⃗″) by the uniqueness at α′ (Proposition 32.29), where W⃗″ is its 𝒩′-part; then C(W⃗″) = 0, so
W⃗″ = W⃗. *Linearity, bounds, continuity:* linearity holds by construction. With the seminorm ‖·‖_(α′) taken as
above, let ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) be the seminorm of Proposition 32.29 (i) at α′ for it, and write ‖F‖ for a seminorm of
𝒴⁰(α) of large enough regularity (Section 32.6): it bounds ‖F‖_(𝒴⁰(α)), and F lies in 𝒴(α′) with
‖F‖^+_(𝒴(α′)) ≤ C‖F‖. By (i) at α′, |q⃗(0)| ≤ C‖F‖ and ‖u(0)‖_(α′) ≤ C‖F‖; so ‖G(0)‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) ≤ C‖F‖ and, as
above, ‖u_0(0)‖_(w_0) ≤ C‖F‖. The bound of Lemma 33.16 then gives |C(0)| ≤ C‖F‖, so |W⃗| ≤ 2|C(0)| ≤ C‖F‖,
and (i) at α′ for the forcing F(W⃗), of size at most C‖F‖ in ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α′)), gives |q⃗(W⃗)| ≤ C‖F‖ and
‖u(W⃗)‖_(α′) ≤ C‖F‖. So |p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(F)| ≤ C‖F‖, and likewise ‖G(W⃗)‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) ≤ C‖F‖ and ‖u_0(W⃗)‖_(w_0) ≤ C‖F‖, with
C uniform for (h, p⃗) small. Continuity at (0, 0) as in Proposition 32.29 (ii), with Lemma 33.17 at b_0,
whose hypothesis (the solutions u_0 bounded) these bounds give. ∎

At a base point with black hole parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, the elimination is Proposition 36.8 with q = 0: when
h_(b,v1) ≠ 0 the v1 terms u^rot of Lemma 33.16 are not removed by the parameters of 𝒫, whose v1 rows carry the
coefficient space 0, and the parameter space is enlarged by the rotation rows of Definition 34.3, whose coordinates
are assigned (Definition 36.6).

### 33.9 Towers with coefficients

From here on α ∈ (4, 4 + ε_K] is admissible, ℓ_3 = α − 4 − ε, and η_1 < η_2 in (ε_K, ε_+), ℰ_col and the pieces of
Proposition 33.15 are as in Section 33.5–Section 33.8. We take η_2 ∈ (ε_+ − δ_+, ε_+) for a number
δ_+ ∈ (0, ε_+ − ε_K) fixed in advance (Section 33.5 allows any η_2 ∈ (ε_K, ε_+) off a finite set), so that the
ι⁺-order 3 + η_2 − 2ε below is as close to 3 + ε_+ as desired.

**Definition 33.19** (Coefficients; [Hin26, Definition 11.58].) For an index set E ⊂ ℂ × ℕ₀, w ∈ ℝ and a
finite-dimensional space Z, Ḣ^(∞,𝒬(E,w))_b([1, ∞]; Z) is the space of the a ∈ C^∞(ℝ; Z) supported in [1, ∞) with

    a − χ_+(t_*) Σ_((z,k)∈E, Re z<w) c_(z,k) t_*^(−z)(log t_*)^k ∈ t_*^(−w) H^∞_b([1, ∞), |dt_*/t_*|; Z),
    c_(z,k) ∈ Z,    (33.14)

where χ_+ ∈ C^∞(ℝ) vanishes on (−∞, 1] and equals 1 on [2, ∞); Ḣ^(∞,w)_b := Ḣ^(∞,𝒬(∅,w))_b. As t_*∂_(t_*) preserves
these spaces, a^((j)) ∈ Ḣ^(∞,𝒬(E+j,w+j))_b.

*Towers.* The rows of the table of roots of Section 26.10 are the pairs ψ = (μ, τ) with roots μ ∈ (−3, 0] and
coefficient spaces 𝒴_ψ (the spaces of the coefficients Y^(μ)_τ). Let ℛ be the set of these rows and ℛ′ the set without
the boost row (−1, s1). For a valued in 𝒴_ψ let T_ψ(a) := h^((μ),≤k_μ)_(b,τ)(a) (Definition 26.37), with

    T_v1(a) := h^(≤2)_(b,v1)(a) = Σ_(j≤2) a^((j)) h̆^j_(b,v1),     h̆⁰_(b,v1) := h_(b,v1),

for the rotations, and h^(≤1)_(b,s1)(a) = h_(b,s1)(a) + h̆¹_(b,s1)(a′) for the boosts. The *spectral tower* of ψ is
T_ψ(σ)Y := Σ_(j≤k_μ) (−iσ)^j h̆^((μ),j)_(b,τ)(Y), so that ℱ(T_ψ(a)) = T_ψ(σ)â(σ) for a independent of x. By
Section 26.11 and Lemma 30.2 (P3), h̆^((μ),j)_(b,τ) is polyhomogeneous at ∂X with the leading order ρ^(μ−j)
(it grows like r^(j−μ)), independent of b, the Myers–Perry corrections being smaller by min Re ℰ_ind > 0. For the
boosts h_(b,s1) ∈ 𝒜³ and h̆¹_(b,s1) ∈ 𝒜² (Section 28.2), and h̆^j_(b,s1), j ≥ 2, has the leading order ρ^(1−j). For
the rotations h̆^j_(b,v1), j ≥ 1, has the leading order ρ^(−j), and h_(b,v1) ∈ 𝒜³ vanishes when b = b_0. We write
d_ψ := μ for the rows other than the boosts and rotations, d_v1 := 0, and d_s1 := 1 for h^(≤k)_(b,s1), k ≥ 2. Then for
a = t_*^(−z) the leading part of T_ψ(a) is homogeneous of degree −z − d_ψ in (t_*, r), so that its K⁺-rate is z (for
v1, z when h_(b,v1) ≠ 0 and z + 1 when h_(b,v1) = 0) and its order at ι⁺ is z + d_ψ; for h^(≤1)_(b,s1)(a) the order at
ι⁺ is z + 3.

*Rates.* For a ∈ Ḣ^(∞,w)_b and ψ ≠ v1, χ_K T_ψ(a) has K⁺-order w, and the term with a^((j)) has K⁺-order w + j; so the
terms with j ≥ 2 of a coefficient of order above α − 2 are of order above α, and the lengths k_μ are immaterial for the
statements below ([Hin26, Remark 11.60 (2)]).

*The index set at ι⁺.* Let

    ℰ_♯ := {(λ, k) : λ ∈ Λ, Re λ ≥ 2, k ≤ k̄(λ)} ∪ ℳ

(Definition 33.1; ℳ is (32.17), the part of ℰ_++ below 2). It is an index set closed under conjugation,
with min Re ℰ_♯ ≥ λ_♯ and ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re < 2} = ℳ. Below 2 it keeps the logarithmic orders of ℰ_++, which the exponents below
2 produced in Section 33.4 carry (Lemma 33.2 (c)); k̄(λ) > k̄_0 would admit more. As ℰ_++ is closed under
the addition of ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind ((32.16)), ℳ + (ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind) lies in ℳ below 2, and above 2 its
logarithmic orders are at most k̄_0 + l_* ≤ k̄. By Lemma 33.2 (b) the part of ℰ_♯ of real part below 3 + ε_+
does not depend on ℰ_+, so ℰ_+ ⊃ ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re < 3 + ε_+} can be required together with (H1)–(H3) ([Hin26, Remark 11.62]).
ℰ_♯ does not depend on b.

### 33.10 The lemmas of the expansion

Let χ ∈ C_c^∞((−1, 1)) be the low frequency cut-off of Section 33.7 (equal to 1 near [−½, ½]), and
χ_zf = χ_0(r̂) with χ_0 ∈ C_c^∞([0, 1)) equal to 1 near 0, so that k := ℱ⁻¹[χ_0(|ζ|)] is a Schwartz function with
∫ k = 1 and ∫ s^m k(s) ds = 0 for m ≥ 1 (these are the derivatives at 0 of χ_0(|ζ|), which is 1 near 0). A *profile*
of *degree* d is a section p on X, conormal at ∂X, with |p| ≲ r^(−d)⟨log r⟩^l for r ≥ 1 and some l, with
b-derivatives; it is *polyhomogeneous* if it is so at ∂X, with leading order ρ^d. The profiles of Theorem 33.24
are in general only polyhomogeneous to a finite order (for instance û_2 and û_3 of Proposition 33.15, and v_0 below),
and some carry a factor log r.

**Lemma 33.20** (The cut-off as an approximate identity.) Let p_0, …, p_k be profiles of degrees
d_j ≥ d − j, P(σ, x) := Σ_j (−iσ)^j p_j(x), and let c = Σ_± 1_(±σ>0)c^± with either (a) c^± ∈
H^(∞,w)_b(±(0, 1), |dσ/σ|), w > −1, or (b) c = |σ|^z(log|σ|)^m sgn(σ)^δ, Re z > −1 (and then w := Re z). Put
y := ℱ⁻¹(χc). Then on {t_* ≥ 1}

    ℱ⁻¹[χ(|σ|)χ_zf(|σ|r)c(σ)P(σ, x)] = χ_K Σ_j (χ_+y)^((j))(t_*) p_j(x) + R,    (33.15)

where R has K⁺-order ∞ (for every N, |R| ≲ (r/t_*)^N t_*^(−w−1)⟨r⟩^(−d) on {r ≤ t_*/8}, up to logarithms, with
b-derivatives) and, near ι⁺, the order w + 1 + d. In case (b), if the p_j are polyhomogeneous, R and
χ_K Σ_j (χ_+y)^((j))p_j are polyhomogeneous at ι⁺, with the exponents z + 1 + d plus those of the expansions of the p_j
(and logarithms up to m); and if p_j = p^ph_j + p^c_j with p^ph_j polyhomogeneous and p^c_j of degree at least d′ − j,
the part from the p^c_j has the order Re z + 1 + d′ at ι⁺; and χ_+y ∈ Ḣ^(∞,𝒬((z+1,m),∞))_b. In case (a),
χ_+y ∈ Ḣ^(∞,w+1)_b.

*Proof.* y satisfies the symbol estimates |(t∂_t)^l y^((j))(t)| ≲ ⟨t⟩^(−w−1−j) (Proposition 20.20 (1) in case (a);
in case (b), y is c_±|t|^(−z−1) times polynomials in log|t| plus a Schwartz function as t → ±∞), so χ_+y lies in the
stated classes. For every x the left side of (33.15) is Σ_j (y^((j)) + e_(j,r))(t_*)p_j(x) (as
ℱ(a′) = −iσâ), with e_(j,r) := ℱ⁻¹[(−iσ)^j χc(χ_0(|σ|r) − 1)]. Let χ_0 = 1 on [0, c_0]. The symbol of e_(j,r) vanishes
for |σ| ≤ c_0/r, so e_(j,r) = 0 for r < c_0; for r ≥ c_0 it satisfies |∂^l_σ[(−iσ)^j χc(χ_0(|σ|r) − 1)]|
≲ |σ|^(j+w−l) on its support, as ∂^l_σ[χ_0(|σ|r)] = r^l χ_0^((l))(|σ|r) sgn(σ)^l lives
where |σ|r ≤ 1, and the jump of c at σ = 0 lies outside the support. Integrating by parts M > j + w + 1 times,

    |e_(j,r)(t)| ≲ |t|^(−M) ∫_(|σ|≥c_0/r) |σ|^(j+w−M) dσ ≲ |t|^(−M) r^(M−j−w−1) = (r/|t|)^(M−j−w−1)|t|^(−j−w−1),

and likewise with b-derivatives (t∂_t and r∂_r preserve this symbol class). On {r ≤ t_*/8}, where χ_K = χ_+ = 1 for
t_* ≥ 2, R = Σ_j e_(j,r)p_j for t_* ≥ 2; with |p_j| ≲ ⟨r⟩^(j−d) (up to logarithms) this
gives |R| ≲ (r/t)^N t^(−w−1)⟨r⟩^(−d) for every N, and the b-derivatives alike. For r ≥ 2, χ = 1 on the support of
χ_0(|σ|r), and the left side is Σ_j (y^((j)) ∗ k_r)(t_*)p_j(x), with k_r(s) := r⁻¹k(s/r). On {r ≥ t_*/8}, r ≥ 2, the
substitution σ = ζ/r gives

    (y^((j)) ∗ k_r)(t) = r^(−1−j) ∫ e^(−iζt/r) χ_0(|ζ|)(−iζ)^j c(ζ/r) dζ/(2π),

of size r^(−1−j−w) uniformly in t/r (by the symbol estimates of c); so the left side is O(r^(−1−w−d)) there, and so is
χ_K Σ_j (χ_+y)^((j))p_j (χ_K vanishes for r ≥ t_*/2, and |y^((j))p_j| ≲ t^(−w−1−j)r^(j−d)); this is the order
w + 1 + d at ι⁺. In case (b) the left side is, for r ≥ 2, r^(−1−z) times a smooth function of t/r (with factors log r
