up to the power m) times the p_j (the conormal parts p^c_j giving the order Re z + 1 + d′), and
χ_K Σ_j (χ_+y)^((j))p_j is a function of t_*, polyhomogeneous at t_* = ∞, times χ_c(r/t_*) and the p_j; both are
polyhomogeneous at ι⁺ (in the coordinates t_*⁻¹, r/t_*) with the stated exponents. ∎

**Lemma 33.21** (The columns at the last level.) Let a > −1, S ∈ H^(∞,a)_b(±(0, 1), |dσ/σ|; 𝒮_(1,ℂ)),
ḃ ∈ H^(∞,a)_b(±(0, 1), |dσ/σ|; 𝔟_ℂ), and put A := χ_+ℱ⁻¹[−χσS] ∈ Ḣ^(∞,a+2)_b and B := χ_+ℱ⁻¹[iχσ²ḃ] ∈
Ḣ^(∞,a+3)_b. Then on {t_* ≥ 1}

    ℱ⁻¹[χσ³ĥ^aug(σ)(S)] = χ_K h^(≤1)_(b,s1)(A) + R_S,          ℱ⁻¹[χσ³ĝ^aug(σ)(ḃ)] = χ_K ġ(B) + R_b,    (33.16)

with R_S, R_b of K⁺-order a + 4 and of order a + 5 at ι⁺.

*Proof.* By (28.8), σ³ĥ^aug(S) = −σΨh(S) + σ²(∂_σΨ)h(S) + iσ²Ψh̆(S) and σ³ĝ^aug(ḃ) = iσ²Ψġ(ḃ), where
Ψ(σ, x) = ∫ e^(iσt)φ_x(t) dt, φ_x := ∂_(t_*)χ_K(·, x), ∫ φ_x = 1; for r ≥ 1, φ_x(t) = r⁻¹φ(t/r) with
φ(s) = ∂_s[χ_c(1/s)] supported in [2, 4] (Lemma 28.5 (b)), and for r ≤ 1, φ_x is supported in [1, 4]. Products
with Ψ and ∂_σΨ are convolutions in t with φ_x and with itφ_x(t). With a_0 := ℱ⁻¹[−χσS] (so that
ℱ⁻¹[χσ²S] = −ia′_0), the left side of the first identity is

    h(S)(∫ (a_0(t − τ) + τa′_0(t − τ))φ_x(τ) dτ) + h̆(S)(∫ a′_0(t − τ)φ_x(τ) dτ)

(S applied to the scalar coefficients). By Taylor's formula, a_0(t − τ) + τa′_0(t − τ) =
a_0(t) − τ² ∫_0^1 s a″_0(t − sτ) ds (the first moments cancel) and a′_0(t − τ) = a′_0(t) − τ ∫_0^1 a″_0(t − sτ) ds; as
τ ≤ 4 max(r, 1) on supp φ_x, on {r ≤ t_*/8} the remainder is bounded by
max(r, 1)²t^(−a−4)|h| + max(r, 1)t^(−a−4)|h̆| ≲ t^(−a−4)r⁻¹ (h ∈ 𝒜³, h̆ ∈ 𝒜²), with b-derivatives: K⁺-order a + 4. On
{r ≥ t_*/8}, r ≥ 2, the right side is O(t^(−a−2)r⁻³ + t^(−a−3)r⁻²) (χ_K vanishes for r ≥ t_*/2), and the left side is
O(r^(−a−5)): for r ≥ 1, Ψ = Φ(σr) and ∂_σΨ = rΦ′(σr) with Φ a Schwartz function (Lemma 28.5 (b)), and the
substitution σ = ζ/r gives

    ℱ⁻¹[χσΦ(σr)S], ℱ⁻¹[χσ²rΦ′(σr)S] = O(r^(−2−a)),          ℱ⁻¹[χσ²Φ(σr)S] = O(r^(−3−a))

uniformly in t/r (by the symbol estimates of S, as in the proof of Lemma 33.20), with h ∈ 𝒜³, h̆ ∈ 𝒜²: the
order a + 5 at ι⁺. Replacing a_0 by A = χ_+a_0 changes the right side only for t_* ≤ 2, where χ_K is supported in
{r ≤ 1}. The second identity is proved in the same way, with b_0 := ℱ⁻¹[iχσ²ḃ] and ġ ∈ 𝒜²:

    ∫ b_0(t − τ)φ_x(τ) dτ = b_0(t) − ∫ τ ∫_0^1 b′_0(t − sτ) ds φ_x(τ) dτ,

the remainder being O(max(r, 1)t^(−a−4)r⁻²), and ℱ⁻¹[iχσ²Φ(σr)ḃ] = O(r^(−3−a)) on {r ≥ t_*/8}. ∎

*Stationary solutions.* Let L_0 := L̂_b(0), L_1 = [L_b, t_*] and L_2 = ½[[L_b, t_*], t_*] (Section 31.10), so that
L_b(a(t_*)p) = aL_0p + a′L_1p + a″L_2p for stationary p, and a tower Σ_j a^((j)) h̆^j satisfies

    L_0h̆^m + L_1h̆^(m−1) + L_2h̆^(m−2) = 0

for m up to its length ((26.45)). In particular the bottom h̆^((μ),0)_(b,τ)(Y) of each row of ℛ′ other than
v1 lies in ker L_0, and so do h_(b,s1)(S) and ġ(ḃ); at b_0 so does h̆¹_(b_0,v1)(V), as h_(b_0,v1) = 0. The following two
lemmas are stated at b_0; their forms at every b ∈ ℬ̄_* are Lemma 33.32.

**Lemma 33.22** (Stationary solutions of moderate growth.) Let b = b_0. Let 𝒢_* be the space of sections on
X that are conormal at ∂X of some order above −3 (in 𝒜^a, a > −3); write h := h_(b_0,s1) and h̆^j := h̆^j_(b_0,s1).

(a) If p ∈ 𝒢_* and L_0p = 0, then p = Σ_ψ h̆^((μ_ψ),0)_(b_0,τ_ψ)(Y_ψ) + h̆¹_(b_0,v1)(V) + ġ(ḃ) + h(S), the sum over the
rows of ℛ′ other than v1, with unique coefficients; the rows with μ_ψ < −s do not occur if p = O(r^s).

(b) If X ∈ 𝒢_*, ḃ ∈ 𝔟_ℂ, S ∈ 𝒮_(1,ℂ) and L_0X = L_1ġ(ḃ) + L_1h̆¹(S) + L_2h(S), then ḃ = 0, and the s1-component of
the ρ⁻¹-coefficient of the reduced section (below: X after the subtraction of the states of lower root) is that of
h̆²(−S). In particular L_1ġ(ḃ) ∈ L_0(𝒢_*) only for ḃ = 0, and the reduction of an element of ker L_0 ∩ 𝒢_* subtracts no
growing boost section h̆²(S′), S′ ≠ 0.

*Proof.* *The reduction.* Let X ∈ 𝒢_* with L_0X ∈ 𝒜³. As L_0 = ρ²A with A b-elliptic (Section 25.6) and
ρ⁻²L_0X ∈ 𝒜¹, Lemma 21.35 (stated on H^(∞,α)_b; passing from 𝒜^a costs an ε in the weight, which is immaterial
here) makes X polyhomogeneous modulo 𝒜^(1−ε), with exponents in the indicial roots of real part in (a, 1) plus ℕ₀; a
logarithm can occur only where a root meets a lower one plus an integer, so the lowest exponent carries none, the roots
being simple. Let μ_0 be the least real part of an exponent of X, and suppose μ_0 ≤ 0. As every indicial root is simple
(Section 26.10), the argument of the proof of Theorem 26.39 (the lowest term) applies: the top logarithm at μ_0
vanishes, μ_0 is a root in 𝒲 (real), and the ρ^(μ_0)-coefficient is Σ_τ h̄_τ(Y_τ) (Lemma 26.32). Subtract, for
every type, the element of ker L_0 listed above with this leading term (for v1 at −1, h̆¹_(b_0,v1)(V)), and for s1 at −1
the section h̆²(S′), h̄_s1(S′) being the s1-component; then μ_0 rises (the corrections of the states are smaller by
min Re ℰ_ind), and L_0 of the new section is the old one plus L_1h̆¹(S′) + L_2h(S′) (the tower relation
L_0h̆² + L_1h̆¹ + L_2h = 0). After finitely many steps all exponents have real part above 0; as there are no roots in
(0, 1] (Proposition 25.6 (a)) and ρ⁻²L_0X ∈ 𝒜¹, the result lies in 𝒜¹.

(b) By the reduction, X = X_1 + (elements of ker L_0 ∩ 𝒢_*) + h̆²(S′) with X_1 ∈ 𝒜¹ and
L_0X_1 = L_1ġ(ḃ) + L_1h̆¹(S + S′) + L_2h(S + S′), h̄_s1(S′) being the s1-component of the ρ⁻¹-coefficient of the
section reached at the root −1. By (28.4), f̂_ḃ(0) = L_1ġ(ḃ) + L_0w_ḃ and f̂_(S″)(0) = L_2h(S″) +
L_1h̆¹(S″) + L_0w_(S″) with w_ḃ, w_(S″) ∈ 𝒜¹ (Lemma 28.3); so f̂_ḃ(0) + f̂_(S+S′)(0) = L_0Q with
Q := X_1 + w_ḃ + w_(S+S′) ∈ 𝒜¹, which lies in the space 𝒳_0 of Chapter 28 (of conormal order in (0, 1)). Choose
u_e ∈ ker L_0 ∩ 𝒳_0 with r(u_e) = −r(Q) (possible by the normalisation (28.9) of the rows f*_1, f*_2 of
L̃_(b_0)(0)). Then L̃_(b_0)(0)(−Q − u_e, ḃ, S + S′) = (0, 0), and Proposition 28.8 gives ḃ = 0 and S′ = −S.

(a) The reduction of p ends in p_1 ∈ 𝒜¹ ∩ ker L_0 once S′ = 0, which is (b) with ḃ = 0 and S = 0. Then p_1 ∈ 𝒜^(2−)
(the next roots are at least 2) lies in the domain of Proposition 25.30 for a small weight, whose nullspace (1) is
spanned by ġ(ḃ) and h(S). Uniqueness: Y ↦ h̄_τ(Y) is injective (Lemma 26.32), and that nullspace is
eleven-dimensional. The last statement: a state of root μ grows like r^(−μ). ∎

**Lemma 33.23** (Formal solutions at K⁺.) Let b = b_0, β ∈ (α − 1, α], and

    w = χ_K Σ_(i∈I) y_i(t_*)p_i(x) + w′,    (33.17)

with I finite, conormal profiles p_i of degrees d_i (not necessarily in 𝒢_*: the companions h̆^((μ),1) of the rows with
μ ∈ (−3, −2] have degree at most −3), y_i ∈ Ḣ^(∞,𝒬(E_i,∞))_b with every (z, k) ∈ E_i satisfying Re z ≥ β − 2 and
Re z + d_i ≥ λ_♯ (*compatibility*), and w′ of K⁺-order β. If L_(b_0)w has K⁺-order β, then

    χ_K Σ_i y_i p_i = χ_K(Σ_(ψ∈ℛ′) T_ψ(a_ψ) + h^(≤1)_(b_0,s1)(a_s) + ġ(a_b)) + w″,    (33.18)

where a_ψ, a_s, a_b are finite sums of terms χ_+t_*^(−z)(log t_*)^k, with exponents in ⋃_i E_i + ℕ₀ (for a_v1,
⋃_i E_i + ℕ₀ − 1), those of a_ψ satisfying Re z + d_ψ ≥ λ_♯ and those of a_b of real part at least β − 1, and w″ has
K⁺-order β; all are linear in (y_i). *Exponents.* Let ℐ_* be the set of the (z + e, k + l), (z, k) ∈ E_i, (e, l) an
exponent of the polyhomogeneous part of p_i (i ∈ I). For every exponent (z, k) of a_ψ such that d_ψ lies below the
degree of the conormal (non-polyhomogeneous) part of every p_i whose coefficient c^((i))_(z,k) in the proof is nonzero,
(z + d_ψ, k) is an element of ℐ_* plus finitely many elements of ℰ_ind.

*Proof.* We remove the pairs (z, k) with Re z < β one at a time, in order of increasing real part and, at equal
exponent, of decreasing k. Let (z_0, k_0) be the first pair whose coefficient section P := Σ_i c^((i))_(z_0,k_0)p_i is
nonzero, c^((i))_(z,k) being the coefficient of t_*^(−z)(log t_*)^k in y_i. In {r ≤ R}, for large t_*, χ_K = 1 and
L_(b_0)(yp) = yL_0p + y′L_1p + y″L_2p, and y′, y″ have the exponents (z + 1, ·), (z + 2, ·); so the coefficient of
t_*^(−z_0)(log t_*)^(k_0) in L_(b_0)w is L_0P, which vanishes, L_(b_0)w and w′ being of K⁺-order β > Re z_0 on every
{r ≤ R}. By compatibility P = O(r^(Re z_0−λ_♯)), with Re z_0 − λ_♯ < β − λ_♯ < 3, so P ∈ 𝒢_*, and
Lemma 33.22 (a) gives P = Σ_ψ h̆^((μ_ψ),0)(Y_ψ) + h̆¹_(b_0,v1)(V) + ġ(ḃ) + h_(b_0,s1)(S) with only rows
μ_ψ ≥ λ_♯ − Re z_0.

*If Re z_0 + 1 < β, then ḃ = 0.* The coefficient of t_*^(−z_0−1)(log t_*)^(k_0) in L_(b_0)w is L_0P_1 − z_0L_1P, P_1
being the coefficient section of (z_0 + 1, k_0) (the pairs (z_0, k), k > k_0, have zero coefficient, and none has real
part below Re z_0), and it vanishes. With the tower relations L_1h̆^((μ),0) = −L_0h̆^((μ),1),
L_1h_(b_0,s1) = −L_0h̆¹_(b_0,s1) and L_1h̆¹_(b_0,v1) = −L_0h̆²_(b_0,v1) (all these rows have k_μ ≥ 1, below),
z_0L_1ġ(ḃ) ∈ L_0(𝒢_*), and z_0 ≠ 0; Lemma 33.22 (b) gives ḃ = 0.

*Subtraction.* Let a := χ_+t_*^(−z_0)(log t_*)^(k_0), and let ã be the polyhomogeneous antiderivative with ã′ = a on
[2, ∞) (exponents (z_0 − 1, ≤ k_0); z_0 ≠ 1 as Re z_0 ≥ β − 2 > 1), and subtract

    w_1 := χ_K(Σ_ψ T_ψ(aY_ψ) + T_v1(ãV) + h^(≤1)_(b_0,s1)(aS) + ġ(aḃ)).

Then w − w_1 is again of the form (33.17): the pair (z_0, k_0) is gone, and the new terms a^((j))h̆^((μ),j),
j ≥ 1, have the exponents (z_0 + j, ≤ k_0), later in the order, and are compatible (z_0 + j with degree μ − j;
h_(b_0,s1) and h̆¹_(b_0,s1) have the degrees 3 and 2). And L_(b_0)w_1 has K⁺-order β: by the tower relations,
L_(b_0)T_ψ(aY) consists of the terms with a^((k_μ+1)) and a^((k_μ+2)) (Lemma 26.38), of K⁺-order
Re z_0 + k_μ + 1; the rows with μ > −2 have k_μ ≥ 1 (the table of Section 26.10), and Re z_0 + 2 ≥ β; rows with
μ ≤ −2 occur only if Re z_0 ≥ λ_♯ + 2 > β − 1; L_(b_0)h^(≤1)_(b_0,s1)(aS) and L_(b_0)T_v1(ãV) involve a″ and higher;
L_(b_0)ġ(aḃ) = a′L_1ġ + a″L_2ġ, with ḃ = 0 unless Re z_0 + 1 ≥ β; and [L_(b_0), χ_K] is supported in
{t_*/4 ≤ r ≤ t_*/2}, away from K⁺. There are finitely many pairs with real part below β, so the process ends;
collecting the subtracted coefficients gives (33.18).

*Exponents.* The ρ^(μ_ψ)-coefficient of P is that of Σ_i c^((i))_(z_0,k_0)p_i less the corrections of the states of
lower root removed in the reduction of Lemma 33.22, which lie at those roots plus elements of ℰ_ind; so
(z_0 + μ_ψ, k_0) is (z_0 + e, k_0) for an exponent e of some p_i, or of a companion subtracted earlier, plus elements of
ℰ_ind (a companion a^((j))h̆^((μ),j) has the exponent z + j and the degree μ − j, so the same sum z + μ); for v1 the
exponent of ã is z_0 − 1, with d_v1 = 0 and μ_v1 = −1. ∎

### 33.11 The expansion modulo the order α

This section is [Hin26, Theorem 11.59, Part 4 of the proof, (11.196), and the ι⁺-part of (11.222)] in dimension 4 + 1.
In it, b = b_0: F ∈ 𝒴⁰(α), (h, p⃗) is a small base point with black hole parameter b_0, p⃗′ is as in
Theorem 33.18, and u is the forward solution of L_(h,p⃗)u = F − D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(p⃗′). The form at every
b ∈ ℬ̄_* is Corollary 33.33.

**Theorem 33.24** (The expansion at K⁺.) For every small ε > 0,

    u = χ_K u_exp + ũ,     u_exp = h^(≤1)_(b_0,s1)(Ṡ_rem) + ġ(ḃ_rem) + Σ_(ψ∈ℛ′) T_ψ(Ẏ_ψ),    (33.19)

with

    Ṡ_rem ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−2−ε)_b([1, ∞]; 𝒮_(1,ℂ)),     ḃ_rem ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−1−ε)_b([1, ∞]; 𝔟_ℂ),
    Ẏ_ψ ∈ Ḣ^(∞,𝒬(ℰ_♯−d_ψ, w_ψ))_b([1, ∞]; 𝒴_ψ),    (33.20)

w_ψ := 3 + η_2 − 2ε − d_ψ for every ψ ∈ ℛ′ (d_v1 = 0), and

    ũ ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(ℰ_♯,3+η_2−2ε),α−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−).    (33.21)

The coefficients are conjugation-symmetric (u being real), linear and continuous in F, with bounds uniform for (h, p⃗)
small. Each term of χ_K u_exp has K⁺-order at least α − 2 − ε, so (33.19) contains the bound
u = O(t_*^(−α+2+ε)) in compact sets of Theorem 33.18; and L_(b_0)(χ_K u_exp) has K⁺-order α − ε ([Hin26, Remark
11.60 (1) and (11.232)]).

The polyhomogeneous parts of the Ẏ_ψ come from the ι⁺-terms of u: an ι⁺-exponent λ gives the coefficient t_*^(−λ+d_ψ)
(Lemma 33.20 (b), (26.55)), hence the index set ℰ_♯ − d_ψ. Their conormal parts, present only for the
rows with μ ∈ (−1, 0] (d_ψ = μ), come from the last Taylor level and have order at least 3 + η_2 − 2ε − μ. The boosts
and the black hole parameters carry only conormal coefficients, of the orders α − 2 − ε and α − 1 − ε, as in [Hin26].
The coefficients of v1 and of the rows with μ ≤ −1 are finite sums of terms χ_+t_*^(−z)(log t_*)^k, so they lie in
these spaces for every w_ψ; the choice of w_ψ makes the ι⁺-order of every χ_K T_ψ(Ẏ_ψ) at least 3 + η_2 − 2ε, as in
[Hin26, (11.227b)].

*Proof.* *Step 0 (the decomposition).* As in the proof of Theorem 33.18, u = u_0 − Σ_ν m_ν(S_ν), where u_0 is
the forward solution of L_(h,p⃗)u_0 = G(W⃗) ∈ 𝒴⁰(α) and the S_ν are its coefficients of Lemma 33.16 (the C_ν
vanish). By the proof of that lemma, u_0 = u_I + u_ι + v (Proposition 33.8 for f′ := G(W⃗) − (L_(h,p⃗) − L_(b_0))u_0,
which lies in 𝒴⁰(α) with K⁺-order α − ε), L_(b_0)v = f^♭, and v = v_hi + v_low with v̂ on 0 < |σ| ≤ c the sum of the
pieces of Proposition 33.15, in which S_0 = 0, ḃ_0 = 0 and S_1 = 0 (its Steps 1 and 6). Moreover
L_(b_0)u = f′ − Σ_ν L_(b_0)m_ν(S_ν) has K⁺-order α − ε: by the tower relations L_(b_0)m_ν consists, near K⁺, of terms
with a_ν^((K_τ+1)) and a_ν^((K_τ+2)), of K⁺-order at least Re e_ν + K_τ + 1 (Section 32.11, Lemma 32.32,
Lemma 26.38), which exceeds 9/2 > α: for s1, K_τ ≥ k_s1 = 3 (Lemma 33.4 (c)) and
Re e_ν ≥ λ_♯ − 1 > ½; for the other rows the rate is at least λ_♯ > 3/2 and K_τ ≥ 2.

*Step 1 (the pieces near K⁺).* We write each part of u, on {t_* ≥ 1}, as χ_K times (polyhomogeneous coefficients
times profiles), plus conormal towers, plus a term of K⁺-order α − ε whose order at ι⁺ is at least 3 + η_2 − 2ε or
which is polyhomogeneous there with exponents in ℰ_♯.

(i) u_I, which contains the solutions u′_(λ_0) at ℐ⁺ of Step 2 of the proof of Proposition 33.8, vanishes near K⁺
(Proposition 33.8 (a)).

(ii) u_ι = Σ_(λ_0) Σ_j (χ_K u^((j))_(b_0,0) + χ_ι t_*^(−λ_0)(log t_*)^j ũ^((j))); u^((j))_(b_0,0) is
(26.55) at λ_0, a sum of towers with coefficients t_*^(−λ_0+μ)(log t_*)^j (and a_s1, a_v1), and
χ_ι t_*^(−λ_0)ũ^((j)) has K⁺-order Re λ_0 + ℓ_K(λ_0) − ε = α − ε (by the proof of Theorem 26.42, near K⁺:
t_*^(−λ)R^(ℓ_K) = t_*^(−λ−ℓ_K)r^(ℓ_K)).

(iii) m_ν(S_ν) = χ_K T_ν(a_ν S_ν) up to K⁺-order at least Re e_ν + k_μ + 1 > α (Definition 32.31,
Lemma 33.4 (c)).

(iv) v_hi has K⁺- and ι⁺-order j for every j (Lemma 29.32).

(v) The zero energy pieces σ^j χ_zf û^±_j, j ≤ 3: by Lemma 33.20 (b) with c = σ^j sgn(σ)^δ (the sign-even and
sign-odd parts of û^±_j) and the single profile û_(j,e) or û_(j,o); for δ = 0, y is a Schwartz function at +∞.
Lemma 33.10 makes û_j polyhomogeneous only to a finite order (û_2 to ε_+ − ε, û_3 conormal); its polyhomogeneous
part gives ι⁺-exponents in Λ (Lemma 33.20 (b)), and its conormal part the ι⁺-order at least 3 + η_2 − 2ε
(3 + ε_+ − ε at the levels 0–2, κ + 2 at level 3).

(vi) The pieces of Proposition 27.55 at the levels 1 and 2: σ^j χ_zf |σ|^(α_0−2)u_b is by (27.53) a finite
sum of terms c(σ)P(σ, x) with c homogeneous and P a spectral tower (G_(μ,τ), G_s1, G_v1, G^exc_s1) or a tower whose
profiles are multiplied by r^β or log r (from l_β(r̂) = (|σ|^β r^β − 1)/β), to which Lemma 33.20 (b) applies.
χ_tf ρ^(α_0−2)_tf u_tf does not vanish near zf: χ_tf = χ_2(ρ + |σ|) is 1 at tf ∩ zf and nonzero at zf over
{r > 2/ρ_0} (Section 27.10), ρ_tf = |σ| + ⟨x⟩⁻¹ (Section 28.1), and u_tf has the zf-class ((0, 0), ℓ_zf)
(Proposition 27.55). We expand σ^j χ_tf ρ^(α_0−2)_tf u_tf at zf to the order ℓ_zf + j, the zf-exponents being j plus
ℕ₀ (from χ_2, from ρ_tf and, if the zf-index set (0, 0) of u_tf is read with its ℕ₀-shifts, from u_tf itself, all
in |σ| and of the same form). Its zf-terms σ^j|σ|^k c^±_k(x), cut off by χ_zf, are pieces of the type (v)
(Lemma 33.20 (b) with c = σ^j|σ|^k sgn(σ)^δ and the single profile c_(k,e) or c_(k,o)), and the zf-remainder,
of weight ℓ_zf + j = α − 1 − ε (the choice of the level in Proposition 33.15), has K⁺-order α − ε
(Proposition 21.45 (2)), with ι⁺-exponents the tf-index set plus 1.

(vii) The columns at the levels 1–3 with constant data (ḃ^±_1, and ḃ^±_j, S^±_j for j = 2, 3):
σ^jĝ^aug(ḃ) = iσ^(j−1)Ψġ(ḃ) and σ^jĥ^aug(S) = −σ^(j−2)G_2(σ)(S) are, as in the proof of Lemma 33.21,
convolutions in t_* of ℱ⁻¹[χσ^m sgn(σ)^δ] with φ_x and tφ_x; Taylor's formula to a finite order writes them as finitely
many terms y(t_*)r^l ġ, y r^l h, y r^l h̆ (y polyhomogeneous, from the moments of φ) plus a remainder of K⁺-order at
least α. Near ι⁺, where χ_K = 0 for r ≥ t_*/2, the piece itself is what is recorded: for r ≥ 1, Ψ = Φ(σr) and
∂_σΨ = rΦ′(σr) (Lemma 28.5 (b)), and σ = ζ/r gives ℱ⁻¹[χσ^m sgn(σ)^δ Φ(σr)] = r^(−1−m)G(t_*/r) + O(r^(−∞)) with
G smooth (and likewise with rΦ′(σr)); so each piece is polyhomogeneous at ι⁺ with the exponent m + 1 plus the degree of
the state (ġ: 2 or 3; h: 3; h̆: 2) and the exponents of its expansion, for instance 3 or 4 at level 1; these lie in Λ
(3 ∈ Λ, Λ + 1 ⊂ Λ, Λ + ℰ_ind ⊂ Λ).

(viii) The pieces of Proposition 27.58 at level 3: σ³χ_zf u_b is by (27.56) a sum of spectral towers times
the conormal scalars σ³|σ|^(α_κ−3)S(σ), σ³|σ|^(α_κ−2)V(σ), σ³|σ|^(α_κ−2−μ)Y(σ), of the zf-weights α_κ, α_κ + 1,
α_κ + 1 − μ; Lemma 33.20 (a) gives conormal towers with coefficients of the orders α_κ + 1 (boosts, tower
h^(≤3)_(b_0,s1)), α_κ + 2 (rotations, tower rate α_κ + 3 > α) and α_κ + 2 − μ, the last of K⁺-order above α unless
μ ∈ (−1, 0]; their order at ι⁺ is α_κ + 2 ≥ κ_3 + 2 = 3 + η_2 − 2ε. In the boost tower the terms with a″, a‴ have
K⁺-order α_κ + 3 > α, and it is truncated to h^(≤1)_(b_0,s1). For σ³χ^♯_tf ũ: Proposition 27.58 gives ũ the zf-class
((0, 0), ℓ_zf), its proof putting χ_zf χ_tf v_0 into ũ with v_0 stationary and conormal of order α_κ − 2 ∈ (−1, 0) (its
other part, |σ|^(α_κ−2)ũ_1, times σ³, joins the zf-remainder of weight ℓ_3 + 3); so σ³χ^♯_tf ũ is
σ³χ^♯_tf χ_zf χ_tf v^±_0, expanded at zf as in (vi) into pieces of the type (v) with the single profiles v_(0,e), v_(0,o)
(of degree α_κ − 2; their sign-odd parts reach the K⁺-exponent 4), plus a zf-remainder of weight ℓ_3 + 3 = α − 1 − ε,
of K⁺-order α − ε (Proposition 21.45 (2)).

(ix) The last level: σ³û_f has zf-weight ℓ_3 + 3 and tf-weight κ + 1 − ε, so K⁺-order α − ε and ι⁺-order
κ + 2 − ε > 4 (Proposition 21.45 (2)); the columns give χ_K h^(≤1)_(b_0,s1)(A) + χ_K ġ(B) with
A ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−2−ε)_b and B ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−1−ε)_b, up to K⁺-order ℓ_3 + 4 = α − ε (Lemma 33.21 with a = ℓ_3).

*Step 2 (assembly).* By Step 1, on {t_* ≥ 1},

    u = χ_K Σ_(i∈I) y_i p_i + χ_K C + w′,    (33.22)

where C consists of the conormal towers of (viii) (the truncated boost tower h^(≤1)_(b_0,s1)(A_5),
A_5 ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α_κ+1)_b, and T_ψ(Y^c_ψ) for the rows with μ ∈ (−1, 0], Y^c_ψ of order at least 3 + η_2 − 2ε − μ) and of
(ix) (h^(≤1)_(b_0,s1)(A) + ġ(B)); w′ has K⁺-order α − ε; and the y_i p_i are the polyhomogeneous terms of (ii), (iii)
and (v)–(viii) (with the zf-terms of (vi) and (viii)). Every exponent (z, k) of y_i satisfies Re z + d_i ≥ λ_♯: z + d_i
is the leading ι⁺-exponent of the piece (Lemma 33.20 (b); (26.55) for (ii)), and these lie in ℰ_♯
(Lemma 33.2 (c), Proposition 33.8 and Lemma 33.10: all exponents produced are Λ-valued with
logarithmic orders at most k̄, and those below 2 lie in ℰ_++, so in ℳ). As u (Theorem 33.18) and χ_K C have
K⁺-order at least α − 2 − ε, so has χ_K Σ_i y_i p_i; in {r ≤ R} its lowest term dominates, so the coefficient section
Σ_i c^((i))_(z,k)p_i of every exponent with Re z < α − 2 − ε vanishes, and we drop these exponents from the y_i (the sum
is unchanged).

*Step 3 (formal solutions).* Lemma 33.23 applies to w := u − χ_K C with β := α − ε: the hypotheses on the y_i
are those of Step 2; L_(b_0)u has K⁺-order α − ε (Step 0); and L_(b_0)(χ_K C) has K⁺-order α − ε, as by the tower
relations it consists of [L_(b_0), χ_K]C (supported away from K⁺) and of terms with A″_5 (of order α_κ + 3 > α),
(Y^c_ψ)^((3)) (of order above 3 + η_2 − μ + 2 > α), A″ and B′ (of order α − ε). It gives (33.18) with a_b of
exponents at least α − 1 − ε.

*Step 4 (the coefficients).* Put Ṡ_rem := A + A_5 + a_s, ḃ_rem := B + a_b, and Ẏ_ψ := a_ψ + Y^c_ψ (with Y^c_ψ := 0
unless μ_ψ ∈ (−1, 0]). Then Ṡ_rem ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−2−ε)_b (α_κ + 1 ≥ 2 + η_2 − 2ε > α − 2, and a_s has exponents of real part at
least α − 2 − ε), ḃ_rem ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−1−ε)_b, and Ẏ_ψ ∈ Ḣ^(∞,𝒬(ℰ_♯−d_ψ,w_ψ))_b: a_ψ is a finite sum of terms
χ_+t_*^(−z)(log t_*)^k; those with Re z < w_ψ have (z + d_ψ, k) ∈ ℰ_♯, by Lemma 33.23 (*Exponents*), as the
polyhomogeneous parts of the pieces have their ι⁺-exponents in ℰ_♯ (Step 2) and their conormal parts the order at least
3 + η_2 − 2ε ((v)), while Λ + ℰ_ind ⊂ Λ and k̄(λ + w) ≥ k̄(λ) + l_* for (w, l) ∈ ℰ_ind (the proof of
Lemma 33.2 (c)), and ℳ + ℰ_ind lies in ℳ below 2 (Section 33.9); those with Re z > w_ψ, and Y^c_ψ, lie in
t_*^(−w_ψ)H^∞_b; and none has Re z = w_ψ for ε off a finite set, the exponents of a_ψ lying in ⋃_i E_i + ℕ₀, whose
elements do not depend on ε, while w_ψ does. So ũ := u − χ_K u_exp = w″ + w′ has K⁺-order α − ε.

*Step 5 (ℐ⁺ and ι⁺).* Near ℐ⁺, χ_K = 0 and ũ = u, which has the ℐ⁺-data of (33.13). Near ι⁺, u is partially
polyhomogeneous with the index set ℰ_♯ up to the order 3 + η_2 − 2ε: u_I and u_ι by Proposition 33.8 (a)–(b) (index
sets Λ-valued below 3 + ε_+, logarithmic orders at most k̄, in ℳ below 2 by Step 2 of its proof, the term
χ_ι t_*^(−λ_0)(log t_*)^j ũ^((j)) being the ι⁺-term (λ_0, j) itself, with the ℐ⁺-weight ℓ_I on ι⁺,
Corollary 26.44); the m_ν, with exponents in ℰ_par ⊂ ℰ_♯ (k̄(λ + j) ≥ k̄(λ)); the pieces (v)–(vii), polyhomogeneous
with the exponents the tf-exponents plus 1 (Lemma 33.20 (b); (vii) as stated there) up to the order
3 + η_2 − 2ε, in ℰ_♯; the pieces (viii)–(ix), of order at least 3 + η_2 − 2ε (Lemma 33.20 (a),
Lemma 33.21, and the tf-weights α_κ + 1, κ + 1 − ε); and v_hi. The same holds for χ_K u_exp: its
polyhomogeneous coefficients give the exponents z + d_ψ ∈ ℰ_♯ plus those of the expansions of the profiles (Λ is closed
under the addition of ℰ_ind, k̄(λ + w) ≥ k̄(λ) + l_*, and ℳ + ℰ_ind lies in ℳ below 2), and its conormal coefficients
have the order at least 3 + η_2 − 2ε at ι⁺ (α_κ + 2 for (viii); at least α + 1 − ε for h^(≤1)_(b_0,s1)(Ṡ_rem) and
ġ(ḃ_rem), as h_(b_0,s1) ∈ 𝒜³ and h̆¹_(b_0,s1), ġ ∈ 𝒜²). So ũ satisfies (33.21).

*Step 6 (the rest).* Every map used is linear and bounded, uniformly for (h, p⃗) small (Lemma 33.16,
Theorem 33.18, Lemma 33.20–Lemma 33.23), and is applied to the forcing f′ of Step 0, whose size
is at most C‖F‖, ‖F‖ being the seminorm of 𝒴⁰(α) of large enough regularity at the end of the proof of
Theorem 33.18. Put w_(α′) := min(α′ − 2, λ_♯ − 1), with α′ ∈ (2, 3) the admissible level fixed in that proof:
‖G(W⃗)‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) and ‖u_0‖_(w_(α′)) are at most C‖F‖ by the bounds there, and ‖(L_(h,p⃗) − L_(b_0))u_0‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) ≤
C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u_0‖_(w_(α′)) by the count of Step 0 of the proof of Lemma 33.16. Reality: u is real and the
towers are real (the conjugate of T_ψ(Y) is T_ψ(Ȳ)), so replacing
every coefficient and ũ by their real parts keeps (33.19)–(33.21), ℰ_♯ being closed under
conjugation. L_(b_0)(χ_K u_exp) has K⁺-order α − ε by the tower relations, as in Step 3. ∎

The proof uses its setting only through the following: u has the K⁺-weight α − 2 − ε and the ι⁺- and ℐ⁺-data of
(33.13); and u = u_0 − Σ_(ν∈𝒩″) m_ν(W_ν) for a finite set 𝒩″ of rows, with u_0 the forward solution of
L_(h,p⃗)u_0 = G for a forcing G ∈ 𝒴⁰(α) and with L_b m_ν of K⁺-order above α for ν ∈ 𝒩″. Step 1 (iii) treats the
m_ν(W_ν) as it treats the m_ν(S_ν).

In this generality the bounds of Step 6 read as follows. Put w_0 := min(α − 2, λ_♯ − 1). Every m_ν(W) has K⁺-weight
at least λ_♯ − 1 − ε and ι⁺-weight λ_♯ − ε, and vanishes near ℐ⁺, so u_0 = u + Σ_(ν∈𝒩″) m_ν(W_ν) satisfies the
hypothesis of Lemma 33.16 with this w_0. Step 0 puts f′ := G − (L_(h,p⃗) − L_(b_0))u_0, and the maps of Step 6
are applied to f′ and, through Step 1 (iii), to the W_ν. For every w ∈ (0, w_0] the count of Step 0 of the proof of
Lemma 33.16 gives

    ‖f′‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) ≤ ‖G‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u_0‖_(w).

So every seminorm of the coefficients in (33.20) and of ũ in (33.21) is at most

    C‖G‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u_0‖_(w) + C Σ_(ν∈𝒩″) |W_ν|,

where ‖·‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) is a seminorm of 𝒴⁰(α) and ‖·‖_(w) one of the space of the hypothesis of Lemma 33.16 with w
in place of w_0, both depending on the seminorm bounded (of large enough regularity, as in Section 32.6), and C
depends on w and these seminorms and is uniform for (h, p⃗) small. This is not a bound by G alone. In the setting of
this section, 𝒩″ = 𝒩, G is the G(W⃗) of Step 0, and the coefficients W_ν are the S_ν of Step 0, which are the row
components of p⃗′ (the C_ν vanish). Take for w the number w_(α′) = min(α′ − 2, λ_♯ − 1) of Step 6, which lies in
(0, w_0]. The bounds at the end of the proof of Theorem 33.18, which hold for every choice of the seminorms of
large enough regularity, give |p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(F)|, ‖G(W⃗)‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) and ‖u_0(W⃗)‖_(w) at most C‖F‖, with ‖F‖ a seminorm of
𝒴⁰(α) of larger regularity, as there; so the three terms are at most C‖F‖, which is the bound of Step 6.

### 33.12 Admissible levels and enlarged sources

Lemma 33.16 reaches the order α > 4 in one step from an admissible level α′ ∈ (2, 3), which needs the K⁺-order
a_K ≥ 4 + ε_K of the background. [Hin26, Remark 11.61] uses only 2 + ε_K orders of K⁺-decay of h, at the price of
passing through every level ([Hin26, Parts 2–3 of the proof of Theorem 11.59]). The linearisation in the black hole
parameters of Chapter 34 carries the difference to the background h + h_(b,rem)(q), of K⁺-order only α − 2 − ε, as a
source, so it passes through every level in steps shorter than α − 4. This section and the next supply those levels,
and the sources that the linearisation produces.

Everything of Section 33.5 is kept except its constant α: (H1)–(H4), (C5), Λ, k̄(λ), ℰ_par, (G), ℰ⁰_src, 𝒴⁰(·),
the rows 𝒩 = 𝒩_ι ∪ 𝒩_σ, the spectral notation and the dictionary; ℰ_♯ is that of Section 33.9. The *rate* of a
triple (τ, λ, k), τ ∈ 𝒯, λ ∈ Λ, is λ − 1 (s1), λ (s0, s2, v1) or λ + d_τ (c0, c1) (Section 32.10); by
Lemma 33.2 (a) the real parts of the rates form a discrete set.

**Definition 33.25** (Admissible levels.) A level β ∈ (3, 4 + ε_K] is *admissible* if (a) β − 2 is not the
real part of a rate; (b) β avoids the finite set of Definition 33.3, the values for which β − Re λ_0, λ_0 ∈ Λ,
Re λ_0 < 2, equals −Re μ for a root μ of L̂_b(0) or lies in Re π_1ℰ_K; and (c) β avoids the exclusion set of
Section 33.5 with β in place of α: the values for which a condition (27.51) of Proposition 27.55 fails
at the levels 1 and 2 with ℓ_zf = β − 1 − j − ε, a condition of Proposition 27.58 fails at level 3, or a value
excluded in Lemma 29.33 or (28.1) is met at level 3 (for β > 4 as in Section 33.5; for β < 4 by
β_tf − β_zf = κ − β + 2 + ε, κ the final tf-weight of Step 4 of the proof of Proposition 33.28), with ε taken small
and off a finite set as there. In particular β ≠ 4, by (a), as 2 ∈ Λ is the rate of (s0, 2, 0). The small ε is moreover
taken with ε < β − 3, with ε < β − 4 if β > 4, and with no rate of real part in [β − 2 − 3ε, β − 2). For β ∈ (2, 3),
admissibility is that of Section 32.6. The excluded values near any level are finitely many, so the admissible
levels are dense in (3, 4 + ε_K]; and every admissible α ≥ 3 of Definition 33.3 is admissible here, as by (G) no
rate has real part in (2 + ε_K − ε′_0, 2 + ε_K]. Put 𝒩_β := {ν ∈ 𝒩 : Re e_ν < β − 2}; 𝒩_β = 𝒩 for β > 4, as every row
of 𝒩 has rate at most 2.

**Definition 33.26** (The enlarged sources.) Let ℰ^♮ be the set of the pairs

    (λ + w_1 + ⋯ + w_m, k + l_1 + ⋯ + l_m)

with m ≥ 1, (λ, k) ∈ ℰ_♯ and (w_i, l_i) ∈ ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind ∪ {(1, 0)}, of real part below 3 + ε_+. For
β ∈ (2, 4 + ε_K], 𝒴^♮_2(β) is the space of the sections supported in supp χ^♯_K ((29.2)) lying in
⋂_ε H^(∞,∞,((ℰ⁰_src∪ℰ^♮)+2, w_+−ε),β)_b(Ω_*; S²T*), and 𝒴^♮(β) := 𝒴⁰(β) + 𝒴^♮_2(β), real sections.

**Lemma 33.27** (The logarithmic count for the enlarged sources.) (a) π_1(ℰ^♮) ⊂ Λ; at
λ′ := λ + w_1 + ⋯ + w_m the logarithmic order k + l_1 + ⋯ + l_m is at most k̄(λ′) − J_*(l_* + 1) − 1; and
ℰ^♮ ∩ {Re < 2} ⊂ ℰ_++.

(b) Lemma 33.2 (c) holds for sources in 𝒴^♮(β): every exponent (λ, k) produced with 2 ≤ Re λ ≤ 3 + ε_+ has
λ ∈ Λ and k ≤ k̄(λ), and those below 2 lie in ℰ_++.

*Proof.* (a) Λ + w ⊂ Λ for the increments (Definition 33.1), and π_1ℰ_♯ ⊂ Λ ∪ π_1ℳ ⊂ Λ (Lemma 33.2 (a)).
The increments have real part at least η_0 > 0, so λ, λ + w_1, …, λ′ are m + 1 elements of Λ with increasing real
parts, and n(λ′) ≥ n(λ) + m; hence k̄(λ′) − k̄(λ) ≥ m(J_* + 1)(l_* + 1), while k ≤ k̄(λ) (for (λ, k) ∈ ℳ,
k ≤ k̄_0 ≤ k̄(λ)) and l_i ≤ l_*; so k + Σ l_i ≤ k̄(λ′) − m(J_*(l_* + 1) + 1). Below 2: ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re < 2} = ℳ ⊂ ℰ_++
(Section 33.9, where ℰ_♯ is ℳ below 2, with the logarithmic orders of ℰ_++); the pairs from ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re ≥ 2} stay
above 2; ℰ_++ is closed under the addition of ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind below 2 ((32.16)); and adding 1 leaves
{Re < 2} (λ_♯ + 1 > 2).

(b) In the induction of the proof of Lemma 33.2 (c), the logarithmic order at λ is the largest over its
contributions plus at most J_*(l_* + 1) from the raises at λ. A forcing exponent of ℰ^♮ is a further contribution, of
logarithmic order at most k̄(λ) − J_*(l_* + 1) − 1 by (a); so the bound k̄(λ) survives, and the induction runs as
there. Below 2 the exponents of the forcing lie in ℰ_++ by (a), as (32.16) and Step 2 of the proof of
Proposition 33.8 require. ∎

The constructions of Section 33.4, Section 33.7 and Section 33.11 see the ι⁺-index set of a forcing only
through this count, the plain weight w_+ − ε and, for the part not supported in supp χ^♯_K, the step at ℐ⁺ (Step 1 of
the proof of Proposition 33.8, which acts on f_1 ∈ 𝒴⁰_1 only; a section of 𝒴^♮_2 enters there as f_2 does, being
supported away from ℐ⁺). This is used in Proposition 33.31.

### 33.13 The expansion at every level

**Proposition 33.28** (The spectral phase at every level.) Let β ∈ (3, 4 + ε_K] be admissible and
f ∈ 𝒴^♮(β), and let f^♭ and v be as in Section 33.5 with β in place of α (f^♭ is the forcing of
Proposition 33.8 (c) for f, and v the forward solution of L_b v = f^♭, of K⁺-weight w_v > 0). Then there are
S_ν ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ), ν ∈ 𝒩_σ ∩ 𝒩_β, linear and continuous in f, with

    v − Σ_(ν∈𝒩_σ∩𝒩_β) m_ν(S_ν) − v^rot_β ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β′_+,β−2−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−),    (33.23)

where v^rot_β := 0 for β < 4, and v^rot_β is the v^rot of Proposition 33.15 at β for β > 4.

*Proof.* Proposition 33.8 holds at the admissible β as stated: its proof uses of α only α ≤ 4 + ε_K (for
ℓ_K(λ_0) < 3), ℓ_K(λ_0) = α − Re λ_0 > α − 2 > 0, the conditions of Definition 33.25 (b), and (G) for the rows of
𝒩_ι, all of which hold for β; for f ∈ 𝒴^♮(β) it holds by Lemma 33.27. Then the proof of
Proposition 33.15 applies with β in place of α, with the following changes.

*Constants.* ℓ_j := β − 1 − j − ε at the level j ∈ {1, 2, 3}, so ℓ_1 ∈ (1, 2 + ε_K), ℓ_2 ∈ (0, 1 + ε_K) and
ℓ_3 ∈ (−1, ε_K); η_1, η_2 as there.

*Steps 0–3* are unchanged; Step 0 uses β_K = β − ε. At level 1 the conditions (27.51) of
Proposition 27.55 hold for 2 ≤ Re α_0 < 2 + η_1 and ℓ_zf = ℓ_1: ℓ_1 − Re α_0 + 2 > β − 2 − η_1 − ε > 0 and ℓ_1 < 3, the
rest by Definition 33.25 (c). At level 2, for 1 + η_1 ≤ Re α_0 < 2 + η_2 and ℓ_zf = ℓ_2:
ℓ_2 − Re α_0 + 2 > β − 3 − η_2 − ε > −ε_ind (η_2 + ε < ε_ind) and ℓ_2 − min(Re α_0 − 2, 0) < ℓ_2 + 1 − η_1 < 3; the
remainder exponents α_0 + ℰ_ind are treated in turn as there. Lemma 33.11 at level 2 needs only the zf-weight
ℓ_2 > 0 of g_2, and gives g_3 the zf-weight ℓ_3.

*Step 4 for ℓ_3 > 0* (β > 4, where ℓ_3 = β − 4 − ε > 0 by Definition 33.25) is that of Proposition 33.15.
*For ℓ_3 < 0* (β < 4), g_3 has no zf-term to remove, and the zero energy solve of level 3 (Lemma 33.10 with
q_3) is omitted. While the tf-weight κ of the current level-3 forcing is at most β − 2 = 2 + ℓ_3 + ε, apply
Proposition 27.58 with α_κ := κ ∈ (1, 2) (κ ≥ κ_3 = 1 + η_2 − 2ε > 1 and κ ≤ β − 2 < 2), ℓ_zf := ℓ_3 ∉ ℕ₀, the order
0 of the zf-index set, and w = ℓ_3 − κ + 2 ∈ [−ε, 1) ⊂ (−ε_ind, ℓ^max_K); its conditions w ≠ −μ and 2 − κ + j ≠ −μ hold
for ε off a finite set, the values of κ being κ_3 + i(ε_g − ε). Each round leaves a remainder of tf-weight
κ + ε_g − ε and the pieces σ³u; after finitely many rounds κ > β − 2, and, lowering κ if necessary,
κ ∈ (β − 2, β − 1 − ε). The rest, g_J (the level-3 forcing after the rounds), lies in H^(∞,(5/2−ε,κ,ℓ_3))_b and is
inverted by Lemma 29.33 with β_scf := 3/2 − 2ε, β_tf := κ − 2, β_zf := ℓ_3,
β_tf − β_zf = κ − β + 2 + ε ∈ (0, 1) (ε off a finite set, Definition 33.25 (c)):

    û_f ∈ H^(∞,(3/2−3ε,κ−2,ℓ_3))_b,          ḃ_f, S_f ∈ H^(∞,ℓ_3)_b(±(0, c], |dσ/σ|),     ℓ_3 > −1.

*Step 5.* The matching and the sorting are unchanged. In (iii), σ³û_f has zf-weight ℓ_3 + 3 = β − 1 − ε, and
σ³ĝ^aug(ḃ_f), σ³ĥ^aug(S_f) give the K⁺-weights ℓ_3 + 3 and ℓ_3 + 2 = β − 2 − ε (Lemma 33.13 with a = ℓ_3 > −1);
the level-3 pieces of Step 4 have zf-weight at least α_κ > 1, so K⁺-weight above 2 ≥ β − 2 for β ≤ 4 (and as there for
β > 4). Lemma 33.7 applies with β_tail := β − 3 − 2ε ∈ (−1, 1 + ε_K), not in ℕ₀ for ε off a finite set, and
(iii) contributes O(t_*^(−β+2+3ε)), as σ³ĥ^aug(S_f) has zf-weight ℓ_3 + 1 = β − 3 − ε > β_tail.

*Step 6.* The stationary columns vanish as there (w_v > 0). Of the towers listed there, those of rate below β − 2 are
the rows of 𝒩_σ ∩ 𝒩_β and, for β > 4, the towers of v^rot: for β ≤ 4 the s0, s2 and v1 towers of rate at least
Re α_0 ≥ 2 ≥ β − 2 are not among them; every tower of rate at least β − 2 has rate above β − 2
(Definition 33.25 (a)), so is O(t_*^(−β+2+3ε)); and the identification with m_ν(S_ν) holds up to terms of rate at
least Re e_ν + 3 > β − 2.

*Step 7* is unchanged, with β in place of α; it gives (33.23). ∎

**Lemma 33.29** (The expansion at every level.) Let β ∈ (3, 4 + ε_K] be admissible, let (h, p⃗) be a base
point with black hole parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, with p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 and h ∈ 𝒳^∞ small, and let G ∈ 𝒴^♮(β). Suppose that the forward
solution u of L_(h,p⃗)u = G lies in ⋂_ε H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β′_+,w_0−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−) with w_0 > 0, w_0 + a_K > β and
β′_+ ∈ (3/2 − (δ_♯ − ε_+), 3/2). Then

    u = Σ_(ν∈𝒩_β) m_ν(S_ν) + u^rot_β + ũ,     ũ ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β_+,β−2−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−)    (33.24)

for every β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+). Here u^rot_β is the sum of the terms of u^rot_ι (Proposition 33.8) with
Re λ_0 < β − 2 and of v^rot_β, for the forcing f′ of the proof; the coefficients S_ν = S^(h,p⃗,β)_ν(G) ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ) are
determined by u − u^rot_β; u^rot_β and the S_ν are conjugation-symmetric and linear in G, and satisfy the bound of
Lemma 33.16 with ‖G‖_(𝒴^♮(β)), one fixed seminorm of 𝒴^♮(β), in place of ‖G‖_(𝒴⁰(α)), for every
w ∈ (0, w_0], with C uniform for (h, p⃗) small and b ∈ ℬ̄_*. When h_(b,v1) = 0, in particular at b_0, u^rot_β is put
into ũ. For β ∈ (2, 3), Lemma 32.27 holds for G ∈ 𝒴^♮(β).

*Proof.* The proof of Lemma 33.16, with Proposition 33.8 at β (as in the proof of Proposition 33.28)
and Proposition 33.28 in place of Proposition 33.15. Step 0 gives f′ ∈ 𝒴^♮(β) (the 𝒴^♮_2-part of G is
untouched, and (L − L_b)u lies in 𝒴⁰(β) as there, with ‖(L − L_b)u‖_(𝒴⁰(β)) ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u‖_(w) by the same count,
w − ε + a_K ≥ β). The rows of 𝒩_ι of rate at least β − 2 have rate above β − 2 (Definition 33.25 (a)), so their
m_ν(S_ν) have K⁺-weight at least β − 2 − ε (Lemma 32.32 (e)) and join ũ; so do the terms
χ_K t_*^(−λ_0)(log t_*)^j h_(b,v1)(V) of u^rot_ι with Re λ_0 > β − 2, whose rate Re λ_0 is that of the triple
(v1, λ_0, j). *Determination:* by Corollary 33.6 on 𝒩_β, all rates there being below β − 2. For β ∈ (2, 3):
the space 𝒴(β) of Section 32.6 records the ι⁺-exponents below 4 in ℰ_++ + 2 and has the plain weight 4 − ε above,
and 𝒴^♮_2(β) lies in it by Lemma 33.27 (a). ∎

**Lemma 33.30** (The coefficients near the reference point, at every level.) Fix b ∈ ℬ̄_*, and let p⃗_b be
as in Lemma 33.17. In Lemma 33.29, if the base points (h_j, p⃗_j) have black hole parameter b,
(h_j, p⃗_j) → (0, p⃗_b), G_j → G in 𝒴^♮(β), and the forward solutions u_j of L_(h_j,p⃗_j)u_j = G_j and u of
L_(0,p⃗_b)u = G satisfy the hypothesis of Lemma 33.29 with the same w_0 and β′_+, the u_j being bounded there,
then S^(h_j,p⃗_j,β)_ν(G_j) → S^(0,p⃗_b,β)_ν(G).

*Proof.* The proof of Lemma 33.17, with Lemma 33.29 in place of Lemma 33.16, 𝒴^♮(β) in place
of 𝒴⁰(α) and (33.24) in place of (33.11). In detail, with L_j := L_(h_j,p⃗_j), the forcing

    R_j := G_j − G − (L_j − L_(0,p⃗_b))u_j

of u_j − u for L_(0,p⃗_b) tends to 0 in 𝒴^♮(β) by the count of Step 0, the u_j being bounded; and
S^(h_j,p⃗_j,β)_ν(G_j) − S^(0,p⃗_b,β)_ν(G) = S^(0,p⃗_b,β)_ν(R_j), which the bound of Lemma 33.29 at (0, p⃗_b)
bounds by C‖R_j‖_(𝒴^♮(β)) + C|p⃗_b|‖u_j − u‖_(w) for every w ∈ (0, w_0]. At b = b_0 this tends to 0. Otherwise fix an
admissible α′ ∈ (2, min(3, 2 + w_0)) and w ∈ (0, α′ − 2). By (33.24) for u_j and u, whose terms m_ν and
u^rot_β have ι⁺-weight above 3/2 as in the proof of Lemma 33.17, u_j − u lies in (32.26) at α′; and
R_j → 0 in 𝒴^♮(β) ⊂ 𝒴^♮(α′), which lies in the class 𝒴(α′) of Section 32.6 (the last sentence of
Lemma 33.29). Uniqueness and (i) of Proposition 32.29 at α′, at the base point (0, p⃗_b), give, as there,
‖u_j − u‖_(α′) → 0, with the seminorm ‖·‖_(α′) of Section 32.6 taken as there; so ‖u_j − u‖_(w) → 0, and
S^(0,p⃗_b,β)_ν(R_j) → 0. ∎

**Proposition 33.31** (The enlarged sources at the top level.) Theorem 33.18 and
Theorem 33.24 hold with F ∈ 𝒴^♮(α) in place of F ∈ 𝒴⁰(α), with the same conclusions.

*Proof.* Their proofs use F through Proposition 33.8, Proposition 33.15, Lemma 33.16 and
Lemma 33.17, Proposition 32.29 at a level α′ ∈ (2, 3), and, in Steps 2 and 5 of the proof of
Theorem 33.24, the statement that the ι⁺-exponents produced lie in ℰ_♯. Each holds for F ∈ 𝒴^♮ by
Lemma 33.27, Proposition 33.28 and Lemma 33.29 (with β = α), and the class of Section 32.6
contains 𝒴^♮(α′) (the last sentence of Lemma 33.29). ∎

At a base point with black hole parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, Proposition 33.31 is used inside Proposition 36.8, as
Theorem 33.18 is.

### 33.14 The expansion at a general base point

Lemma 33.22 and Lemma 33.23 use h_(b_0,v1) = 0: they put h̆¹_(b_0,v1)(V) in ker L_0, and they remove the
v1 content through an antiderivative. At a rotating b both steps change. This section gives their forms at every
b ∈ ℬ̄_*, with the rotation tower T_(v1,b) in place of the antiderivative, and with them the expansion of
Theorem 33.24 at b.

*The rotation state at b.* By Lemma 30.4, for V ∈ 𝒱_1 there is ḃ_V ∈ 𝔟, linear in V,
with |ḃ_V| = O(|b − b_0||V|) and

    h_(b,v1)(V) = ġ_b(ḃ_V),          ker h_(b,v1) = 𝒱⁰_b := {V : ḃ_V = 0}.

*Notation.* In this section L_0 := L̂_b(0), L_1 := [L_b, t_*], L_2 := ½[[L_b, t_*], t_*]; h := h_(b,s1),
h̆^j := h̆^j_(b,s1); 𝒢_* is the space of sections conormal at ∂X of order above −3 (Lemma 33.22); and

    T_(v1,b)(aV) := Σ_(j≤2) a^((j)) h̆^j_(b,v1)(V),     h̆⁰_(b,v1) := h_(b,v1),

is the v1 tower T_v1 of Section 33.9 at b, the truncation to j ≤ 2 of the tower of the rotation rows of
Definition 34.3. Its companion h̆¹_(b,v1)(V) satisfies

    L_0h̆¹_(b,v1)(V) = −L_1ġ_b(ḃ_V),    (33.25)

by the tower relation L_0h̆¹_(b,v1)(V) = −L_1h_(b,v1)(V) and the formula for h_(b,v1) above. At b_0, h̆¹_(b_0,v1)(V)
lies in ker L_0.

**Lemma 33.32** (Lemma 33.22 and Lemma 33.23 at b.) Let b ∈ ℬ̄_*.

(a) If p ∈ 𝒢_* and L_0p = 0, then p = Σ_ψ h̆^((μ_ψ),0)_(b,τ_ψ)(Y_ψ) + h̆¹_(b,v1)(V) + ġ_b(ḃ) + h(S), the sum over the
rows of ℛ′ other than v1, with V ∈ 𝒱⁰_b and unique coefficients.

(b) If X ∈ 𝒢_* and L_0X = L_1ġ_b(ḃ) + L_1h̆¹(S) + L_2h(S), then ḃ + ḃ_(V_X) = 0, where V_X is the v1 coefficient that
the reduction of X in the proof of Lemma 33.22 removes at the root −1. The statement on s1 is as at b_0.

(c) Lemma 33.23 holds at b, with (33.18) read as

    χ_K Σ_i y_i p_i = χ_K(Σ_(ψ≠v1) T_(ψ,b)(a_ψ) + T_(v1,b)(a_v1) + h^(≤1)_(b,s1)(a_s) + ġ_b(a_b)) + w″.

The exponents are as there; those of a_v1 lie in ⋃_i E_i + ℕ₀ − 1, and those of a_b have real part at least β − 1. The
constants are uniform on ℬ̄_*, and no map V ↦ h_(b,v1)(V) is inverted.

*Proof.* (a) and (b). Run the reduction of the proof of Lemma 33.22 at b, with the states at b ((P3)). At the
v1 root −1, subtract h̆¹_(b,v1)(V), whose leading coefficient is h̄_v1(V), independent of b ((P3)). By
(33.25) this adds L_1ġ_b(ḃ_V) to the right side. So the reduced section X_1 ∈ 𝒜¹ satisfies

    L_0X_1 = L_1ġ_b(ḃ + ḃ_(V_X)) + L_1h̆¹(S + S′) + L_2h(S + S′).

(28.4) and Proposition 28.8 at b ((P4)), applied as in the proof of Lemma 33.22 (b), give
ḃ + ḃ_(V_X) = 0 and S′ = −S. This is (b). For (a), p is (b) with ḃ = 0 and S = 0, so ḃ_V = 0. The rest is as at b_0,
the nullspace of Proposition 25.30 at b being spanned by ġ_b and h_b.

(c) The removal of pairs proceeds as at b_0. By (a), the coefficient section of the first pair (z_0, k_0) is

    P = Σ_ψ h̆^((μ_ψ),0)_(b,τ_ψ)(Y_ψ) + h̆¹_(b,v1)(V) + ġ_b(ḃ) + h(S),     V ∈ 𝒱⁰_b.

Two steps change. Write a := χ_+t_*^(−z_0)(log t_*)^(k_0), and let ã be its antiderivative.

*The v1 part of P.* Subtract T_(v1,b)(ãV). Its bottom ã h_(b,v1)(V) vanishes, as V ∈ 𝒱⁰_b = ker h_(b,v1), and its next
term is a h̆¹_(b,v1)(V). It is a tower, so L_b of it involves a″ and higher only, and has K⁺-order Re z_0 + 2 ≥ β. Its
coefficient ãV enters a_v1 at the exponent z_0 − 1, and a_s is unchanged; this is why the exponents are as at b_0.

*The ġ part of P.* If Re z_0 + 1 ≥ β, subtract ġ_b(aḃ) as at b_0. Otherwise the next coefficient gives L_0P_1 = z_0L_1P,
and with the tower relations L_0X = z_0L_1ġ_b(ḃ) for a section X ∈ 𝒢_*. By (b), z_0ḃ = −ḃ_(V_X). Put V″ := −V_X/z_0,
so that ḃ_(V″) = ḃ, and subtract T_(v1,b)(aV″) instead of ġ_b(aḃ). Its bottom is a h_(b,v1)(V″) = aġ_b(ḃ_(V″)) =
aġ_b(ḃ), as required, and L_b of it involves a″ and higher. Its next term, a′h̆¹_(b,v1)(V″), carries the v1 content
V_X that the reduction at the next pair would remove; that content is therefore removed here, at the earlier pair.

The new terms are again compatible: a companion a^((j))h̆^j has the exponent z + j and the degree μ − j, as at
b_0. |V″| ≤ C|V_X|, with C depending only on |z_0|⁻¹, and Re z_0 ≥ β − 2 > 1. The coefficients are read off leading
coefficients, which are independent of b ((P3)) or, for ġ_b, smooth in b; so the bounds are uniform on ℬ̄_*. ∎

**Corollary 33.33** (Theorem 33.24 at b.) Let α > 4 be admissible, b ∈ ℬ̄_*, and (h, p⃗) a small
base point with black hole parameter b. Let G ∈ 𝒴^♮(α−) := ⋂_(ε>0) 𝒴^♮(α − ε), let u_0 be the forward solution of
L_(h,p⃗)u_0 = G, and let u = u_0 − Σ_(ν∈𝒩″) m_ν(W_ν), where 𝒩″ is a finite set of rows of 𝒩 and of rotation rows
m_ν(W) of Definition 34.3, built at b, a_ν = t_*^(−λ)(log t_*)^k, (λ, k) ∈ ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re ≤ 2}, W ∈ 𝒱_(1,ℂ), which equal
χ_K T_(v1,b)(a_ν W) up to terms of K⁺-order Re λ + 3 − ε > α (by Lemma 33.4 (a), the difference consists of
the terms with a_ν^((3)) and a_ν^((4)), the tower length K_v1 of Section 32.11 being 3). Suppose that u has the
K⁺-weight α − 2 − ε and the ι⁺- and ℐ⁺-data of (33.13). Then (33.19)–(33.21) hold at
b, with h^(≤1)_(b,s1), ġ_b and the towers T_(ψ,b) at b in place of those at b_0, the v1 tower being T_(v1,b). The
coefficients and ũ are linear in (G, (W_ν)_(ν∈𝒩″)), conjugation-symmetric when u is real, and bounded at b as follows.
Put w_0 := min(α − 2, λ_♯ − 1). For every small ε > 0, every w ∈ (0, w_0] and every seminorm of the classes
(33.20) and (33.21), that seminorm of the coefficients and of ũ is at most

    C‖G‖_(𝒴^♮(α−ε)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u_0‖_(w) + C Σ_(ν∈𝒩″) |W_ν|,

where ‖·‖_(𝒴^♮(α−ε)) is a seminorm of 𝒴^♮(α − ε) and ‖·‖_(w) one of the space of the hypothesis of Lemma 33.29
with w in place of w_0, both depending on the seminorm bounded (of large enough regularity, as in Section 32.6),
and C depends on ε, w and these seminorms and is uniform in b ∈ ℬ̄_* and in (h, p⃗) small. This is not a bound by G
alone: the second term does not vanish at the reference point (0, p⃗_b) of Lemma 33.17 when b ≠ b_0, and the
W_ν enter as data. Two changes are needed:

- Steps 3 and 4 of the proof use Lemma 33.32 (c) in place of Lemma 33.23, so that the v1 coefficients
  and the early ġ terms enter through the rotation towers T_(v1,b).

- The conormal towers C of Step 1 (viii) include T_(v1,b)(Y^c_v1), and Ẏ_v1 := a_v1 + Y^c_v1. At b the level-3
  conormal rotation tower has the K⁺-rate α_κ + 2 ∈ [3 + η_2 − 2ε, 4), below α, since its bottom h_(b,v1) need not
  vanish. The space (33.20) admits this coefficient (w_v1 = 3 + η_2 − 2ε), and L_b of it has K⁺-order
  α_κ + 5 > α.

The solution of Theorem 33.18 at b_0 and the solution of Proposition 36.8 at b are of this form: the first by
Lemma 32.36 (c), its forcing lying in 𝒴⁰(α) ⊂ 𝒴^♮(α−); the second by Lemma 32.36 (e), the identity
(36.1), whose added term E^ν lies in 𝒴^♮_2(α−), its forcing lying in 𝒴^♮(α−) by Step 2 of the proof of
Proposition 36.8. In both, the three terms of the bound are at most C times a seminorm of the forcing F of that
result: for the first by the remark after the proof of Theorem 33.24, and for the second by the bounds at the
end of Step 3 of the proof of Proposition 36.8.

*Proof.* The proof of Theorem 33.24 uses its setting only through the hypothesis stated here (the remark after
that proof). It uses G through the decomposition of its Step 0 and, in its Steps 2 and 5, through the statement that
the ι⁺-exponents produced lie in ℰ_♯. Both hold at b for G ∈ 𝒴^♮(α−). For G ∈ 𝒴^♮(α) they follow by the argument of
the proof of Proposition 33.31, whose inputs hold at b: Lemma 33.27 concerns only Λ, ℰ_♯ and ℰ^♮, which do
not depend on b, and Proposition 33.28 and Lemma 33.29 are stated at b. The passage to G ∈ 𝒴^♮(α−) is the
argument of the proof of Lemma 34.8: the K⁺-weight of the forcing enters only through β_K = α − ε in Step 0 of
the proof of Proposition 33.15, the K⁺-weight α − ε of f′ in Step 0 of the expansion lemmas and the zf-weights
α − 1 − j − ε of the Taylor levels, each of which a forcing of K⁺-weight α − ε′ for every ε′ > 0 meets for every ε; and
this uses of the base point only the indicial roots and the transition face propositions, uniform in b by
Lemma 30.2 (P2), (P4). Step 0 at b: Lemma 33.29 at β = α (whose hypothesis u_0 = u + Σ_(𝒩″) m_ν(W_ν)
meets with the w_0 of the statement, as in the proof of Theorem 33.18: u has K⁺-weight α − 2 − ε and the ι⁺-
and ℐ⁺-data of (33.13), and the m_ν have K⁺-rates at least λ_♯ − 1 > 0, ι⁺-weight λ_♯ − ε > 3/2 and vanish
near ℐ⁺) gives u_0 = u_I + u_ι + v as there, for the forcing f′ := G − (L_(h,p⃗) − L_b)u_0, the spacetime and spectral v1
terms u^rot_ι and v^rot being polyhomogeneous towers of the types (ii) and (vi) of Step 1; and L_b u has K⁺-order α − ε
by the tower relations, L_b m_ν involving only the top of the tower for the rotation rows as for the other rows (of
K⁺-order Re λ + 4 > α). Step 1 is unchanged at b: its pieces are those of (P2)–(P4). Step 2, the assembly, is unchanged,
with the conormal rotation tower of the second change in C. Step 3 applies Lemma 33.32 (c) in place of
Lemma 33.23 to w := u − χ_K C (L_b(χ_K C) has K⁺-order α − ε, the rotation tower included), and Step 4 reads its
exponents, which are those of Lemma 33.23. Step 5 is unchanged. Step 6 applies its maps, which are uniform in b
by (P1)–(P4) and Lemma 33.32 (c), to f′ and, through Step 1 (iii), to the W_ν, as the remark after the proof of
Theorem 33.24 records. The count of Step 0 of the proof of Lemma 33.16, as in Lemma 33.29
(w − ε + a_K ≥ α), gives ‖(L_(h,p⃗) − L_b)u_0‖_(𝒴⁰(α)) ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u_0‖_(w), with C uniform in b, and 𝒴⁰(α) lies in
𝒴^♮(α − ε) with a bound on the seminorms; so ‖f′‖_(𝒴^♮(α−ε)) ≤ ‖G‖_(𝒴^♮(α−ε)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u_0‖_(w), and Step 6
gives the bound of the statement. Its reality argument holds at b, the towers T_(ψ,b) being real ((P3)). ∎

## 34. Augmentation by the expansion's coefficients and efficient parameterisation

This chapter proves three groups of results on the gauge-fixed Einstein operator in the forward cone, each a part of
[Hin26, Sections 11.8.3 and 12] (pp. 292–318) in dimension 4 + 1.

In Section 34.1–Section 34.3 ([Hin26, Section 11.8.3], pp. 292–296) the parameters of the partial expansion of
Theorem 33.24 become arguments of an augmented gauge-fixed Einstein operator P_5 (Definition 34.2; [Hin26,
Definition 11.63]). Its linearisation in the black hole parameters has the full order of decay at K⁺
(Lemma 34.7 (c); [Hin26, Lemma 11.65]), and the linearised equation at (h, p⃗, q) has, for every right-hand
side, a unique choice of p⃗′ for which the solution splits as h_rem(q′) + h′ with h′ of the decay assumed of h
(Theorem 34.9; [Hin26, Corollary 11.66]).

In Section 34.4–Section 34.5 ([Hin26, Definition 12.1, Section 12.2.1 with Lemma 12.2, Theorem 12.3 and Remarks
12.4–12.6], pp. 296–311) a tuple of data determines (h, p⃗, q) at which P_5 vanishes at ι⁺ to the order 5 + ε_+ and has
the K⁺-order α (Theorem 34.20). The data are the final black hole parameters, the boost and translation, the free
ι⁺-data at each ι⁺-resonance, the conormal remainders of the modification parameters and a remainder tensor.

In Section 34.6–Section 34.7 ([Hin26, Theorem 12.8 and Remark 12.9], pp. 312–318) every solution of the
linearised equation that Theorem 34.9 produces, for a right-hand side of the class ℱ of Definition 34.13, is
D_UΦ(U′) for data U′, so that the map Φ of Theorem 34.20 describes the linear forward solutions exactly
(Theorem 34.24). The tame forms of the estimates of Theorem 34.9 and Theorem 34.24, and their forms at
exact weights, are proved in Chapter 35.

*Dimension 4 + 1.* The argument differs from that of [Hin26] in the following points.

(1) *The linearisation is taken at h, not at h + h_rem(q).* [Hin26] proves [Hin26, Corollary 11.66] by applying [Hin26,
Theorem 11.59] at the background h + h_rem(q), whose K⁺-order is only 2 + ε_K ([Hin26, Remark 11.61]). In dimension 4 +
1 that background has K⁺-order α − 2 − ε, while Theorem 33.18 needs a_K ≥ 4 + ε_K, the remainders r^ν of the rows
need a_K > α + 1 − λ_♯ (Lemma 32.36 (c)), and a perturbation series in q around it loses two derivatives per
term. Instead the forward solution u at h + h_rem(q), which exists and is smooth, satisfies L_(h,p⃗)u = F −
D_(p⃗)P_5(p⃗′) − R_q u, and its decay is raised level by level through the levels of Definition 33.25, each step an
expansion at h, where a_K ≥ 4 + ε_K. The steps are shorter than α − 4, r^ν is only ever taken at h, and the derivatives
of the rows differ only by R_q(h_ν(W)), supported away from K⁺. The new coefficients at each level are the new
parameters up to a small error, as in Theorem 33.18.

(2) *The losses.* The linear theory of Chapter 33 loses an ε at K⁺. The classes are read with the orders "w−", every
order below w (Section 34.1), and the constructions of Theorem 33.18, Theorem 33.24 and
Section 33.13 accept sources of K⁺-order α− and do not depend on the loss (Lemma 34.8). This makes the
class of h′ that of h (Remark 34.10). With a fixed loss, the boost and black hole parameter coefficients would
lose an ε at each application.

(3) *Rotation rows.* At the non-rotating b₀ every rotation is Killing, so the v1 terms of exponent below 2 carry no row
(Section 32.10), and the bookkeeping of [Hin26] would put them into q. But at a rotating b near b₀ the rotation state
h_(b,v1) need not vanish, and such a coefficient would give the linearisation in b the K⁺-order α − 2 + λ_♯ only. These
terms are carried instead by rows of all rotations (Definition 34.3), whose coordinates are fixed in
Theorem 34.9 by the expansion (Step 4′ of its proof). So are the v1 terms of real part 2, whose square would
leave P_5 at a rotating b with the K⁺-order 4 only ((34.15)).

(4) *The exterior family.* [Hin26, (11.228)] contains a tensor χ_−h_(−S), supported there in t_* ≤ 2, which carries the
initial data; [Hin26] permits h_(−S) = 0 in its Section 11.8.3, and we take h_(−S) = 0 throughout this chapter. The
family h_(−S) is built in Proposition 38.4 ([Hin26, (12.33)]). The term is restored in Chapter 38, with a cut-off
χ_−(t^♭_*) supported in {t^♭_* ≤ T̂ + 2}, T̂ ≥ 2 as in Section 38.1, where the map Ψ := (χ_−h_(−S), 0, 0) + Φ is
formed (Definition 38.15): [Hin26, Lemma 12.7], the counterpart of Theorem 34.20 for Ψ, is Lemma 38.16, and
[Hin26, Theorem 12.8] for Ψ, the counterpart of Theorem 34.24, is Lemma 38.17. [Hin26, Corollary 11.67], a
linear stability statement sketched there, is not used in this paper. The linear stability statement proved here is that
of the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini metric g_(b₀), at b₀ only: Theorem 40.4.

(5) *No step at t_*^(−1).* The first step of [Hin26, Section 12.2.1] solves for the t_*^(−1)-term, from the resonance at
λ = 1 and the t_*^(−1)-tail of the black hole. In dimension 4 + 1 the least ι⁺-exponent is λ_♯ = 3/2 + (1 − e_Υ)γ_Υ, a
simple pole with Res_(ι⁺)(L̄, λ_♯) = {0} (Corollary 27.27, Remark 27.37), and the black hole parameters enter
at t_*^(−2). Likewise the first step of the proof of [Hin26, Theorem 12.8] (the t_*^(−3)-terms of the right-hand side)
becomes the removal of the parameters p⃗′_(≤0), and every exponent is then treated by its second step.

(6) *The ι⁺-series below 3 + ε_+ is linear.* Every product of two terms has u-exponent at least 2λ_♯ = 3 + 2δ_♯ > 3 +
ε_+, and the departure of the background from Minkowski space shifts the u-exponent by at least 2. So each step of the
construction is one linear equation L̄ G(λ₀) = −F_0(λ₀) with F_0 depending only on the black hole parameters
(Lemma 34.17), and Φ is affine in the infinite-dimensional data, with coefficients smooth in the black hole, boost
and translation parameters, which gives its smoothness and tame bounds at once. The iteration of [Hin26], nonlinear in
dimension 3 + 1 (its terms of size t_*^(−1) interact), is here a finite sequence of linear model problems.

(7) *The modification parameters* are the rows of Section 32.10 (rates at most 2) with the rotation rows of
Definition 34.3, and the tower coefficients of q (Definition 34.1, rates above 2); the formal solutions at ι⁺ ∩
K⁺ are matched to them by Lemma 33.4 (Lemma 34.18). The conormal V_(1,rem) of [Hin26, (12.11)] has no
counterpart: in dimension 4 + 1 the v1 coefficient of q has no conormal part (Theorem 33.24).

(8) *The resonances used* are those in π_1ℰ_♯: the forward solutions of Theorem 34.9 have ι⁺-exponents in ℰ_♯ and
excite no other, so only these carry data; a pure ι⁺-resonance outside Λ is excited by no right-hand side of the
iteration.

(9) *Orders.* The K⁺-order is α− with α as in Section 34.1, read as there; the ι⁺-order is (3 + ε_+)− for the
metric and (5 + ε_+)− for P_5. The constructions of Chapter 33 give the linear solutions the ι⁺-order (3 + η_2)− with
η_2 < ε_+. Under the condition (G⁺) (Definition 34.11) no exponent lies between, the construction does not depend on
η_2 in that window, and the linear solutions have the ι⁺-order (3 + ε_+)− of the nonlinear class (Lemma 34.23);
without this the scheme would lose ε_+ − η_2 at ι⁺ at every step.

*Base points.* The black hole parameter b ranges near b₀ = (m₀, 0), over the ball ℬ̄_* of Section 34.8.
The coefficients and the augmented operator
(Definition 34.1–Definition 34.3, (34.4)), the towers (Lemma 34.4), the order of L_b
h_(b,rem)(q) (Lemma 34.5 (b)) and the construction of Section 34.4–Section 34.5 are stated and proved
at every such b. Where these proofs use at b a fact that this chapter states at b₀, they cite its form at b:
Lemma 34.5 (a) (Theorem 36.10), the reality of the states (Lemma 30.2 (P3)) and the rate of the
rotation rows (Lemma 36.4).
Lemma 34.5 (a), (c), Lemma 34.6, Lemma 34.7, Lemma 34.8, Theorem 34.9,
Remark 34.10, Lemma 34.23 and Theorem 34.24 are stated and proved at b = b₀, with derivatives in b
taken at b₀. Their forms at a base point whose black hole parameter is near b₀ are proved in Chapter 36;
Section 34.8 states what holds there and where it is proved.

*The inner radius.* Every result of the chapter holds with the inner radius r₀ = r_♭ ∈ (0, ½R₁] of Definition 22.1 as
a parameter, with constants that depend on it. No result names the inner radius: all work on Ω_* = cl_M{t^♭_* ≥ 1}
(Section 29.1) with the spaces of Chapter 14, extendible at the inner boundary, and with the theorems of
Chapter 14–Chapter 20, which hold at every such radius. The fixed radii used are scale-free ({r ≤ 2}, {r ≥ 1}) or far
out (|x| ≥ 5R₁, |x| ≤ 3R₁), and the levels and windows are fixed by weights at infinity and at K⁺.

*Notation.* For a function a of t_*, a′, a″ and a^(j) are its t_*-derivatives; on parameters and tensors (p⃗′, q′, h′,
W′_ν) a prime marks a second element or a direction of linearisation. The double prime of h″ := h + h_(b,rem)(q)
(Definition 34.2), and of the metric g″ built from it, marks the augmented background. The black hole parameter is
b = (m, A), with mass m. The rows of the table of roots are written ψ = (μ, τ), as in Section 33.9. The number of
levels in the proof of Theorem 34.9 is written K; it is unrelated to the K of K⁺, χ_K, K_τ and K_ι(λ).

### 34.1 The coefficients and the augmented operator

Everything of Section 33.9, with w_ψ = 3 + η_2 − 2ε − d_ψ, and of Section 33.12 is kept. α ∈ (4, 4 + ε_K] is
admissible in the sense of Definition 33.3, where Theorem 33.18 and Theorem 33.24 are proved;
Definition 33.25 serves the intermediate levels. The δ_+ of Section 33.9 is taken ≤ η_E := min Re ℰ_ind,
which is positive by the convention for ℰ_ind of Chapter 23. Then 3 + η_2 + η_E > 3 + ε_+, as
η_2 > ε_+ − δ_+ ≥ ε_+ − η_E (Section 33.9). The class 𝒳 is restricted by two requirements, [Hin26, Remark 11.64
(2)]. The first is ℰ_+ ⊃ (ℰ_♯ ∪ ℰ^♮) ∩ {Re < 3 + ε_+}, which can be imposed together with (H1)–(H3) of
Section 32.10, as both sets do not depend on ℰ_+ below 3 + ε_+ (Lemma 33.2 (b), as in Section 33.9).
The second is

    (H5)     a_+ < 3 + η_2.

For a weight w, "order w−" means order w − ε for every ε > 0, and

    Ḣ^(∞,w−)_b := ⋂_ε Ḣ^(∞,w−ε)_b,     𝒴^♮(α−) := ⋂_ε 𝒴^♮(α − ε),

and so on.

**Definition 34.1** (The coefficients; [Hin26, (11.227)].) For ψ ∈ ℛ′ let

    ℰ^α_ψ := {(z, k) ∈ ℰ_♯ − d_ψ : Re z > 2}   (ψ ≠ v1),     ℰ^α_v1 := ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re > 2}.

The v1 terms of exponent in

    ℳ_rot := ℳ ∪ (ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re = 2}),

which is ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re ≤ 2}, are carried by the rotation rows of Definition 34.3. 𝒬 is the real vector space of the
conjugation-symmetric tuples q = (S_rem, b_rem, (Y_ψ)_(ψ∈ℛ′)) with

    S_rem ∈ Ḣ^(∞,(α−2)−)_b([1, ∞]; 𝒮_1),     b_rem ∈ Ḣ^(∞,(α−1)−)_b([1, ∞]; 𝔟),
    Y_ψ ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) Ḣ^(∞,𝒬(ℰ^α_ψ, 3+η_2−2ε−d_ψ))_b([1, ∞]; 𝒴_(ψ,ℂ)).    (34.1)

"q small" means small in one fixed seminorm of large order, at a K⁺-weight a′_K < α − 2 above the level α_1 of Step 1 of
the proof of Theorem 34.9, so that h + h_rem(q) is small in the class 𝒳^d of Section 32.6 with a_K = a′_K.
The rate of a polyhomogeneous term t_*^(−z) of Y_ψ is Re z > 2 for ψ ≠ v1; for v1 it is Re z + 1 > 3 at b₀, where
h_(b₀,v1) = 0, and Re z > 2 at a rotating b. So by the gap (G) of Definition 33.3 (with d_v1 = 0) the rate exceeds
2 + ε_K ≥ α − 2 at every b near b₀.

**Definition 34.2** (Augmentation; [Hin26, Definition 11.63].) For q ∈ 𝒬 and b near b₀ let

    h_(b,rem)(q) := χ_K( h^(≤1)_(b,s1)(S_rem(t_*)) + ġ_b(b_rem(t_*)) + Σ_(ψ∈ℛ′) T_(ψ,b)(Y_ψ(t_*)) ),    (34.2)

with the towers T_(ψ,b) of the table of Section 26.10 for L_b (Definition 26.37, chosen by Lemma 34.4),
with h^(≤2)_(b,v1) for v1, and with ġ_b(ḃ) := ṁ ġ^Υ_b(1, 0) + ġ^Υ_b(0, Ȧ) for ḃ = (ṁ, Ȧ) (Section 28.1). At b = b₀ it
is the tensor χ_K u_exp of (33.19) with the coefficients q. For p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 with black hole parameter b, and h and
q small, put h″ := h + h_(b,rem)(q), the augmented background, and

    P_5(h, p⃗, q) := P_4(h″, p⃗) = P_4(h + h_(b,rem)(q), p⃗)    (34.3)

with P_4 of (32.33). This is [Hin26, (11.228)] with h_(−S) = 0: q and h enter only through h″, both in the
Ricci term and in the gauge term. Since q ↦ h_(b,rem)(q) is linear,

    D_h P_5(h, p⃗, q) = L_(h″,p⃗),     D_q P_5(h, p⃗, q)(q′) = L_(h″,p⃗)(h_(b,rem)(q′)),    (34.4)

which is [Hin26, (11.231)]. We write

    R_q := L_(h″,p⃗) − L_(h,p⃗),     Δ_q := D_(p⃗)P_5(h, p⃗, q) − D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗).

At b = b₀ we write h_rem(q) := h_(b₀,rem)(q).

**Definition 34.3** (Rotation rows.) Let 𝒩_rot := {(rot, λ, k) : (λ, k) ∈ ℳ_rot}, with ℳ_rot of
Definition 34.1, an index set disjoint from the set 𝒩 of rows of Section 32.10, whose v1 rows keep the
coefficient space 𝒱′ = 0. Each ν ∈ 𝒩_rot carries the coefficient space 𝒱_(1,ℂ) of all rotations. For ν = (rot, λ, k) let
a_ν = r_ν = t_*^(−λ)(log t_*)^k, ω_ν, m_ν, h_ν, ϑ_ν and ϑ_(ν,♯) be those that Definition 32.31 assigns to the type v1
and the exponent (λ, k), with W ∈ 𝒱_(1,ℂ); Section 33.2 extends that definition verbatim to every triple. From here
on 𝒫 is the parameter space of Section 32.10 enlarged by the tuples (W_ν)_(ν∈𝒩_rot), conjugation-symmetric (W_(ν̄) =
W̄_ν, ν̄ := (rot, λ̄, k)), and h_tot(p⃗), ϑ_tot(p⃗) of Definition 32.33 are summed over the disjoint union 𝒩 ⊔ 𝒩_rot.
So P_4 and P_5 take p⃗ in the enlarged 𝒫, of which the space of Section 32.10 is the subspace W⃗^rot :=
(W_ν)_(ν∈𝒩_rot) = 0.

At b₀ a rotation row is given the rate Re λ + 1: every rotation is Killing there, so h_v1 = 0, m_ν(W) has K⁺-weight
Re λ + 1 − ε > α − 2 (Lemma 32.32 (e)), and no level of Theorem 33.18 or of Theorem 34.9 eliminates
it; its coordinate is fixed in Theorem 34.9 by the expansion (Step 4′ of the proof). At a rotating b its rate is
Re λ (Lemma 36.4), and the coordinates of the rotation rows are assigned as in Proposition 36.8. The
results of Chapter 32 and Chapter 33 hold with the enlarged 𝒫, except the uniqueness in Theorem 33.18, which
fails there: the solutions form a graph over W⃗^rot (Step 3 of the proof of Theorem 34.9). Theorem 33.18
and Theorem 33.24 are used only with the unknown parameter in the space of Section 32.10 (the background p⃗
may lie in the enlarged one), the rotation-row terms being part of the right-hand side (Step 4′).

Lemma 32.32 (a)–(e) and Lemma 32.34–Lemma 32.36 hold for ν ∈ 𝒩_rot, with e_ν = λ and κ_ν = Re λ +
4: their proofs do not use the coefficient space. Lemma 32.32 (f), the injectivity of h_τ on 𝒲_τ, fails for them,
h_v1 being 0 on 𝒱_1, and is not used for them (Corollary 33.6 excludes v1). Each h_ν(W) is supported in 𝒞 with
ι⁺-exponents in (λ, k) + ℱ ⊂ ℰ_+, as for the v1 rows (v1, λ, k) of 𝒩, which exist as ℳ_rot ⊂ ℰ_par ((33.2));
here (λ, k) + ℱ ⊂ ℰ_+ is (H3) of Section 32.10, which holds below 2 by (32.16) and ℰ_++ + ℰ_ind ⊂ ℰ_++ ⊂
ℰ_+. So (H3) holds and h_tot(p⃗) ∈ 𝒳^∞. Finally, at b = b₀,

    f^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) := D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(W_ν = W) = L_(h,p⃗) m_ν(W) + r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W)

(Lemma 32.36 (b)–(c)), with r^ν_(h,p⃗) of K⁺-weight Re λ + a_K − ε > α and plain ι⁺-weight Re λ + 2 + λ_♯ − ε >
w_+ (Lemma 32.36 (c)). At b ∈ ℬ̄_*, with m_ν built at b, the identity gains the term E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W), of K⁺-weight
κ_ν − ε > α and size O(|b − b₀||W|), and r^ν_(h,p⃗) keeps these orders (Lemma 32.36 (e), which Lemma 36.4
extends to the
rotation rows at b). So these rows enter the constructions exactly as the rows of 𝒩 do.

### 34.2 Properties of the augmented operator

**Lemma 34.4** (Towers near b₀.) For b near b₀ the states of the table of Section 26.10 for L_b and
their companions h̆^((μ),j)_(b,τ) can be chosen smooth in b, equal at b₀ to those of Section 26.10, with leading
terms at ∂X that do not depend on b; the rotation state h_(b,v1) ∈ 𝒜³ is smooth in b and vanishes at b₀; and ġ_b is
smooth in b. Then ∂_b h̆^((μ),j)_(b,τ)(Y) ∈ 𝒜^((μ−j)+ℰ_ind), and for a = χ_+ t_*^(−z)(log t_*)^k the tensor ∂_b(χ_K
T_(ψ,b)(a)) is polyhomogeneous at ι⁺ with exponents in z + d_ψ + ℰ_ind and, for v1, z + 3; all lie in z + d_ψ plus at
most two increments of Λ ((2, 0) ∈ ℰ_ind, Section 32.10).

*Proof.* The pure gauge states and their companions are δ*_(g_b) ω^(≤k)_b with ω^(≤k)_b ∈ ker □^Υ_b polynomial in t_*
and smooth in b (Proposition 23.34). By the remark closing Lemma 23.33 their leading terms at ∂X are the
Minkowski model solutions, which do not depend on b and which (R4) of Section 23.16 fixes uniquely, no root lying at
μ − k. (The tower relations (26.44) alone fix the leading term of a companion only modulo the indicial kernel
at μ − j, Lemma 26.34; it is the construction of Proposition 23.34 that fixes it.) The physical states at −2
(K = 0) are those of Proposition 25.37, smooth in b with the b-independent leading term h̄_τ(Y). Composing each family
with the inverse of the smooth invertible map Y ↦ (its leading coefficient), normalised to be the identity at b₀, keeps
everything at b₀, so Definition 34.2 at b₀ is the tensor χ_K u_exp of (33.19). The corrections lie in
𝒜^((μ−j)+ℰ_ind) with ℰ_ind independent of b (Section 26.11, Proposition 23.34, Proposition 25.37), so their
b-derivatives do too. The rotation state h_(b,v1)(V) = δ*_(g_b) ω^(−1)_(b,v1)(V) ∈ 𝒜³ vanishes at b₀, where every
rotation is Killing (at a rotating b it need not vanish; nothing below uses that it does not); its b-derivative lies in
𝒜³ and gives the ι⁺-exponent z + 3. ġ^Υ_b is the gauge-corrected derivative of the Myers–Perry family, smooth in b; its
leading term may depend on b (through the mass), which is harmless, b_rem having order (α − 1)−. The statement at ι⁺
follows as in Section 33.9: the leading part of T_ψ(a) is homogeneous of degree −z − d_ψ. ∎

**Lemma 34.5** (The augmentation; [Hin26, Remark 11.64].) Let q ∈ 𝒬.

(a) At b = b₀, h_rem(q) is real, linear in q, supported in supp χ_K ∩ {t^♭_* ≥ 10}, so away from ℐ⁺, of K⁺-order (α −
2)−, and at ι⁺ partially polyhomogeneous with exponents in ℰ_♯ ∪ ℰ^♮ to the order (3 + η_2)−, of plain weight ≥ λ_♯;
each of its seminorms is bounded by one of q.

(b) For b near b₀, L_b h_(b,rem)(q) has K⁺-order α−, uniformly and smoothly in b.

(c) Let χ̃ ∈ C^∞(M) vanish near K⁺ and equal 1 near supp(1 − χ_K) (a closed set disjoint from a neighbourhood of K⁺).
Then h + χ̃ h_rem(q) ∈ 𝒳^∞, small for (h, q) small.

*Proof.* (a) By Section 33.9, h^(≤1)_(b₀,s1)(S_rem) has K⁺-order (α − 2)− and ι⁺-order (α + 1)− (h_(b₀,s1) ∈ 𝒜³,
h̆^1_(b₀,s1) ∈ 𝒜²); ġ(b_rem) has K⁺-order (α − 1)− and ι⁺-order (α + 1)− (weights 2 and 3, Section 28.1). A
polyhomogeneous term t_*^(−z) of Y_ψ gives a K⁺-rate > α − 2 (Definition 34.1) and the ι⁺-exponent z + d_ψ ∈ ℰ_♯,
plus the corrections of the profiles, in ℰ^♮; a conormal part of order (3 + η_2 − d_ψ)− gives the ι⁺-order (3 + η_2)−
and a K⁺-order above α − 2. supp χ_K ⊂ {t^♭_* ≥ 10} by (29.2).

(b) By the tower relations for L_b (Lemma 26.38), L_b T_(ψ,b)(Y) consists, near K⁺, of the terms with Y^(k_μ+1)
and Y^(k_μ+2), of K⁺-order at least the rate plus k_μ + 1. This is ≥ λ_♯ + 3 > α for the polyhomogeneous parts and > α
for the conormal ones, as in the proof of Lemma 33.23. Next, with L_1 = [L_b, t_*] and
L_2 = ½[[L_b, t_*], t_*] (Section 31.10),

    L_b h^(≤1)_(b,s1)(S) = S″(L_2 h_(b,s1) + L_1 h̆^1_(b,s1)) + S‴ L_2 h̆^1_(b,s1),

of K⁺-order (α − 2)− + 2; L_b ġ_b(b_rem) = b_rem′ L_1 ġ_b + b_rem″ L_2 ġ_b, of K⁺-order (α − 1)− + 1; and [L_b, χ_K] is
supported away from K⁺. Smoothness in b holds by Lemma 34.4.

(c) χ̃ h_rem(q) vanishes near K⁺, near ℐ⁺ and for t_* < 1. By (a), the requirement ℰ_+ ⊃ (ℰ_♯ ∪ ℰ^♮) ∩ {Re < 3 + ε_+} and
(H5), it has the ι⁺-data (ℰ_+, a_+). ∎

**Lemma 34.6** (The perturbation.) Let b = b₀ and

    u ∈ ⋂_ε H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β′_+,w−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−)

with w > 0 and β′_+ ∈ (3/2 − (δ_♯ − ε_+), 3/2). Then R_q u is supported in supp χ_K, vanishes near ℐ⁺, and lies in
𝒴^0_2(β) for every β < w + α − 2; each seminorm is bounded by C‖q‖ times a seminorm of u, uniformly for (h, p⃗, q)
small.

*Proof.* L_(h″,p⃗) = L^(g″,g_0) with g″ = g_0 + h_tot(p⃗) + h″ (Lemma 32.35), and

    R_q = ∫_0^1 ∂_s L^(g_0+h_tot(p⃗)+h+s h_rem(q), g_0) ds.

The coefficients of L^(g,g_0) are smooth functions of g and its first two derivatives (and of g_0), so R_q is a
second-order operator whose coefficients are linear in h_rem(q) and its first two derivatives, times smooth functions;
it is supported in supp χ_K. As in (29.15) of Proposition 29.12, with h_rem(q) in place of h: at K⁺ the
coefficients have the weight (α − 2)− of h_rem(q) (Lemma 34.5 (a)), so R_q u has K⁺-weight (w + α − 2)−; at ι⁺
they have weight ≥ λ_♯ and each derivative gives a factor ρ_+, so R_q u has the plain weight β′_+ + 2 + λ_♯ − ε > w_+,
as β′_+ > 3/2 − δ_♯ + ε_+; and near ℐ⁺ it vanishes. These are the requirements of 𝒴^0_2(β) (Section 32.10,
Section 33.2), the ι⁺-index set being void below w_+. ∎

**Lemma 34.7** (The parameter derivatives; [Hin26, Lemma 11.65 and Remark 11.64].) At b = b₀, for (h, p⃗,
q) small:

(a) for a row ν and W ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ), Δ_q(W_ν = W) = R_q(h_ν(W)), which has K⁺-order ∞ and plain ι⁺-weight > w_+, and lies in
𝒴^0_2(β) for every β, with norm O(‖q‖|W|);

(b) in the directions S, S^(0)_1, Δ_q takes values in the sections supported in supp χ_K away from K⁺ and ℐ⁺, of plain
ι⁺-weight > w_+, so in every 𝒴^0_2(β), with norm O(‖q‖);

(c) in the direction b, Δ_q(b′) ∈ 𝒴^♮_2(α−) with norm O(‖q‖|b′|); so D_b P_5(h, p⃗, q)(b′) ∈ 𝒴^♮(α−): the linearisation
in b has the full K⁺-order, which is [Hin26, Lemma 11.65].

*Proof.* (a) P_4 depends on W_ν through h_ν(W_ν) in g″ (the metric g′ of (32.33), taken at h″) and through
ϑ_(ν,♯)(W_ν) in ϑ_tot ((32.33)), so

    D_(W_ν)P_5(h, p⃗, q)(W) = L_(h″,p⃗) h_ν(W) + δ*_(g_0,E_C) ϑ_(ν,♯)(W),

and Δ_q = R_q(h_ν(W)). h_ν(W) is supported in 𝒞, whose closure meets ∂M only in a compact subset of (ι⁺)°, and lies in
𝒜^((λ,k)+ℱ) there (Lemma 32.35); the argument of Lemma 34.6 gives the ι⁺-weight ≥ λ_♯ + Re λ + 2 − ε >
w_+.

(b) h_rem(q) does not depend on S, S^(0)_1, so

    Δ_q(S′) = ∫_0^1 (D_S L_(h+s h_rem(q),p⃗))(S′)(h_rem(q)) ds,

where D_S L is the derivative of L^(g″,g_0) in S through g_0 and h_tot(p⃗). By (32.4) g_0 depends on S,
S^(0)_1 only on supp(1 − χ_K), and the terms of h_tot that depend on them are supported in 𝒞 (Lemma 32.6). Their
derivatives have ι⁺-order ≥ 2: ∂_S g_(p⃗) ∈ ρ_+² C^∞ near (ι⁺)° (Lemma 32.4 (c)), and h^(0)_s1(S) ∈ 𝒜^(𝒢+1)
(Lemma 32.6). So Δ_q(S′) is supported in supp χ_K ∩ (supp(1 − χ_K) ∪ cl 𝒞), whose closure meets ∂M only in
(ι⁺)°, with ι⁺-weight ≥ 2 + λ_♯ + 2 − ε > w_+.

(c) On the interior of χ_K⁻¹(1), a neighbourhood of K⁺, g_0 = g_b and h_tot(p⃗) consists of terms supported in 𝒞, and
near K⁺

    P_5(h, p⃗, q) − P_4(h, p⃗) = ∫_0^1 L_(h+s h_(b,rem)(q),p⃗)(h_(b,rem)(q)) ds
                             = L_b h_(b,rem)(q) + ∫_0^1 (L_(h+s h_(b,rem)(q),p⃗) − L_b)(h_(b,rem)(q)) ds,

L_b being the linearisation at g_b. The second term has coefficients of K⁺-order (α − 2)− (h has a_K ≥ 4 + ε_K, h_rem
has (α − 2)−, and the 𝒞-terms vanish near K⁺), applied to a tensor of K⁺-order (α − 2)−, so it has K⁺-order (2α − 4)−,
above α as α > 4. The first has K⁺-order α− by Lemma 34.5 (b), uniformly and smoothly in b, so its b-derivative
has K⁺-order α−. Near K⁺, L_(h+s h_(b,rem)(q),p⃗) = L^(g_b+h+s h_(b,rem)(q),g_b), so, as in the proof of
Lemma 34.6, the coefficients of L_(h+s h_(b,rem)(q),p⃗) − L_b are linear in h + s h_(b,rem)(q) and its first two
derivatives, times smooth functions of g_b and of h + s h_(b,rem)(q). So the b-derivative of the second term at b₀ is a
sum of two kinds of products. The first kind are products of a factor of K⁺-order (α − 2)− (from h_(b₀,rem)(q), or from
h, of order α−) with ∂_b h_(b,rem)(q)b′. The second kind, from the dependence of the coefficients on g_b, are products
of ∂_b g_b(b′) with two such factors: one from the coefficients, which keep their factor h + s h_(b₀,rem)(q), and the
argument h_(b₀,rem)(q). Now ∂_b h_(b,rem)(q)b′ has K⁺-order ≥ 2 − ε. Indeed every coefficient of q has rate > 2 at
every b near b₀ (Definition 34.1: Re z > 2 for ψ ≠ v1 and for v1, whose state h_(b,v1) gives the rate Re z once b
rotates; the conormal parts have rate > 3; S_rem and b_rem the rates (α − 2)− and (α − 1)−), and the states are smooth
in b (Lemma 34.4). So the products of the first kind have K⁺-order ≥ (α − 2)− + 2 = α−; and those of the
second kind, ∂_b g_b(b′) being stationary, have K⁺-order (2α − 4)− > α. This is the argument of [Hin26], with one
change: a v1 coefficient of exponent z ∈ ℳ would give only (α − 2 + Re z)− < α, which is why those terms are carried by
the rotation rows (Definition 34.3). The v1 terms of real part 2 are carried there too, for (34.15), where
their square at a rotating b would have the K⁺-order 4 only.

Away from K⁺, Δ_q(b′) is supported in supp χ_K, away from ℐ⁺, and is

    ∫_0^1 ( (∂_b L)(b′) h_(b₀,rem)(q) + L(∂_b h_(b,rem)(q)b′) ) ds

up to terms quadratic in h_rem. Here ∂_b L has coefficients of ι⁺-order ≥ 2 (∂_b g_b, of weight 2, Section 28.1;
h^(0)(ḃ) ∈ 𝒜^𝒢, Lemma 32.6), giving the plain weight ≥ 2 + λ_♯ + 2 − ε > w_+. And ∂_b h_(b,rem)(q) has the
ι⁺-exponents of Lemma 34.4, in ℰ^♮; below 2 they lie in ℳ, since there ℰ_♯ is ℳ (Section 33.9) and ℳ +
ℰ_ind stays in ℳ below 2. L maps these to the exponents ℰ^♮ + 2, the expansion of L at ι⁺ adding elements of ℰ^ι_ind,
which are increments of Λ. The conormal parts of ∂_b h_(b,rem)(q) are the b-derivatives of T_(ψ,b)(Y^c_ψ) for the rows
with μ_ψ ∈ (−1, 0] (Step 4 of the proof of Theorem 33.24), of ι⁺-order (3 + η_2 + η_E)− by Lemma 34.4
(the leading terms do not depend on b, and the corrections lie η_E further), which L maps to the weight (5 + η_2 +
η_E)− > w_+ (Section 34.1); and those of S_rem, b_rem, of ι⁺-order (α + 3)−. The terms quadratic in h_rem are as in
Lemma 34.6. ∎

**Lemma 34.8** (Sources of order α−; the losses.) Proposition 33.15, Lemma 33.16 and
Theorem 33.18, Theorem 33.24, and Proposition 33.28 and Lemma 33.29 at the level α, hold for
sources in 𝒴^♮(α−), with the same conclusions. The decomposition (33.19) of Theorem 33.24 can be taken
independent of ε, so that its coefficients lie in the classes (33.20) and ũ in (33.21) for every
ε > 0 at once.

*Proof.* The conclusions are statements for every small ε > 0. The K⁺-weight of the right-hand side enters the
constructions only through Lemma 29.32 and Proposition 21.45 (1) with β_K = α − ε (Step 0 of the proof of
Proposition 33.15), through Step 0 of the expansion lemmas (f′ of K⁺-weight α − ε), and through the zf-weights α − 1
− j − ε of the Taylor levels. A right-hand side of K⁺-weight α − ε′ for every ε′ > 0 meets each of these for every ε.

For the independence, fix ε̄ > 0 such that no exponent at hand (of the coefficients of the pieces and of the rows) has
real part in [α − 2 − 3ε̄, α − 2) ∪ [α − ε̄, α); there are finitely many below every bound, and none at α − 2 or α by
admissibility. For ε < ε̄ the constructions do not depend on ε. The zero-energy solves, Proposition 27.55 and
Proposition 27.58 and the inversion at the last level are applied to the same sources: the thresholds 2 + η_1, 2 + η_2
and δ are fixed; the rounds of the loop at level 3 stop when τ > α − 2; and ε enters only the weights in which their
outputs are estimated. The pairs removed in Lemma 33.23 with β = α − ε are those of real part below α − ε̄, and
the exponents dropped in its Step 2 have zero coefficients. The construction at level 3 depends on ε also through the
weights τ_i(ε) = 1 + η_2 + iε_ind − (2 + i)ε, the switch α_τ = min(τ, 2 − δ) (δ fixed independent of ε), the order μ_3 =
τ − ε of the expansions recorded in the zero-energy solve, and the lowering of τ in Step 4 of the proof of
Proposition 33.15. We take ε̄ so small that, for ε < ε̄, none of these crosses an exponent at hand, a root, or a
value excluded in Proposition 27.58: each is affine in ε with nonzero slope, so it crosses each of the finitely many
thresholds at most once. Proposition 27.58 solves (27.57) by Mellin inversion on Re λ = α_τ − 2 − j, and
moving that line without crossing a root does not change the solution; the recorded expansions and the switch are then
the same for every ε < ε̄. So the pieces, the coefficients of (33.19) and ũ are the same for every ε < ε̄,
and the estimates hold for each. ∎

### 34.3 The decay of forward solutions

**Theorem 34.9** ([Hin26, Corollary 11.66] in dimension 4 + 1.) Let h ∈ 𝒳^∞, p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 (b = b₀) and q ∈ 𝒬 be
small, and F ∈ 𝒴^♮(α−). There is a unique p⃗′ ∈ 𝒫 (rotation rows included, Definition 34.3) such that the forward
solution u of

    L_(h+h_rem(q),p⃗) u = F − D_(p⃗)P_5(h, p⃗, q)(p⃗′)    (34.5)

satisfies (33.13):

    u ∈ ⋂_ε H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),β_+,α−2−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−)     for every β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+),

and u = h_rem(q′) + h′ with q′ ∈ 𝒬 (so the v1 coefficient has no term of exponent in ℳ_rot) and

    h′ ∈ ⋂_(ε>0) H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(ℰ_♯,3+η_2−2ε),α−ε)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−),
    D_h P_5(h, p⃗, q)(h′) = F − D_(p⃗)P_5(h, p⃗, q)(p⃗′) − D_q P_5(h, p⃗, q)(q′).    (34.6)

p⃗′, q′ and h′ are linear in F, with bounds uniform for (h, p⃗, q) small.

*Proof.* Write u(p⃗′) for the forward solution of (34.5), and 𝒵_β for the space of (33.13) at the
level β, or of (32.26) for β < 3.

*Step 0 (the forward solution).* L_(h+h_rem(q),p⃗) = L^(g″,g_0) is a wave operator with smooth coefficients, close to
L_(h,p⃗) in every C^k on every slab Ω_(1,T_1). Proposition 17.14 gives a unique forward solution on each slab, as for
L_(h,p⃗) (Lemma 32.34), and these agree. So u(p⃗′) exists, is smooth, and is affine in p⃗′.

*Step 1 (the base level, at h + h_rem(q)).* Fix an admissible α_1 ∈ (2, α − 2) in the sense of Section 32.6. The
hypotheses of Proposition 32.29 on the background ask for K⁺-order only above α_1 (α_1 < min(a_K, 3) there;
Lemma 32.26 and Lemma 32.27 take steps below a_K − 2), so they hold for h + h_rem(q), which has K⁺-order
(α − 2)− and the other data of 𝒳 (Lemma 34.5 (a), (c)). Split p⃗′ = p⃗′_< ⊕ W⃗ with p⃗′_< ∈ 𝒫_(α_1)
(Section 33.8) and W⃗ = (W_ν)_(ν∈𝒩′⊔𝒩_rot). As in the proof of Theorem 33.18 (its paragraph on
Proposition 32.29 for P_4), Proposition 32.29 holds for P_5 at (h, p⃗, q). Indeed P_5 is P_3 at (h + h_rem(q) + Σ_ν
h_ν(W_ν), p⃗_3), the sum over the rows other than the motions (the rotation rows included), up to the term
(∂δ*_(g_0,E_C))ϑ_rows, and in the direction b also up to L(∂_b h_(b,rem)(q)b′). This last term has K⁺-order > α_1:
S_rem and b_rem have the rates (α − 2)− and (α − 1)−, above α_1 < α − 2, every other coefficient of q has
rate > 2 + ε_K ≥ α − 2 at b₀, by (G) and Definition 34.1, and L̂_(b₀)(0)∂_b h_(b,v1) = 0 as h_(b₀,v1) = 0, so
the v1 part has rate ≥ 3. All these terms lie in the class 𝒴(α_1) of Section 32.6 and are O(|W⃗| + ‖q‖); so do
D_(W⃗)P_5 = D_(W⃗)P_4 + Δ_q (Lemma 34.7 (a); Lemma 32.36 (b)) and F (the last sentence of
Lemma 33.29). So for every W⃗ there is a unique p⃗′_<(W⃗) ∈ 𝒫_(α_1), affine in W⃗, with u(p⃗′_<(W⃗) ⊕ W⃗) ∈
𝒵_(α_1). Let 𝒫_0 be the set of these p⃗′: the graph of W⃗ ↦ p⃗′_<(W⃗).

*Step 2 (one level).* Choose admissible levels α_1 = β_0 < β_1 < ⋯ < β_K = α (Section 32.6 below 3,
Definition 33.25 above 3) with β_(k+1) − β_k < α − 4 and β_(K−1) > 4; this is possible as the admissible levels are
dense. Let p⃗′ ∈ 𝒫 with u := u(p⃗′) ∈ 𝒵_(β_k). By (34.5),

    L_(h,p⃗) u = G̃ − D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(p⃗′),     G̃ := F − Δ_q(p⃗′) − R_q u,    (34.7)

and G̃ ∈ 𝒴^♮(β_(k+1)), resp. 𝒴^♮(α−) for k + 1 = K. Indeed R_q u ∈ 𝒴^0_2(β) for β < β_k + α − 4 (Lemma 34.6
with w = β_k − 2; for k = K − 1, β_(K−1) + α − 4 > α), and Δ_q(p⃗′) ∈ 𝒴^♮(α−) (Lemma 34.7). The rows enter
(34.7) through D_(p⃗)P_4 at h, whose defects r^ν_(h,p⃗) have the orders of Lemma 32.36 (c), as a_K ≥
4 + ε_K. At h + h_rem(q) the row directions differ from these by exactly Δ_q(W⃗) = R_q(h_ν(W⃗)) (Lemma 34.7
(a)), supported in 𝒞, so no row defect of the background h + h_rem(q) enters. For β_(k+1) > 3, u_0 := u + Σ_(ν∈𝒩⊔𝒩_rot)
m_ν(W′_ν), with W′_ν the row components of p⃗′ (the motions and the rotation rows included), solves L_(h,p⃗) u_0 = G′,
where

    G′ := G̃ − f^S_(h,p⃗)(S′) − f^b_(h,p⃗)(b′) − f^s1_(h,p⃗)(S^(0)′_1) − Σ_(ν∈𝒩⊔𝒩_rot) r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W′_ν)

lies in 𝒴^♮(β_(k+1)) (Lemma 32.36 (a), (c); Section 33.2), resp. in 𝒴^♮(α−) for k + 1 = K; and u_0 has
K⁺-weight min(β_k − 2, λ_♯ − 1) − ε > 0, with min(β_k − 2, λ_♯ − 1) + a_K > β_(k+1), and ι⁺-weight β′_+.
Lemma 33.29 (with Lemma 34.8 for k + 1 = K) gives
