    u = Σ_(ν∈𝒩_(β_(k+1))) m_ν(C^(k+1)_ν(p⃗′)) + ũ,     ũ ∈ 𝒵_(β_(k+1)),
    C^(k+1)_ν(p⃗′) := S^(h,p⃗,β_(k+1))_ν(G′) − W′_ν,    (34.8)

the m_ν(W′_ν) of the rows outside 𝒩_(β_(k+1)) and of the rotation rows, of K⁺-weight above β_(k+1) − 2
(Definition 34.3), being part of ũ. For β_(k+1) < 3, Lemma 32.27, transferred to P_4 as in Step 1, with
β_(k+1) − β_k < a_K − 2, applied to u gives (34.8) with the motion rows of ℳ_(β_(k+1)) ∖ ℳ_(β_k) and
C^(k+1)_ν the K⁺-coefficient S_(λ,k) of u. In both cases the coefficients of the rows of 𝒩_(β_k) vanish
(Corollary 33.6, as u ∈ 𝒵_(β_k)), and u ∈ 𝒵_(β_(k+1)) if and only if C^(k+1)_ν(p⃗′) = 0 for the rows ν of rate in
[β_k − 2, β_(k+1) − 2), the *new rows* of the level.

*Step 3 (the elimination, level by level).* Let 𝒫_k := {p⃗′ ∈ 𝒫_0 : u(p⃗′) ∈ 𝒵_(β_k)}. We show by induction that 𝒫_k is
the graph of an affine map from the coordinates W_ν of the rows of rate ≥ β_k − 2 to the others. For k = 0 this is
Step 1. On 𝒫_k, C^(k+1) is an affine function of the free coordinates; we claim that in the coordinates of the new rows
it is −id + A_k, with A_k → 0 as (h, p⃗, q) → (0, 0, 0). At the base point, D_(p⃗)P_4(0, 0)(W_ν = W) = L_(b₀) m_ν(W)
(Lemma 32.34), Δ_q = 0 and R_q = 0, so u(p⃗′) = u_F − Σ_ν m_ν(W_ν), with u_F the forward solution of L_(b₀) u_F =
F − D_(p⃗)P_4(0, 0)(p⃗′_<); and p⃗′_<, and the coordinates fixed at the earlier levels, do not depend on the coordinates
of rows of higher rate, as m_ν(W_ν) has no K⁺-coefficient at lower rows (as in the proof of Theorem 33.18, at (0,
0)). So C^(k+1)_ν = C^(k+1)_ν(0) − W_ν there. Near the base point, C^(k+1) depends continuously on (h, p⃗, q), uniformly
for p⃗′ bounded: by Proposition 32.29 (ii) and Lemma 32.28 (the levels below 3), Lemma 33.30 and
Lemma 33.17 for the coefficients, Lemma 32.36 for the r^ν, and Lemma 34.6–Lemma 34.7
for R_q and Δ_q, which are O(‖q‖); and u(p⃗′) is bounded in 𝒵_(β_k) on bounded subsets of 𝒫_k by the induction (finitely
many levels, each losing finitely many derivatives). So −id + A_k is invertible for (h, p⃗, q) small, and C^(k+1) = 0 on
𝒫_k solves for the new coordinates as an affine function of those of higher rate: 𝒫_(k+1) is a graph. At k = K the free
coordinates left are those of the rotation rows (𝒩_α = 𝒩; a rotation row is a new row at no level, its rate Re λ + 1
exceeding α − 2, Definition 34.3): 𝒫_K is the graph of an affine map W⃗^rot ↦ p⃗′(W⃗^rot). *Uniqueness:* if u(p⃗″) ∈
𝒵_α, then u(p⃗″) ∈ 𝒵_(β_k) for all k, so p⃗″ ∈ 𝒫_0 by the uniqueness in Step 1 and then p⃗″ ∈ 𝒫_K; Step 4′ fixes the
rotation coordinates.

*Step 4′ (the rotation coordinates).* For p⃗′ ∈ 𝒫_K split p⃗′ = p⃗′_0 ⊕ W⃗′^rot, with p⃗′_0 in the parameter space of
Section 32.10 (Definition 34.3), and put

    G̃_0 := G̃ − Σ_(ν∈𝒩_rot) f^ν_(h,p⃗)(W′_ν),     so that
    L_(h,p⃗) u = G̃_0 − D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(p⃗′_0)    (34.9)

by (34.7), D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗) being linear. G̃_0 ∈ 𝒴^♮(α−), as f^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) ∈ 𝒴_2(α) (Lemma 32.36 (b),
Definition 34.3). So u = u(p⃗′) ∈ 𝒵_α solves (34.9), whose parameter p⃗′_0 lies in the parameter space
of Section 32.10. By the uniqueness in Theorem 33.18 (Lemma 34.8), p⃗′_0 = p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(G̃_0), and
Theorem 33.24 (Lemma 34.8, Proposition 33.31) applies with F = G̃_0: u = χ_K u_exp + ũ, with ũ of
K⁺-order α− ((33.21)). Let C^rot(p⃗′) be the tuple of the polyhomogeneous coefficients, at the exponents in
ℳ_rot, of the v1 coefficient Ẏ_v1 of u_exp.

*The coefficients are determined by u.* Let ℋ_st be the finite-dimensional space of the stationary tensors

    Σ_ψ h̆^((μ_ψ),0)_(b₀,τ_ψ)(Y_ψ) + h̆^1_(b₀,v1)(V) + ġ(ḃ) + h_(b₀,s1)(S)

of Lemma 33.22 (a), the sum over the rows of ℛ′ other than v1, whose coefficients are unique. Each nonzero
element of ℋ_st is nonzero on an open set, so, the unit sphere of ℋ_st being compact, there is a compact set Z_0 in the
interior of X on which restriction is injective on ℋ_st, and there are continuous linear functionals on C⁰(Z_0) that
return the coefficients; let ℓ be the one returning V. On Z_0, for t_* large, χ_K u_exp is the element of ℋ_st with the
coefficients Ẏ_ψ, Ẏ_v1′, ḃ_rem, Ṡ_rem at t_*, plus the higher terms of the towers, whose coefficients are
t_*-derivatives of these (the v1 bottom is h_(b₀,v1) = 0, and Ẏ_v1 enters through h̆^1_(b₀,v1)(Ẏ_v1′)). Suppose u has
two such expansions with remainders of K⁺-order α−, and let ΔẎ_v1, ΔṠ_rem, … be the differences of their coefficients.
Then ℓ applied to the difference of the expansions gives (ΔẎ_v1)′ plus terms O(t_*^(−3−δ′)), with
δ′ := ½ min(ε_K, α − 4) > 0. The bottoms are removed by ℓ exactly, and what remains is: the remainders (K⁺-order α − ε >
3 + δ′); the derivatives of ΔṠ_rem and Δḃ_rem (order (α − 1)−) and of the other coefficients (rate > 2 + ε_K: every term
of χ_K u_exp has K⁺-order ≥ α − 2 − ε by Theorem 33.24, and (G)); and the second derivative of ΔẎ_v1 (order ≥ Re
λ + 2 ≥ λ_♯ + 2 > 3 + δ′ at the exponents of ℳ_rot, > 4 at the others). The derivative of ΔẎ_v1 at its exponents of real
part > 2, hence > 2 + ε_K, is also O(t_*^(−3−δ′)), while at (λ, k) ∈ ℳ_rot it is triangular in the log power with
diagonal −λ ≠ 0 and has rate Re λ + 1 ≤ 3. As the functions t_*^(−λ−1)(log t_*)^k with Re λ + 1 ≤ 3 are linearly
independent modulo O(t_*^(−3−δ′)), the coefficients of ΔẎ_v1 at ℳ_rot vanish. So C^rot is determined by u, and it is an
affine function of W⃗′^rot, as u is on 𝒫_K.

*The derivative and continuity.* At (0, 0, 0), u = u_F − Σ_ν m_ν(W_ν) (Step 3), where u_F and the m_ν(W_ν) with ν ∉
𝒩_rot do not depend on W⃗′^rot (Step 3). For ν = (rot, λ, k), m_ν(W) is χ_K T_v1(t_*^(−λ)(log t_*)^k W) up to K⁺-order ≥
Re λ + 3 − ε > α: by Lemma 33.4 (a) and the argument of its part (b) for v1, the terms i ≤ 2 of Σ_i a_ν^(i)
h̆^i_v1(W) are the v1 tower of Definition 26.37 at b₀, both being δ*_(g_(b₀)) of the polynomial gauge 1-forms of
Proposition 23.34 (3), with h̆^0_v1 = h_(b₀,v1) = 0; the term i = 3 and the dt_*-term have K⁺-order ≥ Re λ + 3 − ε
((33.3)). Its v1 coefficient is t_*^(−λ)(log t_*)^k W. So C^rot has derivative −id in W⃗′^rot at (0, 0, 0).

Near the base point C^rot tends to its value there, uniformly for W⃗′^rot bounded, by the argument of
Lemma 33.17. Let u_(0) be the solution at (0, 0, 0) with the same W⃗′^rot, and F_tot, F_(tot,(0)) the right
sides of (34.9) for u and u_(0). Then u − u_(0) is the forward solution of

    L_(b₀)(u − u_(0)) = R := F_tot − F_(tot,(0)) − (L_(h,p⃗) − L_(b₀))u,

and R tends to 0 in 𝒴^♮(α−): by the lemmas of Step 3, by which the coordinates of 𝒫_K over W⃗′^rot tend to those at the
base point, and by the count of Lemma 33.17 for the last term. As u − u_(0) ∈ 𝒵_α, its parameter at (0, 0) is 0
(the uniqueness in Theorem 33.18), and Theorem 33.24 at (0, 0), with Proposition 33.8 for the exponents
below 2, bounds its coefficients by R. By the uniqueness just shown, the coefficients of u are those of u_(0) plus those
of u − u_(0). Hence for (h, p⃗, q) small there is a unique W⃗′^rot with C^rot = 0, and this fixes p⃗′.

*Step 4 (the expansion).* With p⃗′ of Step 4′, u ∈ 𝒵_α solves (34.9) with p⃗′_0 = p⃗′_(h,p⃗)(G̃_0) and G̃_0
∈ 𝒴^♮(α−), and R_q u has K⁺-weight (2α − 4)−. Theorem 33.24 with F = G̃_0 (Step 4′) gives u = χ_K u_exp + ũ, with
a decomposition independent of ε. Its coefficients q′ := (Ṡ_rem, ḃ_rem, (Ẏ_ψ)) lie in 𝒬. They lie in the classes
(33.20) for every ε. Every term of χ_K u_exp has K⁺-order ≥ α − 2 − ε, so the polyhomogeneous coefficients of
rate ≤ 2 < α − 2 − ε vanish, which is the condition Re z > 2 of Definition 34.1; and Ẏ_v1 has no exponent in ℳ_rot
(Step 4′), which is its ℰ^α_v1. Conjugation symmetry holds by Step 6 of the proof of Theorem 33.24. Put h′ := ũ,
which satisfies the first statement of (34.6) by (33.21). As χ_K u_exp = h_rem(q′)
(Definition 34.2 at b₀), (34.4) gives

    D_h P_5(h′) + D_q P_5(q′) = L_(h+h_rem(q),p⃗)(h′ + h_rem(q′)) = L_(h+h_rem(q),p⃗) u,

which is (34.6) by (34.5). *Linearity and bounds:* every map used is linear and bounded,
uniformly for (h, p⃗, q) small, and the inverses (−id + A_k)⁻¹ are bounded. ∎

**Remark 34.10** (Orders; [Hin26, Remark 11.64 (1)] and the sentence after [Hin26, Corollary 11.66].) (1)
*The background.* h + h_rem(q) has K⁺-order (α − 2)− only, against a_K ≥ 4 + ε_K for h; Theorem 34.9 never uses
the linear theory at it beyond the levels of Chapter 32 below α − 2 (Step 1), which ask no more.

(2) *The class reproduces.* h′ has the ℐ⁺-data (⟨ℰ^C_I⟩, ℓ_I), the ι⁺-data (ℰ_♯, (3 + η_2)−) and the K⁺-order α−. This
is the class of h if (H2) of Section 32.10 is read as "K⁺-order α−" with α ≤ 4 + ε_K the level used, a_I = ℓ_I (off
the exclusion sets of (H4) of Section 33.2), and a_+ < 3 + η_2 by (H5). Every use of a_K in Chapter 32 and
Chapter 33, and in Section 34.2–Section 34.3, is a strict inequality at an admissible level, or the
membership of f^b_(h,p⃗) in 𝒴_2(α) (Lemma 32.36 (a)), which becomes 𝒴_2(α−) and is accepted by
Lemma 34.8. In Section 34.2–Section 34.3 the inequalities are a_K > α − 2 for the coefficients in the
proof of Lemma 34.7 (c); min(β_k − 2, λ_♯ − 1) + a_K > β_(k+1), β_(k+1) − β_k < a_K − 2 and
Re e_ν + a_K − ε > α for the defects r^ν (Re e_ν ≥ λ_♯ − 1) in Step 2 of the proof of Theorem 34.9. Each holds
with a_K = α − ε for ε small, as β_(k+1) − β_k < α − 4 and β_(k+1) ≤ α. So Theorem 34.9 proves for h′ the
decay at ℐ⁺, ι⁺ and K⁺ that it assumes of h, as [Hin26, Corollary 11.66] does.

(3) *Nonlinear errors.* As in [Hin26], P_5(h, p⃗, q) for general small (h, p⃗, q) is not of the class of F; the
parameterisation that accounts for this is Section 34.4–Section 34.5.

### 34.4 The data space

Everything of Section 34.1 is kept, and through it everything of Chapter 32 and Chapter 33: α, the constants 0 <
ε_K < ε_+ < min(δ_♯, ε_ind) of (32.27), w_+ = 5 + ε_+, η_2, (H1)–(H5), (C5), (G), Λ, k̄(λ), k̄_0, l_*, J_*,
ℰ_par, ℰ_♯, ℳ, ℰ_++, 𝒢 = (2, 0) ∪ (2 + ℰ_ind), ℱ = (0, 0) ∪ ℰ_ind, the rows 𝒩 with the rotation rows 𝒩_rot and the
enlarged 𝒫, the towers T_(ψ,b), ℛ, ℛ′, d_ψ, k_μ, 𝒬, h_(b,rem)(q) and P_5. The black hole parameter b ranges near b₀,
over the ball ℬ̄_* of Section 34.8, and p⃗_(≤0) = (S, b − b₀, S^(0)_1), with g_0 = g_(p⃗_(≤0))
((32.4)). From Chapter 27: the spaces (27.24)–(27.31), the inverse (27.26) of
N_(ι⁺)(L̄, ·) on partially polyhomogeneous spaces, spec^(<ℓ_I)_(ι⁺)(L̄, ℰ^C_I), Corollary 27.30,
Res^k_(ι⁺)(L̄, ℰ^C_I, λ), Res_(ι⁺)(L̄, λ) and the map (27.32). ℓ_I is the one of the class, with
ℓ_I > 3 + ε_+ ((H4) of Section 33.2), and (27.24) holds, s_C being large by (C1). K_ι(λ) denotes the
order of the pole of (27.26) at λ (K(λ) in Proposition 27.36 and in (27.32)). Also from
Chapter 27: the table of Section 26.10, the Minkowski formal solutions (Definition 26.35), Theorem 26.39 and
Lemma 26.41. Two further conditions are imposed, each removing finitely many values.

**Definition 34.11** (The condition (G⁺).) (G⁺) *No λ ∈ Λ has real part in (3, 3 + ε_+].* Λ does not
depend on the constants (Lemma 33.2 (a)), so (G⁺) holds after decreasing ε_+ (with ε_K, η_1, η_2). Every
statement of Chapter 32, Chapter 33 and Section 34.1–Section 34.3 holds for the smaller values
((32.27)), the choices of η_1, η_2, δ_+ and α in Section 33.2–Section 34.1 being made again.

**Definition 34.12** (The condition (A_J).) (A_J) *For every λ₀ ∈ Λ with Re λ₀ < 3 + ε_+, the number ℓ_K(λ₀)
:= α − Re λ₀ is not −Re μ for a root μ of L̂_(b₀)(0), and is not in Re π_1ℰ_K.* Then ℓ_K(λ₀) ∈ (α − 3 − ε_+,
α − λ_♯] ⊂ (0, 3), as ε_+ < δ_♯ < ¼ ((32.27)), so ℓ_K(λ₀) is admissible in Section 27.6 (ℓ^max_K = 3
under (C5), Section 26.10). The admissible α meeting (A_J) are dense in (4 + ε_K − ε′_0, 4 + ε_K] (ε′_0 of
Definition 33.3).

**Definition 34.13** (The classes.) For k ∈ ℕ_0 ∪ {∞}, with the orders read as "w−" (Section 34.1),

    𝒳^k_J := H^(k,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(ℰ_+,(3+ε_+)−),α−)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−),
    ℱ^k := H^(k,(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′,ℓ_I+1),(5+ε_+)−,α−)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−),

the latter with a plain weight at ι⁺; and 𝒬^k_J is the space of tuples (S_rem, b_rem, (Y_ψ)_(ψ∈ℛ′)) with S_rem ∈
Ḣ^(k,(α−2)−)_b, b_rem ∈ Ḣ^(k,(α−1)−)_b and Y_ψ ∈ Ḣ^(k,𝒬(ℰ^α_ψ,(3+ε_+−d_ψ)−))_b. Here ℰ_+ is as in Section 34.1; it
contains ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re < 3 + ε_+}. Since 3 + ε_+ > 3 + η_2, 𝒬^∞_J ⊂ 𝒬; and 𝒳^∞_J is the class of Section 34.1 with
a_+ = (3 + ε_+)− in place of (H5). The class used by Theorem 34.9 is related to these in Lemma 34.23.

**Definition 34.14** (Terms at ι⁺.) A tensor w on Ω_* that is partially polyhomogeneous at ι⁺ has terms
t_*^(−λ)(log t_*)^k w_(λ,k)(R, ω), quasi-homogeneous in the coordinates (t_*, R, ω) near ι⁺. We write

    [w]_λ := Σ_k t_*^(−λ)(log t_*)^k w_(λ,k)

for its *t_*^(−λ)-term*. A term t_*^(−λ−2)(log t_*)^k f of a right-hand side is at the *u-exponent* λ, so [f]_(λ+2) is
the part of u-exponent λ.

By Lemma 26.41, [L_b w]_(λ+2) = L̄[w]_λ when [w]_(λ′) = 0 for Re λ′ ≤ Re λ − 2; here 2L̄(t_*^(−λ)w) =
t_*^(−λ−2)N_(ι⁺)(λ)w, and the cut-off region {|x| ≤ 3R₁} of Lemma 26.41 lies, near ι⁺, in every neighbourhood of
K⁺, where orders are K⁺-orders.

**Definition 34.15** (The data space; [Hin26, Definition 12.1] in dimension 4 + 1.) Let

    Σ := spec^(<3+ε_+)_(ι⁺)(L̄, ℰ^C_I) ∩ π_1ℰ_♯,

a finite set, and ℛ′_0 := {ψ = (μ, τ) ∈ ℛ′ : μ ∈ (−1, 0]} (the rows s0 and s2 at the root 0 and the class rows c0, c1).
For k ∈ ℕ_0 ∪ {∞}, 𝒟^k is the space of tuples

    U = ( b − b₀, S, S^(0)_1, (u^0_λ, f_λ)_(λ∈Σ), S_rem, b_rem, (Y_(ψ,rem))_(ψ∈ℛ′_0), h̃ )    (34.10)

with b ∈ 𝔟; S, S^(0)_1 ∈ 𝒮_1; u^0_λ ∈ Res_(ι⁺)(L̄, λ) and f_λ ∈ Poly^(K_ι(λ))(ℂ_z; H^(k,(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′,≤ℓ_I+1))_b)
((27.31)); S_rem ∈ Ḣ^(k,(α−2)−)_b([1, ∞]; 𝒮_1), b_rem ∈ Ḣ^(k,(α−1)−)_b([1, ∞]; 𝔟), Y_(ψ,rem) ∈
Ḣ^(k,(3+ε_+−d_ψ)−)_b([1, ∞]; 𝒴_ψ); and h̃ ∈ H^(k,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(3+ε_+)−,α−)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−). The components are real,
except (u^0_λ, f_λ), which are conjugation-symmetric: (u^0_λ̄, f_λ̄) is the complex conjugate of (u^0_λ, f_λ). Put

    u_λ := u^0_λ + res_(z=λ)( t_*^(−z) N_(ι⁺)(z)⁻¹ f_λ(z) ),

the image under (27.32); U_0 := (b − b₀, S, S^(0)_1); and U_1 the remaining components. The seminorms are
those of the components, at every loss ε > 0 in the orders "w−".

**Lemma 34.16** (The exponents of the data.) For λ ∈ Σ, K_ι(λ) ≤ 2l_* + 1, and

    u_λ = Σ_(j<K_ι(λ)) t_*^(−λ)(log t_*)^j u^(λ,j)

with (λ, j) ∈ ℰ_♯ for j < K_ι(λ), and u^(λ,j) ∈ H^(k−l,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(ℰ_K,ℓ_K))_b(ι⁺) for ℓ_K < ℓ^max_K, with l of
Proposition 27.36.

*Proof.* The order of the pole of (27.26) at λ is at most the order of λ in Spec_(ι⁺)(L̄) plus k(ℰ^C_(I,♯),
λ) + 1 (Proposition 27.25; [Hin26, Proposition 9.15]), and l_* bounds both the orders of the poles of N_(ι⁺)(L̄, ·)⁻¹
and the log orders of ℰ^C_I (Definition 33.1); so K_ι(λ) ≤ 2l_* + 1, and the residue of a pole of order K_ι(λ) has
log powers below K_ι(λ) (as does u^0_λ, a residue of a pole of N_(ι⁺)(L̄, ·)⁻¹). For Re λ ≥ 2: λ ∈ Λ (as Σ ⊂ π_1ℰ_♯) and
j ≤ 2l_* < k̄(λ), so (λ, j) ∈ ℰ_♯. For Re λ < 2: spec_(ι⁺)(L̄) ⊂ {Re ≥ 2} (Lemma 26.29 (a)), so λ ∈ {λ_♯} ∪
π_1ℰ^C_I (Corollary 27.27), with K_ι(λ_♯) = 1 and K_ι(z) ≤ k(ℰ^C_I, z) + 1 for z ∈ π_1ℰ^C_I, z ≠ λ_♯ (the pole bound
of Proposition 27.25, with m_ι = 0 below 2). And ℰ^♯_+ contains (λ_♯, 0) and, for each z ∈ π_1ℰ^C_I, the extended
union taken k(ℰ^C_I, z) + 1 times ((29.32)), so (λ, j) ∈ ℰ^♯_+ ∩ {Re < 2} ⊂ ℳ
((32.16)–(32.17)). The regularity is Proposition 27.36. ∎

### 34.5 Approximate solutions from data

Let U ∈ 𝒟^∞ be small. The construction assigns to the exponents λ₀ ∈ Λ_* := Λ ∩ {Re < 3 + ε_+}, a finite set, in order
of increasing real part (exponents of equal real part together; their equations below are independent), a correction
h_(λ₀), quasi-homogeneous of degree λ₀ in t_*⁻¹, row coordinates W_ν for the rows ν = (τ, λ₀, j) of 𝒩 and (rot, λ₀, j)
of 𝒩_rot, and the polyhomogeneous coefficients of q at the exponents (λ₀ − d_ψ, j); and then

    h := χ_ι Σ_(λ∈Σ) u_λ + h̃ + χ_ι Σ_(λ₀∈Λ_*) h_(λ₀),     p⃗ := (U_0, (W_ν)),
    q := ( S_rem, b_rem, (Y_(ψ,rem) (ψ ∈ ℛ′_0)) + (the polyhomogeneous coefficients) ),    (34.11)

with χ_ι the cut-off of Section 26.13. The rows m_ν here are those built at b₀ (Definition 32.31,
Definition 34.3); the towers are T_(ψ,b). For (h, p⃗, q) of the form (34.11), and for each λ₀, put

    G(λ₀) := [ h + Σ_(ν∈𝒩⊔𝒩_rot) m_ν(W_ν) + h_(b,rem)(q) ]_(λ₀),     F_0(λ₀) := [ P_4(0, p⃗_(≤0)) ]_(λ₀+2),

the latter with every row coordinate 0.

**Lemma 34.17** (The ι⁺-terms below 3 + ε_+.) For (h, p⃗, q) of the form (34.11), with U small,
P_5(h, p⃗, q) is partially polyhomogeneous at ι⁺ to the weight (5 + ε_+)−, with u-exponents in Λ, and for λ₀ ∈ Λ_*

    [ P_5(h, p⃗, q) ]_(λ₀+2) = F_0(λ₀) + L̄ G(λ₀).    (34.12)

F_0(λ₀) depends only on p⃗_(≤0), smoothly; it vanishes unless λ₀ ∈ π_1𝒢, and its coefficients are compactly supported in
(ι⁺)°.

*Proof.* Write P_5(h, p⃗, q) = P_4(h″, p⃗) ((34.3)), and Taylor-expand P_4 at (0, p⃗_(≤0) ⊕ 0) in h″ and
in the row coordinates W:

    P_4(h″, p⃗) = P_4(0, p⃗_(≤0)) + L_(0,p⃗_(≤0)) h″ + Σ_ν D_(W_ν)P_4(0, p⃗_(≤0))(W_ν) + Q,

with Q at least quadratic in (h″, W). Every term of h″ and every h_ν(W_ν), m_ν(W_ν) has ι⁺-order at least λ_♯: u_λ and
h_(λ₀) as Λ ⊂ {Re ≥ λ_♯} (Lemma 33.2 (a)); h̃ by its class; the rows by Lemma 32.32 (b) (with
Definition 34.3); the towers by Lemma 34.5 (a) (at b, Theorem 36.10). Q is of order two in its
arguments and their first two derivatives, each derivative giving a factor ρ_+ at ι⁺, so its u-exponents are at least
2λ_♯ = 3 + 2δ_♯ > 3 + ε_+ (ε_+ < δ_♯, (32.27)), and it has the weight (5 + 2δ_♯)− > w_+.

L_(0,p⃗_(≤0)) = L^(g_0+h_tot(p⃗_(≤0)),g_0) differs from L_(b₀) by coefficients of ι⁺-order at least 2: g_0 − g_(b₀) and
h_tot(p⃗_(≤0)) have ι⁺-order ≥ 2 ((32.4) and Lemma 32.6, Lemma 32.35). And L_(b₀) differs from
L̄, near ι⁺ away from K⁺, by the term t_*^(−λ−4)v²Bw of (26.53). So for a term w of ι⁺-order ≥ λ_♯,
[L_(0,p⃗_(≤0)) w]_(λ₀+2) = L̄[w]_(λ₀) for Re λ₀ < λ_♯ + 2, a range which contains Λ_*. Likewise D_(W_ν)P_4(0,
p⃗_(≤0))(W) − D_(W_ν)P_4(0, 0)(W) consists of terms linear in W, of size O(|p⃗_(≤0)||W|) (through g_0, h_tot(p⃗_(≤0))
and δ*_(g_0,E_C), (32.33)), of u-exponent ≥ λ_♯ + 2; and D_(W_ν)P_4(0, 0)(W) = L_(b₀) m_ν(W)
(Lemma 32.34; for the rotation rows Definition 34.3), so its term of u-exponent λ₀ is L̄[m_ν(W)]_(λ₀).
Summing gives (34.12).

The conormal remainders: h̃ and the conormal parts of q have ι⁺-order (3 + ε_+)− (Lemma 34.5 (a), at b by
Theorem 36.10, with 3 + ε_+ for 3 + η_2; S_rem, b_rem give (α + 1)−), which L_(0,p⃗_(≤0)) maps to the weight (5 +
ε_+)−. The terms of the rows of u-exponent ≥ 3 + ε_+ have the weight w_+ (Lemma 32.36 (b): the plain weight a_+ +
Re λ + 2 − ε). And P_4(0, p⃗_(≤0)) is smooth in p⃗_(≤0) and supported in supp dχ_K: there g_0 is a pulled-back
Myers–Perry metric, so Ric(g_0) = 0 off supp dχ_K ((32.4)), and h_tot(p⃗_(≤0)), ϑ_tot(p⃗_(≤0)) are supported
in supp dχ_K (Definition 32.7), a set whose closure meets ι⁺ in a compact subset of (ι⁺)° (χ_K is a function of R near
ι⁺, equal to 1 near R = 0 and to 0 near ℐ⁺). Its ι⁺-exponents lie in 𝒢 (Lemma 32.6, Lemma 32.35), and
those of every other term lie in Λ (Lemma 34.19, which (34.12) does not use). ∎

**Lemma 34.18** (Rows and towers at ι⁺.) Let λ₀ ∈ Λ_* and j ∈ ℕ_0.

(a) Let ν = (τ, λ₀, j), whose ι⁺-exponent is λ₀ (Lemma 32.32 (b)), with τ ∈ 𝒯 ∖ {v1}; put μ_s0 = μ_s2 := 0, μ_s1
:= −1, and μ_c0, μ_c1 the class roots; and let W ∈ 𝒲_(τ,ℂ). Then [m_ν(W)]_(λ₀) is χ_K times t_*^(−λ₀) times a finite sum
Σ_(i≤j)(log t_*)^i φ_i, whose expansion as R → 0 is the formal solution of Theorem 26.39 of type τ at the root μ_τ
with coefficient c_τ(λ₀)W in the top log power j, plus formal solutions of the same type with lower log powers, plus
terms of K⁺-order ≥ Re λ₀ + 3. Here c_s1(λ₀) = λ₀(λ₀ − 1) and c_τ = 1 otherwise. The same holds for the rotation rows
ν = (rot, λ₀, j), (λ₀, j) ∈ ℳ_rot, W ∈ 𝒱_(1,ℂ), with the v1 formal solution and c_v1 = −λ₀.

(b) For ψ = (μ, τ) ∈ ℛ′ and Y ∈ 𝒴_ψ, [χ_K T_(ψ,b)(t_*^(−(λ₀−d_ψ))(log t_*)^j Y)]_(λ₀) is χ_K times the formal solution
of type τ at μ with coefficient Y (and, for v1, coefficient −λ₀Y) in the top log power, plus lower log powers, plus
terms of K⁺-order ≥ Re λ₀ + 3; it does not depend on b.

*Proof.* (a) By Lemma 33.4 (a),

    m_ν(W) = χ_K( Σ_(i≤K_τ) a_ν^(i) h̆^i_τ(W) + a_ν^(K_τ+1) dt_* ⊗_s ω̆^(K_τ)_τ(W) ).

The stationary tensors h̆^i_τ are polyhomogeneous at ∂X with leading terms homogeneous of degree μ_τ − i (for s1 the
leading orders are ρ³, ρ², then ρ^(1−i) for i ≥ 2; for s0, h̆^0_s0 = 0 and h̆^(i+1)_s0 has degree −i), the Myers–Perry
corrections being smaller by ℰ_ind (Section 26.11.2, Lemma 33.4 (b), (32.31)); and a_ν^(i) is a
combination of t_*^(−e_ν−i)(log t_*)^(i′), i′ ≤ j. Write h̆̄ for the leading term at ∂X of a stationary tensor h̆, as in
Section 26.11.2. Near ι⁺, r = Rt_*, so a_ν^(i) h̆̄^i_τ is quasi-homogeneous of degree λ₀ in t_*⁻¹ (for s0, s2, c0,
c1, e_ν + μ_τ = λ₀, as d_τ = −μ_τ; for s1, whose h̆̄^i has degree 1 − i, e_ν + 1 = λ₀; for v1, e_ν = λ₀) and has
K⁺-order Re e_ν + i; the corrections have u-exponents in λ₀ + ℰ_ind. For s1 the terms i = 0, 1 (ρ³, ρ²) have u-exponent
λ₀ + 2, and the rest is

    Σ_(i≥2) a_ν^(i) h̆̄^i_s1 = h̄^(≤K_s1)_s1(a_ν″),     a_ν″ = λ₀(λ₀ − 1) t_*^(−λ₀−1)(log t_*)^j + ⋯

((26.48)). For s0, where a_ν = A_ν with A_ν′ = r_ν (Definition 32.31), Σ_(i≥1) A_ν^(i) h̆̄^i_s0 = Σ_i r_ν^(i)
h̆̄^(i+1)_s0 with r_ν = t_*^(−λ₀)(log t_*)^j. For s2, c0, c1, Σ_i a_ν^(i) h̆̄^i_τ = h̄^((μ_τ),≤K_τ)_τ(a_ν) with a_ν =
t_*^(−λ₀+μ_τ)(log t_*)^j. Comparing with (26.51) of Theorem 26.39 (and its (log t_*)^j-version,
Corollary 27.30 (2)): the terms with i ≤ k_(μ_τ) (for s1 the convention h̄^(≤3)_s1, i ≤ 3) are the formal solution,
with coefficient c_τ(λ₀)W in the top log power; derivatives of (log t_*)^j produce the lower powers; and the terms with
i > k_(μ_τ) and the dt_*-term have K⁺-order ≥ Re e_ν + k_(μ_τ) + 1 ≥ Re λ₀ + 3 (the table of Section 26.10: k_μ ≥ 2 +
μ, and for s1, k = 3). For the rotation rows the same argument applies with h̆^0_v1 = h_(b₀,v1) = 0
(Definition 34.3): Σ_(i≥1) a_ν^(i) h̆̄^i_v1 = h̄^(≤K_v1)_v1(a_ν′) ((26.48)), with a_ν′ = −λ₀
t_*^(−λ₀−1)(log t_*)^j + ⋯.

(b) T_(ψ,b) = h^((μ),≤k_μ)_(b,τ) (Definition 26.37), whose leading part at ∂X is the Minkowski tower of
Definition 26.35 and does not depend on b (Lemma 34.4). Take a = t_*^(−λ₀+μ)(log t_*)^j Y for ψ other than
v1; for v1, h^(≤2)_(b,v1)(a) has the leading part h̄^(≤2)_v1(a′), a = t_*^(−λ₀)(log t_*)^j Y ((26.48),
(26.50)), and h_(b,v1) ∈ 𝒜³ contributes at u-exponent ≥ λ₀ + 3. ∎

#### 34.5.1 The step at an exponent λ₀

Suppose every choice for the exponents of real part below Re λ₀ is made. Let T(λ₀) := G(λ₀) computed with these choices
only (no datum, correction, row or coefficient at λ₀ itself): the t_*^(−λ₀)-terms of the rows and towers already chosen,
which arise from their Myers–Perry corrections (λ₀ ∈ λ + π_1ℰ_ind). Put

    f := −F_0(λ₀) − L̄ T(λ₀),     v := u_(λ₀) + 𝒮_(λ₀)(f),

with u_(λ₀) := 0 if λ₀ ∉ Σ, and 𝒮_(λ₀)(f) the solution of L̄𝒮 = f that Corollary 27.30 (1), which solves 2L̄u = ·,
gives for 2f, with ℓ_K = ℓ_K(λ₀). By Corollary 27.30 (2) and Remark 27.32, v = χ_K v_0 + ṽ, with v_0 a sum of
formal solutions of Theorem 26.39 (with powers (log t_*)^i, i bounded as in Corollary 27.30 (2)) at the roots μ
∈ 𝒲(ℓ_K(λ₀)), and ṽ a sum of terms t_*^(−λ₀)(log t_*)^i H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),ℓ_K(λ₀))_b(ι⁺), so of K⁺-order α−. Each
formal solution in v_0, of type τ at the root μ, has K⁺-order Re(λ₀ − μ) < α, as −Re μ < ℓ_K(λ₀), and is carried below
by a row or a tower, of rate Re(λ₀ − μ), except for the boost row s1 (rate Re λ₀ − 1) and for v1 at a rotating b (rate
Re λ₀). We assign, top log power first:

(i) the terms of type τ ∈ 𝒯 ∖ {v1} at μ_τ whose row has rate Re e_ν ≤ 2 to the row ν = (τ, λ₀, i), with W_ν := c_τ(λ₀)⁻¹
times the coefficient; by (G) these are all the s1, s0, s2, c0, c1 terms of rate ≤ 2 + ε_K, and the s1 terms have Re λ₀
≤ 3;

(ii) the v1 terms with Re λ₀ ≤ 2, whose exponents lie in ℳ_rot (Lemma 34.19; Definition 34.1), to the rotation
row (rot, λ₀, i), with W := c_v1(λ₀)⁻¹ times the coefficient;

(iii) every other term, of type τ at μ with rate in (2, α) (the s0, s2, c0, c1 terms of rate > 2, the v1 terms with Re
λ₀ > 2, and the rows of the table of Section 26.10 with μ ≤ −1 other than s1 and v1, of rate ≥ Re λ₀ + 1 > 5/2), to
the coefficient of Y_ψ, ψ = (μ, τ), at the exponent (λ₀ − d_ψ, i): the coefficient itself (for v1, −λ₀⁻¹ times it).

Since the lower log powers that each assignment produces (Lemma 34.18) are of the same type, the assignment
proceeds downward in the log power and is unique. Let R(λ₀) be the sum of [m_ν(W_ν)]_(λ₀) and [χ_K T_(ψ,b)(·)]_(λ₀) over
the rows and coefficients just assigned, and put

    h_(λ₀) := 𝒮_(λ₀)(f) − R(λ₀).

Then [h]_(λ₀) = u_(λ₀) + h_(λ₀) = v − R(λ₀) has, by Lemma 34.18, the same formal solutions removed, so it is ṽ
plus terms of K⁺-order ≥ Re λ₀ + 3 > α: its K⁺-order is α−. And G(λ₀) = [h]_(λ₀) + R(λ₀) + T(λ₀) = v + T(λ₀), so by
(34.12) and L̄u_(λ₀) = 0

    [ P_5(h, p⃗, q) ]_(λ₀+2) = F_0(λ₀) + L̄ 𝒮_(λ₀)(f) + L̄ T(λ₀) = 0.    (34.13)

The choices at higher real part change no t_*^(−λ₀)-term: their own terms and their corrections have u-exponents of
larger real part.

The hypotheses of Corollary 27.30 hold. First, Re λ₀ < 3 + ε_+ < ℓ_I. Second, ℓ_K(λ₀) is admissible by (A_J)
(Definition 34.12). Third, f has no ℐ⁺-expansion: it vanishes near ℐ⁺ ∩ ι⁺, as F_0 is supported in supp dχ_K and the
rows and towers in supp χ_K. Fourth, the coefficients of f have K⁺-order ≥ α, so they lie in H^(∞,ℓ_K(λ₀)−2)_b at R = 0:
F_0 is compactly supported in (ι⁺)°, and L̄T(λ₀) = [L_(b₀) Σ m_ν + L_b χ_K Σ T_(ψ,b)]_(λ₀+2) by the proof of
Lemma 34.17 ([L_b w]_(λ+2) = L̄[w]_λ as for L_(b₀), L_b − L̄ raising the u-exponent by 2 near ι⁺ away from K⁺,
(26.53)). Here L_(b₀) m_ν = f^ν_(0,0) has K⁺-weight κ_ν − ε > 9/2 > α (Lemma 32.32 (d)), and L_b
T_(ψ,b)(a) consists of the terms with a^(k_μ+1), a^(k_μ+2), of K⁺-order ≥ Re λ₀ + 3 (Lemma 26.38), the
commutators with χ_K being supported away from K⁺. As f has no ℐ⁺-expansion, (27.26) acts on it as the inverse
of Theorem 26.27 (2) (the construction of Proposition 27.25 with f of plain ℐ⁺-weight), whose poles lie in
spec_(ι⁺)(L̄) ⊂ {Re ≥ 2}: below 2, 𝒮_(λ₀) raises no log power, and above 2 it raises it by at most l_*.

In particular no right-hand side f of a step carries the exceptional term v^(1+λ_♯)e₇ at ℐ⁺ ∩ ι⁺ of Section 27.7,
and the pole of (27.26) at λ_♯ enters the construction only through the datum f_(λ_♯).

**Lemma 34.19** (The log count.) Every exponent (λ₀, i) of the construction (of [h]_(λ₀), of the rows
assigned, and of the coefficients of q, shifted by d_ψ) lies in ℰ_♯; the rows assigned lie in 𝒩 ⊔ 𝒩_rot, and the
coefficients of q in 𝒬^∞_J.

*Proof.* By induction over Λ_* in order of real part. The log powers at λ₀ come from: the data u_(λ₀), ≤ 2l_*
(Lemma 34.16); F_0(λ₀), ≤ k̄_0 (𝒢, Definition 33.1); the corrections of rows and towers chosen at λ < λ₀, ≤
k̄(λ) + l_* by induction, as λ₀ ∈ λ + π_1ℰ_ind and the log orders of ℰ_ind are ≤ l_*; and 𝒮_(λ₀) adds at most l_* for Re
λ₀ ≥ 2 and nothing below 2. For Re λ₀ ≥ 2, λ₀ ∈ Λ has n(λ₀) ≥ n(λ) + 1 for each such λ, so k̄(λ₀) ≥ k̄(λ) +
(J_* + 1)(l_* + 1) ≥ k̄(λ) + 2l_* and k̄(λ₀) ≥ k̄_0 + (J_* + 1)(l_* + 1): every log power is ≤ k̄(λ₀). Below 2: the data
lie in ℳ (Lemma 34.16), F_0(λ₀) = 0 (𝒢 ⊂ {Re ≥ 2}), the corrections of terms at exponents in ℳ lie in ℳ + ℰ_ind,
which below 2 is in ℳ ((32.16), Section 33.9), and no log is raised. So (λ₀, i) ∈ ℰ_♯. The rows: a row
assigned in (i) is (τ, λ₀, i) with (λ₀, i) ∈ ℰ_♯ and Re λ₀ ≤ 3 (its rate Re λ₀ + d_τ ≤ 2, d_τ ≥ −1), hence (λ₀, i) ∈
ℰ_par ((33.2)) and ν ∈ 𝒩; the rotation rows of (ii) are in 𝒩_rot, their exponents lying in ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re ≤ 2} =
ℳ_rot. The coefficients of (iii): (λ₀ − d_ψ, i) ∈ ℰ_♯ − d_ψ with rate > 2, which is ℰ^α_ψ (Definition 34.1; for v1,
Re λ₀ > 2), and Re(λ₀ − d_ψ) < 3 + ε_+ − d_ψ, below the conormal order of 𝒬^∞_J. ∎

**Theorem 34.20** ([Hin26, Theorem 12.3] in dimension 4 + 1.) There are d ∈ ℕ and ε_0 > 0 such that for U ∈
𝒟^∞ with ‖U‖_(𝒟^d) < ε_0 the construction defines

    Φ(U) = (h, p⃗, q) = Φ_0(U_0) + A(U_0)U_1 ∈ 𝒳^∞_J × 𝒫 × 𝒬^∞_J,    (34.14)

with Φ_0 smooth on {|U_0| < ε_0}, Φ_0(0) = 0, and A(U_0) linear, smooth in U_0, and bounded from the U_1-components of
𝒟^(k+d) to 𝒳^k_J × 𝒫 × 𝒬^k_J for every k, with bounds uniform in |U_0| < ε_0. So Φ extends continuously to 𝒟^(k+d) →
𝒳^k_J ⊕ 𝒫 ⊕ 𝒬^k_J, is smooth (in particular N-fold differentiable for every N), and is tame: ‖Φ(U)‖_k ≤
C_k‖U‖_(𝒟^(k+d)). Moreover

    P_5(Φ(U)) ∈ ℱ^(k−2)     for U ∈ 𝒟^(k+d),    (34.15)

and:

(1) the components S, b − b₀, S^(0)_1 of p⃗ are those of U;

(2) the components S_rem, b_rem of q are those of U, the conormal part of Y_ψ is Y_(ψ,rem) for ψ ∈ ℛ′_0 and 0 otherwise,
and replacing h̃ by h̃ + h̃′ replaces h by h + h̃′;

(3) if U and U′ differ only in (u^0_(λ₀), f_(λ₀)), by (u′^0, f′), and u′_(λ₀) is the image of (u′^0, f′) under
(27.32), then (h′, p⃗′, q′) := Φ(U′) − Φ(U) has: h′ with ι⁺-terms only at exponents of real part ≥ Re λ₀; no
row or coefficient of q at an exponent of real part below Re λ₀; and [h′]_(λ₀) = u′_(λ₀) − R′(λ₀), where R′(λ₀), the
t_*^(−λ₀)-term of the rows and coefficients of (p⃗′, q′) at λ₀, has the same formal solutions at R = 0 as u′_(λ₀) of
rate below α;

(4) Φ commutes with conjugation: h and q are real and the row coordinates conjugation-symmetric.

*Proof.* The construction is well defined by Lemma 34.17–Lemma 34.19 and Corollary 27.30.

*Membership.* h: its ℐ⁺-data are (⟨ℰ^C_I⟩, ℓ_I) (those of the u_λ, 𝒮_(λ₀)(f) and h̃; the R(λ₀) vanish near ℐ⁺); at ι⁺ it
is partially polyhomogeneous with exponents in ℰ_♯ ⊂ ℰ_+ (Lemma 34.19) to the order (3 + ε_+)− (that of h̃); at K⁺
each [h]_(λ₀) has order α− (the step at λ₀), so χ_ι[h]_(λ₀) does, and h̃ does. p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 and q ∈ 𝒬^∞_J by
Lemma 34.19.

*(34.15).* At ι⁺: by Lemma 34.17 and (34.13), every u-exponent of real part below 3 + ε_+ has
vanishing term, so P_5(Φ(U)) has the plain weight (5 + ε_+)−. At ℐ⁺: h + h_(b,rem)(q) + h_tot(p⃗) is small in the class
(29.4) with the ℐ⁺-data (⟨ℰ^C_I⟩, ℓ_I), the rows and towers vanishing near ℐ⁺, so Corollary 29.14 gives the
ℐ⁺-order (⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′, ℓ_I + 1). At K⁺: near K⁺, g_0 = g_b, the rows enter only through ϑ_(ν,♯), of K⁺-weight κ_ν − ε > α
(Lemma 32.32 (d); h_ν is supported in 𝒞), and

    P_5 − P_4(h, p⃗) = L_b h_(b,rem)(q) + ∫_0^1 (L_(h+s h_(b,rem)(q),p⃗) − L_b) h_(b,rem)(q) ds,

with L_b h_(b,rem)(q) of K⁺-order α− (Lemma 34.5 (b)) and the integral of K⁺-order (2α − 4)− > α at every b
near b₀, as in the proof of Lemma 34.7 (c). Indeed h_(b,rem)(q) has K⁺-order (α − 2)− there, its v1 part
included, whose exponents have real part > 2, hence > 2 + ε_K ≥ α − 2 by (G), even where h_(b,v1) does not vanish
(Definition 34.1; the v1 terms of real part ≤ 2 are those of the rotation rows, which enter only through h_ν and
ϑ_ν). And P_4(h, p⃗) near K⁺ is Ric(g_b + h) − δ*_(g_b,E_C)(Υ(g_b + h, g_b) − ϑ_tot), whose linear part L_b h has
K⁺-order α− (h has it; L_b is stationary), and whose nonlinear part has K⁺-order ≥ 2(α−).

*Structure.* Given U_0, every map of the construction is linear in U_1: F_0 depends on U_0 only (Lemma 34.17), and
T(λ₀), 𝒮_(λ₀), the coefficient functionals of Theorem 26.39 and Corollary 27.30 (2), the assignment and R(λ₀)
are linear. The dependence on U_0 is through F_0, smooth in p⃗_(≤0), and through the towers T_(ψ,b), smooth in b
(Lemma 34.4). This is (34.14), Φ_0(U_0) being the construction with U_1 = 0.

*Bounds.* There are finitely many steps. Each uses Corollary 27.30 on a strip containing λ₀, with a fixed loss of
b-regularity there (Proposition 27.25), the functionals of Theorem 26.39 (continuous on H^(k+2)_b) and
Proposition 27.36 (loss l); d is the sum of these losses plus 2. The bounds are uniform for |U_0| small, since F_0 and
the towers are. As U_0 is finite-dimensional, |U_0| ≤ C‖U‖_(𝒟⁰), and the tame bound follows from (34.14).

*(1), (2)* hold by (34.11). *(3)* By linearity in U_1, Φ(U′) − Φ(U) = A(U_0)(0, …, (u′^0, f′), …, 0). In the
construction with these data, every step below Re λ₀ has u = 0, F_0 = 0 and T = 0, so assigns nothing; at λ₀, f = 0
and v = u′_(λ₀), so [h′]_(λ₀) = u′_(λ₀) − R′(λ₀) with R′(λ₀) removing exactly the formal solutions of u′_(λ₀). *(4)* L̄,
χ_K, χ_ι, the states (at b, Lemma 30.2 (P3)) and the cut-offs are real, conjugation maps the construction at λ₀
to that at λ̄₀, and the data are conjugation-symmetric. ∎

**Remark 34.21** (Linearisation; [Hin26, Remark 12.4].) Differentiating (34.15) in U: for U′ ∈ 𝒟^∞,
D_(Φ(U))P_5(D_UΦ(U′)) ∈ ℱ^∞, and

    D_UΦ(U′) = DΦ_0(U_0)U′_0 + (DA(U_0)U′_0)U_1 + A(U_0)U′_1;

parts (1)–(4) of Theorem 34.20 hold for D_UΦ with the obvious changes. So D_UΦ(U′) is an approximate solution of the
linearised equation at Φ(U), to the orders of ℱ.

**Remark 34.22** (Interpretation and the forward problem; [Hin26, Remarks 12.5–12.6].) By Theorem 34.20
(3), each datum (u^0_λ, f_λ) enters h as u_λ minus the rows and tower coefficients that remove its expansion at K⁺ below
the rate α. The removed terms are pure gauge (for g_(b₀)) for the rows (types s1, v1, s0, s2, c0, c1 at rates ≤ 2) and
zero energy towers for q. As in [Hin26], the construction is much simpler than the forward problem of Chapter 32,
Chapter 33 and Section 34.3: it uses only the Minkowski model at ι⁺ and the formal solutions at ι⁺ ∩ K⁺, whereas
the K⁺-expansion of the forward solutions requires the full spectral analysis. In dimension 4 + 1 it is moreover linear
below 3 + ε_+, by the count of exponents in the proof of Lemma 34.17.

### 34.6 The ι⁺-order of the linear solutions

Everything of Section 34.4–Section 34.5 is kept: α with (A_J), (G⁺), the classes 𝒳_J, ℱ, 𝒬_J, the data space 𝒟
with Σ and ℛ′_0, Λ_* = Λ ∩ {Re < 3 + ε_+}, the t_*^(−λ)-terms [·]_λ and the map Φ of Theorem 34.20. Moreover Λ_* =
π_1ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re < 3 + ε_+} (Lemma 33.2 (a), Section 33.9). The parameters are at b = b₀ unless said otherwise
(p⃗′ may still have a component b′, the direction of the derivative).

**Lemma 34.23** (The ι⁺-order under (G⁺).) Under (G⁺), Proposition 33.15, Theorem 33.24 and
Theorem 34.9 hold with η_2 replaced by ε_+ in their ι⁺-orders: in (33.20)–(33.21), w_ψ =
(3 + ε_+ − d_ψ)− and ũ has the ι⁺-data (ℰ_♯, (3 + ε_+)−); in (34.6), h′ has the ι⁺-data (ℰ_♯, (3 + ε_+)−),
and q′ ∈ 𝒬^∞_J.

*Proof.* In Proposition 33.15, η_2 enters as the threshold of level 2 (Step 3 of its proof: the tf-exponents α_0 of
g_2 with Re α_0 < 2 + η_2 are treated), as the order μ_2 = 2 + η_2 of the zero-energy solve there (Lemma 33.10
with μ′ = 2 + ε_+ − ε), and through the resulting tf-weight τ_3 = 1 + η_2 − 2ε of g_3, a lower bound; with the
conditions η_2 ∈ (ε_K, ε_+), η_2 > η_1, no λ ∈ Λ of real part 3 + η_2, and 2ε < ε_+ − η_2. The tf-exponents of the
sources at level 2 (of g_2 and of the remainders α_0 + ℰ_ind of the rounds of the loop) are u-exponents minus 1, so they
lie in Λ − 1: at level 2 the tf-exponent α_0 is the u-exponent α_0 + 1 (Section 33.7; Lemma 33.2 (c)). By
(G⁺) none has real part in (2, 2 + ε_+]. So for every η_2 in (η^0_2, ε_+), η^0_2 the value fixed in Section 33.9,
level 2 treats the same exponents. Lemma 33.10 applies L̃_(b₀)(0)⁻¹ at the weight μ_2 − 4, and moving μ_2 within
(2 + η^0_2, 2 + ε_+) crosses neither an exponent of its right-hand side (those exceed 2 + ε_+, again by (G⁺), as the
last sentence of that lemma records them Λ-valued) nor an indicial root (none has real part in (0, 1),
Proposition 25.6); so its output is the same (Proposition 28.8: its inverses on two such weights agree). Hence g_3
is one tensor for all these η_2, and has the tf-weight 1 + η_2 − 2ε for each of them with 2ε < ε_+ − η_2. Given ε, take
η_2 := ε_+ − 3ε; so g_3 has the tf-weight τ_3 := 1 + ε_+ − 5ε.

Step 4 of the proof of Proposition 33.15 (level 3) and everything after it in Chapter 33 and
Section 34.2–Section 34.3 use τ_3 only as a lower bound on the tf-weight of g_3, through: α_τ ≥ τ_3 > 1 + ℓ_3
(true, as ε_+ > ε_K > ℓ_3); the zf-weight α_τ ≥ τ_3 of the pieces at level 3, so their K⁺-weight ≥ 2 + ε_+ − 5ε > α − 2;
their ι⁺-order α_τ + 2 ≥ 3 + ε_+ − 5ε (Step 2 (viii) of the proof of Theorem 33.24); and w_ψ, chosen in
Section 33.9 as the ι⁺-order of the pieces at level 3 minus d_ψ. With τ_3 = 1 + ε_+ − 5ε these give the ι⁺-order
3 + ε_+ − 5ε and w_ψ = 3 + ε_+ − 5ε − d_ψ, for every small ε; the polyhomogeneous parts are unchanged below 3 + ε_+,
there being no exponent in [3 + η^0_2, 3 + ε_+]. The independence of the decomposition from ε is Lemma 34.8,
whose parameters at level 3 now are τ_i(ε) = 1 + ε_+ + iε_ind − (5 + i)ε, stable in the same way. Theorem 34.9
takes its ι⁺-orders from Theorem 33.24 (Step 4 of its proof), and its intermediate levels do not enter h′, q′. So
h′ has (ℰ_♯, (3 + ε_+)−) at ι⁺, and q′ ∈ 𝒬^∞_J: its polyhomogeneous parts are those of Definition 34.1 (exponents
below 3 + ε_+ − d_ψ), and its conormal parts Ṡ_rem, ḃ_rem and Y^c_ψ (ψ ∈ ℛ′_0 only, Step 4 of the proof of
Theorem 33.24) have the orders (α − 2)−, (α − 1)−, (3 + ε_+ − d_ψ)−. ∎

### 34.7 Linear forward solutions

**Theorem 34.24** ([Hin26, Theorem 12.8] in dimension 4 + 1, at b₀.) There is d such that for U ∈ 𝒟^∞ with
b = b₀, small in 𝒟^d, and (h, p⃗, q) := Φ(U), the following holds. For every f ∈ ℱ^∞ there is U′ ∈ 𝒟^∞ with

    D_((h,p⃗,q))P_5( D_UΦ(U′) ) = f.    (34.16)

U′ is linear in f, and for every k there are d_k and C_k with ‖U′‖_(𝒟^k) ≤ C_k‖f‖_(ℱ^(k+d_k)) for U small in 𝒟^(d_k).

*Proof.* *Step 0 (the solution of Theorem 34.9).* (h, p⃗, q) = Φ(U) is admissible in Theorem 34.9: h ∈
𝒳^∞_J is in the class 𝒳 of Section 34.1 with (H2) read as "α−" (Remark 34.10 (2)) and a_+ any value below
3 + ε_+ ((H5) for η_2 close to ε_+, Lemma 34.23); p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 at b₀; q ∈ 𝒬^∞_J ⊂ 𝒬; all small with U. And f ∈ ℱ^∞ ⊂
𝒴^0(α−): ℱ has the ℐ⁺-data of 𝒴^0_1, a plain ι⁺-weight (5 + ε_+)−, which the ι⁺-data (ℰ^0_src + 2, w_+ − ε) of 𝒴^0_1
contain, and the K⁺-order α−. Theorem 34.9 with Lemma 34.23 gives p⃗′ ∈ 𝒫, q′ ∈ 𝒬^∞_J and h′ with the
ι⁺-data (ℰ_♯, (3 + ε_+)−), the ℐ⁺-data (⟨ℰ^C_I⟩, ℓ_I) and the K⁺-order α−, such that

    D_((h,p⃗,q))P_5(h′, p⃗′, q′) = f.    (34.17)

We now subtract from (h′, p⃗′, q′) values of D_UΦ, each time keeping (34.17) with a new f in ℱ^∞
(Remark 34.21), until nothing is left but conormal remainders.

*Step 1 (the parameters p⃗′_(≤0)).* Let U′_0 := p⃗′_(≤0) = (S′, b′, S^(0)′_1), and replace (h′, p⃗′, q′) by (h′, p⃗′,
q′) − D_UΦ(U′_0 ⊕ 0). By Theorem 34.20 (1), linearised, the new p⃗′_(≤0) vanishes. This step has no t_*^(−1)-term to
treat: the parameters p⃗_(≤0) enter at the u-exponents of 𝒢 ⊂ {Re ≥ 2} (Lemma 34.17).

*Step 2 (the exponents of Λ_*).* Suppose p⃗′_(≤0) = 0, and that for every λ ∈ Λ_* with Re λ < Re λ₀ the term [h′]_λ, the
rows W′_ν with ν = (τ, λ, k) or (rot, λ, k), and the polyhomogeneous coefficients of q′ at the exponents (λ − d_ψ, k)
vanish. Put

    G′(λ₀) := [ h′ + Σ_(ν∈𝒩⊔𝒩_rot) m_ν(W′_ν) + h_(b₀,rem)(q′) ]_(λ₀).

Differentiate Lemma 34.17 at (h, p⃗, q) in the direction (h′, p⃗′, q′): the quadratic part contributes at
u-exponents ≥ 2λ_♯ > 3 + ε_+, the dependence of F_0 and of L_(0,p⃗_(≤0)) on p⃗_(≤0) drops out as p⃗′_(≤0) = 0, and the
terms below λ₀ vanish; so

    [ D_((h,p⃗,q))P_5(h′, p⃗′, q′) ]_(λ₀+2) = L̄ G′(λ₀),

and as f has no ι⁺-term below (5 + ε_+)−, L̄G′(λ₀) = 0. Now G′(λ₀) = Σ_j t_*^(−λ₀)(log t_*)^j g_j with g_j ∈
H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(ℰ_K,ℓ_K))_b(ι⁺), ℓ_K := ℓ_K(λ₀) − ε. Indeed [h′]_(λ₀) has these ℐ⁺-data and, from the K⁺-order α− of
h′, the weight ℓ_K at R = 0; the rows and towers are supported in supp χ_K, away from ℐ⁺, and at R = 0 consist of formal
solutions of Theorem 26.39 (exponents −μ + i ≥ 0, in ℰ_K below ℓ_K, Corollary 26.40) and terms of K⁺-order ≥ Re
λ₀ + 3 (Lemma 34.18). So G′(λ₀) ∈ Res^∞_(ι⁺)(L̄, ℰ^C_I, λ₀) (Definition 27.31).

*Case A: λ₀ is not a pole of (27.26).* Then Res^∞_(ι⁺)(L̄, ℰ^C_I, λ₀) = 0 (Lemma 27.34: its elements
are residues of t_*^(−z)N_(ι⁺)(z)⁻¹f(z) with f polynomial), so G′(λ₀) = 0. The coefficients of q′ have rate < α (the
proof of Lemma 33.23 removes only the pairs below β = α − ε; Step 4 of the proof of Theorem 34.9), and so
do those of D_UΦ ((iii) of the step at λ₀, Section 34.5.1), the rows having rate ≤ 3 (for s1 the order of the formal
solution is Re λ₀ + 1 ≤ 4). So every row and coefficient at λ₀ carries a formal solution of K⁺-order below Re λ₀ +
ℓ_K(λ₀) = α, visible below ℓ_K. Then the rows and coefficients at λ₀ vanish. Indeed the expansion of G′(λ₀) at R = 0
below ℓ_K is the sum of the formal solutions that the rows and coefficients at λ₀ carry (Lemma 34.18), as
[h′]_(λ₀) = O(R^(ℓ_K)); the coefficients of Theorem 26.39 are determined by the tensor (Theorem 26.39,
Lemma 26.32: distinct rows have independent, injective leading terms); and Lemma 34.18 expresses them
through the rows and coefficients triangularly in the log power, with the nonzero factors c_τ(λ₀). So, downward in the
log power, every row and coefficient at λ₀ is 0. Then [h′]_(λ₀) = G′(λ₀) = 0.

*Case B: λ₀ is a pole of (27.26).* Then λ₀ ∈ spec^(<3+ε_+)_(ι⁺)(L̄, ℰ^C_I) ∩ Λ_* ⊂ Σ. By Proposition 27.36
(its right inverse at k = ∞),

    G′(λ₀) = u^0_(λ₀) + res_(z=λ₀)( t_*^(−z)N_(ι⁺)(z)⁻¹ f_(λ₀)(z) )

for some (u^0_(λ₀), f_(λ₀)) in the domain of (27.32), linear and continuous in G′(λ₀). It is
conjugation-symmetric, as G′(λ₀) and G′(λ̄₀) are conjugate; at real λ₀, (27.32) being real, the real part of
the output of the right inverse is taken. Let U′_(λ₀) ∈ 𝒟^∞ have these data at λ₀ and λ̄₀ and all else 0. By
Theorem 34.20 (3), linearised, D_UΦ(U′_(λ₀)) has no term, row or coefficient below Re λ₀, and its total
t_*^(−λ₀)-term is u_(λ₀) − R′(λ₀) + R′(λ₀) = G′(λ₀). Replacing (h′, p⃗′, q′) by (h′, p⃗′, q′) − D_UΦ(U′_(λ₀)) makes the
new G′(λ₀) zero and leaves the lower terms zero; the argument of Case A then makes every term, row and coefficient at λ₀
vanish.

Exponents of equal real part are treated together, independently. After the finitely many exponents of Λ_*: p⃗′ = 0
(every row (τ, λ, k) or (rot, λ, k) of 𝒩 ⊔ 𝒩_rot has λ ∈ Λ_*, as Re λ ≤ 3; p⃗′_(≤0) = 0 by Step 1); q′ has no
polyhomogeneous part (each has ι⁺-exponent z + d_ψ ∈ Λ_*, Definition 34.1 and Lemma 34.23); and h′ has no
ι⁺-term below 3 + ε_+, so h′ ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(3+ε_+)−,α−)_b(Ω_*)^(•,−), the class of h̃ in Definition 34.15.

*Step 3 (conclusion).* Now q′ = (S′_rem, b′_rem, (Y′^c_ψ)_(ψ∈ℛ′_0)) with the orders of Definition 34.15
(Lemma 34.23), and (h′, 0, q′) = D_UΦ(U′_c) with

    U′_c := (0, 0, 0, (0, 0), S′_rem, b′_rem, (Y′^c_ψ), h′):

these components enter Φ additively (Theorem 34.20 (2)) and contribute to no t_*^(−λ₀)-term with λ₀ ∈ Λ_* (their
ι⁺-orders are (3 + ε_+)− and (α + 1)−), so they enter no step of the construction. Summing, the data U′ := U′_0 ⊕ Σ_(λ₀)
U′_(λ₀) + U′_c satisfy (h′, p⃗′, q′) = D_UΦ(U′) for the (h′, p⃗′, q′) of Step 0, and (34.17) is
(34.16). *Linearity and bounds.* The solution of Theorem 34.9 is linear in f with bounds uniform for
(h, p⃗, q) small; each subtraction is D_UΦ (bounded, Theorem 34.20) of data that are continuous linear functions of
the current (h′, p⃗′, q′) (Proposition 27.36 with loss l; finitely many steps). ∎

**Remark 34.25** (Non-uniqueness; [Hin26, Remark 12.9].) Neither D_((h,p⃗,q))P_5 nor D_UΦ is injective: a
part of b′_rem of order α can be moved into h′, and the conormal parts of the data overlap with h̃ in the same way.
Theorem 34.24 asserts that the particular solution of Theorem 34.9 is of the form D_UΦ(U′), with U′ obtained
constructively from it, so U′ inherits its bounds. The construction of U′ from (h′, p⃗′, q′) (Steps 1–3) is linear, with
fixed losses and with coefficients that depend on U only through finitely many derivatives at the exponents of Λ_*. The
tame form of the bound of Theorem 34.24, ‖U′‖_k ≤ C_k(‖f‖_(k+d) + ‖U‖_(k+d)‖f‖_d) as [Hin26] states it, is
Theorem 35.8, and its form at exact weights is Theorem 35.32.

### 34.8 The statements at a base point near b₀

The results of Section 34.1–Section 34.7 that are stated at b = b₀ hold at every base point whose black hole
parameter b lies in the closed ball ℬ̄_* about b₀ of Section 29.6, shrunk as in Chapter 31 (to a radius at most
1/(2C_B), Lemma 31.1, and for Proposition 31.19), in Proposition 32.14, in Lemma 36.3 and in
Proposition 36.8, with constants and smallness conditions uniform in b (Theorem 36.10). The statement at b of
each of them is obtained by replacing L_(b₀), g_(b₀) near K⁺, the states, towers and companions at b₀ and the index set
ℰ_ind by those at b, by taking derivatives in b at b, and by treating the v1 terms as in Chapter 36. In detail (items
(1) and (3) also name the results that are stated above at every b):

(1) Lemma 34.5 (a), (c), Lemma 34.6–Lemma 34.8 and Remark 34.10 (2) hold at b;
Definition 34.2, (34.4) and Lemma 34.5 (b) are stated at b above. The proof of
Lemma 34.7 (c) above is written for every b near b₀; it uses that every coefficient of q has rate > 2 at every
such b. The point of Step 1 of the proof of Theorem 34.9 that uses L̂_(b₀)(0)∂_b h_(b,v1) = 0 needs only that
the q-terms have K⁺-order above α_1. At b, L̂_b(0)∂_b h_(b,v1) = −(∂_b L̂_b(0))h_(b,v1) need not vanish, but the v1
coefficients of q have rate > 2 + ε_K > α_1 (Definition 34.1, (G)), so the K⁺-order of L(∂_b h_(b,rem)(q)b′) is
still > α_1 (S_rem and b_rem having the rates (α − 2)− and (α − 1)−).

(2) Theorem 34.9 holds at b in the form of Proposition 36.8: the p⃗′ there is unique among the parameters
whose rotation coordinates are the assigned ones (Remark 36.9), and at b₀ it is the p⃗′ of Theorem 34.9
(Proposition 36.8). Step 4′ of the proof of Theorem 34.9 is not used at b.

(3) Lemma 34.17, Lemma 34.18, Theorem 34.20 and Remark 34.21 are stated above at every b, under
the convention that the rows m_ν are built at b₀, the towers T_(ψ,b) at b and the corrections at b₀. Their proofs at b
use Lemma 34.5 (a) at b, by (1), and the reality of the states at b (Lemma 30.2 (P3)). P_5 and the
coordinates W_ν do not depend on whether the rows are built at b₀ or at b, as the rows enter P_4 only through the
corrections and counterterms built at b₀ (Lemma 34.7 (a)), and Step 2 of the proof of Theorem 34.24 uses
only the λ₀-terms of the rows, which do not depend on b (Lemma 34.18). The pure gauge of Remark 34.22 refers
to g_(b₀).

(4) Lemma 34.23 holds for the output of Proposition 36.8, and Theorem 34.24, with its tame and exact
forms, holds at every base point U ∈ 𝒟^∞ small in 𝒟^d, whose black hole parameter then lies in ℬ_*, with constants
uniform in U; at a rotating b the right inverse is the one constructed from Proposition 36.8 (Corollary 36.12).
These are the right inverses that Theorem 20.1 (iii) asks for at every point of its domain.
## 35. Tame estimates and exact weights

This chapter proves two properties of the forward solutions of Chapter 29–Chapter 34 that the nonlinear theorem of
Chapter 38 needs in order to apply the Nash–Moser theorem Theorem 20.1. The first, in
Section 35.1–Section 35.4, is tameness: the solution map of the forward problem with parameters
(Theorem 34.9) and the right inverse of the linearised equation in the data (Theorem 34.24) satisfy
estimates linear in the highest norm, with a loss of b-regularity independent of the order, and the map
U ↦ P_5(Φ(U)) has tame bounds. [Hin26, Remark 11.13, p. 226] asserts that the tameness of the initial tame estimate
propagates through all the arguments; [Hin26, Corollary 11.66, pp. 294–295] and [Hin26, Theorem 12.8, p. 312] state the
tame estimates without proof, and [Hin26, Section 13.1, Step 3 (2)–(3), pp. 321–322] uses them. Here the propagation is
proved: a calculus of tame families (Section 35.1); the elementary families, with finite-order forms of the model
statements that Chapter 26–Chapter 34 state at b-regularity ∞ (Section 35.2); the inventory of every construction
of Chapter 29–Chapter 34 as a composition of these (Section 35.3); and the theorems (Section 35.4).

The second, in Section 35.5–Section 35.10, is that the solution map of Theorem 34.9 and the right inverse
of Theorem 34.24 lose nothing in the weights. A right side at the fixed weights (ℓ_I + 1, 5 + ε_+, α) at
(ℐ⁺, ι⁺, K⁺) gives a solution at (ℓ_I, 3 + ε_+, α), with one fixed admissible α (Theorem 35.30,
Theorem 35.32). This is how [Hin26] states its Corollary 11.66 (pp. 294–295) and Theorem 12.8 (p. 312), at the
weights (4 + ε_I, 5 + ε_+, 4 + ε_K) and (3 + ε_I, 3 + ε_+, 4 + ε_K). The Nash–Moser theorem asks for one pair of Banach
scales, and the forward map gains nothing in the weights (Proposition 35.9); with the exact weights the tame
estimates hold on one pair of scales (Corollary 35.33).

*Dimension 4 + 1.* (1) [Hin26] omits the intermediate tame statements; they are written out here. (2) One model map
loses b-regularity growing with the order: Corollary 20.27 (high frequencies), with the loss ⌈kδ⌉ + ℓ,
δ = δ_Γ(−η). The operator 2L_b is strongly trapping admissible at every b near b_0 (Proposition 29.19), so for each
order k the trapping data can be taken with (k + 1)δ ≤ 1 (Corollary 29.20), and the loss is at most ℓ + 1 at every
k (Lemma 35.3 (f)). (3) Choices that depend on the order (the trapping data, and the low-energy radius c_k of
Corollary 28.11) enter only decompositions of a solution that does not depend on them, so they cost constants, not
derivatives (Remark 35.4). (4) The losses in the weights are removed where they arise; nothing is improved after
the fact. Of the statements of Chapter 29–Chapter 34 that take a right side at an exact weight and conclude an order
"w−", only those whose loss reaches a final weight matter: every other one feeds an open condition with fixed room. Those
losses have three roots. (a) At K⁺, Corollary 26.44 writes the ι⁺-terms in powers of log t_*. At the corner
t_*⁻¹ = ρ_+ρ_K, so each log t_* hides a log ρ_K, and a logarithm times a conormal function of exact weight lies in no
weighted L²-b space of that weight. In that convention Corollary 26.44 cannot be applied at the exact weight, the
two classes being incomparable (Remark 35.17). Written in powers of log ρ_+, the convention of [Hin26, Definition
2.8, p. 48] in which the classes of Chapter 29–Chapter 34 are defined, the same construction is exact
(Corollary 35.18). (b) Lemma 33.21 and Lemma 33.20 bound their outputs pointwise, at K⁺ and at the
corner of ι⁺ and K⁺, which gives only the L²-weight w−; at the final weight they are proved in L² (Lemma 35.24,
Lemma 35.25 and Lemma 35.27). The Fourier characterisation Proposition 21.45 is itself exact and only
transmits the loss of (a) (Proposition 35.21). (c) At ι⁺, the level-2 margin η_2 < ε_+ of Proposition 33.15 and
the 5ε of Lemma 34.23 are choices, not losses of an estimate: at the closed endpoint of (G⁺) every map is exact
(Proposition 35.23), as in Part 4 of the proof of [Hin26, Theorem 11.59, pp. 289–291]. At ℐ⁺ every class and every
main statement is already exact. (5) The K⁺-weight is one fixed admissible α, not the number 4 + ε_K; α = 4 + ε_K itself
is admissible off a finite set of ε_K (Definition 35.13, (A_K)). (6) The conditions (Ex2)–(Ex4) of Definition 35.13,
each excluding finitely many values, are of the kind of (G⁺) and of admissibility, and are not in [Hin26]; (Ex1) is (G⁺)
at its closed endpoint. No condition on spec_ι⁺(L̄) beyond (G⁺) is needed, as no improvement after the fact is made.

*Base points.* Throughout, the base point has black hole parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, the neighbourhood of b_0 of
Section 29.6, shrunk so that Lemma 36.3 and Proposition 36.8 hold on it. The results of
Chapter 29–Chapter 34 are used at b, with constants uniform in b (Section 34.8 (1)–(3), and the statements
at b of Chapter 29–Chapter 33): L_(b_0), g_(b_0) near K⁺, the states, towers and companions at b_0 and the index set
ℰ_ind are replaced by those at b, derivatives in b are taken at b, and the v1 terms of exponent of real part at most 2
are the rotation rows with the assigned coordinates of Definition 36.6. At a rotating b the solution map of
Theorem 34.9 is the one constructed in Proposition 36.8, and those of Theorem 33.18 and
Proposition 33.31 are used only inside Lemma 36.7 and Proposition 36.8, the latter with q = 0 being
their form there.

*The inner radius.* Every result of the chapter holds with the inner radius r₀ = r_♭ ∈ (0, ½R₁] of Definition 22.1
as a parameter, with constants that depend on it. No result names the inner radius: all work on Ω_* = cl_M{t^♭_* ≥ 1}
(Section 29.1) with the spaces of Chapter 14, extendible at the inner boundary, and with the theorems of
Chapter 14–Chapter 20, which hold at every such radius. The regions used are bounded by fixed radii that do not depend
on r_♭ ({r ≥ 1}, and {r ≥ 2} near the corner of ι⁺ and K⁺) or by multiples of t_* ({r ≤ t_*/8}, {t_*/8 < r < t_*/2}),
and the loops, levels and windows of Section 35.3 are fixed by weights at infinity and at K⁺, not by the inner
radius.

*Notation.* As in Chapter 34. In particular w_+ := 5 + ε_+; ρ_+ and ρ_K are the defining functions of ι⁺ and K⁺ near
their corner, ρ_+ = 1/r and ρ_K = R = r/t_*, so t_*⁻¹ = ρ_+ρ_K there (Section 29.15); μ runs over the indicial roots
of L̂_(b_0)(0) (Proposition 25.6), which do not depend on b (Lemma 30.2 (P2)), and −μ is read as −Re μ; the
non-real roots have real part below −101 or above 1, outside every interval used. The neighbourhoods ℬ_1 ⊃ ℬ_* of b_0
and their closures are the B_1 ⊃ B_* of Section 29.6. The rows of the towers are indexed by ψ ∈ ℛ′, as in
Chapter 33 and Chapter 34 (Y_ψ, d_ψ, w_ψ, T_ψ).

### 35.1 Tame families

A *background* is β = (h, p⃗, q) with h ∈ 𝒳^∞, p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 and q ∈ 𝒬^∞ in the classes of the statement at hand
(Section 29.1 for h alone; Section 34.1, with 𝒫 enlarged by the rotation rows; for Theorem 34.24,
β = Φ(U)), and

    ‖β‖_k := ‖h‖_(𝒳^k) + |p⃗| + ‖q‖_(𝒬^k).

The black hole parameter b of β is given by the component b − b_0 of p⃗. A *graded space* is a family of Banach spaces
E^k, k ∈ ℕ₀, with continuous inclusions E^(k+1) ↪ E^k of norm at most 1 (Remark 20.3), and E^∞ := ⋂_k E^k. The
spaces of Chapter 29–Chapter 34 are of this kind: weighted b-Sobolev spaces of b-regularity k; partially polyhomogeneous
ones, normed by the order-k norms of their finitely many coefficients and of the remainder; finite-dimensional spaces
(E^k = E); and direct sums.

Several of those spaces carry orders read "w−" (Section 34.1, Definition 34.15): they are intersections over a
loss ε > 0, and their order-k spaces are Fréchet, not Banach. Such a space is taken here at a fixed loss: E^k_ε is the
Banach space with every order w− replaced by w − ε, and E^∞_ε := ⋂_k E^k_ε. For ε″ ≤ ε, E^k_(ε″) ⊂ E^k_ε continuously,
the weight being larger. A statement of Chapter 29–Chapter 34 from a "w−" space to a "w−" space is a continuous linear
map between Fréchet spaces (closed graph theorem), so for every loss ε of the output and every order k there is a loss
ε′(ε, k) ∈ (0, ε] of the input at which it is bounded. Decreasing ε′(ε, k) keeps the bound, so ε′(ε, ·) is taken
non-increasing in k. Then the spaces E^k_(ε′(ε,k)), k ∈ ℕ₀, form a graded space (renormed as in Remark 20.3), the
input space of the statement at the output loss ε; in a composition the output of one statement is taken in the graded
input space of the next. For the statements whose proofs choose every margin from the loss the output is to have, ε′
can be taken independent of k: Proposition 29.35, Lemma 31.24–Lemma 31.26 and Proposition 31.27, the
level-3 loop of Proposition 33.15 (the margin ε_ind − ε), the levels β_k of Theorem 34.9, Lemma 34.23
(η_2 := ε_+ − 3ε, which gives the ι⁺-order 3 + ε_+ − 5ε) and Corollary 20.27 (β_scf := β′_I + ε); no margin there
depends on k. For the other statements the independence of k is not shown, and it is not needed: at the exact weights
of Section 35.5 the input and the output are taken at the loss 0 for every k (Corollary 35.33).

Below, ε ∈ (0, ε_1] is fixed, where ε_1 > 0 satisfies

    5ε_1 < ε_+ − max(η^0_2, η_1, ε_K) = ε_+ − η^0_2,        ε_1 < α − 4,

with η_1 and η^0_2 the values of η_1 and η_2 fixed in Section 33.5 and Section 33.9
(ε_K < η_1 < η^0_2 < ε_+), and is so small that every statement of Chapter 29–Chapter 34 used below holds at every loss
ε ∈ (0, ε_1]. A statement proved for every small ε off a finite set (Section 33.5) holds at every
ε ∈ (0, ε_1], as its output space at the loss ε contains that at every smaller loss. By the first condition the choice
η_2 := ε_+ − 3ε of Lemma 34.23 is admissible: η_2 ∈ (η^0_2, ε_+) and 2ε < 3ε = ε_+ − η_2. It also gives
1 + ε_+ − 5ε > 1 + ε_K, so the level-3 tf-weight τ_3 = 1 + ε_+ − 5ε of Lemma 34.23 exceeds 1 + ℓ_3, and the
K⁺-weight 2 + ε_+ − 5ε of the level-3 pieces exceeds α − 2, as ℓ_3 ≤ ε_K and α ≤ 4 + ε_K. By the second, h_rem(q) has
the K⁺-order α − 2 − ε > 2 (Lemma 35.3 (a)), and the zf-weight ℓ_3 = α − 4 − ε of level 3 in the proof of
Proposition 33.15 is positive. Theorem 35.7 and Theorem 35.8 take their output at the loss ε and their
input in the graded space of the losses ε′(ε, k) that the statement they estimate assigns.

**Definition 35.1** (Tame families.) Let E, G be graded spaces, d_0, d ∈ ℕ, δ_𝔹 > 0, and
𝔹 := {β : ‖β‖_(d_0) < δ_𝔹}. A family (T_β)_(β∈𝔹) of linear maps E^∞ → G^∞ is *tame with loss d* if for every
k ∈ ℕ₀ there is C_k with

    ‖T_β e‖_(G^k) ≤ C_k (‖e‖_(E^(k+d)) + ‖β‖_(k+d) ‖e‖_(E^d)),        β ∈ 𝔹,  e ∈ E^∞.    (35.1)

A family (v_β) in G^∞ is *tame with loss d* if ‖v_β‖_(G^k) ≤ C_k (1 + ‖β‖_(k+d)) for every k.

**Lemma 35.2** (Closure.) Let δ_𝔹 ≤ 1.

(a) Sums of families tame with loss d are tame with loss d; a family tame with loss d is tame with every loss d′ ≥ d.

(b) If (T_β), E → G, is tame with loss d, (S_β), G → H, with loss d′, and d_0 ≥ d + d′, then (S_β T_β) is tame with
loss d + d′.

(c) (*Finite rank.*) If ℓ_β : E^∞ → ℂ^m satisfies |ℓ_β e| ≤ C ‖e‖_(E^d) on 𝔹, and v¹_β, …, v^m_β are tame with loss d,
then e ↦ Σ_i (ℓ_β e)_i v^i_β is tame with loss d. In particular a family of linear maps between finite-dimensional
spaces, bounded on 𝔹, is tame with loss 0.

(d) (*Fixed maps.*) A linear map T independent of β that is bounded E^(k+d) → G^k for every k is tame with loss d.

(e) A composition of m families, each tame with loss at most d, is tame with loss md if d_0 ≥ md; here m is fixed,
independent of k.

(f) (*Regularity statements.*) If a statement takes e ∈ E and an a priori solution u in a space E′ to u ∈ G, and the
family (e, u) ↦ u, E ⊕ E′ → G, is tame with loss d, then for (S_β), E → E′, tame with loss d′, the map e ↦ u = S_β e
into G is tame with loss d + d′. A statement of this kind independent of β that is a membership statement between
Banach spaces at each order k has, by the closed graph theorem, the bound ‖u‖_(G^k) ≤ C_k (‖e‖_(E^(k+d)) +
‖u‖_(E′^(k+d))), and is then tame with loss d.

(g) Definition 35.1 asks one bound for each k: a family whose order-k bound is proved with choices made for the
order k (Remark 35.4) is tame with loss d if each of these bounds has the loss at most d.

*Proof.* (a) is immediate, the norms being non-decreasing in k. (b) By (35.1) for S and then for T,

    ‖S_β T_β e‖_k ≤ C_k (‖T_β e‖_(k+d′) + ‖β‖_(k+d′) ‖T_β e‖_(d′))
                 ≤ C_k (‖e‖_(k+d+d′) + ‖β‖_(k+d+d′) ‖e‖_d + ‖β‖_(k+d′) (‖e‖_(d+d′) + ‖β‖_(d+d′) ‖e‖_d)),

and ‖β‖_(d+d′) ≤ ‖β‖_(d_0) < 1, ‖β‖_(k+d′) ≤ ‖β‖_(k+d+d′) and ‖e‖_d ≤ ‖e‖_(d+d′) give (35.1) with loss
d + d′. (c) ‖Σ_i (ℓ_β e)_i v^i_β‖_k ≤ C ‖e‖_d Σ_i ‖v^i_β‖_k ≤ C_k ‖e‖_d (1 + ‖β‖_(k+d)), which is at most the right
side of (35.1). (d) is (35.1) without its second term. (e) follows from (b) by induction. (f) The
map e ↦ (e, S_β e) is tame with loss d′ by (a), and (b) applies. (g) is Definition 35.1. ∎

### 35.2 The elementary families

**Lemma 35.3** (The elementary tame families.) For d_0 large and δ_𝔹 small the following are tame, with
losses independent of k, and with constants that depend on the base point through finitely many seminorms, continuous
in b ∈ ℬ̄_*.

(a) (*Forward solutions.*) The forward solution operators of the operators L^(g,g_0), g = g_0 + h̃, used in
Chapter 29–Chapter 34: h̃ = h (Theorem 29.17, at b with continuity in (b, S, h) by Corollary 29.25);
h̃ = h + h^(−1)(S) and h + h_tot(p⃗) (the operators L_(h,S) of Chapter 31 and L_(h,p⃗) of Chapter 32; the gauge
modifications δ*_(g_0,E_C) ϑ_tot(p⃗) do not enter them, D_h removing them, Lemma 31.13 and Lemma 32.9
(a)); and h̃ = h + h_rem(q) + h_tot(p⃗) (Step 0 of the proof of Theorem 34.9, and of Proposition 36.8),
between the spaces of (29.18) and its target. For h̃ = h this is (29.19), with the loss d of
Theorem 29.17, the same at b (Corollary 29.25). In general h̃ lies in the class of Theorem 29.17
(h_rem(q) has K⁺-order (α − 2)− > 2, Remark 34.10 (1)), the operator is L^(g_0+h̃,g_0) with g_0 = g_S or g_p⃗
(Lemma 31.13, Lemma 32.9 (a), Lemma 32.23, and Lemma 32.35 with h + h_rem(q) in place of
h), and Theorem 29.17 holds for it with h̃ in place of h, the parameters of g_0 being components of p⃗
(Lemma 31.13, Lemma 32.4 (b), Lemma 32.9 (b)). So (29.19) holds with ‖h̃‖_(𝒳^(k+d))
in place of ‖h‖_(𝒳^(k+d)), for ‖h̃‖_(𝒳^d) and |p⃗| small. The proof of Theorem 29.17 applies Theorem 19.14
(with Remark 19.31; at b, Theorem 29.24) with the loss d − 5, and bounds ‖P − P_0‖_((0;k+d−5)) by
C_k(|p⃗| + ‖h̃‖_(𝒳^(k+d))), the 5 being the derivatives that Corollary 29.16 costs (h ∈ 𝒳^k gives the class
(0;k−5)). In terms of β: at h, h + h^(−1)(S) and h + h_tot(p⃗), ‖h̃‖_(𝒳^m) ≤ C_m ‖β‖_m, as ‖h^(−1)(S)‖_(𝒳^m) ≤ C_m|S|
and ‖h_tot(p⃗)‖_(𝒳^m) ≤ C_m|p⃗| (Lemma 31.13, Lemma 32.9 (a), Lemma 32.23, Lemma 32.35).
At h + h_rem(q) + h_tot(p⃗), ‖h̃‖_(𝒳^m) ≤ C_m ‖β‖_(m+3): by (34.2) and (26.50), h_(b,rem)(q) is
a finite sum of fixed tensors, smooth in b (Lemma 30.2 (P3)), times the components of q and their
t_*-derivatives of order at most 3 (S_rem with one, through h^(≤1)_(b,s1), b_rem with none, and Y_ψ with at most
k_μ ≤ 3, the towers being those of Definition 33.19 with the k_μ of Definition 26.31); on functions of t_*,
∂_(t_*) = t_*⁻¹(t_*∂_(t_*)), where t_*∂_(t_*) is the b-vector field of the spaces of (34.1) and t_*⁻¹ only
adds decay; so ‖h_(b,rem)(q)‖_(𝒳^m) ≤ C_m ‖q‖_(𝒬^(m+3)). Hence, with E^j the space of (29.18) and G^j that of
the solution at the order j, the forward solution operator T_β satisfies

    ‖T_β f‖_(G^k) ≤ C_k (‖f‖_(E^(k+d)) + ‖β‖_(k+d) ‖f‖_(E^d))        at h, h + h^(−1)(S) and h + h_tot(p⃗),
    ‖T_β f‖_(G^k) ≤ C_k (‖f‖_(E^(k+d)) + ‖β‖_(k+d+3) ‖f‖_(E^d))      at h + h_rem(q) + h_tot(p⃗),

and ‖P − P_0‖_((0;k+d−5)) ≤ C_k ‖β‖_(k+d), respectively C_k ‖β‖_(k+d+3), for d_0 ≥ d + 3 and δ_𝔹 small, which make
‖h̃‖_(𝒳^d), at most C‖β‖_(d+3), and |p⃗| as small as Theorem 29.17 asks. The norms being non-decreasing in the order,
T_β is tame with loss d at the first three backgrounds and with loss d + 3 at the fourth: the 3 enters the order of
‖β‖ only, and the orders k + d and d of f are those of (29.19).

(b) (*Background coefficients.*) u ↦ (L^(g,g_0) − L_b)u, u ↦ R_q u, Δ_q, the sources f^S_(h,p⃗), f^b_(h,p⃗),
f^s1_(h,p⃗), f^ν_(h,p⃗), r^ν_(h,p⃗), L_b h_rem(q) and the remainder L̃ of Lemma 29.26, between the weighted spaces
of (29.15), Lemma 32.36 and Lemma 34.5–Lemma 34.7; and the errors E^ν_(h,p⃗) of
Lemma 36.1, bounded by C|b − b_0||W| in a fixed seminorm. Each is a b-differential operator of order
at most 2 whose coefficients are polynomial in the background, g⁻¹ and their derivatives (or such a coefficient applied
to a fixed section); by Corollary 14.57 and Lemma 14.55, with Lemma 20.6 for the nonlinear functions of the
background,

    ‖Au‖_k ≤ C_k (‖u‖_(k+2) + ‖β‖_(k+d) ‖u‖_d)

for ‖β‖_(d_0) small, the weights adding as in the cited membership statements (Lemma 35.6 in the partially
polyhomogeneous spaces).

(c) (*Finite-dimensional algebra and coefficients.*) The inverses (S^(−1)_(h,S))⁻¹ (Corollary 31.20, at b with
the bound of Proposition 31.19), (S^(−1)_(h,p⃗))⁻¹ (Corollary 32.18, at b with the bound of
Proposition 32.14), T_(h,p⃗)⁻¹ (Proposition 32.29, Theorem 33.18), the inverses
(−id + A_k)⁻¹ of the elimination (Step 3 of the proofs of Theorem 34.9 and Proposition 36.8), at b_0 the
inverse of C^rot in W⃗′^rot (Step 4′ of the proof of Theorem 34.9), and (z − 3/2 − Ā)⁻¹ (Proposition 29.29):
bounded on 𝔹 by the cited statements (close to ±id, or fixed). The coefficient functionals (Ṡ, S_ν, C^(k+1)_ν, C^rot,
the dual functionals of Step 4′ of the proof of Theorem 34.9, the t_*-coefficients at K⁺), and at a rotating b
the assigned rotation coordinates A_b of Definition 36.6, which read the ι⁺-data and the tf-data of the right side
(Proposition 36.5): bounded by a fixed low norm of the solution or right side they are applied to, by the cited
statements and Lemma 33.22 (a). The finite-dimensional states, the rows m_ν (the rotation rows among them), the
towers T_(ψ,b) and the states of Lemma 34.4 they are paired with are fixed smooth sections, smooth in b
(Lemma 30.2 (P3)). So, composed with tame families, they give tame families by Lemma 35.2 (b)–(c).
The conormal components Ṡ_rem, ḃ_rem, Ẏ_ψ of q′ are not finite-dimensional: they are functions of t_* that Step 4 of
the proof of Theorem 33.24 assembles (Ṡ_rem := A + A_5 + a_s, ḃ_rem := B + a_b, Ẏ_ψ := a_ψ + Y^c_ψ) from the
outputs of its Steps 1–3, so they are outputs of a composition of the families of its entry in Section 35.3, tame
with a fixed loss by Lemma 35.2 (e).

(d) (*Integrations along faces.*) Lemma 21.33 and Lemma 21.42 (membership statements, which take the a
priori norm of the solution as an input: Lemma 35.2 (f)) and Lemma 29.30: order k to order k (loss 0);
Lemma 29.31: loss ℓ, independent of k, as stated.

(e) (*Transforms, and the low and middle frequencies.*) Proposition 21.45 (1) (Fourier transform, loss l),
Proposition 20.18 (1) (loss 1), Proposition 20.20 (loss ℓ) and Corollary 20.24 ((1): loss j + ℓ for ∂^j_σ, j fixed
by the weights; (2): loss ℓ), Proposition 28.8 (L̃_b(0)⁻¹, loss 1), Corollary 28.11 (on |σ| < c_k, no loss) and
Lemma 29.33 (loss ℓ): as stated, at every order with the loss independent of the order.

(f) (*High frequencies.*) Corollary 20.27 loses ⌈kδ⌉ + ℓ, δ = δ_Γ(−η) ((12.4)), where ℓ = 2ℓ_3 + ℓ_4 + ℓ_5
depends only on the orders and the weights, not on η, the trapping data or the constant C_0. At every b ∈ ℬ̄_1 ⊃ ℬ̄_*
the operator 2L_b is strongly trapping admissible (Proposition 29.19), and for every k the fibre inner product of
(Γ.4) in Section 12.1.5 and η can be chosen with (k + 1)δ_Γ(−η) ≤ 1, uniformly in b ∈ ℬ̄_1 (Corollary 29.20);
then the loss at the order k is at most ℓ + 1, with constants uniform in b. Lemma 29.32 composes this with (e)
and the invertibility of Corollary 28.13 on the middle frequencies; it has loss at most ℓ + 1 plus the losses of (e).

(g) (*Model inverses stated at order ∞.*) Each of the following holds at every order k with a loss independent of k, by
its own proof, read at the order k:

- Theorem 26.27 (2): N_ι⁺(λ)⁻¹ has the loss d at every k, as stated, finite-meromorphic in λ with principal parts
  independent of k. Theorem 26.42 and Corollary 26.44 compose it with a contour integral over a fixed circle on
  which λ ∉ spec_ι⁺(L̄) (bounded at each order, uniformly on the circle), with the towers at b (fixed sections paired
  with finitely many coefficients) and with L_b (loss 2): loss d + 2. The same holds for Corollary 27.30,
  Proposition 27.25 and Proposition 27.36, whose losses are fixed, as the proof of Theorem 34.20 records (the
  loss l of Proposition 27.36).

- Corollary 25.12: N_tf(L̂_b, ±1)⁻¹ has the loss ℓ at every k, as stated. Theorem 27.46,
  Proposition 27.55 and Proposition 27.58 compose it with L̃_b(0)⁻¹ ((e)), cut-offs, a Mellin inversion on a fixed
  vertical line not crossing a root (bounded at each order), and finitely many rounds whose number is fixed by the
  weights (each raises the order by at least ε_ind − ε): fixed loss.

- Proposition 29.27 and Proposition 29.29: compositions of (d), of (z − 3/2 − Ā)⁻¹ ((c)) and of L̃ ((b), loss
  max(2, d) with d the order in the background of the bound of (b), its coefficients depending on h);
  Proposition 29.27 is a regularity statement, the family (f, u) ↦ u with the a
  priori norm of u as an input (Lemma 35.2 (f)), as is Lemma 21.42 within it; in finitely many steps whose
  number is fixed by ℓ_I, ℓ_+ and the index sets: fixed loss.

- Lemma 29.34: b̂ ↦ χG_1(b̂) and Ŝ ↦ χG_2(Ŝ) multiply finite-dimensional data by fixed sections built from the
  states: loss 0.

*Proof.* (a)–(c) are proved in their statements; the continuity in b of the constants is that of the objects at b
(Lemma 30.2 (P1)–(P4) and Lemma 36.1), and the bound on E^ν is Lemma 36.1. (d) and (e) are the cited
statements, each of which is stated at every order with the loss independent of it, and with constants uniform in b
(Lemma 30.2 (P1), (P4)). (f) That ℓ depends only on the orders and the weights is read off from the proof of
Corollary 20.27: ℓ_4 = ℓ_1 + ℓ_2 + 2ν + ⌈(δ_2 − δ_1)_+⌉ is the loss of Proposition 20.26, with ℓ_1, ℓ_2 and ν from
Lemma 20.25, and ℓ_3, ℓ_5 are the losses of Proposition 20.20 (2) and Proposition 20.18 (2). For δ:
Corollary 29.20 gives, for every k, an inner product and ε_k > 0 with δ_Γ(−η) ≤ 1/(k + 1) for η ∈ (0, ε_k] and every
b ∈ ℬ̄_1; its proof bounds γ_+ by the bound (29.20) of Proposition 29.19 and γ_+ − γ_− from below by
ν_min/(2 sup_Γ q^Γ), where β_Γ, ν_min and q^Γ do not depend on the inner product and are continuous and positive on ℬ̄_1.
So (k + 1)δ ≤ 1 and ⌈kδ⌉ ≤ 1. The constants of Corollary 20.27 at the order k, with the inner product h_(η_k,b) of
Corollary 29.20, are uniform in b ∈ ℬ̄_1. Indeed Lemma 20.25, Proposition 20.18 and Proposition 20.20 do not
involve the operator, and Proposition 20.26 takes its constants and C_0 from Theorem 12.2 (3) and (5), whose
constants are uniform in b by Section 12.9: (H5)–(H8) hold continuously in b ((B1) in Section 29.6), and h_(η_k,b)
is smooth in b (Proposition 29.19). This is (ii) of the proof of Theorem 29.21 (Lemma 30.2 (P4)). The
remark after Proposition 20.26 treats only γ_+ ≤ 0 and is not used. (g) Each statement is a finite composition of maps
of (b)–(e) and of the two face inverses cited, at a fixed number of steps; Lemma 35.2 (e)–(f) applies, β entering
only through the families of (b) (in Proposition 29.27 and Proposition 29.29, through L̃). ∎

**Remark 35.4** (Choices that depend on the order.) In Lemma 35.3 (e)–(f) two choices depend on k:
the radius c_k of the low-energy cut-off, and the trapping data. Both enter only decompositions u = u_hi + u_reg +
u_sing (and their analogues) of a solution u that does not depend on them, used to show that u lies in a
better-weighted space; at the order k the decomposition made with the order-k choices gives the order-k bound. So the
choices change the constants C_k, which may depend on k, and not the losses (Lemma 35.2 (g)).

**Lemma 35.5** (Smallness in one norm.) There is d_* such that every smallness condition on the background
in Chapter 29–Chapter 34 is smallness of ‖h‖_(𝒳^(d_*)) + |S| + |p⃗| + ‖q‖_(𝒬^(d_*)), and every statement there that a
finite-dimensional map is close to ±id, or that a family is continuous at the background 0, holds in the topology of
this norm. Hence Lemma 35.3 and Section 35.3 hold with d_0 := d_* + D, D the total loss of the compositions
of Section 35.3 (the d of Theorem 35.7), and one d_0 serves every order k.

*Proof.* Theorem 29.17 asks ‖h‖_(𝒳^(d_T)) < ε_0, d_T being its loss d, and Theorem 19.14, which its proof
applies with the loss d_T − 5, asks ‖P − P_0‖_((0;d_T−5),(2ℓ_I,ℓ_+,ℓ_K)) < ε_0; at the backgrounds h̃ of
Lemma 35.3 (a), that lemma bounds ‖h̃‖_(𝒳^(d_T)) and ‖P − P_0‖_((0;d_T−5)) by C‖β‖_(d_T+3). The proof of
Lemma 31.17 (b) gives the continuity of (h, S) ↦ Ṡ_(h,S) with h in the 𝒳^d-topology, d ≥ k_1 + d_T + 7, whence
S^(−1)_(h,S) is close to the identity. Chapter 32 fixes "h small" as small in 𝒳^d, d fixed, for Lemma 32.9,
Lemma 32.10 (c), Lemma 32.12, Lemma 32.15, Lemma 32.17 and Corollary 32.18, and takes the
same convention for Proposition 32.29 and T_(h,p⃗); Theorem 33.18 takes the continuity of T_(h,p⃗) from
Proposition 32.29 (ii). Chapter 34 fixes "q small" as small in one fixed seminorm of large order, so that
h + h_rem(q) is small in that 𝒳^d. Steps 3 and 4′ of the proof of Theorem 34.9 take A_k → 0 and the derivative
of C^rot at 0 also from Lemma 32.28, Lemma 32.36, Lemma 33.17, Lemma 33.30 and
Lemma 34.6–Lemma 34.7. Of these, Lemma 32.36 is continuous with h ∈ 𝒳^k, k ≥ 5, under the
same convention for "small"; Lemma 34.6–Lemma 34.7 bound R_q and Δ_q by C‖q‖ in the one fixed
seminorm of q; and Lemma 32.28, Lemma 33.17 and Lemma 33.30 (by the proof of
Lemma 33.17) state (h_j, p⃗_j) → (0, 0) without naming a topology, but their proofs give

    S^(h_j,p⃗_j)_ν(G_j) − S^(0,0)_ν(G) = S^(0,0)_ν(R_j),        R_j := G_j − G − (L_j − L_(b_0)) u_j,

with S^(0,0)_ν bounded by one fixed seminorm (Lemma 35.3 (c)), so they need R_j → 0 only in that seminorm:
G_j → G there, and (L_j − L_(b_0)) u_j → 0 there, which holds for h_j → 0 in 𝒳^(d′), d′ fixed (Lemma 35.3 (b)
at that order), with u_j bounded at a fixed order. Step 4′ needs R → 0 only at one loss ε and one order. At a base point
with parameter b, the continuity is read at b through Lemma 36.7 at (0, p⃗_b), p⃗_b the parameter whose only
nonzero component is b − b_0, and through the direct bound |A_k| ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + ‖q‖ + |b − b_0|) of Step 3 of
the proof of Proposition 36.8, both in fixed seminorms; the orders of the rotation rows are among those just named.
None of these orders depends on k, and d_* is their maximum. For Theorem 34.24,
‖Φ(U)‖_(d_*) ≤ C‖U‖_(𝒟^(d_*+d)) (Theorem 34.20). ∎

**Lemma 35.6** (Tame products in partially polyhomogeneous spaces.) Let E, E′ be partially polyhomogeneous
spaces of Section 35.1 at one or more faces, at the loss ε, and G the space that the membership statements
(Lemma 27.5) give to products. There is d_1 ≥ 3 with

    ‖uv‖_(G^k) ≤ C_k (‖u‖_(E^(k+3)) ‖v‖_(E′^(d_1)) + ‖u‖_(E^(d_1)) ‖v‖_(E′^k)),

and the same with the roles of u and v exchanged; and if the exponents of E have positive real parts, as those of the
background do, then for a smooth Θ, depending also on the point (through g_0, g_0⁻¹ and their derivatives), with
Θ(·, 0) = 0, there is δ_Θ > 0 with ‖Θ(u)‖_(G^k) ≤ C_k ‖u‖_(E^(k+3)) for ‖u‖_(E^(d_1)) ≤ δ_Θ, G the space of Θ(u) by
the same statements.

*Proof.* The coefficient of uv at an exponent is a finite sum of products of coefficients of u and of v, functions on
the face, of dimension at most 4, bounded by Lemma 20.6 (2) there with d = 3 > 4/2; a product with a remainder
factor is bounded by Lemma 20.6 (2) with d = 3 > 5/2 in the weighted b-Sobolev space, the weights adding
(Corollary 14.57) and a coefficient being extended from its face by a cut-off; in each product the factor from u is
the one that (2) measures at the order k + 3; and a term whose exponent lies beyond the remainder's weight is put in
the remainder with the same bound. As the norms are non-decreasing in the order and d_1 ≥ 3, this gives the bound
stated, and by symmetry the one with u and v exchanged. For Θ: Taylor's formula to an order M, fixed by the weights,
at which M times the least real part of the exponents exceeds the remainder's weight. The polynomial part is a finite
sum of terms c u^γ, |γ| < M, with c smooth; Lemma 20.6 (2), applied |γ| − 1 times with one factor u at the
order k + 3 and the product of the others at the order 0, bounded through (1) by the L^∞-norms of its factors, gives
‖c u^γ‖_(G^k) ≤ C_k ‖u‖_(E^(k+3)) ‖u‖_(E^(d_1))^(|γ|−1). The Taylor remainder is bounded by Lemma 20.6 (3) with
d = 3 in the weighted b-Sobolev space after a finite partition of unity: the proof of (3), by the chain rule and
(20.13), applies verbatim to a function smooth also in the point, with bounded derivatives on the chart
domains, and δ_Θ is fixed by the domain of Θ and C_Sob. ∎

loop is fixed by the weights and orders of the statement, never by k. At a base point with parameter b each statement
is used in its form at b, named in the entry where it differs from the form at b_0.

- Theorem 29.17 (at b, Corollary 29.25): FWD (Corollary 19.15); one step.

  L_b u = f − (L^(g,g_0) − L_b)u, finitely many.

### 35.4 The tame theorems

**Theorem 35.7** (The tame form of the forward problem with parameters.) Let ε ∈ (0, ε_1], and let
ε′(ε, j) ∈ (0, ε], j ∈ ℕ₀, non-increasing in j, be the input losses that Theorem 34.9 assigns to the output loss
ε (Section 35.1; independent of j for the statements listed there). There are d, d_0 ∈ ℕ and δ_𝔹 > 0 such that for
(h, p⃗, q) with ‖h‖_(𝒳^(d_0)) + |p⃗| + ‖q‖_(𝒬^(d_0)) < δ_𝔹 the maps F ↦ (h′, p⃗′, q′) of Theorem 34.9 (at a
rotating black hole parameter, of Proposition 36.8) satisfy, for every k ∈ ℕ₀,

    ‖h′‖_k + |p⃗′| + ‖q′‖_k ≤ C_k (‖F‖_(k+d) + (‖h‖_(k+d) + |p⃗| + ‖q‖_(k+d)) ‖F‖_d),    (35.2)

with ‖h′‖_k and ‖q′‖_k the norms of the order-k spaces of (34.6) and of 𝒬^k ((34.1)) at the loss
ε, the background norms at the loss ε, and ‖F‖_j the norm of the order-j space of 𝒴^♮(α−) at the loss ε′(ε, j). On the
exact scales of Section 35.5 it holds with ε′(ε, j) = ε = 0 for every j (Corollary 35.33). Here δ_𝔹 is at most the
radius of a ball about b_0 in ℬ_*, so the black hole parameter b of p⃗ lies in ℬ_*, and d, d_0, δ_𝔹 and the C_k do not
depend on b. The same holds for the solution maps of Chapter 29–Chapter 33 in their spaces (at a rotating b, those of
Theorem 33.18 and Proposition 33.31 read as in Lemma 36.7 and Proposition 36.8, with q = 0), and
for Theorem 34.9 with η_2 replaced by ε_+ (Lemma 34.23).

This is the tame estimate that [Hin26, Corollary 11.66, pp. 294–295] states.

*Proof.* By induction over the entries of Section 35.3 in their order. Each solution map is, by Section 35.3, a
composition of a fixed number of the families of Lemma 35.3 and of the solution maps of earlier entries, which
are tame by the induction; each loop has a length fixed independently of k. Lemma 35.2 (b)–(g) gives a tame
family with a loss d equal to the sum of the losses, independent of k, for d_0 ≥ d and δ_𝔹 small
(Lemma 35.5); the weights compose in the same way, each family taking its input in the graded space of the
losses its statement assigns (Section 35.1). For Theorem 34.9 the background is β = (h, p⃗, q), and
(35.1) is (35.2). At a base point with parameter b the entries are used in their forms at b; the
constants of Lemma 35.3 are uniform on ℬ̄_*, and d_* of Lemma 35.5 does not depend on b; so neither do
d, d_0 and the C_k. ∎

**Theorem 35.8** (The tame form of the right inverse.) Let ε ∈ (0, ε_1], and let ε′(ε, j), non-increasing in
j, be the input losses that Theorem 34.24 assigns, as in Theorem 35.7. There are d, d_0 ∈ ℕ and ε_0 > 0 such
that for U ∈ 𝒟^∞_ε with ‖U‖_(𝒟^(d_0)_ε) < ε_0, whose black hole parameter then lies in ℬ_*, the solution U′ of
(34.16) satisfies, for every k,

    ‖U′‖_(𝒟^k_ε) ≤ C_k (‖f‖_(ℱ^(k+d)_(ε′(ε,k+d))) + ‖U‖_(𝒟^(k+d)_ε) ‖f‖_(ℱ^d_(ε′(ε,d)))),    (35.3)

with C_k independent of U. On the exact scales of Section 35.5 it holds with ε′(ε, j) = ε = 0 for every j
(Corollary 35.33). At a rotating black hole parameter, U′ is built from the solution map of Proposition 36.8. The
smallness is in one norm for every k (Lemma 35.5), which replaces the orders d_k of Theorem 34.24.

This is the estimate of [Hin26, Theorem 12.8, p. 312].

*Proof.* Step 0 of the proof of Theorem 34.24 applies Theorem 35.7 at the background Φ(U), with ‖Φ(U)‖_k ≤ C_k
‖U‖_(𝒟^(k+d)) (Theorem 34.20) and ‖Φ(U)‖_(d_0) small for ‖U‖_(𝒟^(d_0+d)) small; composed with U ↦ Φ(U),
(35.2) has the form (35.1) in the background U. At a rotating black hole parameter b,
Lemma 34.23 holds for the output of Proposition 36.8: the indicial roots are those at b_0 (Lemma 30.2
(P2)), Proposition 28.8 holds at b ((P4) there), and neither A_b, which reads only ι⁺-data and level-1 tf-data
(Definition 36.6), nor E^ν, a fixed tensor (Lemma 36.1), depends on η_2. Steps 1–3, which hold at b with the rows
