built at b_0 (Section 34.8 (3)), subtract D_UΦ(U′_•) for finitely many U′_•: the finite-dimensional data of
Step 1 (bounded by a low norm of (h′, p⃗′, q′), Lemma 35.3 (c)); the data of Case B of Step 2,
f_(λ_0) ∈ Poly^(K_ι(λ_0))(ℂ; H^(k,…)) and G′(λ_0) ∈ Res^k, which are not finite-dimensional and are mapped by the right
inverse of Proposition 27.36, independent of U with the loss l, on the finitely many λ_0 ∈ Λ_* (Lemma 35.3 (g),
Lemma 35.2 (d)); and the conormal remainders of Step 3 (the conormal components of q′, Lemma 35.3 (c)).
By Remark 34.21,

    D_UΦ(U′) = DΦ_0(U_0)U′_0 + (DA(U_0)U′_0)U_1 + A(U_0)U′_1:

the first and third terms are tame in U′, uniformly in U_0 small (Theorem 34.20), and the second is bounded by
C|U′_0| ‖U_1‖_(𝒟^(k+d)), of the form (35.1), as |U′_0| is bounded by a low norm of f. Lemma 35.2
gives (35.3). ∎

**Proposition 35.9** (The forward map.) There are d and ε_0 such that for b near b_0, ε ∈ (0, ε_1] and
U ∈ 𝒟^∞_ε with ‖U‖_(𝒟^(3d)_ε) < ε_0,

    ‖P_5(Φ(U))‖_(ℱ^k_ε) ≤ C_k (1 + ‖U‖_(𝒟^(k+d)_ε)),        k ≥ d,

and the first and second derivatives of U ↦ P_5(Φ(U)) satisfy (20.3) with the norms of 𝒟^(3d)_ε and
ℱ^(2d)_ε. The map gains nothing in the weights: it takes 𝒟_ε to ℱ_ε.

This is [Hin26, Section 13.1, Step 3 (2), p. 322] in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* Φ is affine in U_1 with coefficients smooth in the finite-dimensional U_0, and tame (Theorem 34.20).
P_5(h, p⃗, q) = P_4(h + h_(b,rem)(q), p⃗) is Ric − δ*Υ of a metric that is a smooth function of p⃗ plus
h + h_(b,rem)(q), so a smooth function of (h, ∂h, ∂²h) and of q with coefficients smooth in p⃗; Lemma 20.6 (with
Lemma 14.55) bounds it and its first two derivatives tamely in the b-Sobolev norms. The weights are those of
(34.15), which holds at every b near b_0 (Theorem 34.20). The cancellation enters only qualitatively: the
terms of u-exponent below 3 + ε_+ cancel identically ((34.13)), so P_5(Φ(U)) lies in the partially
polyhomogeneous space with exponents in Λ + 2 whose coefficients below 5 + ε_+ vanish, and its ℱ^k_ε-norm is the sum of
the norms of the remaining coefficients and of the remainder, each a finite sum of products bounded by
Lemma 35.6, the weights adding as in the proof of (34.15). The linear terms L_b h keep the loss of h,
which is why no weight is gained. The second derivative is bilinear with two factors at the low norm. ∎

**Remark 35.10** (The hypotheses of the Nash–Moser theorem.) In the notation of Theorem 20.1, with the
map U ↦ P_5(Φ(U)) in the role of the map there and the right inverses of Theorem 35.8 in the role of Ψ(u),
Theorem 20.1 asks, on one pair of Banach scales: (i) smoothing operators on the spaces of 𝒟 (Proposition 20.4;
[Hin26, p. 322]); (ii) the tame forward map (Proposition 35.9), mapping U ∩ B^∞_η into F^∞_η; and (iii) tame right
inverses (Theorem 35.8) at every point of a neighbourhood of 0, so at b ≠ b_0 too, with Ψ(u)F^∞_η ⊂ B^∞_η for
u ∈ U ∩ B^∞_η. [Hin26, Section 13.1, Step 3 (3), p. 322] meets these support conditions by finite speed of
propagation. The pair of scales is that of Corollary 35.33, on which Proposition 35.9 maps 𝒟 to ℱ and the right
inverse maps ℱ to 𝒟, both without loss in the weights; the right inverses at b ≠ b_0 are those of Theorem 35.8
and Theorem 35.32, stated at every b ∈ ℬ_*. The support conditions, the smoothing operators on the exact spaces
𝒟_ex and the exterior family h_(−S) of Chapter 37 are supplied with the nonlinear theorem in Chapter 38.

### 35.5 The exact classes and the exactness conditions

Throughout Section 35.5–Section 35.10, α is a fixed K⁺-weight, admissible in the sense of Definition 33.3,
with α ∈ (4 + ε_K − ε′_0, 4 + ε_K], satisfying (A_J) of Definition 34.12 and Definition 35.13 below. The exact
classes and the conditions of Definition 35.13 do not involve the black hole parameter b of the base point: the
exponents, indicial roots and index sets in them are those at b_0, which serve at every b ∈ ℬ̄_*
(Lemma 30.2 (P2)–(P3)).

**Definition 35.11** (Exact classes.) Each class below is the class named after it with every order "w−"
replaced by w and every index set unchanged:

- 𝒳^k_(J,ex) := H^(k,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(ℰ_+,3+ε_+),α)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−) (the class 𝒳^k_J of Definition 34.13);
- ℱ^k_ex := H^(k,(⟨ℰ^C_I+1⟩′,ℓ_I+1),w_+,α)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−), a plain weight at ι⁺ (the class ℱ^k of
  Definition 34.13);
- 𝒴^0_ex(β) and 𝒴^♮_ex(β): the classes 𝒴^0(β) of Section 33.2 and 𝒴^♮(β) of Definition 33.26 with the
  ι⁺-weight w_+ − ε replaced by w_+ (their K⁺-weight β is exact already);
- 𝒬_ex: the class 𝒬 of (34.1) with S_rem ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−2)_b, b_rem ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−1)_b and
  Y_ψ ∈ Ḣ^(∞,𝒬(ℰ^α_ψ,3+ε_+−d_ψ))_b;
- 𝒟^k_ex: the class of Definition 34.15 with S_rem ∈ Ḣ^(k,α−2)_b, b_rem ∈ Ḣ^(k,α−1)_b,
  Y_(ψ,rem) ∈ Ḣ^(k,3+ε_+−d_ψ)_b and h̃ ∈ H^(k,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),3+ε_+,α)_b, normed by the norms of its components at these
  fixed weights.

These are the classes of [Hin26, (11.226), p. 292; (11.227b), p. 293; (11.233), p. 294; (12.12c)–(12.12d), p. 301;
(12.31), p. 310], with (3 + ε_I, 4 + ε_I) read as (ℓ_I, ℓ_I + 1) and 4 + ε_K as α. Each 𝒟^k_ex and ℱ^k_ex is a Banach
space.

**Remark 35.12** (Inclusions.) Each exact class is continuously embedded in its "w−" class: the index sets
are the same and the weight is larger. And ℱ_ex ⊂ 𝒴^0_ex(α): a plain weight w_+ is the class (ℰ^0_src + 2, w_+) with
vanishing coefficients, as Step 0 of the proof of Theorem 34.24 argues for the "w−" classes. So every statement of
Chapter 29–Chapter 34 applies to exact inputs. Only statements whose output must lie in an exact class are proved anew
below.

**Definition 35.13** (The exactness conditions.) Besides admissibility and (A_J):

- (Ex1) (G⁺) of Definition 34.11, used with its closed endpoint: no λ ∈ Λ has real part in (3, 3 + ε_+], that is,
  ε_+ < min{Re λ − 3 : λ ∈ Λ, Re λ > 3}, a smallness condition. With Lemma 33.2 (c) (every exponent produced
  with real part in [2, 3 + ε_+] lies in Λ), no exponent produced has u-exponent of real part 3 + ε_+.
- (Ex2) 3 + ε_+ ∉ Re π_1ℰ^tot_I ∪ {λ_♯}: the exclusions of Proposition 29.29 (Re π_1ℰ^C_I and λ_♯) and of
  Proposition 29.27 (Re π_1ℰ^tot_I) at the ι⁺-weight 3 + ε_+; here ℰ^tot_I ⊃ ℰ^C_I ((27.8)).
- (Ex3) No K⁺-exponent at hand (of the coefficients of the pieces, of the rows, and their ℕ₀-shifts, as in
  Lemma 34.8) has real part α − 2, α − 1 or α. The first and the last are contained in admissibility (the
  proof of Lemma 34.8); the middle one is an additional condition.
- (Ex4) α − Re α_0 ≠ −μ and α − 1 − Re α_0 ≠ −μ for every root μ and the finitely many tf-exponents α_0 of levels 1–2
  of Proposition 33.15: the conditions (27.51) at ℓ_zf = α − 2 and α − 3.
- (A_K) (Optional.) α := 4 + ε_K is admissible and satisfies (A_J), (Ex3) and (Ex4).

No condition is needed for the final zero-energy solve: Lemma 29.33 excludes no real part and asks only
β_tf − β_zf = α_sf + 2, where α_sf denotes the weight α of (28.1) (not the K⁺-weight α of this chapter), and
α_sf + 2 ∈ (0, 1).

**Lemma 35.14** (The conditions are generic.) (Ex1) is a smallness condition on ε_+, (Ex2) excludes finitely
many ε_+ in any bounded range, (Ex3)–(Ex4) exclude finitely many α, and (A_K) excludes finitely many ε_K at fixed ε_+. So
admissible α with (Ex3)–(Ex4) exist in (4 + ε_K − ε′_0, 4 + ε_K], and ε_+, ε_K may be decreased to meet (Ex1)–(Ex2) and
(A_K), as (G⁺) and (G) already permit.

*Proof.* The excluded numbers are built from finitely many numbers that do not depend on α, ε_+ or ε_K within the ranges
used: the roots μ, discrete with finitely many in any bounded set (Proposition 25.6); Λ and the tf-exponents α_0 of
levels 1–2, Λ-valued below 3 and finitely many (Lemma 33.2); the exponents at hand below α + 1, finitely many
and Λ-generated (the proof of Lemma 34.8); λ_♯; and Re π_1ℰ^tot_I, an index set, finite below any bound. Each
of (Ex2)–(Ex4) and (A_K) removes the values of α, ε_+ or ε_K equal to one of finitely many such numbers; (Ex1) is (G⁺)
itself, an upper bound on ε_+. ∎

### 35.6 Two elementary lemmas

**Lemma 35.15** (Diagonal terms at ι⁺ ∩ K⁺.) Near the corner let a = t_*^(−c) G(t_*) with
G ∈ H_b([1, ∞), |dt_*/t_*|), and let P be homogeneous of degree −m in r. Then aP ∈ ρ_+^(c+m−η) ρ_K^c H_b and
aP ∈ ρ_+^(c+m) ρ_K^(c−η) H_b for every η > 0, while in general aP ∉ ρ_+^(c+m) ρ_K^c L²_b.

*Proof.* With t_*⁻¹ = ρ_+ρ_K and r⁻¹ = ρ_+,

    ρ_+^(−a_+) ρ_K^(−a_K) aP = ρ_+^(c+m−a_+) ρ_K^(c−a_K) G(1/(ρ_+ρ_K)) P_0,

with P_0 smooth on the sphere. In s := −log ρ_+ and σ := −log ρ_K the squared L²_b-norm at (a_+, a_K) = (c + m, c) is
∫_0^∞ T |G(e^T)|² dT, T = s + σ, which G ∈ L²(dT) does not bound; with the extra factor e^(−2ηs) or e^(−2ησ) it is at
most (2η)⁻¹ ‖G‖², as ∫_0^T e^(−2ηs) ds ≤ (2η)⁻¹. Derivatives are treated in the same way. ∎

**Lemma 35.16** (Circle integrals of bounded families.) Let Z ↪ Z_− be a continuous injection of Hilbert
spaces, γ a circle, and F : γ → Z_− continuous with sup_γ ‖F‖_Z ≤ M. Then I := ∫_γ F dλ (in Z_−) lies in Z, and
‖I‖_Z ≤ |γ|M.

*Proof.* The Riemann sums S_n converge to I in Z_− and satisfy ‖S_n‖_Z ≤ |γ|M. A subsequence converges weakly in Z to
some I′; the injection is weakly continuous, so the subsequence converges weakly in Z_− to I′. Hence I = I′ and
‖I‖_Z ≤ liminf ‖S_n‖_Z. ∎

### 35.7 The graft at the exact K⁺-weight

Fix φ ∈ C^∞((0, ∞)), positive, with φ(R) = R for R ≤ 1/2 and φ = 1 for R ≥ 2, and put ρ_+ := (t_* φ(R))⁻¹ near ι⁺.
Near ι⁺ ∩ K⁺ it is 1/r, near ι⁺ ∩ ℐ⁺ it is 1/t_* (Section 29.15); so it is a boundary defining function of ι⁺. The
expansions of [Hin26, Definition 2.8, p. 48], in which the classes of Chapter 29–Chapter 34 are defined (Chapter 21),
are in powers of ρ_+ and log ρ_+, with coefficients on ι⁺ that carry the weights of the adjacent faces. Near the corner
log ρ_+ = −log t_* − log ρ_K, so

    ρ_+^z (log ρ_+)^ℓ a = t_*^(−z) Σ_(j≤ℓ) (ℓ choose j) (−1)^ℓ (log t_*)^j (log ρ_K)^(ℓ−j) ρ_K^(−z) a.    (35.4)

**Remark 35.17** (The two conventions at the exact weight.) Corollary 26.44 takes

    f = Σ_(j≤k) χ_ι t_*^(−λ_0−2) (log t_*)^j f^(j)_+ + f′,        f^(j)_+ ∈ ⋂_ε H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,ℓ_K−2−ε)_b(ι⁺),

and concludes (26.57) at the K⁺-weight λ_0 + ℓ_K − ε. By (35.4) a right side of exact K⁺-weight α
in the sense of [Hin26, Definition 2.8] has t_*-coefficients containing (log R)^(ℓ−j) R^(−z) a_ℓ, which lie in
H^(α−Re z−ε) for every ε > 0 but in general not at ε = 0:

    ‖R^(−w+ε) (log R)^k g‖ ≤ (k/(eε))^k ‖R^(−w) g‖,

as sup_(0<R<1) R^ε |log R|^k = (k/(eε))^k, and this is sharp. Conversely, for k = 1, f^(0) = 0 and f^(1) = g generic in
H^(ℓ_K−2), the coefficient of ρ_+^(λ_0+2) in the expansion of [Hin26, Definition 2.8] is −(log φ) φ^(λ_0+2) g, as
log t_* = −log ρ_+ − log φ, and it is not in H^α. So for k ≥ 1 the two classes at the exact weight are incomparable (for
k = 0 they coincide), and Corollary 26.44 cannot be applied at ε = 0 to a right side of the class of [Hin26,
Definition 2.8]; in its own convention it is stated with the loss, with constants of order ε^(−k). Whether an exact
statement exists in that convention is not decided here; none is needed. [Hin26, Corollary 9.12, p. 179] has the same
loss; [Hin26, Proposition 11.34] states the exact weight after the same step ([Hin26, (11.120b), p. 254]), which
Corollary 35.18 justifies.

**Corollary 35.18** (Corollary 26.44 at the exact K⁺-weight.) Let Re λ_0 > 1, let l_0 be the order of the
pole of N_ι⁺(L̄, ·)⁻¹ at λ_0 (0 if none), let ℓ_I be as in Theorem 26.42 with Re λ_0 < ℓ_I, and let α ∈ ℝ with
ℓ_K := α − Re λ_0 ∈ (−1, ℓ^max_K), ℓ_K ≠ −μ for every root μ, and ℓ_K ∉ Re π_1ℰ_K. Let k ∈ ℕ₀ and

    f = Σ_(j≤k) χ_ι ρ_+^(λ_0+2) (log ρ_+)^j a_j + f′,
    a_j ∈ H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,α)_b(ι⁺),        f′ ∈ H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,∞,α)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−),    (35.5)

the weight α of a_j being at ι⁺ ∩ K⁺, as [Hin26, Definition 2.8] prescribes for a right side of K⁺-weight α. Then
there are u^(j)_(b,0) of the form (26.55), with λ_0 for λ and a factor (log t_*)^j, and
v_m ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_(ι⁺,ℐ)⟩,ℓ_I),α)_b(ι⁺), m ≤ k + l_0, all linear in (a_j, f′), such that
u := Σ_j χ_K u^(j)_(b,0) + Σ_m χ_ι ρ_+^(λ_0) (log ρ_+)^m v_m satisfies

    f − L_b u ∈ H^(∞,(ℰ^tot_(ι⁺,ℐ)+2,ℓ_I+1), λ_0+2+ℰ_ind+(0,k+l_0), α)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−),    (35.6)

the ι⁺-index set taken with respect to ρ_+. For each k′ there are d and C bounding every order-k′ seminorm of u and of
f − L_b u by C(Σ_j ‖a_j‖_(k′+d) + ‖f′‖_(k′+d)). By (35.4), (35.5) implies the hypotheses of
Corollary 26.44 and (35.6) implies (26.57). For k = l_0 = 0 it is Theorem 26.42 at
λ = λ_0.

This is [Hin26, Corollary 9.12, p. 179] in the convention of [Hin26, Definition 2.8], and the exact form of
Corollary 26.44 in dimension 4 + 1. The proof uses a lemma on the family of Theorem 26.42 along a circle.

*The circle.* Choose δ ∈ (0, 1/4) with δ < min(Re λ_0 − 1, ℓ_I − Re λ_0, ℓ^max_K − ℓ_K), such that
D̄ := {|λ − λ_0| ≤ δ} meets spec_ι⁺(L̄) at most in λ_0, and J := [ℓ_K − 3δ, ℓ_K + δ] ⊂ (−1, ℓ^max_K) contains no −μ and
no point of Re π_1ℰ_K. This is possible, as the spectrum has finitely many points in each half plane
(Lemma 26.29 (a)) and the roots and ℰ_K are discrete. On ∂D, ℓ_K(λ) := α − Re λ ∈ J, λ ≠ 1,
1 < Re λ < ℓ_I, and the window 𝒲(ℓ) of Theorem 26.27 is the same for every ℓ ∈ J. For a ∈ H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,α)_b(ι⁺)
put f_+(λ) := φ^(−λ−2) a. Near R = 0, |R^(−λ−2)| = R^(−Re λ−2) and (R∂_R)^i R^(−λ−2) = (−λ − 2)^i R^(−λ−2), and φ = 1
near ℐ⁺; so ‖f_+(λ)‖_(H^(k′,ℓ_I+1,ℓ_K(λ)−2)) ≤ C ‖a‖_(H^(k′,ℓ_I+1,α)) uniformly on D̄. Theorem 26.42 at λ ∈ ∂D,
with ℓ_K(λ) and the right side f_+(λ), gives u(λ) = χ_K u_(b,0)(λ) + χ_ι t_*^(−λ) ũ(λ) and the remainder
r(λ) := χ_ι t_*^(−λ−2) f_+(λ) − L_b u(λ), whose K⁺-weight in (26.56) is Re λ + ℓ_K(λ) = α for every λ. By
the choice of ρ_+, χ_ι t_*^(−λ−2) f_+(λ) = χ_ι ρ_+^(λ+2) a and t_*^(−λ) ũ(λ) = ρ_+^λ U(λ) with U(λ) := φ^λ ũ(λ). Since
∂_λ brings the factor −log φ and R^δ |log R| is bounded, f_+ is holomorphic near D̄ with values in
H^(ℓ_I+1,ℓ_K−3δ−2); at that fixed weight the family of Theorem 26.42 is holomorphic off the spectrum ([Hin26,
(9.42), p. 178]), so u(λ) and r(λ) are holomorphic near ∂D and meromorphic in D, with at most a pole at λ_0, in spaces
Z_− of K⁺-weight α − 4δ.

**Lemma 35.19** (Exact bounds on the circle.) There are d and C such that for every λ ∈ ∂D

    ‖U(λ)‖_(H^(k′,(⟨ℰ^C_(ι⁺,ℐ)⟩,ℓ_I),α)_b(ι⁺)) + Σ |Y^(μ)_τ(λ)| ≤ C ‖a‖_(k′+d),

and r(λ) = Σ_((e,p)) χ ρ_+^(λ+2+e) (log ρ_+)^p c_(e,p)(λ) + r_M(λ), a finite sum over (e, p) ∈ ℰ_ind with Re e < M,
with each c_(e,p)(λ) bounded by C‖a‖_(k′+d) in H^(k′,(ℰ^tot_(ι⁺,ℐ)+2,ℓ_I+1),α)_b(ι⁺) and r_M(λ) in the space of plain
ι⁺-weight Re λ_0 + 2 + M − δ and K⁺-weight α.

*Proof.* (i) *At the lower weight.* Theorem 26.27 (2) bounds N_ι⁺(λ)⁻¹ at the fixed weight ℓ_K^− := ℓ_K − 3δ,
locally uniformly in λ off the poles, hence uniformly on the compact circle ∂D; and the coefficients Y^(μ)_τ are
continuous linear functionals of (u, f) there. So Y(λ) and ũ(λ) are bounded in H^(ℓ_K^−) uniformly on ∂D.

(ii) *Up to the exact weight, uniformly.* Near R = 0, (26.29) gives R²N_ι⁺(λ) = A_0 + RA_1(λ) with
A_0 = L̃(0)(ω, −R∂_R, ∂_ω) independent of λ, b-elliptic, with boundary spectrum {−μ}. With ũ = u_+ − χ_K u_0 and
N_ι⁺(λ)u_+ = 2f_+,

    A_0(χũ) = χ[2R² f_+(λ) − RA_1(λ)ũ − R² N_ι⁺(λ)(χ_K u_0(λ))] + [A_0, χ]ũ =: g(λ).

Its terms lie in R^(ℓ_K(λ)) H_b (the first), in R^(ℓ_K^−+1) H_b ⊂ R^(ℓ_K(λ)) H_b (the second, as 4δ ≤ 1), in
R^(−μ+k_μ+1) C^∞ ⊂ R³ C^∞ (the third, by the form of u_0, (26.49) and Lemma 26.38), and have compact
support in R > 0 (the last); all uniformly on ∂D, bounded by C‖a‖. The strip {Re ζ ∈ J} avoids {−μ}, so

    C_J := sup_(Re ζ∈J) Σ_(i≤2) |ζ|^(2−i) ‖N(A_0, ζ)⁻¹‖_(H^s→H^(s+i)) < ∞,

by the elliptic estimate with parameter of Section 21.9.1 for |Im ζ| large and by continuity on the compact rest of
the strip, where N(A_0, ζ) is invertible by (E3) of Section 21.9.1. Then the Mellin transform of χũ is N(A_0, ·)⁻¹
applied to that of g; it continues holomorphically from Re ζ < ℓ_K^− to Re ζ ≤ ℓ_K(λ) with no pole in the strip; moving
the line as in the proof of Lemma 21.35 and using Plancherel on Re ζ = ℓ_K(λ) gives

    ‖χũ(λ)‖_(R^(ℓ_K(λ)) H^(k′)_b) ≤ C′_J ‖g(λ)‖_(R^(ℓ_K(λ)) H^(k′−2)_b) + C ‖ũ(λ)‖_(R^(ℓ_K^−) H^(k′)_b),

with C′_J depending only on C_J and J. This is Lemma 21.35 with its constant uniform over the weights in J, which
its Mellin proof gives. As φ^λ is b-smooth with |R^λ| = R^(Re λ), ‖U(λ)‖_α ≤ C ‖ũ(λ)‖_(ℓ_K(λ)).

(iii) *The remainder.* Near the corner, where χ_K = χ_ι = 1, Lemma 26.41 for t_*^(−λ) ũ gives

    r(λ) = ½ t_*^(−λ−2) N_ι⁺(λ)u_0 − L_b u_(b,0) − ½ t_*^(−λ−4) v² B ũ.

The explicit part has K⁺-exponents ≥ λ − μ + k_μ + 1 ≥ λ + 3 and ι⁺-exponents in λ + 2 + ℰ_ind, with coefficients
polynomial in λ times Y(λ); since Re λ + 3 − α ≥ 3 − ℓ_K − δ > 0 it lies at K⁺-weight α with uniform bounds, its
log ρ_K powers sitting strictly above α. In the last term t_*^(−λ−4) v² = ρ_+^(λ+4) φ^(λ+2) ϖ², ϖ := φ/R; Taylor
expansion of the coefficients of B in 1/r = ρ_+ϖ gives terms ρ_+^(λ+4+m) ϖ^(m+2) φ² B^λ_m U(λ) with
B^λ_m := φ^λ B_m φ^(−λ) polynomial in λ and coefficients in H^(α+2) ⊂ H^α at R = 0. Near K⁺ with r bounded,
r(λ) = χ_ι ρ_+^(λ+2) a − L_b(ρ_+^λ U(λ)) − L_b u_(b,0) with ρ_+ = 1/r smooth, and L_b ∈ Diff_b there
(Section 29.15), so every term is at weight α uniformly. Away from K⁺, the proof of Theorem 26.42 applies
verbatim with u_+(λ) uniformly bounded. This exhibits the decomposition of r(λ) with the stated bounds. ∎

*Proof of Corollary 35.18.* Since ∂^j_λ ρ_+^(λ+2) = (log ρ_+)^j ρ_+^(λ+2), Cauchy's formula gives

    χ_ι ρ_+^(λ_0+2) (log ρ_+)^j a_j = (j!/(2πi)) ∮_(∂D) (λ − λ_0)^(−j−1) χ_ι t_*^(−λ−2) f_(+,j)(λ) dλ,
                                                                          f_(+,j)(λ) := φ^(−λ−2) a_j.

Let Φ_(ι,b)(λ) be the map f_+ ↦ u of Theorem 26.42 at λ, and put
u := Σ_j (j!/(2πi)) ∮ (λ − λ_0)^(−j−1) Φ_(ι,b)(λ) f_(+,j)(λ) dλ, an integral in Z_−, with which L_b commutes. With
U_j and r_j the functions U and r of the circle for a := a_j,

    f − L_b u = f′ + Σ_j (j!/(2πi)) ∮ (λ − λ_0)^(−j−1) r_j(λ) dλ.

Expanding ρ_+^(λ+c) = ρ_+^(λ_0+c) Σ_m (log ρ_+)^m (λ − λ_0)^m/m! pointwise, the ι⁺-part of u is
χ_ι ρ_+^(λ_0) Σ_m (log ρ_+)^m v_m with

    v_m = Σ_j (j!/m!) (1/(2πi)) ∮ (λ − λ_0)^(m−j−1) U_j(λ) dλ,

which vanish for m > k + l_0 (the order of the Laurent series); the coefficients of the remainder are circle integrals
of the c_(e,p)(λ), which are polynomial in λ, Y(λ) and U(λ), hence meromorphic in D with pole order at most l_0, so the
same Laurent cut-off applies to them, and its rest is the circle integral of r_M(λ). Lemma 35.16, with Z the
space at the exact weight α (the coefficient spaces on ι⁺, and the space of plain ι⁺-weight Re λ_0 + 2 + M − δ) and
Z_− the same at α − 4δ, with Lemma 35.19 bounding the integrands, gives v_m ∈ H^((⟨ℰ^C⟩,ℓ_I),α)(ι⁺), the
coefficients of f − L_b u in H^((ℰ^tot+2,ℓ_I+1),α)(ι⁺) with exponents in λ_0 + 2 + ℰ_ind + (0, k + l_0), and the rest
at K⁺-weight α. As M is arbitrary, this is (35.6). The u_(b,0)-part becomes Σ_j χ_K u^(j)_(b,0) with the
Laurent coefficients of Y(λ) (the form (26.55)). The linearity and the bounds, with constants
Cδ^(−k−l_0−1), follow from Lemma 35.19. ∎

**Proposition 35.20** (The uses of the graft at the top level.) Let f ∈ 𝒴^0_ex(α), with (Ex1)–(Ex3). Then
Proposition 33.8 holds with: (a) u_I of ι⁺-data (ℰ_I, 3 + ε_+); (b) K⁺-weight α − 2 in place of α − 2 − ε;
(c) f^♭ ∈ H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,(ℰ^♭+2,w_+),α)_b. And the piece (ii) of Theorem 33.24, the graft remainder, has K⁺-order
exactly α.

*Proof.* (a) Step 1 of the proof of Proposition 33.8 takes ℓ̆_+ := w_+ − 2 − ε off its exclusions, for all but
finitely many ε; the exclusions are those of Proposition 29.29 (Re π_1ℰ^C_I and λ_♯) and of Proposition 29.27
(Re π_1ℰ^tot_I), and by (Ex2) ℓ̆_+ := w_+ − 2 = 3 + ε_+ is allowed. Proposition 29.27 and Proposition 29.29 are
exact at an allowed weight; (Ex2) is used again in the removals at ℐ⁺ of Step 2 and in the regularity at ℐ⁺ in
Proposition 35.23 (Proposition 29.27 at ℓ_+ = 3 + ε_+).

(c) At K⁺: Step 2 takes c_K := α and applies the graft to the coefficients of the current right side, which lie in
H^(∞,ℓ_I+1,α)_b(ι⁺) with respect to ρ_+ (𝒴^0(α) is a class of [Hin26, Definition 2.8], exact at K⁺);
Corollary 35.18 replaces Corollary 26.44, and each graft error has the exact K⁺-weight α by (35.6), so
the iteration closes at α. The part of the right side that does not reach ι⁺ near the corner (the difference between
the cut-off of [Hin26, Definition 2.8] and χ_ι) goes into f′. The K⁺-weight α − ε of Step 1 is a free weakening (f_1
has K⁺-weight α). At ι⁺: f^♭ = f − L_b(u_I + u_ι) with f at (ℰ^♭ + 2, w_+), L_b u_I at (ℰ_I + 2, w_+) by (a), and u_ι
a finite sum of single ι⁺-terms; by (Ex1) no exponent has real part w_+, so the integrations of Lemma 21.33 and
Lemma 21.35, which are exact at weights that are not exponents, are applied at such a weight (the class of
[Hin26, Definition 2.8] itself expands every exponent of real part at most the weight).

(b) Its K⁺-ingredients are the ι⁺-part of u_λ, of K⁺-weight α > α − 2; the rows, identified up to K⁺-weight
Re λ_0 + 1 − ε > 5/2 > α − 2; and the c-rows of rate > 2 + ε_K ≥ α − 2, of weight their rate minus ε, which exceeds
α − 2 for ε small; each inequality is strict. At a rotating b the v1 terms of exponent of real part below 2 are the
rotation rows with the coefficients of Proposition 36.5 (a), read from the ι⁺-data of the graft, which do not
depend on the loss; they are identified up to K⁺-order Re λ_0 + 1 − ε > α − 2, with room. The piece (ii) of
Theorem 33.24 is the graft remainder χ_ι ρ_+^(λ_0) (log ρ_+)^m v_m of Corollary 35.18, of K⁺-order exactly α.
∎

### 35.8 The spectral construction at exact weights

**Proposition 35.21** (Proposition 21.45 is exact at K and zf.) For
β_K ∈ (0, ∞) ∖ (ℕ ∪ Re π_1E_K), Proposition 21.45 (1) maps the exact K-weight β_K to the exact zf-weight β_K − 1
((21.66)) and (2) maps it back ((21.68)); the losses ε there sit at ℐ and scf only. The constants are
bounded for β_K in compact subsets of (0, ∞) ∖ (ℕ ∪ Re π_1E_K), the other data fixed.

*Proof.* The chain below Proposition 21.45 is: Lemma 20.8, Plancherel as an equivalence of norms at every
weight; Proposition 20.14, which converts H^(β−1/2) into |σ|^(β−1) L²(|dσ/σ|) modulo the Taylor polynomial, in both
directions, for β ∈ (0, ∞) ∖ ℕ, losing derivatives only, through the Hardy inequalities of Lemma 20.9 (b)–(c),
whose constants are built from 2^(±(θ−1/2)), θ the fractional part of β − 1/2, and are bounded for |θ − 1/2| ≥ c,
that is, for β away from ℕ; and Proposition 20.18 (1) and Proposition 20.20 (1), exact at K, whose loss ε is at scf.
The proof of Proposition 21.45 raises its auxiliary weight β̃_K back to β_K, with the full weight β_K at K, and
integrates at zf by Lemma 21.33 at weights different from the exponents, with the constant of (21.52),
the reciprocal of the distance of the weight from the exponent, bounded away from them. The losses of derivatives are
piecewise constant in the weights. ∎

At the weights used below, α, α − 1 and α − 2, the fractional part of β − 1/2 differs from 1/2 by
α − 4 ≥ ε_K − ε′_0 > 0.

**Lemma 35.22** (Lemma 33.7 (b) without δ.) Under the hypotheses of Lemma 33.7, (b) holds
with O(t^(−β−1)) in place of O(t^(−β−1+δ)), also after applying (t∂_t)^l.

*Proof.* ∫_(|σ|<1/|t|) |σ|^β dσ = (2/(β + 1)) |t|^(−β−1) (β > −1). On (1/|t|, c), integrate by parts m := ⌈β⌉ + 1
times, using |∂^j_σ(χ r^±)| ≤ C|σ|^(β−j) (from the hypothesis and ∂^j_σ = σ^(−j) Σ_(i≤j) a_(ji) (σ∂_σ)^i): the boundary
terms at |σ| = 1/|t| are O(|t|^(−β−1)), and the integral is at most

    |t|^(−m) ∫_(1/|t|)^c σ^(β−m) dσ ≤ |t|^(−β−1)/(⌈β⌉ − β),

with ⌈β⌉ − β > 0 as β ∉ ℕ₀. And t∂_t ℱ⁻¹v = ℱ⁻¹(−(1 + σ∂_σ)v) preserves the hypothesis. ∎

**Proposition 35.23** (Proposition 33.15 at exact weights.) Let α satisfy Definition 35.13, and let
f^♭ and u_I be as in Proposition 35.20. Run Proposition 33.15 with the zf-parameter 0 (zf-weights
ℓ_j := α − 1 − j, ℓ_3 := α − 4 ∈ (0, ε_K]), the level-2 threshold Re α_0 < 2 + ε_+, μ_2 := 2 + η^0_2 (the value fixed
in Section 33.5), μ′ := 2 + ε_+, and the first level-3 tf-weight τ_3 := 1 + ε_+. Then (33.10) holds
with ι⁺-data (ℰ_ι, 3 + ε_+) for v_low minus the constant columns and with K⁺-weight α − 2, with the same S_ν;
(33.11) of Lemma 33.16 and (33.13) of Theorem 33.18 hold at K⁺-weight α − 2; and
all tensors are those of the construction of Proposition 33.15.

*Proof.* We follow the steps of the proof of Proposition 33.15; only the weights change.

*Step 0.* Lemma 29.32 with β_K = α ∈ (4, 5), then Proposition 21.45 (1) with β_ι = w_+, E_ι = ℰ^♭ + 2,
E_I = ∅, β_K = α, E_K = ∅; its hypotheses hold (w_+ ∉ Re π_1E_ι by (Ex1); ℓ_I + 1 > w_+ − 1 by (H4) of
Section 33.2). By Proposition 35.21, g_0 ∈ H^(∞,(5/2−ε,(ℰ^♭+1,w_+−1),((0,0),α−1)))_b.

*Levels 0–1.* Lemma 33.10 at μ′ = w_+ − 1 and 3 + ε_+ rests on Lemma 21.35 at β = μ′ − 2 = 2 + ε_+,
resp. 1 + ε_+: not the real part of a root, since these numbers are not integers and the non-integer roots
with |μ| ≤ 50 have d(Re μ, ℤ) ≥ ε_ind > ε_+ ((25.10)). Lemma 33.11 lowers the tf-weight by 1 and the
zf-weight ((0,0), z) to ((0,0), z − 1) exactly. Proposition 27.55 at level 1 with ℓ_zf = α − 2: its conditions
(27.51) hold (−ε_ind < α − Re α_0; α − 2 − min(Re α_0 − 2, 0) < 3 = ℓ^max_K under (C5) of
Section 33.2; α − 2 ∉ ℕ₀; the root condition is (Ex4)), and its remainder keeps zf ((0,0), α − 2) exactly. So g_1,
g_2 have tf-weights 3 + ε_+, 2 + ε_+ and zf-weights α − 2, α − 3.

*Level 2.* The tf-exponents of the level-2 right sides are u-exponents minus 1, (Λ − 1)-valued; by (Ex1) none has real
part in (2, 2 + ε_+], so the threshold 2 + ε_+ treats the same (α_0, k) as 2 + η^0_2, and the conditions of
Proposition 27.55 are those already met (with (Ex4) at ℓ_zf = α − 3). After the rounds the zf-coefficient F of the
level-2 right side lies in H^(∞,(E,2+ε_+))_b(X̄) with min Re E > 2 + ε_+. Lemma 33.10 with μ = μ_2 and
μ′ = 2 + ε_+: μ_2 ∈ (2, 3), μ′ ∈ (μ_2, 5], min Re E > μ; Proposition 28.8 at the interior weight
μ_2 − 2 = η^0_2 ∈ (0, 1); Lemma 21.35 up to μ′ − 2 = ε_+, not a root, as no root has real part in (0, 1]
(Proposition 25.6 (a)). So û_2 ∈ H^(∞,ε_+)_b, and Lemma 33.11 gives g_3 of tf-weight exactly 1 + ε_+, with no
tf-exponent of real part ≤ 1 + ε_+ (the exponents of E − 1 exceed 1 + ε_+; those of 2 + ℰ_col are ≥ 2), and zf
((0,0), ℓ_3).

*Level 3.* Proposition 27.58 at α_τ = 1 + ε_+, ℓ_zf = ℓ_3: α_τ ∈ (1, 2); w := ℓ_3 − α_τ + 2 = ℓ_3 + 1 − ε_+ ∈
(1 − ε_+, 1), as 0 < ℓ_3 ≤ ε_K < ε_+ ((32.27)), so −ε_ind < w < ℓ^max_K; ℓ_3 ∉ ℕ₀; w ≠ −μ and
2 − α_τ = 1 − ε_+ ≠ −μ, as both lie within ε_+ < ε_ind of the integer 1 without being integers ((25.10)).
Its proof uses the conditions
2 − α_τ + j ≠ −μ only for j ≤ ⌊ℓ_zf⌋ = 0. The output is exact at tf and zf: the piece σ³u has tf-weight 2 + ε_+ and
zf ((0,0), ℓ_3). Later rounds start from tf-weights ≥ 1 + ε_+ + ε_ind − ε, with fixed room above 2 + ε_+ − 1; their α_τ
may be lowered freely, so their conditions hold off a finite set of α_τ, and their zf-weight ℓ_3 is kept. The final
zero-energy solve: Lemma 29.33 with β_zf := ℓ_3 (Lemma 29.33 puts no condition on β_zf) and
β_tf − β_zf ∈ (0, 1) gives ḃ_f, S_f ∈ H^(∞,ℓ_3)_b and û_f with zf-weight ℓ_3.

*Step 5.* Lemma 35.22 with β := α − 3 ∉ ℕ₀: the exponents with Re z < α − 3 are in E, those above in r^±, none
at α − 3 by (Ex3); r^± = O(|σ|^(α−3)) follows from the zf-weight α − 3 of σ³ĥ^aug(S_f) by the one-dimensional
b-Sobolev embedding in log|σ|. This gives O(t_*^(−α+2)) in {r ≤ R}; Step 6 needs only o(t_*^(−2)).

*Step 7.* The pieces have zf-data ((0,0) ∪̄ (E_K − 1), α − 3) and tf-data (E_tf, 2 + ε_+) with E_tf + 1 Λ-valued below
3 + ε_+: the zero-energy pieces σ^j χ_zf û_j (j ≤ 2) at tf 2 + ε_+; the tf-model pieces, polyhomogeneous at tf; the
first level-3 round at 2 + ε_+ and the later ones above. Proposition 21.45 (2) with β_ι := 3 + ε_+ (not in
Re π_1E_ι by (Ex1)) and β_K := α − 2 (not in ℕ ∪ Re π_1E_K by admissibility) gives v_low minus the constant columns in
H^(∞,3/2−4ε,(E_ι,3+ε_+),(E_K,α−2))_b; the constant columns are polyhomogeneous at ι⁺ with Λ-valued exponents, none at
3 + ε_+. The matching and the identification of the coefficients are as in the proof of Proposition 33.15.
Lemma 33.16 and Theorem 33.18 need only the count of Step 0, which has room (w_0 + a_K > α).

*At a rotating b.* The v1 terms of the spectral phase at level 1 and real part 2 are the rotation rows with the
coefficients of Proposition 36.5 (b), read from the tf-data, which do not depend on the loss; the argument above is
unchanged.

*Same tensors.* Moving μ′ only moves where Lemma 21.35 stops; the level-2 solve is at μ_2 as before (the inverses
of Proposition 28.8 at two such weights agree); the threshold treats the same exponents; and Proposition 27.58
solves by Mellin inversion on Re λ = α_τ − 2, and moving that line from η^0_2 − 1 − 2ε to ε_+ − 1 crosses no root (a
root in (−1, −1 + ε_+] would lie within ε_+ < ε_ind of −1). ∎

**Lemma 35.24** (Lemma 33.21 in L².) In Lemma 33.21 let a > −1 with a + 2, a + 3 ∉ ℕ. Then
A ∈ Ḣ^(∞,a+2)_b, B ∈ Ḣ^(∞,a+3)_b, and the remainders R_S, R_b have K⁺-order a + 4 in the L²-b sense:
χ_({r≤t_*/8}) R_S ∈ t_*^(−a−4) r⁻¹ H^∞_b (L² in |dt_*/t_*|, locally in x, with b-derivatives), and likewise R_b.

*Proof.* A and B are exact by Proposition 20.14 (2) at the non-integer weights a + 2, a + 3 (zf-weights a + 1, a + 2
of −χσS and iχσ²ḃ, zero Taylor polynomial). With a_0 := ℱ⁻¹[−χσS] ∈ H^(∞,a+2)_b(ℝ) and ∂_t = t⁻¹(t∂_t) on t ≥ 1,
a_0″ ∈ t^(−a−4) H^∞_b([1, ∞), |dt/t|). The remainder is

    −h(S) ∫∫_0^1 τ² θ a_0″(t − θτ) dθ φ_x(τ) dτ

plus the h̆-term with τa_0″. On {r ≤ t/8, t ≥ 8}, supp φ_x ⊂ [0, 4 max(r, 1)] ⊂ [0, t/2], so t − θτ ∈ [t/2, t],
t^(a+4) ≤ C(t − θτ)^(a+4) and dt/t ≤ 2 d(t − θτ)/(t − θτ); Minkowski's inequality in (θ, τ) bounds
‖t^(a+4) ·‖_(L²(|dt/t|)) by C max(r, 1)² ‖a_0‖_(H^(2,a+2)_b). The field t∂_t commutes with the translation up to the
factor t/(t − θτ) ∈ [1, 2] and its derivatives, and the x-derivatives fall on φ_x, h and h̆; with |h| ≲ r⁻³
and |h̆| ≲ r⁻² this is t^(−a−4) r⁻¹ in L². ∎

The same applies to the Taylor remainder of the piece (vii) of Theorem 33.24 (of K⁺-order at least α): taking the
Taylor order one higher makes its pointwise order strictly greater than α, hence its L²-order at least α.

**Lemma 35.25** (Lemma 33.20 (a) in L².) In Lemma 33.20 (a), if moreover w + 1 ∉ ℕ, then
χ_+ y ∈ Ḣ^(∞,w+1)_b exactly.

*Proof.* The coefficient is χ_+ ℱ⁻¹(χc) with c of zf-weight w; Proposition 20.14 (2), with zero Taylor polynomial and
β = w + 1 ∉ ℕ, gives the exact weight. A proof by symbol estimates is pointwise and gives only the L²-weight (w + 1)−.
∎

**Proposition 35.26** (Theorem 33.24 at exact weights.) Let α satisfy Definition 35.13 and let the
right sides be as in Proposition 35.20 and Proposition 35.23. Then Theorem 33.24 holds with
Ṡ_rem ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−2)_b, ḃ_rem ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−1)_b, w_ψ := 3 + ε_+ − d_ψ with
Ẏ_ψ ∈ Ḣ^(∞,𝒬(ℰ_♯−d_ψ,3+ε_+−d_ψ))_b, and ũ ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(ℰ_♯,3+ε_+),α)_b.

*Proof.* *Step 0.* f′ has K⁺-weight α: G(W⃗) ∈ 𝒴^0_ex(α); (L − L_b)u_0 has K⁺-weight w_0 − ε + a_K > α for small ε (the
weight α − ε there is a free weakening); the graft by Proposition 35.20; and L_b m_ν is of order > 9/2 > α.

*Step 1.* (ii) by Proposition 35.20. (vi), (viii): the zf-remainders have weight ℓ_zf + j = α − 1 by
Proposition 35.23, and Proposition 21.45 (2) at β_K = α (its Taylor coefficients below α − 1 vanish on both sides)
gives K⁺-order α. (vii): after Lemma 35.24. (ix): σ³û_f has zf-weight ℓ_3 + 3 = α − 1, so K⁺-order α, and
Lemma 35.24 with a = ℓ_3 gives A ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−2), B ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−1) and R_S, R_b of L²-order α.

*Step 2.* u has K⁺-order α − 2 (Proposition 35.23); χ_K C has order ≥ α − 2; the coefficient sections at exponents
with real part < α − 2 vanish as before, none at α − 2 by (Ex3).

*Step 3.* Lemma 33.23 at β := α, as it allows (β ∈ (α − 1, α]): its three meetings of an exponent with the
weight, at α, α − 2 and α − 1, are excluded by (Ex3). It gives w″ of K⁺-order α and a_s, a_b with exponents of real
part > α − 2, resp. > α − 1.

*Step 4.* Ṡ_rem = A + A_5 + a_s ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−2) (A_5 at 2 + ε_+ > α − 2, exactly by Lemma 35.25 as
2 + ε_+ ∉ ℕ); ḃ_rem = B + a_b ∈ Ḣ^(∞,α−1); ũ = w″ + w′ of K⁺-order α.

*The ι⁺-side.* The conormal tower coefficients Y^c_ψ (μ_ψ ∈ (−1, 0]) come from σ³|σ|^(α_τ−2−μ) Y(σ),
Y ∈ H^(∞,0)_b, of zf-weight 2 + ε_+ − μ; Lemma 35.25 gives Ḣ^(∞,3+ε_+−μ) exactly, as 3 + ε_+ − μ ∈ ℕ would need
μ = ε_+ − 1, excluded as at level 3 in the proof of Proposition 35.23. No polyhomogeneous coefficient sits at w_ψ.
Let z be an exponent of a_ψ. If d_ψ lies below the degree of the conormal part of every profile whose coefficient at z
is nonzero, z falls under the clause of Lemma 33.23 on exponents, so z + d_ψ is Λ-valued and ≠ 3 + ε_+ by
(Ex1). Otherwise some such profile has a conormal part of degree d′ ≤ d_ψ. That profile is a conormal profile at the
edge: û_j, j ≤ 2, of degree d′ = μ′_j − 2 ∈ {2 + ε_+, 1 + ε_+, ε_+}, or v_0, of degree d′ = ε_+ − 1; and
z + d′ = 3 + ε_+. As d_ψ ∈ {μ, 0, 1} differs from each of these degrees (μ = ε_+ − 1 being excluded as above), d′ < d_ψ,
so z + d_ψ > 3 + ε_+.

*The corner.* Near ℐ⁺ and on {r ≥ t_*/2}, χ_K = 0 and ũ = u, exact at ι⁺ by Proposition 35.23 (with u_I of
Proposition 35.20). On the transition region {t_*/8 < r < t_*/2}, away from the corner, ũ = u − χ_K u_exp with both
terms exact at ι⁺: u by Proposition 35.23, and u_exp as a sum of coefficients of exact order times homogeneous or
exact-degree profiles, exact at ι⁺ where r ∼ t_*. Near the corner of ι⁺ and K⁺, ũ is the sum over the pieces of Step 1
of the proof of Theorem 33.24 of each piece minus its part in χ_K u_exp. Two kinds of piece reach ι⁺-order
exactly 3 + ε_+. The first is the conormal parts of (v), and of the pieces of type (v) inside (vi) and (viii). These
come from Lemma 33.20 (b) with c = σ^j |σ|^k sgn(σ)^δ (m = 0) and a single profile, whose conormal part lies in
the exact space of its degree (Proposition 35.23). The second is the level-3 towers of (viii). These come from
Lemma 33.20 (a) with w = α_τ + 1 − μ and the profiles of the tower, homogeneous of degree d_ψ − j
(Section 33.9), so w + 1 + d_ψ = α_τ + 2 = 3 + ε_+. For each, the part in χ_K u_exp is the main term
χ_K Σ_j (χ_+ y)^(j) p_j of (33.15), and what is left in ũ is its R. This is literal for the conormal towers.
For the pieces of type (v) the main terms are reorganised by Lemma 33.23 (Step 3), and the coefficient sections
at exponents below α are exactly sums of states (Lemma 33.22 (a)), so again what is left is R and terms of the
kinds below; so the dichotomy below is exhaustive. Lemma 35.27 puts R in ρ_+^(3+ε_+) ρ_K^κ H^∞_b near the
corner, for every κ. Every other term of ũ there is exact at one face with room at the other (Lemma 35.15): it
has K⁺-order ≥ α (Steps 0–4) and either ι⁺-order > 3 + ε_+, or is polyhomogeneous at ι⁺ with exponents in ℰ_♯, none of
real part 3 + ε_+ (Ex1). So ũ has (ℰ_♯, 3 + ε_+) at ι⁺ jointly with α at K⁺. ∎

**Lemma 35.27** (Lemma 33.20 at the corner, in L².) In Lemma 33.20, near the corner of ι⁺
and K⁺, on {r ≥ 2, t_* ≥ 8r} with ρ_+ = 1/r and ρ_K = r/t_*, and in the b-Sobolev spaces of the density
(dt_*/t_*)(dr/r) dω (that of μ_b there):

(a) in case (a), if |(r∂_r)^a ∂_ω^β p_j| ≲ r^(j−d) on {r ≥ 1} for all a, β (degree exactly d − j, without logarithms),
then R ∈ ρ_+^(w+1+d) ρ_K^κ H^∞_b for every κ;

(b) in case (b) with m = 0, if r^(d−j) p_j ∈ H^∞_b near ∂X for the density |(dr/r) dω|, then
R ∈ ρ_+^(Re z+1+d) ρ_K^κ H^∞_b for every κ. Moreover, on {r ≥ 2} the left side of (33.15) is
Σ_j r^(−1−j−z) F_j(t_*/r) p_j(x), with

    F_j(s) := (1/(2π)) ∫ e^(−iζs) χ_0(|ζ|) (−iζ)^j |ζ|^z sgn(ζ)^δ dζ

smooth and bounded with all its s∂_s-derivatives on bounded sets.

*Proof.* Put s := t_*/r ≥ 8. Then (dt_*/t_*)(dr/r) = (ds/s)(dr/r), and the b-vector fields t_*∂_(t_*), r∂_r are s∂_s
and r∂_r|_s − s∂_s. So it suffices to bound r^a s^κ R, a the stated ι⁺-weight, in L²((ds/s)(dr/r) dω), and likewise
after applying s∂_s, r∂_r|_s and ∂_ω. As in the proof of Lemma 33.20, R = Σ_j e_(j,r)(t_*) p_j(x) there, and
σ = ζ/r gives

    e_(j,r)(t_*) = r^(−1−j) (1/(2π)) ∫ e^(−iζs) (−iζ)^j (χc)(ζ/r) (χ_0(|ζ|) − 1) dζ.

The amplitude vanishes for |ζ| ≤ c_0 and for |ζ| ≥ r. Integrating by parts M times gives s^(−M) times the integral of
the M-th ζ-derivative of the amplitude. A derivative falling on (χc)(ζ/r) gives ζ⁻¹((σ∂_σ)(χc))(ζ/r), and one falling
on χ_0(|ζ|) − 1 gives a factor supported in {c_0 ≤ |ζ| ≤ 1}.

(a) Write (σ∂_σ)^l (χc) = |σ|^w c̃_l with c̃_l ∈ H^∞_b(±(0, 1), |dσ/σ|). Then

    |e_(j,r)(t_*)| ≤ C r^(−1−j−w) s^(−M) Σ_l ∫_(|ζ|≥c_0) |ζ|^(w+j−M) |c̃_l(ζ/r)| dζ.

By Minkowski's inequality and the dilation invariance of dr/r,

    ‖∫_(|ζ|≥c_0) |ζ|^(w+j−M) |c̃_l(ζ/r)| dζ‖_(L²(dr/r)) ≤ ‖c̃_l‖_(L²(dσ/σ)) ∫_(|ζ|≥c_0) |ζ|^(w+j−M) dζ < ∞

for M > w + j + 1, uniformly in s. As |r^(d−j) p_j| ≤ C,
‖r^(w+1+d) s^κ R‖_(L²) ≤ C(∫_8^∞ s^(2(κ−M)) ds/s)^(1/2) < ∞ for M > κ. The field s∂_s acting on e^(−iζs) is ζ∂_ζ,
moved onto the amplitude by parts; r∂_r|_s acting on (χc)(ζ/r) gives −((σ∂_σ)(χc))(ζ/r). Both keep the form above,
and (r∂_r)^a ∂_ω^β p_j keeps the bound.

(b) Here (χc)(ζ/r) = r^(−z) |ζ|^z sgn(ζ)^δ χ(ζ/r), and the derivatives of the amplitude are O(|ζ|^(Re z+j−M)) uniformly
in r (a derivative of χ(ζ/r) gives r⁻¹ ≤ |ζ|⁻¹ on its support). So e_(j,r)(t_*) = r^(−1−j−z) E_j(s, r)
with |(s∂_s)^a (r∂_r|_s)^b E_j| ≤ C_(ab) s^(−M) for M > Re z + j + 1, and

    ‖r^(Re z+1+d) s^κ R‖_(L²) ≤ C Σ_j (∫_8^∞ s^(2(κ−M)) ds/s)^(1/2) ‖r^(d−j) p_j‖_(L²((dr/r)dω)),

likewise with b-derivatives. For r ≥ 2, χ = 1 on the support of χ_0(|σ|r), so the left side of (33.15) is
Σ_j (y^(j) ∗ k_r)(t_*) p_j(x), with

    (y^(j) ∗ k_r)(t_*) = r^(−1−j) (1/(2π)) ∫ e^(−iζs) χ_0(|ζ|) (−iζ)^j c(ζ/r) dζ = r^(−1−j−z) F_j(s).

F_j is the inverse Fourier transform of a compactly supported integrable function, as Re z + j > −1, so it is smooth;
and s∂_s F_j is the same transform of −∂_ζ(ζ ·) applied to the amplitude, again integrable. ∎

### 35.9 The theorems at exact weights

**Lemma 35.28** (The step at λ_0 of the construction of Theorem 34.20 at the exact K⁺-weight.) For
each λ_0 ∈ Λ_* fix δ_(λ_0) ∈ (0, δ_1], δ_1 := min(min_ν(κ_ν − ε), Re λ_0 + 3) − α > 0, such that no −μ and no point of
Re π_1ℰ_K lies in (ℓ_K(λ_0), ℓ′_K], ℓ′_K := ℓ_K(λ_0) + δ_(λ_0) < 3. Then the t_*^(−λ_0)-term [h]_(λ_0) of the
construction has K⁺-order exactly α (with room), in place of α−.

*Proof.* The right side f = −F_0(λ_0) − L̄T(λ_0) of the step has room: F_0 is compactly supported in (ι⁺)°
(Lemma 34.17), and the coefficients of L̄T(λ_0) have K⁺-order ≥ min(κ_ν − ε, Re λ_0 + 3) > α, as κ_ν − ε > 9/2
and Re λ_0 + 3 ≥ λ_♯ + 3 > 9/2; so its coefficients lie in H^(∞,ℓ′_K−2)_b at R = 0. Corollary 27.30 (2) and
Remark 27.32, for every solution of the form (27.28) and every ℓ_K < ℓ^max_K, apply at ℓ′_K to the same
v = u_(λ_0) + 𝒮_(λ_0)(f) (to u_(λ_0) by Lemma 34.16), giving v = χ_K v′_0 + ṽ′ with
ṽ′ ∈ Σ_j t_*^(−λ_0) (log t_*)^j H^(∞,ℓ′_K)(ι⁺). By the choice of δ_(λ_0), v′_0 has the same formal solutions as v_0, all
of rate < α, which the rows and towers of Theorem 34.20 remove. So [h]_(λ_0) = ṽ′ plus terms of order
≥ Re λ_0 + 3 > α; and a term t_*^(−λ_0) (log t_*)^j w, w ∈ ρ_K^(ℓ′_K) H_b, lies in ρ_K^(α+δ_(λ_0)−η) H_b for every
η > 0, hence in ρ_K^α H_b, its ι⁺-factor being an index-set term. Here the room is real, so no circle family is needed.
∎

**Proposition 35.29** (Lemma 34.5–Lemma 34.7 with q ∈ 𝒬_ex.) (a) h_rem(q) has K⁺-order
exactly α − 2; (b) L_b h_(b,rem)(q) has K⁺-order exactly α, smoothly in b; (c) at the top level of
Theorem 34.9, R_q u ∈ 𝒴^0_(ex,2)(α) and Δ_q(b′) ∈ 𝒴^♮_(ex,2)(α).

*Proof.* (a) h^(≤1)(S_rem) and ġ(b_rem) are linear in S_rem, b_rem and their t_*-derivatives with stationary tensors,
and ∂_(t_*) = t_*⁻¹(t_*∂_(t_*)) shifts an exact weight by exactly 1; the polyhomogeneous Y_ψ-terms have
rates > 2 + ε_K ≥ α − 2 and Y^c_ψ the rate 3 + ε_+ − d_ψ > α − 2 (room). (b) L_b h^(≤1)(S) = S″(L_2h + L_1h̆¹) + S‴L_2h̆¹
and L_b ġ(b) = b′L_1ġ + b″L_2ġ (the proof of Lemma 34.5), with S″, b′ exact at α; the ι⁺-weights of the
profiles have room (Lemma 35.15) and the towers give rates ≥ λ_♯ + 3 > α. (c) R_q u: the "every β < w + α − 2"
of Lemma 34.6 is used at the top level with w > 2, so β = α is admitted strictly; its ι⁺-weight
β′_+ + 2 + λ_♯ − ε > w_+ has room. Δ_q(b′): its first term is (b), exact at α; its products have factors of K⁺-order
α − 2 (exact) or α, times ∂_b h_(b,rem)(q)b′ of order > 2 strictly (rates of q: α − 2 > 2, α − 1, and > 2 + ε_K), so
each is at K⁺-order > α; at ι⁺ the exponents are in Λ, none at 3 + ε_+ by (Ex1), and the conormal parts at
3 + ε_+ + η_E have room. ∎

**Theorem 35.30** (The forward problem with parameters at exact weights.) Assume Definition 35.13, (H2)
of Section 32.10 read as a_K = α and (H5) of Section 34.1 as a_+ ≤ 3 + ε_+. Let h ∈ 𝒳^∞_(J,ex), p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 with
black hole parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, and q ∈ 𝒬_ex be small, and F ∈ 𝒴^♮_ex(α). Then the p⃗′ of Theorem 34.9 (at a
rotating b, of Proposition 36.8) is unchanged, the forward solution u has K⁺-weight α − 2 and every ι⁺-weight
β_+ < min(3/2, min Re ℰ_+), and u = h_rem(q′) + h′ with q′ ∈ 𝒬_ex and

    h′ ∈ H^(∞,(⟨ℰ^C_I⟩,ℓ_I),(ℰ_♯,3+ε_+),α)_b(Ω_*; S²T*)^(•,−).    (35.7)

The maps F ↦ (p⃗′, q′, h′) are linear and bounded between these fixed-weight spaces, uniformly for small background and
in b.

This is [Hin26, Corollary 11.66, pp. 294–295] with [Hin26, (11.234)], in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* Steps 0–1 of the proof of Theorem 34.9, and its Step 2 at the levels below α, are unchanged: their
inputs lie in the "w−" classes (Remark 35.12) and their outputs feed only open conditions. At the top level,
G̃ = F − Δ_q(p⃗′) − R_q u ∈ 𝒴^♮_ex(α) by Proposition 35.29; G′ adds f^S, f^b, f^s1, linear in h with stationary
coefficients and so exact at a_K = α (Lemma 32.36 (a)), and r^ν at Re e_ν + α − ε > α. Proposition 33.28 at the
level α runs the constructions of Proposition 33.15–Theorem 33.24 at that level, which Proposition 35.20,
Proposition 35.23 and Proposition 35.26 make exact. Step 3 and its uniqueness are unchanged (𝒵_ex ⊂ 𝒵); Step 4′
uses G̃_0 ∈ 𝒴^♮_ex(α), and its comparisons have room (δ′ = ½ min(ε_K, α − 4)); Step 4 is Proposition 35.26. The
coefficients killed by "rate ≤ 2 < α − 2" are killed as before. The tensors are those of Theorem 34.9; only the
weights in which they are estimated change.

At a rotating b the same argument applies to Proposition 36.8. The errors E^ν are exact there, having K⁺-weight
κ_ν − ε > α and ι⁺-exponents in ℰ^♮ + 2, which (Ex1) covers (Lemma 33.27 (a)); A_b does not depend on the loss,
being computed from ι⁺- and tf-data (Remark 36.9); and the errors of the identification of the rotation rows
have K⁺-order Re λ_0 + 1 − ε > α − 2, with room. Step 4′ is not used at b, the condition (36.3) of
Proposition 36.8 replacing it; the uniqueness of Proposition 36.8 together with (36.3) identifies the
exact and the "w−" solutions, as A_b is the same on both classes. Proposition 35.20 and Proposition 35.23 carry the
rotation rows of Proposition 36.5. ∎

**Proposition 35.31** (Theorem 34.20 and (34.15) at exact weights.) For U ∈ 𝒟^∞_ex small,
Φ(U) ∈ 𝒳^∞_(J,ex) × 𝒫 × 𝒬_ex, and P_5(Φ(U)) ∈ ℱ^(k−2)_ex for U ∈ 𝒟^(k+d)_ex; the same holds for D_UΦ and
D_(Φ(U))P_5 ∘ D_UΦ; and the tame bounds of Theorem 34.20 and Proposition 35.9 hold with these norms. The forward
map gains nothing in the weights.

*Proof.* We follow the proof of Theorem 34.20.

*h.* At ℐ⁺ as before. At ι⁺ the exponents lie in ℰ_♯ ⊂ ℰ_+ (Lemma 34.19) and h̃ is at the plain weight
3 + ε_+; no exponent sits at 3 + ε_+ (Ex1). At K⁺, each χ_ι[h]_(λ_0) has order α by Lemma 35.28, and h̃ by
hypothesis.

*q.* Its components are S_rem, b_rem, Y_(ψ,rem), exact, plus polyhomogeneous coefficients with real parts below
3 + ε_+ − d_ψ (Lemma 34.19).

*(34.15) at ℐ⁺:* Corollary 29.14 as before; (29.14) is exact.

*At ι⁺:* the terms of u-exponent below 3 + ε_+ vanish by the identity (34.13); the quadratic part is at
(5 + 2δ_♯)− > w_+; L_(0,p⃗_≤0) h̃ is exact at w_+ by (29.14); the terms of the rows of u-exponent ≥ 3 + ε_+ are
in Λ, so above 3 + ε_+ by (Ex1), with defects at a_+ + Re λ + 2 − ε ≥ 2λ_♯ + 2 − ε > w_+; the conormal parts T_ψ(Y^c_ψ)
of the towers are diagonal terms of Lemma 35.15 (c = 3 + ε_+ − d_ψ, m = d_ψ), exact at ι⁺ with K⁺-weight
c − η > α − 2, and vanish near ℐ⁺; S_rem, b_rem give ι⁺-orders above 3 + ε_+ (Lemma 35.15 with their profiles);
P_4(0, p⃗_≤0) is compactly supported in (ι⁺)°. So the result has the plain weight w_+.

*At K⁺:* L_b h has order α (L_b is stationary and a b-operator there, Section 29.4); the nonlinear part is ≥ 2α;
P_5 − P_4 = L_b h_(b,rem)(q) + ∫(…), the first exact at α (Proposition 35.29 (b)), the integral ≥ 2α − 4 > α; the
rows enter through ϑ_(ν,♯) at κ_ν − ε > α, the rotation rows at Re λ + 4 > α. Products of exact weights are exact
(Lemma 20.6 (2), ρ^a ρ^b = ρ^(a+b)).

*Linearisation and tameness.* Φ = Φ_0(U_0) + A(U_0)U_1 ((34.14)), and the δ_(λ_0) depend only on λ_0, so D_UΦ
is the same construction with the same classes; the proof of Proposition 35.9 is unchanged with fixed weights. ∎

**Theorem 35.32** (The right inverse at exact weights.) There is d such that for U ∈ 𝒟^∞_ex, small in
𝒟^d_ex, whose black hole parameter then lies in ℬ_*, and f ∈ ℱ^∞_ex, there is U′ ∈ 𝒟^∞_ex with (34.16),
linear in f, with ‖U′‖_(𝒟^k_ex) ≤ C_k ‖f‖_(ℱ^(k+d)_ex), C_k independent of U. At a rotating black hole parameter, U′ is
built from the solution map of Proposition 36.8.

This is [Hin26, Theorem 12.8, p. 312] in dimension 4 + 1.

*Proof.* Step 0: Φ(U) is admissible in Theorem 35.30 (Proposition 35.31), and f ∈ ℱ_ex ⊂ 𝒴^0_ex(α)
(Remark 35.12); Theorem 35.30 gives (h′, p⃗′, q′) in the exact classes, with (H5) satisfied as a_+ = 3 + ε_+.
Steps 1–2 of the proof of Theorem 34.24, which hold at b with the rows built at b_0 (Section 34.8 (3)),
subtract values of D_UΦ, which lie in the exact classes and whose images under D_(Φ(U))P_5 lie in ℱ_ex
(Proposition 35.31); Step 2 reads g_j at ℓ_K(λ_0) − ε, a loss it tolerates, as it needs only the formal solutions of
rate < α to be visible below ℓ_K. Step 3: after the subtractions h′ has no ι⁺-term below 3 + ε_+, so its class
(ℰ_♯, 3 + ε_+) with vanishing coefficients is the plain weight 3 + ε_+, and its K⁺-weight is α; so h′ is in the exact
class of h̃, and the conormal parts of q′ have the exact orders. The bounds compose finitely many bounded maps; the
order d is fixed by Lemma 35.5. ∎

The ι⁺-order of Lemma 34.23 is thus exactly 3 + ε_+ under (Ex1); its choice η_2 := ε_+ − 3ε and the resulting
loss 5ε are not needed.

### 35.10 Tame estimates on one pair of scales

**Corollary 35.33** (The tame theorems without loss in the weights.) Let 𝒟^k := 𝒟^k_ex and ℱ^k := ℱ^k_ex.
Then Theorem 35.7 and Theorem 35.8 hold with the input and the output at the same fixed weights
(ε′ = ε = 0 in Section 35.1), and Proposition 35.9 maps 𝒟 to ℱ on these scales: the right inverse and the forward
map act on one pair of Banach scales. This holds at every base point U small in 𝒟^d_ex, whose black hole parameter
then lies in ℬ_*, with constants uniform in U.

*Proof.* The calculus of Section 35.1 and Lemma 35.5 are statements about graded Banach spaces; take the
exact spaces. The elementary families of Lemma 35.3 are tame between fixed-weight spaces: the forward solutions
(Theorem 29.17, exact), the background coefficients (products of exact weights, Lemma 35.6), the
finite-dimensional maps, the integrations (Lemma 21.33 and Lemma 21.42, without loss at weights that are
not exponents), and the model inverses, all stated at fixed weights. The statements of Section 35.5–Section 35.9
are finite compositions of these families at fixed weights with fixed losses: Corollary 35.18 is
Theorem 26.42 on a fixed circle with the Mellin inverse of Lemma 35.19 and the Cauchy integrals of
Lemma 35.16 (constants Cδ^(−k−l_0−1), δ fixed); Proposition 35.20, Proposition 35.23 and
Proposition 35.26 replace weights, not maps, in the entries of Section 35.3; Lemma 35.22,
Lemma 35.24 and Lemma 35.25 are fixed maps; Lemma 35.28, Proposition 35.29 and
Proposition 35.31 are compositions of the maps of Theorem 34.20.

The statements that are not proved anew here run at "w−" weights, with the input losses ε′(ε, k) of the closed graph
theorem (Section 35.1); among them are Proposition 29.35, Proposition 31.6, Proposition 31.21,
Lemma 32.26–Lemma 32.28 below the top level, Steps 1–2 of the proof of Theorem 34.9 below α, the
spaces 𝒵_β, and the weights β_+ < 3/2 of Lemma 33.16. Their losses feed open conditions with room. Every chain
of the inventory starts from exact data (the right side in ℱ_ex and the background in its exact class), which lies in
every lossy class, and ends in a statement of Section 35.5–Section 35.9 at an exact weight. So for each k the
intermediate margins can be chosen backwards from the output. This changes C_k but not the loss of derivatives d, as
these losses are ceilings of continuous functions of the weights and stay bounded as the margins shrink. So the
induction of the proof of Theorem 35.7 runs from exact inputs to exact outputs, with losses independent of k, and
the input loss ε′ is 0 for every k and every statement of the inventory. The exactness of the outputs rests on
Proposition 35.26, with Lemma 35.27. The proof of Theorem 35.8 then gives (35.3) with
ℱ^(k+d)_ex and 𝒟^k_ex, and Proposition 35.31 gives Proposition 35.9 on the same scales. At a base point with black
hole parameter b the results used are stated at b (Theorem 35.7, Theorem 35.8, Theorem 35.30,
Theorem 35.32), with constants uniform in b, and the exact classes do not involve b (Section 35.5). ∎

## 36. Base points near b₀

The statement at b (Definition 30.1), the model objects (P1)–(P5) of Lemma 30.2, the ball ℬ_*
(Lemma 30.3), the rotation state at b (Lemma 30.4) and the results of Chapter 29 at b
(Proposition 30.5) are in Chapter 30; the sixth property (P6) of the model at b, which uses Chapter 32–Chapter 34,
is Lemma 36.1 below.

This chapter proves that the linear theory of Chapter 29–Chapter 35 holds at every base point whose black hole
parameter b lies in a fixed neighbourhood ℬ_* of b₀ = (m₀, 0), with constants and smallness conditions uniform in b
(Theorem 36.10 for Chapter 29–Chapter 34, Corollary 36.11 for Chapter 35). That theory consists of the forward
solutions in the cone and their improvement at ι⁺ and K⁺, the boost parameter, almost boundedness, the extraction and
the elimination of the parameters, the centre-of-mass motions, the corrections of the fourth kind, the expansion at
the Kerr face, the augmentation by its coefficients, the parameterisation by data, the tame estimates and the exact
weights. With it, the right inverses that the Nash–Moser theorem (Theorem 20.1) asks for exist at every base
point near the one of the iteration, with uniform bounds (Corollary 36.12). [Hin26] states its Sections 11.2–12
at base points with |b − b₀| small; Theorem 36.10 and Corollary 36.11 are that statement in dimension 4 + 1,
and the lemmas and propositions that prove them are new in this dimension.

Three ingredients are proved for this. The model objects at b are those of Lemma 30.2 (Chapter 30): the forward
solutions; the ι⁺- and tf-normal operators and the indicial roots, which do not depend on b; the zero energy states,
towers and physical states at b, real and smooth in b and equivariant under the antipodal map; the augmented low-energy
theory; and the Killing time translation. Section 36.1 adds the identity (36.1), which compares the rows
built at b with the corrections built at b₀ (Lemma 36.1), and proves the joint injectivity of the states at b by
perturbation from b₀ (Lemma 36.3); the rotation state at b is a change of the black hole parameter alone
(Lemma 30.4). Section 36.2 treats the rotation terms: the v1 terms of exponent of real part at most 2 are
rotation rows whose coefficients are assigned from the construction that produces them (Proposition 36.5,
Definition 36.6), and with them the decay theorem Theorem 34.9 holds at b (Proposition 36.8).
Section 36.3 states the theorem and its corollary for the tame and exact forms, and records where a step proved
at b₀ uses a property of b₀ that a general b need not have, and what replaces it at b. Three such steps need more
than a substitution: the boost identity, the parameter identities and the expansion at a rotating b. They are proved
at b, with direct bounds in place of continuity in b, in Lemma 31.18 and Proposition 31.19 (Chapter 31),
Lemma 32.11 and Proposition 32.14 (Chapter 32), and Lemma 33.32 and Corollary 33.33
(Chapter 33).

*What changes in dimension 4 + 1.* At b₀ every rotation is Killing. At a rotating b only the rotations commuting with
the spin are, and the rotation state h_(b,v1) is O(|b − b₀|) but not zero (Section 24.12.2). The v1 terms of
exponent of real part at most 2 then decay at K⁺ one order less than at b₀, below the levels' target α − 2. An
elimination through their K⁺-coefficients would invert V ↦ h_(b,v1)(V), a map that degenerates as b → b₀. As in
[Hin26, pp. 279–280] ("for a suitable V^(1,0)′ ≈ V̇"), they are assigned directly: the coefficient of the rotation row
is read from the construction that produced the term, the ι⁺-data of the graft or the tf-data of the spectral pieces.
No K⁺-coefficient is inverted (Proposition 36.5). The rotation rows of Definition 34.3, whose coefficient
space is all of 𝒱_1, are what makes this possible, and they are introduced there for the same reason. The rest
transfers by continuity in b, and the joint injectivity of the states, proved at b₀ by spherical symmetry, transfers by
perturbation (Lemma 36.3).

*Notation.* The notation is that of Chapter 29–Chapter 35. The black hole parameters are b = (m, A), b₀ = (m₀, 0) and
R₁ = m₀^(1/2), and |b − b₀| is the norm of Definition 22.1. ℬ_1 and ℬ_*, with ℬ̄_* ⊂ ℬ_1, are the neighbourhoods of b₀
of Section 29.6; ℬ_* is the ball about b₀ of radius at most 1/(2C_B) of Lemma 30.3 (Lemma 31.1
takes its constant C_B as a supremum over that ball, which is at most the one of Lemma 30.3, so its condition on
the radius holds already and shrinks nothing), shrunk further in Lemma 36.3 and Proposition 36.8 (and in
Proposition 31.19 and Proposition 32.14), each time to a smaller ball about b₀, and every statement below holds
on the final ℬ_*. (P1)–(P5) are the properties of Lemma 30.2, and (P6) is that of Lemma 36.1. As in
Chapter 26, λ ∈ ℂ is an exponent at ι⁺; it is not the wavelength. The letter ε > 0 is small, and "order w−" means
order w − ε for every ε > 0 (Section 34.1). The types 𝒯 = {s1, v1, s0, s2, c0, c1}, the rows ν = (τ, λ, k) with
their K⁺-exponents e_ν and weights κ_ν, the index set 𝒩 = 𝒩_ι ⊔ 𝒩_σ, the coefficient spaces 𝒲_(τ,ℂ), the parameter space
𝒫, the operator P_4 and the classes of sources 𝒴_2(α), 𝒴(α) are those of Section 32.10 and Section 32.11 (with (G)
and the levels of Chapter 33); ℳ, ℰ_(++), λ_♯ and the class 𝒴(α_1) of the levels below 3 are those of Section 32.6;
ℰ_♯, ℰ^♮, 𝒴^♮_2(β), 𝒴^♮(β) and the spaces 𝒵_β are those of Chapter 33 (Definition 33.26); 𝒬, h_(b,rem), P_5, R_q, Δ_q,
𝒩_rot and ℳ_rot are those of Definition 34.1–Definition 34.3. The corrections of the first to fourth kinds are
those of Definition 31.9, Definition 32.5, Definition 32.19 and Definition 32.31, with their counterterms
ϑ_(ν,♯). L̂_b(0), its augmentation L̃_b(0) and the states ġ_b(ḃ), h_b(S) = h_(b,s1)(S), h̆_b(S) and h_(b,v1)(V) are those
of Chapter 30.

*The inner radius.* Every result of the chapter holds with the inner radius r₀ = r_♭ ∈ (0, ½R₁] of Definition 22.1
as a parameter, with constants and neighbourhoods of b₀ that may depend on it. The chapter names no inner radius and
no fixed radius. It works on Ω_* = cl_M{t^♭_* ≥ 1} with the spaces of Chapter 14–Chapter 20, extendible at the inner
boundary, and with the results of Chapter 14–Chapter 35, which hold at every such r_♭; its levels and weights are fixed
by weights at infinity and at K⁺, not by the inner radius. The neighbourhoods ℬ_1 and ℬ_* are those chosen in
Section 29.6 for the given r_♭.

### 36.1 Rows at b and the joint injectivity

**Lemma 36.1** (Rows at b, corrections at b₀.) For b ∈ ℬ̄_*, uniformly in b, the model objects of
Lemma 30.2 have the following sixth property.

(P6) *Rows at b, corrections at b₀.* The rows and towers are built at the base point's b (the towers T_(ψ,b) of
Definition 34.2, smooth in b by Lemma 30.2 (P3)); the corrections of the first to fourth kinds and their
counterterms are the tensors built from b₀-objects, as [Hin26, p. 275, Definition 11.55] builds them; the operator of
[Hin26, Definition 11.56] is at b. At a base point (h, p⃗) with parameter b,

    D_p⃗P_4(h, p⃗)(W_ν = W) = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν(W) + r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) + E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W).    (36.1)

Here f^ν_b := L_(h,p⃗)m_ν + r^ν_(h,p⃗), with r^ν_(h,p⃗) of Lemma 32.36 (e), every object in it (rows,
corrections, counterterms) built at b, and r^ν_(h,p⃗) in the class of (32.35) uniformly in b. And

    E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) := L_(h,p⃗)(h^(b₀)_ν − h^b_ν)(W) + δ*_(g_0,E_C)(ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) − ϑ^b_(ν,♯))(W),

the difference between the corrections and counterterms built at b₀ and at b, lies in 𝒴^♮_2(α−) ∩ 𝒴(α_1), with norm
O(|b − b₀||W|). Its support is in supp χ_K, its K⁺-weight is κ_ν − ε > α, and its ι⁺-exponents below w_+ lie in
ℰ^♮ + 2 (Definition 33.26).

*Proof.* The identity (36.1), with r^ν_(h,p⃗) in the class of (32.35) uniformly in b, is
Lemma 32.36 (e). Its errors near K⁺ are L_(h,p⃗) − L_b, which gains a_K there, as g_0 = g_b near K⁺
(Lemma 29.11); its objects are smooth in b (P3), so the bounds are uniform. For E^ν:

- The differences h^(b₀)_ν − h^b_ν and ϑ^(b₀)_(ν,♯) − ϑ^b_(ν,♯) are b-differences of the 1-form towers and of their
  commutators with χ_K, so O(|b − b₀|) by (P3), and supported in supp χ_K.
- Near K⁺ the corrections vanish (they are supported in 𝒞), but the counterterms do not: there ϑ_(ν,♯) = ½□ω_ν
  (Section 32.11). Their difference has the K⁺-weight κ_ν of the tops of the towers (Lemma 32.32 (a), (d),
  and (P3)). So E^ν has K⁺-weight κ_ν − ε > α.
- At ι⁺, the b-differences of the towers have exponents λ_ν + ℰ_ind (for v1 also λ_ν + 3; Lemma 34.4), with
  λ_ν the row's ι⁺-exponent in ℰ_par ∩ {Re ≤ 3} ⊂ ℰ_♯. L and δ* add 2 and increments, and the parts of L_(h,p⃗) − L_b
  from h and h_tot gain ρ_+^(λ_♯). So below w_+ the exponents lie in ℰ^♮ + 2 (Definition 33.26), with log orders
  bounded by Lemma 33.27 (a), and above it the plain weight is Re λ + 2 + λ_♯ > w_+.
- So E^ν ∈ 𝒴^♮_2(α−), and E^ν ∈ 𝒴(α_1) as ℰ^♮ ∩ {Re < 2} ⊂ ℰ_(++) (Lemma 33.27 (a)). ∎

**Remark 36.2** (Rows at b and corrections at b₀.) [Hin26] makes the same choice: its corrections are
built at b₀, its operator is at b ([Hin26, Definition 11.56]), and the towers of its expansion are those of L_b
([Hin26, Theorem 11.59]). Rows built at b₀ would leave (L_b − L_(b₀))m^(b₀)_ν near K⁺, of K⁺-order only Re e_ν + 2.
Rows at b move the mismatch into the b-differences of the corrections and counterterms, which near K⁺ enter only
through the counterterms, at the weight κ_ν. The corrections of the first and second kinds are commutator terms in
supp dχ_K (Definition 31.9, Definition 32.5), so f^S, f^b and f^(s1) vanish near K⁺, and their b₀/b mismatch lies
at ι⁺ only, with the gain ρ_+² of g_b − g_(b₀). For f^S of Chapter 31 that mismatch is the error E^S_b of
Lemma 31.18, carried by Proposition 31.19; for f^S, f^b and f^(s1) of Chapter 32 it is the error E^mot_b of
Lemma 32.11, carried by Proposition 32.14. The corrections of the third kind are not commutators, and
their counterterms do not vanish near K⁺ (Lemma 32.20); their rows (s1, λ, k) are rows of the set 𝒩 of
Section 32.10 (Definition 32.31), so they enter through (36.1). At b₀, E^ν = 0 and
(36.1) is the identity of Lemma 32.36 (c).

**Lemma 36.3** (Joint injectivity at b.) Shrinking ℬ_*, Lemma 33.5 and Corollary 33.6 hold
at every b ∈ ℬ̄_*, for the states at b: if Σ_(τ≠v1) h_(b,τ)(W_τ) = 0 then every W_τ = 0; and a finite sum of rows
ν ≠ v1 at b with K⁺-weight above the largest of their rates has all its coefficients zero. Moreover, there are a compact
set 𝔎_0 ⊂ X° and c > 0, independent of b, with sup_(𝔎_0)|Σ_(τ≠v1) h_(b,τ)(W_τ)| ≥ c Σ_(τ≠v1) |W_τ|. For the s1 states
alone this is Lemma 31.2.

*Proof.* The space 𝒲 := ⊕_(τ≠v1) 𝒲_(τ,ℂ) is finite-dimensional. At b₀ the map Θ_(b₀): W ↦ Σ_τ h_(b₀,τ)(W_τ) is
injective (Lemma 33.5). Each nonzero element of its range is a nonzero smooth tensor on X°, nonzero on an
open set, so by compactness of the unit sphere of 𝒲 there is a compact 𝔎_0 ⊂ X° on which
sup_(𝔎_0)|Θ_(b₀)W| ≥ 2c|W|. Θ_b depends continuously on b in C⁰(𝔎_0) (P3), so the bound with c holds for b near b₀.
The proof of Corollary 33.6 uses only Lemma 33.5 and Lemma 32.32 (e), the K⁺-weight
Re e_ν + 1 − ε of m_ν(W) − χ_K r_ν h_τ(W), which follows from the tower relations alone and holds at b (P3). ∎

By Lemma 30.4, h_(b,v1)(V) = ġ_b(ḃ_V) with |ḃ_V| = O(|b − b₀||V|). So v1 stays excluded from
Lemma 36.3 at b, as at b₀, and for a quantitative reason: a K⁺-extraction that read a v1 coefficient beside the
b- and S-coefficients would invert a map that degenerates as b → b₀. This is why the v1 coefficients are assigned in
Section 36.2, not read from the K⁺-expansion.

### 36.2 The rotation rows at b

Let 𝒩_rot, ℳ_rot = ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re ≤ 2} and the rotation rows m_ν, ν = (rot, λ, k), be those of Definition 34.1 and
Definition 34.3, built at the base point's b. With the v1 tower T_(v1,b) at b of Section 33.14,

    m_ν(W) = χ_K T_(v1,b)(a_ν W),     a_ν = t_*^(−λ)(log t_*)^k,     W ∈ 𝒱_(1,ℂ),

up to the terms with a_ν^((3)) and a_ν^((4)), of K⁺-order Re λ + 3 − ε > α (Lemma 33.4 (a): the tower of
Definition 34.3 has the length K_v1 = 3 of Section 32.11, and T_(v1,b) is its part j ≤ 2).

**Lemma 36.4** (Rotation rows at b.) At b ∈ ℬ̄_*, m_ν(W) has K⁺-weight Re λ − ε (its bottom
a_ν h_(b,v1)(W), of size O(|b − b₀||W|)), and m_ν(W) − χ_K a_ν h_(b,v1)(W) has K⁺-weight Re λ + 1 − ε.
Lemma 32.32 (a)–(e) and Lemma 32.34–Lemma 32.36 hold for ν at b, with e_ν = λ and
κ_ν = Re λ + 4; in particular

    f^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) := D_p⃗P_4(h, p⃗)(W_ν = W) = f^ν_b(W) + E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W)

as in (36.1), with f^ν_b(W) = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν(W) + r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) ∈ 𝒴_2(α) uniformly in b, and
E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) ∈ 𝒴^♮_2(α−) ∩ 𝒴(α_1) of size O(|b − b₀||W|).

*Proof.* As Definition 34.3 states for b₀: the proofs of Lemma 32.32 (a)–(e) and
Lemma 32.34–Lemma 32.36 use the tower relations and not the coefficient space, and hold at b by (P3) and
(P6). The only change is the bottom, which at b₀ vanishes and at b is a_ν h_(b,v1)(W); it has K⁺-weight Re λ − ε and
is O(|b − b₀||W|) by (P3). The term L_(h,p⃗)m_ν(W) involves only the top of the tower, as T_(v1,b) solves L_b to its
length (the tower relations), so its K⁺-order is unchanged. ∎

**Proposition 36.5** (The v1 terms are rotation rows with assigned coefficients.) Let b ∈ ℬ̄_* be the
black hole parameter of the base point.

(a) *The spacetime phase.* In Proposition 33.8 at b, for each u-exponent λ₀ with Re λ₀ < 2 the graft's tower part
χ_K u^(j)_(b,0) ((26.55) at b) equals

    Σ_(τ∈𝒯∖{v1}) m_((τ,λ₀,j))(W^(j)_τ) + m_((rot,λ₀,j))(V^(j))

up to K⁺-weight Re λ₀ + 1 − ε. Here V^(j) is the graft's v1 coefficient of t_*^(−λ₀)(log t_*)^j, read from the ι⁺-data
u_+ by Theorem 26.39, in the normalisation of the rows of Chapter 33, in which a (log t_*)^j-term keeps the
prefactor of the term j = 0; for j = 0 it is −λ₀⁻¹V^(−1)_1, by a_v1 = −λ₀⁻¹t_*^(−λ₀) ((26.54)). It is linear
and continuous in the forcing f of Proposition 33.8, uniformly in b. (λ₀, j) ∈ ℳ ⊂ ℳ_rot, so the rotation row exists.
So Proposition 33.8 (b) holds at b with the rows 𝒩_ι ⊔ 𝒩_(ι,rot), 𝒩_(ι,rot) the rotation rows (rot, λ₀, j) that arise
here, and these coefficients.

(b) *The spectral phase.* In Proposition 33.15 at b, the v1 term c_v1(σ)T_(v1,b)(σ) of (33.8)
(Lemma 33.12) now has the bottom c_v1(σ)h_(b,v1)(Y), and its rate is α₀ (at b₀, α₀ + 1). At level 1
(2 ≤ Re α₀ < 2 + η_1) this is below α − 2 only for Re α₀ = 2 (by (G), no rate lies in (2, 2 + ε_K]). Those exponents
lie in ℰ_♯ ∩ {Re = 2} ⊂ ℳ_rot, and the term is, by Lemma 33.20 (b), m_((rot,α₀,k))(Y′) up to K⁺-weight
Re α₀ + 1 − ε, with Y′ the coefficient that Lemma 33.12 gives the v1 tower: Y times the constant of c_v1, read
from the tf-data. It is linear and continuous in the right-hand side, uniformly in b by (P2) and (P4). At level 2 the
v1 rate is α₀ + 1 ≥ 2 + η_1 > 2 + ε_K ≥ α − 2, as for the s0 and s2 towers there. So Proposition 33.15 holds at b
with the rows 𝒩_σ ⊔ 𝒩_(σ,rot), 𝒩_(σ,rot) the rotation rows (rot, α₀, k) that arise here, and these coefficients.

(c) *No other v1 term.* Every v1 coefficient of the expansion has its exponents in ℰ_♯ (Theorem 33.24, at b
Corollary 33.33: an ι⁺-exponent λ of u gives the coefficient t_*^(−λ+d_ψ), d_v1 = 0). So it either has real
part at most 2, and is one of (a)–(b), or real part above 2 + ε_K ≥ α − 2, and is carried by q (Definition 34.1,
whose rates at a rotating b are Re z > 2 + ε_K).

*Proof.* (a) At b, Theorem 26.42 gives the v1 term h^(≤2)_(b,v1)(a_v1 V^(−1)_1) of (26.55), with
V^(−1)_1 from u_+, which does not depend on b ((P2): u_+ = N_ι⁺(λ)⁻¹(2f_+), and the decomposition of
Theorem 26.39 is of u_+ on ι⁺). By (26.54), a_v1 = −λ₀⁻¹t_*^(−λ₀), so
χ_K h^(≤2)_(b,v1)(a_v1 V) = m_((rot,λ₀,0))(−λ₀⁻¹V) up to the tower terms of order ≥ 3, of K⁺-weight
Re λ₀ + 3 − ε (Definition 34.3, the rotation rows using h^(≤2) and the tower of Section 32.11). The other rows
are identified as in Proposition 33.8 at b, by Lemma 33.4 (c) at b (P3).

(b) The proof of Lemma 33.12 at b is unchanged except that the v1 tower
T_(v1,b)(σ) = Σ_i (−iσ)^i h̆^i_(b,v1)(Y) has h̆^0_(b,v1) = h_(b,v1) ≠ 0. Its contribution with c_v1 is a piece of type
(b) of Lemma 33.20, a tower with polyhomogeneous coefficient. Its rate is that of ℱ⁻¹(χc_v1), which at
level 1 is α₀ (the piece is σu_((α₀,k)), and c_v1 contributes |σ|^(α₀−1) to it). The level-2 count is that of
Proposition 33.15, with the rate lowered by 1.

(c) As stated. ∎

**Definition 36.6** (The assigned rotation coordinates.) Let (h, p⃗) be a base point with parameter
b ∈ ℬ̄_*, β ∈ (3, 4 + ε_K] admissible, and G ∈ 𝒴^♮(β) such that the forward solution u of L_(h,p⃗)u = G satisfies the
hypothesis of Lemma 33.29 with some w_0. The *assigned rotation coordinates* A_(b,ν)(G) ∈ 𝒱_(1,ℂ), ν ∈ 𝒩_rot,
are the coefficients of the rotation rows that Proposition 36.5 (a)–(b) produces in u: the graft's v1 coefficients
at the exponents of ℳ (spacetime phase), and the spectral level-1 coefficients at the exponents of real part 2. They do
not depend on β or on ε, and neither does E^ν ((P6)). A_b commutes with complex conjugation: A_(b,ν̄)(Ḡ) is the complex
conjugate of A_(b,ν)(G), as L_(h,p⃗) is real and the objects of Proposition 36.5 are real ((P3)). So for real G the
tuple (A_(b,ν)(G))_ν is conjugation-symmetric, as (36.3) and Definition 34.3 need. A_b := (A_(b,ν))_ν is
linear in G and has the bound of Lemma 33.29: for every w ∈ (0, w_0],

    |A_b(G)| ≤ C‖G‖_(𝒴^♮(β)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u‖_(w),

with the seminorms of Lemma 33.29 and C depending on w and uniform in b and in (h, p⃗) small. Indeed
Proposition 36.5 reads A_b(G) from the forcing f′ := G − (L_(h,p⃗) − L_b)u = L_b u of the proof of
Lemma 33.29, by maps linear and bounded uniformly in b ((P2), (P4)); and the count of Step 0 of the proof of
Lemma 33.16, as in Lemma 33.29, gives ‖f′‖_(𝒴^♮(β)) ≤ ‖G‖_(𝒴^♮(β)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u‖_(w). This is
not a bound by G alone: the last term does not vanish at (0, p⃗_b), p⃗_b the parameter whose only nonzero component is
b − b₀, when b ≠ b₀ (Lemma 33.16). No continuity in b is claimed or needed (Step 3 of the proof of
Proposition 36.8). A_(b₀) is defined at b₀ by the same formulas.

**Lemma 36.7** (Lemma 33.29 and Lemma 33.30 at b.) Let β ∈ (3, 4 + ε_K] be admissible,
(h, p⃗) a base point with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_* and h ∈ 𝒳^∞ small, G ∈ 𝒴^♮(β), and let the forward solution u of
L_(h,p⃗)u = G satisfy the hypothesis of Lemma 33.29. Then

    u = Σ_(ν∈𝒩_β) m_ν(S_ν) + Σ_(ν∈𝒩^(<β)_rot) m_ν(A_(b,ν)(G)) + ũ,
        𝒩^(<β)_rot := {ν ∈ 𝒩_rot : Re λ_ν < β − 2},    (36.2)

with ũ in the class of (33.24) and S_ν = S^(h,p⃗,β)_ν(G) determined by
u − Σ_(𝒩^(<β)_rot) m_ν(A_(b,ν)(G)), conjugation-symmetric and linear in G, with the bound of Lemma 33.29: for
every w ∈ (0, w_0], w_0 that of the hypothesis,

    |S^(h,p⃗,β)_ν(G)| + |A_b(G)| ≤ C‖G‖_(𝒴^♮(β)) + C(‖h‖ + |p⃗|)‖u‖_(w),

with the seminorms of Lemma 33.29 and C depending on w and uniform for (h, p⃗) small and b ∈ ℬ̄_*. This is not a
bound by G alone (Definition 36.6). At a fixed b: if (h_j, p⃗_j) → (0, p⃗_b), with p⃗_b the parameter whose only
nonzero component is b − b₀, and G_j → G in 𝒴^♮(β), with the hypothesis of Lemma 33.30, then
S^(h_j,p⃗_j,β)_ν(G_j) → S^(0,p⃗_b,β)_ν(G). At b₀ the second sum in (36.2) is absent (the rotation rows' rates
there are Re λ + 1 > α − 2 ≥ β − 2), and (36.2) is (33.24). For β < 3 no rotation row has rate
below β − 2 (Re λ − ε > 1, Lemma 36.4), and Lemma 32.27 holds at b as at b₀.

*Proof.* By Lemma 33.29, which is stated at b, u = Σ_(ν∈𝒩_β) m_ν(S_ν) + u^rot_β + ũ with ũ in the class of
(33.24), and the S_ν are determined by u − u^rot_β. There u^rot_β is the sum of the terms of u^rot_ι
(Proposition 33.8) with Re λ₀ < β − 2 and of the spectral v1 terms v^rot_β (Proposition 33.28), and
Proposition 36.5 (a) and (b) identify these two kinds of terms; the identifications do not involve the level, and
β − 2 ≤ α − 2. So the terms of u^rot_β are the rotation rows with the coefficients A_(b,ν)(G) of Definition 36.6,

    u^rot_β = Σ_(ν∈𝒩^(<β)_rot) m_ν(A_(b,ν)(G))     up to K⁺-weight Re λ + 1 − ε > β − 2,

which goes into ũ. Indeed, for (λ, k) ∈ ℳ_rot, λ lies in Λ (π_1ℳ_rot ⊂ π_1ℰ_♯ ⊂ Λ), so λ + 1 ∈ Λ has real part at least
λ_♯ + 1 > 2 (Lemma 33.2 (a)), hence above 2 + ε_K by (G), while β − 2 ≤ 2 + ε_K. As u^rot_β − Σ_(𝒩^(<β)_rot)
m_ν(A_(b,ν)(G)) has K⁺-weight above β − 2, the S_ν, read by Corollary 33.6 at b (Lemma 36.3) from the rows
of rate below β − 2, are also determined by u − Σ_(𝒩^(<β)_rot) m_ν(A_(b,ν)(G)). They are the S_ν of Lemma 33.29,
whose conjugation symmetry, linearity and bound they have; A_b has the same bound (Definition 36.6). The continuity
at fixed b is Lemma 33.30. Continuity across b is not claimed: the proofs perturb from a reference operator, and
L_b − L_(b₀) gains only 2 at K⁺. ∎

**Proposition 36.8** (Theorem 34.9 at b.) Let h ∈ 𝒳^∞, p⃗ ∈ 𝒫 with parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, and
q ∈ 𝒬 be small, and F ∈ 𝒴^♮(α−). For p⃗′ ∈ 𝒫, with motion components (S′, b′, S^(0)′_1) and row components W′_ν, let
u(p⃗′) be the forward solution of (34.5), and (as in Step 2 of the proof of Theorem 34.9, with
(36.1))

    G′(p⃗′) := G̃ − f^S_(h,p⃗)(S′) − f^b_(h,p⃗)(b′) − f^(s1)_(h,p⃗)(S^(0)′_1)
              − Σ_(ν∈𝒩⊔𝒩_rot) (r^ν_(h,p⃗) + E^ν_(h,p⃗))(W′_ν),          G̃ := F − Δ_q(p⃗′) − R_q u(p⃗′).

There is a unique p⃗′ ∈ 𝒫 with

    W′_ν = A_(b,ν)(G′(p⃗′))     (ν ∈ 𝒩_rot)    (36.3)

such that u(p⃗′) satisfies the conclusions of Theorem 34.9: (34.5)–(34.6), and
u = h_(b,rem)(q′) + h′ with q′ ∈ 𝒬. p⃗′, q′ and h′ are linear in F, with bounds uniform for (h, p⃗, q) small, b
included. At b₀, (36.3) is the condition C^rot = 0 of Step 4′ of the proof of Theorem 34.9, and p⃗′
is that of Theorem 34.9.

*Proof.* *Steps 0–1* are those of the proof of Theorem 34.9 at b, by (P1)–(P6). E^ν ∈ 𝒴(α_1), by (P6), joins
the terms of Step 1. The rotation rows, of K⁺-weight Re λ − ε > 1 > α_1 − 2 (Lemma 36.4), lie above the base
level.

*Step 2 at b.* Let u := u(p⃗′) ∈ 𝒵_(β_k). As in Step 2 of the proof of Theorem 34.9, by (36.1),
u_0 := u + Σ_(𝒩⊔𝒩_rot) m_ν(W′_ν) solves L_(h,p⃗)u_0 = G′(p⃗′) ∈ 𝒴^♮(β_(k+1)) (resp. 𝒴^♮(α−) for k + 1 = K).
Lemma 36.7 gives, for β_(k+1) > 3 (below 3, Lemma 32.27, as in Step 2 of the proof of
Theorem 34.9),

    u = Σ_(ν∈𝒩_(β_(k+1))⊔𝒩^(<β_(k+1))_rot) m_ν(C^(k+1)_ν(p⃗′)) + ũ,     ũ ∈ 𝒵_(β_(k+1)),    (36.4)

with C^(k+1)_ν := S^(h,p⃗,β_(k+1))_ν(G′(p⃗′)) − W′_ν for ν ∈ 𝒩_(β_(k+1)), and C^(k+1)_ν := A_(b,ν)(G′(p⃗′)) − W′_ν for
ν ∈ 𝒩^(<β_(k+1))_rot. The m_ν(W′_ν) of the other rows, of K⁺-weight above β_(k+1) − 2, are part of ũ. The *new rows*
of the level are those of 𝒩_(β_(k+1)) of rate in [β_k − 2, β_(k+1) − 2), as at b₀, and the rotation rows of
𝒩^(<β_(k+1))_rot ∖ 𝒩^(<β_k)_rot. If the conditions of the lower levels hold, then the coefficients of the old rows
vanish. For a rotation row, C^(k+1)_ν is the same function of p⃗′ at every level, A_b not depending on β. For the other
rows, Σ_(𝒩_(β_k)) m_ν(C^(k+1)_ν) ∈ 𝒵_(β_k), so they vanish by Lemma 36.3. Hence u ∈ 𝒵_(β_(k+1)) if
C^(k+1)_ν(p⃗′) = 0 for the new rows. The converse is not claimed for the rotation rows (Remark 36.9).

*Step 3 at b.* Let 𝒫_k be the set of p⃗′ ∈ 𝒫_0 with C^j_ν(p⃗′) = 0 for the new rows of every level j ≤ k; by Step 2,
u(p⃗′) ∈ 𝒵_(β_k) on 𝒫_k. As in Step 3 of the proof of Theorem 34.9, 𝒫_k is, by induction, the graph of an
affine map from the coordinates of the rows of rate ≥ β_k − 2 to the others. The rotation rows enter by their rates
Re λ at b. On 𝒫_k, C^(k+1) restricted to the new coordinates is −id + A_k, with A_k → 0 as (h, p⃗, q) → (0, 0, 0),
the parameter of p⃗ tending to b₀. The bound on A_k is direct, with no continuity in b. By Step 2,
C^(k+1)_ν(p⃗′) = S^(h,p⃗,β_(k+1))_ν(G′(p⃗′)) − W′_ν, resp. A_(b,ν)(G′(p⃗′)) − W′_ν, and G′ is affine in p⃗′. Its
dependence on the coordinates W′_ν of the rows of 𝒩 ⊔ 𝒩_rot is through:

- (r^ν_(h,p⃗) + E^ν_(h,p⃗))(W′_ν). At the base point (0, p⃗_b), Lemma 32.36 (e) gives
  f^ν_b = L_(0,p⃗_b)m_ν + r^ν_(0,p⃗_b) with r^ν_(0,p⃗_b) = O(|b − b₀||W|). So r^ν_(h,p⃗) + E^ν_(h,p⃗) has norm
  O(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|) in 𝒴^♮_2(α−) (the bounds of Lemma 32.36 (e), and (P6)).
- Δ_q(p⃗′) and R_q u(p⃗′), of norm O(‖q‖) (Lemma 34.6, Lemma 34.7).

The motion coordinates (S′, b′, S^(0)′_1) enter through f^S, f^b, f^(s1) in full: these are linear in their
finite-dimensional arguments, with values in 𝒴⁰(α) (Section 33.2) and so in the class of every level, as in
Step 2, and norms O(|S′|), O(|b′|), O(|S^(0)′_1|) (Lemma 32.10 (c), Lemma 32.36 (a)).
They lie at the base level, below every new row, and along 𝒫_k they change only by O(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + ‖q‖ + |b − b₀|)
times the change of the row coordinates; this is (36.5) below.

*The induction bound.* Write ‖·‖_(𝒴,k) for the seminorm of 𝒴^♮(β_k) of Lemma 33.29 (of 𝒴(β_k) of
Section 32.6 when β_k < 3, and of 𝒴^♮(α − ε) when k = K, as in Lemma 34.8), and ‖F‖ for a seminorm of F
in 𝒴^♮(α − ε), of large enough regularity (Section 32.6). The induction carries a bound: on 𝒫_k the coordinates
and u(p⃗′) are affine in F and in the free coordinates W⃗_free, and |p⃗′| and the seminorms of u(p⃗′) in 𝒵_(β_k) that
are used below are at most C(‖F‖ + |W⃗_free|), C uniform in b and in (h, p⃗, q) small. At k = 0 this is
Proposition 32.29 (i) at b (Step 1); the step from k to k + 1 is shown below.

*The motion coordinates.* Put h″ := h + h_(b,rem)(q), and write D_(W⃗)P_5(W⃗) for D_(p⃗)P_5(h, p⃗, q) in the direction
with p⃗′_<-component 0 and row components W⃗ = (W_ν)_(ν∈𝒩′⊔𝒩_rot) (the split below), as in Step 1. For Ψ ∈ 𝒴(α_1) let
p⃗′_(α_1)(Ψ) ∈ 𝒫_(α_1) be the parameter that Proposition 32.29, for P_5 at (h, p⃗, q) (Step 1), assigns to the forcing
Ψ: the unique one for which the forward solution u_Ψ of L_(h″,p⃗)u_Ψ = Ψ − D_(p⃗)P_5(h, p⃗, q)(p⃗′_(α_1)(Ψ)) lies in
𝒵_(α_1). By (i) of that proposition, Ψ ↦ p⃗′_(α_1)(Ψ) is linear and |p⃗′_(α_1)(Ψ)| ≤ C‖Ψ‖^+_(𝒴(α_1)), with
‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α_1)) the seminorm of that (i) and C uniform in b and in (h, p⃗, q) small. A point of 𝒫 is p⃗′_< ⊕ W⃗, with
p⃗′_< ∈ 𝒫_(α_1) (the motion coordinates and the motions of ℳ_(α_1)) and W⃗ = (W_ν)_(ν∈𝒩′⊔𝒩_rot) the other row
coordinates (Step 1). By (34.5) and the linearity of D_(p⃗)P_5(h, p⃗, q) in the direction, u(p⃗′_< ⊕ W⃗) is
the forward solution of

    L_(h″,p⃗)u = (F − D_(W⃗)P_5(W⃗)) − D_(p⃗)P_5(h, p⃗, q)(p⃗′_<),

so the point of 𝒫_0 over W⃗ (Step 1) has the p⃗′_<-component

    p⃗′_<(W⃗) = p⃗′_(α_1)(F − D_(W⃗)P_5(W⃗)) = p⃗′_(α_1)(F) − p⃗′_(α_1)(D_(W⃗)P_5(W⃗)).

We show that, with C uniform in b and in (h, p⃗, q) small,

    |p⃗′_(α_1)(D_(W⃗)P_5(W⃗))| ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + ‖q‖ + |b − b₀|)|W⃗|.    (36.5)

(1) *The decomposition.* By Definition 34.2, D_(p⃗)P_5(h, p⃗, q) = D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗) + Δ_q and
L_(h,p⃗) = L_(h″,p⃗) − R_q; by (36.1) (for the rotation rows, Lemma 36.4),
D_(p⃗)P_4(h, p⃗)(W_ν = W) = L_(h,p⃗)m_ν(W) + r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) + E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W). Summing over the rows ν ∈ 𝒩′ ⊔ 𝒩_rot, with
m_rows(W⃗) := Σ_ν m_ν(W_ν),

    D_(W⃗)P_5(W⃗) = L_(h″,p⃗)m_rows(W⃗) + e_rows(W⃗),
    e_rows(W⃗) := Σ_ν (r^ν_(h,p⃗) + E^ν_(h,p⃗))(W_ν) − R_q m_rows(W⃗) + Δ_q(W⃗).

As W⃗ is conjugation-symmetric, m_rows(W⃗) is real (Definition 32.31: m_(ν̄)(W̄) is the complex conjugate of
m_ν(W)), and D_(W⃗)P_5(W⃗) is real; so e_rows(W⃗) is real.

(2) *The remainder is small.* The class 𝒴(α_1) contains the class 𝒴_2(α_1) of Section 32.6, which holds every
conormal section supported in supp χ_K ⊂ supp χ^♯_K ((29.2)) of K⁺-weight above α_1 and plain ι⁺-weight
above 4 (below the weight 4 − ε its ι⁺-index set ℰ_++ + 2 is then not used); the seminorm ‖·‖^+_(𝒴(α_1)) of such a
section is at most a seminorm of it in those weights at the same regularity, and the bounds below hold in that
seminorm, d and the order of the seminorm of q being large (Section 32.6, Section 34.1). The four kinds of
terms of e_rows(W⃗):

- r^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) is supported in supp χ_K and lies in the class (32.35), of plain ι⁺-weight
  Re λ + 2 + λ_♯ − ε > 4 and K⁺-weight Re e_ν + a_K − ε > α_1, with norm at most C|W|(‖h‖ + |p⃗|), uniformly on ℬ̄_*
  (Lemma 32.36 (e); for the rotation rows, Lemma 36.4).
- E^ν_(h,p⃗)(W) lies in 𝒴(α_1), with norm at most C|b − b₀||W| ((P6); for the rotation rows, Lemma 36.4).
- m_rows(W⃗) has K⁺-weight λ_♯ − 1 − ε, ι⁺-weight λ_♯ − ε > 3/2 (above every β′_+ < 3/2), vanishes near ℐ⁺ and for
  t^♭_* < 10, and has seminorms O(|W⃗|) (Lemma 32.32, Lemma 36.4). So Lemma 34.6 at b (*The
  augmentation at b* in the proof of Theorem 36.10), with w := λ_♯ − 1, applies: R_q m_rows(W⃗) is supported
  in supp χ_K, has K⁺-weight (λ_♯ + α − 3)− > α_1 (as λ_♯ > 1 and α_1 < α − 2) and plain ι⁺-weight above w_+ > 4
  (the proof of that lemma), with seminorms at most C‖q‖|W⃗|.
- Δ_q(W⃗) = Σ_ν R_q(h_ν(W_ν)) is supported in supp χ_K, has K⁺-order ∞ and plain ι⁺-weight above w_+, with norm
  O(‖q‖|W⃗|) (Lemma 34.7 (a), at b as in the same paragraph).

So, as |p⃗| ≤ |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |p⃗_b| = |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + |b − b₀|,

    ‖e_rows(W⃗)‖^+_(𝒴(α_1)) ≤ C(‖h‖ + |p⃗ − p⃗_b| + ‖q‖ + |b − b₀|)|W⃗|,     C uniform in b.

(3) *The rows carry no parameter.* m_rows(W⃗) vanishes for t^♭_* < 10 (Lemma 32.32 (c)), so it is the forward
solution of L_(h″,p⃗)u = L_(h″,p⃗)m_rows(W⃗) (Step 0). It lies in 𝒵_(α_1). Every row of 𝒩′ has K⁺-rate above
α_1 − 2: the s0, s2, c0 and c1 rows have rates at least λ_♯ > 1 > α_1 − 2, and an s1 row of 𝒩′ has rate at least
α_1 − 2 and, by admissibility, not equal to it (the paragraph *The map* of the proof of Theorem 33.18, with α_1
in place of α′). So its m_ν(W_ν) has K⁺-weight α_1 − 2 − ε for every ε > 0 (Lemma 32.32 (e)). A rotation row
has K⁺-weight Re λ − ε > 1 > α_1 − 2 (Lemma 36.4). Every m_ν(W) has ι⁺-weight λ_♯ − ε > 3/2 and vanishes
near ℐ⁺ (Lemma 32.32 (b), (c)), which are the other conditions of (32.26) at α_1. Moreover
L_(h″,p⃗)m_rows(W⃗) = D_(W⃗)P_5(W⃗) − e_rows(W⃗) lies in 𝒴(α_1), by Step 1 and (2). So the parameter 0 has, for the
forcing L_(h″,p⃗)m_rows(W⃗), the property that defines p⃗′_(α_1), and by the uniqueness in Proposition 32.29,
p⃗′_(α_1)(L_(h″,p⃗)m_rows(W⃗)) = 0. This is the argument of the paragraph *The level map* of the proof of
Proposition 32.29, and of the paragraph *At (0, 0)* of the proof of Theorem 33.18.

(4) *The bound.* By (1), (3) and the linearity of p⃗′_(α_1), p⃗′_(α_1)(D_(W⃗)P_5(W⃗)) = p⃗′_(α_1)(e_rows(W⃗)), and
