s_out = −10), and let β_+ ∈ (½, 3/2), β_I ∈ (β_+, 3/2), with the weights α_+ = β_+ − 5/2 and α_I = β_I − 2 of the proof
of Theorem 29.17. Then Theorem 29.24, in the form of Remark 19.31 with margin 1, holds with d = 20,175 at
every b ∈ B̄_1, and Corollary 29.25 holds with d = 20,180 at every b ∈ B̄_*. In particular, at every base point with
black hole parameter b ∈ ℬ̄_*, the forward solution operators of Lemma 35.3 (a) satisfy (29.19), in the
form of Lemma 35.3 (a), with d = 20,180.

*Proof.* By its proof, the d of Theorem 29.24 at b is the d that the proof of Theorem 19.14 fixes when it is run
with P_0 := 2L_b, the order 𝗌 of (B4) (input (iii) of the proof of Theorem 29.24) and the results it cites applied
relative to 2L_b (inputs (i), (iv) and (v)); in the form of Remark 19.31 with d̄_ℵ = 1 it is

    d = D_0 + D_1 + d′ + d″ + 1,

with D_0, D_1, d′, d″ of (19.46)–(19.47) for these orders. Theorem 49.9 bounds the four numbers
at b₀. Its proof uses P_0 = 2L_(b₀) at three places, and at each the statement at b ∈ B̄_1 is the statement at b₀.

(1) *The orders.* Lemma 49.10 checks the thresholds of the construction of Section 15.13.2 for 2L_(b₀). At b the
order is not built again: by (B4), the order built for 2L_(b₀) is admissible for 2L_b with the same weights and margin.
So inf 𝗌 = −10, sup 𝗌 = 11, 𝗌_0 = 𝗌 − 3, s_u = −12 and N = N′ = 13 at every b, and d′ = 10, d″ = 11, which are functions
of 𝗌 alone ((49.9)). Lemma 49.11 and Lemma 49.23 use 𝗌 also through its constant values 11 near the
horizon, the trapped set, ∂R_(∂K⁺,in) and ∂R_(ℐ⁺,in,+), and −10 near ∂R_(∂K⁺,out) and ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out). The four sets over ∂K⁺
and ℐ⁺ are given in the fibre coordinates of Section 15.13.2 and Definition 15.15 over the boundary faces, the same for
every b, and 𝗌 is the same function. By (3) and (4) of Definition 15.29 for 2L_b, which (B4) gives, 𝗌 is constant over a
set {r ≤ r_Γ} that contains the horizon and the trapped set Γ_b of 2L_b; the constant is s_in = 11, as 𝗌 = s_in on Ω_♮
(Lemma 19.19), which meets that set in its points with r < min(r_Γ, r_0 + 4). So the constant orders (s, s_0) at
which the radial and trapping estimates are used, (12, 8) at the horizon, ∂R_(ℐ⁺,in,+) and ∂R_(∂K⁺,in), (11, 8) at the
trapped set and (−10, −13) at ∂R_(∂K⁺,out) and ∂R_(ℐ⁺,out), are those at b₀.

(2) *The cited results.* D_1 and D_0 are maxima of the losses d and of the coefficient indices d_0 of Theorem 17.26,
Proposition 17.14, Proposition 17.17, Proposition 17.19 and Lemma 19.24 at the orders of (1), and of
Proposition 17.14 (i) at s′ = s_u. At b these results are applied relative to 2L_b, at the same orders. The losses d are
the closed forms (49.10) that their proofs fix in terms of the orders and of N (Lemma 49.11), and P_0
enters none of them; so D_1 = 49 at b. For D_0: Proposition 49.21 and Lemma 49.22 concern the calculus of
Chapter 14 alone, symbols and Sobolev spaces of variable order on ρℬ, and involve no operator. In Lemma 49.23, the
proof of Theorem 19.14 at b applies the same sites in the same pattern: the radial estimates (R) at the radial sets
of 2L_b, the estimate (Γ) at Γ_b, which is normally hyperbolic with the data of (B1) and strongly trapping admissible
(Proposition 29.19), and its other sites, from (G) to (F), at the orders of (1), with N′ = 13 and the operator order
m = 2. So their parameters, and the symbol orders, Sobolev orders, numbers N and numbers of quantizations computed from
them, are those at b₀, and the box conditions hold at every site. The increments of Lemma 49.24 count the
coefficient derivatives that the constructions inside the sites consume: the symbols of the radial and trapping
estimates, the stable and unstable manifolds of Proposition 15.55, the extension h̃_F of Lemma 17.11, the flow box
of Lemma 14.47 and the tame bounds with d_0 ≥ d_1 + 2. Each is fixed by the proof of its site, for every P
admissible relative to a smooth stationary P_0, and does not depend on P_0. The results that use 2L_b only as a smooth
operator, Theorem 29.23 (with Section 19.1 run with 2L_(b₀) inside it) and Theorem 29.21, are not sites, as
at b₀. So D_0 ≤ 𝔐(100) + 4 = 20,104 at b.

(3) *The two raisings.* The margin d̄_ℵ = 1 of Remark 19.31 is that with which 2L_b is 2-admissible
(Theorem 29.21), as at b₀. So the d of Theorem 29.24 is at most 20,104 + 49 + 10 + 11 + 1 = 20,175 at
every b ∈ B̄_1, and every larger d serves. The proof of Corollary 29.25 is that of Theorem 29.17 with
P_0 := 2L_b, and it raises this d by 5 as at b₀: (iii) of that proof takes h ∈ 𝒳^(k+d+5) by Corollary 29.16, the 5
being the two b-derivatives of the metric in the coefficients of P − P_0 and the three of Sobolev embedding in
dimension five. In the tame form, read with the reference metric g_b, the difference g_(b₀,b,−S) − g_b has every
seminorm O(|b − b₀| + |S|) (Lemma 29.11), so ‖P − 2L_b‖_((0;k+d)) ≤ C_k(|b − b₀| + |S| + ‖h‖_(𝒳^(k+d+5))),
and the constant term contributes C_k(|b − b₀| + |S|)‖f‖_(H^d) ≤ C_k‖f‖_(H^(k+d)), as C_k|S|‖f‖_(H^d) does at b₀.
So Corollary 29.25 holds with d = 20,175 + 5 = 20,180 at every b ∈ B̄_*, its proof using b only through b ∈ B̄_1
and (B5), which is a condition on B̄_*. The last statement follows, as Lemma 35.3 (a) takes the forward
solution operators at a base point with parameter b from Corollary 29.25, and ℬ̄_* ⊂ B̄_*. ∎

**Remark 49.26** (Sharpness.) Only the term D_0 is crude. The counts of Proposition 49.21 at T = 100
are at most 15,852 (item (f) with six quantizations), so the same proof gives D_0 ≤ 15,858 and d ≤ 15,934; the value
𝔐(100) = 20,100 keeps a margin. Counting each application of the calculus at its own orders (symbol orders at most 71,
Sobolev orders in [−51, 38], at most five quantizations, by Lemma 49.23) would lower D_0 further. The terms d′, d″
and D_1 are the exact values that the proofs of Section 19.6.1, Theorem 17.26 and Proposition 17.19 fix for
these orders.

### 49.5 Two long iterations and the loss of a round

Among the iterations of the inventory of Section 35.3, three constructions of Chapter 32–Chapter 34 repeat one
step many times.

- *The levels.* Step 2 of the proof of Theorem 34.9 climbs through admissible levels
  α_1 = β_0 < β_1 < ⋯ < β_K = α with β_(k+1) − β_k < α − 4, where α ∈ (4, 4 + ε_K] and α_1 ∈ (2, α − 2). Level k + 1
  takes R_qu as part of its forcing, R_q of second order and u the solution at level k ((34.7)). No level
  equals 3: below 3 the levels are those of Section 32.6, above 3 those of Definition 33.25.
- *The transition face rounds below 3.* At a level β < 3 the step is Lemma 32.27 with β in place of α. Its proof
  runs, while τ_i ≤ β − ε′, rounds that apply Proposition 27.58 and put f̂^((i+1)) := f̂^((i)) − σL̂_b(σ)v_i, with
  τ_0 = 2 + ε_g − 2ε and τ_(i+1) = τ_i + ε_g − ε, ε_g = min(ε_Υ, ε_ind) (Definition 32.1).
- *The level-3 rounds above 3.* At a level β ∈ (3, 4) Step 4 of the proof of Proposition 33.28 runs, while the
  tf-weight κ of the level-3 forcing is at most β − 2, rounds that apply Proposition 27.58 with α_κ := κ, each
  leaving a remainder of tf-weight κ + ε_g − ε as the next forcing, from κ_3 = 1 + η_2 − 2ε.

In each round of the last two kinds, the solution v_i of Proposition 27.58 is built from the inverse N_tf(L_b, ±1)⁻¹
of Corollary 25.12, and the next forcing is obtained from it by the second-order operator L̂_b(σ).

**Lemma 49.27** (The loss of one round.) In the accounting of Definition 49.5:

(a) a transition face round below 3, or a level-3 round above 3, is charged at least 2 + ℓ_tf, with ℓ_tf the lower
bound of Lemma 49.7 (d) for the loss of Corollary 25.12 at the weights of the round;

(b) a round of the iteration at ι⁺ of Proposition 31.21, which applies Corollary 26.44 to the terms of the
forcing at one exponent ϰ_0 and removes the error by Proposition 29.29, is charged at least 4 + d_ι(ϰ_0). If
3 < ℓ_I < 3.5 and λ_♯ ≤ Re ϰ_0 < 2 − δ_ι, this is at least 15.

*Proof.* (a) The round maps its forcing to v_i by a construction that composes N_tf(L_b, ±1)⁻¹, of loss at least
ℓ_tf, with maps of non-negative loss, and v_i to the next forcing by L̂_b(σ), of loss 2 (Remark 49.8); the
next round takes that forcing as its input. By the composition rule the round is charged at least 2 + ℓ_tf.
(b) Lemma 35.3 (g) charges Corollary 26.44 the loss d_ι + 2 of Theorem 26.27 (2) composed with L_b,
and Proposition 29.29 a loss that includes one application of L̃, of loss max(2, d_BG) ≥ 2
(Remark 49.8); the next forcing is formed from their outputs. So a round is charged at least
4 + d_ι(ϰ_0). For 3 < ℓ_I < 3.5 and λ_♯ ≤ Re ϰ_0 < 2 − δ_ι, 1 < ℓ_I − Re ϰ_0 < 2, so d_ι(ϰ_0) = 11 by
Lemma 49.7 (e). ∎

**Lemma 49.28** (Sums over the levels.) Let g ≥ 0 be non-decreasing on ℝ with g(y) − g(x) ≤ y − x for
x ≤ y, let c > 0, and let x_1 < x_2 < ⋯ < x_m with x_(j+1) − x_j < c for every j. Then

    c Σ_(j=1)^(m) g(x_j) ≥ ∫_(x_1)^(x_m) g − (c/2)(x_m − x_1).    (49.21)

*Proof.* Put h_j := x_(j+1) − x_j < c. On [x_j, x_(j+1)], g(x) ≤ g(x_j) + (x − x_j), so
∫_(x_j)^(x_(j+1)) g ≤ h_j g(x_j) + h_j²/2 ≤ c g(x_j) + c h_j/2. Summing over j < m, and adding c g(x_m) ≥ 0, gives
(49.21), as Σ_(j<m) h_j = x_m − x_1. ∎

### 49.6 The constant ε_Υ, and a lower bound for d

The transition face rounds and the level-3 rounds of Section 49.5 raise their weights by ε_g − ε, and ε_g =
min(ε_Υ, ε_ind) (Definition 32.1). The constant ε_Υ of Section 23.13 is fixed below half the least distance
between distinct points of the set ℳ of the numbers Re ι + j in [−10, 10], with j ∈ ℤ and ι an indicial root of
(□^Υ_b)^(0) with |Re ι| ≤ 10. At the computational point that distance is set by two roots of high angular order, and
it is much smaller than δ_50. Throughout, z = 4·10⁻⁶ and, for l ≥ 1, d₂(l) and d₁(l) are the numbers d₂ and d₁ of
Proposition 24.66 (i) at u = l + 1, so that ι^Υ_(sl,l+1) = l + 1 + d₂(l) and ι^Υ_(sl,l+2) = l + 2 + d₁(l); 𝔡₀ =
ι^Υ_(s0,2) − 2 is as in Section 49.2.

**Lemma 49.29** (The least distance of ℳ.) At the computational point let 𝔡_ℳ be the least distance
between distinct points of ℳ. Then 𝔡_ℳ = d₁(8) − d₂(7) and

    2.9239·10⁻¹⁰ < 𝔡_ℳ < 2.92428·10⁻¹⁰.    (49.22)

Hence every admissible choice of ε_Υ satisfies ε_Υ < 1.46214·10⁻¹⁰, and so ε_g < 1.46214·10⁻¹⁰, at every h; and ε_Υ =
1.4619·10⁻¹⁰ is an admissible choice.

*Proof.* *The points of ℳ.* By Lemma 23.3 the indicial roots of (□^Υ_b)^(0) that are not integers are 2 + 𝔡₀
and −1 − 𝔡₀ (type s0), and l + 1 + d₂(l), −l − d₂(l), l + 2 + d₁(l), −l − 1 − d₁(l) (type sl, l ≥ 1); all the others
are integers, among them 0. As 0 < 𝔡₀, d₂(l), d₁(l) < 1 (Proposition 24.66 (i), (23.9)), those with real
part in [−10, 10] are 2 + 𝔡₀, −1 − 𝔡₀, l + 1 + d₂(l) for l ≤ 8, −l − d₂(l) for l ≤ 9, l + 2 + d₁(l) for l ≤ 7 and −l −
1 − d₁(l) for l ≤ 8. Put

    S₊ := {𝔡₀} ∪ {d₂(l) : 1 ≤ l ≤ 8} ∪ {d₁(l) : 1 ≤ l ≤ 7},     S₋ := {𝔡₀} ∪ {d₂(l) : 1 ≤ l ≤ 9} ∪ {d₁(l) : 1 ≤ l ≤ 8}.

Then ℳ consists of the integers in [−10, 10] and of the numbers n + x and n − y in [−10, 10] with n ∈ ℤ, x ∈ S₊ and y
∈ S₋; and for every integer n ∈ [−9, 10] and every y ∈ S₋ the number n − y lies in ℳ, being one of the roots −1 − 𝔡₀,
−l − d₂(l), −l − 1 − d₁(l) shifted by an integer. By the table below every element of S₋ lies in (9·10⁻⁸, 1.4·10⁻⁶).
So two points of ℳ near different integers are at distance more than ½, and two distinct points near one integer n are
at one of the distances |x − x′| (x, x′ ∈ S₊), |y − y′| (y, y′ ∈ S₋), x + y, x or y. As S₊ ⊂ S₋ and x + y > y, and as
the pair n − y, n − y′ occurs for every y, y′ ∈ S₋ (take n = 0),

    𝔡_ℳ = min(min S₋, min{|y − y′| : y, y′ ∈ S₋, y ≠ y′}).

*The enclosures.* By (24.50), d₂(l) = c z(1 + θ₂) with c = l/(2(l + 1)(2l + 1)) and −z/(4l) − z/(2(2l + 1)²)
≤ θ₂ ≤ 0, and d₁(l) = c z(1 + θ₁) with c = (l + 2)/(2(l + 1)(2l + 3)) and −2z/(2l + 3)² ≤ θ₁ ≤ z/(4(l + 2)); and
1.3333327·10⁻⁶ < 𝔡₀ < 1.3333334·10⁻⁶ (the proof of Proposition 49.3). Rounding the lower bounds down and the upper
bounds up gives the intervals of the following table, listed in increasing order; the last column is the lower bound
of the next row minus the upper bound of this row, rounded down. Every entry of that column is positive, so the
eighteen numbers are distinct and the order is as listed.

| number | c | lower bound (10⁻⁷) | upper bound (10⁻⁷) | gap to the next (10⁻¹⁰) |

with 7z/240 = 1.1666666666…·10⁻⁷; and for d₁(8), −2z/361 ≤ θ₁ ≤ z/40, so 5z/171 · (1 − 2.3·10⁻⁸) ≤ d₁(8) ≤ 5z/171 · (1 +
10⁻⁷), with 5z/171 = 1.1695906432…·10⁻⁷.

The least element of S₋ is d₂(9) > 9.47·10⁻⁸. The least distance between two elements of S₋ is the least entry of the
last column (the elements being ordered as listed), which is that between d₂(7) and d₁(8), more than 2.9239·10⁻¹⁰;
every other entry exceeds 4.84·10⁻¹⁰. So 𝔡_ℳ = d₁(8) − d₂(7) > 2.9239·10⁻¹⁰, and from the table d₁(8) − d₂(7) <
(1.1695907603 − 1.1666664896)·10⁻⁷ < 2.92428·10⁻¹⁰. (The leading coefficients differ by 5/171 − 7/240 = 1/13680, and
z/13680 = 2.92397…·10⁻¹⁰.)

*The constant.* ε_Υ is fixed below ½𝔡_ℳ < 1.46214·10⁻¹⁰, and any positive number below ½𝔡_ℳ may be taken; as ½ ·
2.9239·10⁻¹⁰ > 1.4619·10⁻¹⁰, the value 1.4619·10⁻¹⁰ is admissible. ε_Υ is fixed by the gauge parameters (γ_Υ, e_Υ)
alone, through z, so the bound holds at every h. ∎

**Remark 49.30** (The two gaps.) At the computational point ε_ind(10⁻⁶) = δ_50 > 1.94·10⁻⁸
(Corollary 24.80), so ε_Υ < δ_50/132 (as 132 · 1.46214·10⁻¹⁰ < 1.9301·10⁻⁸), and ε_g = ε_Υ whenever ε_ind
is taken at least ε_Υ, as it may be. In every case ε_g ≤ ε_Υ < 1.46214·10⁻¹⁰. The construction of Chapter 32 and
Chapter 33 advances its transition face and level-3 weights by ε_g − ε and asks ε_K < ε_Υ (Definition 33.3); both
long iterations of Section 49.5 are therefore governed by ε_Υ, the separation of the shifted roots of the gauge
potential operator, and not by ε_ind.

**Proposition 49.31** (The number of rounds.) At the computational point, for every choice of ε_K, ε_+,
η_2, α, the levels and the losses ε, ε′ admissible for Theorem 34.9, Lemma 32.27 and
Proposition 33.28, the transition face rounds at the levels below 3 and the level-3 rounds at the levels in (3, 4)
number together

    R > (1 − 3ε_K − 2δ̂ − δ̄)/(ε_K δ̂) > (1 − 5δ̂ − δ̄)/δ̂² > 4.6775 × 10¹⁹,     δ̂ := 1.46214·10⁻¹⁰.

The same bound holds at every h ∈ 𝖧, with the same (γ_Υ, e_Υ).

*Proof.* The weights satisfy 0 < ε_K < ε_Υ < δ̂ and ε_g ≤ ε_Υ: ε_K < ε_Υ is asked with the gap condition of
Theorem 3.9 (Definition 33.3), ε_g = min(ε_Υ, ε_ind) (Definition 32.1), and ε_Υ < ½𝔡_ℳ <
½ · 2.92428·10⁻¹⁰ = δ̂ (Lemma 49.29). Also η_2 < ε_+ < ε_ind ≤ δ_50 < δ̄ (Proposition 24.66 (iii)). The proof of
Lemma 32.27 takes ε < ½ε_g, so ε < δ̂. The loss ε′ of Lemma 32.27 satisfies ε′ ≤ ε: Steps 4–5 of its
proof give ũ the K⁺-weight α − 2 − ε′, while its conclusion at the output loss ε, at which the tame accounting takes it
(Section 35.1), is the K⁺-weight α − 2 − ε, so a run of the proof that gives it has ε′ ≤ ε. So ε′ < δ̂. Each
round raises the tf-weight by ε_g − ε < δ̂, and the level spacing is below α − 4 ≤ ε_K. The count below uses the
increments only through their upper bound δ̂, so it holds as well if a round raises the weight by less than ε_g − ε,
which a construction may do, a forcing of tf-weight κ having every smaller tf-weight.

*Below 3.* At a level β ∈ (2, 3), τ_0 = 2 + ε_g − 2ε < 2 + δ̂ and τ_i < 2 + (i + 1)δ̂, and the rounds run for every i
with τ_i ≤ β − ε′, the τ_i being increasing; so their number is at least the number of i ≥ 0 with 2 + (i + 1)δ̂ ≤ β −
δ̂, which is at least g_1(β)/δ̂ with g_1(x) := (x − 2 − 2δ̂)_+. The levels in (2, 3) form a sequence b_1 < ⋯ < b_m
with b_1 = α_1 < α − 2 ≤ 2 + ε_K, and b_m > 3 − ε_K, because the next level exceeds 3 and lies within ε_K of b_m. By
Lemma 49.28 with c = ε_K, and as g_1 vanishes below 2 + 2δ̂ > b_1,

    Σ_j g_1(b_j)/δ̂ ≥ (1/(ε_Kδ̂))(∫_(2+2δ̂)^(3−ε_K) (x − 2 − 2δ̂) dx − ε_K/2)
                   = (1/(ε_Kδ̂))((1 − ε_K − 2δ̂)²/2 − ε_K/2).

*Between 3 and 4.* At a level β ∈ (3, 4), κ_i := κ_3 + i(ε_g − ε) < 1 + δ̄ + iδ̂, as κ_3 = 1 + η_2 − 2ε < 1 + δ̄,
and the rounds run for every i with κ_i ≤ β − 2; their number is at least g_2(β)/δ̂ with g_2(x) := (x − 3 − δ̄)_+.
The levels in (3, 4) form a sequence c_1 < ⋯ < c_p with c_1 < 3 + ε_K (the previous level lies below 3 within ε_K)
and c_p > 4 − ε_K (the next level is at least 4, as β_(K−1) > 4, and lies within ε_K). As ε_K < δ̄, g_2 vanishes
below 3 + δ̄ > c_1, and by Lemma 49.28

    Σ_j g_2(c_j)/δ̂ ≥ (1/(ε_Kδ̂))((1 − ε_K − δ̄)²/2 − ε_K/2).

Adding, and using (1 − a)²/2 > ½ − a for a > 0, R > (1 − 3ε_K − 2δ̂ − δ̄)/(ε_Kδ̂); with ε_K < δ̂ this exceeds
(1 − 5δ̂ − δ̄)/δ̂². Here 5δ̂ + δ̄ < 7.32·10⁻¹⁰ + 1.95·10⁻⁸ < 2.1·10⁻⁸ and δ̂² = 2.13785…·10⁻²⁰ < 2.13786·10⁻²⁰, and
4.6775 · 2.13786 = 9.9998… < 10 · (1 − 2.1·10⁻⁸), so the quotient exceeds 4.6775·10¹⁹. Nothing in the proof used h
beyond the bound ε_Υ < δ̂, which holds at every h as ε_Υ is fixed by (γ_Υ, e_Υ) alone (Lemma 49.29), and
ε_ind(h) ≤ δ_50 (Proposition 24.66 (iii)). ∎

**Theorem 49.32** (The loss d and the regularity N_NM.) Let d_acc be the accounted loss of
Definition 49.5, and d_NM the loss with which the proof of Theorem 38.19 applies the Nash–Moser theorem
Theorem 20.1: the largest of the d's of Lemma 38.16, Lemma 38.17 and Proposition 35.9 that their
proofs fix (Proposition 49.110 at the computational point), each at least the loss of its estimate, that of
Lemma 38.17 accounted by Definition 49.5, and the orders at which its proof asks U small. Then
Theorem 35.7 and Theorem 35.8 hold with d = d_acc, Theorem 20.1 is applied at the regularity N_NM =
21d_NM + 6, d_NM ≥ d_acc, and:

(i) d_acc is composed, by the rules of Definition 49.5, of elementary losses and of the numbers of steps of the
iterations of the inventory of Section 35.3, among them the three of Section 49.5, each round of those three and
of the iteration at ι⁺ of Proposition 31.21 being charged at least the loss of Lemma 49.27; the elementary
losses are closed forms in the weights, the small numbers that the proofs choose, the thresholds ϑ_in, ϑ_ℋ, the
regularity orders s_c, the counts n(E, β) of the index sets and the order d_BG of the bounds of the background terms
(Lemma 49.7, Remark 49.8), except the loss of the forward solution operators, which at every
base point (Theorem 49.9 at b₀, Corollary 49.25 at b ∈ ℬ̄_*) is at most 20,180 at the backgrounds h,
h + h^(−1)(S) and h + h_tot(p⃗), and at most 20,183 at the backgrounds h + h_rem(q) + h_tot(p⃗) (Lemma 35.3 (a));

(ii) at the computational point, for every admissible choice of the weights there,

    d_acc ≥ Σ_rounds (2 + ℓ_tf) ≥ 3R > 1.403 × 10²⁰,        N_NM ≥ 21d_acc + 6 > 2.946 × 10²¹,

with R the number of rounds of Proposition 49.31, the sum over those rounds, and ℓ_tf ≥ 1 the lower bound of
Lemma 49.7 (d) for the loss of Corollary 25.12 at the weights of each round;

(iii) when the levels of Theorem 34.9 are more than ½(α − 4) apart, d_acc is bounded from above by
Proposition 49.40, explicitly in the numbers of steps of the long iterations, which Lemma 49.39 counts, in the
losses of their single steps, and in finitely many further losses, each assigned to a finite composition.

The bounds (ii) are lower bounds for the loss that this proof's choices produce, not for the least loss with which the
tame estimates hold; for the index sets as the proofs construct them, (G) asks ε_K < μ_G (Theorem 49.72), and the lower
bound rises to 3R > 1.2497 × 10²⁴ (Corollary 49.45). The bound (iii) is explicit in the numbers of steps, which
Lemma 49.39 bounds through the spacing of the levels, below ε_K, and in the further losses, which contain counts of
the index sets. At the computational point Theorem 49.59 evaluates every number of steps and every such count, and
Lemma 49.108 and Proposition 49.110 the orders at which the proof of Theorem 38.19 asks U small: d_acc
and d_NM are at most an integer below 1.57157 × 10⁵⁰, and N_NM at most one below 3.30029 × 10⁵¹.

*Proof.* Theorem 35.7 and Theorem 35.8 hold with d_acc by Lemma 35.2, which gives the tame estimates
with any loss at least the accounted one; N_NM = 21d_NM + 6 is the regularity of Theorem 20.1 at the loss d_NM
((20.5)). *d_NM ≥ d_acc.* Hypothesis (iii) of Theorem 20.1 asks (20.4), with the loss d_NM, of the
right inverse Zℛ(U) of the proof of Theorem 38.19, where ℛ(U) is that of Lemma 38.17 and the multiplication Z
loses nothing; so d_NM, the largest of the d's of the three results, is at least the loss of ℛ(U), the loss of
(35.3) for it. By
the proof of Lemma 38.17, ℛ(U) is the construction of Theorem 35.8 at the base point Ψ(U), with two more
terms, linear in the finite-dimensional boost and translation components, added to the forcing of Step 2 of the proof of
Theorem 34.9 and entering its Steps 1 and 3 as terms of the same kind; and the construction of Theorem 35.8
applies that of Theorem 35.7 to the right side and assembles U′ from its output by maps of non-negative loss (Step
0 of the proof of Theorem 34.24). The elementary losses do not depend on the base point (Lemma 35.3: only
its constants do). By Definition 49.5, a further summand does not lower the largest of the losses of a sum, and
a further factor of non-negative loss does not lower the loss of a composition; so the loss of ℛ(U) is at least the
numbers assigned to both constructions, and d_NM ≥ d_acc. (i) is Definition 49.5 with Lemma 49.7,
Remark 49.8, Lemma 49.27, Theorem 49.9, Corollary 49.25 and Lemma 35.3 (a), which
charges the forward solution operators 3 more at the backgrounds h + h_rem(q) + h_tot(p⃗).

(ii) Level k + 1 of Theorem 34.9 takes the solution of level k as input through R_qu, and at each level the
rounds of Section 49.5 are composed one after another, each round's output being the next round's forcing, and
the level's solution being assembled from the outputs of all its rounds and from the inverse applied to the last
forcing. So all the rounds of all the levels lie on one chain of compositions, and by Definition 49.5 and
Lemma 49.27 (a), d_acc ≥ Σ_rounds(2 + ℓ_tf). By Lemma 49.7 (d), whose proof uses
Lemma 49.6, ℓ_tf ≥ 1 at every round; so by Proposition 49.31, d_acc ≥ 3R > 3 · 4.6775 × 10¹⁹ = 1.40325 ×
10²⁰ > 1.403 × 10²⁰, and N_NM = 21d_NM + 6 ≥ 21d_acc + 6 > 21 · 1.403 × 10²⁰ = 2.9463 × 10²¹ > 2.946 × 10²¹. Every lower
bound for d_acc in this chapter holds for d_NM and N_NM as well, because d_NM ≥ d_acc and N_NM increases with d_NM.

(iii) is Proposition 49.40. ∎

### 49.7 What the proof's formulas give for δ and λ1

**Proposition 49.33** (The thresholds δ and λ1.) In the proof of Theorem 3.9, let d be the loss
d_NM with which Theorem 38.19 applies Theorem 20.1 (d ≥ d_R ≥ d_acc, d_R the accounted loss of the right
inverse ℛ(U) of Lemma 38.17 (Lemma 49.58); Theorem 49.32, Proposition 49.110), and let the Nash–Moser
threshold be ε_NM = θ_0^(−(8d+2)), with θ_0 as chosen in the proof of Theorem 20.1. Let ε be the data threshold
of Corollary 38.28, chosen, as in the proof of Theorem 38.19, with ε ≤ s̃ and C_(2d)ω̃(ε) < ε_NM, where C_(2d) is
the constant of Lemma 38.16 (d) at the order 2d, and ω̃ := ω_(2d+3) and s̃ := min(s_(2d+3), s_P) are the modulus
and the threshold with which (d) holds there (ω_(2d+3) and s_(2d+3) those of Proposition 38.4 (3) at the order 2d + 3,
and s_P that of Lemma 38.16 (d)), enlarged if necessary so that C_(2d) ≥ 1 and ω̃(t) ≥ t on [0, s̃]; and let
C_R ≥ 1 be the constant of Corollary 39.19. Then δ = ½ε and λ1 satisfy

    λ1 < δ,     ω̃(2δ) ≤ 2^(−(32d+8)),     δ ≤ 2^(−(32d+9)),     log₁₀ δ < −(59/196)(32d + 9).

As d ≥ d_acc, the bound of Theorem 49.32 (ii) gives, at the computational point, log₁₀ δ < −1.351 × 10²¹.

*Proof.* Replacing C_(2d) by max(C_(2d), 1) and ω̃(t) by max(ω̃(t), t) keeps Lemma 38.16 (d) true,
and the modulus still tends to 0 with t, which is all that the proof of Theorem 38.19 uses of it; so these are
choices that proof allows. The proof of Theorem 20.1 chooses θ_0 ≥ 16η_0^(−2) with η_0 ≤ 1, so θ_0 ≥ 16 and
ε_NM ≤ 16^(−(8d+2)) = 2^(−(32d+8)). So ω̃(2δ) = ω̃(ε) < ε_NM/C_(2d) ≤ 2^(−(32d+8)), and as ε ≤ s̃,
ε ≤ ω̃(ε) ≤ 2^(−(32d+8)), that is, δ = ½ε ≤ 2^(−(32d+9)). The proof of Theorem 3.9 (Section 41.3) takes λ1
with C_Rλ1 < ½ε = δ, so λ1 < δ/C_R ≤ δ. Next, 2^10 = 1.024·10³, so 2^196 = 2^190·2^6 = 1.024^19·10^57·64, and by the
binomial expansion, all of whose terms are positive, 1.024^19 > 1 + 19x + 171x² + 969x³ > 1.5678 > 100/64 with
x = 0.024; so 2^196 > 10^59 and log₁₀ 2 > 59/196, and log₁₀ δ ≤ −(32d + 9) log₁₀ 2 < −(59/196)(32d + 9). With
d ≥ d_acc > 1.403·10²⁰, (59/196)(32d + 9) > (59/196) · 32 · 1.403·10²⁰ = 1.35146…·10²¹ > 1.351·10²¹. ∎

The bounds hold whatever the other constants are, once each constant of an upper bound is taken at least 1, which
enlarging it allows. A lower bound for δ or λ1 would need lower bounds for θ_0^(−1), the inverse of ω̃ and 1/C_R,
that is, upper bounds for every constant of the proof that enters them; Remark 49.114 says where those
stop.

### 49.8 An upper bound for the accounted loss

This section bounds d_acc from above, at choices of the levels more than ½(α − 4) apart. The bound is explicit in the
numbers of steps of the long iterations, which it counts from above, and in the losses of their single steps; the
remaining steps of the construction enter through finitely many further losses, each finite and charged once per
level, once per step of the base or once in all. First, a rule for families whose loss differs in the two norms of
(35.1), which shows how the background terms enter.

**Lemma 49.34** (Families with a split loss.) Call a family (T_β), E → G, *tame with split loss* (a; c,
b), a, c, b ∈ ℕ₀, if for every k there is C_k with

    ‖T_β e‖_(G^k) ≤ C_k (‖e‖_(E^(k+a)) + ‖β‖_(k+c) ‖e‖_(E^b)),     β ∈ 𝔹, e ∈ E^∞.    (49.23)

Let δ_𝔹 ≤ 1. (a) Such a family is tame with loss max(a, c, b) in the sense of Definition 35.1. (b) If (T_β) has
split loss (a; c, b), (S_β), G → H, has split loss (a′; c′, b′), and d_0 ≥ b′ + c, then (S_βT_β) has split loss (a +
a′; max(c′, a′ + c), max(b, a + b′)). (c) Let T_1, …, T_m have split losses (a_i; c_i, b_i), and let d_0 ≥ Σ_i a_i +
max_i c_i + max_i b_i. Then T_m ⋯ T_1 is tame with loss

    Σ_i a_i + max_i (max(c_i, b_i) − a_i)_+,

and a sum of families with split losses (a_i; c_i, b_i) has split loss (max a_i; max c_i, max b_i). (d) Let X ∈ ℕ₀,
and let an expression be built by compositions and sums from families T_i with split losses (a_i; c_i, b_i), c_i,
b_i ≤ a_i + X. Let A be the number that the rules of Definition 49.5 assign to the expression when each T_i
is charged a_i, and let d_0 ≥ A + 2X. Then the expression has a split loss (A; c, b) with c, b ≤ A + X, and so is
tame with loss A + X.

*Proof.* (a) The norms are non-decreasing in k, so ‖e‖_(k+a) ≤ ‖e‖_(k+d), ‖β‖_(k+c) ≤ ‖β‖_(k+d) and ‖e‖_b ≤ ‖e‖_d for
d := max(a, c, b). (b) By (49.23) for S and then for T,

    ‖S_βT_βe‖_k ≤ C_k (‖T_βe‖_(k+a′) + ‖β‖_(k+c′) ‖T_βe‖_(b′))
               ≤ C_k (‖e‖_(k+a+a′) + ‖β‖_(k+a′+c) ‖e‖_b + ‖β‖_(k+c′) (‖e‖_(b′+a) + ‖β‖_(b′+c) ‖e‖_b)),

and ‖β‖_(b′+c) ≤ ‖β‖_(d_0) < 1 and ‖e‖_b, ‖e‖_(a+b′) ≤ ‖e‖_(max(b,a+b′)) give the split loss stated. (c) By (b) and
induction, T_m ⋯ T_1 has split loss (Σ_i a_i; max_i(c_i + Σ_(j>i) a_j), max_i(b_i + Σ_(j<i) a_j)), the hypotheses d_0
≥ b′ + c of the steps holding by that on d_0. Each of c_i + Σ_(j>i) a_j and b_i + Σ_(j<i) a_j is at most Σ_j a_j +
(max(c_i, b_i) − a_i)_+, and (a) gives the loss. Sums: as in Lemma 35.2 (a). (d) By induction over the
expression. A family T_i has the property by hypothesis. The number assigned to a part of the expression is at most A,
the rules adding or taking the largest of non-negative numbers. Let the parts E_1, E_2 have split losses (A_1; c_1,
b_1), (A_2; c_2, b_2) with c_j, b_j ≤ A_j + X. Their sum has split loss (max(A_1, A_2); max(c_1, c_2), max(b_1, b_2))
by (c), and max(c_1, c_2), max(b_1, b_2) ≤ max(A_1, A_2) + X. For the composition E_2E_1, b_2 + c_1 ≤ A_1 + A_2 + 2X ≤
A + 2X ≤ d_0, so (b) gives the split loss (A_1 + A_2; max(c_2, A_2 + c_1), max(b_1, A_1 + b_2)), and both maxima are
at most A_1 + A_2 + X. At the top, (a) gives the loss max(A, c, b) ≤ A + X. ∎

The families of Lemma 35.3 fall into this frame. A linear map independent of β bounded E^(k+m) → G^k has split
loss (m; 0, 0) (Lemma 35.2 (d)). The forward solution operators have split loss (d_F; d_F, d_F), d_F the loss d
of Theorem 29.17 and of Corollary 29.25 ((29.19)), at most 20,180 (Theorem 49.9,
Corollary 49.25), at the backgrounds h, h + h^(−1)(S) and h + h_tot(p⃗). At h̃ = h + h_rem(q) + h_tot(p⃗), where
‖h̃‖_(𝒳^m) is bounded through ‖q‖_(𝒬^(m+3)), they have split loss (d_F; d_F + 3, d_F), and so (d_F + 3; d_F + 3,
d_F + 3), the charge of Lemma 49.97 (e). The background terms of Lemma 35.3 (b), and the operator L̃ of
Lemma 35.3 (g) where its coefficients depend on h, have split loss (2; d_BG, d_BG), d_BG the order in the
background of their bound ‖Au‖_k ≤ C_k(‖u‖_(k+2) + ‖β‖_(k+d_BG)‖u‖_(d_BG)); in the sense of Definition 35.1 they are
tame with loss max(2, d_BG), the charge of Remark 49.8. A finite-rank map e ↦ Σ_i (ℓ_βe)_i v^i
with |ℓ_βe| ≤ C‖e‖_(d_ℓ) and fixed sections v^i, as the rows and the coefficient maps of the construction are
(Lemma 35.3 (c)), has split loss (d_ℓ; 0, d_ℓ). So every family other than the background terms has c, b ≤ a, and
the background terms have c, b ≤ 2 + (d_BG − 2)_+. By (d) with X := (d_BG − 2)_+, the excess over 2 need only be paid
once: an expression built by compositions and sums from these families, in which every background term is charged 2 and
every other family its loss, is tame with the number so assigned plus (d_BG − 2)_+, whatever the number of background
terms in it, once d_0 is at least that number plus 2(d_BG − 2)_+, which Lemma 35.3, taking d_0 large, allows. The
fixed operators L_b, L̂_b(σ) and L̃_b at the background 0, which alone enter the rounds and windows of the long
iterations, have split loss (2; 0, 0), so the excess does not enter those iterations either way.

**Lemma 49.35** (The gaps of the index sets at ι⁺.) The index set ℰ^ι_ind of Theorem 26.42
((26.56)) satisfies ε^ι_ind := min Re ℰ^ι_ind ≥ ε_Υ, and the number η_0 of Definition 33.1 satisfies η_0
≥ ε_Υ.

*Proof.* By the proof of Theorem 26.42 (its paragraph on the ι⁺-order of the remainder near K⁺ ∩ ι⁺), ℰ^ι_ind
collects the index sets of the corrections of the states of Chapter 23 and Chapter 25 relative to their leading terms,
the set 2 + ℕ₀, and (2, 1) when ϰ = 1. The first have least real part at least ε_Υ: this is the convention of
Section 23.13 for ℰ_ind, kept in Chapter 25 for the states of L_b, and Section 27.10 and Lemma 27.54
state it for the corrections of the states; the others have real part at least 2. So ε^ι_ind ≥ min(ε_Υ, 2) = ε_Υ. The
increments of Definition 33.1 are π_1(ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind) ∪ {1}, the first being the index sets of the corrections of
the states (Section 33.2), of least real part at least ε_Υ; so η_0 ≥ min(ε_Υ, ε^ι_ind, 1) = ε_Υ. ∎

The loss of the inverse of the transition face model enters every round of the long iterations. Its incoming
threshold is non-negative in every fibre inner product (Lemma 49.6); in one inner product it is 0, and this
fixes the loss up to the regularity order.

**Lemma 49.36** (The incoming threshold is 0.) Let γ_Υ, γ_C > 0, 0 < e_Υ < 1, 0 < e_C < 1 and
v_C > −1, and let the sets γ_Υ{1, 2, 1 − e_Υ} and (1 + v_C)γ_C{1, 2, 1 − e_C} be disjoint, as they are at the
computational point. Then at every point of ∂X the endomorphism A + S of Lemma 49.6 (b) is diagonalisable,
with eigenvalues in

    {0, γ_Υ, 2γ_Υ, (1 − e_Υ)γ_Υ, (1 + v_C)γ_C, 2(1 + v_C)γ_C, (1 − e_C)(1 + v_C)γ_C},

0 among them, and there is a smooth fibre inner product h in which A + S is h-self-adjoint and non-negative at every
point of ∂X. In h, the incoming thresholds ϑ_in of (2L_b)^(σ) and of N_tf((2L_b)^(·), ±1) are 0.

*Proof.* By Lemma 49.6 (b) it suffices to work at a point x with |x| > 0, where ρ = |x|⁻¹. Write ⟨·, ·⟩ for
ḡ⁻¹ and put Z := ḡ⁻¹ζ and c := ρ⁻¹c̄_C = dt̄ − v_C d|x| (Section 25.2). As ḡ = −dt̄² + Σ_i (dx^i)²,
⟨dt̄, dt̄⟩ = −1, ⟨d|x|, d|x|⟩ = 1 and ⟨dt̄, d|x|⟩ = 0; so ζ = dt̄ + d|x| is null, ⟨ζ, dt̄⟩ = −1, ⟨c, ζ⟩ = −(1 + v_C),
⟨c, dt̄⟩ = −1, ι_Zḡ = ζ and ω(Z) = ⟨ω, ζ⟩. Let Ang ⊂ T*_x be the 3-dimensional space of the ω with ⟨ω, dt̄⟩ =
⟨ω, d|x|⟩ = 0; then T*_x = Ang ⊕ span(ζ, dt̄), and ⟨ω, ζ⟩ = ⟨ω, dt̄⟩ = ⟨ω, c⟩ = 0 for ω ∈ Ang.

By (49.3), A + S = U_1V_1 + U_2V_2 = UV with U_1 := −ρ⁻¹Ē^C and U_2 := ζ ⊗_s · from T* to S²T*, V_1 :=
ι_ZḠ and V_2 := ρ⁻¹Ē^ΥḠ from S²T* to T*, U := (U_1 U_2) : T* ⊕ T* → S²T* and V := (V_1; V_2). First, V_1U_2 = 0:
ι_Z(ζ ⊗_s ω) = ½(⟨ζ, ζ⟩ω + ⟨ω, ζ⟩ζ) = ½⟨ω, ζ⟩ζ and tr(ζ ⊗_s ω) = ⟨ζ, ω⟩, so ι_ZḠ(ζ ⊗_s ω) = ½⟨ω, ζ⟩ζ −
½⟨ζ, ω⟩ι_Zḡ = 0. Next, with ḠĒ^Cω = γ_C(2c̄_C ⊗_s ω − e_C ḡ⟨c̄_C, ω⟩) ((21.45), as in the proof of
Lemma 25.2), T^C := V_1U_1 is

    γ_C⁻¹T^Cω = −(⟨c, ζ⟩ω + ⟨ω, ζ⟩c − e_C⟨c, ω⟩ζ) = (1 + v_C)ω − ⟨ω, ζ⟩c + e_C⟨c, ω⟩ζ,

which is (1 + v_C)ω on Ang, (1 − e_C)(1 + v_C)ζ on ζ, and (1 + v_C)dt̄ + c − e_Cζ = 2(1 + v_C)dt̄ − (v_C + e_C)ζ on
dt̄, as c = (1 + v_C)dt̄ − v_Cζ. With Ē^ΥḠh = −γ_Υρ(2ι_Yh − e_Υ dt̄ tr h), Y := ḡ⁻¹dt̄ (as in the proof of
Lemma 25.2), T^Υ := V_2U_2 is

    γ_Υ⁻¹T^Υω = −(⟨ζ, dt̄⟩ω + ⟨ω, dt̄⟩ζ − e_Υ⟨ζ, ω⟩dt̄) = ω − ⟨ω, dt̄⟩ζ + e_Υ⟨ω, ζ⟩dt̄,

which is ω on Ang, 2ζ on ζ, and (1 − e_Υ)dt̄ + ζ on dt̄. Let p_C(ν) := (ν − (1 + v_C)γ_C)(ν − (1 − e_C)(1 + v_C)γ_C)
(ν − 2(1 + v_C)γ_C) and p_Υ(ν) := (ν − γ_Υ)(ν − 2γ_Υ)(ν − (1 − e_Υ)γ_Υ). The factors of p_C(T^C) commute and preserve
Ang and span ζ; the first vanishes on Ang, the second on ζ, and the third maps dt̄ into span ζ. So p_C(T^C) vanishes
on Ang, ζ and dt̄, that is, p_C(T^C) = 0; in the same way p_Υ(T^Υ) = 0.

In the splitting T* ⊕ T*, VU has the blocks V_1U_1 = T^C, V_1U_2 = 0 (first row) and V_2U_1, V_2U_2 = T^Υ (second
row). Lower block-triangular maps form an algebra, and the diagonal blocks of f(VU) are f(T^C) and f(T^Υ) for every
polynomial f. So p_C(VU) has the blocks 0, 0 (first row) and Q_1, Q_2 (second row), and p_Υ(VU) the blocks Q_3, 0
(first row) and Q_4, 0 (second row), for some maps Q_1, …, Q_4; and the product p_Υ(VU)p_C(VU) has the blocks
Q_3·0 + 0·Q_1, Q_3·0 + 0·Q_2 and Q_4·0 + 0·Q_1, Q_4·0 + 0·Q_2, that is, it is 0. As (UV)^(n+1) = U(VU)^nV,
UVf(UV) = Uf(VU)V for every polynomial f, so m(UV) = 0 for m(ν) := ν p_Υ(ν)p_C(ν). The seven roots of m are
distinct, real and non-negative: the six other than 0 are positive, those of each of the two sets of the statement
are distinct as 0 < e_Υ, e_C < 1, and the two sets are disjoint. Let P_μ := Π_(μ′≠μ)(UV − μ′)/(μ − μ′) for each root
μ, the product over the other roots. Then Σ_μ P_μ = Id (the polynomial Σ_μ Π_(μ′≠μ)(ν − μ′)/(μ − μ′) has degree at
most 6 and equals 1 at the seven roots), (UV − μ)P_μ and P_μP_μ′ (μ ≠ μ′) are multiples of m(UV) = 0, and so
P_μ² = P_μ and A + S = UV = Σ_μ μP_μ: A + S is diagonalisable with eigenvalues among the roots of m. By
Lemma 49.6 (b) its kernel is non-zero.

The roots of m do not depend on the point, and A + S depends smoothly on it, so the P_μ, polynomials in A + S, are
smooth. Fix a smooth fibre inner product h_0 and put h(u, v) := Σ_μ h_0(P_μu, P_μv), at ∂X, extended to a smooth fibre
inner product near ∂X (homogeneous of degree 0, and glued to h_0 by a partition of unity, a convex combination of
inner products being one). If h(u, u) = 0, every P_μu vanishes and u = Σ_μ P_μu = 0. As P_μ′P_μ = 0 for μ′ ≠ μ and
P_μ² = P_μ, h(P_μu, v) = h_0(P_μu, P_μv) = h(u, P_μv); so A + S = Σ_μ μP_μ is h-self-adjoint, Re_h(A + S) = A + S,
and h((A + S)u, u) = Σ_μ μ h_0(P_μu, P_μu) ≥ 0. By (49.2), p_in − (S + S^(∗h)) = −2(A + S) at every point
of ∂X, whose largest eigenvalue is −2 times the least eigenvalue of A + S, that is, 0. So ϑ_in = 0. The transition
face model has the same endomorphism (the end of the proof of Lemma 49.6 (b)), so the same holds for it. At
the computational point the two sets are {10⁻², 2·10⁻², 0.99·10⁻²} and 1.5·10⁶{1, 2, 1 − 1/102400}. ∎

**Lemma 49.37** (The loss of the transition face inverse.) Let β_sctf ∈ [1, 3/2) and β_ztf ∈ [−1, 0), and
let s ≥ 1 be the integer regularity order of the spaces of Theorem 13.14 at which the proof of Corollary 25.12
applies Corollary 13.16; the tf-admissibility of Proposition 25.11 does not depend on it (Definition 13.15), so any
such s may be taken, s = 1 among them (Proposition 49.47). In the proof of Corollary 25.12 take, at the incoming
radial sets, the fibre inner product of Lemma 49.36 ((O3) of Definition 11.2 chooses the inner
products separately for each radial set) and the incoming order 𝗋_in := −¼. Then that proof gives (25.14)
with the loss

    ℓ_tf(s) := max(1, s − 1),

and the lower bound ℓ_tf of Lemma 49.7 (d) is ℓ_tf(s) at every ϵ the proof takes. Take ℓ_scf := 3/2 − ε
in every application of Proposition 27.55 and Proposition 27.58 at the levels and in the rounds of the proofs of
Lemma 32.27, Proposition 33.15 and Proposition 33.28; then all of them apply Corollary 25.12 with the
loss ℓ_tf(s).

*Proof.* Theorem 13.14 takes s ∈ ℝ, and Corollary 13.16 (a)–(b) holds at every s (Definition 13.15). The face tf
carries no event horizon, and the orders of Lemma 11.32 that Theorem 13.14 uses concern only the boundary face;
so the condition s_c > ½ + ϑ_ℋ of (O3) of Definition 11.2, which concerns the radial sets ∂ℛ_± over the
horizon, does not enter. The proof of Corollary 25.12 takes α_+ := 0, ϵ < ϵ_0 := ¼(3/2 − β_sctf) ≤ 1/8 (the number
it calls δ), 𝗋_out := β_sctf − 2 − ϵ/2 < −½ and the orders of Lemma 11.32 at σ_* = ±1. By Lemma 49.36
the incoming threshold of N_tf((2L_b)^(·), ±1) is 0 in the inner product chosen, so Lemma 11.32 asks 𝗋_in > −½
and 𝗋_in ≥ 𝗋_out, which 𝗋_in = −¼ satisfies. Its order 𝗋 = 𝗋_out + (𝗋_in − 𝗋_out)Θχ_c takes the values 𝗋_out and 𝗋_in
and no value outside [𝗋_out, 𝗋_in] (extended with values in that interval, as in the proof of Corollary 20.24), so
sup 𝗋 = 𝗋_in and inf 𝗋 = 𝗋_out. So in Lemma 20.23, sup 𝗋 − 𝗋_out = 7/4 − β_sctf + ϵ/2 lies in (¼, 13/16), as
7/4 − β_sctf ∈ (¼, ¾] and ϵ/2 < 1/16; its ceiling is 1, and 𝗋_out − inf 𝗋 = 0. As s ≥ 1, ℓ = max(1, s − 1) and ℓ̃ = 0
for every ϵ ∈ (0, ϵ_0). They do not depend on ϵ, so the last step of the proof, which replaces k by k + ℓ̃ and enlarges
ℓ until it does not depend on ϵ, gives (25.14) with the loss ℓ + ℓ̃ = ℓ_tf(s) for ϵ < ϵ_0, and so for every
ϵ > 0, a larger ϵ giving a weaker statement. Near ztf the proof's spaces have the orders s − 2 + k and s + k, and
s − 2 < ℓ and s ≥ 0, so nothing is lost there. The expression of Lemma 49.7 (d) is ℓ + ℓ̃ at these orders.

Finally, Step 3.4′ of the proof of Lemma 32.27 and Step 2 of the proof of Proposition 33.15 take ℓ_scf :=
3/2 − ε; at the levels 2 and 3 the forcings have scf-weight 5/2 − ε (Lemma 33.11), which allows ℓ_scf := 3/2 − ε
there too. Proposition 27.58 and Theorem 27.46, through which Proposition 27.55 applies the inverse, take
β_sctf = ℓ_scf, and 3/2 − ε ∈ [1, 3/2) as 0 < ε < ½. ∎

**Lemma 49.38** (The losses of single rounds, from above.) In the accounting of
Definition 49.5, let ℓ⁺_tf be the largest of the losses with which the construction applies
Corollary 25.12 in the rounds of (a) and the applications of (b), which are finitely many; at the choices of
Lemma 49.37, ℓ⁺_tf = ℓ_tf(s) = max(1, s − 1), which is 1 at s = 1 (Proposition 49.47). Then:

(a) a transition face round of the proof of Lemma 32.27, and a level-3 round of the proof of
Proposition 33.28 at a level β < 4, map the current forcing to the next one with a loss at most ℓ⁺_tf + 2; a level-3
round of the proof of Proposition 33.15 at a level β > 4 does so with a loss at most ℓ⁺_tf + 4;

(b) one application of Proposition 27.55 at level 1 or 2 of the proof of Proposition 33.15, to the term of the
forcing at one exponent with all its logarithmic powers, maps that term to u and to the remainder (27.52)
with a loss at most ℓ⁺_tf + 2;

(c) one window of Step 2 of the proofs of Proposition 31.21, Lemma 32.26, Lemma 32.27 and
Proposition 33.8 maps the current forcing to the next one with a loss at most d^max_ι + 2 + 2(⌊ℓ_I − 5/2⌋ + 1),
where d^max_ι is the largest value of d_ι(ϰ) of (49.5) on λ_♯ ≤ Re ϰ < 2. If 3 < ℓ_I < 3.5 and
δ_ι < 3.5 − ℓ_I, then d^max_ι ≤ 12, and the loss is at most d^max_ι + 4 ≤ 16.

*Proof.* We read the proofs at a finite b-regularity k and charge each map with its loss. Multiplication by smooth
functions, by powers of σ and by the cut-offs, the coefficients of a partial expansion, the stationary states and the
formal solutions with their coefficients, and holomorphic families evaluated or differentiated in a parameter on a
fixed circle cost nothing. Two facts are used. First, if R ∈ H^(k,b)_b near ztf and the contour shift of
Lemma 27.49 is made, then the Mellin transform of R on the new line is N₀(λ)⁻¹Φ(λ), where Φ involves the
Mellin transform of PR at the order k − 2 and that of N₁R, shifted by 1, at the order k − 1; by (E1) and (E2) of
Section 21.9.1, N₀(λ)⁻¹ gains two orders jointly in λ and on 𝕊³, so R̃ and the residues lie at the order k: each
step of the expansions of Theorem 27.46 and of Step 2 of the proof of Proposition 27.58 costs nothing. Second,
N_tf does not depend on σ and commutes with σ∂_σ, so the loss of Corollary 25.12 holds in the joint b-regularity in
(σ, r̂, ω).

(a) In Step 3.4′ of the proof of Lemma 32.27, Proposition 27.58 is applied with k₀ = 1 > ⌊ℓ_zf⌋ (ℓ_zf < 0),
so Step 1 of its proof is empty: f₁ is the forcing cut off, u₁ = N_tf⁻¹(|σ|^(−α)f₁) costs at most ℓ⁺_tf, the
expansion (27.59) and u₂ cost nothing, and the remainder f₁ − L̂_b(σ)u₂ costs 2 more, L̂_b(σ) being of
second order and fixed. The next forcing f̂^((i+1)) = f̂^((i)) − σL̂_b(σ)v_i is σ times that remainder. So the round
costs at most ℓ⁺_tf + 2. At a level β ∈ (3, 4), Step 4 of the proof of Proposition 33.28 applies Proposition 27.58
with ℓ_zf = ℓ_3 < 0 and the order 0 of the zf-index set, so again ⌊ℓ_zf⌋ < 0, Step 1 is empty, and the round costs at
most ℓ⁺_tf + 2. At β > 4, ℓ_3 ∈ (0, ε_K), and Step 1 runs for j = 0 only: v_0 solves 𝒩v_0 = ρ^(α−2)χ₃f^((0)) by
Mellin inversion on a line free of roots, which costs nothing (𝒩 is elliptic and dilation invariant, (E1)–(E2) of
Section 21.9.1), and the terms e_0, which apply to U_0 the operators L̂_b(σ) − L̄̂(σ), ρ(ρ∂_ρ − 3/2 − S̄) and the
commutators with the cut-offs, cost at most 2; then f₁ costs at most 2, and the round at most ℓ⁺_tf + 4.

(b) In the proof of Proposition 27.55, f₀ is a coefficient of the term (no loss), u_(tf,α) = N_tf⁻¹(ρ_ztf^(−α)f₀)
costs at most ℓ⁺_tf, its expansion (27.42) costs nothing (the first fact), W_α and u_α are built from it and
from the states (no loss), and F_α = χ_tf ρ_tf^α f₀ − L̂_b(σ)u_α costs 2 more. Step 2 takes ∂^k_α at α₀, a Cauchy
integral over a small circle of holomorphic families bounded at each order, which costs nothing. So u costs at most
ℓ⁺_tf and the remainder at most ℓ⁺_tf + 2.

(c) In a window, Corollary 26.44 is applied to the terms of the forcing F at each λ_0 of the window, in parallel.
By Lemma 35.3 (g) its error, which is the terms of F at λ_0 minus L_bu_(λ_0), has the loss d_ι(λ_0) + 2. The
expansion at 𝓘⁺ of that error is removed by Proposition 29.29: its 𝓘⁺-exponents are those of ℰ^tot_(ι⁺,𝓘) + 2 to the
order ℓ_I + 1, with no ρ_I^(z+1)-term for Re z < 5/2 (Step 2 of the proof of Proposition 31.21; here z is an
exponent at 𝓘⁺). As ℰ^tot_(ι⁺,𝓘) = ⋃_(μ∈σ_Υ)(3/2 + μ, 0) has no logarithms, the terms to be removed sit at
z ∈ 5/2 + σ_Υ + ℕ₀ with Re z ≤ ℓ_I, all of logarithmic order 0, and they lie in the ⌊ℓ_I − 5/2⌋ + 1 windows
[5/2 + j, 7/2 + j), 0 ≤ j ≤ ⌊ℓ_I − 5/2⌋, of the proof of Proposition 29.29. That proof treats the terms of one window
in parallel, each by Lemma 21.33 and the fixed inverse (z − 3/2 − Ā)⁻¹, at no cost, and passes to the next
window the remainder f − L_b(χρ_I^z u^((z,0))), which costs 2 and creates only terms of logarithmic order 0 at z + j,
j ≥ 1. So u′_(λ_0) costs at most 2⌊ℓ_I − 5/2⌋ beyond the error. The next forcing is F − Σ_(λ_0) L_b(u_(λ_0) +
u′_(λ_0)), that is, the terms of F outside the window, unchanged, plus the errors minus L_bu′_(λ_0), which costs 2 more.
So a window costs at most d_ι(λ_0) + 2 + 2(⌊ℓ_I − 5/2⌋ + 1). The bound d^max_ι ≤ 12 is Lemma 49.7 (e) on
λ_♯ ≤ Re ϰ < 2 < ℓ_I, and ⌊ℓ_I − 5/2⌋ + 1 = 1 for 3 < ℓ_I < 3.5. ∎

**Lemma 49.39** (The lengths of the long iterations, from above.) Make admissible choices of the weights of
Theorem 34.9 and of the results it uses, and put

    Δτ := ε_g − ε,     Δβ := min_k (β_(k+1) − β_k),

with ε the loss of Lemma 32.27 and Proposition 33.28 (so ε < ½ε_g and Δτ > ½ε_g) and β_0 = α_1 < β_1 < ⋯ <
β_K = α the levels of Step 2 of the proof of Theorem 34.9. Let a♭_K ∈ (α_1, α − 2) be the K⁺-order of the
background h + h_rem(q) with which Step 1 of that proof applies Proposition 32.29, Lemma 32.26 and
Lemma 32.27 (their number a_K at that background, whose K⁺-order is (α − 2)−; it is not the K⁺-order
a_K ≥ 4 + ε_K of h in Step 2). Let α_0 be the admissible level from which the proof of Proposition 32.29 at α_1
starts, taken, as that proof allows, with α_1 − α_0 < a♭_K − 2, so that it has the single level step α_0 → α_1. Then:

(a) at most N_< := (3 − α_1)/Δβ of the levels β_1, …, β_K lie in (2, 3), at most N_> := (α − 3)/Δβ + 1 lie in
(3, α], and, if Δβ > ½(α − 4), at most two lie in (4, α];

(b) at a level β ∈ (2, 3) the transition face rounds number at most (β − 2)/Δτ + 1, and summed over the levels in
(2, 3) at most

    T_< := (1 + Δβ/2)²/(2ΔβΔτ) + N_<;

(c) at a level β ∈ (3, α] the level-3 rounds number at most (β − 3)/Δτ + 2, and at a level β ∈ (4, α] less than
1/Δτ + 2; summed over the levels in (3, α] they number at most

    T_> := (α − 3 + Δβ/2)²/(2ΔβΔτ) + 2N_>;

(d) at a level β ∈ (3, α], the applications of Proposition 27.55 at level 1 act on separate terms of g_1 and none on
the output of another, every exponent of the remainder of an application at level 2 has real part at least ε_Υ above
the exponent it is made at, and at level 2 every exponent treated is reached from an exponent of g_2 through at most
(1 + η_2 − η_1)/ε_Υ remainders of earlier applications;

(e) every window loop (Step 2 of the proofs of Proposition 31.21, Lemma 32.26, Lemma 32.27 and
Proposition 33.8) has at most W := (2 − λ_♯)/ε_Υ + 1 windows;

(f) in the base, the rounds of Proposition 31.21 that Step 0 of the proof of Lemma 32.26 runs number at most
N_b := 1/(a♭_K − 2) + 1, and the steps of Proposition 29.35 that the start of its proof runs at most N_b + 1.

*Proof.* (a) The levels are increasing, at least Δβ apart, and β_1 ≥ α_1 + Δβ. Those in (2, 3) lie in [α_1 + Δβ, 3),
so there are at most (3 − α_1)/Δβ of them; those in (3, α] lie in an interval of length α − 3 closed at the top, so
there are at most (α − 3)/Δβ + 1; those in (4, α] lie in an interval of length α − 4 < 2Δβ.

(b) In Step 3.4′ of the proof of Lemma 32.27 at the level β, τ_0 = 2 + ε_g − 2ε > 2 and τ_(i+1) = τ_i + Δτ, and
the rounds run for the i with τ_i ≤ β − ε′; so i ≤ (β − 2)/Δτ, and there are at most (β − 2)/Δτ + 1 of them. Let
b_1 < ⋯ < b_m be the levels in (2, 3). Then b_j < 3 − (m − j)Δβ, so

    Σ_j (b_j − 2) < Σ_(i=0)^(m−1) (1 − iΔβ) = m − Δβ m(m − 1)/2 ≤ (1 + Δβ/2)²/(2Δβ),

the last as the quadratic −(Δβ/2)(m − 1/Δβ − ½)² + (Δβ/2)(1/Δβ + ½)² in m is at most its maximum. Summing the bound on
the rounds over the m ≤ N_< levels gives T_<.

(c) At a level β ∈ (3, 4), Step 4 of the proof of Proposition 33.28 starts at κ_3 = 1 + η_2 − 2ε > 1, raises κ by
Δτ per round, and runs while κ ≤ β − 2; so there are at most (β − 3)/Δτ + 1 rounds. At a level β ∈ (4, α], Step 4 of
the proof of Proposition 33.15 fixes a number δ₄ > 0 (its δ) and takes α_κ = min(κ, 2 − δ₄); while κ < 2 − δ₄ each
round raises κ by at least Δτ, and the first round with κ ≥ 2 − δ₄ ends the loop; so there are at most
(2 − δ₄ − κ_3)/Δτ + 2 rounds, which is less than 1/Δτ + 2 ≤ (β − 3)/Δτ + 2, as κ_3 > 1. As in (b), for levels
c_1 < ⋯ < c_p in (3, α], Σ_j (c_j − 3) ≤ (α − 3 + Δβ/2)²/(2Δβ), and summing gives T_>.

(d) At level 1 (Step 2 of the proof of Proposition 33.15) the remainders have tf-exponents of real part at least
2 + ε_g > 2 + η_1, outside the window [2, 2 + η_1) of level 1; so no application acts on the output of another. At
level 2 (Step 3) the window is [1 + η_1, 2 + η_2), and the application at (α_0, k) leaves its remainder at the
exponents (α_0, k) + ℰ_ind and (4, k + 1) + ((0, 0) ∪ ℰ_ind) ((27.52)), with min Re ℰ_ind ≥ ε_Υ; the second
lie above the window, and the first have real part at least Re α_0 + ε_Υ. So along a sequence of applications each of
which acts on a remainder of the previous one, the real parts increase by at least ε_Υ inside a window of length
1 + η_2 − η_1, and there are at most (1 + η_2 − η_1)/ε_Υ + 1 applications in it.

(e) In each window loop the least real part m_ι of the ι⁺-exponents to be treated starts at least at λ_♯, each window
raises it by at least ε^ι_ind ≥ ε_Υ (Lemma 49.35; Step 2 of the proof of Proposition 31.21), and the loop
ends once m_ι ≥ α^♯_+, where α^♯_+ < 2 (in Proposition 33.8, once no u-exponent below 2 is left). So there are at
most (2 − λ_♯)/ε_Υ + 1 windows.

(f) Each round of Proposition 31.21 raises α′_K to min(α′_K + a♭_K − 2, α_K), from α′_K > 1 to α_K < 2; so there
are at most (α_K − 1)/(a♭_K − 2) + 1 < N_b rounds. Each step of Proposition 29.35 raises α′_K by
min(a♭_K − 2, α_K − α′_K), from α′_K ≥ ½ to α_K < 1; so there are at most (α_K − ½)/(a♭_K − 2) + 1 < N_b + 1 steps. ∎

To state the bound, set apart the losses of the remaining steps. Let c(β_k) be the loss that Definition 49.5
assigns to the step of Theorem 34.9 that passes from the level β_(k−1) to β_k (Lemma 32.27 or
Lemma 33.29, with the background terms of Step 2 of its proof) when every transition face round, level-3
round, application of Proposition 27.55 at levels 1 and 2 and window of its iterations is charged 0. Let c_b be the
largest loss of one round of Proposition 31.21 in the base with its windows charged 0, and c′_b the largest loss of
one step of Proposition 29.35 there. Let c_0 be the largest loss assigned to the remaining steps of the larger of
the two constructions of Theorem 35.7 and Theorem 35.8: Step 0 of the proof of Theorem 34.9 (the
forward solution); the rest of Step 1 (the base), with the windows of Steps 0 and 2 of the proof of Lemma 32.26
and of the level step α_0 → α_1 of Proposition 32.29 charged 0; Steps 3, 4′ and 4, with all their steps charged
(they apply Theorem 33.18 and Theorem 33.24 at the top level, finitely many times); and for
Theorem 35.8 the map U ↦ Φ(U) and Steps 1–3 of the proof of Theorem 34.24. Each of these numbers is finite,
being assigned by the rules of Definition 49.5 to a composition of finitely many elementary families.

**Proposition 49.40** (An upper bound for the accounted loss.) In the setting of Lemma 49.39, with
Δβ > ½(α − 4),

    d_acc ≤ (ℓ⁺_tf + 2)(T_< + T_> + T_2) + 4(1/Δτ + 2) + r_ι W (N_< + N_> + N_b + 3)
            + Σ_(k=1)^K c(β_k) + N_b c_b + (N_b + 1) c′_b + c_0,    (49.24)

where T_2 := N_>((1 + η_2 − η_1)/ε_Υ + 2) and r_ι := d^max_ι + 2 + 2(⌊ℓ_I − 5/2⌋ + 1). If Δβ ≥ Δβ_0, Δτ ≥ Δτ_0 and
a♭_K − 2 ≥ Δβ_0 for some Δβ_0 ∈ (0, 1] and Δτ_0 > 0, then

    N_< ≤ 1/Δβ_0,     N_> ≤ (1 + ε_K)/Δβ_0 + 1,     N_b ≤ 1/Δβ_0 + 1,
    T_< ≤ (1 + Δβ_0/2)²/(2Δβ_0Δτ_0) + 1/Δβ_0,
    T_> ≤ (1 + ε_K + Δβ_0/2)²/(2Δβ_0Δτ_0) + 2(1 + ε_K)/Δβ_0 + 2.    (49.25)

*Proof.* *The chain.* By Definition 49.5, a composition is charged the sum and a sum or an assembly the
largest of the charges of its parts; so d_acc is the largest total charge along a chain of maps in which each takes
the output of the previous one as input. Splitting the charges into those of the rounds, applications and windows
counted in Lemma 49.39 and all others, d_acc is at most the largest total of the first kind along a chain plus
the largest total of the second kind along a chain. The construction of Theorem 34.9 is the forward solution
(Step 0), the base (Step 1), the level steps in the order of the levels, each taking the solution of the previous
level through R_qu ((34.7)) and the a priori membership of Lemma 32.27 or Lemma 33.29, and
Steps 3, 4′ and 4; the finite-dimensional data p⃗′ enter through finite-rank maps (Lemma 35.2 (c)), which add
no charge beyond those of the maps their functionals are applied to (Lemma 49.34). Theorem 35.8
composes this with U ↦ Φ(U) and with Steps 1–3 of the proof of Theorem 34.24.

*Levels 1 and 2.* In a level step at β ∈ (3, α], let α_1′, …, α_n′ be the exponents at which level 2 applies
Proposition 27.55, in an order of non-decreasing real part, in which the construction may treat them, as every
exponent of the remainder of an application has larger real part than the exponent it is made at (Lemma 49.39
(d)). The application at α_i′ maps the current forcing F to F − B_iF, B_i := L̂_b(σ)A_i, with A_iF the solution that
Proposition 27.55 gives for the term of F at α_i′ with all its logarithmic powers; B_iF is that term minus the
remainder (27.52). So for j ≠ i the term of B_iF at α_j′ is minus that of the remainder, and A_jB_i = 0
unless α_j′ is an exponent of the remainder of the application at α_i′; call (i, j) a link then. Expanding the
products, the forcing passed on is

    (1 − B_n) ⋯ (1 − B_1)F = F + Σ (−1)^r B_(i_r) ⋯ B_(i_1)F,

the sum over the chains i_1 < ⋯ < i_r whose consecutive pairs are links, and the solution
Σ_j A_j(1 − B_(j−1)) ⋯ (1 − B_1)F is the sum of the A_jF and of the terms ±A_jB_(i_r) ⋯ B_(i_1)F over the chains for
which (i_r, j) is a link too. Each term is a composition along a chain, each map taking the output of the previous one
as input, and this is how Definition 49.5 applies to level 2, whose applications take as input only the term
of the forcing at their exponent; the rules charge a sum the largest of its terms, so the applications at level 2 are
charged at most the largest total along a chain of links. The map is the same in either form, so this charge also
gives a loss with which Theorem 35.7 and Theorem 35.8 hold (Lemma 35.2). At level 1 there are no
links (Lemma 49.39 (d)), and every chain has one application.

*The second kind.* Along a chain the charges other than those of the counted iterations are, by the definitions above,
at most Σ_k c(β_k) over the level steps, c_b per round of Proposition 31.21 in the base and c′_b per step of
Proposition 29.35 there, and c_0 for the rest, the background terms being among them with the charge max(2, d_BG) of
Remark 49.8. By Lemma 49.39 (f) this is the second line of (49.24). (Charging the background
terms 2 and adding (d_BG − 2)_+ once instead, as Lemma 49.34 (d) allows, gives a loss with which
Theorem 35.7 and Theorem 35.8 hold, bounded by the same expression with c(β), c_b, c′_b and c_0 lowered by
the excess of their background terms, plus (d_BG − 2)_+; it is not d_acc, which charges every application of a
background term max(2, d_BG).)

*The first kind.* A level step at β ∈ (2, 3) runs one window loop (Steps 1–2 of the proof of Lemma 32.27) and
its transition face rounds, one after another; a level step at β ∈ (3, α] runs one window loop (Step 2 of the proof of
Proposition 33.8, through Lemma 33.29), the applications at level 1, those at level 2 and the level-3
rounds (Steps 2–4 of the proof of Proposition 33.15, through Proposition 33.28). By Lemma 49.39 (d), the
paragraph on levels 1 and 2 and Lemma 49.38 (b), a chain passes through at most one application at level 1
and at most (1 + η_2 − η_1)/ε_Υ + 1 at level 2 in a level step, each charged at most ℓ⁺_tf + 2; this gives
T_2(ℓ⁺_tf + 2) over the levels in (3, α]. By Lemma 49.39 (b), (c) and Lemma 49.38 (a) the rounds
give at most (ℓ⁺_tf + 2)(T_< + T_>), plus 2 for each level-3 round at the at most two levels in (4, α], at most
2 · 2(1/Δτ + 2) in all. The window loops counted are one per level step, one per round of Proposition 31.21 in the
base, and those of Steps 0 and 2 of the proof of Lemma 32.26 and of the level step α_0 → α_1 of
Proposition 32.29 in the base (the choice of α_0 in Lemma 49.39 makes that level step one): at most
N_< + N_> + N_b + 3 of them, each of at most W windows charged at most r_ι (Lemma 49.39 (e),
Lemma 49.38 (c)). This is the first line of (49.24).

*The counts.* N_< ≤ (3 − α_1)/Δβ ≤ 1/Δβ, as α_1 > 2; N_> ≤ (α − 3)/Δβ + 1 ≤ (1 + ε_K)/Δβ + 1, as α ≤ 4 + ε_K; and
N_b ≤ 1/(a♭_K − 2) + 1. For L ≥ 1 the function x ↦ (L + x/2)²/(2x) = L²/(2x) + L/2 + x/8 decreases on (0, 2L], and
Δβ < α − 4 ≤ ε_K < 2; so the bounds of Lemma 49.39 (b), (c) decrease in Δβ and in Δτ, which gives
(49.25). ∎

**Remark 49.41** (The upper bound at the computational point.) At the computational point ε_g ≤ ε_Υ <
1.46214·10⁻¹⁰ (Lemma 49.29, Remark 49.30), and for the index sets as the proofs construct them 𝔡₀ and 𝔡₁
are increments of Λ (Corollary 49.45, Remark 49.46) and (G) holds exactly for ε_K < μ_G, where μ_G <
1.64160217198·10⁻¹⁴ (Theorem 49.72). The levels are then less than μ_G apart, and the first line of (49.24) is
of the order 3/(ε_Kε_g), the order of the lower bound 3R of Proposition 49.31. Proposition 49.57 evaluates it at the
admissible choice of Definition 49.52, with ε_K = 1.6416·10⁻¹⁴ and ε_g = ε_Υ = 1.4619·10⁻¹⁰: it is less than
1.2587·10²⁴, of which less than 4.30775·10²¹ comes from the window loops at ι⁺ (bounded there through ε^ι_ind = 𝔡₁,
Lemma 49.54), and less than 1.0072 times the lower bound 3R > 1.2498·10²⁴ at the same choice (Theorem 49.59).
The losses c(β_k), c_b and c′_b of single steps enter the second line with the multiplicities K < 1.22077·10¹⁴ and N_b,
N_b + 1 < 6.10383·10¹³, and c_0 once; Proposition 49.105 bounds their largest value c_* by 6.4368·10³⁵.

**Remark 49.42** (The inputs of the upper bound.) Four inputs separate Proposition 49.40 from an integer;
at the computational point all four are bounded: (1), (2) and (4) are evaluated, and (3) through one number, c_*, which
Proposition 49.105 bounds. (1) ε_K, N_Λ, k̄_0 and l_*: (G) asks that no element of the set Λ of Definition 33.1 have
real part in (2, 2 + ε_K] or in (3, 3 + ε_K], and that no λ + d_c0 or λ + d_c1, λ ∈ Λ, have real part in (2, 2 + ε_K].
Proposition 49.3 and Remark 49.4 settle the three windows for ε_K < 5.019·10⁻⁸ on the part of Λ built from 2, 3,
λ_♯ and the offsets 𝔡₁, 1 + 𝔡₀, 1 + δ₂, 1 + δ′₁. With ℰ_ind as the proofs construct it, 𝔡₀ and 𝔡₁ are themselves
increments, and (G) holds exactly for ε_K < μ_G, 1.64160217197·10⁻¹⁴ < μ_G < 1.64160217198·10⁻¹⁴ (Theorem 49.72,
Corollary 49.45); Proposition 49.73 and Corollary 49.93 give 1.62066·10¹³ < N_Λ < 1.67472·10¹³, k̄_0 = 3, J_* =
15,000,015 and the admissible l_* = 50, and Proposition 49.57 the numbers of levels, rounds, applications and windows
at an admissible choice. (2) ℓ⁺_tf = 1 at the choices of Lemma 49.37 with s = 1 (Proposition 49.47). (3) The
single-step losses c(β), c_b, c′_b and c_0: each is a finite composition of the elementary losses of
Lemma 49.7 and Remark 49.8 and of the forward loss, at most 20,180 (Theorem 49.9,
Corollary 49.25) and 20,183 at the backgrounds h + h_rem(q) + h_tot(p⃗) (Lemma 49.97 (e)), charged at each
forward solution they apply; they contain the counts n(E, β) of the index sets entering (49.6), which
Lemma 49.56 bounds through N_Λ, k̄_0, l_* and J_*; c_0 contains, besides, the iterations of Steps 4′ and 4 at the
top level, each bounded as in Lemma 49.39, and the loss of
Theorem 34.20, which its proof takes as the sum of the losses of its steps over the exponents of Λ ∩ {Re < 3 + ε_+}
(Lemma 49.50). Their largest value c_* enters Theorem 49.59 with the coefficient 2.44153·10¹⁴;
Proposition 49.105 bounds it by 6.4368·10³⁵. (4) d_BG = 11 serves (Proposition 49.48); it enters c(β), c_b, c′_b and c_0
through the charge max(2, d_BG). For d_NM, and so for N_NM, the losses of Lemma 38.16 and Proposition 35.9 are
at most 62N_Λ + 10 < 1.04·10¹⁵ (Lemma 49.50, Lemma 49.55), that of Lemma 38.17 satisfies
(49.24) in the form of Lemma 49.58, and Lemma 49.108 and Proposition 49.110 bound the orders at
which these results ask U small, and with them d_NM (Theorem 49.59). Given ε_K, the explicit part
of (49.24) is of the order 1/(ε_Kε_g), the order of the lower bound of Proposition 49.31; ℓ⁺_tf multiplies terms
of that order, c(β) enters at most N_< + N_> times, about 2/ε_K, and c_b and c′_b at most about 1/ε_K times each. All
these numbers depend on the point through z, which fixes ε_Υ (Remark 49.30), and through the index sets.

### 49.9 The inputs of the upper bound for the accounted loss

This section takes the inputs that Proposition 49.40 leaves free, evaluates them at the computational point, and
assembles the bound. Two are fixed by general statements of this paper. The loss of the inverse of the transition face
model is 1 at the weights at which the construction may use it, so ℓ_tf = 1 (Proposition 49.47); and the order of the
background terms may be taken to be d_BG = 11 (Proposition 49.48). The others are fixed by the index sets that define the
set Λ of Definition 33.1 and by the orders of the poles of N_ι⁺(L̄, ·)⁻¹: the admissible ε_K of the gap condition
(G), the counts n(E, β) of the index sets entering the Fourier steps of the levels (Lemma 49.49), and the
loss of the map Φ of Theorem 34.20, which governs the other two losses (Lemma 49.50). Memberships
and least real parts of the index sets alone fix no admissible ε_K (Proposition 49.43); and if both offsets of the class
roots are increments of Λ, as they are for the index sets that the proofs construct, every admissible ε_K lies below
1.6417·10⁻¹⁴ (Corollary 49.45). Section 49.10 lists the exponents of the index sets as constructed, and Section 49.11
the poles of N_ι⁺(L̄, ·)⁻¹ at real part at most 5, all simple. With them (G) holds exactly for ε_K < μ_G
(Theorem 49.72), and N_Λ, k̄_0, l_* and J_* are explicit (Proposition 49.73, Corollary 49.93). Section 49.9.6 fixes an
admissible choice of the weights, evaluates every count of (49.24) at it, and proves Theorem 49.59: d_acc
and d_NM are at most an integer D_acc < 1.57157·10⁵⁰, the largest single-step loss being below 6.4368·10³⁵
(Proposition 49.105) and the orders of smallness being bounded in Section 49.12.7, against the lower bound
1.2497·10²⁴; Remark 49.60 states what the bound rests on. Throughout
we work at the computational point of Definition 49.1, so z = 4·10⁻⁶ = 1/250000 and λ_♯ = 15099/10000, and 𝔡₀ = d_c0,
𝔡₁ = d_c1 are the offsets of Section 49.2.

#### 49.9.1 The index sets of the gap condition

The gap condition (G) of Definition 33.3 quantifies over the set Λ and over the offsets 𝔡₀ and 𝔡₁ of the two class
roots (Definition 32.30). By Definition 33.1, Λ is the smallest set, closed under conjugation, that contains the
generators

- π_1ℰ_++, with ℰ_++ the least index set of (32.16): the closure of ℰ^♯_+ ∩ {Re < 2} under the addition of
  ℰ^ι_ind ∪ ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ_+, where ℰ^♯_+ is the set (29.32) of Proposition 29.29 with Ĕ_+ = ∅
  (Section 32.6);
- π_1𝒢, with 𝒢 = (2, 0) ∪ (2 + ℰ_ind) ((32.2));
- π_1ℰ^C_I, the index set at 𝓘⁺ of the class, subject to (2)–(3) of Definition 27.6 (Definition 29.1);
- λ_♯ and 3;
- 2 + π_1ℰ_col, with ℰ_col = ({(0, 0), (1, 0)} ∪ ℰ_ind ∪ (1 + ℰ_ind)) + ℕ₀ (Lemma 33.9), a subset of
  π_1𝒢 + ℕ₀;

and that is closed under the addition of the increments

- π_1ℰ_ind, where ℰ_ind is the union of the index sets of Proposition 23.28 and Proposition 25.26
  (Section 32.1), of Proposition 23.34 (2) (Section 32.6), and of Proposition 23.34 (1), (3), (4)–(7)
  and (2, 0) (Section 32.10), taken at b₀ and serving at every b near b₀ ((P3) of Lemma 30.2);
- π_1ℰ^ι_ind, the index set of Theorem 26.42 ((26.56));
- 1.

Each of these sets enters the statements of this paper through memberships of the form u ∈ 𝒜^E (or a partially
polyhomogeneous space with the index set E) and a lower bound for its real parts, and it is fixed by a construction.
ℰ_ind is built in the proofs of Proposition 23.28 ((F1) there), Lemma 25.25 and Lemma 23.33 by
Lemma 21.35, from the indicial roots of (□^Υ_b)^(0), which Lemma 23.3 and Proposition 24.66 (i) give in
closed form, and from exponents of the right sides that are integers or such roots shifted by integers. ℰ^ι_ind
collects the index sets of the states of Chapter 23 and Chapter 25, 2 + ℕ₀ and (2, 1) (the proof of
Theorem 26.42); the physical states of Chapter 25 are built by Lemma 21.35 from the roots of L_b^(0)
(Proposition 25.6), among them ι^C − 1 for the roots ι^C of the polynomials of Proposition 24.3 (the proof of
Proposition 25.37). The least ℰ^C_I is generated from σ_Υ by (3) of Definition 27.6, and the least ℰ_++ by
(32.16). So the exponents of these sets below the real part 5 are algebraic numbers fixed by this paper;
Section 49.10 lists them. A space with an index set E is contained in the space with any index set E′ ⊃ E, the
coefficients at the added exponents being 0.

**Proposition 49.43** (Memberships fix no admissible ε_K.) Let t > 0 and

    E_t := ℰ_ind ∪ {(3 − λ_♯ + t + j, 0) : j ∈ ℕ₀}.

Then E_t is an index set with min Re E_t ≥ ε_Υ, every membership that Proposition 23.28, Proposition 23.34 and
Proposition 25.26 assert with ℰ_ind holds with E_t in its place, the conditions (32.3), (32.16)
and (H3) on ℰ_+ being met by enlarging ℰ_+, and for the set Λ_t that Definition 33.1 builds from E_t, (G) fails for
every ε_K ≥ t. So no positive number can be shown to be an admissible ε_K from information about ℰ_ind that consists of
such memberships and of the bound min Re ℰ_ind ≥ ε_Υ; the exponents of ℰ_ind themselves are needed. The proposition
concerns enlargements of ℰ_ind: enlarging an admissible index set, like decreasing ε_K, only lowers the admissible ε_K,
so it bounds neither the admissible ε_K of the index sets that the proofs construct nor d from above.

*Proof.* E_t is a union of two index sets, so it has finitely many exponents below each bound, finitely many
logarithms at each, and is closed under (z, k) ↦ (z + 1, k); its new exponents have real part at least
3 − λ_♯ = 1.4901 > ε_Υ. A membership with ℰ_ind implies the same membership with E_t ⊃ ℰ_ind. The conditions
(32.3), (32.16) and (H3) involve ℰ_ind only through lower bounds for ℰ_+ and for ℰ_++ ⊂ ℰ_+, which
an enlargement of ℰ_ind only strengthens (Section 32.6). The proof of Lemma 33.2 (b), which uses of ℰ_ind
only that its exponents have positive real parts, shows that they are conditions on ℰ_+ alone, met by the least index
set that contains ℰ_+, 2 + E_t and ℰ_par + ℱ, with ℰ_par built from Λ_t, and that is closed under the addition of
ℰ^ι_ind ∪ E_t and of itself. In Λ_t, λ_♯ is a generator and 3 − λ_♯ + t ∈ π_1E_t is an increment, so 3 + t ∈ Λ_t. Its
real part lies in (3, 3 + ε_K] as soon as ε_K ≥ t, which (G) excludes. ∎

Enlargements of the same kind, by finitely many exponents of real parts in [ε_Υ, 1), each with its translates by ℕ₀
and with any logarithmic orders, raise the number of points of Λ below 3 + ε_+ and the bounds l_* and k̄_0 of
Definition 33.1 beyond any given bound: each such exponent z gives the point λ_♯ + z < 3 of Λ, and the exponent
2 + z < 2λ_♯ of 𝒢 with its logarithmic order. So memberships and least real parts alone do not bound these numbers
either.

**Lemma 49.44** (Two class offsets near 3.) Let a := 1,109,655 and b := 31,682. Then

    1.6415·10⁻¹⁴ < λ_♯ + a𝔡₀ + b𝔡₁ − 3 < 1.6417·10⁻¹⁴.    (49.26)

*Proof.* *The offsets.* 𝔡₀ = (9/4 + z)^(1/2) − 3/2 (Section 49.2), and 9/4 + z = 562501/250000, so
𝔡₀ = (√562501 − 750)/500. By Lemma 23.3 and its proof, ι^Υ_(s1,2) = ½ + (¼ + s_(1,1))^(1/2), where s_(1,1) is
the smaller root of Q_1(s) = s² − (8 + z)s + 12 + 3z (κ = 3), whose discriminant is 16 + 4z + z² = D/250000² with
D := 1000001000001. So 4(¼ + s_(1,1)) = 17 + 2z − √D/125000 =: I, ι^Υ_(s1,2) = ½ + ½√I, and 𝔡₁ = (√I − 3)/2.

*The square roots.* Squaring the decimal numbers below gives

    750.0006666663703706337445² = 562500.99999999999999999990500…,
    750.0006666663703706337446² = 562501.00000000000000000005500…,
    1000000.500000374999812500² = 1000001000000.99999999999995312…,
    1000000.500000374999812501² = 1000001000001.00000000000195312…,

so √562501 and √D lie strictly between the two numbers squared. With 2z = 0.000008 and
1000000.500000374999812500/125000 = 8.0000040000029999985, the second pair gives

    9.000003999997000001499992 < I < 9.0000039999970000015,

and, as 3.0000006666660925929701631² = 9.00000399999700000149999177…, which is below the lower bound for I, and
3.0000006666660925929701645² = 9.00000399999700000150000017…, which is above the upper one, √I lies strictly between
3.0000006666660925929701631 and 3.0000006666660925929701645.

*The sum.* Hence

    1.333332740741267489·10⁻⁶ < 𝔡₀ < 1.3333327407412674892·10⁻⁶,
    3.3333304629648508155·10⁻⁷ < 𝔡₁ < 3.3333304629648508225·10⁻⁷,

and, multiplying the four bounds exactly,

    1.479539342427251175506295 < a𝔡₀ < 1.479539342427251175728226,
    0.0105606575727652403536671 < b𝔡₁ < 0.0105606575727652403758445.

Adding, a𝔡₀ + b𝔡₁ − 1.4901 lies between 1.64158599…·10⁻¹⁴ and 1.64161040…·10⁻¹⁴. As 3 − λ_♯ = 1.4901, this is
(49.26). (Also a𝔡₀ + (b − 1)𝔡₁ < 1.4901, by 𝔡₁ > 3.3·10⁻⁷, so b is the least integer that works with
this a.) ∎

**Corollary 49.45** (The gap condition when both offsets are increments.) (a) Suppose that 𝔡₀ and 𝔡₁
lie in π_1(ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind), as they do for ℰ_ind as constructed ((b) and Remark 49.46). Then every ε_K with
which (G) holds satisfies ε_K < 1.6417·10⁻¹⁴. For every admissible choice of the weights, the number R of
Proposition 49.31 then satisfies R > 4.1659·10²³, so that d_NM ≥ d_acc > 1.2497·10²⁴ and
N_NM = 21d_NM + 6 > 2.624·10²⁵.

(b) For ℰ_ind as the proof of Proposition 23.28 constructs it, 𝔡₀ and 𝔡₁ lie in π_1ℰ_ind. So the hypothesis of (a)
holds for the index sets as constructed, and for them every ε_K with which (G) holds is below 1.6417·10⁻¹⁴.

*Proof.* (a) λ := λ_♯ + a𝔡₀ + b𝔡₁, with a and b of Lemma 49.44, is obtained from the generator λ_♯ by
a + b additions of increments, so λ ∈ Λ, and Re λ − 3 < 1.6417·10⁻¹⁴ by (49.26). If
ε_K ≥ 1.6417·10⁻¹⁴, then Re λ ∈ (3, 3 + ε_K], against (G). By Proposition 49.31,
R > (1 − 3ε_K − 2δ̂ − δ̄)/(ε_Kδ̂) with δ̂ = 1.46214·10⁻¹⁰ and δ̄ = 1.94137057·10⁻⁸, and the right side decreases in ε_K.
At ε_K = 1.6417·10⁻¹⁴ the numerator exceeds 1 − 1.98·10⁻⁸ > 0.99999998 and ε_Kδ̂ = 2.400395…·10⁻²⁴ < 2.4004·10⁻²⁴, so
R > 4.16597·10²³. By Theorem 49.32 (ii), d_NM ≥ d_acc ≥ 3R > 1.2497·10²⁴, and 21 · 1.2497·10²⁴ > 2.624·10²⁵.

(b) The step of the proof of Proposition 23.28 that corrects the translations applies the fact (F1) of that proof
with k = 2. There Lemma 21.35 is applied with a weight α ∈ (2 − ε_Υ, 2), and the index set ℰ it gives contains
E(α), the smallest index set that contains the elements (ι, 0) of the boundary spectrum of ρ⁻²(□^Υ_b)^(0), of every
type, with Re ι > α. By Lemma 23.3, ι^Υ_(s0,2) = 2 + 𝔡₀ (type s0) and ι^Υ_(s1,2) = 2 + 𝔡₁ (type s1) are simple
roots, and their real parts exceed 2 > α. (F1) writes ℰ as (2, 0) ∪ (2 + ℰ_ind), and 2 + 𝔡₀ and 2 + 𝔡₁ differ from 2;
so (𝔡₀, 0) and (𝔡₁, 0) lie in that ℰ_ind, which is part of the union ℰ_ind of Section 49.9.1. ∎

**Remark 49.46** (The offset 𝔡₀ as an increment.) Remark 49.4 lets 𝔡₀ enter Λ through the increment
1 + 𝔡₀ only, and Proposition 49.3 shows that the windows of (G) are then not met by the sums it considers for
ε_K < 5.019·10⁻⁸. For ℰ_ind as the proof of Proposition 23.28 constructs it, 𝔡₀ and 𝔡₁ are exponents: (F1) there,
with k = 2, takes the boundary spectrum above a weight in (2 − ε_Υ, 2), at every type (Corollary 49.45 (b)). So
with ℰ_ind as constructed, (G) fails at every ε_K ≥ 1.6417·10⁻¹⁴ (Corollary 49.45). Whether a smaller
admissible ℰ_ind omits 𝔡₀ is not decided by this paper; Theorem 49.77 reduces it to the vanishing of one family of
coefficients. The root ι^Υ_(s0,2) = 2 + 𝔡₀ of (□^Υ_b)^(0) lies above the weights in (0, ι^Υ_(s1,2)) at which
Proposition 23.28 solves for the corrections of the states, and these corrections start at the order (2, 0), so a
smaller admissible ℰ_ind keeps the exponent 𝔡₀ wherever a term at that root has a nonzero coefficient. At b₀ the
operator commutes with the rotations, and the corrections of the states of types s1 and v1 do not meet the roots of
type s0. At a rotating b the metric couples the angular types at the order |x|⁻³ ((23.20)), and ℰ_ind is one
index set serving at every b near b₀. So (G) at an ε_K ≥ 1.6417·10⁻¹⁴ needs a smaller admissible ℰ_ind ∪ ℰ^ι_ind that
omits 𝔡₀ or 𝔡₁; omitting 𝔡₀ means the vanishing of these coefficients at every b near b₀.

#### 49.9.2 The loss of the inverse of the transition face model

**Proposition 49.47** (The loss of Corollary 25.12 is 1.) Let β_sctf ∈ [1, 3/2) and β_ztf ∈ [−1, 0). The
proof of Corollary 25.12 runs with the regularity s := 1, the weight α_+ := 0, the incoming order 𝗋_in := −¼ and, at
the incoming radial sets, the inner product of Lemma 49.36, and gives (25.14) with ℓ = 1, for
every k ∈ ℕ₀ and every ϵ ∈ (0, ¼(3/2 − β_sctf)). So with these choices the loss of Corollary 25.12 is 1, which is
the value of ℓ_tf in Lemma 49.7 (d), and its least possible value there. Every application of
Corollary 25.12 in the construction of Theorem 34.9 and of Theorem 34.24 can be made with
β_sctf = 3/2 − ε, with 0 < ε < ¼; so ℓ_tf = 1 at all of them, and in Proposition 49.40 and Lemma 49.38
ℓ⁺_tf = 1.

*Proof.* *The regularity.* Proposition 25.11 gives the tf-admissibility of L_b^(·) with every weight in (0, 1], in
particular with β := −β_ztf. By Definition 13.15, tf-admissibility does not depend on the choices of s, α_+ and the
orders, and Corollary 13.16 (a)–(b) holds with s and α_+ as in Theorem 13.14, which takes s and α_+ in ℝ and uses
the order pair of Lemma 11.32 only through its decay order at the boundary face of tf. The face tf carries no
event horizon, so the condition s > ½ + ϑ_ℋ that Proposition 25.11 meets for the spectral families on X (whence its
"s large") does not enter the bound on tf. So (13.17) holds at
s = 1 and α_+ = 0, and with Theorem 13.14 (4) for k further b-derivatives, N_tf(±1)⁻¹ is bounded from
H^((s−2;k),(𝗋+1,q−2))_(sc,b;b) to H^((s;k),(𝗋,q))_(sc,b;b), as in the proof of Corollary 25.12.

*The orders.* That proof takes δ_0 := ¼(3/2 − β_sctf) ∈ (0, 1/8], ϵ < δ_0, the outgoing order
𝗋_out := β_sctf − 2 − ϵ/2, and the orders 𝗋_± of Lemma 11.32 at σ_* = ±1 with that outgoing value; it arranges
𝗋_out < −½ + S̄_L at R_out with an inner product there. Lemma 11.32 also asks 𝗋_in > (−1 + ϑ_in)/2 − α_+ and
𝗋_in ≥ 𝗋_out, with ϑ_in in an inner product of our choice at the incoming radial sets ((O3) of Section 11.1.4). With
the inner product of Lemma 49.36, ϑ_in = 0, so (−1 + ϑ_in)/2 = −½ < −¼ = 𝗋_in; and
𝗋_out < −½ < 𝗋_in. The order of Lemma 11.32 is 𝗋 = 𝗋_out + (𝗋_in − 𝗋_out)Θχ_c with 0 ≤ Θχ_c ≤ 1, equal to
𝗋_out near R_out and to 𝗋_in near the incoming radial sets; so inf 𝗋 = 𝗋_out and sup 𝗋 = 𝗋_in.

*The losses.* In Lemma 20.23 at s = 1, ⌈(s − 1)_+⌉ = ⌈(−s)_+⌉ = 0, so ℓ = ⌈sup 𝗋 − 𝗋_out⌉ and
ℓ̃ = ⌈𝗋_out − inf 𝗋⌉ = 0. Here 0 < sup 𝗋 − 𝗋_out = 𝗋_in − 𝗋_out = 7/4 − β_sctf + ϵ/2 < 3/4 + 1/16 < 1, as β_sctf ≥ 1
and ϵ < 1/8; so ℓ = 1 for every such ϵ, and the last step of the proof of Corollary 25.12 (k replaced by k + ℓ̃,
ℓ made independent of ϵ) changes nothing. Near ztf the two spaces are H^(s−2+k)_(b,β_ztf−2) = H^(k−1)_(b,β_ztf−2) and
H^(s+k)_(b,β_ztf) = H^(k+1)_(b,β_ztf), which the input order k + 1 and the output order k accommodate. So
(25.14) holds with ℓ = 1. The expression of Lemma 49.7 (d) at these orders is ℓ + ℓ̃ = 1, and it
is at least 1 at every choice.

*The applications.* Theorem 27.46 uses Corollary 25.12 with β_sctf = ℓ_scf, and Proposition 27.55 and
Proposition 27.58 use it through Theorem 27.46 or directly with β_sctf = ℓ_scf. The construction may apply them
with ℓ_scf := 3/2 − ε, as Lemma 49.37 takes it: in Step 3.2 of the proof of Proposition 31.27, in Step 3.4′
of the proof of Lemma 32.27, at level 1 of the proof of Proposition 33.15, and at levels 2 and 3 there and in
Proposition 33.28 and Proposition 35.23, whose forcings keep the scf-order 5/2 − ε of Step 0
(Lemma 33.11), which allows ℓ_scf := 3/2 − ε there. In each of them ε is a loss that the proof takes small, and
the bounds on it there give ε < ¼: ε < ½ε_g < ¼ in Lemma 32.27, 2ε < ε_+ − η_2 in Section 33.5, and
5ε ≤ 5ε_1 < ε_+ in Section 35.1, with ε_+ < δ_♯ < ¼ ((32.27)). So β_sctf = 3/2 − ε ∈ (1, 3/2) at every
application; and an application at another sctf-weight in [1, 3/2), such as the weight 3/2 − 2ε of the level-3
solution, has ℓ = 1 as well, by the first part of the proof. ∎

#### 49.9.3 The order of the background terms

**Proposition 49.48** (d_BG = 11 serves.) For ‖β‖_(d_0) small, with d_0 ≥ 11, every family A of
Lemma 35.3 (b) applied to a solution satisfies

    ‖Au‖_k ≤ C_k (‖u‖_(k+2) + ‖β‖_(k+11) ‖u‖_2),    (49.27)

and each family v_β of sources in Lemma 35.3 (b) satisfies ‖v_β‖_k ≤ C_k(1 + ‖β‖_(k+11)). So the families of
Lemma 35.3 (b) have split loss (2; 11, 2) in the sense of Lemma 49.34, the bound of
Lemma 35.3 (b) holds with d = 11, and the charge max(2, d_BG) of Remark 49.8 may be taken to be 11.

*Proof.* *The background as a metric.* The families depend on β = (h, p⃗, q) through h̃ := h + h_tot(p⃗) + h_(b,rem)(q)
and through p⃗. By Lemma 32.35, ‖h_tot(p⃗)‖_(𝒳^k) ≤ C_k|p⃗|. By (34.2) and Definition 26.37,
h_(b,rem)(q) is a finite sum of fixed smooth tensors times the components of q and their t_*-derivatives of order at most
3 (the towers use the derivatives a^((j)), j ≤ k_μ ≤ 3, Lemma 26.38). On functions of t_*,
∂_(t_*) = t_*⁻¹(t_*∂_(t_*)), and t_*∂_(t_*) is the b-vector field of the spaces of (34.1), while t_*⁻¹ only
adds decay; so ‖h_(b,rem)(q)‖_(𝒳^k) ≤ C_k‖q‖_(𝒬^(k+3)). Hence ‖h̃‖_m ≤ C_m‖β‖_(m+3) for every m.

*The coefficients.* By Lemma 35.3 (b), A is a b-differential operator of order at most 2 whose coefficients, in
the frame and in local b-coordinates on a finite atlas, are polynomials in the metric, its inverse and their
derivatives, the background g_0 being smooth in p⃗; the derivatives of the metric are of order at most 2, A being a
difference of linearisations of the second-order operator P of (21.44), or such a difference applied to a
fixed section. Let A′ be A with h̃ replaced by 0; its coefficients are smooth in x and p⃗ alone, so
‖A′u‖_k ≤ C_k‖u‖_(k+2). Then A = A′ + Σ_(|γ|≤2) Φ_γ(x, p⃗, w) D^γ_b, where w := (h̃, D_b h̃, D²_b h̃) and Φ_γ is
smooth with Φ_γ(x, p⃗, 0) = 0.

*The estimates.* We use Lemma 20.6 on the five-dimensional manifold with corners, with d = 3 > 5/2, after a
finite partition of unity (on which the norms are equivalent) and after factoring the weights, whose powers of the
defining functions commute with b-derivatives up to smooth factors. The proof of its (3), by the chain rule and
(20.13), applies verbatim to a smooth function Φ(x, p⃗, w) of a vector w with Φ(x, p⃗, 0) = 0 and bounded
derivatives in x and p⃗ on the chart domains; so ‖Φ_γ(·, p⃗, w)‖_m ≤ C_m‖w‖_(m+3) ≤ C_m‖h̃‖_(m+5) for ‖w‖_3 small. By its
(2), with Φ_γ in the place of the factor measured at the high order,

    ‖Φ_γ D^γ_b u‖_k ≤ C_k (‖Φ_γ‖_3 ‖u‖_(k+2) + ‖Φ_γ‖_(k+3) ‖u‖_2) ≤ C_k (‖h̃‖_8 ‖u‖_(k+2) + ‖h̃‖_(k+8) ‖u‖_2),

and ‖h̃‖_8 ≤ C‖β‖_11 ≤ C‖β‖_(d_0), ‖h̃‖_(k+8) ≤ C_k‖β‖_(k+11). This is (49.27) on the remainders. At a face
where the spaces carry an expansion, the coefficients of a product are finite sums of products of coefficients, and
the coefficients of Φ_γ(·, p⃗, w) are polynomials in those of w, functions on a face of dimension at most 4, which
(2) and (3) of Lemma 20.6 bound with the same d = 3 > 4/2; so the coefficient norms obey the same bound. The
sources are the case of a fixed section u, or of a fixed operator applied to the background. ∎

#### 49.9.4 The Fourier steps and the map Φ

**Lemma 49.49** (The Fourier step of a level above 3.) At a level β ∈ (3, α] of
Theorem 34.9, Step 0 of the proof of Proposition 33.15 (through Proposition 33.28 when β < 4) applies
