So |𝒯_(k+1)| ≤ ℬ_k + (44/27)(c_d + 2k)/a ≤ ℬ_k + 2(c_d + 2k + 1)/a = ℬ_(k+1). Finally, on 𝔻_(k+1), |R_(k+1)| ≥ |R_0| −
2(k + 1)ϱ − ℬ_(k+1) ϱ², and since k + 1 ≤ n + 1, a ≥ 3/4 and c_d ≤ 13,

    2(k + 1)ϱ ≤ (n + 1)/(12(n + 2)²) ≤ 1/36,      ℬ_(k+1) ϱ² ≤ (n + 1)(n + 14)/(216(n + 2)⁴) ≤ 15/(216 · 27) < 1/388,

so |R_(k+1)| ≥ 7a/8 − 1/36 − 1/388 > 7a/8 − 0.031 ≥ 7a/8 − a/8 = 3a/4, as a/8 ≥ 3/32 > 0.031. ∎

### 55.11 The hypotheses, for every order

**Proposition 55.28** (The hypotheses for the envelope env_C.) Let env be (55.20), or
exp(−1/(v − v_s)); let n ≥ 1 be an integer and x_n := 1/(96(n + 2)²). Then: (a) on (v_s, v_s + x_n], env^(k) > 0 for k ≤
n + 2, and |env^(j)| ≤ κ^j env for j ≤ n + 2; (b) on (v_s, v_s + x_n], for every k ≤ n, env^(k) is strictly log-concave,
99/100 ≤ κ_k/κ ≤ 1 and |κ_k′| ≤ c_R κ_k^(3/2), with c_R = 12/5 for (55.20) and c_R = 21/10 for exp(−1/(v −
v_s)); (c) on (v_s, v_s + 1/200], |κ′| ≥ c_t κ^(3/2) with c_t = 2.13951, resp. c_t = 2, and 3/4 ≤ κx² ≤ 81/100, resp.
κx² = 1; (d) (H_D) holds for every c > 0.

*Proof.* Here R_0 = x²κ is (55.22) for (55.20) and 1 for exp(−1/x); put a := 3/4, resp. a := 1.
For (55.20), on 𝔻, where ϱ = 1/(24(n + 2)²) ≤ 1/216, (55.23) gives |R_0 − 3/4| ≤ 12ϱ + ϱ²/7 ≤
0.056 < 3/32, so |R_0| ≥ 21/32 = 7a/8, and |R_0′| ≤ 12 + ϱ/2 ≤ 13. So Lemma 55.27 applies, with c_d := 13, resp.
c_d := 0. Fix 0 < x ≤ x_n = ϱ/4 and k ≤ n + 1. 𝒯_k is holomorphic on the disc of radius ϱ_(n+1) ≥ ϱ/2 about 0, which
contains the disc of radius ϱ/4 about x, so |𝒯_k(x)| ≤ ℬ_k and, by Cauchy's estimate, |𝒯_k′(x)| ≤ 4ℬ_k/ϱ ≤ ℬ_k/x.
Hence, R_k being real on the real axis,

    |R_k(x) − R_0(x) + 2kx| ≤ ℬ_k x²,      |x R_k′(x) − x R_0′(x) + 2kx| ≤ |x(2x𝒯_k + x²𝒯_k′)| ≤ 3ℬ_k x².

For both envelopes ℬ_k x ≤ 2(n + 1)(n + 14)/((3/4) · 96 (n + 2)²) ≤ (n + 14)/(36(n + 2)) ≤ 15/108 < 1/7 and 2kx ≤
2(n + 1)/(96(n + 2)²) ≤ 1/144; and R_0(x) ≥ a by (55.24). Therefore

    R_k(x) − R_0(x) ≥ −1/144 − x/7 ≥ −1/140,      R_k(x) − R_0(x) ≤ x(1/7 − 2k) < 0   for k ≥ 1,

the first because x ≤ x_1 = 1/864 and 1/144 + 1/6048 < 1/140; so R_k(x) ≥ a − 1/140 > 0. So
Lemma 55.25 applies on (0, x_n] with m = n + 1. By its (a), env^(k) > 0 for k ≤ n + 2. By (b),
κ_k/κ = R_k/R_0 ≥ 1 − 1/(140R_0) ≥ 1 − 1/(140a) ≥ 99/100, since 4/(3 · 140) < 1/100, and κ_k/κ ≤ 1; and
env^(j)/(κ^j env) = Π_(i<j) R_i/R_0 ∈ (0, 1] for j ≤ n + 2. This is (a) and the bounds of κ_k/κ in (b). For the rest
of (b), |R_0′(x)| ≤ 12 by (55.24) (R_0′ = 0 for exp(−1/x)), so

    |x R_k′(x)| ≤ 12x + 2kx + 3ℬ_k x² ≤ 12/864 + 1/144 + 3/(7 · 864) < 0.0214,   resp.  1/144 + 3/(7 · 864) < 0.0075,

while R_k ≥ 0.74, resp. R_k ≥ 0.99; in both cases |x R_k′/R_k| ≤ 1/30. By (55.21), R_k − R_(k+1) =
x(2 − x R_k′/R_k) ∈ [59x/30, 61x/30] for k ≤ n. By Lemma 55.25 (c), env^(k) is strictly log-concave
and |κ_k′| ≤ c κ_k^(3/2) with c = (61/30) R_k^(−1/2) ≤ (61/30)/0.86 < 12/5, as √0.74 ≥ 0.86, resp.
c ≤ (61/30)/0.99 < 21/10, as √0.99 ≥ 0.99.
(c) For (55.20) and 0 < x ≤ 1/200, (55.24) gives 3/4 ≤ R_0 ≤ 3/4 + 12x ≤ 81/100 and, as
2x²/7 ≤ 0.002x,

    2R_0 − xR_0′ ≥ 3/2 + 24x − 2x²/7 − 12x ≥ 3/2 + 11.998x > 0.

By Lemma 55.25 (d), |κ′|/κ^(3/2) = (2R_0 − xR_0′)/R_0^(3/2) ≥ h(x) := (3/2 + 11.998x)/(3/4 + 12x)^(3/2).
The derivative of log h has the sign of 11.998(3/4 + 12x) − 18(3/2 + 11.998x) = −18.0015 − 71.988x < 0, so h
decreases and h(x) ≥ h(1/200) = 1.55999/0.81^(3/2) = 1.55999/0.729 = 2.13990… > 2.13951, which proves (c) with
c_t = 2.13951. For exp(−1/x), (2R_0 − xR_0′)/R_0^(3/2) = 2 and κx² = 1.
(d) For 0 < x ≤ 1/200, κ = R_0/x² ≤ 1/x² by (c), and (55.25) with sin(πx/3) ≤ 1 and 1/(3 − x) > 0 gives
env(v_s + x) ≤ c_e e^(1 − 3/(4x)). So for 0 < y ≤ 1/800 and every c > 0

    κ(v_s + y/2) κ(v_s + 4y)^c env(v_s + 4y) ≤ 4y⁻² (16y²)^(−c) c_e e^(1 − 3/(16y)),

which tends to 0 as y ↓ 0, e^(−3/(16y)) decaying faster than every power of y. For exp(−1/x) the left side equals
4y⁻² (16y²)^(−c) e^(−1/(4y)), which tends to 0 likewise. ∎

**Corollary 55.29** (Every hypothesis, for every order.) Let env be (55.20) or exp(−1/(v −
v_s)), N ≥ 2, J ≥ N + 4, and x0 := x_(J−2) = 1/(96 J²). On (v_s, v_s + x0], (H_N) and (H_N+2) hold with α = 1/2, the
c_R of Proposition 55.28 and c_j = 1; (B_J) holds with c_j = 1; for v_s < v′ ≤ v ≤ v_s + x0 and j ≤ J

    κ(v′)^j env(v′) ≤ κ(v)^j env(v) e^(−κ(v)(v − v′)/2);    (55.27)

(H_t) holds with c_t = 2.13951, resp. 2; (H_*) holds with c_* = 3/4, resp. 1; and (H_D) holds. So every hypothesis that
Theorem 55.22, Proposition 55.18 and Theorem 55.11 place on the envelope holds for these two envelopes, for every K
≥ 6 (N = K + 3), with J the largest order those results use.

*Proof.* Proposition 55.28 with n = J − 2 ≥ N + 2: (a) and (b) give, for k ≤ N + 2, env^(k) > 0, strictly
log-concave, κ_k/κ ∈ [99/100, 1] ⊂ [1/2, 2] and |κ_k′| ≤ c_R κ_k^(1+1/2), and for j ≤ J, |env^(j)| ≤ κ^j env; this is
(H_N+2), which contains (H_N), and (B_J). For (55.27): as x0 ≤ 1/200, (c) gives κx² ≥ 3/4, resp. κx² = 1, on
(v_s, v_s + x0], so κ^(−1/2) ≤ 2x0/√3 there; κ′ < 0 there since env is strictly log-concave; and, as c_R ≤ 12/5,
j c_R κ^(−1/2) ≤ J (12/5)(2/√3) x0 = √3/(60 J) < 1/2. Hence (log(κ^j env))′ = κ + jκ′/κ ≥ κ − j c_R κ^(1/2) ≥ κ/2 ≥
κ(v)/2 on [v′, v], and integrating over [v′, v] gives (55.27). (c) also gives c_t and c_*. By
Lemma 55.25 (e) with n = N − 1, which uses the strict log-concavity of env^(k) for k ≤ N − 2,
κ − κ_(N−1) ≥ |κ′|/κ ≥ c_t κ^(1/2): this is (H_t) with α = 1/2. (H_D) is (d). ∎

The hypotheses are thus proved on (v_s, v_s + 1/(96 J²)], an interval that shrinks as N and J grow; Theorem 55.22,
Proposition 55.18 and Theorem 55.11 take their interval (v_s, v_s + x0] as given and use the hypotheses only on
subintervals (v_s, v_s + x0′] with x0′ ≤ x0, so this interval is all they need.

**Remark 55.30** (The constants at the edge.) By (55.26), as x ↓ 0, R_k → R_0(0),
x R_k′ → 0 and (R_k − R_(k+1))/(x R_k^(1/2)) → 2R_0(0)^(−1/2); so κ_k/κ → 1 and env^(j)/(κ^j env) → 1. Hence, as
x0 ↓ 0, the best constants c on (v_s, v_s + x0] in |κ_k′| ≤ c κ_k^(3/2) and in |κ′| ≥ c κ^(3/2) tend to
2R_0(0)^(−1/2), which is 4/√3 = 2.309… for (55.20) and 2 for exp(−1/x); in (H_t) with α = 1/2 the best
constant tends to 2(N − 1)R_0(0)^(−1/2), since κ − κ_(N−1) = Σ_(k<N−1) (R_k − R_(k+1))/x² with each term ~ 2/x and
κ^(1/2) = R_0^(1/2)/x. The values 12/5 and 21/10 of c_R exceed these limits by 3.9 % and 5 %. The value 2.13951 of
the constant in |κ′| ≥ c κ^(3/2) is 7.4 % below its limit 4/√3, because it holds on all of (v_s, v_s + 1/200]: the
lower bound h in the proof of Proposition 55.28 (c) decreases from h(0) = 4/√3 to h(1/200) = 2.13990….

**Remark 55.31** (The edges exp(−a/x).) Let a > 0 and env(v) = exp(−a/(v − v_s)) for v > v_s. As a function
of x̃ := x/a, env is exp(−1/x̃), and d/dx = a⁻¹ d/dx̃; so κ_k = a⁻¹ κ̃_k, where κ̃_k are the logarithmic derivatives of
exp(−1/x̃) in x̃. Hence κ_k/κ, env^(j)/(κ^j env) and κ(v)(v − v′) are those of exp(−1/x̃) at x̃ = x/a, |κ_k′|/κ_k^(3/2)
and |κ′|/κ^(3/2) are those multiplied by a^(−1/2), and κx² = a. So Corollary 55.29 holds for this envelope on (v_s,
v_s + a x0], with c_R = (21/10)a^(−1/2), c_j = 1, c_t = 2a^(−1/2) and c_* = a, (H_D) included.

**Remark 55.32** (An envelope outside the class.) The envelope sin⁴(π(v − v_s)/3) for v ≥ v_s, 0 for
v < v_s, is C³ and not C⁴ at v_s: near v_s it is (πx/3)⁴(1 + O(x²)), so env^(4)(v_s+) = 4!(π/3)⁴ = 8π⁴/27, while
env^(4) = 0 for v < v_s. So it lies outside the class of Theorem 3.1. It also satisfies no (H_N) with N ≥ 3, since
κ = 4/x + O(x) and κ_3 = env^(4)/env^(3) = 1/x + O(x) give κ_3/κ → 1/4 < 1/2.

### 55.12 One switch per column

In the band λ^(3+δ) ≤ E ≤ λ^(3−δ) of Proposition 54.34 (iii) the ratio R decides the boundary's character up to
the factor 1 ± 2λ^γ, γ = 1/10. For an envelope increasing at its edge, the ratio crosses 1 once per column, and the
boundary switches once.

**Theorem 55.33** (One switch per column.) Let K ≥ 6, N = K + 3, δ ∈ (0, 1/2], γ = 1/10, and let g_λ be the metric
of Theorem 3.1. Let env be increasing on (v_s, v_s + x0] and satisfy (H_N) there. There is λ_24 > 0 such that for λ ≤
λ_24 and every x̂ ∈ S³ the following holds. Divide the band λ^(3+δ) ≤ E ≤ λ^(3−δ) into consecutive carrier periods I_k
of length 2πλ, starting at its left end, and put M_k := max_(I_k) g_λ⁻¹(dΦ0, dΦ0) at x̂. Then M_k > 0 for every period
whose midpoint has R ≥ 1 + 2λ^γ, M_k < 0 for every period on which R ≤ 1 − 2λ^γ, and M_(k+1) < M_k for every two
consecutive periods one of which meets {|R − 1| ≤ 2λ^γ}; periods of the first kind exist and precede all others, and
periods of the second kind exist and follow all others. So the sequence (M_k) changes sign exactly once: before the
switch every carrier period has points where the boundary is timelike at x̂, and after it the boundary is spacelike
throughout every period at x̂.

The proof is given at the end of Section 55.13, where the margin and the first-degree amplitude are compared. It
also uses a bound for the remainder beyond the first degree.

**Lemma 55.34** (The remainder beyond the first degree.) Let v1 ≤ v_♯ with ε_4(v1) ≤ λ, and let R_w be
the region of Lemma 54.21. At every boundary point X ∈ R_w, with a fixed cost c,

    |(w − e)(X)| ≤ C (λ^(N−6) ε_c(v1)² + λ^(N−2) ε_c(v1)),    (55.28)

where w = g_λ − g_app and e = h^(1) − h_app^(1).

*Proof.* By (54.25) and (55.10), w − e solves −(1/2) g_λ^(ab) ∂_a ∂_b (w − e) = f′, the
operator of (54.25) being written around the seed, where f′ is the sum of four parts. (i) The part of
degree at least two of Ric^H(g_app), at most C λ^(N−1) ε_c² with each derivative costing λ⁻¹, by (F2) of
Section 54.8 and the argument of Lemma 54.18 (d). (ii) The part of first degree of Ric^H(g_app) minus that
of (55.10): as g_app stops at λ^N, the part of first degree of Ric^H(g_app) is λ^N Re[R_X(H_N) e^(iv/λ)]
as in the proof of Lemma 55.16 (i), so this part is λ^N Re[(R_X H_N + λ R_X H_(N+1)) e^(iv/λ)], at most C λ^N
ε_c. (iii) The differences between the coefficients of (54.25) and those of dRic^H, which are of degree
at least one, acting on w and on e: the coefficient of a derivative of order q is at most C λ^(q−1) ε, each of its
derivatives costing λ⁻¹, and the order q = 2 occurs only on e, the operator on the left being that of w. (iv) The terms
quadratic in w, smaller still.

Step 6 of the proof of Lemma 54.21 needs Σ_(i≤2) ‖∂^i f′‖ on the slices. Put ε := ε_c(v1), c ≥ M*. By the
graded energies of the proof of Lemma 54.22, E^(i) ≤ C λ^(N−3−i) ε, so ‖∂^p w‖ ≤ C λ^(N−3) ε for p ≤ 1
and ‖∂^p w‖ ≤ C λ^(N−2−p) ε for 1 ≤ p ≤ 3. The same bounds hold for e, and for e also at p = 4: e solves an equation with
the seed's coefficients, its data, those induced by U^(1), are of size λ^(N−2−j) ε with j derivatives, and its forcing
term is of size λ^(N+1) ε, each derivative costing λ⁻¹. A term of ∂^i of (iii), i ≤ 2, is a derivative of order m of a
coefficient of order q times ∂^(q+i−m) u, u = w or e, so it is at most C λ^(q−1−m) ε ‖∂^(q+i−m) u‖: at most C λ^(N−3−i)
ε² if q + i − m ≥ 1, and at most C λ^(N−4−i) ε² if q + i − m = 0. So Σ_(i≤2) ‖∂^i f′‖ ≤ C (λ^(N−6) ε² + λ^(N−2) ε): from
(iii) the largest term is ∂²(coefficient) · w, at most λ^(−3) ε · λ^(N−3) ε; (i) gives λ^(N−3) ε² and (ii) λ^(N−2) ε. The
data of w − e on Σ_τ0 are those induced by U − U^(1), at most C λ^(N−2−j) ε² with j derivatives
(Lemma 55.6), and those of G(X, u/λ) − g_app, which is λ^(N+1) times profiles with an oscillating factor
(Section 7.5); they contribute C λ^(N−5) ε² + C λ^(N−2) ε to E_2(τ0). Steps 1, 5, 6 and 7 of the proof of
Lemma 54.21, with these forcing terms and data, then give (55.28). ∎

### 55.13 The growth of the margin at the crossover

The proof of Theorem 55.33 compares, over one carrier period, the growth of the margin m0 with the change of the
first-degree amplitude S. It uses two inequalities at the points of the band: m0′ ≥ 1.9 κ m0, and m0′ − |S′| ≥ c κ m0
with a fixed c > 0 where R ≤ 1.1. This section proves both, with explicit constants and thresholds. The first holds,
for λ below an explicit threshold, for every envelope that is positive and log-concave on an interval (v_s, v_s + x0]
with κ(v_s + x0) > 0, which is part of the hypothesis (H_N) of Theorem 55.33; for the two envelopes of
Section 55.9 the thresholds are written out. The second holds with c = 0.89 where R ≤ 1.1, with c = 0.93 where
R ≤ 1.06 and with c = 0.99 where R ≤ 1.005, for every S with |S′| ≤ 1.001 κ |S| and |S| ≤ 1.001 R m0. The first-degree
amplitude has these two properties at the points of the band where R ≥ 1/2, once λ is small (Proposition 55.40),
and the proof of Theorem 55.33 uses them at no other points. The factor is 2 − R up to small terms: for S that also
satisfies the reverse bounds |S′| ≥ 0.999 κ |S| and |S| ≥ 0.999 R m0, as the first-degree amplitude does at the same
points, no c above 0.904 holds at R = 1.1 once λ is small (Remark 55.41). Corollary 55.42 gives the decrease
over one carrier period that the proof of Theorem 55.33 draws from these inequalities, and Remark 55.43 compares the
degree-two terms of that proof with m0.

*Setting.* As in Chapter 54, μ0 > 0 is the seed's mass, A > 0 the amplitude of the waves and v_s := inf supp
env; no sign of the envelope env is assumed, and in the results below it is positive on an interval (v_s, v_s + x0]. The
margin of the boundary {r = r_q} at equality is

    μ(v) := μ0 + (2/9) A² ∫_(v_s)^v env²,    r_q := (μ0 μ)^(1/4),    m0 := √(μ/μ0) − 1 + r_q μ′/(2μ),    (55.29)

so that μ′ = (2/9) A² env² and μ ≥ μ0. A prime is d/dv. Where env > 0 we write κ := (log env)′. We put E(v) :=
sup_(v′≤v) |env(v′)|, the level of (54.7); the band is the set of v with λ^(3+δ) ≤ E(v) ≤ λ^(3−δ), where 0 <
δ ≤ 1/2; at a point (v, x̂) of the boundary, R(v, x̂) := λ³ A |env(v)| |ν(v − τ0)| |d(ϑ)|/m0(v), with ν and d as in
Chapter 54; and S is the first-degree amplitude of Theorem 55.33 at fixed x̂, a continuously differentiable
complex function of v. In this section only, p := (μ/μ0)^(1/2) ≥ 1.

**Lemma 55.35** (The logarithmic growth of the margin.) Let v > v_s, let env be positive and log-concave on
(v_s, v], and let κ(v) > 0. Put

    ς := μ′/(μ0 κ) = 2A² env²/(9 μ0 κ)     at v.    (55.30)

Then at v

    (2 − 3ς/4) κ m0 ≤ m0′ ≤ (2 + (1 + ς/8)/(√μ0 κ)) κ m0.    (55.31)

*Proof.* Write ℓ := log env and κ for κ(v). As ℓ is concave and differentiable on (v_s, v], ℓ(t) ≤ ℓ(v) + κ(t − v) for
v_s < t ≤ v, so env(t)² ≤ env(v)² e^(2κ(t − v)) there, and

    μ − μ0 = (2/9) A² ∫_(v_s)^v env² ≤ (2/9) A² env(v)² ∫_(−∞)^v e^(2κ(t − v)) dt = μ′/(2κ).    (55.32)

*The two terms of m0.* From μ = μ0 p², r_q/(2μ) = μ0^(1/4) μ^(−3/4)/2 = 1/(2 √μ0 p^(3/2)), and p − 1 = (p² − 1)/(p + 1) =
(μ − μ0)/(μ0 (p + 1)). So m0 = p − 1 + μ′/(2 √μ0 p^(3/2)), and

    κ m0 = a_1 + a_2,      a_1 := κ (μ − μ0)/(μ0 (p + 1)) ≥ 0,      a_2 := κ μ′/(2 √μ0 p^(3/2)) > 0.    (55.33)

*The derivative.* μ″ = (2/9) A² · 2 env env′ = 2κ μ′, and p′ = μ′/(2 √(μ0 μ)) = μ′/(2 μ0 p). Hence
(μ′ p^(−3/2))′ = 2κ μ′ p^(−3/2) − (3/2) μ′ p^(−5/2) p′ = 2κ μ′ p^(−3/2) − 3μ′²/(4 μ0 p^(7/2)), and

    m0′ = μ′/(2 μ0 p) + κ μ′/(√μ0 p^(3/2)) − 3μ′²/(8 μ0^(3/2) p^(7/2)).    (55.34)

*Comparison with 2κ m0.* The second term of (55.34) is 2a_2. Since 1/(p + 1) − 1/(2p) = (p − 1)/(2p(p + 1)),
the first term is μ′/(μ0 (p + 1)) − b_1 with b_1 := μ′ (p − 1)/(2 μ0 p (p + 1)) ≥ 0. With b_2 := 3μ′²/(8 μ0^(3/2)
p^(7/2)) and 2κ m0 = 2a_1 + 2a_2 this gives

    m0′ − 2κ m0 = (μ′ − 2κ (μ − μ0))/(μ0 (p + 1)) − b_1 − b_2.    (55.35)

*Lower bound.* The first term of (55.35) is nonnegative by (55.32). Since p − 1 = (μ − μ0)/(μ0
(p + 1)) ≤ (μ − μ0)/(2μ0) and p ≥ 1,

    b_1 ≤ μ′ (μ − μ0)/(4 μ0² p (p + 1)) ≤ μ′ (μ − μ0)/(4 μ0² (p + 1)) = (ς/4) a_1,
    b_2 = (3μ′/(4 μ0 κ p²)) a_2 ≤ (3ς/4) a_2.

So b_1 + b_2 ≤ (3ς/4)(a_1 + a_2) = (3ς/4) κ m0, which is the left inequality of (55.31).

*Upper bound.* In (55.35), (μ′ − 2κ(μ − μ0))/(μ0 (p + 1)) − b_1 ≤ μ′/(μ0 (p + 1)) − b_1 = μ′/(2 μ0 p) and
b_2 ≥ 0, so m0′ − 2κ m0 ≤ μ′/(2 μ0 p) = (p^(1/2)/(√μ0 κ)) a_2 ≤ (p^(1/2)/(√μ0 κ)) κ m0. Finally p² = 1 + (μ − μ0)/μ0 ≤
1 + ς/2 by (55.32), and (1 + y)^(1/4) ≤ 1 + y/4 for y ≥ 0, so p^(1/2) ≤ 1 + ς/8. ∎

**Proposition 55.36** (The margin in the band.) Let x0 > 0, let env be positive and log-concave on
(v_s, v_s + x0] with κ̂ := κ(v_s + x0) > 0, and let 0 < δ ≤ 1/2 and 0 < λ < 1 with λ^(5/2) < env(v_s + x0). Then every
v with 0 < E(v) ≤ λ^(3−δ), in particular every point of the band, lies in (v_s, v_s + x0), and at v

    ς ≤ 2A² λ^(6−2δ)/(9 μ0 κ̂) ≤ 2A² λ⁵/(9 μ0 κ̂),      m0′ ≥ (2 − A² λ⁵/(6 μ0 κ̂)) κ m0.    (55.36)

So m0′ ≥ 1.9 κ m0 at every such v once λ⁵ ≤ 3μ0 κ̂/(5A²), and ς ≤ 10⁻³ there once λ⁵ ≤ 9μ0 κ̂/(2000 A²).

*Proof.* As log env is concave on (v_s, v_s + x0], κ is nonincreasing there, so κ ≥ κ̂ > 0 and env is increasing on
(v_s, v_s + x0]. If v ≤ v_s, then E(v) = 0. If v ≥ v_s + x0, then E(v) ≥ env(v_s + x0) > λ^(5/2) ≥ λ^(3−δ), since
3 − δ ≥ 5/2 and λ < 1. Hence v_s < v < v_s + x0; env is positive and log-concave on (v_s, v], κ(v) ≥ κ̂ > 0, and
env(v) = E(v) ≤ λ^(3−δ). So ς = 2A² env(v)²/(9 μ0 κ(v)) ≤ 2A² λ^(6−2δ)/(9 μ0 κ̂), which is at most 2A² λ⁵/(9 μ0 κ̂)
as 6 − 2δ ≥ 5, and Lemma 55.35 gives m0′ ≥ (2 − 3ς/4) κ m0 with 3ς/4 ≤ A² λ⁵/(6 μ0 κ̂). The two thresholds are
the conditions A² λ⁵/(6 μ0 κ̂) ≤ 1/10 and 2A² λ⁵/(9 μ0 κ̂) ≤ 10⁻³. ∎

**Corollary 55.37** (The two envelopes.) Let 0 < δ ≤ 1/2 and let v satisfy 0 < E(v) ≤ λ^(3−δ).

(a) For env = exp(−1/(v − v_s)) on v > v_s and 0 < λ ≤ e^(−1): at v, ς ≤ 8A² λ⁵/(225 μ0) and
m0′ ≥ (2 − 2A² λ⁵/(75 μ0)) κ m0. So m0′ ≥ 1.9 κ m0 once λ⁵ ≤ 15μ0/(4A²), and ς ≤ 10⁻³ once λ⁵ ≤ 9μ0/(320 A²).

(b) For the envelope (55.20), with c_e its constant, and 0 < λ < 1 with λ^(5/2) < (729/4096) e^(−1/8) c_e:
at v, ς ≤ 2A² λ⁵/(63 μ0) and m0′ ≥ (2 − A² λ⁵/(42 μ0)) κ m0. So m0′ ≥ 1.9 κ m0 once λ⁵ ≤ 21μ0/(5A²), and ς ≤ 10⁻³ once
λ⁵ ≤ 63μ0/(2000 A²).

*Proof.* Put x := v − v_s. (a) Here log env = −1/x, κ = 1/x² > 0 and (log env)″ = −2/x³ < 0, so env is positive,
increasing and log-concave on (v_s, ∞), E(v) = env(v) for v > v_s, and E(v) > 0 gives x > 0. From e^(−1/x) ≤ λ^(3−δ) ≤
λ^(5/2) we get 1/x ≥ (5/2) log(1/λ) ≥ 5/2, so x ≤ 2/5. Lemma 55.35 applies at v, with
ς = (2A²/(9 μ0)) x² e^(−2/x) ≤ (2A²/(9 μ0))(4/25) λ⁵ = 8A² λ⁵/(225 μ0) and 3ς/4 ≤ 2A² λ⁵/(75 μ0). The thresholds
are 2A² λ⁵/(75 μ0) ≤ 1/10 and 8A² λ⁵/(225 μ0) ≤ 10⁻³.
(b) By (55.25), on 0 < x < 3, log env = log c_e + 1 + 12 log sin(πx/3) − (3/4)(1/x + 1/(3 − x)), so

    κ = 4π cot(πx/3) + (3/4)(1/x² − 1/(3 − x)²),      κ′ = −(4π²/3)/sin²(πx/3) − (3/2)(1/x³ + 1/(3 − x)³) < 0.

So env is positive and log-concave on (v_s, v_s + 3). At x = 1, cot(π/3) = 1/√3 gives κ = 4π/√3 + 9/16 > 7, since
16π² > 147; and sin²(π/3) = 3/4 gives env(v_s + 1) = c_e e^(1 − 9/8) (3/4)⁶ = (729/4096) e^(−1/8) c_e. So
Proposition 55.36 applies with x0 := 1 and κ̂ > 7: ς ≤ 2A² λ⁵/(63 μ0) and 3ς/4 ≤ A² λ⁵/(42 μ0). The thresholds are
A² λ⁵/(42 μ0) ≤ 1/10 and 2A² λ⁵/(63 μ0) ≤ 10⁻³. ∎

In both cases the lower bound of (55.31) needs only log-concavity of env, which holds on the whole
increasing part of each envelope, and not the finer hypotheses that Corollary 55.29 proves on (v_s, v_s + x0].

The next lemma uses one more part of (H_N): the bound on κ′ (Definition 55.1, k = 0).

**Lemma 55.38** (The size of κ in the band.) Let x0 > 0, let env be positive and log-concave on
(v_s, v_s + x0] with env′ > 0 and |κ′| ≤ c_R κ^(1+α) there, where c_R > 0 and 0 < α < 1, and let env(v) → 0 as v ↓ v_s.
For v_s < v ≤ v_s + x0 put x := v − v_s. Then

    κ(v) ≥ (α c_R x)^(−1/α),    (55.37)

and if moreover v ≤ v_s + x0/2,

    κ(v) ≤ max{(2/(α c_R x0))^(1/α), (2^(1/α) α c_R log(env(v_s + x0)/env(v)))^(1/(1−α))}.    (55.38)

Let 0 < δ ≤ 1/2 and 0 < λ < 1 with λ^(5/2) < env(v_s + x0/2) and env(v_s + x0) ≤ λ^(−1/2), and let x_λ ∈ (0, x0/2) be
defined by env(v_s + x_λ) = λ^(5/2). Then every point v of the band satisfies v_s < v ≤ v_s + x_λ and

    (α c_R x_λ)^(−1/α) ≤ κ(v) ≤ κ̄_λ := max{(2/(α c_R x0))^(1/α), (2^(2+1/α) α c_R log(1/λ))^(1/(1−α))},
    κ(v) (v − v_s) ≥ (α c_R)^(−1/α) x_λ^(1−1/α).    (55.39)

As λ → 0, x_λ → 0 and λ κ̄_λ^j → 0 for every j ≥ 1. So κ and κ(v − v_s) tend to ∞ uniformly on the band, and for every
δ′ ∈ (0, 1) there is a threshold on λ below which λκ ≤ λ^(δ′) at every point of the band.

*Proof.* As log env is concave and differentiable, κ is nonincreasing and κ′ ≤ 0; and κ > 0 since env′ > 0. If κ
were bounded by a number B on (v_s, v_s + x0], then log env(v) ≥ log env(v_s + x0) − B x0 for every v there, against
env(v) → 0; so κ(t) → ∞ as t ↓ v_s. Now (κ^(−α))′ = −α κ^(−α−1) κ′ = α κ^(−α−1) |κ′| lies in [0, α c_R]. For v_s < t < v,
κ(v)^(−α) ≤ κ(t)^(−α) + α c_R (v − t), and letting t ↓ v_s gives (55.37).
For (55.38) put h := κ(v)^(−α)/(α c_R). If h > x0/2, then κ(v) < (2/(α c_R x0))^(1/α). Otherwise
v + h ≤ v_s + x0, and for v ≤ t ≤ v + h, κ(t)^(−α) ≤ κ(v)^(−α) + α c_R h = 2κ(v)^(−α), so κ(t) ≥ 2^(−1/α) κ(v). As env
is increasing,

    log(env(v_s + x0)/env(v)) ≥ ∫_v^(v+h) κ ≥ 2^(−1/α) κ(v) h = 2^(−1/α) κ(v)^(1−α)/(α c_R),

which is (55.38) in this case.
Let v be a point of the band. Then E(v) ≥ λ^(3+δ) > 0, so v > v_s. If v_s + x_λ < v ≤ v_s + x0, then E(v) ≥ env(v) >
env(v_s + x_λ) = λ^(5/2); if v > v_s + x0, then E(v) ≥ env(v_s + x0) > λ^(5/2). Both contradict E(v) ≤ λ^(3−δ) ≤ λ^(5/2),
so v ≤ v_s + x_λ, and env(v) = E(v) ≥ λ^(3+δ), as env is increasing on (v_s, v]. Hence log(env(v_s + x0)/env(v)) ≤
(1/2 + 3 + δ) log(1/λ) ≤ 4 log(1/λ), and (55.38) gives κ(v) ≤ κ̄_λ. The lower bounds of
(55.39) follow from (55.37) with x ≤ x_λ, since −1/α < 0 and 1 − 1/α < 0. Finally, env is
continuous and positive on (v_s, v_s + x0], so for every y in (0, x0/2) we have x_λ < y once λ^(5/2) < env(v_s + y);
and κ̄_λ grows like a power of log(1/λ), so λ κ̄_λ^j → 0 and λ^(1−δ′) κ̄_λ → 0. ∎

**Proposition 55.39** (The first-degree term against the margin.) Let (v, x̂) be a point at which
Lemma 55.35 applies with ς ≤ 10⁻³ (by Proposition 55.36, every point of the band once λ is below the thresholds
there), and suppose that

    |S′| ≤ 1.001 κ |S|,      |S| ≤ 1.001 R m0      at (v, x̂)    (55.40)

(by Proposition 55.40, at every point of the band with R ≥ 1/2 once λ is small). Then at (v, x̂)

    m0′ − |S′| ≥ (2 − 3ς/4 − 1.002001 R) κ m0 ≥ (1.99925 − 1.002001 R) κ m0;    (55.41)

in particular m0′ − |S′| ≥ 0.89 κ m0 where R ≤ 1.1, m0′ − |S′| ≥ 0.93 κ m0 where R ≤ 1.06, and m0′ − |S′| ≥ 0.99 κ m0
where R ≤ 1.005.

*Proof.* By (55.40), |S′| ≤ 1.001² κ R m0 = 1.002001 κ R m0, and by Lemma 55.35,
m0′ ≥ (2 − 3ς/4) κ m0; subtracting gives the first inequality, and 3ς/4 ≤ 0.00075 gives the second. Finally
1.99925 − 1.002001 · 1.1 = 0.8970489, 1.99925 − 1.002001 · 1.06 = 0.93712894 and 1.99925 − 1.002001 · 1.005 =
0.992238995. ∎

The two bounds (55.40) are the properties of S that the proof of Theorem 55.33 uses. They are needed only at
points where R lies near 1, and they follow there, for λ small, from the first-degree horizon value. We use it in the
following form. Let N ≥ 9 and let (H_N) of Definition 55.1 hold on (v_s, v_s + x0], with constants c_R > 0 and α
∈ (0, 1), and with x0 at most the x0′ of Proposition 55.17; put r0 := v − τ0, T := λ κ_(N−1), c_N := N
μ0/(r0² + μ0) and Λ := λ^(N−2) env^(N−1)/env. The first-degree horizon value, Proposition 55.17, gives, with a
constant C independent of λ, v and x̂, at every point (v, x̂) with v_s < v ≤ v_s + x0 and λκ(v) ≤ 1 (the factor ϵ′ +
1/κ + λ of (55.17) being bounded),

    S = S_st + S_U + E_S,      S_st := λ³ A ν(r0) d(ϑ) env (1 + 2iλκ),
    S_U := −λ^(N+1) A i^N d(ϑ) Γ_R(r0) Ξ env^(N−1),      Ξ := ((1 − c_N) T − i c_N)/(T + i),
    |E_S| + |E_S′|/κ ≤ C [λ³ env (|ν(r0)| (λκ)² + λ) + |S_U|],    (55.42)

where ν and Γ_R > 0 are real functions of r0, smooth near r0 = v_s − τ0, d is a bounded function of the polar angle ϑ,
and either ν(v_s − τ0) ≠ 0 or ν(v_s − τ0) = ν′(v_s − τ0) = 0 ≠ ν″(v_s − τ0). The factor |1 + 2iλκ| makes |S_st| = R m0
(1 + 4λ²κ²)^(1/2), so S_st carries R exactly; the work is to show that S_U and E_S, and their derivatives, are small
against R m0 and κ R m0.

**Proposition 55.40** (The first-degree amplitude where R ≥ 1/2.) Assume (55.42) with the
properties stated after it, and let 0 < δ ≤ 1/2. There is λ_S ∈ (0, 1), independent of v and x̂, such that for
0 < λ < λ_S, at every point (v, x̂) of the band with R(v, x̂) ≥ 1/2,

    0.999 κ |S| ≤ |S′| ≤ 1.001 κ |S|,      0.999 R m0 ≤ |S| ≤ 1.001 R m0.    (55.43)

In particular (55.40) holds at these points, and Λ ≤ λ and λκ ≤ λ^(δ′) (any fixed δ′ < 1) hold at every
point of the band once λ is small.

*Proof.* Put x := v − v_s. As Γ_R, ν and c_N are smooth near r0 = v_s − τ0 and d is bounded, there are x_1 > 0 and C such
that Γ_R, |Γ_R′|, |ν|, |c_N′| and |d| are at most C for 0 < x ≤ x_1, and c_N ≤ N everywhere. Moreover, after decreasing
x_1, |ν′(r0)| ≤ C (1 + 1/x) |ν(r0)| for 0 < x ≤ x_1: if ν(v_s − τ0) ≠ 0, take x_1 so small that |ν(r0)| ≥ |ν(v_s −
τ0)|/2; otherwise r0 − (v_s − τ0) = x, and Taylor's formula gives ν(r0) = (ν″(v_s − τ0)/2) x² (1 + O(x)) and ν′(r0) =
ν″(v_s − τ0) x (1 + O(x)), so x ν′/ν → 2 and |ν′/ν| ≤ 3/x for x small. Take λ below the thresholds of Proposition 55.36
and Lemma 55.38, with x_λ ≤ min(x_1, 1), α c_R x_λ ≤ 1 and λ κ̄_λ ≤ 1. Let (v, x̂) be a point of the band with R ≥
1/2. By Lemma 55.38, 0 < x ≤ x_λ, env(v) = E(v) lies in [λ^(3+δ), λ^(3−δ)] and 1 ≤ κ ≤ κ̄_λ, so λκ ≤ 1 and
(55.42) applies; by Proposition 55.36, ς ≤ 10⁻³. Put

    ε_λ := λ^(1−δ) (1 + λ κ̄_λ² + λ^(N−3) κ̄_λ^(N−1)) + λ κ̄_λ + x_λ^(1/α − 1),

which depends on λ alone and tends to 0 with λ, by Lemma 55.38. By (55.37) and x ≤ x_λ ≤ 1, 1/κ and
1/(κx) are at most (α c_R)^(1/α) x_λ^(1/α − 1); so 1/κ, 1/(κx) and λκ are at most Cε_λ. Below, C is independent of λ, v
and x̂ and may change from line to line.

*The size of |ν| |d|.* By (55.33), m0 ≥ a_2/κ = A² env²/(9 √μ0 p^(3/2)), and p^(3/2) ≤ (1 + ς/2)^(3/4) ≤ 10/9
by the proof of Lemma 55.35; so m0 ≥ A² env²/(10 √μ0). As R m0 = λ³ A env |ν(r0)| |d(ϑ)| and R ≥ 1/2,

    |ν(r0)| |d(ϑ)| ≥ A env/(20 √μ0 λ³) ≥ (A/(20 √μ0)) λ^δ,

and, |ν| and |d| being at most C, both |ν(r0)| and |d(ϑ)| are at least λ^δ/C. In particular ν(r0) ≠ 0.

*The size of S − S_st.* By (H_N), env^(N−1) = κ_0 κ_1 ⋯ κ_(N−2) env with 0 < κ_k ≤ 2κ, so Λ ≤ 2^(N−1) λ^(N−2) κ^(N−1) ≤
2^(N−1) λ^(N−2) κ̄_λ^(N−1) ≤ C ε_λ λ^δ, which is also at most λ for λ small. As |T + i| ≥ max(T, 1), |Ξ| ≤ |1 − c_N| +
c_N ≤ C, and Γ_R ≤ C; hence, with |ν| ≥ λ^δ/C,

    |S_U| ≤ C Λ λ³ A |d| env = C (Λ/|ν|) R m0 ≤ C ε_λ R m0.

Dividing the bound on E_S in (55.42) by R m0 = λ³ A env |ν| |d| and using the lower bounds on |d|
and |ν| |d|,

    |E_S| ≤ C [(λκ)²/|d| + λ/(|ν| |d|)] R m0 + C |S_U| ≤ C [λ^(2−δ) κ̄_λ² + λ^(1−δ) + ε_λ] R m0 ≤ C ε_λ R m0.

So |S − S_st| ≤ C ε_λ R m0. As R m0 ≤ |S_st| = R m0 (1 + 4λ²κ²)^(1/2) ≤ (1 + 2ε_λ²) R m0,

    (1 − C ε_λ) R m0 ≤ |S| ≤ (1 + 2ε_λ² + C ε_λ) R m0.    (55.44)

*The derivative.* At fixed x̂, d(ϑ) does not depend on v, and r0′ = 1. So S_st′ = S_st (κ + ν′/ν + 2iλκ′/(1 + 2iλκ)),
and with |ν′/ν| ≤ C (1 + 1/x) and |κ′| ≤ c_R κ^(1+α) ≤ c_R κ² (κ ≥ 1),

    |S_st′ − κ S_st| ≤ (C (1 + 1/x) + 2 c_R λκ²) |S_st| ≤ C ε_λ κ |S_st|,

since 1 + 1/x = κ (1/κ + 1/(κx)) and λκ² ≤ ε_λκ. In S_U, (env^(N−1))′ = κ_(N−1) env^(N−1) with κ_(N−1) ≤ 2κ; Ξ is affine
in c_N with ∂Ξ/∂c_N = −1, and ∂Ξ/∂T = i/(T + i)², so |Ξ′| ≤ |c_N′| + |T′| ≤ C + c_R λ (2κ)^(1+α) ≤ Cκ, by (H_N) for
κ_(N−1) and λκ^α ≤ λκ ≤ 1. Hence |(Γ_R Ξ env^(N−1))′| ≤ Cκ |env^(N−1)|, and |S_U′| ≤ C κ Λ λ³ A |d| env ≤ C ε_λ κ R m0.
By (55.42), |E_S′| is at most κ times the bound on |E_S| used above, so |E_S′| ≤ C ε_λ κ R m0. Since R m0
≤ |S_st| and, by (55.44), |S_st| ≤ |S| + C ε_λ R m0 ≤ |S| + C ε_λ |S_st|,

    | |S′| − κ |S| | ≤ |S′ − κ S| ≤ |S_st′ − κ S_st| + |S_U′| + κ |S_U| + |E_S′| + κ |E_S| ≤ C ε_λ κ |S|/(1 − C ε_λ).

As ε_λ → 0 with λ, this and (55.44) give (55.43) once λ is small. The bound Λ ≤ λ was shown
above, and λκ ≤ λ^(δ′) is Lemma 55.38. ∎

Where R is small the bounds are not claimed. The bound on E_S in (55.42) keeps the term C λ⁴ env, which
carries no factor |ν| |d|, while R m0 = λ³ A env |ν| |d|; so E_S need not be small against R m0 at points where |ν| |d|
is of order λ or smaller. The proof of Theorem 55.33 uses (55.40) only where R ∈ [1 − 2λ^γ, 1 + 2λ^γ], which
lies in [1/2, 1.1] once 2λ^γ ≤ 1/10. So, for λ small, the conclusions of Proposition 55.39 hold at every point of
the band with 1/2 ≤ R ≤ 1.1.

On the band, for λ small, R is strictly decreasing in v and varies little over two carrier periods. At fixed x̂ with
d(ϑ) ≠ 0, (log R)′ = κ + ν′/ν − m0′/m0. By Lemma 55.35 with ς ≤ 10⁻³ and √μ0 κ ≥ 2, 1.99925 κ ≤ m0′/m0 ≤
2.6 κ. As in the proof of Proposition 55.40, |ν′/ν| ≤ C(1 + 1/x) ≤ κ/10. So −1.7 κ ≤ (log R)′ ≤ −0.89 κ, and
log R varies by at most 7πλκ̄_λ on every interval of length 4πλ. Hence two consecutive carrier periods, one of which
meets {1 − 2λ^γ ≤ R ≤ 1 + 2λ^γ}, lie where 1/2 ≤ R ≤ 1.1 once λ is small. Along the band, the points with
R ≥ 1 + 2λ^γ precede those with |R − 1| < 2λ^γ, and these precede those with R ≤ 1 − 2λ^γ.

**Remark 55.41** (The factor 2 − R.) The constant 2 of Lemma 55.35 is approached as v ↓ v_s. Let env
be positive and log-concave on (v_s, v_s + x0] with env(v) → 0 as v ↓ v_s. Then κ is nonincreasing there and κ(v) → ∞ as
v ↓ v_s, since a finite limit B would give log env(v) ≥ log env(v_s + x0) − B x0 for every v in (v_s, v_s + x0]; so ς →
0, and both bounds of (55.31) tend to 2. So the constant 2 in (55.41) cannot be raised;
nor can the coefficient of R be lowered, as follows. If at (v, x̂) also |S′| ≥ 0.999 κ |S| (as for any constant multiple
of env, for which |S′| = κ|S|) and |S| ≥ 0.999 R m0, with ς ≤ 10⁻³ and √μ0 κ ≥ 10³, then (1 + ς/8)/(√μ0 κ) ≤ 1.001 ·
10⁻³, 0.999² ≥ 0.998, and the upper bound of (55.31) gives

    m0′ − |S′| ≤ (2.001001 − 0.998 R) κ m0,

which is 0.903201 κ m0 at R = 1.1 and below 0.93 κ m0 for every R ≥ 1.075. For such S no bound m0′ − |S′| ≥ 0.93 κ m0
holds on 1.075 ≤ R ≤ 1.1, and at R = 1.1 the constant 0.89 of Proposition 55.39 is within 0.014 of the best
constant for such S. The first-degree amplitude is such an S at every point of the band with R ≥ 1/2 once λ is small:
the reverse bounds are part of (55.43), ς ≤ 10⁻³ is Proposition 55.36, and √μ0 κ ≥ 10³ holds since κ
tends to ∞ uniformly on the band (Lemma 55.38).

**Corollary 55.42** (One carrier period.) Let t be real and I := [t, t + 2πλ]. Suppose that at every point
of I Proposition 55.39 applies with R ≤ 1.1 and √μ0 κ ≥ 2, and that

    2πλ sup_I (|κ′|/κ + 3κ) ≤ 1/26.    (55.45)

Then

    m0(t + 2πλ) − m0(t) + Re[(S(t + 2πλ) − S(t)) e^(it/λ)] ≥ 1.7 πλ κ(t) m0(t).    (55.46)

Under (H_N) on I with κ ≥ 1 there, |κ′|/κ ≤ c_R κ^α ≤ c_R κ, so (55.45) holds once
2π (c_R + 3) λ sup_I κ ≤ 1/26. For a carrier period I contained in the band on which 1/2 ≤ R ≤ 1.1, every hypothesis
holds once λ is small: Proposition 55.39 applies at each point of I by Proposition 55.36 and
Proposition 55.40; and by Lemma 55.38, (α c_R x_λ)^(−1/α) ≤ κ ≤ κ̄_λ on I, so √μ0 κ ≥ 2 and κ ≥ 1 once
x_λ is small, and 2π (c_R + 3) λ κ̄_λ ≤ 1/26 once λ is small.

*Proof.* By Lemma 55.35 with ς ≤ 10⁻³ and √μ0 κ ≥ 2,
0 < m0′/m0 ≤ (2 + 1.000125/2) κ ≤ 3κ. So |(log(κ m0))′| = |κ′/κ + m0′/m0| ≤ |κ′|/κ + 3κ, and by (55.45)
log(κ m0) varies by at most 1/26 on I. As e^y < 1/(1 − y) for 0 < y < 1, e^(1/26) < 26/25, so κ m0 ≥ (25/26) κ(t) m0(t)
on I. The left side of (55.46) is ∫_I (m0′(s) + Re[S′(s) e^(it/λ)]) ds ≥ ∫_I (m0′ − |S′|) ds, and by
Proposition 55.39 this is at least 0.89 · 2πλ · (25/26) κ(t) m0(t) ≥ 1.71 πλ κ(t) m0(t). ∎

**Remark 55.43** (The degree-two terms against the margin.) The proof of Theorem 55.33 bounds the degree-two
terms at the boundary through the costs ε_c(v) := Σ_(i≤c) sup_(v′≤v) |env^(i)(v′)| for fixed c ≥ 1, among them
c = M* := 2N + 8, the cost of the expansion on the boundary in Chapter 54. No bound m0 ≥ c′ ε_c² with c′ > 0
independent of λ holds in the band: there ε_c ≥ env′ = κ env, while by (55.33) and (55.32)
m0 = (a_1 + a_2)/κ ≤ (A² env²/(9 √μ0)) (1 + 1/(2 √μ0 κ)), so m0/ε_c² ≤ C/κ², which tends to 0 with λ by
Lemma 55.38. What holds, and suffices, is (54.29) of Corollary 54.24, applied
with m := 84c: its hypotheses are c ≥ 1, m ≥ 84c, λ ≤ 1 and λ^(3+δ) ≤ E(v) ≤ 1, and at a point of the band E(v) ≤
λ^(3−δ) ≤ 1. So at every point v of the band

    ε_c(v)² ≤ C λ^(−1/8) m0(v),    (55.47)

with C depending on c, A, μ0, μ(v_end) and sup |env^(84c)|, and not on λ or v.

*Proof of Theorem 55.33.* Take x0 at most the x0′ of Proposition 55.17, and λ below the thresholds of
Proposition 54.34 (iii), Proposition 55.36, Lemma 55.38, Proposition 55.40 and Corollary 55.42.
By Proposition 55.36 the band lies in (v_s, v_s + x0), and as env is increasing it is the interval on which λ^(3+δ) ≤
env ≤ λ^(3−δ), with E = env there. By Proposition 55.40, λκ ≤ λ^(δ′) and Λ ≤ λ on the band.

*The decomposition.* From g_λ = g_app + w and h^(1) = h_app^(1) + e, g_λ − g0 = h^(1) + (g_app − g0 − h_app^(1)) + (w −
e). At a boundary point X = (t, r_q(t), x̂), Lemma 54.14 and Proposition 55.17 give

    g_λ⁻¹(dΦ0, dΦ0) = −m0 − Re[S(t) e^(it/λ)] + ρ_s + ρ_r,      ρ_r := −(w − e)(Φ0♯, Φ0♯),

where ρ_s is the rest: −(g_app − g0 − h_app^(1))(Φ0♯, Φ0♯), the difference between h^(1)(Φ0♯, Φ0♯) and h^(1)_vv(t,
√μ0) (the shift from √μ0 to r_q and the β_Φ-terms), and q of Lemma 54.14. S has the form
(55.42), as λκ ≤ 1.

*The increments.* For t ∈ I_k write Δf := f(t + 2πλ) − f(t). As e^(i(t+2πλ)/λ) = e^(it/λ),

    Δ g_λ⁻¹(dΦ0, dΦ0) = −[Δm0 + Re(ΔS e^(it/λ))] + Δρ_s + Δρ_r.

Let I_k or I_(k+1) meet {|R − 1| ≤ 2λ^γ}. By the last paragraph of Section 55.13 both lie where 1/2 ≤ R ≤ 1.1,
and Corollary 55.42 gives Δm0 + Re(ΔS e^(it/λ)) ≥ 1.7πλκ(t) m0(t). We show |Δρ_s| + |Δρ_r| ≤ πλκ(t) m0(t)/2.
Then Δ g_λ⁻¹(dΦ0, dΦ0) ≤ −1.2πλκ m0 < 0 for every t ∈ I_k, so every value on I_(k+1) is below a value on I_k, and
M_(k+1) < M_k.

The points t, t + 2πλ and t + O(λ) used below lie in the band, R varying by o(1) over O(λ) there, and m0 varies by a
factor at most 2 over O(λ), since 0 < m0′/m0 ≤ 3κ (Lemma 55.35, as in the proof of Corollary 55.42) and
λκ → 0. By (55.47) at those points, ε_c² ≤ C λ^(−1/8) m0(t) for every fixed cost c. Moreover ε_c ≥ E ≥ λ^(3+δ)
and ε_c ≤ C E^(1−c/m) ≤ C λ² by (54.27).

(a) g_app − g0 − h_app^(1) = Σ_(j≤N) λ^j([g_j] − Re[H_j e^(iθ)]) − λ^(N+1) Re[H_(N+1) e^(iθ)] at θ = t/λ is a sum of λ^j
G_j(X, θ), G_j 2π-periodic in θ. At a fixed phase its increment is G_j(X(t + 2πλ), θ) − G_j(X(t), θ), at most 2πλ
sup |∂_X G_j| |dX/dt|, with |dX/dt| ≤ C on the boundary. By (54.22) with i = 1 and Lemma 54.18
(c), |∂_X G_j| ≤ C ε_c² for j ≤ N and |∂_X H_(N+1)| ≤ C ε_c. So this increment is at most C λ² ε_c² + C λ^(N+2) ε_c ≤ C
λ^(15/8) m0 + C λ^(N+2−3−δ−1/8) m0, using ε_c ≤ ε_c²/λ^(3+δ). The shift and the β_Φ-terms are at most C ε_0² ε_c ≤ C λ²
ε_c² (Corollary 54.20), and q at most C (λ² ε_c + λ ε_c² + |w|)², with |w| ≤ C λ^(N−5) ε_c
(Lemma 54.22); their increments are at most twice their sizes, C λ^(15/8) m0 at most.

(b) By Lemma 55.34, |Δρ_r| ≤ 2 sup |w − e| ≤ C(λ^(N−6) ε_c² + λ^(N−2) ε_c) ≤ C(λ^(N−6−1/8) + λ^(N−5.5−1/8))
m0.

As N ≥ 9 and κ ≥ 1 in the band, each of these is below πλκ m0/8 for λ small.

*The signs.* By Proposition 54.34 (iii), if R ≥ 1 + 2λ^γ at the midpoint of I_k, the boundary has timelike points
in I_k at x̂, so M_k > 0; and if R ≤ 1 − 2λ^γ on I_k, it is spacelike there, so M_k < 0.

*Exactly once.* Every period is of the first kind, or of the second, or meets {|R − 1| ≤ 2λ^γ}, by continuity of R. As R
is strictly decreasing along the band (the last paragraph of Section 55.13), the periods of the first kind precede
the others and those of the second kind follow them. Both kinds occur. At the left end of the band env = λ^(3+δ), and on
the first period env ≤ 2λ^(3+δ), as λκ → 0; there m0 ≤ (2A²/(9√μ0)) env² by the bound in Remark 55.43, so R ≥
(9√μ0 |ν| |d|/(2A)) λ³/env ≥ (6√μ0 |ν|/A) λ^(−δ), using |d| ≥ 8/3. Off ρ*, |ν| ≥ ν_*; at ρ*, |ν| ≥ c x² and x ≥ κ^(−α)/(α
c_R) ≥ κ̄_λ^(−α)/(α c_R) by Lemma 55.2 (a) and Lemma 55.38, a power of 1/log(1/λ). So R ≥ 2 on the first
period for λ small. At the right end env = λ^(3−δ), and on the last period env ≥ λ^(3−δ)/2; there m0 ≥ A² env²/(10√μ0)
(the proof of Proposition 55.40), so R ≤ (10√μ0 |ν| |d|/A) λ³/env ≤ C λ^δ ≤ 1/2. So the sequence (M_k) is positive
on the periods of the first kind, strictly decreasing from the last of them to the first period of the second kind, and
negative from there on: it changes sign exactly once. ∎

**Remark 55.44** (Numerical observation.) In a model of the band with exp(−1/x), λ = 10⁻⁶, a slowly
varying degree-two term of size λ^(1/10) m0 and an unstructured one of size λ³ m0, the maxima over 80 consecutive
carrier periods around R = 1 decreased strictly and changed sign once; with an unstructured term of size m0/3 they
changed sign more than once. No proof uses this observation.

### 55.14 Dips

Some regularity of the edge is needed for the conclusions of Theorem 55.22 and Theorem 55.11 at every level
below λ^(3+δ): for an envelope whose intervals of zeros accumulate at v_s the boundary is spacelike throughout some
intervals of length 4πλ below that level, for every small λ.

**Proposition 55.45** (Dips.) Let ϕ(t) := e^(−1/(1−t²)) for |t| < 1 and ϕ(t) := 0 otherwise, and near v_s
let

    env(v) := Σ_(n≥n0) h_n ϕ(s_n (v − v_s − 2^(−n))),      h_n := e^(−n²),      s_n := 2^(n+2),    (55.48)

continued to a C_c^∞ envelope; it is smooth and flat at v_s, as h_n s_n^k → 0 for every k. The bump n lives on v − v_s
∈ [3/4, 5/4] · 2^(−n), so env = 0 on J_n := v_s + (5/4, 3/2) · 2^(−n). Let δ ∈ (0, 1/2]. There is λ_25(δ) > 0 such that
for λ ≤ λ_25(δ), with n the least index with h_n ≤ λ^(3+δ), at every x̂ ∈ S³ and every v ∈ J_n′ := v_s + [(5/4)2^(−n),
(3/2)2^(−n) − ρ_w], ρ_w = O(λ) the reach of Lemma 54.22 (resp. Lemma 54.32),

    g_λ⁻¹(dΦ0, dΦ0)(v, r_q(v), x̂) ≤ −m0(v)/2 < 0,

for the metric of Theorem 3.1, K ≥ 6, and for that of Theorem 3.7. J_n′ lies in the layer, below the
level λ^(3+δ) (E = h_n/e there), and is longer than 4πλ. So for this envelope, for every small λ, intervals of length
4πλ below λ^(3+δ) on which the boundary is spacelike throughout occur on every column.

*Proof.* Fix v ∈ J_n′ and x̂, and put X := (v, r_q(v), x̂), v1 := v + ρ_w and L := log(1/λ).

(1) *The oscillating profiles vanish at X.* W, χ, the ĝ_m and the phase terms of the fixed-phase rewriting solve, at
fixed v, transports along ℓ whose forcing terms and data at that v are polynomials in env^(k)(v) and in the oscillating
profiles at that v, every monomial with an oscillating factor ((F1) of Section 54.8, and step (i) of the proof of
Lemma 7.4); this is the argument of the proof of Proposition 3.5 outside the shell, applied at a v with
env^(k)(v) = 0 for every k. By induction on the order they vanish at X. The phases φ_m, which the means drive, enter
g_app only through the phase of the oscillating profiles. So at X, g_λ − g0 = Σ_(j≥1) λ^j m_j + w. The same holds for
the stages of Theorem 9.10, which are transports at fixed v from past null infinity.

(2) *Bounds.* With B_k := Σ_(i≤k) sup |ϕ^(i)|, ε_k(v1) ≤ 2 h_n s_n^k B_k: the bump n − 1 starts at (3/2)2^(−n), beyond
v1, and the bumps m > n add at most h_n s_n^k B_k, as h_(m+1) s_(m+1)^k ≤ h_m s_m^k/2 once e^(2m+1) ≥ 2^(k+1). By
Lemma 54.18 (b) (by Lemma 54.31 for the metric of Theorem 3.7), |m_j| ≤ C ε_(2j+1)(v)².
By Lemma 54.22, for the metric of Theorem 3.1, |w| ≤ C λ^(N−5) ε_(M*)(v1) given ε_4(v1) ≤ λ; by
Lemma 54.32, for the metric of Theorem 3.7, |w| ≤ C λ^(N_P−3) ε_(M_P)(v1) given
ε_(M_P)(v1) ≤ λ³. Both hypotheses hold for λ small, since h_n ≤ λ^(3+δ) and s_n^k B_k = e^(O(L^(1/2))).

(3) *The margin.* m0 ≥ √(μ/μ0) − 1 ≥ (μ − μ0)/(3μ0), as √x − 1 = (x − 1)/(√x + 1) and μ ≤ 4μ0 in the layer, so

    m0(v) ≥ (2A²/(27μ0)) ∫_(v_s)^v env² ≥ (2A²/(27μ0)) h_n² s_n⁻¹ I_ϕ,      I_ϕ := ∫_(−1)^1 ϕ².

(4) *The ratio.* Lemma 54.14 with k = g_λ − g0 gives |g_λ⁻¹(dΦ0, dΦ0) + m0| ≤ C|k| ≤ C′(max_(j≤N) λ^j
ε_(2j+1)(v)² + λ^(N−5) ε_(M*)(v1)) for the metric of Theorem 3.1, and the same with N_P, M_P and λ^(N_P−3) for the
metric of Theorem 3.7. Its ratio to the bound of (3) is at most

    C″ (max_(j≤N) λ^j s_n^(4j+3) B_(2j+1)² + λ^(N−5) h_n⁻¹ s_n^(M*+1) B_(M*)).

Since h_(n−1) > λ^(3+δ), h_n = h_(n−1) e^(−(2n−1)) > λ^(3+δ) e^(−(2n−1)), and n ≤ ((3 + δ)L)^(1/2) + 1; so h_n ≥
λ^(3.4+δ) once 2((3 + δ)L)^(1/2) + 1 ≤ 0.4L, that is for λ ≤ λ_h(δ) := exp(−y_h²), y_h := (2(3 + δ)^(1/2) + (4(3 + δ) +
1.6)^(1/2))/0.8; for instance λ_h(1/10) = 10^(−35.79…) and λ_h(1/2) = 10^(−40.14…). Then the ratio is at most C″ (max_j
λ^j s_n^(4j+3) B_(2j+1)² + λ^(N−8.4−δ) s_n^(M*+1) B_(M*)), which tends to 0 as λ → 0, since N − 8.4 − δ ≥ 0.1 for N ≥ 9
and δ ≤ 1/2, and s_n = 2^(n+2) grows slower than every power of 1/λ; for the metric of Theorem 3.7 the
exponent is N_P − 6.4 − δ. Let λ_25(δ) be the least of λ_h(δ) and the thresholds below which the hypotheses of (2) and
(4)'s ratio ≤ 1/2 hold. Then g_λ⁻¹(dΦ0, dΦ0) ≤ −m0 + m0/2.

Finally, sup_(v′≤v) env = h_n ϕ(0) = h_n/e ≤ λ^(3+δ) on J_n′, the layer contains J_n′ for λ small (μ − μ0 there is
of order h_n², against 4μ0 C_Φ λ, as in the proof of Theorem 54.26), and J_n′ has length at least 2^(−n−3) ≫ 4πλ. ∎

**Remark 55.46** (Where the ratio decides.) At a boundary point in the deep layer write g_λ⁻¹(dΦ0, dΦ0) =
−m0 − Re[S e^(iv/λ)] + ρ with |ρ| ≤ D(v), where (S, D) is the following: on a zero interval as in Proposition 55.45,
S := 0 and D the bound of its step (4), the first-degree terms being part of w there; in the band λ^(3+δ) ≤ E ≤
λ^(3−δ), S the first-degree amplitude of Proposition 54.34 (iii) and D ≤ λ^γ m0; on an edge where (H_N), (H_D) and
(B_(c′)) hold, S of Proposition 55.17 (for the metric of Theorem 3.1) or of Lemma 55.10 (for that
of Theorem 3.7) and D = C κ^(2c′) env². On an interval J = [v, v + 4πλ] on which S varies little, the
boundary has timelike points at x̂ if max_J (|S| − m0) ≥ C(λ^γ m0 + D), and none if max_J (|S| + D) < min_J m0, since
g_λ⁻¹(dΦ0, dΦ0) ≤ −m0 + |S| + D. So the ratio |S|/m0 decides up to the factor 1 ± 2λ^γ in the band, a zero interval as in
Proposition 55.45 is spacelike, and the very edge of Theorem 55.11 and Theorem 55.22 has timelike points; where
env > 0 and no listed D is below m0, at a dip of a general envelope, the criterion decides nothing.

**Remark 55.47** (Numerical observation.) The three terms of step (4) of the proof of
Proposition 55.45 were evaluated in log10 with unit constants (A = μ0 = 1, every constant of the lemmas 1). At δ = 1/10
the ratio for the metric of Theorem 3.1 was +221, −86, −6544, −82950 and −877515 in log10 at λ = 10^(−10²), …,
10^(−10⁶), and at δ = 1/2 it was +286, +335, −2578, −42399 and −476461: the decay λ^(0.1) wins only from λ about
10^(−10⁴) on. The ratios for the metric of Theorem 3.7 and of the means were negative throughout. With the
zero intervals removed, or with the bump heights h_n near λ⁴, the ratio became large. No proof uses these figures.

### 55.15 The thresholds

**Remark 55.48** (What the thresholds are.) The thresholds λ_E, λ_1E, λ_26, λ_28 and λ_24 of this
chapter depend only on the constants of Chapter 7, Chapter 6 and Chapter 9, on the bounds
of the stage profiles, and on the envelope's constants of Definition 55.1, and so does λ_D, which the proof of
Lemma 55.8 writes in terms of them; they are not evaluated. The constants C_L11 and C_L4 of the threshold
λ_L of Theorem 54.26 ((54.35)) are not evaluated (Remark 54.39);
Lemma 55.49 writes them, and the threshold λ_P of Theorem 3.7, in terms of the constants
of the results they come from.

The threshold λ_25(δ) of Proposition 55.45 is explicit. Write λ = 10^(−E) and s := ((3 + δ) ln 10)^(1/2), so that n +
2 ≤ s E^(1/2) + 3. With h_n ≥ λ^(3.4+δ) (for λ ≤ λ_h(δ)) and ε_k(v1) ≤ 2h_n s_n^k B_k, each condition of the proof
reads −aE + b E^(1/2) + c + 𝔤 ≤ log10 𝔮 and holds for every E ≥ E_i := y₊², y₊ := (b + (b² + 4a(c + 𝔤 − log10
𝔮))^(1/2))/(2a). For the remainder of the metric of Theorem 3.1, a = N − 8.4 − δ, b = (M* + 1) s log10 2, c =
log10(27/I_ϕ) + log10 B_(M*) + 3(M* + 1) log10 2 and 𝔮 = 1/4; for its means, each j ≤ N, a = j and 𝔮 = 1/(4N); the
same for the metric of Theorem 3.7 with N_P and M_P; for the hypotheses ε_4(v1) ≤ λ and ε_(M_P)(v1) ≤ λ³
of the remainder lemmas, a = 2 + δ and a = δ; and λ ≤ λ_h(δ), e^(2n+1) ≥ 2^(M_P+1), and the length of J_n′. Here 𝔤 is
log10 of a product of the constant of Lemma 54.14, that of the remainder lemma or of Lemma 54.18 (b),
μ0 and A⁻², and for the length of J_n′ 𝔤 = log10(4π + C_ρ), C_ρ λ := ρ_w. Then

    λ_25(δ) = min(λ_rec, 10^(−E_25(δ))),      E_25(δ) := max_i E_i(δ),

λ_rec the threshold below which the lemmas used hold. The constants in 𝔤 and λ_rec are not evaluated, but the condition
ε_(M_P)(v1) ≤ λ³ involves none of them: there a = δ ≤ 1/2, b = M_P s log10 2 and c = 3M_P log10 2 + log10(2B_(M_P)), with
𝔮 = 1 and 𝔤 = 0. Its threshold gives an upper bound for λ_25(δ) whatever the other constants are
(Proposition 55.50); no proof uses it.

**Lemma 55.49** (The constants of the layer.) Let N = K + 3, ε := ε_(M*)(v) and Δτ := τ_end − τ0.

(a) Let C_H(j) and C_I(j), 1 ≤ j ≤ N, be constants with |H_j| ≤ C_H(j) ε and |g_j − Re[H_j e^(iθ)]| ≤ C_I(j) ε² at
the points of Ω with v ≤ v_♯ (Lemma 54.18 (c) and (54.22) at order zero), C′_H one with the
bound C′_H ε for |∂_r H_3| there, and put C_β := (A²/(9μ0))(1 + (μ0 μ(v_end))^(1/4)/2) and C_r := A²/(18√μ0). Then the
three bounds of (54.23) hold with

    C_L11 := (1 + 2C_β)² max{ Σ_(j=1)^N λ0^(j−1) (C_H(j) + C_I(j)),  Σ_(j=2)^N λ0^(j−2) C_H(j),
                              Σ_(j=4)^N λ0^(j−4) C_H(j),
                              Σ_(j=1)^N λ0^(j−1) C_I(j) + λ0² (C′_H C_r + (2 + C_β) C_β C_H(3)),  1 }.

(b) Let C_en be the constant of the energy inequality of step 6 of the proof of Lemma 54.21 (that of
Lemma 5.5 with the coefficient bounds of step 3, Gronwall's inequality included), C_L a constant with L_ij ≤ C_L
λ^(j−i) in the proof of Lemma 54.22, C_D(i) constants with E^(i)(τ0) ≤ C_D(i) λ^(N−3−i) ε_(M*)(v1) for
the data of step 5, C_d one with |∂^i Ric^H(g_app)| ≤ C_d λ^(N−1−i) ε_(M*)(v1) (Lemma 54.18 (d), i ≤ 2), V_Σ the
largest volume of a slice Σ_τ, and C_S the constant of step 7. Put Ĉ_0 := C_en (C_D(0) + Δτ V_Σ^(1/2) C_d) and, for i =
1, 2, Ĉ_i := C_en (C_D(i) + Δτ V_Σ^(1/2) C_d + Δτ C_L Σ_(j<i) Ĉ_j). Then Lemma 54.22 holds with

    C_L4 := C_S (Ĉ_0 + Ĉ_1 + Ĉ_2).

(c) λ_P is the least of λ1 and d0/20 (Section 9.2), of the thresholds of Proposition 9.11, of
Proposition 9.12 and of the limit, and of the threshold of Theorem 6.1 with this K applied on Ω in
Section 9.5. Written out with the constants named in those proofs: λ ≤ 1/C in the data bound of
Proposition 9.11, C λ ≤ ε_P/2 for the margin of Lemma 9.1 (f) under the bootstrap bound there, and λ^(K′−5)
≤ (4 C² e^(6C) M_F)⁻¹, which closes C e^(6C) C M_F² λ^(2K′−5) ≤ M_F λ^(K′)/4 there; in Proposition 9.12, C″ λ ≤ 1/8
for the nonlinear terms, the absorption of the terms with a profile g_j, j ≥ 3, each carrying a factor λ, and the
margin; and in Section 9.5, the hypothesis Data(w_n) ≤ C M_N λ^(K′−2β0−1) of Theorem 6.1.

*Proof.* (a) At a boundary point X, k = Σ_(j≤N) λ^j [g_j] + w (Corollary 54.20). By concavity of the root, the
modulus of β_Φ is at most (μ − μ0)/(2μ0) + r_q μ′/(4μ0) ≤ C_β ε², since μ − μ0 ≤ (2/9) A² (v − v_s) ε_0² with v − v_s ≤
1, μ′ = (2/9) A² env² and r_q ≤ (μ0 μ(v_end))^(1/4); and r_q − √μ0 ≤ (μ − μ0)/(4√μ0) ≤ C_r ε². In Cartesian components
Φ0♯ = (1 − β_Φ) ∂_τ + β_Φ x̂·∂_x, so |Φ0♯|_e ≤ 1 + 2|β_Φ| ≤ 1 + 2C_β, as ε ≤ 1. The bound for |k| is Σ_j λ^j (C_H(j) ε +
C_I(j) ε²) + |w| ≤ λε Σ_j λ0^(j−1) (C_H(j) + C_I(j)) + |w|. For k(Φ0♯, ·): H_1 has only angular components, so H_1(Φ0♯,
·) = 0, and |H_j(Φ0♯, ·)| ≤ (1 + 2C_β) C_H(j) ε for j ≥ 2; the rest is as for |k|, times 1 + 2C_β. For k(Φ0♯, Φ0♯): H_1
and H_2 lie in 𝔖 (Proposition 54.12), so H_j(Φ0♯, Φ0♯) = 0 for j ≤ 2; and H_3(Φ0♯, Φ0♯) is H_3,vv(v, √μ0) +
(H_3,vv(v, r_q) − H_3,vv(v, √μ0)) + 2β_Φ H_3,vr + β_Φ² H_3,rr, where the first term is A env d ν(v − τ0)
(Proposition 54.12 (d)), the second is at most C′_H ε C_r ε², and the last two at most (2 + C_β) C_β C_H(3) ε³; the
terms j ≥ 4 are at most λ⁴ ε Σ_(j≥4) λ0^(j−4) C_H(j) (1 + 2C_β)²; and the degree-two parts and w contribute λ ε² Σ_j
λ0^(j−1) C_I(j) (1 + 2C_β)² + (1 + 2C_β)² |w|. Each coefficient is at most C_L11.

(b) In the triangular argument of the proof of Lemma 54.22, E^(i)(τ) ≤ C_en (E^(i)(τ0) + ∫_(τ0)^(τ)
(‖∂^i Ric^H(g_app)‖ + Σ_(j<i) L_ij E^(j))), with ‖∂^i Ric^H(g_app)‖ ≤ V_Σ^(1/2) C_d λ^(N−1−i) ε_(M*)(v1). By induction
on i, E^(i) ≤ Ĉ_i λ^(N−3−i) ε_(M*)(v1), since λ^(N−1−i) ≤ λ^(N−3−i) and L_ij λ^(N−3−j) ≤ C_L λ^(N−3−i). Step 7
gives |w(X)| ≤ C_S Σ_(i≤2) E^(i) ≤ C_S (Ĉ_0 λ² + Ĉ_1 λ + Ĉ_2) λ^(N−5) ε_(M*)(v1) ≤ C_L4 λ^(N−5) ε_(M*)(v1), as λ ≤ 1.

(c) Each condition listed is the place where the proof named says "for λ small" or "for λ ≤ λ_N", written as the
inequality it needs; the other steps of those proofs hold for every λ ≤ min(λ1, d0/20). ∎

**Proposition 55.50** (An upper bound for the threshold of the dips.) For every δ ∈ (0, 1/2] and every
K ≥ 6, the threshold λ_25(δ) of Remark 55.48, the one the proof of Proposition 55.45 delivers, satisfies
λ_25(δ) ≤ 10^(−6282). This bounds that threshold; it says nothing about the largest λ for which the conclusion of
Proposition 55.45 holds.

*Proof.* Let E_H be the threshold E_i of the condition ε_(M_P)(v1) ≤ λ³ in Remark 55.48, so that λ_25(δ) ≤
10^(−E_25(δ)) ≤ 10^(−E_H). As a = δ, 𝔮 = 1 and 𝔤 = 0, E_H = y₊² with

    y₊ = b/(2δ) + (b²/(4δ²) + c/δ)^(1/2),      b = M_P log10 2 (ln 10)^(1/2) (3 + δ)^(1/2),
    c = 3M_P log10 2 + log10 2 + log10 B_(M_P).

(1) *Reduction to δ = 1/2 and M_P = 44.* y₊ increases with b and with c. M_P = 2N_P + 8 with N_P = K + 4 + ⌈4β0⌉ and
β0 ≥ 2 (Proposition 9.12, Section 9.5), so N_P ≥ K + 12 ≥ 18 and M_P ≥ 44; b and c increase with M_P, B_k
being nondecreasing in k. The function (3 + δ)^(1/2)/(2δ) decreases on (0, 1/2], its derivative being (δ − 2(3 + δ))/
(4δ²(3 + δ)^(1/2)) < 0, so b/(2δ) is at least its value at δ = 1/2; and c/δ ≥ 2c. Hence

    y₊ ≥ b₁ + (b₁² + 2c₁)^(1/2),      b₁ := 44 log10 2 (3.5 ln 10)^(1/2),      c₁ := 133 log10 2 + log10 B_44.

(2) *A lower bound for B_44.* ϕ vanishes on [1, ∞), so ϕ and all its derivatives vanish at t = 1, and Taylor's formula
at 1 with integral remainder gives, for 0 < t < 1, ϕ(t) = ∫_1^t ((t − u)^43/43!) ϕ^(44)(u) du, hence ϕ(t) ≤
sup|ϕ^(44)| (1 − t)^44/44!. At t = 87/88, 1 − t² = 175/7744, and so

    B_44 ≥ sup|ϕ^(44)| ≥ 44! 88^44 e^(−7744/175).

Here 44! = 2658271574788448768043625811014615890319638528000000000 ≥ 2.6582 · 10^54, so log10 44! ≥ 54 + log10 2.6582 ≥
54.4245; 44 log10 88 ≥ 85.5572; and 7744/(175 ln 10) ≤ 19.2182, as ln 10 ≥ 2.302585. So log10 B_44 ≥ 120.7635.

(3) *The number.* With log10 2 ≥ 0.301029, c₁ ≥ 40.0368 + 120.7635 ≥ 160.79; with (3.5 ln 10)^(1/2) ≥ 2.838846 (its
square is below 8.059047 < 3.5 · 2.302585 = 8.0590475), b₁ ≥ 44 · 0.301029 · 2.838846 ≥ 37.601. Then

    y₊ ≥ 37.601 + (37.601² + 2 · 160.79)^(1/2) ≥ 37.601 + (1735.415)^(1/2) ≥ 37.601 + 41.6583 = 79.2593,

as 41.6583² ≤ 1735.414, and E_H ≥ 79.2593² ≥ 6282.03. ∎

## 56. The threshold λ0 at a numerical point

The threshold λ0 of Theorem 3.1 is not evaluated. This chapter bounds it from above at one choice of the parameters,
the numerical point of Definition 56.1. The proof of Theorem 3.1 takes λ0 so small that C λ0 ≤ ε1, where the
solution satisfies |g_λ − g0| ≤ C λ on Ω. The constant C is at least the size of the first-order profile g1 at the
point where the wave is largest, and ε1 is limited by the distance from g0 to degenerate forms. Both depend on how |·|
is read on symmetric 2-tensors, and the bound is proved in three readings: the operator norm, the Frobenius norm and
the largest absolute entry (Proposition 56.8).

On the way we prove the constants on which these bounds rest: those of the domain at the point (Lemma 56.2),
the envelope constant c_e (Lemma 56.3), whose lower end c_e > 1 is also what Remark 54.39
uses, and ε1 and C_app in the three readings (Proposition 56.6); the admissible range of ε1 there is that of
Section 2.5. Every number below outside Remark 56.9 is justified by an inequality between explicit rationals,
or by the value of an elementary function at a rational point, and can be checked by hand. The last section also records
a numerical value of the first stage's mean correction at the point where the wave is largest, which would sharpen the
bounds and which no proof uses (Remark 56.9).

### 56.1 The numerical point

**Definition 56.1** (The numerical point.) The numerical point is l5 = 1/10, μ0 = 1, A = 1, T = 1,
τ0 = −2, the envelope env of Lemma 56.3, with v_start = 1/2 and v_end = 7/2, and a = δ0 = q0/2. Then
V = v_end + T = 9/2, and μ' = (2/9) A² env² ((2.14)).

These parameters satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1: l5, A and T are positive; μ0 = 1 > √72 l5² = √72/100, since 72
< 10⁴; v_start − τ0 = 5/2 > √μ0 + 1 = 2; env ∈ C_c^∞([1/2, 7/2]) by Lemma 56.3 (a); and 0 < δ0 = q0/2 <
q0. As μ0 > √72 l5², the point is not one of equality, and Theorem 54.26 does not apply there.

**Lemma 56.2** (The domain at the numerical point.) At the numerical point:

(a) q0⁸ = 9/1250, 0.539717577 < q0 < 0.539717578, 0.2698587885 < a < 0.269858789, and μ0/a² = 4/q0² > 13;

(b) μ_end = 227/192 and 1.042752 < μ_end^(1/4) < 1.042753;

(c) q_end := q0 μ_end^(1/4), the value of r_q at v = V, lies in (0.5627915, 0.5627922), and
V − q_end ≤ τ_end ≤ V − q0;

(d) m* := sup_Ω μ/r² equals μ_end/a² = (227/48) q0⁻², lies in (16.23497014, 16.23497021), and is attained at the
corner τ = τ_end, r = a of Ω;

(e) v − r_q(v) increases in v, so τ_end = V − q_end.

*Proof.* (a) q0 = (√72 μ0 l5²)^(1/4) gives q0⁸ = 72/10⁴ = 9/1250 = 0.0072. Three squarings give
0.539717577⁸ < 0.0072 < 0.539717578⁸, and a = q0/2. Then μ0/a² = 4/q0² > 4/0.539717578² > 13.73.

(b) μ_end = μ0 + (2/9) A² ∫ env² = 1 + (2/9)(105/128) = 227/192 by Lemma 56.3 (a), and
1.042752⁴ < 227/192 < 1.042753⁴.

(c) r_q(v) = q0 μ(v)^(1/4), as μ0 = 1, and μ(V) = μ_end since V > 7/2, so r_q(V) = q_end; the bounds on q_end are
the products of those in (a) and (b). As τ_end is the maximum of v − r_q(v) over v ≤ V, τ_end ≥ V − q_end. As
μ ≥ μ0 = 1, r_q ≥ q0, so v − r_q(v) ≤ V − q0 for v ≤ V, and τ_end ≤ V − q0.

(d) On Ω, μ ≤ μ_end and r ≥ a, so μ/r² ≤ μ_end/a² = (227/192)(4/q0²). The corner τ = τ_end, r = a lies in Ω: by (c),
τ0 = −2 < V − q_end ≤ τ_end, and there v + τ − τ_end = v = τ_end + a ≤ V − q0 + a < V + 1. At the corner, by (c) and
(a), v = τ_end + a ≥ 9/2 − q_end + a > 4.2 > v_end, so μ = μ_end. The bounds follow from (a):
(227/48)/0.539717578² > 16.23497014 and (227/48)/0.539717577² < 16.23497021.

(e) r_q' = (q0/4) μ^(−3/4) μ' ≤ (q0/4)(2/9) c_e² < 0.06, using μ ≥ 1 and env ≤ c_e < 1.33
(Lemma 56.3). So v − r_q(v) increases, its maximum over v ≤ V is at v = V, and τ_end = V − q_end. ∎

### 56.2 The envelope and its constant

Put, for y ∈ ℝ,

    β(y) := cos¹²(πy/2) exp(−y²/(1 − y²))  for |y| < 1,     β(y) := 0  for |y| ≥ 1,
    I := ∫_(−1)^1 β(y)² dy,      c_e := (35/(64 I))^(1/2),      env(v) := c_e β((2v − 4)/3).    (56.1)

This is the envelope env_C of Remark 3.2, and c_e is the constant written c there.

**Lemma 56.3** (The envelope constant.) (a) env ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ) with support [1/2, 7/2],
∫ env² = 105/128, and max env = env(2) = c_e. With μ' = (2/9) A² env² and μ = μ0 before v = 1/2, μ is smooth,
nondecreasing, constant outside [1/2, 7/2], and μ_end = μ0 + (2/9) A² (105/128).

(b) 0.3119281 < I < 0.3119286, and therefore

    1.3240867 < c_e < 1.3240879;   in particular   1.3240711 < c_e < 1.3241035.    (56.2)

*Proof.* (a) exp(−y²/(1 − y²)) = e · exp(−1/(1 − y²)), so β = e cos¹²(πy/2) φ(1 − y²) with φ(t) = exp(−1/t) for t > 0
and φ(t) = 0 for t ≤ 0. For t > 0, φ^(k)(t) = P_k(1/t) exp(−1/t) with P_0 = 1 and P_(k+1)(x) = x² (P_k(x) − P_k'(x)),
by induction from d/dt [P(1/t) e^(−1/t)] = t⁻² (P − P')(1/t) e^(−1/t); since P_k(x) e^(−x) → 0 as x → ∞, every
derivative of φ tends to 0 at 0+, and φ ∈ C^∞(ℝ). Composition with 1 − y² and the product with cos¹² keep C^∞, and
β > 0 exactly on |y| < 1, so env has support [1/2, 7/2]. The substitution y = (2v − 4)/3 gives ∫ env² = (3/2) c_e² I =
(3/2)(35/64) = 105/128. Since 0 ≤ β ≤ 1 = β(0), max env = c_e at v = 2. The statements on μ follow from μ' ≥ 0.

(b) *The substitution.* Put y = tanh s. Then dy = sech² s ds, 1 − y² = sech² s and y²/(1 − y²) = sinh² s, so

    I = ∫_ℝ G(s) ds,        G(s) := cos²⁴((π/2) tanh s) exp(−2 sinh² s) sech² s.

G is even, positive, and decreasing on [0, ∞), each of its three factors being so.

*Bounds in a strip.* G extends holomorphically to |Im s| < π/4. Let s = x + it with x real and |t| ≤ d < π/4. From
tanh(x + it) = (sinh 2x + i sin 2t)/(cosh 2x + cos 2t) one has |Im tanh s| ≤ sin 2|t|/(1 + cos 2t) = tan |t| ≤ tan d;
with |cos w|² = cos²(Re w) + sinh²(Im w) ≤ cosh²(Im w) this gives |cos²⁴((π/2) tanh s)| ≤ cosh²⁴((π/2) tan d). From
sinh s = sinh x cos t + i cosh x sin t, Re sinh² s = sinh² x cos 2t − sin² t, so |exp(−2 sinh² s)| ≤
exp(2 sin² d − 2 cos(2d) sinh² x). And |cosh s|² = sinh² x + cos² t ≥ cos² d. Since sinh² x ≥ x²,

    ∫_ℝ |G(x + it)| dx ≤ M_d := cosh²⁴((π/2) tan d) e^(2 sin² d) sec² d (π/(2 cos 2d))^(1/2),    (56.3)

and |G(x + it)| → 0 as |x| → ∞ uniformly in |t| ≤ d.

*The trapezoidal rule.* Let Ĝ(ω) := ∫_ℝ G(s) e^(−iωs) ds. Moving the line of integration to Im s = −d sgn ω, which
Cauchy's theorem on long rectangles allows by the uniform decay, gives |Ĝ(ω)| ≤ M_d e^(−d|ω|) by (56.3).
We use the Poisson summation formula in the following form: if G is continuous and integrable on ℝ, h > 0, the series
Σ_(n∈ℤ) G(x + nh) converges uniformly for x ∈ [0, h], and Σ_(k∈ℤ) |Ĝ(2πk/h)| < ∞, then h Σ_(n∈ℤ) G(nh) =
Σ_(k∈ℤ) Ĝ(2πk/h). Indeed, F(x) := Σ_(n∈ℤ) G(x + nh) is then continuous and h-periodic, and integration term by term
gives its Fourier coefficients (1/h) ∫_0^h F(x) e^(−2πikx/h) dx = (1/h) Ĝ(2πk/h). These are absolutely summable, so
the Fourier series of F converges uniformly to a continuous h-periodic function with the same Fourier coefficients as
F; that function is F, since a continuous periodic function is determined by its Fourier coefficients (Fejér's
theorem), and at x = 0 this is the formula. The hypotheses hold here. G is continuous, and 0 < G(s) ≤ e^(−2s²) since
cos²⁴((π/2) tanh s) ≤ 1, sech² s ≤ 1 and sinh² s ≥ s², so G is integrable. As G is even and decreasing on [0, ∞), for
x ∈ [0, h] one has G(x + nh) ≤ G(nh) ≤ e^(−2n²h²) when n ≥ 0 and G(x + nh) ≤ G((|n| − 1)h) ≤ e^(−2(|n| − 1)²h²) when
n ≤ −1, a summable majorant independent of x; and Σ_k |Ĝ(2πk/h)| ≤ Σ_k M_d e^(−2πd|k|/h) < ∞. Hence, as Ĝ(0) = I,
for every h > 0

    T_h := h Σ_(n∈ℤ) G(nh) = Σ_(k∈ℤ) Ĝ(2πk/h),     |T_h − I| ≤ 2 M_d Σ_(k≥1) e^(−2πkd/h) = 2 M_d/(e^(2πd/h) − 1).

Take d = 1/2 and h = 1/8, so 2πd/h = 8π and e^(8π) > 8.2 · 10¹⁰. The four factors of M_(1/2) are
cosh((π/2) tan(1/2)) = 1.39134…, whose 24th power is below 2770, e^(2 sin²(1/2)) < 1.5836, sec²(1/2) < 1.2985 and
(π/(2 cos 1))^(1/2) < 1.7051. So M_(1/2) < 9720 and |T_(1/8) − I| < 2.4 · 10⁻⁷.

*The nodes.* The values of G at the nodes, each within 5 · 10⁻¹³ of the printed decimal, are

    G(0) = 1,                    G(1/8) = 0.601818088179,     G(2/8) = 0.133828260085,
    G(3/8) = 0.011630921782,     G(4/8) = 0.000428710754,     G(5/8) = 0.000007358228,
    G(6/8) = 0.000000064420,     G(7/8) = 0.000000000311.

For s ≥ 1, cos((π/2) tanh s) ≤ cos((π/2) tanh 1) < 0.366 and sech² s ≤ 1, sinh² s ≥ s², so
G(s) ≤ 0.366²⁴ e^(−2s²), and since n²/32 ≥ n/4 for n ≥ 8,

    Σ_(n≥8) G(n/8) ≤ 0.366²⁴ Σ_(n≥8) e^(−n/4) = 0.366²⁴ e^(−2)/(1 − e^(−1/4)) < 3 · 10⁻¹¹.

The seven printed values for n = 1, …, 7 sum to 0.747713403759, so T_(1/8) = (1/8)(1 + 2 Σ_(n≥1) G(n/8)) lies in
(0.31192835093, 0.31192835095 + 10⁻¹¹). With the error bound, 0.3119281 < I < 0.3119286.

*The constant.* c_e² = 35/(64 I). Now 1.3240867² · 64 · 0.3119286 < 35 < 1.3240879² · 64 · 0.3119281, which is
(56.2). ∎

**Remark 56.4** (Which end of c_e each bound uses.) The two ends of (56.2) enter
different bounds. (i) The lower end enters every bound on λ0 at the numerical point that rests on the size of the wave.
In the operator norm, whatever the mean m1, every admissible C_app is at least (4/3) c_e a^(−3/2), the operator norm
of W_TT at the point X* of Section 56.5 at the phase ψ = 0 (Proposition 56.6 (i) and its proof), and by
Lemma 56.2 (a), a^(−3/2) > 7.133376, so

    (4/3) c_e a^(−3/2) ≥ (4/3) · 1.3240711 · 7.133376 > 12.593309.

This uses c_e ≥ 1.3240711 and nothing else about c_e; with any proven lower bound c₋ for c_e in its place the constant
is (4/3) c₋ a^(−3/2). Combined with ε1 < s0 < 0.030768560 (Section 56.3), the quotient of the two is
0.030768560/12.593309 < 0.0024433, which is the operator-norm bound of Proposition 56.8; that bound therefore holds
exactly as far as the lower end of c_e does. The Frobenius and largest-entry bounds 0.0019079 and 0.0012228 use the
lower end in the same way, and no other property of c_e (Remark 56.7). (ii) The upper end enters only
through env ≤ c_e, in Lemma 56.2 (e), where any c_e < 3 suffices and which no bound of Section 56.5
uses.

### 56.3 The admissible range of ε1

At the numerical point, items (i)–(iii) at the end of Section 2.5 give three facts. First, μ0/a² − 1 > 12, so the
standing condition 0 < ε1 < min(s0, μ0/a² − 1) of Section 2.5 reads 0 < ε1 < s0. Second, no ε1 ≥ 0.6013096
serves for Lemma 2.6 (e). Third, 0.030768559 < s0 < 0.030768560, where s0 = (m*² + 1)^(1/2) − m* and m* = μ_end/a²
is the number of Lemma 56.2 (d). So every admissible ε1 is below 0.030768560.

### 56.4 The second harmonic of stage 0

The wave W_TT and the second harmonic χ are those of Lemma 4.5 and (4.9). Here c² = cos² ϑ,
s² = sin² ϑ and ζ = cos 2ϑ = c² − s² are the angular functions of Section 2.6, and h² = 2/(1 + ζ²).

**Lemma 56.5** (The second harmonic.) On Ω × S¹,

    χ = −(1/12) A² env(v)² h² (4ζ sin 2θ + (1 − ζ²) cos 2θ) (r⁻² − (v − τ0)^(−1/2) r^(−3/2)).

*Proof.* With ∂_θ y1 = −(α/3) a1, ∂_θ y2 = (α/3) a2, a1 := 2c² sin θ + s² cos θ, a2 := 2s² cos θ + c² sin θ, one has
a1² − a1 a2 + a2² = 3(c⁴ sin² θ + s⁴ cos² θ + c² s² sin θ cos θ). With sin² θ = (1 − cos 2θ)/2, cos² θ =
(1 + cos 2θ)/2, c⁴ − s⁴ = ζ and c² s² = (1 − ζ²)/4, the definition of F_2 after Lemma 4.5 becomes

    F_2 = (α²/3)((c⁴ − s⁴) cos 2θ − c² s² sin 2θ) = (α²/12)(4ζ cos 2θ − (1 − ζ²) sin 2θ),   α² = A² env² h² r⁻³.

Along ℓ = ∂_r at fixed (v, ϑ, φ1, φ2), the transport (∂_r + 3/(2r)) Z = r⁻³ κ, κ independent of r, with Z = 0 at
r = v − τ0 (that is, on Σ_τ0), has the solution Z = −2κ (r⁻² − (v − τ0)^(−1/2) r^(−3/2)), since (r^(3/2) Z)' =
r^(−3/2) κ. The θ-primitive of 4ζ cos 2θ − (1 − ζ²) sin 2θ with zero mean is (1/2)(4ζ sin 2θ + (1 − ζ²) cos 2θ). ∎

### 56.5 The threshold in three norms

The bounds of Proposition 56.8 compare ε1 with a constant C_app such that |g_app − g0| ≤ C_app λ. Both depend on
how |·| is read on symmetric 2-tensors of Cartesian components. This section treats three readings: the operator
norm of Section 2.5, the Frobenius norm |·|_F, and the largest absolute entry |·|_max. Let X* be the point
τ = 2 − a, x = (a, 0, 0, 0) (so r = a, v = 2, ϑ = 0). It lies in Ω of (2.8): τ0 < 2 − a < V − q_end ≤ τ_end
by Lemma 56.2 (c), and v + τ − τ_end = 4 − a − τ_end < 4 < V + 1. Put

    α* := c_e a^(−3/2),      χ* := (c_e²/3)(a⁻² − a^(−3/2)/2),      B := (4/3) α*² + 4 χ*²,

so that α* is the value at X* of α = A env h r^(−3/2).

**Proposition 56.6** (ε1 and C_app in three norms.) At the numerical point let g_app = g0 + λ [g1] +
Σ_(j≥2) λ^j [g_j] be an approximant of Theorem 4.11, built from any stage data, and let C_app be a number such
that |g_app − g0| ≤ C_app λ on Ω for every λ in some interval (0, λ̄], λ̄ > 0. Let ε1 > 0 be such that every symmetric
g̃ with |g̃ − g0| ≤ ε1 on Ω is nondegenerate, as Lemma 2.8 requires of it, and let M_22 be the (x2, x2)
Cartesian component of the mean m1(X*) of g1 at X*. Then:

(i) in the operator norm, ε1 < s0 and C_app ≥ (4/3) α* + |M_22|;

(ii) in the Frobenius norm, ε1 < s0 and C_app² ≥ B + |m1(X*)|_F²;

(iii) in the largest absolute entry, ε1 < 1/(4m*) and C_app ≥ (4/3) α* + |M_22|.

In particular, whatever the stage data, C_app > 12.593309 in (i) and (iii) and C_app > 16.127552 in (ii), and

    ε1/C_app < 0.0024433 in (i),    ε1/C_app < 0.0019079 in (ii),    ε1/C_app < 0.0012228 in (iii).    (56.4)

*Proof.* *C_app bounds g1 at every point.* Fix (X, θ) ∈ Ω × S¹ with v(X) > 0, and take θ ∈ (0, 2π]. For n = 1, 2, …
put λ_n := v(X)/(θ + 2πn). Then λ_n → 0 and v(X)/λ_n = θ + 2πn, so at X, (g_app − g0)/λ_n = g1(X, θ) +
Σ_(j≥2) λ_n^(j−1) g_j(X, θ). The profiles g_j are bounded, so letting n → ∞ gives |g1(X, θ)| ≤ C_app. At X*, v = 2.

*g1 at X*.* By Theorem 4.11, g1(X*, θ) = m1(X*) + W_TT(X*, ψ) + χ(X*, ψ) D with ψ := θ + φ1(X*), where φ1(X) is
the phase shift in g1 = m1 + W(X, θ + φ1(X)) there, and D := dv ⊗ dv; as θ runs over S¹, so does ψ. At X*, A = 1,
env(2) = c_e β(0) = c_e, ζ = cos 2ϑ = 1 and h = 1, and x1 = a, x2 = x3 = x4 = 0, cos²ϑ = 1, sin²ϑ = 0. The Cartesian
formula of Lemma 2.9 (a), at the phase ψ, gives λ W_TT = 2 a^(−3/2) (G dx2² − (G/3)(dx2² + dx3² + dx4²)), where G is
the polarization of Section 2.6 at the phase ψ, so G/λ = A env h cos ψ = c_e cos ψ. Hence in the components (τ, x1, x2,
x3, x4)

    W_TT(X*, ψ) = α* cos ψ Λ,      Λ := diag(0, 0, 4/3, −2/3, −2/3).

By Lemma 56.5, with ζ = 1, h = 1 and v − τ0 = 4, χ(X*, ψ) = −(1/3) c_e² sin 2ψ (a⁻² − a^(−3/2)/2) =
−χ* sin 2ψ. And dv = dτ + dx1 at X*, so D = U Uᵀ with U = (1, 1, 0, 0, 0): D_22 = 0 and |D|_F = |U|² = 2.

*(i) and (iii).* The (x2, x2) entry of g1(X*, θ) is M_22 + (4/3) α* cos ψ. It is e2ᵀ g1 e2 for the unit vector e2,
so it bounds both the operator norm and the largest absolute entry, and its supremum over ψ is |M_22| + (4/3) α*.

*(ii).* Write W(ψ) := W_TT(X*, ψ), χ := χ(X*, ψ) and Y(ψ) := g1 at the phase ψ. Since W(ψ + π) = −W(ψ),
χ(X*, ψ + π) = χ and χ(X*, ψ ± π/2) = −χ, the parallelogram law gives |Y(ψ)|_F² + |Y(ψ + π)|_F² =
2|m1(X*) + χD|_F² + 2|W(ψ)|_F² and |Y(ψ + π/2)|_F² + |Y(ψ − π/2)|_F² = 2|m1(X*) − χD|_F² + 2|W(ψ + π/2)|_F².
Here |W(ψ)|_F² + |W(ψ + π/2)|_F² = α*² |Λ|_F² = (8/3) α*² and |m1(X*) + χD|_F² + |m1(X*) − χD|_F² =
2|m1(X*)|_F² + 8χ², so the four squares sum to 4|m1(X*)|_F² + 16χ² + (16/3) α*², and the largest of them is at
least |m1(X*)|_F² + 4χ² + (4/3) α*². At ψ = π/4, χ² = χ*², so C_app² ≥ |m1(X*)|_F² + B.

*The thresholds for ε1.* At a point of Ω where μ/r² = m*, let e be the unit eigenvector of g0 with eigenvalue −s0
(Lemma 2.8). Then g0 + s0 e eᵀ annihilates e, and |s0 e eᵀ| = s0 in the operator and in the Frobenius
norm, e eᵀ having rank one; so ε1 < s0 in (i) and (ii). For (iii) take the point (τ_end, (a, 0, 0, 0)) of Ω, where
μ/r² = m* (Lemma 56.2 (d)) and x̂ = e1. There the (τ, x1) block of g0 is [[−1 + m*, m*], [m*, 1 + m*]], with
inverse [[−1 − m*, m*], [m*, 1 − m*]], and g0 is the identity on the other directions. For ξ := (1, −1, 0, 0, 0),
ξᵀ g0⁻¹ ξ = (−1 − m*) − 2m* + (1 − m*) = −4m*, so the rank-one formula gives det(g0 + t ξ ξᵀ) = det g0 (1 − 4m* t) =
4m* t − 1. Every entry of t ξ ξᵀ is ±t or 0, so g0 + ξ ξᵀ/(4m*) is degenerate and |ξ ξᵀ/(4m*)|_max = 1/(4m*); so
ε1 < 1/(4m*).

*The numbers.* By Lemma 56.2 (a), 0.2698587885 < a < 0.269858789, so a^(−3/2) > 7.1333765,
a^(−3/2) < 7.1333766 and a⁻² > 13.7317809: indeed 0.269858789³ · 7.1333765² < 1, 0.2698587885³ · 7.1333766² > 1 and
0.269858789² · 13.7317809 < 1. Hence a⁻² − a^(−3/2)/2 > 13.7317809 − 3.5666883 = 10.1650926. With c_e > 1.3240711
((56.2)),

    (4/3) α* > (4/3)(1.3240711)(7.1333765) > 12.5934635,      χ* > (1.3240711²/3)(10.1650926) > 5.9403588,
    B > (3/4)(12.5934635)² + 4 (5.9403588)² > 260.097942 > 16.127552² = 260.0979335….

By Section 56.3, s0 < 0.030768560, and by Lemma 56.2 (d), m* > 16.23497014, so 1/(4m*) <
0.0153989. Now 0.0024433 · 12.593309 > 0.03076918, 0.0019079 · 16.127552 > 0.03076975 and 0.0012228 · 12.593309 >
0.01539909, which with these bounds give (56.4). ∎

Proposition 56.8 carries these bounds over to the threshold λ0 of Theorem 3.1. A nonzero M_22 lowers the bounds of
(i) and (iii), and a nonzero m1(X*) that of (ii).

**Remark 56.7** (The constant c_e in the three bounds.) Proposition 56.6 uses about c_e only
a lower bound, through α*, χ* and B, which increase with c_e; s0 and m* depend on a and μ_end = 227/192 alone, and the
upper end of c_e enters nowhere: the facts on Ω that the proposition rests on are Lemma 56.2 (c) and (d),
whose proofs use no bound on c_e. The figure 12.593309 holds for every c_e ≥ 1.3240549 and 16.127552 for every
c_e ≥ 1.3240711, while the three bounds of (56.4) hold for every c_e ≥ 1.32404: at c_e = 1.32404 the
arithmetic above gives (4/3) α* > 12.593167 and B > 16.12696², and 0.0024433 · 12.593167, 0.0019079 · 16.12696 and
0.0012228 · 12.593167 exceed 0.030768560, 0.030768560 and 0.0153989. With the sharper lower end c_e > 1.3240867 of
(56.2) one gets C_app > 12.593611 in (i) and (iii) and C_app > 16.127845 in (ii).

### 56.6 The bound on λ0

**Proposition 56.8** (An upper bound for λ0.) Let K ≥ 6. At the numerical point, let λ0 > 0 and C be
numbers with the properties that the proof of Theorem 3.1 gives them: for an approximant g_app of Theorem 4.11
with N = K + 3 stages, built from any stage data, and for every λ ∈ (0, λ0], a metric g_λ on Ω (in Theorem 3.1, the
solution) satisfies

    |g_λ − g_app| ≤ C λ^(K−3),      |g_λ − g0| ≤ C λ      on Ω,

and C λ0 ≤ ε1, where ε1 > 0 is such that every symmetric g̃ with |g̃ − g0| ≤ ε1 on Ω is nondegenerate. Then

    λ0 < 0.0024433   if |·| is the operator norm,
    λ0 < 0.0019079   if |·| is the Frobenius norm,
    λ0 < 0.0012228   if |·| is the largest absolute entry,    (56.5)

the same reading of |·| being used in all three conditions on λ0, C and ε1. In the operator norm of Section 2.5,
with ε1 the number fixed there, the λ0 and C of Theorem 3.1, as its proof takes them, have these properties: so the
threshold λ0 that the proof of Theorem 3.1 delivers at the numerical point is below 0.0024433.

*Proof.* Fix one of the three readings, and let λ̄ ∈ (0, λ0]. For λ ∈ (0, λ̄], on Ω,

    |g_app − g0| ≤ |g_λ − g0| + |g_λ − g_app| ≤ C λ + C λ^(K−3) ≤ C (1 + λ̄^(K−4)) λ,

since K − 4 ≥ 2. So the number C_app := C (1 + λ̄^(K−4)) and ε1 satisfy the hypotheses of Proposition 56.6,
which gives C (1 + λ̄^(K−4)) > 12.593309 in the operator norm and in the largest absolute entry, and
C (1 + λ̄^(K−4)) > 16.127552 in the Frobenius norm. As λ̄ is arbitrary in (0, λ0] and λ̄^(K−4) → 0 as λ̄ → 0,
C ≥ 12.593309, respectively C ≥ 16.127552; in particular C > 0, and λ0 ≤ ε1/C. By Proposition 56.6 (i) and
(ii), ε1 < s0 < 0.030768560 in the operator and the Frobenius norm (Section 56.3); by (iii) and
Lemma 56.2 (d), ε1 < 1/(4m*) < 0.0153989 in the largest absolute entry. Hence λ0 is below
0.030768560/12.593309, 0.030768560/16.127552 and 0.0153989/12.593309 in the three readings, and these quotients are
below 0.0024433, 0.0019079 and 0.0012228, since 0.0024433 · 12.593309 > 0.03076918, 0.0019079 · 16.127552 >
0.03076975 and 0.0012228 · 12.593309 > 0.01539909.

The proof of Theorem 3.1 takes g_app of Theorem 4.11 with N = K + 3 stages and the stage data of
Lemma 7.4, obtains |g_λ − g_app| ≤ C λ^(K−3) and |g_λ − g0| ≤ C λ on Ω for λ ≤ λ0 from
Theorem 6.1, and takes λ0 so small that C λ0 ≤ ε1; and by Lemma 2.8 every symmetric g̃
with |g̃ − g0| ≤ ε1 < s0 on Ω is Lorentzian, hence nondegenerate. This gives the last statement. ∎

At the numerical point 10 l5 = 1, and 409 · 0.0024433 < 1; so in each reading the wavelength 10 l5 exceeds λ0 by a
factor above 409. Of the conditions that the proofs of Theorem 3.1 and Theorem 6.1 place on λ0, the bound
uses only C λ0 ≤ ε1; the others can only make λ0 smaller, and no lower bound for λ0 is given.

**Remark 56.9** (Numerical observation.) The bounds of Proposition 56.6 hold whatever the mean m1 of
g1 at X* is: in (i) and (iii) it enters only through its entry M_22, and in (ii) through |m1(X*)|_F ≥ |M_22|. For the
envelope of (56.1) and the stage data of Lemma 7.4, the first stage was solved numerically in
floating point: its data on Σ_τ0, which solve the order-one mean of the constraint equations (a linear system with
explicit coefficients), harmonic by harmonic in the Legendre polynomials of cos 2ϑ, and its evolution on the past of
X* in Ω by a spectral method in r and in cos 2ϑ. The value found is M_22 = 2.207738, stable under refinement to
1.4 × 10⁻⁷ and reproduced by a second discretisation. With this value, C_app > 12.593309 + 2.207738 in (i) and (iii) and
C_app² > 16.127552² + 2.207738² in (ii), and the three quotients of (56.4) would be below 0.0020789,
0.0018902 and 0.0010404. No proof uses this value, and no bound on M_22 is proved, so these three figures are not
proved; the bounds proved are those of (56.5).

## 57. At the prescribed wavelength 10 l5

Theorem 3.1 is a statement for small λ. This chapter treats the problem at the prescribed wavelength λ = 10 l5, at
two seeds, with the envelope sin⁴(π(v − 1/2)/3) on [1/2, 7/2]. That envelope is C³ and not C⁴, so Theorem 3.1 does
not apply to it at any λ (Remark 3.2); for the smooth envelope of Definition 56.1, whose
parameters are those of the first seed below, the threshold λ0 that the proof of Theorem 3.1 delivers lies below
0.0024433 in the operator norm (Proposition 56.8), and 10 l5 exceeds it by a factor above 409. At 10 l5 the wavelength
is not small against the curvature length (Proposition 57.2), and the problem is posed as a characteristic initial
value problem in double-null gauge: the seed on an ingoing cone, the incoming wave on an outgoing one.

The chapter proves the following. The problem has a solution where the solution is the seed (Theorem 57.18). Wherever
a vacuum solution exists in the gauge with the seed's transverse derivative of R on the seed's cone, its leaves inside
the seed's horizon generator are outer trapped, and its T²-invariant marginally outer trapped sections lie at or outside
that generator and, under a condition on the generators through them, in an explicit band (Proposition 57.20,
Corollary 57.22). On the data cone the outgoing constraint has exact solutions, and an explicit approximant satisfies
it up to an explicit residual (Section 57.2). Two explicit metrics of the class on a region beyond the seed
have explicit residual bounds (Section 57.9). A continuation lemma states what existence beyond the seed would
need (Lemma 57.43). No existence is proved beyond the seed, and Remark 57.44 says why. Numerical
observations, which no proof uses, are kept as remarks.

### 57.1 The seeds and the scales

**Definition 57.1** (The two seeds.) Fix l5 > 0 and the wavelength λ := 10 l5. The first seed is the
five-dimensional Schwarzschild–Tangherlini metric of mass μ0 = 100 l5², the second that of mass μ0 = 1000 l5². Lengths
are measured in units of the horizon radius r_h := √μ0, so that μ0 = 1 and f(r) := 1 − r⁻²; then l5 = 1/10 and λ = 1
at the first seed, and l5 = 1000^(−1/2) and λ = 10^(−1/2) at the second. The envelope is env(v) := sin⁴(π(v − 1/2)/3)
for 1/2 < v < 7/2 and env(v) := 0 otherwise, with amplitude A = 1. The first seed has the μ0 and l5 of
Definition 56.1.

**Proposition 57.2** (No separation of scales.) Let 𝒦 = 72 μ0²/r⁸ be the Kretschmann scalar of the seed
(Proposition 2.5 (b)) and L := 𝒦^(−1/4) its curvature length. At both seeds λ/L = 10 on x_K = 1, that is at
r = r_q := (√72 μ0 l5²)^(1/4). At the horizon r = √μ0,

    λ/L = 72^(1/4) ∈ (2.912, 2.913)  (first seed),      λ/L = (72/100)^(1/4) ∈ (0.9211, 0.9212)  (second seed).

Against the areal radius, λ/r = 1 and λ/r = 10^(−1/2) ∈ (0.3162, 0.3163) at the horizon, and on x_K = 1

    λ/r_q = 10^(1/2) 72^(−1/8) ∈ (1.852, 1.853)  (first seed),
    λ/r_q = 10 · 72^(−1/8) 1000^(−1/4) ∈ (1.041, 1.042)  (second seed).

*Proof.* On x_K = 1, l5² √𝒦 = 1 by the definition of x_K (Chapter 2), so L = l5 and λ/L = 10. At r = √μ0,
𝒦 = 72/μ0² and L = √μ0 · 72^(−1/4), so λ/L = 10 l5 · 72^(1/4)/√μ0; this is 72^(1/4) when √μ0 = 10 l5 and
72^(1/4)/√10 = (72/100)^(1/4) when √μ0 = √1000 l5. Likewise λ/√μ0 = 10 l5/√μ0 is 1 and 10^(−1/2). On x_K = 1,
r_q⁸ = 72 μ0² l5⁴, so (λ/r_q)⁸ = 10⁸ l5⁴/(72 μ0²), which is 10⁴/72 at the first seed and 10²/72 at the second. The
bounds follow from 2.912⁴ < 72 < 2.913⁴, 0.9211⁴ < 0.72 < 0.9212⁴, 0.3162² < 0.1 < 0.3163², 1.852⁸ < 10⁴/72 < 1.853⁸
and 1.041⁸ < 10²/72 < 1.042⁸. ∎

So the expansion parameter of a high-frequency theorem, the wavelength over the curvature length, is 10 on x_K = 1 and
of order one at the horizon. The statement of Section 3.1 that the waves are high-frequency on D_T once
λ < l5/10 concerns the approximant, not the threshold λ0. Against the scale r on which the curvature varies the ratio
is of order one as well; that is the parameter a construction from waves exact on a locally linear background, in the
manner of [AB26, Section 3.1], would see, and there the wavelengths are chosen, while here λ is prescribed.

**Remark 57.3** (Numerical observation.) A numerical scheme in the Bondi chart, which evolves
ingoing null slices from a timelike excision boundary inside x_K = 1 and whose premise is that the outgoing expansion of
the round spheres has one zero on each column and that the boundary is outflow, was run at λ = 10 l5 at both seeds. The
premise fails before the peak of the shell: a second zero holds over 0.04 in v from v = 1.50 at the first seed (1.496
on a finer grid) and from v = 1.583 at the second (three grids agreeing to 0.0005), and the boundary ceases to be
outflow within 0.1 after; deeper excisions, at r = 0.39 and 0.25 at the first seed and at r = 0.21 at the second, fail
earlier. Up to the failure the growth factor of the radiation field, the exponential of the integral in v of the largest
v-derivative of its two polarizations, is 1.9 and 2.1, and a finite-difference amplification of the data along one
direction, a lower bound for the norm of the propagator, is 1.28 and 1.00; at λ = l5 at the first seed, where the scheme
completes, they are 6.9 and 1.71, while the sup-norm Grönwall factor is 17, 2 × 10⁵ and 6 × 10³ in the three cases.
These breakdown times were measured at one angular resolution; at its own time step the scheme is unstable in angle at
the two finer angular resolutions tried, on the seed itself, before the wave arrives. No approximant on D_T comes from
that scheme at 10 l5, and no proof uses these observations.

### 57.2 The data cone: an explicit approximant and exact data

This section concerns the characteristic data on the outgoing cone u = −10 at the two seeds of Definition 57.1, whose
wavelength parameters are λ = 1 (the first seed) and λ = 1/√10 (the second seed). On this cone the Raychaudhuri
constraint determines the areal radius R from the other data. We prove two things. First, an explicit approximant
R_app, a tensor Chebyshev series with the coefficients of Section B.7, satisfies the constraint
up to an explicit residual (Proposition 57.8). Second, the constraint has an exact solution on every generator,
positive and within an explicit distance of the Tangherlini radius (Proposition 57.13); the approximant equals it
for v ≤ 1/2, lies within 10⁻⁶ of it for 1/2 ≤ v ≤ 7/2, and departs from it at most linearly in r beyond
(Corollary 57.14).

### 57.3 The constraint on the data cone

The metrics of the class are written in double-null gauge as

    g = −4 e^(2W) du dv + G_x (dx − β du)² + R² ((1 + x)/2) e^(2P) dφ1² + R² ((1 − x)/2) e^(2Q) dφ2²,
    G_x = R² e^(−2(P + Q))/(4(1 − x²)),

with R > 0, P, Q, W and β functions of (u, v, x), and x ∈ [−1, 1]. The choice of G_x is the gauge: the leaves
u = const, v = const carry the volume element (R³/4) dx dφ1 dφ2.

**Lemma 57.4** (The outgoing constraint.) For every metric of the class, at every point
with |x| < 1,
